generated_text: Honestly, I’m shattered. Little Leo kept me up half the night. Teething, I think. Or just a general protest against sleep. Oh, bless him. They’re little terrorists, aren’t they? Still, you look… relatively human. I expected zombie-level exhaustion. That’s kind. It’s the coffee. And sheer willpower. Though I'm seriously considering a lie-down once your here. Are you still up for Saturday night? Gemma’s finally booked that Italian place. Yes! Absolutely. I need a night out. Proper grown-up conversation and someone else cooking. Though knowing Gemma, “grown-up conversation” will involve detailed recounts of the latest drama at the school gates. It probably will. She’s… invested. But it'll be good. It feels like ages since we just properly chilled. How’s Ben coping with you being out? He usually looks like you’ve abandoned him to the wolves if you so much as pop to the shops. He’s alright. He’s been really good actually, he's taken on a lot with work and insists he needs a night out too. He’s started this new project at work which is completely consuming him. Something about streamlining logistics for… well, honestly, it goes over my head after the first sentence. Sounds like Ben. Always needing a challenge. Speaking of work, I landed that new client – the garden centre. Proofreading their website and social media stuff. It’s not glamorous, but it’s steady income. That’s brilliant, Sarah! See? All that networking is paying off. You’re a marketing whiz, that’s what. Are you still seeing much of Mum and Dad? We went over on Tuesday. Mum’s got a new obsession - genealogy. She’s convinced we’re descended from royalty. She was showing me charts and everything. Apparently, we have a distant relative who was a minor baron or something. Oh, Mum! That’s fantastic. She's always been a bit of a history buff. She told me once we were related to pirates. I think she just makes it up as she goes along. Probably. But it keeps her entertained. And Dad’s just happy she’s occupied. He spends most of his time in the garden now. He’s really getting into roses, you know? Keeps muttering about “hybrid teas” and “deadheading”. He always did have a green thumb. It's such a shame the kids never really took an interest.

Honestly, the queues at Stansted were  insane  last month. I nearly missed my flight to Amsterdam. Oh, really? I went through Gatwick - it wasn’t too bad, surprisingly. Though they were grilling everyone about their return ticket, you know, just to prove you weren’t planning on overstaying. Felt a bit…much. Exactly! It's just different now, isn’t it? Used to just breeze through, flash your passport, done. Now it’s like an interrogation. And the queues… I was thinking about that trip we did interrailing after uni? Can’t believe how easy it was then. Just hop on a train, no questions asked. God, that was brilliant. Remember getting completely lost in Prague? We ended up in some tiny pub, filled with locals, and nobody spoke a word of English. Oh, I remember! You tried to order a beer, and pointed frantically at someone else’s pint. It was chaos. But they were so friendly, kept topping us up anyway. It felt so…free, travelling like that. It did, didn’t it? Before all the border checks and extra paperwork. I’m doing a conference in Berlin next month, and I’m already dreading the airport. I used to just chuck everything in a bag the day before, now I’m making spreadsheets. Spreadsheets! You're a PhD student, I expected nothing less. But seriously, it’s a palaver. It’s amazing how much the goalposts have moved. I was talking to my mam about it, and she was saying it's nothing like her trips to Spain in the 70s. No chance. My uncle told me stories about driving all the way to Greece in a campervan back then. Just…go. Now? It’s visas, permits, insurance... the list is endless. And the cost! Getting a coach to Paris used to be cheaper than a train to London. Now it feels like they’re trying to price people  out  of travelling. It’s a shame, really. Those spontaneous trips were the best. Discovering hidden little towns, meeting random people… You can't really plan for that, can you? You need that freedom to just  go . You can't. I’m thinking of maybe just sticking to the UK for my holidays this year. A bit boring, but at least it’ll be stress-free. Maybe a caravan trip to the Lake District? Now  that  sounds like a plan.

Right, so, dessert options. We’ve got apple crumble, chocolate brownies, or… I could whip up a trifle? Trifle! Trifle’s the best! With the jelly and the cream and the strawberries! Brownies are better. Chocolate is  always  better. Okay, okay, we’ll vote. Two for trifle, one for brownies. Trifle it is then. Though you, young man, are getting extra vegetables with your dinner to balance out all that chocolate craving. Aw, Mum! That’s not fair! Life isn’t fair, darling. Now, who wants to set up Monopoly? Me! Me! I want to be the thimble! No way! I called dibs on the dog last time, you always get the thimble! Right, let’s not start a war over playing pieces. You can be the car, and your sister can have the thimble. Happy? Yes! Fine. But I’m getting all the hotels this time. That’s the spirit! Now, let’s remember the rules. No cheating, no arguing over rent, and no deliberately bankrupting each other… too quickly. What does ‘bankrupting’ mean? It means… when someone runs out of money and can’t pay what they owe, they have to leave the game. Oh. So, like, when someone lands on my Park Lane with a hotel and they have to give me  everything ? Exactly. And that’s why it's important to manage your money wisely. Don't just buy up all the properties immediately, think about building strategically… Can I buy Mayfair? It's pink! Pink is my favourite! You can definitely try, darling. But someone else might want it too. It all comes down to the dice and a bit of luck. And maybe some clever trading. I’m saving all my money for the orange ones. They're the best ones to build on. Everyone lands on those. Smart thinking. Now, let's get this game started before I change my mind and decide we're all doing spelling practice instead. Noooo! Monopoly is much better! Yeah! Monopoly! Alright, alright. Here we go. Bank’s open… and may the best player win! I  will  win! Yes! Six! Ugh. Two. Boo. It's going to be a long evening, isn’t it? It’s going to be  fun ! Not if she keeps getting lucky! We'll see about that. Let's play! Can I buy Old Kent Road? Please? It’s only sixty pounds! Don’t bother, it’s a terrible property.

Honestly, the traffic was  mental  getting out of Durham. I thought I was going to be stuck there forever. Did you see that van trying to merge onto the A1? Absolutely bonkers. No, thankfully I was lost in thought. Probably contemplating the existential dread of another week at work. Though, to be fair, the A1 is always a gamble, isn't it? It’s like a slow-motion car crash waiting to happen. It is. And the people who just…stop. Like, mid-lane. No warning, no indication. Just…brake. What is  that  about? Probably looking at their phones. It’s the only logical explanation. People are utterly glued to those things, it’s frightening. I saw someone actually  reading  a book on the motorway the other day. A physical book! No way! Seriously? That’s…a new level of recklessness. I mean, I listen to podcasts, which isn’t ideal, but at least my hands are on the wheel. A book?! Swear on it. Nearly caused a pile-up. Anyway, enough complaining about terrible drivers. How was your weekend? Did you manage to get any of that corpus work done? A little. I’m so behind. Professor Davies is breathing down my neck about the metadata tagging. Apparently, I'm "not prioritising sufficiently." Like, I have a life, you know? It's not all 15th-century manuscripts and databases. Sounds stressful. Academia will do that to you, eh? All those deadlines and passionate academics. I’m wrestling with a particularly stubborn drainage issue at the moment. It’s a new build, and they’ve completely botched the stormwater management. It's a headache. Oh, that sounds…fun. Not. What kind of botched? Like, flooding kind of botched? Potentially. If we get another downpour like last week, yes. It’s all very politically sensitive, obviously. The developers don't want to admit fault, the local council is breathing down  my  neck…it's a whole thing. It’s just…engineering, you know? It should be straightforward. It  should  work. Right? You'd think something as basic as drainage... It's like when the washing machine breaks and you just want someone to fix it, not explain the complex mechanics of the impeller. Precisely! I just want it to  not leak ! Is that too much to ask? Apparently. So, Durham aside, how’s family? Has your grandma been keeping busy with her knitting?

Right then, finished the crossword. Took me ages with 23 down, "Maritime mammal, six letters". Thought it was a whale at first, but the crossing letters didn’t fit. Turns out it was a seal. A seal, eh? I never could get on with those crosswords. Too much thinking. Give me a good detective novel any day. Something with a proper twist. Not these modern ones where it's obvious who did it halfway through. Oh, I used to enjoy a good crossword. Keeps the brain ticking, you know. Though I haven't done one in… well, a good while now. Since Arthur's been less mobile, I’ve been spending more time just sitting with him, really. Understandable, love. It's good of you, it is. He's a lucky man. Did you see young Kevin down the road? New car, bright red. Showed off something awful when he drove past this morning. Kevin? The one who used to leave his motorbike engine running outside our house at seven in the morning? Good riddance to bad rubbish, I say. A fancy car won’t change his manners. Now, now, Arthur. That's a bit harsh. He's just a young lad trying to get on. Though I agree, the noise  was  dreadful. Reminded me of your motorbike days, though, didn't it? Roaring around the countryside. Those were the days, eh? Before speed cameras and health and safety. Good times. Still, at least Kevin's got a job to pay for it. Seems hard to come by these days, decent work. They all seem to be working in warehouses now, boxed up like sardines. No pride in their work, none at all. Used to be, you learned a trade. Bricklaying, carpentry, something you could  do  with your hands. My brother, George, he was a brilliant carpenter. Could build anything. Made a lovely rocking horse for little Emily when she was born. Still got it, up in the attic. Emily’s grown now, isn't she? Doesn't seem five minutes ago she was a little 'un climbing all over us. Time flies, doesn't it? Flies like a greased whippet. Remember when we used to take her to the beach at Cromer? Building sandcastles until her little hands were raw? And she’d always insist on wearing those bright pink wellies, even on sunny days! She was a determined one, that girl.

Right, so I was thinking about the packaging, and I genuinely think we need to step it up. The jars are…fine, but they just feel a bit, well, cheap. Especially when we’re positioning ourselves as a natural, premium brand. Yeah, I get that. It's hard though, isn’t it? Because the frosted glass ones, the ones I showed you, are nearly triple the price per unit. That really eats into the profit margin, especially when we’re trying to keep everything affordable. I know, I know. It's a balance. But think about it – people  judge  a book by its cover. And skincare, even more so. It’s a visual product. They see it on Instagram, they see it in someone’s bathroom, it needs to  look  expensive, even if it's not astronomically priced. What about a compromise? Maybe slightly thicker glass? And we could look at a different lid – something rose gold, maybe? Rose gold… hmm. Potentially? I’m a bit worried about trends, though. Rose gold feels a bit…last year, doesn't it? Would silver be better? More timeless? Hmm, good point. Silver is safer. Okay, silver lids. But definitely thicker glass. And we need to get the dimensions right. I’ve been trying to visualise it with the labels, and I’m worried the current jars look a bit squat. Squat? What do you mean? Just…not elegant. I was looking at some competitor packaging online, and theirs are taller, more streamlined. I have some measurements here, actually. Their standard jar is 70mm in diameter and 85mm high. Ours are 65mm diameter and 75mm high. It’s not a massive difference, but it could make a big impact. Okay, that’s helpful. I can send those specs to the supplier, see how much of a price difference it makes. It might be worth getting a sample made, just to compare. Speaking of suppliers, I finally managed to get hold of Mark - he's been swamped. He's confirmed the organic rosehip oil order, which is brilliant. It’s arriving next week. Oh, fantastic! That’s a relief. We were getting low. I’ve been meaning to ask, how’s the Etsy shop doing? Have you seen a boost since that influencer posted about us? It was crazy for about 48 hours. We completely sold out of the face balm!

Honestly, the price of everything is just… scandalous now, isn’t it? I went to get a loaf of bread yesterday – a  loaf  – and nearly choked. Three pounds! Three pounds for a basic white loaf. You’re telling me! I filled the car up this morning. Nearly a hundred quid. A hundred! Used to be able to do it for sixty, comfortably. They say it’s the global situation, but it feels like they’re just taking the mickey. Aye, that’s what I think. Taking advantage, the lot of them. Did you see that piece on the news about the water companies? Pumping sewage into the sea! Utterly disgraceful. I did. Shocking. And they’re still getting away with it. Bonuses for the executives, while everyone else is struggling to pay their bills. Makes you wonder where it'll all end. It does indeed. Though, to be fair, I’m mostly worried about the heating. I’ve been trying to be sensible, keeping the thermostat down, wearing layers… but it’s still going to be a hefty bill this winter. You’re better off than some, at least you’ve got a decent house. Old Man Hemmings next door is practically living in a tent in his living room, he says, just to save a few pounds. Oh, the poor man. I must pop round with a tin of biscuits, he always appreciates a bit of shortbread. How are things with you and Margaret? Still planning that trip to Cornwall? We are, yes. Booked the cottage for a week in October. Hopefully, the weather will be kind. Margaret’s been a bit… anxious about it lately. Oh? What’s the matter? Her sister, Brenda, isn't well. Not serious, thankfully, but she's got some sort of chest infection. Margaret’s worried about leaving her on her own, you see. Brenda lives alone and… well, she’s not the most self-sufficient. Oh, dear. That’s a worry. Is there anyone else who can help Brenda out while you’re away? Her son, perhaps? He’s offered to pop in, but he lives up in Manchester. It’s a long drive for just a quick check-in. Margaret was thinking of asking Mrs. Davies, you know, from down the road. She's always been very kind to Brenda. Mrs. Davies is a good soul. She'd be happy to help, I'm sure.

Honestly, this weather is ridiculous for November. It feels like… April. Tell me about it. I was wearing a t-shirt walking the dog this morning. The dog was looking at me like  I  was the weird one. It's unsettling, isn't it? My mum keeps moaning that the birds haven't started nesting properly. She’s convinced it’s a sign of the apocalypse. Your mum’s a character. Still, she’s probably not entirely wrong. Nature’s usually a pretty good indicator. Though, frankly, I’m not complaining about being able to work in the shed without needing three layers. Speaking of the shed, are you still battling with that router table? You were muttering about it last time we saw you. Oh, don’t even get me started. It’s a temperamental beast. I think the fence is slightly off, and I can’t seem to get it perfectly aligned. It’s driving me mental. I’m starting to think I should just sell it and go back to hand-planing. Sounds stressful. Remind me to steer clear of any requests for bespoke furniture then. You’re always so productive though. I’m struggling to even  think  about Christmas presents. I feel so behind. Have you started planning, Amy? A little. Primarily focusing on food. I’m thinking a full roast this year – turkey, all the trimmings. I'm trying to get ahead and order everything online. Trying to avoid the supermarket chaos, you know? Good plan. I’ve learned my lesson trying to leave it to the last minute. Remember that year I tried to get a goose? Ended up with a frozen chicken because all the geese were gone! Oh god, yes! The Great Goose Hunt of 2018. Sounds traumatic. I’m thinking of doing a vegetarian feast. My sister's converted, and it makes things slightly less complicated. That sounds lovely. It’s nice to mix it up. We're having… well, my dad’s already starting to talk about his retirement plan. It involves moving to Spain and spending his days picking mulberries. Mulberries? Apparently, they’re a superfood! He’s read something online. Keeps going on about the ‘Mediterranean diet’. He’ll be sunburnt and complaining within a week, I guarantee it. Bless him. He’s always been a bit of a dreamer. Is he any good at DIY? Because if he  is , Spain might not be ready.

Honestly, this cutlery is dreadful. It’s like eating with plastic spoons. Bit harsh, isn't it? It's just…normal cutlery. Mum’s always had pretty basic stuff. Now, now, don’t be like that, love. It gets the job done, doesn’t it? It’s clean, and it holds your food. What more do you want? She’s got a point, you know. It’s perfectly serviceable. Though, I do recall your grandmother having silver. Proper silver. Polish it ‘til your arm aches, that stuff. I just… I keep bending the forks. It’s embarrassing when you're trying to get the last bit of potato. Aye, forks bendin’. Used to happen all the time wi’ the cheap stuff we had. Me dad, he’d just straighten ‘em out wi’ pliers. Not very elegant, mind. Pliers? Really? Aye. Resourceful, he was. Couldn’t afford new ones every time one got a little bent. Times were different then, you see. He sounds like my father. "Make do and mend" was his motto. I remember him patching up my brother’s trousers with bits of old flour sacks. Oh, bless. Speaking of patching things up, how's the leak in the roof going, Mum? Oh, don’t even ask. The man came round, had a look, said it’s worse than he thought. Needs more than just a patch, apparently. Wants to replace a whole section. Oh, dear. That sounds expensive. You have no idea. I’m waiting for a quote. Probably going to have to raid my savings. That’s rough. Maybe I could help out a bit? I’ve got a little saved from my bonus. Oh, that’s very kind, love, but I couldn’t possibly. You need that for yourself. No, honestly, Mum, let us help. It’s your house, and we want you to be comfortable. They’re right, you know. Don't be proud. Family helps each other. Aye. That's what family’s for. Offering a hand when someone's down. Don't let her struggle on her own. Alright, alright. If you insist. But I swear, I’ll pay you back as soon as I can. Don’t worry about it, Mum. It’s not a loan. How was Sarah’s hen do, by the way? Did you have a good time? Oh, it was chaos! She insisted on karaoke. Honestly, the noise… and the outfits!

Honestly, the meeting was dreadful. Just… endless spreadsheets and people arguing about percentages. You wouldn't believe it. Mmm hmm. Are we still going skiing? Of course, we're still going skiing! I just announced that to the entire office, actually. Used it as a threat to get them to finish their reports. “If these aren’t on my desk by Friday, I’m taking a week off to go skiing!” Good! Can I take my sparkly skis? The pink ones? The pink ones? Darling, you’ve barely used those. They’re practically brand new. And remember what happened last time? You kept complaining they were too… sparkly. They  were  too sparkly. They made my eyes hurt. But I still want to bring them. Just in case. We’ll talk about the skis later. Have you finished your peas? I’m worried about you being good on the slopes if you don’t eat your greens. You need your energy. They're yucky. Can I have more bread instead? Just a few more peas, please. Then bread. So, I was thinking about the ski school. Should we book you in for another lesson, or do you feel confident enough to stick with me? I want a lesson. Miss Sophie is nice. She doesn’t shout when I fall over. That’s good. I do get a bit…enthusiastic when you’re wobbling. Okay, I’ll book you in with Miss Sophie. We’ll sort that out tomorrow. Did you tell your teacher about the holiday? Yes! She said I’ll miss a maths test. But that’s okay because I don’t like maths. Well, that's a good attitude. Though, you still have to  try  to do your homework before we go. No excuses! I don't want to spend the holiday chasing after worksheets. But skiing is more important than maths! Mathematically speaking, probably not. But we can agree to disagree. Right, last few peas and then no more arguments. I need to finish this report, and then we can start planning what snacks we’re taking. Can we take chocolate coins? Lots and lots of chocolate coins? We can  discuss  chocolate coins. Let’s focus on the peas for now. Honestly, some days that office feels like herding cats. It's a miracle anything ever gets done. What's a cat? Never mind about the cats. Just eat your peas.

Ugh, Spanish is  killing  me. I just… I don’t get the subjunctive. At all. Tell me about it! Mrs. Hernandez just keeps saying “it’s about expressing doubt or possibility!” Like, thanks, super helpful. I spent all of yesterday trying to conjugate verbs and I still feel like I'm making stuff up. Seriously! And she gave us that practice sheet with, like, twenty sentences. Twenty! It’s supposed to prepare us for the speaking test next week. I’m going to sound like a robot. I’m more worried about the listening test. Her accent… it’s beautiful, obviously, but when she speaks quickly I just hear a blur of sounds. Yeah, same. At least English is going okay. Mr. Davies is actually pretty good at explaining things. Though he keeps going on about analyzing poetry like it’s the most exciting thing in the world. He's a bit intense, isn’t he? But yeah, English is a relief after Spanish. What about Maths? Still a struggle? Oh god, don’t even  start  me on Maths. Mr. Peterson is convinced we’re all secretly geniuses who just haven’t unlocked our potential. He’s already talking about calculus. Calculus! We’re in year ten! No way! Ours is still on algebra. Though honestly, even algebra feels like a different language sometimes. Did you see Leo’s face during the last lesson? He looked genuinely traumatised. Haha, yeah! He whispered to me that he was considering a career change. To a shepherd. A shepherd? That’s specific. Well, at least it wouldn’t involve numbers. What did you have for food tech today? We made pasta from scratch. It was… messy. I somehow managed to get flour  everywhere . And mine tasted like cardboard. Ooh, pasta! We did cookies. They were okay, but I think I added too much sugar and now I’m buzzing. Miss Patel kept telling us about potential careers in catering. Like, I appreciate the thought, but I'm not sure I want to spend my life covered in icing sugar. Right? I’m thinking something completely different. Maybe a wildlife photographer? I saw this documentary about someone who travels the world taking pictures of animals and it looked amazing. That sounds cool. I’ve been thinking about… I don't know, something to do with music. Maybe a sound engineer? I love gigging with the band, and it’d be awesome to be the one making everything sound perfect.

Honestly darling, I don't know what’s happened to films these days. They just aren’t  made  like they used to be, are they? All explosions and no story. Oh, Grandma, you always say that! It's just different now. What did you see that was so bad? Oh, it was… something with robots, I think. Your cousin Sarah recommended it. Said it was “visually stunning.” Visually stunning nonsense, more like! Just a lot of metal bashing into each other. I wanted characters, you know? People to  care  about. Right… So not Transformers then? Oh, goodness no! Something a bit…pretentious. More trying to be clever than actually  being  clever. It reminded me of that awful French film we tried to watch on holiday in Cornwall, years ago. The one with the… the existential sheep? Oh,  that  one! You’ve never let that go. You were absolutely fuming! Well, I was! Three hours of my life wasted watching sheep ponder the meaning of life! Honestly. Give me a good Cary Grant film any day.  North by Northwest …now  that  was a film! Hitchcock knew how to build suspense. Okay, okay, classic cinema is the best. I get it. I actually saw ‘Barbie’ last week, and it was surprisingly good. ‘Barbie’? Isn’t that the one with all the pink? Yeah, loads of pink. But it's actually really clever, it's a satire. About societal expectations and… well, it's hard to explain. It’s not just fluff. Sounds a bit…modern for me, dear. I doubt I’d understand half of it. Though, to be fair, I didn’t understand half of that art house film with the existential sheep either. You could give it a try. Ryan Gosling is hilarious as Ken. Ryan Gosling… is he the one who was in… ‘La La Land’? I quite liked that one. Yep, that’s him. He’s brilliant. Speaking of films, are you free next Saturday? There’s that film festival on at the Arts Cinema. They're showing an old Audrey Hepburn film,  Roman Holiday . Oh, now  that  sounds lovely! Audrey Hepburn…she was an angel. Yes, I'd be delighted. We could have lunch beforehand? Perfect! I’ll book tickets. And maybe we can steer clear of anything with robots or philosophical livestock. Yes, dear. Definitely steer clear of the livestock. Though, you know, sometimes even a bad film is good for a laugh.

Honestly, Mum, the traffic was  brutal  getting up here. I left ages ago and it still took nearly two hours. Did you see the weather forecast? More rain predicted for the weekend. Fantastic. Oh, you poor thing. Two hours! Birmingham’s getting worse, I tell you. Absolutely jammed. And yes, I did see. More of the same, really. This summer’s been a washout. Still, at least it’s good for the garden. Are you sure you don't want another biscuit? I got those nice ginger ones you like. No thank you, really. I’m trying to be good. Although, ginger biscuits are my weakness… How was work yesterday? Anything exciting happening in the court? Exciting? Darling, it’s the magistrates’ court. ‘Exciting’ isn’t exactly a word I’d use! Mostly shoplifting and noise complaints. Though, there was a rather dramatic case about a neighbour dispute. Apparently, someone’s been deliberately parking across another person’s driveway for months. It escalated into a proper shouting match, and now it’s in court. Honestly, the things people argue about. Oh, wow. That sounds… stressful. Still, at least it's something different from the usual. How’s Mr. Henderson getting on? Is he still threatening to retire every other Thursday? You know him. He threatened it again this week. Said his knees are playing up. Honestly, he just wants a bit of attention. He’s been a court usher for forty years, he wouldn’t know what to do with himself if he actually retired! Speaking of knees, have you managed to book that physio appointment? You were saying yours were bothering you after that run. I did, finally. It’s next Tuesday. I feel awful about cancelling our plans for last weekend, though. I really wanted to go to that vintage fair with you. Don’t you worry about it, love. Your health is more important. We can always go another time. Besides, I ended up having a lovely afternoon with Margaret. We went for a walk around Cannon Hill Park and had a gossip. She’s been reading a new crime novel, says it’s brilliant. Oh nice! I've been meaning to start a new book actually. I've got a huge pile waiting. I just haven’t had the time. School starts properly next week – prepping lessons, marking… It’s going to be hectic. Are you still fussing over Buster?

Honestly, that seminar was… a lot. Old Man Hemmings really went off on one about post-structuralism again. You’d think, after ten years, he’d find a new hobby. Sounds about right. Still clinging to his Derrida, is he? Mine wasn’t too bad, just a surprisingly high number of students who hadn’t read the assigned chapters. It’s always the same few, isn't it? Always. It's like they think osmosis will somehow transfer the information directly into their brains. Did you manage to get through the marking? I barely made a dent. I did a chunk of it on the train. It’s awful, isn’t it? Trying to decipher handwriting and…well, sometimes just  thoughts . I think one student attempted to argue that Hamlet was a socialist. Oh, no. Really? That’s… ambitious. Though, I suppose you can find socialist interpretations in everything if you squint hard enough. I’m going to need a very large glass of wine tonight. I wholeheartedly agree. Speaking of needs, we are out of milk. And possibly bread. Did you want me to grab something on the way back? There’s that little bakery just off the main road. Oh, that would be amazing, thank you. They do a really good sourdough, don’t they? And yeah, milk would be a lifesaver for my tea tomorrow morning. I’m completely running on fumes today. Sourdough it is. Anything else? I think I saw some plums at the market yesterday. Relatively ripe plums, which is a rarity. Plums would be lovely! Maybe one for later, and I could make a crumble if we’ve got enough sugar. It’s been ages since I've made a crumble. A crumble sounds perfect. Right, mental shopping list activated. Anything for dinner? I was thinking maybe we could just do something quick and easy. Stir-fry? That sounds good. We’ve got loads of veg that needs using up in the fridge. I'll get it prepped while you're at the bakery. Honestly, this is a good plan. A bit of peace and quiet, a crumble, and a glass of wine… Sounds like a perfect evening. You deserve it, after battling the post-structuralists. Plus, you’re a superstar with a crumble, everyone knows that. Oh, you flatter me. Now, let's just get home before it starts raining. Those clouds are looking rather ominous.

Right, so, Grandma's definitely free on Saturday, which is brilliant. That means we can actually go to the cinema, doesn’t it? Yay! Can we see the sparkly unicorn movie? Please? We’ll see, sweetheart. We'll look at what’s on. It might be a bit… pink for your brother, though. Unicorns  are  cool! They have swords! They do, actually. Some of them do. Okay, so Saturday cinema. I need to book tickets. And then… oh! I promised Sarah I’d try that new sourdough recipe with her. She's bringing the fancy flour. Are you making cookies too? Chocolate chip ones? Maybe. If we have time. First, sourdough. Then, potentially, cookies. It’s going to be a busy weekend! Can I help with the cookies? I can sprinkle the chocolate chips! You absolutely can. But you have to promise not to eat  all  the chocolate chips before they go in the dough. I can help too! I’m really good at stirring! You are a very good stirrer. Right. Then there’s Leo’s hair. He needs a haircut, doesn’t he? It’s getting in his eyes. No! I like my hair! It's for swishing! Like a superhero! It  is  very swishy. But it'll grow back, won't it? We can make it a bit shorter, so you can see when you're building Lego castles. He looks like a lion. A fluffy lion. He does, doesn’t he? A very handsome lion. Okay, haircut sorted. And Auntie Chloe wants to do that photoshoot with us all on Sunday. She's bringing props. Props?! What kind of props? She didn't say. Probably silly hats and big glasses and things like that. It'll be fun. I want to wear my princess dress! And my sparkly shoes! Perfect! You can wear  all  the sparkly things. Okay, so… Saturday: cinema, sourdough. Sunday: photoshoot. I think that's everything... Oh! Dinner! What are we having for dinner tonight? I need to defrost something. Pizza! Can we have pizza?!? Hmmm… maybe. If you both eat your vegetables at lunchtime. Vegetables… Don't groan at me! They're good for you. And then  maybe , pizza. Now, who wants to read a book while I check the cinema times? Me! I want the dinosaur one! I want the one with the fairy! And the glitter! Okay, okay. One dinosaur, one fairy.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think my pasta's actively trying to escape the plate. Tell me about it! Remember last week when Chloe swore her curry tasted like feet? Oh god,  yes ! And she’s usually so polite. That’s how you know it was bad. I’m starting to think bringing packed lunches is the way forward, even if it means getting up an extra half hour. Seriously. I’m considering just living off granola bars. It’s less traumatic. Are you going out tonight, then? Heard anything good happening? A few people are heading to Pryzm, apparently. But, knowing Pryzm, it’ll be sticky floors, questionable music, and a tenner for a vodka lemonade. Not exactly tempting. Ugh, Pryzm. Yeah, no. I’d rather stay in and watch reruns of  Great British Bake Off . What about that new bar, ‘The Roost’ everyone’s been talking about? Is that any good? Near the station, right? I went last week with Liam and Maya. It’s actually really nice! Bit pricey, but the cocktails are proper. And they do decent small plates. Not canteen pasta, anyway. They’ve got those board games too, if you’re feeling competitive. Ooh, sounds way more my vibe. Board games are good. I'm shockingly competitive, even at things like Connect Four. It's a problem. I believe it. You nearly caused an international incident last time we played Monopoly. It was a perfectly legitimate land grab! He  knew  I wanted Park Lane! Anyway, what are you studying, again? I always forget. Apart from suffering through university catering. Law. It's... a lot. Honestly, I spend most lectures questioning all my life choices. What about you? Still doing psychology? Yup. Though honestly, after dissecting Freud for the last three years, I’m starting to think  I  need therapy. It’s fascinating, but… heavy. Plus, all the stats! My brain hurts. Tell me about it. I’m drowning in case law. It’s like trying to learn a whole new language. Speaking of languages, did you ever get around to learning Tagalog? Your mum keeps asking, right? Don't remind me. I started a Duolingo course, got to level three, and then completely abandoned it. My mum’s convinced I’m deliberately rejecting my heritage. Oh, mums are  always  convinced of something. Mine thinks I should be interning at a law firm every waking hour.

Honestly, I’m already dreaming of being anywhere but here. Just… sun. Proper sun. Not this grey drizzle pretending to be summer. Tell me about it. I was looking at flights to Greece last night. Santorini looks… expensive, though. Seriously expensive. Santorini’s always pricey, isn’t it? You're paying for the caldera views, I suppose. Have you considered Crete? A bit more down to earth, still gorgeous. My Auntie went last year, said it was brilliant. Loads of hiking too, if you fancy that. Ooh, hiking's good. I've been trying to get back into it. Though, ‘hiking’ for me currently involves walking to the shops and back without getting breathless. That’s a start! I’ve been so useless. I keep meaning to join a gym, but then I just… watch another episode of that awful reality TV show. Which one? Don’t tell me you’re hooked on ‘Love Island’ again? It’s… compellingly terrible. I can't look away. It’s like watching a car crash in swimwear. Oh, I tried an episode. I genuinely didn’t understand what was happening. All sculpted abs and manufactured drama. I’d rather watch paint dry, honestly. See, that’s me. I’ve been binge-watching this documentary series about deep-sea creatures. Fascinating stuff. Giant squid, anglerfish… terrifying, amazing. Oh, I love a good documentary! I watched one about sloths the other day. Turns out, they're surprisingly complex creatures. And so slow. It was blissfully calming. Speaking of calming… anyone fancy ordering a takeaway? I can’t be bothered to cook. I’m craving a proper curry. Curry sounds excellent. Though, I had a disastrous attempt at making a vindaloo last week. It was… intensely spicy. I think I lost a layer of tastebuds. You and spicy food! Remember that time in Thailand when you ordered the “mild” curry and nearly cried? Oh god, don’t remind me. My face was on fire. I think I single-handedly kept a local pharmacy in business with the amount of milk I bought. Right, curry it is, then. Indian or Thai? Any preferences? And what about next weekend? Should we try and actually  do  something? Not just sit around and watch TV? Indian sounds good. And yes! We should definitely do something. Maybe go to that new botanical garden? I heard it’s really nice. Botanical garden sounds lovely.

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘im, he’s gone and bought another one. Another motorbike. Oh, not again! He’s a menace on those things, isn't he? Doesn’t he learn? Honestly, I worry sick about him. He does live on the edge, doesn't he? Still, keeps life interesting, I suppose. Better than sitting around doing nothing. Though, buying another one when the last one’s still being paid off... that’s not terribly sensible. Sensible went out the window years ago with that lad. He says this one’s different, a classic. Said it’ll be worth money one day. They all say that, don’t they? "It’s an investment." It’s always an investment until it needs fixing, then it’s a money pit. Remember that old car of his? Oh, don’t even  start  me on that. He promised he’d get it sorted, then left it rusting in your garden for six months, didn’t he? Thought you were running a scrap yard! Aye, well, he’s got a generous aunt, let’s put it that way. Always bailing him out. Speaking of bailing out… have you seen the price of petrol lately? Highway robbery, I tell you. It's dreadful. Makes you think twice about driving anywhere, doesn't it? Especially after that trip to London. The congestion charge… That was a nightmare. Twenty quid just to drive into the city centre! And then trying to find parking… honestly, I’d rather take the train, even if it is slower. I still reckon we got a good deal on the theatre tickets though. Twenty-five pound each for ‘Matilda’. It was lovely. Though I kept thinking about all the money we could have saved if we’d stayed local. We could have gone to that fete in Costessey. True, but you don't get 'Matilda' at the Costessey fete. Plus, it was good to get away. I’m already thinking about our next trip. Remember that youth hostel in Cornwall we were talking about? Cornwall? Oh, I don’t know about that. All those hills. My knees aren’t what they used to be. Plus, you’re crammed in with other folks, all sorts. It's just an idea. We don't  have  to go to a youth hostel. We could look at little cottages. I saw some lovely ones on eBay the other day, actually, near Padstow.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a failure at this breastfeeding thing. She just…won’t latch properly half the time. It's so frustrating. Oh, love, don’t beat yourself up. It took me ages with Leo. Ages. He was practically refusing at first, and I was convinced I couldn’t produce enough. I was in tears, honestly. See, that's what I'm worried about! Is she getting enough? She’s definitely not gaining weight as quickly as they said she should. The health visitor keeps saying 'just keep offering’ but it’s exhausting when she’s screaming and pushing me away. They always say that, don’t they? "Just keep offering." Like it’s that simple! Leo was latching for like, two minutes, then falling asleep, then wanting more five minutes later. It was a nightmare cycle. Did you try different positions? That helped me a bit. I’ve tried everything! Football hold, laid-back breastfeeding, cradle hold... she just prefers a bottle, I swear she does. And then I feel awful for even  thinking  that, like I’m a bad mum. You’re not a bad mum! Honestly. It’s just…some babies are fussier than others. And honestly, a fed baby is a happy baby, right? If she’s happier with a bottle, and she's gaining  some  weight, don’t stress too much. Mum’s mental health is important too. Easier said than done, though, isn’t it? Mum keeps going on about how she breastfed all three of us for a year each, and Dad just nods along like it was the easiest thing in the world. Honestly, they just don’t understand how different things are now. Oh, they never do, do they? They had a different generation of advice, and they think their way is the only way. And Dad…well, Dad just agrees with Mum, doesn’t he? He's a lost cause. Completely. It's just...I wanted to do this. I wanted to  feel  connected to her through breastfeeding. I feel like I'm failing at that, too. You’re not failing anything. You're connected to her in a million other ways. Cuddles, changing her nappy, singing to her… breastfeeding doesn’t define your bond. Honestly, just focus on enjoying her, and try not to listen to anyone else's opinions. How’s Auntie Carol been with all this?

Honestly, did you see that article about the water companies? Absolutely outrageous. Pumping raw sewage into the rivers. It's scandalous, isn't it? And they’re still giving themselves massive bonuses. The sheer audacity. It makes you wonder what else they're getting away with. Everything feels a bit… rotten at the moment, politically and environmentally. It does. Though I’m trying not to dwell on it too much first thing. Need a bit of positivity with my tea. What’s everyone got on today? I’ve got a full ward, predictably. Mrs. Higgins is finally going home, which is good, but we’ve a new admission with suspected pneumonia. It’s going to be busy. I’ve got that meeting with the board this afternoon. The usual performance reviews and budget discussions. Ugh. Wish they’d just let me get on with the job. I’m mostly WFH today, thankfully. Got a deadline looming for that campaign for the new vegan burger. It's surprisingly difficult writing compelling copy about a bean patty. Oh, that sounds… challenging. I'm on shift at the clinic. Hopefully, it won’t be too hectic. Though Old Man Hemmings is due for his weekly check-up and he always has a story to tell. Usually involves pigeons. Honestly, Hemmings and his pigeons! He’s a character. Did anyone remember to put the bins out? It's collection day. I did! Just before I came in. It was raining, naturally. Good work, Dad. Saved someone a trip. Are we still on for a roast at Mum's next Sunday? Yes, absolutely. I spoke to her yesterday, she’s already planning the menu. Apparently, she’s attempting a Yorkshire pudding with a herb crust. Oh, that sounds ambitious. Mum's Yorkshire puddings are legendary, though. A herb crust… that's a bold move. It'll be interesting, that’s for sure. She's always experimenting. Remember that time she tried to make beetroot brownies? How could I forget? They tasted… earthy. And looked terrifying. They were a disaster! The dog wouldn’t even go near them. Speaking of pets, have you seen Winston lately? He’s been hiding under the sofa all morning. He's probably just grumpy. He gets like that when it's cold. I gave him a little cuddle earlier but he just swatted me with his paw. He’s a majestic beast, but he has his moments.

Ugh, I genuinely think Mr. Davies is actively trying to make us fail the Physics test. It was  impossible . Seriously! I spent like, three hours revising, and I still didn’t understand half of it. Did you get the one about the…the resistors? The ones in series and parallel? Don’t even. I just guessed. I think I put like, seven for the total resistance. Which is definitely wrong. Seven?! Oh, God. I think I wrote down a fraction. A very complicated fraction. It's gonna be a disaster. Honestly, I’m more stressed about that than the Maths one next week. Maths is bad, obviously, but at least I understand  some  of it. Physics…it’s like another language. Ooh, speaking of disasters, did you see what Elsie wore today? Elsie? What, her uniform again? She always messes with the skirt length, doesn't she? Worse. She’d safety-pinned a massive Christmas badge onto her blazer. It was covered in glitter and bells. Mrs. Peterson nearly had a heart attack. No way! Elsie is fearless. She’ll push boundaries until the end of time. Christmas is getting a bit much though, isn’t it? Everywhere you look, decorations, songs… I don’t mind it. Mum’s already planning the garden. She's got these…I don't even know what they’re called, but they’re these really vibrant red plants she wants to put in pots by the front door. Poinsettias? Yeah! That's them. She’s obsessed. She’s been collecting stamps for them, apparently. Something to do with a gardening magazine promo. Mum's hobbies are…unique. Haha, yeah. My nan's obsessed with collecting those little ceramic mushrooms. She has like, a hundred. Anyway, are you going to the Ed Sheeran concert with Chloe and Maya? I am! I’m so excited. It’s ages away though, isn’t it? July. I need to start saving. I’m doing extra Art club to earn some money. Oh nice! What are you making? I always feel so uninspired in Art. I can’t even draw a decent stick figure. We’re doing textile art at the moment. I’m making a landscape with different fabrics. It's kinda cool. Mrs. Hayes is really good at explaining things. She says it’s like painting, but with…stuff. Sounds way more interesting than memorising the periodic table.

Honestly, that rat puppet… little Timmy’s got a right obsession with it. Carries it everywhere. Even to his mother’s! Oh, bless him. He does love his little Ratty, doesn’t he? Though it  is  a bit creepy, isn’t it? All grey and staring. Creepy? It’s a puppet, Margaret. Children love puppets. A bit of imagination, that's all. Aye, well, it gives  me  the willies. Reminds me of old man Hemmings’ ferret. Used to sneak into our garden that did. Oh, don’t start on Hemmings and his ferret, Arthur! We’ve heard that story a hundred times. The ferret in the marrows, the ferret in Mrs. Gable’s washing… It’s a true story! And a cautionary one. Keeps the vegetables safe, I always say. Speaking of which, have you two lot been to the optician lately? My eyes are playing up something dreadful. I had mine done last month. All clear. Though the young man said I could do with some tinted lenses. Said I’m squinting too much in bright light. Tinted? Sounds fancy. I just want to be able to read the racing post without holding it a foot away from my face. Honestly, Arthur, you and your racing post. You’d think it was the Bible! I’m due mine next week. Dreadful waiting room, the optician's. Always full of people with ailments. It’s a necessary evil, Margaret. Can’t be bumping into things, can you? Worse than bumping into things is trying to read the bus numbers! They’re so small now. And they change ‘em all the time, don’t they? Always ending up on the wrong bus. They do. And the drivers never wait, do they? Zoom off the second you get anywhere near the stop. You need to travel like I do, live in a village where you can cycle everywhere. No buses needed. Peaceful. Easy for you to say, Cecil, living in Little Puddleton. We’re stuck out here with a bus every hour if we’re lucky. And half the time they're late. Gets right on my nerves, it does. Honestly, you'd think, with all the council tax we pay, they could run a more reliable service. It's not as if we're asking for much. No. Just a bus that arrives when it's supposed to. And maybe a bit less bumpy ride, wouldn’t go amiss.

Right, so after this, wanna actually  do  something with the day, or just head back and I can crack on with this dissertation? It’s looming, honestly. Ooh, definitely do something! We’re in Venice, love. Can’t waste a day cooped up inside. What did you fancy? We could wander over to Rialto, maybe grab some cicchetti… little snacks, you know? Cicchetti? Never even heard of 'em. Sounds fancy. And yeah, Rialto sounds good. I’ve just been reading about it. Apparently, it used to be the beating heart of Venice, like the main trading hub. It was! My nan used to tell me stories about it. She came here in the fifties on her honeymoon. Used to say it was absolutely  bustling . Fruit and veg piled high, fishmongers shouting… all the boats crammed on the Grand Canal. It was a proper market then, not all tourist shops and glass. Wow. It’s hard to imagine now, isn’t it? It’s still busy, but it's…different. Lots of selfie sticks. Aye, too many. Still, the architecture is incredible. And the food! We  have  to try some proper Venetian seafood. I read about this little place near the market, Trattoria Al Gatto Nero… apparently, they do the best ‘spaghetti alle vongole’ you’ll ever taste. Spaghetti alle vongole… clams, right? Sounds amazing. I’m definitely up for that. Though, I’m already regretting having that pastry with my coffee. Gotta leave room for seafood! Oh, don’t worry about it. A little pastry won’t hurt. Besides, we'll walk it off. We can take a vaporetto – water bus - down to Burano afterwards. Have you seen pictures? All the brightly coloured houses? I have! It looks incredible. Like something out of a fairytale. How long does it take to get there? About forty minutes. It's a bit out of the way, but worth it. They used to paint the houses bright colours so the fishermen could see them from out at sea, apparently. Another one of me nan’s stories. She was full of ‘em. That’s a lovely story. It’s good to hear about what Venice  used  to be like, alongside seeing it now. It gives it a bit more depth, you know? It does. This place has so much history. And the coffee’s still pretty good, even if it’s served in tiny little cups!

Honestly, the gym was rammed today. Like, genuinely couldn’t get on a treadmill for a solid ten minutes. Ugh, that’s the  worst . I went yesterday evening and it was surprisingly quiet. Maybe you should switch to evenings? Though, then I’d be hogging everything again, wouldn’t I? Sorry! No, no, it’s fine! I think I’m just doomed to the lunchtime rush. It’s the only time I can realistically fit it in around work. Speaking of work, it’s… a lot. This new project is just endless meetings and spreadsheets. Tell me about it! Bupa is manic at the moment. Everyone’s trying to push all their stuff through before the end of the quarter. I’m drowning in reports. At least we have Nandos to look forward to, right? This peri-peri chicken is a lifesaver. Absolutely. Though, I'm regretting the extra-hot marinade slightly. My mouth is on fire! Oh no! Beginner’s mistake. You know better. So, are you still on for Portugal next month? Have you booked anything yet? Flights are booked! Just need to sort out accommodation. I’m thinking an Airbnb in Lagos. It looks beautiful. You definitely need to come, it would be so much fun. Honestly, I'd love to. I’m just… trying to save a bit of money at the moment, you know? Everything’s so expensive. Plus, Sarah’s having a massive birthday bash the weekend we’re thinking of going. It's a whole themed thing… ‘Hollywood Glamour’ apparently. Oh god, Sarah’s parties are legendary. And a bit terrifying. Hollywood Glamour… seriously? Seriously. She's gone all out. I feel like I need a personal stylist just to  think  about attending. And speaking of terrifying, have you spoken to Ben recently? Oh,  him . No. Thankfully. He messaged me last week, just a random "Hey, how are you?". I replied with a very polite “Good, thanks”. And then ignored everything else. Good for you! He’s still trying, isn’t he? Honestly, I can’t believe you put up with him for so long. I was young and naive! Honestly, looking back, I have no idea what I saw in him. Well, you’re much better off now. So much happier. Right, on a completely different note - are you free next Saturday? There’s a new bar opened up near Mill Road, apparently it does amazing cocktails.

…and honestly, the sheer exhaustion of it all! But worth every single second, of course. Little Elsie arrived perfectly healthy, screaming blue murder, just as she should. Good, good. A healthy scream is always reassuring. Though a quiet one might be nice for a change, eh? Reminds me, you know, of when Penelope was born. Perfectly silent, she was. Scared the living daylights out of the doctor. Thought something was terribly wrong. Oh, heavens! Elsie wasn’t giving anyone that option. My daughter’s utterly besotted, naturally. Though she keeps questioning whether she’s doing everything right. Isn’t that always the way? Always. It’s the eternal burden of motherhood. Though the principles haven’t changed much over the centuries, have they? I’ve been rereading some of my notes on Philip and Mary, you know. Remarkable business, that marriage. The Spanish archives were fascinating. Though the cataloguing,  mon Dieu ! A complete shambles. Nothing like the British Library, I must say. I can imagine. You were saying last time about the property records? Were they as chaotic as you expected? More so! Trying to trace land ownership in sixteenth-century Spain is a nightmare. So much overlapping jurisdiction, so many disputes. It’s a wonder anything ever got built. Which, of course, explains why so much didn't. Reminds me, in a strange way, of the situation with these new landlords down the road. Utterly useless, the lot of them. My neighbour, Mrs. Higgins, having terrible trouble with a leaking roof. Sent three different contractors, each contradicting the last. It's appalling, isn’t it? They promised improvements, but it’s just gone downhill. I heard old Mr. Davies is threatening to chain himself to one of those ridiculous bollards they put up. Ah, the bollards! An absolute debacle. Completely pointless, utterly obstructive. A monument to bureaucratic ineptitude, if you ask me. Though, I suspect, if one were to propose removing them, a whole new layer of red tape would emerge. It’s like France in some ways, you know? Property laws, endless paperwork… it’s a wonder anyone ever starts a business. Speaking of France, how were the visitors from Bordeaux? Did they enjoy London? They enjoyed the museums, predictably. Though they couldn’t quite grasp our obsession with queuing. And they were horrified by the state of some of our pavements. Said they hadn't seen anything so badly maintained since the war.

This sweet and sour sauce is way too sticky, honestly. It’s like glue. Nah, it’s alright. You just gotta get a good chunk of chicken with it, balances it out. Speaking of chicken, did you see old Man Henderson in history today? He was going on  again  about the war. Henderson? Ugh, always. It’s like, sir, we get it, you were there. We’ve heard the story approximately a thousand times. It's just… exhausting. Seriously! I swear he’s got a pre-recorded speech he just plays now. Literally word for word the same every time. It's worse than Mr. Davies droning on about the quadratic equation. And Davies thinks he’s hilarious. Remember when he tried to do a maths pun? Oh god, don't remind me. Something about… ‘roots’ being essential? Everyone just stared at him. It was brutal. It was. But, like, Mrs. Chen actually smiled. She thinks he’s brilliant. It's terrifying. Mrs. Chen thinks everything’s brilliant as long as it involves numbers. Remember when Liam brought in a drawing of a cat and she tried to work out its angles? Oh my god, yes! Poor Liam. He looked so confused. Speaking of confused, have you guys started thinking about applying to uni yet? My mum’s been giving me the Third Degree every night. Ugh, don’t even. My dad’s already got a spreadsheet, listing potential courses, entry requirements, costs… the works. It’s insane. I just want to finish sixth form without having a breakdown. Same. I’m thinking about doing something design-related, maybe graphic design. But I have no idea where to even start looking. I’m leaning towards computer science. My brother’s doing it at Bristol, says it’s good. Although he also spends approximately 20 hours a day staring at a screen, which doesn’t sound ideal. True. You need a life, you know? Anyone read the new  Voidwalker  comic yet? It’s amazing. The art style is… wow. Ooh, I saw it in the shop yesterday. Thinking about getting it. Is it better than the last series? The last one kind of fizzled out. Way better. They've brought in a new writer and it’s seriously dark. And they finally revealed the backstory of Zephyr! Zephyr’s awesome. Although I still think Orion is the coolest. He’s just… misunderstood.

Honestly, this house is brimming. Absolutely brimming. I don’t know how Jonathan copes. It's like a museum, not a home. Well, you know how he is, Elsie. He holds onto  everything . “It might be useful someday!” he always says. It's a bit much, though, even for a collector. Yeah, I found a box of old Beanie Babies yesterday. Beanie Babies! Who even remembers those? Oh, the nineties. A dark time for collectible plushies. Though, honestly, I’m more concerned about the three different bread makers. What does one man  need  with three bread makers? He always did like a good loaf. Your Grandad used to make the best sourdough, you know. Used to bring a whole basketful down every Sunday. Never measured a thing, just… felt it. Those were the days, weren't they, Margaret? Simple pleasures. Now it’s all gadgets and gizmos and things that need charging. Speaking of which, I can’t get the smart speaker to connect to the WiFi. It just keeps saying “Error 404.” Whatever  that  means. Oh, leave that to me, Elsie. I’m practically a tech wizard these days, thanks to having to troubleshoot everything for my students. Though, honestly, half the time I just tell them to turn it off and on again. Works wonders. It always does. My computer did that last night, and Dad just turned it off and on and it worked. Right, so birthday plans. I was thinking we could try that new Italian place in town? ‘Bella Vita,’ I think it’s called. I heard good things about their tiramisu. Ooh, tiramisu sounds lovely. But is it easy to get to? My knees aren’t what they used to be, you know. And parking in town is a nightmare. I could pick you up, Margaret? No problem at all. And Bella Vita does have some disabled parking spaces, I believe. I’ll check. That would be wonderful, dear. Thank you. Perhaps we could have a little buffet at home afterwards? I’ve been experimenting with some new canapé recipes. Little smoked salmon things, and some mini quiches... Can I help make the canapés? I’m pretty good at spreading things. Excellent! A culinary team in the making. Maybe we should theme it? A “Jonathan Through the Decades” party? We could all dress up as his favourite era. Oh, that's a brilliant idea! Although, knowing Jonathan, we might end up with sixteen different versions of him from the 1970s.

Ugh, I’m so stressed about options. Like, seriously. I have  no  idea what to pick. Tell me about it! I’m kinda leaning towards Art, but then I worry it won’t be… useful? Like, what job do you even  get  with an Art GCSE? Exactly! My mum keeps going on about how I need something “solid.” She's all about the Sciences, but honestly, the thought of more chemistry makes me want to scream. My dad's the same. He's always like “Engineering is the future!” But I’m not exactly building robots in my spare time, am I? Have you seen what some people are doing on YouTube now though? Like, full-time bloggers and stuff? Yeah! It's insane. There's that girl, Cleo, who just reviews stationery.  Stationery , Liv! And she makes, like, a fortune. Right? And she’s got, like, a million followers. It’s just… weird. Still, kinda tempting. Imagine getting paid to talk about pens. I know, right? Better than dissecting a frog, anyway. Speaking of weird jobs, did you see that article about the professional cuddler?  No way!  Seriously? People get paid to cuddle? Apparently! It’s a thing. A very strange thing. Although, honestly, sometimes I just want someone to give me a hug and tell me everything’s going to be okay, especially with these options looming. Me too. Okay, okay, new strategy. What are you absolutely, definitely  not  picking? Geography. One hundred percent no. I hate maps. And Mr. Harris is the most boring teacher  ever . He just drones on and on. Ha! True. He does have a seriously monotone voice. I'm pretty sure I zoned out for the entire lesson on plate tectonics. I’m thinking maybe… History? I like learning about famous people and stuff. Oh, good shout! I’m alright at History. Though, I’m terrible at remembering dates. I always get Henry VIII and Elizabeth I mixed up. Same! They both had complicated love lives, that's all I remember. What about Music? You play the clarinet, don’t you? Yeah, but I’m not amazing. And Mrs. Davies is super strict. She's all about perfect duty. It's so stressful trying to get everything  exactly  right. Ugh, I get that. It kind of sucks the fun out of it, doesn't it? We  have  to do PE, though, right? I am seriously dreading that.

Honestly, the state of that roundabout on the A47… you’d think they’d have sorted it by now. Been months, hasn’t it? Months, Reginald, months. Could’ve built a Roman fort in the time it’s taken ‘em. And the traffic… used to be able to get to Yarmouth for a proper kipper breakfast, now it’s a military operation. Speaking of Romans, did you two see that documentary about the Boudiccan revolt? Fascinating. Apparently, they found evidence of a really significant battle site just outside Colchester. All those poor souls… Gran, you and history. Always knew you had a secret life as an archaeologist. Oh, don’t be silly, dear. Just a keen interest. It’s good to remember where we come from, isn't it? Unlike some people glued to their… what is it you lecturers call it? Digital spaces? Digital spaces, yes. It’s a way of life now, I’m afraid. Though I agree, a bit of real-world history is good for the soul. I was actually trying to get this new software to work this morning – a program for analysing historical data. Utter nightmare. Keeps crashing. Software. Bah. Give me a slide rule any day. Reliable. No updates. No ‘compatibility issues’. Though, I suppose even slide rules don’t last forever. Everything falls apart eventually. Like old cars. You and your cars, Reginald. Always going on about your old Austin. You know, young Thomas down the road, he's restoring a Morris Minor. Bright blue. Lovely thing. Said he needed advice on the carburetors. Carburetors! The bane of my existence. Should’ve stuck to simpler engines. Triumph Spitfire, now  that  was a car. Though even those had their quirks. Remember that time I got stranded in Suffolk with a broken distributor cap? Oh, don’t remind me! I had to drive out and rescue you with a thermos of tea and a biscuit. You were muttering about Lucas electrics for weeks. Sounds like a classic Reginald adventure. It's no wonder you became an engineer, always tinkering. Well, someone had to keep things running. Speaking of running, saw a deer this morning, just by the river. Magnificent beast. Stood there for a good five minutes, just watching me. Lovely. We had a fox in the garden last week, bold as brass. Scared the life out of Mrs. Higgins' cat. Nearly had a heart attack, she did.

…and young Timmy, bless ‘im, he comes up to me, all serious, and says, “Mr. Peterson, is it true what they say about dinosaurs?” I said, “What’s that, Timmy?” He says, “That they all got poorly and died?” I nearly choked on me tea, I did! Poorly, he said! Oh, that’s lovely! Children are wonderful, aren't they? Though, honestly, the things they tell you… I had little Maisie ask me once if fairies were real and if they paid taxes. Taxes! Where do they get these ideas? They absorb everything, don’t they? My lot are all talking about TikTok now. It’s terrifying. I don’t understand half of it. It’s just… people dancing and making faces. TikTok? Sounds right daft. Give me ‘Coronation Street’ any day. Though even that’s gone downhill. They’ve got that new character, the one with the dodgy hair, and she’s just… dreary. Oh, don't get me started on television! It’s all repeats and reality shows. Used to be you could rely on a good detective drama. Now it’s all ‘Love Island’ and shouting. Though, I did get sucked into that baking show last week. The Great British Bake Off? It’s alright. Harmless. Though, I confess, I’m more of a ‘Line of Duty’ man myself. Gripping stuff. Speaking of gripping, did you see the state of my wardrobe the other day? It was a disaster zone! Apparently, the delivery fella just dumped the parcel  on  it. Didn’t even knock! Honestly, these delivery men… no respect. They’re always in a rush, aren't they? I had one try to deliver a package through the letterbox – for something the size of a washing machine! You’re joking! I wish I were! I had to practically wrestle it off him. Said he was “on a tight schedule”. A tight schedule for what? Crushing pensioners’ furniture? You tell 'em! Remember old Arthur next door? He once chased a delivery man down the street with his walking stick because he parked on his rose bed. Now  that’s  a story! Honestly, it's a good job I’m a teacher, I need all the anecdotes I can get. Keeps the kids entertained. Though they're less impressed with stories about delivery men and more interested in… well, I won't repeat what they said about the headmaster.

Right, honestly, this snow is mental. I was proper bracing myself walking back from the lab. It's like a blizzard out there! Tell me about it! I nearly went flying on Blackett Avenue. Saw old Mrs. Higgins doing a proper wobble, bless her. Makes you glad we’ve got the fire on, eh? Definitely. Though, it’s massively putting the brakes on my gardening plans. I was hoping to get the tulip bulbs in this weekend. They can wait a bit, can't they? Unless you fancy a trip to B&Q in the snow? I’m not volunteering. Absolutely not! No amount of spring flowers is worth that. Speaking of plans…did you manage to book that table at The Eagle for Sarah’s hen do pre-drinks? Yeah, got us in for 7pm next Friday. I figured we could have a quick one there, then head to that cocktail bar she picked. Although, knowing everyone, ‘quick’ is a relative term. Oh, it  always  is. And have you spoken to Mark about his stag? He was being very vague last time. Just kept saying ‘something involving paintball and potentially a questionable hat’. Mark. Honestly. I think Ben’s organising it, so I’m steering clear. They’ll probably end up in Prague dressed as pirates or something. Sounds about right. It's terrifying to think of the budget for that. Anyway, we need to actually  make  some holiday plans. Remember we said we wanted to go somewhere in February? I do. I was looking at that little cottage in the Cotswolds, with the log burner. It looked really cosy. Oh, that sounds lovely! We could walk, pubs, generally just chill. Anything’s better than being stuck inside with the snow, honestly. It reminds me of that disastrous ‘Come Dine With Me’ episode we watched last week. Oh god, the one where the guy tried to make a soufflé? Pure chaos. I still can’t believe he served raw chicken. And then blamed the oven! Honestly, the audacity. It was brilliant telly, though. It really was. Right, Cotswolds cottage. I'll have a proper look tonight and send you some links. We should probably book soon, before everything gets snapped up. Perfect. And maybe we can sneak in a trip to a garden centre while we're there. Just… not for tulips. Definitely not tulips yet. Deal. So, snowed in, hen and stag dos looming, a potentially disastrous soufflé replaying in our minds… sounds like a typical week, aye?

This is a lovely bit of pork, this is. Really tender. Your mother always did know her way around a joint. She did, didn’t she? Used to spend hours in the butcher’s, picking out just the right cut. None of this pre-packaged stuff for Elsie. She’d quiz them, ask where it came from, how it was raised… It  is  good. Mum’s really outdone herself. And the roast potatoes are perfect – crispy on the outside, fluffy inside. Absolutely. Best roast potatoes I’ve had in ages. Honestly, I’ve been trying to get mine to turn out like this for months. Just can’t seem to crack the secret. Secret’s goose fat, lad. Always goose fat. Don't you be using vegetable oil, that's for the birds. Proper goose fat, gives ‘em that golden colour and a real flavour. He’s right, you know. Elsie swore by goose fat. Said it was what her mother always used, and her mother before her. Generations of perfect roast potatoes. I'll have to try that. I've been using olive oil, trying to be a bit healthier… maybe that’s where I’m going wrong. Probably. Healthy can wait. Tonight is for roast potatoes and gravy. Speaking of which… is there any more gravy, Elsie? Coming right up, dear. Help yourself to the Yorkshire puddings, they're still warm. Good Yorkshire puddings, those. Not like the flat ones you get in some pubs these days. Proper risen, they are. They’re fantastic. Mum, you should open a bed and breakfast or something. Seriously, people would travel miles for a roast dinner like this. Don’t be silly, love. I’m far too old to start a new career now. Besides, I enjoy having you all here. That’s what matters. It really does. It’s so nice to just come here and… relax. Not have to think about marking or meetings or… students. Students, eh? Still got a handful of rascals in your class, I wager. A few. It’s that time of term, everyone’s getting distracted. Thinking about holidays, exams looming… the usual. The essays are getting… interesting. One student argued that Shakespeare invented the internet. Shakespeare invented the internet? Well, I’ll be… Oh, don’t get me started on the youngsters today. No respect, no manners… always glued to those blinking phones. Mum!

Honestly, Mum, this roast is incredible. You’ve really outdone yourself. Aye, well, years of practice, lass. It helps when you’ve got a captive audience like this lot. Though your Dad nearly set the kitchen on fire trying to help with the potatoes. Now, now, that's a slight exaggeration, love. I merely had a  small  oil-related incident. The smoke alarm’s still recovering. Small? The entire house smelled like a chip shop for an hour! I thought you’d decided to deep-fry the kitchen. Deep-fry the kitchen, eh? Sounds a bit modern for me. Back in my day, we stuck to a good old-fashioned boil. Everything tasted the same, mind, but it was simple. It sounds…efficient, Grandad. Though, I’m very grateful for Mum’s slightly more ambitious approach to cooking. Speaking of ambitious, I was talking to Brenda from work today, and she’s decided to renovate her kitchen. Gut the whole thing. Said she’s going for one of those walk-in pantries. Fancy, eh? Walk-in pantry? That’s a bit excessive, isn’t it? We barely have room for a walk-in  closet  in our flat. Tell me about it. Honestly, finding somewhere with even a small garden in this market is proving impossible. Everything's either tiny flats or massive, unaffordable houses. You young ‘uns and your housing woes. Back when I retired, you could buy a perfectly decent semi for a song. It’s a different world now, that’s for sure. A song? More like a penny whistle! I remember when houses cost less than a good suit. Now they're bigger than whole villages. Anyway, Brenda was going on about granite worktops and induction hobs and all sorts. I just told her she was mad. Give me a good Formica countertop any day. Reliable and easy to clean. Though, I’ll admit, an induction hob  is  tempting. No more burnt fingers trying to adjust the gas. You’re getting fancy on me, aren’t you? Next, you’ll be wanting a robot chef. Don't give me ideas! Actually, Mum, do you remember that story about Auntie Maureen and her disastrous attempt at making a soufflé? Oh, don't even get me started on Maureen! That soufflé was a tragedy. Collapsed before it even made it to the table. She blamed the altitude. Altitude in Middlesbrough?

Right, so I was reading this article about a guy who started a coding bootcamp… but not just  any  coding bootcamp. He guarantees a job at the end, or he refunds the entire fee. Bold, right? Very. And terrifyingly risky. What if half the cohort are completely hopeless? He’d be bankrupt in a month. Is it a reputable program, though? Or is it massively selective upfront? That’s the clever bit. He says the selection process is brutal. He basically weeds out anyone who isn’t genuinely motivated  and  capable. He compares it to Special Forces selection – really high attrition rate at the beginning. But the ones who make it through… they're landing six-figure salaries. Hmm. So a really high barrier to entry, then. It’s not necessarily innovative teaching, it's just incredibly rigorous selection. I wonder if that model could work with teacher training. Exactly! We were talking about that problem with attrition rates on PGCE courses, weren’t we? Loads of bright people start, then buckle under the pressure of placement. What if you redesigned the application process to be more… predictive? Not just interviews and academic results, but simulated classroom scenarios, problem-solving challenges… really push them. I love that. Create a mini-teaching gauntlet. But it would be a logistical nightmare. And you’d have to be incredibly careful about bias. You don't want to exclude people who just learn differently. Remember that training we did on unconscious bias? True. It's a balancing act. But imagine the outcome! Fewer burnt-out teachers, higher quality provision… It feels like a better approach than just throwing money at retention schemes after they’ve already qualified. Absolutely. It’s preventative, not reactive. It’s a complete shift in mindset. You’re almost treating it like a start-up – identifying a problem, iterating on a solution, high risk, high reward. Speaking of start-ups, did you see that video going viral of the kid who built a whole vending machine dispensing… miniature succulents? No! Seriously? That’s amazing. Kids these days… they're entrepreneurial little monsters. He probably made a fortune. I bet he started with a YouTube tutorial and a pile of recycled materials. That’s what I heard. It's those practical, hands-on things. Thinking about this teaching thing, maybe a pre-course ‘maker’ challenge – build a resource, design a lesson, troubleshoot a classroom management issue… something tangible to assess their problem-solving skills.

Right, I’m officially declaring dinner a disaster. This butternut squash risotto is… an experience. It tastes vaguely of sadness. Oh no! That’s ambitious, risotto is fiddly. What went wrong? Too much stock? Not enough stirring? The culinary mysteries are endless. Everything, probably. I think I underestimated the amount of stirring required. It’s just… gluey. And it doesn’t really  taste  of butternut squash, more like slightly orange rice. Don’t beat yourself up about it. It’s Friday night, we can order a takeaway. What are you fancying? Indian? Pizza? Ooh, Indian sounds amazing. I've been craving a proper Madras all week. Work’s been… intense. Had a meeting today that could have been an email. Seriously. Three hours of people talking in circles. Tell me about it. I had a particularly tricky patient today. Really agitated, convinced everyone was trying to poison him. It takes a lot of patience, and a lot of explaining that the tea  doesn't  contain secret ingredients. Oh, bless. That sounds exhausting. You’re a saint, you are. Seriously. All that emotional labour. It’s rewarding, mostly. Just… draining. Anyway, enough shop talk. What are your weekend plans then? Anything fun lined up? Not much, actually. Sarah and Ben are having a Halloween party next Saturday, which should be good. They’re going all out – apparently Ben's building a haunted garden. Oh, clever! They always do a good party. Are you dressing up? I’ve got that witch costume I wore a few years ago. It’s a bit… dramatic, but fun. I haven’t decided yet. I was thinking maybe something easy, like a cat. Or a rogue pumpkin. I’m notoriously lazy when it comes to costumes. A rogue pumpkin is brilliant. You could just… wander around menacingly. Exactly! Passive-aggressive autumnal vibes. Speaking of the future, I was thinking… five-year plan time. Terrifying, isn’t it? Oh god, don’t even. It's always terrifying. Where do you see yourself in five years? Still coordinating projects, but hopefully, maybe a bit higher up the ladder? That’s the dream, yeah. Maybe managing a whole team. Or even… … living somewhere different. I've been scrolling through Rightmove looking at cottages in the Cotswolds. Ridiculous, I know. The Cotswolds! That’s lovely. Very picturesque. I always thought I’d end up somewhere near the coast, maybe Cornwall. But realistically, I’ll probably still be in London, battling the commute.

Honestly, the price of everything these days… absolutely scandalous. I went to get a loaf of bread yesterday, and nearly fainted when I saw the cost! Tell me about it, Nan. Rent is just… ridiculous. I'm saving as much as I can, but it feels like I'm running on the spot. You young people have it tough, I’ll say that. When your Grandad and I first moved into a flat, it was a fraction of what you pay now. Of course, he was earning good money then, being a builder. Not like nowadays with all the…well, everything. Yeah, it’s different. It’s not just the money either. Everyone's so stressed, trying to balance work and life and…everything else. Speaking of stressed, your Auntie Maureen is driving me up the wall. She rang again this morning, going on about her new garden gnome. A  garden gnome , darling! As if I have time to listen to tales of porcelain figures. Oh, Maureen. She’s… consistent. Has she named it yet? Oh, naturally. It's called Bartholomew. Bartholomew! Honestly. She’s been showing pictures to everyone at the bingo, apparently. Said Mrs. Higgins was most impressed. Mrs. Higgins always is. Remember when Maureen claimed Mrs. Higgins was a secret spy? Oh, don’t remind me! That was a whole saga. She was convinced Mrs. Higgins was sending coded messages through her knitting patterns. Honestly, the things she comes up with. Well, it keeps things interesting, doesn’t it? So, have you managed to get hold of Uncle George? I was trying to ring him yesterday about the weekend, but it went straight to voicemail. I spoke to him briefly on Tuesday. He’s down at the allotment, as usual. Says the tomatoes are doing well this year. But he’s been complaining about the slugs. Apparently, they’re having a field day. He's tried everything – beer traps, copper tape, even sprinkling coffee grounds around. Nothing seems to work! Poor George. Slug wars. Sounds exhausting. Are you still going to his allotment for tea on Saturday? Yes, dear. Unless the slugs finally win and he refuses to leave the house. He’s promised to make his famous Victoria sponge. You know how much you love that. Oh, I  do  love George's Victoria sponge. It's the best. I'm bringing the jam, then. Homemade, of course.

Right, so I genuinely think I’m failing organic chemistry. Like, properly failing. It's just… abstract. Oh no! Seriously? I thought you were, like, naturally good at science stuff? You always aced biology in sixth form. Biology was remembering things. This is… thinking about things that don’t  exist  in a visible way. It’s maddening. Like, electrons and orbitals? What even  are  those? I get it. My physics lecturer is the same. Explains everything in terms of wave-particle duality and then looks really offended when you ask him to explain wave-particle duality. Exactly! It's like they enjoy making it complicated.
