Have you started thinking about dissertation topics yet? The deadline's looming, isn't it? It is. I'm leaning towards something about the societal impact of AI-generated art. It's a bit broad, I know, but it feels… relevant. Plus, I can use all the cool images I've been making with Midjourney as examples. What about you? I was thinking about the correlation between football fandom and regional identity in Yorkshire. Pretty niche, I know. But I’ve been doing a bit of reading, and it’s surprisingly complex. It’s not just about supporting a team; it’s practically woven into people’s sense of self. That sounds fascinating, actually. Proper fieldwork potential, right? Getting out to pubs during matches, observing the atmosphere… Yeah, that's the plan. Although my supervisor thinks it's "too qualitative" and wants me to find some quantifiable data. Like, how do you quantify the feeling of being a Doncaster Rovers supporter? Ugh, academics. Always needing numbers. Speaking of football, did you see the Champions League last night? Arsenal got absolutely rinsed. I did! Honestly, embarrassing. I don’t even  support  Arsenal, but it was painful to watch. Bayern Munich were just… on another level. Completely. They just dismantled them. It makes you wonder if the Premier League is actually  that  good, you know? We always bang on about it being the best league in the world, but… It’s hype, mostly. Plus, loads of the best players are going to Saudi now, aren't they? Really diluting the talent pool. Exactly. It’s a bit sad, actually. All that money just… vanishing into a country with questionable human rights records. Tell me about it. It feels ethically murky, to say the least. Oh, and speaking of murky - I tried translating a bit of a French newspaper article for my translation class today, and I swear, half the sentences lost all meaning.

Honestly, I nearly jumped out of my skin this morning. Oh, what happened? Did one of the kids do something? Worse. A spider. A huge one. Right in the doorway of the bathroom. I hate spiders, you know I do. Oh, ugh, yeah, they're not my favourite, either. Though, I’ve been more worried about mice lately, to be honest. Had a little nibble on a packet of biscuits in the kitchen last week. Had to chuck the lot. Oh, no! That's awful. I can’t stand mice. Spiders, I can usually just… deal with. But mice are just…dirty. Have you set any traps? Yeah, got a couple down. Haven’t caught anything yet, thankfully. Keeps me on edge though, always listening for scratching in the walls. Reminds me of my nan’s house, always had mice. Oh, that’s grim. We haven’t had any issues with mice, thankfully. Just the occasional spider. This one was a monster though, seriously. Like a huntsman. Oh,  those  are scary! Big and hairy. You didn't… you didn’t try to catch it, did you? Absolutely not! My husband, Dave, dealt with it. He’s the brave one. Honestly, I just shrieked and ran. He said it was a ‘harmless house spider’ but I don’t believe him. It had legs the length of my fingers! Men are all the same, aren't they? Downplaying everything to make you feel silly. I had a robin build a nest in my guttering last spring. Honestly, it was lovely at first, all the little chirps. Oh, how lovely! But then the mess! Everywhere. And the fledglings, constantly falling out, me having to rescue them. Nearly had a heart attack a couple of times. Lovely birds, but a lot of responsibility. That sounds… stressful. I prefer to admire them from a distance. We get a few blue tits in the garden, it’s nice. Dave puts out birdseed in the winter. Oh, that’s kind. Though, that probably attracts the mice, doesn’t it? Everything’s connected, isn't it? Spiders eat flies, birds eat worms, mice eat biscuits… and I'm stuck cleaning up after them all! It certainly seems that way! Well, at least you’ve got a good story to tell. And hopefully, you’ll catch that mouse soon. I hope so. It’s just… unsettling, knowing it’s there.

…and then, of course, Great-Grandad Silas was a bit of a rogue, apparently. A travelling salesman, always on the road. My grandmother used to tell stories about him turning up with exotic gifts – silk scarves, little carved animals – but never actually  being  around. Oh, that’s interesting. My side seems to be filled with farmers, mostly. Stolid, reliable types. Not much excitement. Though, my grandfather, Old Man Davies, he was a miner. Very different life. Hard as nails, he was. Lungs full of coal dust, poor man. Miners had it rough, didn’t they? It's amazing how much we don’t know about our ancestors. I’ve been trying to trace back the women in my family – it’s so much harder, isn’t it? Names change with marriage, records are patchy… It is a proper puzzle. I did a little bit myself after I retired. Used those online family tree websites. Found a distant cousin in Canada, as it happens. Never met him, of course. Just exchanged a few emails. Turns out we both have the same penchant for baking, can you believe it? That's lovely! Such a small connection, but it feels…significant. It’s funny, isn’t it? Speaking of baking, I’ve been meaning to ask, how  are  you coping? It’s only been a few months since… well, since your Mum passed. It's… it's quiet. Very quiet. We were so close, my Mum and I. She was the linchpin, you know? Everything revolved around her. And the dementia… it was awful watching her slip away, piece by piece. It wasn’t a quick decline, it went on for years. I’m so dreadfully sorry. My own mother – she went relatively quickly, thankfully. But it was still… traumatic. She had heart trouble, and it just… gave out. No warning. It feels selfish to say ‘thankfully’ when she’s gone, of course, but the prolonged suffering… that would have been so much harder. You're right. It’s the  seeing  them disappear before they actually go that's the cruelest part. Mum didn't even recognise me towards the end. Would just look through me, like I wasn't there. That was… heartbreaking. It must have been. It’s good you had all those years with her beforehand though, to make memories. Were you a teacher as well, like me? I gathered from Margaret on the phone you’d been in education.

Oh look, a hot air balloon! Isn’t that incredible? It’s so…peaceful just watching it drift. It is, isn’t it? Though I always wonder about the landing. Seems a bit precarious, doesn't it? Especially around here with all the fields and… well, everything. Everything being… power lines, mostly? Yes, you’re right. It's a bit of a gamble. Still, it looks wonderful. Did you see that hare run across the field just now? I did! Blasted off like a rocket. Honestly, the wildlife here is amazing. We don’t get that in London. It’s all pigeons and the occasional fox trying to steal a bin bag. Exactly! It's the reason I love it here so much. Remember that time Barnaby nearly chased a deer in Richmond Park? Absolute chaos. Oh, don’t remind me. He was convinced he was a hunting dog. He’s a miniature dachshund, for goodness sake! Deer are far too big for him. He has no sense of self-preservation, that dog. Speaking of which, are you sure we packed enough dog biscuits for him? He’s been giving me  the look  all morning. I think so. I practically filled a whole bag. Although, knowing Barnaby, he'll pretend he hasn't had any and then try to steal your sandwich. It's a talent. He's a master manipulator. It’s amazing how much money we spend on that little creature. He lives a better life than most people, honestly. It’s true. Designer dog beds, organic food… he’s spoiled rotten. But then, what’s life without a bit of spoiling, eh? Especially when you've worked hard for it? You're right. Though I’m starting to think a weekend camping might be a cheaper alternative to hotels. We could bring Barnaby, and it would be lovely and quiet. Camping? You know I’m not a huge fan of bugs and sleeping on the ground. And Barnaby sheds everywhere. It’ll be a hairy tent. Okay, okay, point taken. Maybe not camping. But a little mini-break somewhere would be nice. We haven't had one in ages. We could look at that little cottage near the coast? The one with the fireplace? Oh, yes! That sounds perfect. We deserve a bit of peace and quiet. Away from marking essays and… hot air balloons that might crash into power lines.

Honestly, this weather is just… relentless, isn’t it? Still grey, still drizzly. Feels like autumn’s just decided to stay put. Aye, you’re right about that. Proper Yorkshire weather down ‘ere, it is. Usually you get a bit of frost this time o’ year, but nothing. Just damp. Makes going to work a bit grim, even. Tell me about it! Though, at least being indoors most of the day shields me from the worst of it. How are things at the gyms? Still busy with the January rush dying down? It was a madhouse for a few weeks, everyone suddenly deciding they needed a ‘new year, new me’ transformation. Now it's settled back down thankfully. Still steady though, gotta keep pushing those memberships, y’know? It’s all targets, targets, targets. Sometimes I feel like a car salesman, not an area manager. Oh, I can imagine. It must be exhausting constantly having to motivate people. I try to do that with my students, but languages are… a different beast. You can’t  make  someone speak French, can you? No, you can’t. Different skillset altogether. I’ve always admired language teachers, though. It’s a proper skill. My daughter tried to learn Spanish at school, didn’t get very far. Said it was too much grammar. Oh, the grammar. It’s the bane of everyone’s existence! I’m trying to get them to focus on communication first, the grammar can come later. I’ve been reading this book, actually, about communicative language teaching… it’s fascinating. Oh yeah? What’s it called? I'm always up for something to read on the train. Keeps me from stewing about membership targets. It's called ‘The Lexical Approach’ by Dave Willis. He argues you should focus on chunks of language, phrases, rather than individual words and grammar rules. It’s made me rethink a lot of my methods. Sounds… clever. I'm more of a ‘get stuck in’ kind of guy, if I'm honest. In coaching, I find the best way to motivate people is to just push them a little bit outside their comfort zone. Not too much, mind, or they’ll give up. Small steps. That’s interesting. It’s similar, I suppose, to scaffolding in language learning. Giving them just enough support to attempt something challenging. Actually, I was thinking about taking a coaching qualification.

Right, now then, has anyone seen my glasses? Honestly, I swear they sprout legs and wander off. Not me, Gran. Did you leave them in the kitchen with your cuppa? No, I definitely had them on when I was marking those dreadful GCSE papers. Honestly, the things these kids write… it's like another language sometimes. Oh, don't I know it. Back in my day, sums were sums. No fancy algorithms or… what do you call ‘em? Logarithms? Algorithms, love. And logarithms were around in our day too, mind. Just not in such a complicated form. Well, whatever they are, they’re giving me a headache. I need my glasses to even  look  at them. Right, I'm retracing my steps. Kitchen, living room… bedroom maybe? I'll help you look, Gran. Maybe they're under a cushion? You were having a nap earlier. Speaking of naps, I could murder a biscuit. Are there any of those nice ginger snaps left? Aye, I think there are a few in the tin. I’ll get ‘em. Though they’re not quite as good as the ones your mother used to make, are they? Nobody makes biscuits like my mother. She had a secret ingredient, she did. Always refused to tell me what it was. Said it was a family secret. No luck. Absolutely nowhere. Honestly, it's infuriating. I'm convinced the cat's stolen them as a toy. Though she usually prefers the curtain cords. Maybe she’s upgraded to glasses, Gran! Very funny. Right, well, never mind the glasses for a minute. Have you two settled in alright? Is the room warm enough? I put the electric blanket on your bed last night. Aye, it's lovely and warm, thank you. You're always looking after us, aren’t you? We appreciate it, love. It’s nice to get out of the house, even if it’s just to Malton. Hull's getting a bit much these days, too many new builds popping up. Changes everything, y’know? They’re building loads of new houses near our school too. It’s a bit annoying because all the traffic gets worse. Well, they have to put houses somewhere, don't they? Though I agree, it can be a nuisance. Right, I'm just going to check the windowsill, sometimes I leave them there when I’m deadheading the geraniums. Geraniums? You’ve got geraniums blooming in November?

Honestly, this satnav is driving me round the bend. It keeps wanting to take us down lanes barely wider than the car! Aye, well, you know what they’re like. They think they know best. I still reckon a proper map is the way to go, though. You can  see  the landscape, understand where you are in relation to things. Easier said than done in the dark, love! And I’m trying to get us to this gig in vaguely on time, remember? Though, judging by how long we’ve been going, ‘vaguely’ is the operative word. Did you see that forecast? More rain. Oh, fantastic. Just what we needed. Though it might be good for the sheep. Old Man Hemmings was complaining his fields were getting a bit dry. Said the wool wasn't coming through as nicely. You and your sheep! Honestly, you spend more time talking about wool than you do about your writing these days. Are you at least making progress on the new novel? Slowly, slowly. It’s a bit…stuck at the moment. Trying to get the dialogue right for this character, a retired pilot, and it just sounds daft. I was reading this biography of Amy Johnson the other day, and she made flying sound so effortless. I need to capture that, you know? That almost…poetic quality. Amy Johnson, now there was a woman. Remember that story about her flying solo to Australia? Incredible. And completely mad, if you ask me. Mad and brilliant. Speaking of mad, did you hear about Brenda and Derek? They're planning a ceilidh as part of their wedding reception. Oh, dear. Derek dancing? That’ll be a sight! Brenda has always been keen, though. Should be fun. Though I’m dreading being dragged onto the floor by Uncle Arthur. He’s convinced he’s a professional. Aye, he’s a menace. Remember when he sprained his ankle trying the Gay Gordons at the last wedding? Oh, I’ll never forget it. The dramatics! He nearly called an ambulance. Honestly, the man’s a walking injury. Oh, and look at this satnav now… "Recalculating…" It's trying to send us through a farmyard! Right. I’m taking control. Pull over, let me have a look at a map. I think I know a shortcut. It'll involve going back a couple of miles, but it'll save us the trauma of a muddy track.

Honestly, that site visit was…an experience. Did you  see  the state of the foundations? It’s a miracle the whole thing hasn’t sunk. Tell me about it. I’m pretty sure I spotted damp rising in the Victorian bit. Damp! In 2024. The client wants ‘exposed brickwork’, though. The irony is painful. Did you manage to grab a coffee on the way over, or are you operating purely on spite and adrenaline like me? Spite and adrenaline, definitely. I figured we needed serious caffeine intervention before tackling this brief. I’m going for the full works - bacon roll, flat white, the whole shebang. You? Just a sausage bap and a black coffee. Trying to be…responsible. Although, frankly, after that site, responsibility feels like a distant memory. Speaking of distant memories, have you spoken to Liam recently? Oh, no. Not since Friday, I think. Is he still having a rough time with that City office refurbishment? He sounded completely frazzled. Frazzled doesn’t even  begin  to cover it. Apparently, the client keeps changing their mind about the layout, and he’s having to redo the 3D renders every other day. He’s practically living on energy drinks and self-loathing. Oh, blimey. That sounds awful. Tell him to just say no, honestly. It's a nightmare client, he needs to push back. He’s too nice, that’s his problem. Remember that presentation he did back at uni? About communal living? Oh god, yes. The one where he tried to convince everyone that micro-apartments were the future of urban housing? Complete chaos. Everyone was asking about storage space and he just kept saying, “Minimalism promotes happiness!” Exactly! He genuinely believed it. Though, actually, I’m starting to see his point about communal spaces. I was reading an article about co-living developments… they're springing up everywhere. Are they? I'm not entirely sure about the whole shared-kitchen thing. The potential for passive-aggressive notes about whose turn it is to wash up fills me with dread. Plus, imagine the noise. True, true. Though, they do seem to be catering to a lot of young professionals who just want a convenient, affordable base in London. It’s clever, architecturally speaking, designing spaces that encourage interaction. Have you started sketching ideas for the university project yet? The brief is incredibly vague. ‘Reimagine the library as a community hub’… what even  is  that?

So, how was Chloe's birthday night? Did you all have a good time? You were a bit quiet on the phone yesterday, sounded like you were still recovering! It was…good. A bit chaotic, honestly. Chloe went  all out . Like, a whole themed outfit for everyone, a DJ, the works. It was fun, but my feet are still killing me. I think I danced for about four solid hours. Oh, Chloe. She does love a theme. Remember that pirate one? The amount of eye patches… Still finding glitter in the garden from that one, I swear. Oh god, the pirate one! That was a mess. Although, I think Dad enjoyed dressing up as a pirate a little  too  much. Anyway, getting back to last night, the traffic getting into town was horrendous. Honestly, people need to learn how to use a roundabout properly. Tell me about it! I was trying to get to the shops yesterday afternoon and it was nose-to-tail. It’s always bad on a Friday, but it's gotten worse recently. Some people just completely ignore the give-way lines. Do they even  look ? Exactly! And then you get the ones who speed up as you’re trying to merge. It’s terrifying. One woman nearly took my door off. I may have given her a little…honk. A little honk? You’re a saint. I probably would have wound the window down and had a word! Honestly, the roads are getting more stressful. Are you still meeting up with Liam and Sophie next week? Yeah, we’re going for pizza on Wednesday. Liam's been going on about this new place near the train station. Apparently, they do these massive sharing pizzas. Sounds good. You two are always finding new places to eat. You should bring him round for dinner sometime, it feels like ages since I’ve met him properly. Oh, that's a good idea! He's really nice, you'd like him. We could maybe do next Sunday? Although, I'm not sure what I’m doing after work on Monday…there’s a team meeting that’s been sprung on us. Sunday works for me. We can do a roast. It's been ages since I've made a proper one. What time would you guys be free? And don’t worry about Monday, you can tell them you've got plans.

Right, so you’ve got the job description open? Let’s have a proper look. It's quite a long one, isn't it? It is. It’s… thorough. Which is good, I suppose, but a bit daunting. I’ve read it a couple of times, but I’m still not entirely sure what they  want  exactly, beyond someone who can “tell stories”. A lot of people can tell stories. Okay, well let's break it down. See this bit here - "demonstrable experience in creating content for multiple platforms"? That's you, isn't it? Radio, podcasts, social media... Yeah, definitely. I just worry about phrasing it, you know? I don’t want to sound like I’m just listing everything I’ve ever done. It needs to be… tailored. Ugh, I hate tailoring. You're good at tailoring! Remember that time you rewrote your entire personal statement for that MA just three days before the deadline? That was impressive tailoring. This is nothing. Focus on the bits that  specifically  relate. They mention a focus on video content, right? Yeah, which is… a little terrifying. I’ve done some basic video editing, but nothing fancy. Mostly just putting things together for social media. Okay, don’t downplay that. Social media video is huge! And you know about audience engagement and analytics, which is what they’re looking for. Think about that series you did on local musicians – that had really good reach, didn’t it? You could talk about the challenges of adapting storytelling for a visual medium, how you learned to keep it concise and engaging... Hmm, that’s a good point. I did spend ages learning how to use Premiere Pro for that. And the analytics were pretty interesting. Okay, okay, writing that down. “Experience adapting storytelling techniques for visual platforms, demonstrated through the ‘Local Sounds’ series, utilising Premiere Pro and audience analytics to maximise reach and engagement.” Is that… awful? No! That’s excellent! See? You  can  do this. It's much better than just saying "I've used Premiere Pro". It shows you understand the bigger picture. What about this section on "managing and mentoring junior team members"? That's… a bit trickier. I’ve supervised interns, but haven’t really had formal managerial responsibility. Don’t feel you need to fabricate experience, but you can highlight your skills in guiding and supporting others. Think about how you’ve helped colleagues develop their skills, even if it wasn’t officially part of your job description.

Right, so realistically, if we want to actually  do  this, properly do this, and not just talk about it over a glass of Australian Shiraz… we need a business plan. A proper one. Not one scribbled on a napkin. You think a napkin plan wouldn’t cut it with the bank, do you? You’re right, though. A proper one. And we need to figure out the legal structure, don't we? Sole trader, partnership, limited company... all that fun stuff. Yep. I’m leaning towards limited company. Protects us, even if it’s just a small operation at first. And then there’s the website, branding… all the things I used to roll my eyes at when people talked about "building a brand”. Now  I’m  the one talking about it. It feels a bit… odd, doesn’t it? After years of reliable paychecks and pensions, suddenly you’re a ‘brand’. But honestly, I’m excited. This photography thing… it’s been just a hobby for too long. I feel like I could genuinely make something of it, especially here. The light, the landscapes… it's incredible. You’re brilliant at it. Seriously. And there’s a market for it. Tourists, local businesses needing content… even just selling prints online. We could focus on wildlife photography too, that’s always popular. Wildlife’s good. And events. Weddings, birthdays… even corporate events. I’ve been quietly networking a bit with some of the local event planners while we’ve been housesitting, just gauging interest. Seems promising. What about you? What’s the “brand” going to be for the consultancy side of things? Still a bit hazy. Definitely focusing on small businesses, helping them with strategy and digital marketing. I’m toying with the idea of specialising in eco-tourism. There’s a real demand for sustainable practices, and a lot of businesses are struggling to navigate that. That sounds… you. You and your slightly obsessive commitment to recycling. Hey! It's not obsessive! It's… conscientious. Regardless, it feels like a good niche. Less competition, more purpose. Okay, so first things first, let’s block out a couple of days next week to really hammer out that business plan. We need financials, market research… the works. Sounds good. And we need to start thinking about a name. Something that reflects both our ventures, maybe? Something… Australian-inspired, but not  too  cliché.

Honestly, Leo, you've got peas  all  over your chin. Look at you, a little green man. Man! He's a messy eater, alright. Reminds me of little Jamie MacIntyre back in '87. Used to fling porridge. Porridge, mind you! Covered the whole classroom. Ah, the exuberance of youth. Though I confess, I never understood the appeal of flinging perfectly good porridge. A waste, that. It  is  a waste, isn’t it? Speaking of waste, did that HelloFresh delivery come today? I completely forgot to prep anything. Aye, it came. I put it in the fridge. Looks…complicated. Lots of little sachets. You’ll need your glasses for that one, dear. Wonderful. Complicated and tiny sachets. Just what a sleep-deprived mother needs. It's just, I feel so bad, I haven’t been properly  present  lately. Always rushing, always tired. You’re doing a magnificent job, darling. Don’t beat yourself up. Bringing up a wee one is a full-time occupation, and a demanding one at that. Remember, it’s the quality of time, not the quantity. Your grandfather is right. And Leo seems happy enough, doesn’t he? Look at him, beaming. Beam! He is beaming. It's just… I saw Sarah from school today. She's planning a 40th. A big one. And it made me realise I haven't really  done  anything for myself in years. Forty is just a number, my dear. Don’t get caught up in these arbitrary milestones. Though, a good party is always welcome. Speaking of which, have you seen young Thomas’s beard? It’s quite remarkable. Like a Viking. Thomas? Oh, from the garden centre? Yes, it’s…substantial. A bit much for Cambridge, perhaps? It’s a  beard . Let the man have his beard. It’s not hurting anyone. Though, I always thought beards looked better on men slightly older. Nonsense! A well-maintained beard transcends age. It’s a statement. Now, what’s truly concerning is the state of things around here. Have you seen the waiting lists for primary schools? Appalling. Absolutely appalling. Tell me about it. I was trying to look at options for Leo, and it's just a nightmare. Everything is oversubscribed. It’s the housing shortage, isn’t it? Too many people moving south, not enough homes, not enough school places… And the influx of…well, let’s just say varied nationalities. Not that there's anything  wrong  with that, per se.

Honestly, the state of that car park at the train station now. It’s ridiculous. They’ve changed the whole system with the passes… Oh, don't even  start  me. I tried to use my usual spot yesterday, and the machine wouldn't recognise the new code. Spent ten minutes faffing about with it, nearly missed my train! And there was a queue building up behind me, all glaring. Exactly! It was supposed to be simpler, wasn't it? They said it would reduce congestion. All it’s done is create a whole new level of stress. Did you manage to sort it eventually? Eventually, yes. A kindly gentleman helped me. Turns out I needed to input my registration number  before  the code. Such a simple thing, but nobody tells you that! Honestly, some of these systems… Anyway, how's your mum doing? I haven’t spoken to her properly in ages. She’s… okay. A bit achy, still. The arthritis is playing up, especially with this weather. She’s trying to do her little walks, but she gets tired quickly. She keeps muttering about needing a housekeeper, but you know what she’s like, she’d never actually  get  one. She’s fiercely independent, isn’t she? Like her mother, always wanting to do everything herself. Remember when she tried to repaint the shed, single-handedly? That was a disaster! Oh, I do! Covered head to toe in green paint! Dad was furious, but she just laughed it off. Speaking of disasters, did you hear about old Mr. Peterson from sixth form? Peterson? The one who was obsessed with cricket? What’s he been up to? Apparently, he tried to take up marathon running. At sixty-five! His daughter told me he pulled a muscle just getting out of bed the day after his first training run. Sounds about right, though, doesn’t it? Always pushing himself. He was always a bit of a show-off. Remember how he used to boast about his cricket scores? Though he was a decent player, I’ll give him that. It’s funny who you remember from those days, isn’t it? People you haven't thought about in years. It is. It makes you realise how long ago it was. Oh, and Liam’s piano lessons are going well. He’s actually practicing now, without me having to nag him. That's good!

Honestly, the amount of time I spend on Twitter these days… it’s ridiculous. And it’s  work . Supposedly. Tell me about it. I’m starting to feel like a professional doom-scroller. Though, admittedly, it is a surprisingly useful barometer for student anxieties. See a few complaints about, say, the library hours, and preemptively send out an email. Crisis averted. Exactly! It's the preemptive strike thing. Saves a deluge of emails later. Though, the negativity can get to you. I had a wee rant yesterday about some nonsense policy change at the council, and some bloke just… came for me. Full-on character assassination over 280 characters. Oh, the joys of online discourse. You can’t win those battles, honestly. Best to just block and move on. Did you not report him? I did. Reported him for being a… well, a bit of a berk. Doubt anything will happen. It just sucks the energy out of you, you know? I was trying to highlight a valid point and ended up arguing with someone who clearly hadn't read past the headline. It’s the echo chamber effect. Everyone just shouting into the void, confirming their own biases. I try to use it more for… showcasing the good stuff, you know? Department events, student successes. Positive reinforcement. Good shout. I should probably steer clear of the political stuff. It’s just… tempting. Especially on a Friday night with a pint. Very tempting. Though, I did fall down a rabbit hole last week comparing different university branding strategies on TikTok. Don’t ask. Lost about two hours of my life. TikTok? You’re on TikTok? That’s… unexpected. Research! Purely research. Gotta know what the students are doing, right? Trying to figure out if we could use it to promote some of the open days. But honestly, it’s just a whole world of dances and lip-syncing. I feel ancient. I can imagine. I stick to Twitter and LinkedIn. LinkedIn’s alright, actually. Good for keeping tabs on old colleagues. And generally feeling inadequate about everyone's career progression. Oh, classic LinkedIn. The highlight reel of everyone else's life. It's designed to make you question all your life choices. Precisely! Still, beats scrolling through endless rants on Twitter, I suppose. Though, I did see someone post a picture of a particularly aggressive seagull in Princes Street Gardens yesterday...

Honestly, this weekend was  wild . I’m still recovering. Did you even manage to relax at all? Relax? Barely. Hospital was absolutely rammed - apparently, there was some sort of… incident down by the river. Loads of overdoses, plus the usual Saturday night stuff. It was just constant. I literally collapsed on the sofa last night. How wild was  your  weekend then? Don’t tell me you went climbing again? Worse. Mum decided to ‘surprise’ us with a full roast dinner for eight people. Eight! And she insisted on doing everything herself. I tried to offer to help, but she just waved me away saying I ‘never do things properly’. Ugh, your mum. She’s… a force of nature, isn’t she? A well-meaning, slightly terrifying force of nature. Did at least the dinner  taste  good? It was okay. A bit dry. She overcooked the Yorkshire puddings, naturally. And then Aunt Carol started recounting the entire history of the village cricket team to everyone. Honestly, I nearly lost the will to live. Oh God, Aunt Carol. She’s a professional rambling machine. So, not exactly a relaxing weekend then? At least you had food! I just grabbed a sandwich at the hospital both days. It wasn’t about the relaxing! It was the… control. She just  takes over . And then she complained the whole time about how tired she was! Like, you brought yourself a flock of people to feed, what did you expect? Classic Mum. Honestly, it's a miracle you haven't developed a twitch. Speaking of food, I’m starving. I haven’t had anything proper since that pathetic sandwich. What’s in the fridge? Not much. There’s some leftover chicken from Friday, a sad-looking cucumber, and half a jar of pesto. I was thinking of just ordering a takeaway. Fancy pizza? My treat, as penance for subjecting you to the Mum saga. Pizza sounds AMAZING. Definitely need something cheesy and carb-loaded after the weekend I’ve had. Oh! And tell me everything about Liam. You were texting all Saturday afternoon. Is it still… tense? Oh, Liam. Don't even. He messaged saying he "needed space" after our argument. “Space”! Like we live in separate galaxies! It’s just… frustrating, you know? He never actually  says  what's wrong, he just gets passive-aggressive. Oh, darling. That’s awful. Seriously, you deserve someone who can actually communicate.

Right, so, the turkey’s looking good, isn’t it? Bit pink still, perhaps. It’ll be fine, Dad. It’s a big one, takes a while. Are you sure Uncle Barry's definitely coming on the 23rd? He’s notoriously…flexible with dates. He said he was, didn’t he? Said he’d booked the train. Though, knowing Barry, he probably booked it to the wrong station. Still, he seemed definite enough. Helen was on about getting him a little something for Christmas. Oh, good. He’ll love that. Anything’s better than him moaning about the lack of Quality Street. Did anyone manage to get through to Mark? He hasn’t returned my calls all week. I texted him yesterday, just a quick "thinking of you" message. No reply. Maybe he’s just busy with work. It's that time of term, isn't it? Reports due, parents’ evenings… Busy, or avoiding. He’s been a bit…distant lately. Since, you know…the thing with Claire. Don’t, Clive. Not at the table. It’s hardly festive to rehash that now. She’s moved on, he should too. He needs to start thinking about his daughter, not his own hurt feelings. I just worry, that’s all. He’s a bit like his mother, internalises everything. Doesn’t talk it out. It’s a terrible habit. You’re right, it’s not helpful to dwell. Speaking of things to worry about… Dad, have you got used to the car yet? You were a bit apprehensive about it at first. Oh, the car’s brilliant! Absolutely brilliant. Automatic, you know? No more clutching the gears. And the parking sensors! Divine. I reversed into Mrs. Higgins’ rose bushes last week – wouldn't have happened with the sensors. She wasn't impressed, naturally. Classic Clive. Though, maybe a bit more care on the reversing front, eh? Oh, it was a momentary lapse! Anyway, it’s far more comfortable than the old Ford. Makes a difference on long journeys. Though I haven't had a long journey since I got it. Just pops to the shops. Good. That’s what it’s for, isn't it? Are we all set for the meal then? Carrots are cooked, potatoes are roasting… I’m thinking gravy next. I’ve made the stuffing, with the sage and onion. And I snuck a bit of chestnut in, don’t tell Clive – he hates chestnuts.

Honestly, this Spanish… it’s kicking me, it really is. I thought French was bad enough, but this is another level of… complexity. Oh, I know the feeling. I dabbled a bit when we were in Tenerife, tried one of those evening classes, you know? Thought I’d impress the locals. Didn’t work. Just ended up confusing them, mostly. Confusing them is putting it mildly! I’m using Duolingo, and it’s alright for vocabulary, but the grammar… the verbs! It’s like they’ve got a hundred different ways to say the same thing, depending on whether the cat’s looking at the moon or not. Exactly! And the subjunctive! Don't even get me started on the subjunctive. It's a construct designed purely to torment English speakers. I remember the teacher trying to explain it… it went right over my head. Right over your head, like a plane! I’ve been trying to find good YouTube videos, but they all assume you’ve already got a grasp of the basics. Which, let's be honest, I haven't. I can order a coffee and ask where the bathroom is, that’s about it. That’s progress! I couldn’t even manage the coffee. I kept accidentally asking for a donkey. Apparently, ‘burro’ and ‘café’ sound a bit too alike when pronounced by a Londoner. A donkey! Oh, Arthur, you are terrible. It makes me feel a bit better, actually. I was starting to think I was losing my marbles. It’s just so different from anything I’ve tackled before. I mean, German’s logical. French is… French. But Spanish has just got its own weird rules. It's the rhythm, isn’t it? It’s so fast and flowing. Hard to keep up. And then there's the regional differences. You go to Barcelona, and they're speaking Catalan, then you go to Madrid and it’s Castillian. It's a nightmare. Oh, I’ve read about that. It’s fascinating, really. Like…Switzerland with German, French, and Italian all swirling about. But confusing as heck if you’re trying to learn the language. Do people there just… switch effortlessly between them? Apparently so. It's something they grow up with. I was reading an article about it. They said in places like Catalonia, kids learn both Catalan and Castillian in school from a young age.

Right, so I think we’ve got most of the bank statements sorted. Just these few from… 2018? Why are these still here, Dad? Oh, those. I thought I might need ‘em. You never know with… you know… things. Things? Like what? An audit from HMRC about a tenner interest earned in 2018? It’s not just that! Things happen. Plus, I like to keep records. It’s just… sensible. Sensible would have been scanning them onto a hard drive five years ago. Honestly, this whole room is like a paper graveyard. Speaking of which, have you seen that old scanner? The one I got you for Christmas, like, a decade ago? Somewhere… I think it's under a pile of magazines. No, wait, that’s just old copies of  Hello! . Still got one with Kelly Brook on the cover. She was… a vision, wasn’t she? Right. Focus. We’re trying to declutter, not reminisce about 90s glamour models. So, scanner. Want me to dig it out? We could at least digitize the essential stuff. Yeah, go on then. If it still works. Haven’t used it in… well, a long time. While you’re at it, see if you can find that little USB stick with all my holiday photos. I want to check the flight details for that trip to Alicante next year. Alicante? You’re going back to Alicante? Thinking about it. Brenda and Ken are going. Thought it’d be nice. And it’s cheap as chips. But I need to confirm the dates. It's all on that stick somewhere. Right, these documents… are these your university stuff? Yep. Got to sort through my old dissertation research. It’s all corpus linguistics based, so mostly just text files listing word frequencies. Not exactly riveting stuff. Corpus… what now? Sounds complicated. Is that what you do, with the English? Teach people how to… use big words? Something like that. I teach English as a foreign language, but my research focuses on how language  is  actually used, not how it  should  be. It involves analysing huge collections of text. That sounds… draining. I’d rather deal with actual people complaining about their broadband. Actually, talking of which, I need to call Sky about that bill. They’ve charged me twice. Classic. So, you want me to find the scanner, the USB stick with the flight details  and  mentally prepare to help you battle Sky customer services?

Honestly, that was a right palaver getting petrol, wasn’t it? It was a bit of a queue, yeah. What was going on? Seemed like everyone and their dog decided they needed fuel  right  then. Aye, I dunno. And the price! Honestly, it’s criminal, the amount they charge at motorway services. I always try and fill up before we get on, but I completely forgot this time. It’s daylight robbery. They always hike it up knowing people are stuck. I swear the gauges are rigged too, makes it look like you're getting less than you are. They well could be! You can never tell wi’ them. It feels like a scam, honestly. I nearly had a heart attack when I saw the total. Did you remember your loyalty card at least? I nearly forgot mine the other day. Saved a good few pence. Oh, aye, I did. Saved a couple of quid. Every little helps, eh? Still, it’s just… stressful, y’know? Especially driving in this traffic. Tell me about it. This M25 is a nightmare. I thought leaving at this time would avoid the worst of it, but… nope. It’s always bad, isn't it? They need to sort it out. More lanes, something. Speaking of stressful drivers, did you see that biker weaving in and out of the lanes back there? Oh, yeah! The one in the leather jacket? Bit reckless, wasn’t he? I hate it when they do that. It's dangerous for everyone. Dangerous! It's just asking for trouble. They think they own the road, some of them. Just because they  can  squeeze through gaps doesn’t mean they should. Exactly. They clearly haven’t thought about the consequences. What if someone pulls out? Or a lorry changes lanes? They wouldn’t even notice! They’re just focused on getting ahead. I swear, some of them go way over the speed limit too. I saw him glance at his speedo… definitely pushing it. Honestly, it's a miracle there aren't more accidents. It is. And they don’t wear proper gear half the time. Just a helmet and a jacket. What about protecting the rest of themselves? You’d think they'd invest in decent protection, considering the risk. Maybe it’s a confidence thing? Thinking they're invincible? Maybe. Or just daft. Honestly, it frightens me to see them.

Right, so you’re still going to the coaching session on Saturday then? Don’t forget your kit. Yeah, yeah. It’s fine. I’ve packed it already. Good lad. It's good you're keeping it up, even when it gets colder. Remember how much you moaned last autumn? Frozen fingers, apparently. It  was  freezing! And my serve was awful. It’s a bit of dedication, isn’t it? Getting better at anything takes dedication. Have you been practicing the stuff Coach Mark showed you? The little adjustments to your grip? A bit. I tried. It feels weird. Like I’m holding the racket upside down. It always feels weird at first. Think about Djokovic, eh? He probably felt ridiculous when he first started working on new techniques. Look at him now. Oh, he’s just incredible. The way he moves…and his mental strength. He just doesn't give up. He’s good, I guess. I prefer Alcaraz. Alcaraz is brilliant, he’s really exciting to watch. So much energy. But Djokovic is just…consistent. He’s a machine. They’re both phenomenal, though, aren’t they? It’s a really interesting rivalry. It's good for the sport. Remember when Federer was dominating? That was a different era. Oh, Federer. Such an elegant player. I used to love watching him. There was just something so graceful about his game. I remember when he beat Sampras at Wimbledon. I was absolutely thrilled. Who's Sampras? Oh, you wouldn't know him. He was before your time. An American player. Brilliant serve. Dominated Wimbledon for years before Federer came along. He was a bit of a showman too, wasn’t he? Threw his racket around a bit. Not like the controlled aggression of Djokovic or Alcaraz. No, not at all. More…boisterous. Anyway, back to you. Have you thought about entering a tournament soon? Just a local one to get some experience. I don’t know… I’m not very good. Nonsense. You’re improving all the time. That’s the point of the coaching, isn't it? You have to test yourself. Your coach thinks you’re really promising, you know. He says you have a natural aptitude for the game. He’s just saying that. No, I’ve overheard him talking to other parents. He genuinely thinks you have potential. Don’t be so modest, son. Oh, the chicken’s nearly done.

These napkins… seriously? They look like… underpants. Oh, don’t be daft, Liam! They’re festive! Little snowflakes! They  do  kind of resemble a pair of briefs, though. Especially when you fold them. Your mum got them in the sale, didn't she, love? Everything was half-price after Boxing Day last year. Don’t start on me about the sales! Absolute chaos. I went for biscuits and ended up with a garden gnome. A  garden gnome , I ask you! What happened to the normal ones? The red ones? I used them all making the Christmas Eve boxes. Everyone loves a Christmas Eve box. Speaking of Christmas Eve, did anyone actually manage to stay awake for the Queen’s speech this year? Nope. Exhausted. Too much turkey prep. Though I did record it. Haven’t watched it yet. Oh, the turkey! A magnificent bird, it was. Though I'm still picking out feathers. Honestly, the state of it! It  was  good though. Best turkey ever. Your dad did a fantastic job. Though he nearly set the kitchen on fire trying to baste it. Nearly. A little smoky. But we averted disaster. Remember last year, when Auntie Carol tried to pull the wishbone and nearly took Uncle Barry’s eye out? Oh, don’t remind me! I had to grab an ice pack. Barry was dramatic as ever. “I’ve lost an eye! I’m blind!” He always is. So, Lucy, how was Florida? Did you get any good Christmas shopping done? It was mental, honestly. The airport was packed. Getting through security felt like a military operation. Was it warm? Baking! Completely different to this. Though I missed a proper Christmas. It’s all palm trees and fake snow over there. Did you see any alligators? Very funny, Liam. No alligators. Mostly just people wearing Christmas jumpers with shorts. That sounds… odd. Still, at least you had a break from the weather. This has been a dreadful December. Non-stop rain. It’s alright when you're not travelling, though. It makes you appreciate a cozy evening in. Exactly. Snuggled up with a good film. I watched  Downton Abbey  again. Still gets me every time. That’s so old! It’s a classic! And the music is beautiful. Do you remember when they had that ballroom scene, and… Mum, we’ve had this conversation. Leave her alone. She’s a  Downton Abbey  devotee.

Honestly, this week has been  insane  at work. Just back-to-back meetings, everyone panicking about deadlines… It’s exhausting. Oh, tell me about it. Exams are looming, and you get the most dramatic behaviour from the kids, and their parents, at this time of year. One mother actually accused me of deliberately making the timetable difficult for her son! Deliberately! Sounds about right. People are always looking for someone to blame. Reminds me of a deal I was trying to close last month. Farmer wouldn’t budge on price, blamed the weather, blamed the government subsidies, blamed the phase of the moon. The phase of the moon? Seriously? Swears blind! Said it affected the growth of the barley. You learn to just nod and smile in this business. Anyway, enough about my woes, how’s the flat hunt going? Still looking? It’s…slow. Everything is either tiny and overpriced, or a bit further out than we’d like. It’s just frustrating, you know? Saving for a deposit feels like an impossible task when rent is so high. It is a nightmare, isn't it? We were lucky when we bought this place, back in the day. Prices were…comparatively reasonable. Though, your father was convinced we were throwing money away on bricks and mortar. He always was a bit of a pessimist, your father. Though a shrewd businessman, I’ll give him that. Speaking of throwing money away, have you spoken to Sarah and Mark recently? Heard they’re thinking of taking the children to Disney World. Oh, no! Not again. They went two years ago! That must cost a fortune. They always seem to have money for these lavish holidays. Well, Mark's doing well with his investments, apparently. Though I do wonder if they ever think about saving for the future. Still, it’s their money, isn’t it? I suppose. It just feels a bit…flaunted, sometimes. Especially when you're scrimping and saving just to afford a basic life. It’s easy to fall into that trap, comparing yourself. Remember when old Geoff next door won the lottery? Drove us all mad with his new sports car and constant boasting. Oh, Geoff! He couldn’t drive to save his life, let alone a sports car. Nearly took out Mrs. Higgins' prize-winning roses. Right, okay, enough complaining about other people’s finances. I’m making a chilli tonight, anyone fancy staying for dinner?

Right, I’m just going to get the pasta on. Do you want me to do a tomato sauce or something a bit creamier? Creamy sounds lovely actually, after the day I’ve had. Honestly, the appraisal… it was just… so much box-ticking. Oh, those things are the worst, aren’t they? All ‘strengths’ and ‘areas for development’… It’s just corporate speak for ‘you’re alright, but could do better’. Exactly! And then she spent ten minutes talking about synergy. Synergy! What does that even  mean  in accounts payable? Probably something to do with spreadsheets. Speaking of utterly pointless things, have you seen the new M&S food hall? It’s… overwhelming. Overwhelmingly expensive, you mean? Well, yes, that too. But they’ve got these little pizzas, individual ones, all different flavours. Looked rather good. Though I suspect we could get a takeaway for the same price as two of those. Definitely. Still, tempting. Did you see they’re doing that duck confit again? Oh, good point. We should probably get that. Oh, and they’ve got those little vegan scotch eggs. Vegan scotch eggs... the world has gone mad. How can something be a scotch egg without sausage meat and a boiled egg? It defies logic. Exactly! Right, pasta’s on. How was Buster today? Did he try and eat the houseplants again? He did. I caught him attempting to scale the fern. Little monster. Honestly, sometimes I think he believes he  is  a jungle cat. He’s got the attitude, that’s for sure. I was reading an article earlier about equine welfare, and it’s just heartbreaking what some of those horses endure. It is grim, isn’t it? People just don’t seem to understand they're sentient beings. It’s the same with cats, really. People think they’re aloof and independent, but they feel things deeply. Absolutely. Right, sauce is simmering. I’m thinking of tackling that crossword later. That cryptic one from Saturday is proving particularly devious. Ooh, good luck with that. I haven’t even looked at it yet. I was thinking we could watch another episode of  The Walking Dead  tonight? Mmm, maybe. Or we could finally get round to starting  Trapped ? I’ve heard really good things about that one.  Trapped  sounds good. We’ve had enough zombies for one week, I think. Oh, and I found that bottle of wine in the cellar, the one we’ve had for… fourteen years?

Honestly, I’ve spent way too much money this month. Like, legitimately worried about my bank account. Tell me about it! I impulse bought a dress online last night. It was on sale, but still...sale or not, it was a bad idea. Proper “need it now” vibes. Oh god, don't even  start  on online shopping. It’s a black hole. I was scrolling through ASOS earlier and nearly bought six different pairs of boots. Six! You lot are terrible. I’m trying to be good. I’m really hoping I can get away with wearing these jeans again tonight. They’re… mostly clean. Mostly? What does that even  mean ? Is there a suspicious stain? Maybe… a slight chip shop residue. Don't judge me. It was a good night. Oh, we’ve all been there. Though, chip shop stains are a whole other level. What are you wearing tonight, anyway? I'm thinking the black skirt, but I can’t decide on a top. I’m wearing that sparkly thing I got from Primark. It’s ridiculously over the top, but it’s a Saturday night, innit? Gotta embrace the chaos. I'm going for comfy-chic. Black leggings, a nice jumper, and… probably trainers. I’m already dreading the thought of trying to walk in heels all night. Heels are the devil. Seriously. I wore them last week and my feet were screaming by 10 pm. I ended up borrowing someone else's trainers. I'm attempting heels. I’ve got these new platforms, but I’ve only worn them around the house, so it’s a bit of a gamble. I'm predicting needing a piggyback by the end of the night. Oh, you'll be fine. Just pace yourself with the drinks, yeah? Speaking of which… pre-drinks at mine? I’ve got some prosecco chilling. Yes! Prosecco is a  must . But not too much prosecco before we head out. We don’t want any embarrassing incidents. Remember Sarah last month? Oh,  god  don't remind me. She tried to have a full-blown conversation with a lamppost. It was a very serious conversation, apparently. About the importance of street lighting. Right. Okay, prosecco in moderation. And I'm bringing the snacks. Because we all know we need fuel for a night of questionable decisions. Perfect! What time shall we all be over? Like, sevenish?

Honestly, I just… I don’t  get  people who are relentlessly optimistic. It’s exhausting. Like, everything’s rainbows and unicorns, even when their cat’s just died. You think they're faking it? No, not faking. Just… fundamentally different wiring. I need a bit of realism. A bit of “Oh, this is awful, isn’t it?” before leaping to solutions. It’s the constant positivity that grates. Brenda at work is like that. Drives me mad. Brenda, huh? Sounds a bit… much. Remember Auntie Mavis? Similar vibe. Always talking about finding her ‘spiritual path’. Oh god, yes. The crystals, the incense, the whispered pronouncements about energy fields. It was… a lot. You always handled her with such grace, though. I just wanted to roll my eyes. Someone had to. But she  was  harmless. I think she genuinely believed she was on some grand spiritual journey. Made her happy, I suppose. You ever feel like that, by the way? Like you're supposed to be  searching  for something bigger? Occasionally. But then I remember I just want a quiet evening and a good book and think, “No, I’m probably fine as I am." Do you believe in soulmates? Honestly? I used to. Very emphatically, in my twenties. Now… I think it’s a lovely idea, but probably a bit romanticised. I’m quite happy with a very compatible and affectionate life partner. You? I'm leaning towards compatible as well. The idea of one perfect person out there is a bit terrifying, actually. Too much pressure. Although, sometimes, when we’re just… being comfortable together, I do think, “Yeah, this is pretty good.” See? That's better than needing a soulmate. Imagine if we’d both spent our lives looking for 'the one' and missed out on this. True. It’s just… sometimes I fantasise about visiting different periods in history. Like, what would it have been like to be a flapper in the twenties? Or a Victorian lady in a huge dress? You’d be terrible as a Victorian lady. Too much sass. You’d have scandalised everyone. Probably. Although, imagine the parties! Those grand balls, the elaborate etiquette… I’d be all over that. I’m planning an imaginary party right now. It’s 1928, everyone’s wearing sequins, there’s a jazz band…and Brenda from work is banned. Harsh. But fair. I’m inviting Oscar Wilde.

Honestly, this new client is driving me round the bend. They want everything yesterday, and then complain when it’s not perfect first time. You wouldn’t believe the emails. Oh, tell me about it. I had a bloke today who wanted me to expedite a form… which he’d only  just  submitted. Like, I physically can’t make it go faster, mate. Men! Honestly. They think we have some sort of magic button. Though, actually, I had a right drama with Brenda this morning. She’s called in sick  again . Oh no, not Brenda? What’s she claiming this time? Migraine. I’m starting to think she enjoys a duvet day. I mean, honestly, twice in one month? I’m not saying she’s lying, but… People take the mick, don’t they? Though, a proper migraine is awful. My mum gets them. Makes her see spots. True, true. Still, it messes up the admin no end. Anyway, enough about work. How’s the knitting going? Did you finish that jumper for your nephew? Nearly! Just the sleeves left. It's a bit wonky, I’ll be honest. I’m not exactly a master knitter. It’s more…rustic. He’ll love it. He’s five, he doesn't care. That’s sweet. I keep meaning to take it up again. It’s so relaxing. Though, I worry I’d just end up with a pile of unfinished projects. Like I do with everything. Speaking of projects, have you two seen that documentary about cemeteries? The Victorian ones, all the elaborate tombstones? Oh, the one on Channel 4? Yes! It was fascinating, wasn't it? All that symbolism. And the stories behind the people. I missed that. Was it good? I love graveyards, weirdly. They’re so…peaceful. And you can learn so much about history. It’s amazing. Apparently, the bigger the tombstone, the more… important you were. And they used to write these incredibly long, poetic epitaphs. It’s a completely different attitude to death than we have now. It is. Everything's so rushed and clinical these days. My aunt’s just had her funeral. Very simple. It felt… wrong, somehow. Not celebrating her life enough. I think it depends on the person, doesn’t it? My grandad wouldn’t have wanted a fuss. Just wanted to be… gone. Fair enough. Although, I do think we’ve become a bit desensitised to death.

Honestly, I’m starting to think Millie’s just…making it up. About the landlord being rubbish. Like, every week it’s something new. Making it up? Really? She seemed pretty stressed when she was telling us about the leak last week. Proper soaked her trainers, she said. Yeah, but then she was bragging about how she got him to agree to fix the bathroom  and  give her a discount on rent. Bit sus, innit? Exactly! She's a master manipulator. I swear she enjoys the drama. Remember when she said her flatmate stole her pasta? Oh god, yes! And then it turned out she’d just…misplaced it in the back of the cupboard. Classic Millie. It’s exhausting being around her sometimes. Like, can’t we just have one conversation that  doesn’t  involve a crisis? Tell me about it. Speaking of exhausting, has anyone sorted out their tax code thing yet? I keep getting emails from HMRC and honestly, it just looks like code to me. Nah, I’m putting it off. It feels like a trap. I'm pretty sure as soon as I click anything, they’ll demand all my student loan and then some. I’ve started it, but I’m already confused. Apparently, I ‘earned’ £3,000 from…existing? Is that a thing? They just say that to mess with us, I reckon. It’s probably just the maintenance loan. Anyway, are we still going to the match on Saturday? I managed to snag tickets. Sick! Yeah, definitely. Unless… Wait, what time is it again? I promised Jamie I’d help him with his essay. It’s about post-structuralism or something. Sounds horrific. Oh dear god. Jamie and post-structuralism. That’s a recipe for disaster. He spent two hours trying to explain nihilism to me last week and I still haven’t recovered. Just tell him you’re busy! The football's more important. Plus, apparently, there's a new burger van outside the stadium. They do loaded fries. Loaded fries? Now  that  is a good enough reason to ditch post-structuralism. Consider Jamie ditched. Good. Speaking of ditching things, I need to go to the shops later. I’m out of biscuits. Actually, no, scratch that. I'm out of  everything . I think I survived on pesto pasta for three days straight last week. You’re a minimalist. You're just living the simple life.

This seafood risotto is  amazing . Honestly, the best thing I’ve eaten all week. Glad you're enjoying it, love. It's good, isn’t it? A bit different to Greggs, eh? Mmmph. It’s good. Can I have some of your chips, Dad? You’ve barely touched your own! Finish those first, then we’ll talk chips. So, Sarah, still loving university? How’s the dissertation going? It's… a process. Honestly, I spend more time procrastinating on Facebook than actually writing it. I found like, five old school photos of me and Liam today. Ridiculous. Facebook, honestly. It’s a time thief. I only go on to look at pictures of people’s grandchildren. And confirm I haven't missed any sudden births. Gran, you always say that! Like, you just check for babies! Well, someone has to, don't they? It's a demanding job, you know. Had a tricky one last week – mum came in, convinced she was in labour, turned out to be gas! Sounds stressful. My days are mostly spreadsheets and powerpoint presentations, thankfully. Although, I had a client last week who wanted to redesign his entire company based on… moped culture. Moped culture? What even  is  that? Apparently, it’s a thing. A very niche thing. Lots of talk about vintage Vespas and artisanal helmets. Dad, you're making that up. I assure you, I am not. He wanted the office to look like a 1960s Italian scooter repair shop. Oh, bless him. He sounds a bit lost. Anyway, Liam, how’s school? Any plans for the summer? Just… chilling, I guess. Probably playing FIFA with Ben. Maybe get a new bike. You still playing football then? You were talking about giving it up… Nah, I still play. Just not as much. It’s alright. It’s getting harder with everyone getting bigger and stronger though. Remember when you used to complain about the bus being late for football practice? That seems like ages ago. Oh god, don’t remind me. That number 8 bus was the bane of my life. Always fifteen minutes late. And the smell! It always smelled like wet dog and chips. Speaking of dogs, how's Winston doing, Hazel? He alright? He's good. He's been getting a lot of walks with Emily. He’s getting a bit grey around the muzzle now, poor thing. Starting to slow down.

Right then, well that's the bags mostly unpacked. Didn’t half rain on the way back, did it? Thought we were bringing the Cornish weather  with  us. You always say that, dear. It always rains when you come back from somewhere nice. It’s a law of nature, I reckon. How did you get on with unloading everything from the car? Your back must be playing up again. Managed alright. Young David next door gave me a hand with the heavier bits. Good lad, he is. Though he kept going on about this cycle race that went through the village yesterday. Said it was “massive.” Didn’t see a thing, of course, stuck in traffic most of the afternoon. Oh, the Tour of Britain passed through near me too, actually. Went through Solihull. It was quite a spectacle. Loads of people lining the streets. Though I mostly saw it on the telly, let’s be honest. Easier on the knees. So, Cornwall. Tell me  everything . You were volunteering at the YHA again, weren’t you? How was that? Oh, lovely. Absolutely lovely. Different bunch this time. A couple from Australia, a German student… and a rather quiet young man who just kept taking photographs. Spent hours up at the lighthouse, he did. The lighthouse? Which one? St. Michael’s Mount? No, the one at Godrevy. You know, the one Virginia Woolf wrote about. He was obsessed with it. Kept taking pictures of the waves crashing against it. Said it was “elemental.” Sounds a bit pretentious, doesn’t it? Sounds artistic. He probably had a whole project dedicated to lighthouses! Did you talk to him much? Not really. He was a bit stand-offish. But the others were a good laugh. We had a day trip to St Ives, and then a walk along the coast path. Got absolutely drenched, as I said. Saw some crabs though, big ones! Crabs, eh? Always reminds me of holidays as a kid. Trying to catch them with a bucket and a net. Never had much luck. Remember that time we tried to do Yorkshire in a day? Absolute disaster. Drove for hours and saw nothing but rain and sheep. Don’t remind me! Honestly, it was a complete waste of petrol. We should have just stayed in bed. Though, thinking about it, we did find a particularly nice tea room in Haworth. Oh, I remember that one!

This is actually really good, isn’t it? You’ve outdone yourself, Chloe. Proper comfort food. It is! Seriously, after a week of salads trying to be ‘good’, this is exactly what I needed. What  is  in it, though? It’s not just beef mince and tomato, is it? There’s a load of Worcestershire sauce. Secret ingredient. Me mum always puts it in her chilli. Makes all the difference. Oh, that’s clever. I always forget about Worcestershire sauce. It's a game changer. Right, so, anyone got any…drama to spill? My week’s been spectacularly uneventful, which is nice for once. Just spreadsheets and lukewarm coffee, the dream. Oh, you say that like it’s a good thing! I thrive on drama. Though, honestly, work's been a bit hectic. We had a massive production delay because one of the suppliers, apparently, their van broke down. Full of vital components. Classic. Always a van, innit? Always a van! I had to stay till nine last night trying to sort it out. Honestly, sometimes I think I should’ve stuck with my original plan of becoming a florist. Less stressful. A florist? I didn’t know that! You, a florist? I can’t picture it. You’d be too…efficient. You'd have perfectly organised bouquets and colour-coded flowers. Probably. It’s just, the thought of sunshine and pretty things is really appealing right now. Speaking of appealing, how are things with Ben? Still going strong? It’s…complicated. We had another conversation last night. About, you know, the future. And whether we actually  want  the same future. Oh, bugger. That sounds…tense. It was. He’s brilliant, honestly, he is. But he’s so…content. He loves his job, his routine, his PlayStation. And I'm, like, planning world domination and booking weekend trips to Iceland. You need someone who can keep up with your energy, definitely. It's no good being with someone who dampens everything. Yeah, you need ambition in a partner. Someone who's always up for a laugh and a bit of adventure, you know? Not just…settled. Don't get me wrong, settled's good eventually, but not when you're twenty-something. Exactly! He just doesn’t  get  why I want to go skydiving. He thinks it's a waste of money. Oh, my god. That’s a dealbreaker right there. Seriously.

Oh my god, Barcelona was  amazing . Seriously, you would have loved it. Did you have a good weekend? You didn't mention going anywhere with… Mark? It was alright, pretty chilled actually. Mark was working all weekend, sadly. Just had a proper duvet day, really. Needed it after last week, honestly. How was Barcelona though? Spill! Was it as good as you hyped it up to be? Better! Honestly. The food was incredible. I ate so much tapas, I think I’ve gained about five pounds. And the architecture! Gaudí is a genius. We went to Park Güell… honestly, it was like stepping into a fairytale. Ooh, Park Güell sounds incredible. I've seen pictures. Did you manage to actually, like,  relax  at all? You're always rushing around on holiday. I did! A bit. We spent a whole afternoon just sitting on the beach, people-watching. And drinking sangria, obviously. It was bliss. Thinking about it makes me want to book flights back already. We should go together next year! Maybe Paris? Paris would be lovely! Although, expensive. Maybe we should start saving now? How much did Barcelona actually set you back? Hmm, probably around seven hundred quid, all in. Flights were reasonable, but the accommodation was a bit pricey. And I did a bit of shopping… don't tell my bank account. Anyway, enough about my spending habits. What did  you  get up to, aside from the duvet day? Did you watch anything good? Not much, honestly. Watched the new series of ‘The Fall of the House of Usher’ on Netflix, that was pretty good. Dark, as you’d expect from Mike Flanagan. And I attempted to bake a cake, which was… a disaster. It’s currently residing in the bin. Oh no! Baking fails are the worst. I tried making macarons once. It did  not  end well. Mum was over visiting last week and was going on about my cousin Sarah getting married next year. Apparently, it's going to be huge. Oh really? Where? I haven't spoken to your aunt in ages. Devon. She's always wanted a big posh wedding. Mum's already stressing about what to wear. She's asked me to be a bridesmaid, which is… a lot. Oh wow. That’s a big commitment! But good, you'll have fun. Speaking of commitments, any news on the boyfriend front? Still seeing… what’s his name, Ben? Ugh, Ben.

…and honestly, the paperwork was just relentless. Mountains of it. You’d mark thirty essays, finish feeling quite pleased with yourself, and then realise there were another fifty reports to write. It felt like the marking was just a sort of…interlude between the actual  work  of being a teacher. Sounds brutal. My worst paperwork experience was definitely trying to get a small business loan. You wouldn't believe the hoops they make you jump through. Business plan, projections, personal guarantees…it felt like they wanted to know what I had for breakfast every morning before they’d consider giving me a tenner. Oh, I can imagine! It’s that feeling of being utterly scrutinised. And then judged, regardless of what you present. What sort of business was it, if you don’t mind me asking? It was a pop-up cinema, actually. A bit niche, I know. We did themed nights – classic silent films with live music, cult favourites, that sort of thing. It went down really well, initially. But scaling it up…that’s where the headaches started. Finding suitable venues, getting the licenses, insurance…it was a logistical nightmare. That sounds fantastic, though! So different from my world of Year 11 English Literature. A pop-up cinema! I’d have loved to have gone. Did you ever show any Hitchcock? Sometimes.  Psycho  always went down well, naturally. Though finding a venue with soundproofing for  that  was…an experience. Actually, the biggest logistical challenge wasn’t the films themselves, it was the popcorn. Seriously. Trying to get a reliable supplier for decent popcorn was a full-time job. The popcorn! That’s brilliant. It’s always the little things, isn’t it? You spend all this time thinking about artistic vision, and then get bogged down in the practicalities of snack provisions. Exactly! And people are  very  particular about their popcorn. It has to be perfectly salted, perfectly buttered…it’s a minefield. I’m glad I moved onto something a bit less…granular now. I import olive oil from Greece. Less drama. Olive oil? That sounds lovely. And far more relaxing. What made you decide to make that switch? I always thought entrepreneurs were relentlessly driven, always chasing the next big thing. Relentlessly driven to avoid stress, more like! The cinema was fun, but it was exhausting. And frankly, I realised I preferred the slower pace of building relationships with suppliers, ensuring quality…it’s a different kind of satisfaction.

Honestly, I’m starting to think living with Chloe and Liam was a mistake. Oh, not again. What’s happened now? Did Liam leave his dirty socks everywhere  again ? Worse. Chloe used my good shampoo. The expensive one, the one I only use for special occasions. She just… used it. No way! You told her that was your fancy stuff, didn’t you? Of course I did! I specifically said “Don’t touch the purple bottle, that’s for emergencies!” Apparently, a bad hair day constitutes an emergency now. Cheeky. They’re both a bit clueless sometimes, aren’t they? But hey, at least the flat’s usually clean…ish. That’s only because  I  clean! Liam just moves the mess from one corner to another, and Chloe thinks dusting involves waving a cloth vaguely in the direction of the furniture. You’re exaggerating. Am I? Last week, I found biscuit crumbs in the bathroom!  The bathroom,  Ben! Okay, fair point. Biscuit crumbs in the bathroom is a crime against hygiene. But think about it, you need them to balance out all the tidiness. It’s… feng shui. Feng shui doesn’t involve rogue digestive biscuits, Ben. And it's not just the mess. Chloe keeps borrowing my clothes without asking! I went to get my favourite jumper yesterday and it wasn’t there. Found her wearing it to the supermarket. Right, that’s proper annoying. Have you said anything? I tried. It just turns into a whole ‘Oh, I thought you wouldn’t mind’ and a dramatic sigh. It’s exhausting. I spend half my time feeling like their mum, not their housemate. Hmm. Maybe you should have a proper sit-down chat with them? Like, lay down some ground rules? I don’t want to be  that  person. The controlling housemate. But honestly, I’m starting to dread coming home sometimes. You're not being controlling, you just want a bit of respect for your stuff and a bit of help around the place. It’s reasonable! And honestly, a slightly cleaner bathroom would be a blessing. It would be a miracle. I just… I don’t know. Maybe we should start looking for a new place when our lease is up. Whoa, hold on. Let’s not jump to that yet. Maybe a chat will make things better. We can even practice what you're gonna say in the car, if you want.

Right then, that was a bit of a kerfuffle wasn’t it? Parking was awful. Awful doesn't even begin to cover it, Arthur. I thought I’d never get a space. Ended up right at the back, near the delivery entrance. Nearly lost a wing mirror to a van. You and me both, nearly took out old Mrs. Higgins’ shopping trolley trying to squeeze in. She gave me a right look, she did. Said I was a menace to society. Oh, she always does. She's a character, that one. Did you manage to get the biscuits I asked for? The ginger snaps? Course I did. They were on offer, two for three pound. Couldn’t resist. Figured we could have a little dunk in our tea later. Lovely. And the milk? Did they have the semi-skimmed? I swear they're trying to force us all onto that fancy whole milk stuff. They did, but they were nearly out. Only a pint left. Thought I'd grab it, rather than risk them not having any tomorrow. Good thinking. That’ll do nicely. Oh, and did you remember to pick up that tin of peaches for Betty? She’s been craving them. Oh, blast it all, no! I completely forgot Betty's peaches. I was thinking about the tomatoes for your salad and… slipped my mind. Arthur! She’ll be ever so disappointed. She was looking forward to having some with her custard. Oh dear. I'm terribly sorry, love. I'll pop back out tomorrow, first thing. Promise. It's not far, is it? It's not the distance, Arthur, it’s the hassle. Getting there, parking… it’s a nightmare. But alright, tomorrow then. Tomorrow it is. I’ll make a note. How’s your knee feeling today? Any better after the heat? A little, yes. Still a bit stiff, but not throbbing like it was. I managed a little potter in the garden this afternoon. Deadheaded a few roses. Good, good. Don't overdo it though. You don't want to have another flare-up. Why don’t you put your feet up now, I’ll make us a nice cup of tea with those ginger snaps? That sounds perfect, dear. Just perfect. And maybe we can watch that detective programme you like on the telly? Certainly can. A nice cuppa, biscuits, and a bit of Poirot… doesn’t get much better than that, does it?

Right, now then, tea’s nearly ready. You two behave yourselves for your Grandad and Gran. Don’t be winding them up too much. I wasn’t planning on it. Oh, don’t you worry about him, Margaret. He's all bark and no bite, aren’t you, lad? Though he did try to convince me the other day the TV was spying on us. It  is  spying on us, Elsie! They’re collecting data, I tell you! It's in the news! Oh, here we go. Your Grandad's read another article on the internet. He believes everything he sees, bless him. Seriously? Spying? What data would it want from us? Like, what we had for tea? It's more complicated than that, lad! They know where you go, what you buy, who you talk to… He thinks they’re building a robot army, Margaret. A robot army controlled by the television! Honestly, it’s exhausting. Anyway, how was school today, Leo? Any dramas? Not really. Maths was alright. We started on quadratic equations. Oh, good. Those are the tricky ones. Honestly, marking those GCSE papers… the things kids try and write! You wouldn’t believe. She’s a clever woman, our Margaret. Always was good with numbers. Remember in school, she used to correct the teachers? Now, Mum, don't exaggerate! I just… pointed out a few errors. Few? She practically ran the maths department! She’d have ‘em all in a state, she would. Sounds scary. It wasn’t scary, Dad, just… thorough. How are you both feeling? Did you have a nice journey over? Lovely journey, dear. A bit bumpy on the A64, but nothing we couldn't handle. And the driver was a nice young man, very polite. He was going a bit slow, though. I kept telling Elsie, I said, "Put your foot down, Elsie! We haven’t got all day!” You always were impatient, Dad. Actually, I was thinking… Could we watch a film later? Maybe that new superhero one? Oh, that sounds nice. I do enjoy a good film. As long as it’s not too scary, mind. I jumped a mile last time we watched that horror one. Elsie’s a scaredy-cat, always has been. Unless it’s a documentary about pigeons, then she’s fearless! They’re fascinating creatures, Arthur! Very intelligent. Honestly, you wouldn’t understand. Alright, alright, let’s not have a pigeon debate.

Honestly, this wait is ridiculous. I’ve been scrolling through TikTok for a solid twenty minutes now. Brain is turning to mush. Tell me about it. I should be replying to me nan, she sent me about fifty photos of her new cat. Seriously, fifty. Each one slightly different. Fifty? Blimey. My mum just keeps sending me links to these… health products. Apparently, this new “superfood” is going to cure everything. Saw one yesterday claiming it reverses aging. Oh, bless her. She’s fallen for it then? They’re always advertising that stuff on Facebook, aren’t they? My uncle got sucked into one about magnetic bracelets. Said it cured his arthritis. Classic. Honestly, the amount of misinformation on there is scary. I saw someone arguing the other day that 5G causes… well, everything. It's a wild west out there. Speaking of wild, anyone seen that new phone Samsung brought out? The one that folds? Yeah, it's mental, innit? Seems a bit… fragile though. Like, what happens if you drop that thing? Explodes? Probably. And it costs like, a grand. I’d rather just stick with my cracked screen, cheers. At least I know it’s battle-tested. I’m holding out for the next iPhone. Always been an Apple guy, me. Although, I will say, the camera on the new Pixels is seriously impressive. Saw some photos online, unreal. I think Jamie’s dad got one of those Pixels. Apparently, he’s taken up photography now. Said he’s going to enter a competition. Old Jamie? That’s brilliant! Remember him always filming us doing stupid stuff at uni? Maybe he's found his calling. He was always more interested in the filming than the actual ‘stupid stuff’ though, wasn’t he? Right, I'm just going to quickly text me nan and tell her the cat is lovely. Again. Did anyone watch that new series on Netflix? “Dark Horizon” or something? It was… a bit out there. Nah, I’ve been stuck on “The Crown” again. Proper binge-watching material. Makes me feel slightly guilty knowing how much privilege they had, though. Compared to, like, struggling through essays. I tried it, but I got to the Diana episodes and it just made me sad. I needed something a bit lighter. Been watching a load of baking shows. Baking shows? You? I thought you lived off instant noodles and questionable takeaways.

Right, so, shopping list. Milk’s definitely on there, isn’t it? We’re almost out. Aye, milk, bread… and get some more of them disinfectant wipes. I swear, this house attracts flies like nobody’s business. I just batted one away from Leo’s head a minute ago. Mum! You didn’t  bat  it, you tried to swat it with the TV remote! Well, it were the closest thing, weren’t it? And it nearly worked. Sounds like a scene from a cartoon. Honestly, the wildlife you get in Bolton… It's ridiculous. I swear the bins are a beacon. Oh! And loo roll. Definitely need loo roll. And… what about fruit? Apples? Bananas? Can we get those little oranges, the satsumas? Please? Yeah, satsumas are good. Right, fruit sorted.
