Mum, did you put anything on that bite on your arm? It looks awful. Just some antihistamine cream. Still itching though, the little blighter. I think it might be a mosquito, even though they’re not really around this time of year. Could be a horsefly. Nasty things. They leave a really nasty reaction. Perhaps some calamine lotion would help? Oh, good shout. I forgot about calamine. Add that to the list, love. Done. Calamine. Right, anything else? Oh! Biscuits! Need biscuits. Digestive or… Chocolate digestives! Definitely chocolate digestives. Always chocolate digestives with this lot. Of course. Now, speaking of things being bitten… did you see the game yesterday? United absolutely hammered them. YES! I told you they would! Rashford was on fire. Honestly, all that shouting at the telly. You'd think your life depended on it. It kinda does, doesn't it? It’s the only joy we have sometimes! A bit dramatic, perhaps. Though, I have to admit, it was a good match. I saw the highlights. Highlights? You have to  watch  the whole thing! You miss all the best bits. He's right, Dad. You miss the dodgy tackles and the angry managers. It's crucial viewing. Alright, alright. Don't you two gang up on me. Just get me that calamine lotion on the list, will you? And maybe a fly swatter that isn’t a TV remote. Consider it done. Calamine, fly swatter, milk, bread, loo roll, satsumas, chocolate digestives... Anything else before I finalise this masterpiece? Can we get those Monster Munch crisps? The Pickled Onion flavour? Leo! Seriously? We just had crisps yesterday!

Ugh, P.E. was  awful  today. Miss Davies made us do shuttle runs. Shuttle runs! Like, seriously? No way! Shuttle runs are the worst. I thought she liked us? I mean, we're in her form. Apparently not enough to spare us the torture. My legs are still burning. And then Ben kept trying to… well, you know… show off. Ben? Showing off? Groundbreaking. What was he doing this time? Trying to do like, a flip or something? Worse. He was trying to run the shuttle runs sideways. Sideways! Miss Davies just stared at him. It was glorious. Oh my god, I wish I’d seen that. Speaking of glorious, have you seen what Holly’s posted on Instagram? It’s just…filters. So many filters. She looks completely different. Ugh, Holly. She's obsessed. I saw a TikTok about how everyone on Instagram looks the same now because of those filters. It’s kind of scary, actually. Totally. Remember when people used to just…post normal pictures? Before everyone wanted to look like a cartoon version of themselves? Yeah. It’s all about the aesthetic now, isn’t it? It's exhausting. Did you finish the science homework? The one on… what was it, osmosis? Almost. I’m stuck on question three. It doesn't make any sense. Something about potatoes and salt? Oh, that one! It's a trick question. You have to remember what happens to the water inside the potato cells. It's all to do with… Wait, let me try and explain. Imagine the potato cells are like balloons… Okay, balloons… go on. And the skin of the potato is like the balloon's surface. If you put it in salty water, the water  leaves  the cells, so they shrivel up. It's like the balloons are deflating. Oh! Okay, okay, I think I get it now. You're a lifesaver. Seriously. Mr. Henderson would have my hide if I didn't understand osmosis. He’s so intense about science. I know! He's the kind of teacher who gets genuinely excited about chemical reactions. It’s a bit…much. Have you seen that new YouTuber, ‘Science Sam’? She explains things really clearly. Science Sam? No, I haven't. I’ll check her out. I need all the help I can get. Oh! And did you hear what happened with Chloe and Mr. Peterson? Ooh, spill! What?

Honestly, I feel like death warmed up. My throat is absolutely killing me. Oh, no! That’s awful. Still? You said you were feeling a bit rough yesterday, but I thought you'd bounced back. Bounced back? Ha! More like face-planted into a duvet and stayed there. It’s proper bad, like the kind of cold where you can  feel  your eyeballs aching. Ugh, those are the worst. Have you taken anything? Lemsip? Paracetamol? I’ve got loads if you need. Yeah, downed a load of Lemsip earlier. Doesn't seem to be doing much good, to be honest. It feels like one of those ones that settles in your chest. I’m worried about getting proper ill right before Christmas. You and everyone else, I suspect. Hospitals are already rammed, even before the winter really hits. Remember when I had that, uh,  incident  with the dodgy prawns last summer? Oh god, don’t remind me. You were practically green! And the noises… Let’s not dwell. But seriously, A&E was absolute chaos. All this talk about strain on the NHS, it’s true. And you’ve had your flu jab, haven’t you? Yeah, ages ago. Honestly, I'm starting to wonder if these jabs even  work . All my colleagues have been dropping like flies, vaccinated or not. It's never a guarantee, is it? It just reduces the severity, hopefully. Speaking of feeling rubbish, I was watching that old "MasterChef" episode last night with Lloyd Grossman… Oh, bless him. A national treasure. Seriously! And he was talking about how he always used to get food poisoning on set, because he was constantly tasting everything. Proper dedication, that. Makes my little cold seem a bit pathetic. Don't say that! It's a proper vile cold and I need sympathy. Besides, Lloyd Grossman probably had a team of doctors on speed dial. True. It's just… it makes you think. He was always so cheerful, even when no doubt feeling absolutely dreadful. You know, I was reading an article the other day about how they're developing AI that can read body language accurately. Really? Like, tell if someone's lying? That's part of it. But also detect subtle cues about how someone is  feeling  - pain, discomfort, even just mild annoyance. Imagine the implications for TV interviews, or even just everyday conversations. It's a bit creepy, actually.

Right, my turn. Hmm… Let’s see. I’m going to play ‘quixotic’ across the double word score. That’s… oh, a hefty 38 points! Sorry, David. Ouch! Quixotic, eh? Showing off a bit now, aren’t you, Margaret? I was saving up for a good one myself, but you’ve rather scuppered my plans. You two are at it again. Just like your father and I used to be, always trying to one-up each other at Scrabble. Though,  he  always accused  me  of having a dictionary hidden up my sleeve. A likely story, Moira. You always had a knack for words. Remember that time you corrected the Bishop’s grammar during the village fete? Caused quite a stir, that did. Oh, Grandad, you always have a story! It’s lovely. Though, I think that story might be slightly embellished. Anyway, David, you’re looking a bit glum. Don’t worry, there are plenty of tiles left. Just a bit frustrated. I was hoping to use that ‘x’ for something spectacular. Speaking of spectacular, did you see the gridlock at the Trafford Centre today? Absolute chaos. I spent forty minutes just trying to find a parking space. Oh, dear. That sounds dreadful. I’m glad I stayed in and finished that recipe I saw in that new cooking magazine. It was for a Moroccan tagine, absolutely delicious. You must try it, Margaret. I could send you the recipe. Oh, yes please! I’ve been meaning to try more Moroccan food. We had that lovely tagine in Marrakech a few years ago, remember? Marrakech… splendid city. Though, rather noisy. I prefer quieter holidays, myself. More conducive to reading. I’ve been re-reading my old copies of ‘The Gramophone’. Found a fascinating article on early jazz recordings. You and your jazz, Dad. You live and breathe it. I saw Michael posting on Facebook about his new band’s gig next week. He’s getting quite good, actually. Oh, that’s wonderful! I must send him a message of encouragement. He’s so shy about performing. It’s good he has a creative outlet. Keeps him stimulated. Though, I do worry about him. He works so hard. Reminds me of you, David, always burning the candle at both ends. I’m trying to take it easy, honestly! Although… I did promise to pick up some sausages from Mr. Henderson’s butcher shop tomorrow.

Goodness, this queue is moving slowly, isn’t it? Though I suppose it’s to be expected on a day like this. Lovely sunshine, everyone wanting to get out and about. It is rather. I’m just trying to sort out my ticket for the steam train. Been meaning to do this for ages. Used to come to these sorts of things with my father when I was a boy. Though, admittedly, they weren’t quite as…well, organised. Oh, you’re going on the steam train? How lovely! I’m just volunteering today, helping with the TME – the Taunton Model Engineers, you know. I dabble in a bit of miniature painting myself, so it seemed a fitting way to spend a Saturday. Miniature painting, you say? Interesting. I spent my working life surrounded by rather larger machinery, you see. Printing machinery, specifically. Oh really? That sounds…technical. It was. I spent a good thirty years inventing and marketing printing systems. Mostly offset lithography, though we dabbled in flexography too. Kept me busy, it did. Had a little company, built it up from nothing. Goodness me! That sounds incredibly demanding. I was always more of an…artistic type. Antiques, mostly. Had a gallery for a while, down in Devon. Trying to convince people that slightly chipped porcelain was ‘characterful’. I can imagine. A different skill set entirely, that's for sure. My biggest challenge wasn’t convincing people of character, but convincing them of efficiency! We did a lot of work in Germany, you know. Exhibitions in Frankfurt and Düsseldorf. The Germans are very keen on precision engineering. Oh, Germany! I’ve been a few times. To art fairs, mostly. Quite different from Somerset, wouldn’t you say? Always felt very…efficient, as you say. Very. And demanding customers. They weren’t afraid to tell you if something didn’t work. But it kept you on your toes. We developed a system for colour separation that was rather innovative at the time. Made life a lot easier for commercial printers. I’d spend weeks at those exhibitions, demonstrating the systems, explaining the intricacies…sometimes felt like I lived in a hotel room. I can imagine. Though I suspect explaining the subtleties of a Ming vase is a slightly different beast. It’s all about the narrative, you know? The provenance, the history…making people  feel  something. A narrative, yes. I suppose there  is  a narrative to a well-engineered machine.

Right, nearly at the M5 then, eh? Feels like we’ve been driving for days already. Tell me about it. My legs are all cramped. Are we stopping at Gloucester Services? They do the best pasties. Gloucester Services it is, then. Though I maintain, they’re a bit pricey for a pasty. Still, better than those motorway ones that look like they’ve been sat under a heat lamp since 1972. True. Speaking of things that look ancient, did you realise how weird English is when you think about it? Like, all the exceptions to the rules. Mrs. Davies was going on about it in English today. Oh? What's she been drilling into you now? She was a stickler for proper grammar, your Mrs. Davies. She was saying how there's no logical reason why 'though' is spelled with a 'gh' when it's pronounced 'tho'. And 'knight' has a 'k' but 'know' doesn't. It’s madness. It's evolution, love. Language changes. Words get borrowed, spellings get muddled up over the centuries. ‘Knight’ comes from Old English, originally pronounced with a hard ‘k’ sound. ‘Know’… well, that’s a whole different story. It’s practically a different language now than it was back then. It's just… frustrating when you’re trying to remember all the rules for the A-Level. Especially the etymology bits. Honestly, tracing words back to Old English and Latin feels like detective work. It  is  detective work, in a way. That’s the fascinating part. And it helps you understand  why  things are the way they are. You thinking about what you want to study at Uni still? Yeah. Still torn between English Lit and Philosophy. Philosophy's just… so abstract. Like, we were talking about free will today and my brain just short-circuited. Philosophy’s got a habit of doing that. It's good to challenge you though, isn’t it? Makes you think about things differently. Your Mum always said you were a deep thinker. Mum says I overthink everything. She’s right! But it’s a good quality. Right, approaching the services now. Do you fancy a browse in the farm shop? They usually have some decent local stuff. Ooh, yes! Actually, I saw on Instagram they had a farmer’s market in Padstow on Saturday. We should go. Padstow, eh? Sounds good. Always a good place to get fresh seafood.

Right, so I reckon if we chuck all this into the pot, it’ll be grand. It's just a posh shepherd’s pie, innit? My Nana used to make it all the time. Posh shepherd’s pie? Sounds fancy for a Tuesday night, doesn't it? My mum just used to throw mince at potatoes. Same result, though, I suppose. Your mum sounds a woman after my own heart. No point in fussing, is there? Just get it on the table. Though, a bit of gravy never hurt anyone. Nana always said the secret was a splash of red wine. And loads of Worcestershire sauce. Gives it a little…oomph. Red wine, eh? Alright, sounds alright. I’m on spud-mashing duty, then. Can I at least have butter in ‘em? Don’t want them being dry as a bone. Absolutely! Loads of butter. And a good dollop of cream cheese, if you're feeling particularly naughty. Cream cheese in mash? Now there’s a thing. Sounds a bit modern for me, that. I stick to a good knob of butter and a bit of milk. Simple. Oh, you’re old school, aren’t you, Geoff? You wouldn’t know a flavour explosion if it hit you in the face. I know what I like, lass. And I like things that taste like they’re supposed to. Speaking of liking things… how’s your sister, the one who went travelling? Still gallivanting around Thailand? Yeah, she’s still out there. Just sent me another load of pictures of beaches and monkeys. Makes me properly jealous, honestly. Says she’s thinking of going to Vietnam next. Vietnam, proper? That's a bit…out there, isn't it? Sounds mental. Is she going on her own still? Mostly. She met a bloke in Bali, apparently. Some Australian surfer dude. Mum's a bit worried, naturally. Wants her to come home and get a “proper job”. Mothers, eh? Always wanting their chicks to settle down. My Elsie was the same. Wanted me to take over the shop, but I weren’t having any of it. Too much work, that. Speaking of work, this job’s killing me, honestly. Been on that building site all week, shifting bricks in the rain. My back is screaming. Aw, that sounds awful! You deserve a proper break. Maybe we could all go out for a pub lunch on Sunday?

Right, so this is… significantly busier than I expected it to be for a Tuesday morning. Thought I could just grab a quick coffee and a scone before my shift. Tell me about it. I was hoping to get a bit of marking done, but there’s barely a spare seat. I should have known, it’s right next to the swimming pool, all the parents dropping kids off and grabbing a coffee. You a teacher then? I guessed something academic with the marking and all. Yeah, languages actually. French and Spanish. Secondary school. It's… rewarding, most of the time. What about you? You look a bit too young to be retired already. No, thankfully. I’m a bartender down at The Flute. It's alright, keeps me busy. Just finished my degree last year in History, but jobs weren’t exactly flooding in. History, that’s interesting! I always loved history at school. It's just, trying to make a career out of it… yeah, I can see why you ended up behind a bar. It's a good source of stories though, right? You must hear some good ones. Oh, you have no idea. Though most of them are probably best left unsaid. It's less ‘historical accounts’ and more ‘people making questionable life choices’. What age group do you teach? Year 7 mostly, so eleven and twelve-year-olds. It’s… a lot. It's amazing how much energy they have. Speaking of energy, are you doing anything sporty to keep fit? You mentioned a shift, is it a busy one? Nah, I’m pretty useless at sports. Tried football for a bit, was spectacularly bad. Keep meaning to join a gym, but… well, you know how it is. The shift is usually alright. Weekends are mental, obviously. Tonight's pretty standard, though. I know the feeling. I keep saying I'll take up swimming again, got a membership here, haven't been in three months. Just… life gets in the way. Have you been driving long? I saw you pull up in a pretty… compact car. Oh, Betsy. That’s her name. It's a Fiat 500. It was cheap. And small, which is essential for parking in Birmingham. I’ve had my license about five years, so yeah, fairly new to it all. Still get nervous on the motorways. I remember that feeling! I passed on my fourth attempt.

Oh, honestly, time's flown. I meant to have a proper coffee break ages ago. Are you wanting one, Arthur? Please, Doreen. And yes, a cuppa would be lovely. Though it'll have to be instant, I reckon. Don't want to keep David waiting while you get the cafetière out. Don't worry about me delaying things. I'm perfectly happy hovering. Though, I did notice the hydrangea looks a bit peaky. Needs watering, doesn't it? Oh, you're right, David. I meant to do that this morning. Honestly, I’m all over the place. I keep forgetting things. It’s probably age, isn't it? Probably. Or maybe you're just thinking about that trip to the Gambia. You were saying it was hot, wasn't it? Blisteringly hot? Oh, it was! Beautiful, though. And the people were so friendly. I was reading something the other day about a woman there... or maybe it was in Africa somewhere… who pretended to be ill to get attention. Apparently, it’s called Munchausen Syndrome. Dreadful, really. Deliberately making yourself sick. A fascinating, disturbing condition. I read a case study once about a mother doing it  to  her child. Utterly appalling. Sounds it. Anyway, Doreen, about those banners for the bell ringing… do you think we should keep them simple? Just ‘Bell Ringing – Open Day’ or something? Simple is good, Arthur. Less is more, as they say. Though we could maybe add a picture of the bells, couldn’t we? I’ve got that digital camera, I could take a photo. I can design something on the computer, if you'd like. Make it look proper and professional. I used to do a bit of graphic design for the old firm. That would be brilliant, David. You're a star. While you're at it, perhaps something for the donation box too? We need a new one for the village hall roof fund. Oh, yes. A nice little sign saying ‘Help Restore Our Village Hall Roof!' Something like that. And a little slot, of course. Easily done. Though have you two thought about how you’re getting the banners and the donation box to the hall? Arthur, you were saying your car's playing up again? That's the truth. It’s hesitating again. I think it might need a new fuel filter. Though I’m loath to take it to a garage, they charge an arm and a leg these days.

Honestly, this pasta is amazing, Chloe. Did you make the sauce from scratch? Yeah, pretty much. Just chucked a load of stuff in really. Tomatoes, garlic, a bit of chilli… didn’t measure anything. It’s so good! Way better than anything I could manage. My cooking skills peak at beans on toast, and even that’s a disaster half the time. Speaking of disasters, have you guys seen that new app, “FailFeed”? It’s just compilations of people’s cooking fails, DIY blunders…it's hilarious. Ooh, no, I haven't. I’m currently obsessed with “PlantSnap”. It identifies plants from a photo. I was walking in the park yesterday and finally figured out what that weird purple flower was! That sounds…surprisingly useful. I'm still stuck on TikTok, endlessly scrolling. It's a black hole. TikTok is dangerous. You lose hours. I was just saying to Liam the other day - we  need  to plan a holiday. We've been talking about Greece for ages. Oh, Greece! Yes! I went to Santorini with my family years ago, it was stunning. Ridiculously expensive, but stunning. Santorini's on my list. I'm leaning towards Italy, though. More affordable, and pizza. Honestly, pizza is a life goal. Pizza is  always  a good idea. Did anyone catch that new horror film, “The Hollow”? Everyone's been raving about how terrifying it is. Oh god, I heard! Apparently, there’s this one scene with… never mind, I don’t want to ruin it. I’m such a scaredy-cat. I can’t even watch trailers. I love a good scare! I’ll probably watch it this weekend. Although, I'm still recovering from “Hereditary”. That one messed me up for weeks. Oh, "Hereditary" is genuinely disturbing. It’s not just jump scares, it’s… unsettling. Anyway, changing the subject slightly – how’s Ben? I haven’t seen him out with you lately, Leo. Oh, Ben’s… good. We're taking a bit of a break, actually. It’s complicated. Oh no, Leo, I’m sorry to hear that. Everything alright? You can tell us, you know. Yeah, we’re all ears. It’s just… we want different things right now, I guess. He’s really focused on his music, trying to get a band together. And I just… need someone a little more settled. It's stupid, I know. It doesn’t sound stupid at all.

Right well that was a nice little visit wasn’t it. Bit chilly walking back from the bus stop though. It is. Still, good to see Maureen. Haven’t seen her properly since… well, ages. It was lovely. She’s looking well, considering. Still on about that new electric car she’s thinking of getting, though. Oh, is she? What sort of range does she need, really? She doesn’t do a lot of miles. Exactly. I said to her, Maureen, you mostly potter around Norwich, you don’t need something that’ll get you to John O’Groats on a single charge! She said it’s the principles of it, you know? Doing her bit for the environment. Principles don't keep you warm on the A11 when the battery runs out, that’s what I say. Though, I suppose, they’re getting better, aren’t they? The range. That’s what they say. But the price! You'd need to win the lottery. And where do you even  charge  the blasted things around here? There’s a couple of those charging points at the Long John Hill car park now. Oh, are there? Didn’t notice them. They’re probably always full. Full of Teslas, no doubt. Exactly! All these fancy cars. I’m perfectly happy with my old Fiesta. It gets me from A to B, and doesn’t cost a fortune to run. It's reliable, that's the main thing. I’m starting to worry about my Mondeo though. It’s getting on a bit, and the exhaust’s started rattling again. Oh dear. Don’t tell me you're thinking of getting a new one? No, no. Not a  new  one. Just…a newer one. Something a bit more sensible. Something that won’t bankrupt me every time I take it for an MOT. You wouldn't get away with a newer one. Doreen would have your hide. She likes a bit of comfort, doesn't she? She does. It’d have to have leather seats, at least. And heated ones. It’s getting cold enough these days! You’ll have to be careful driving home this evening, though. They said on the news there’s going to be icy patches. Icy patches? Oh, brilliant. Just what we need. I hate driving in the ice. Makes my hands shake. We could have got the bus. Oh, don’t be silly.

Honestly, the M6 is just relentless, isn't it? Always something. Though, I suppose it’s a luxury to be complaining about traffic when we’re actually  going  somewhere. Manchester, here we come! It is a bit of a slog. Still, better than being stuck packing boxes, I suppose. How are you holding up with all that, by the way? It must be exhausting. She’s coping. She’s always coping. It’s just…the sheer volume of  stuff  people accumulate. It’s terrifying. I’m mostly supervising and occasionally lifting things that look deceptively light. My back is reminding me I’m not twenty anymore. Oh, don't start, Arthur! You were lifting all those boxes of books yesterday. I told you to let the removal men do it! It’s just…thirty years in one house. You don’t realise how much you’ve got until you have to sort through it. And half of it is things I haven't touched since…well, since the kids were little. It's the sentimental stuff that's the hardest, isn't it? I tried decluttering recently and ended up keeping a broken ceramic frog because ‘it reminds me of a holiday.’ Oh, you and your ceramic frogs! That's exactly what I mean! I found old school reports. Honestly, I was a terrible child. A polite, well-behaved terrible child, but terrible nonetheless. I’m sure you were a delight. Though, having taught at secondary level for so long, I have a sneaking suspicion children are  always  terrible. It’s just a matter of how effectively they hide it. That’s probably true. Speaking of school, how are you finding retirement, Mary? You always seemed so…dedicated to your teaching. Is it a big adjustment? It is, it really is. I miss the routine, I miss the…the mental stimulation. Though, honestly, not marking essays. Definitely not marking essays. I'm trying to fill my time. Volunteering at the library, pottery classes... I even considered learning to drive again! Drive? You gave that up years ago! Remember that near-miss at Luton Airport? That was… memorable. Don’t remind me. It was a terrifying experience. It put me off airports, too, for ages. And driving. Mostly driving. But I think I could manage now. Just local trips, mind you. Not attempting Luton again. Maybe a good way to get back into it would be shorter trips, like visiting us?

…and honestly, I couldn’t believe it when PC Davies rang this morning. He said they’d found it! No way! Seriously? Where was it? Down by the harbour, apparently. Leaning against one of the old warehouses. He said a couple of teenagers were trying to ride off on it, but a passerby recognised it from the police report and stopped them. Oh my gosh, that's amazing! Is it okay? Is it all…broken? A little scuffed, mostly. The lock was completely wrecked, obviously. And the gear cable’s a bit bent, but nothing major. They’ve given it a once-over at the station, and said it's rideable. I’m going to take it to Mr. Henderson at the bike shop later, just to get him to check it properly. That’s such a relief. I was so gutted when it went. I mean, I know it’s just a bike, but… it was the one I used to cycle to Willow’s, and to college, you know? I know, darling. And you’ve been having to get the bus, which is a nightmare with the timetable changes. Speaking of college, how are things going? Any drama? Ugh, drama central. Chloe’s convinced Ben likes her, but he literally just asked her for a pen yesterday. She's posting cryptic stuff on TikTok all day - it's embarrassing! Oh teenagers. It’s always something. Honestly, social media is a minefield. I don't understand half of it. It's just… everyone needs to know everything all the time. And if you’re not posting, you don’t exist, apparently. Well, you certainly exist to  me . Anyway, I’m making lasagne tonight. Your favourite! Are you still hungry after college? Always! Lasagne sounds amazing. Did you get that new pesto for it? The one with the pine nuts? I did! It’s lovely. I even managed to get some decent mozzarella. Oh, and I picked up those little chocolate biscuits you like with your hot chocolate. You’re the best, Mum! Honestly. I can’t wait to get back on my bike now, though. Maybe cycle down to the beach tomorrow, if the weather's nice. That sounds lovely. Just be careful, alright? And maybe stick to cycling with a friend. I still get worried about you going on your own. I will, promise. I’ll go with Willow.

Right, okay, so I think I’m going to try and get from Plymouth to… oh, hang on. Bristol. Yes! Bristol. Bold move. That’s a long way with those little train bits. Is that a grey one? You need a grey one, don’t you? You need two grey ones, actually, if you want to go all the way. Unless you want to stop in Exeter, which no one does. Okay, okay. Two grey ones. I just… I really want to get rid of these pinks. They’re mocking me. Pink is the colour of ambition, my dear. Don’t underestimate the power of pink. Especially in Ticket to Ride. Ooh, I nearly completed my route! Just need a yellow bit from… oh, blast. Someone’s already taken it. Typical. That’ll be me. Needed it for my connection to Cardiff. Strategery, you see. Strategery? Is that even a word? It is now. It’s Welsh for… well, it doesn’t really  mean  anything. But it sounds good, doesn’t it? It sounds like something you’d say while building a ridiculously complicated Lego castle. Speaking of complicated, did anyone see that documentary about the Flying Scotsman? Fascinating bit of engineering. The thermodynamics alone… absolutely astounding. Oh, trains. Lovely. Can we talk about the lemon drizzle cake again instead? Because I'm rather craving it. It  was  good. I think I had three slices. Don’t tell anyone, but I may have snuck a bit before dinner too. Don’t worry, your secret’s safe with me. Though, I did see the crumbs… Honestly, you two. It’s a holiday. Eat cake! What’s the point of rationing lemon drizzle? It’s a fundamental violation of human rights. Exactly! It’s self-care. And I need all the self-care I can get, considering my entire train network is currently being sabotaged by pinks and yellows. You know, the early steam trains didn't have nearly the sophisticated braking systems we have now. A runaway train was a very real danger. Imagine the chaos! Chaos is basically what's happening on this board right now. It’s a railway war zone. Hold on a minute… if I take this green route… yes! That connects me to Manchester! Take  that , Rhys! You fiend! You’ve cut me off! Okay, I’m officially abandoning the Bristol route. I'm going for… Aberdeen!

Right, your go. Honestly, this game is taking  ages . I feel like we've been building this railway for hours. It is a bit of a marathon, isn’t it? But that’s Ticket to Ride, isn’t it? Slow burn, strategic… unlike, say, Codenames, which is just pure frantic energy. Oh, massively. Codenames feels like a pub quiz, but with more shouting and potential for accidental international incidents. Speaking of pubs… your mum keeps offering me sherry. That’s Mum. Sherry is her default setting for hospitality. It's like a reflex. She probably thinks we’re insufficiently hydrated. I think she’s worried I don’t appreciate a good sherry. She gave me a whole lecture on the nuances of different amontillados. I just nodded and pretended to understand. I can barely tell the difference between sherry and white wine, let alone the  nuances . You handled that brilliantly. She’ll test you again though, you know. This is a cultural immersion course disguised as a weekend at her house. It’s all about learning the Norfolk ways. The Norfolk ways being polite acceptance of fortified wine? And a healthy skepticism towards anyone who doesn’t think Cromer crabs are the best thing in the world. And a deep, abiding love for Alan Partridge. Okay, point taken. It’s… different, isn't it? It's a very gentle pace of life here. London feels utterly manic in comparison. Everyone rushing around, clutching coffees… it's exhausting just thinking about it. It is. And it’s not just the speed. It’s the  drinking  culture too. In London, it’s very… performative. ‘Let’s go for cocktails!’ ‘Let’s find a trendy wine bar!’ It’s about being  seen  drinking. Exactly! Here, it's… functional? A pint at the local after work, or sherry with your mum. It's less about the experience, and more about… just being. Precisely. And it’s definitely less about Instagramming it. Mum would actively frown if you tried to take a picture of her sherry. Right, I’m connecting Bristol to… oh, someone's already got that route! Typical. You’re building towards Edinburgh, aren't you? Maybe. Or maybe I'm just strategically blocking you. It's all part of the game. Speaking of games, you know, my brother’s getting really into Dungeons and Dragons. Oh, really? That's... a commitment. I always found the whole thing a bit overwhelming, all the character sheets and dice.

Honestly, this lasagne is divine, Kerrie. You’ve outdone yourself. It is really good. What's the secret? More cheese? Always more cheese, right? It's a proper béchamel sauce, that's the key. None of that ready-made stuff. Takes time, mind, but it’s worth it. Reminds me of my Nain’s, she made a béchamel like nobody’s business. Ooh, family recipes are the best. I’m trying to get into making more things from scratch, but it feels… daunting. Moving house has completely thrown my cooking routine. Tell me about it. Boxes everywhere, trying to figure out where everything  goes . It's chaos. Did you manage to sort the white goods situation yet? You were saying the washing machine was on the blink? Yeah, thankfully. Managed to find a decent second-hand one online. Saved a lot of money. Though, honestly, the delivery driver nearly gave me a heart attack trying to get it up the stairs. Oh, those delivery drivers! No spatial awareness whatsoever. Remember when Gareth's new fridge nearly took out the hallway wallpaper? He was mortified. Oh god, yes! That was a disaster. Speaking of disasters, have you had any luck with the bins at the new place? I remember you were saying the collection schedule was completely different. It's…a learning curve. It's a fortnightly collection, which is fine, but they're incredibly strict about what goes in each bin. I accidentally put a yogurt pot in the wrong one and got a sticker on it. A sticker! Oh, they're all like that now, aren’t they? So fussy. It’s all about meeting targets, you know. They wouldn't understand a bit of common sense if it slapped them in the face. I swear, council workers these days… It’s all a bit much. You’d think after paying council tax, they’d just take  anything  we throw at them. Anyway, enough complaining about bins. How’s the furniture coming together? Found any treasures in charity shops yet? Found a lovely little bookcase! Perfect for the living room. Needs a bit of sanding and painting, but it's a project. I’m thinking a nice teal colour. Honestly, I'm craving a bit of a crafty outlet after all this unpacking. I used to do a lot of cross-stitch. Oh, I love cross-stitch! My sister used to make the most beautiful samplers.

Honestly, this traffic is mental. Like, what’s even  happening  up ahead? It's barely moving. It’s always like this heading towards Finchley, isn't it? Especially around this time. People trying to get the kids, I suppose. Though honestly, it’s a bit early for the school rush, isn't it? Yeah, you’d think so. It’s not even half past four. Seriously though, I’m starting to regret offering to drive. Don’t be silly. You're a good lad for offering. And frankly, I’d rather not attempt a manoeuvre in this mess. You’re much more…composed behind the wheel. Unlike your father. Oh god, Dad. Road rage incarnate. Remember that time in France? The horn, the shouting… Oh, don’t remind me. The poor French driver looked absolutely terrified. He didn’t understand a word your father was saying, of course, but the  tone  was quite sufficient. It was horrifying  and  hilarious. It was a disaster. He insists he was perfectly reasonable. Reasonable? He was practically apoplectic! Anyway, how are things going with the dissertation? Still on the… what was it? The post-structuralist deconstruction of online fan fiction? Don’t remind me. It’s…progressing. Slowly. I’m starting to think I’ve bitten off more than I can chew. It feels so… niche. Nonsense. It sounds fascinating. And rather contemporary, which is good. Though I must admit, I find it hard to keep up with all this digital stuff. I still firmly believe there’s nothing quite like holding a book in your hands. You and everyone at the TLS, Mum. Still battling the good fight against ebooks, I see. Of course! Although, even  we’re  having to acknowledge the shift. Circulation’s still good, thankfully, but it’s… different. More focus on online content, reviews streamed through podcasts… it’s all changing so quickly. It’s inevitable, isn’t it? It’s just… sad, in a way. Feels like something’s being lost. Perhaps. Though new things are gained, too. It just requires adaptation, that’s all. Speaking of gaining, have you thought any more about what you want for your birthday? Your aunt Susan asked. Ugh, Aunt Susan. Always asking. Honestly, I don’t need anything. Just…a quiet evening, maybe. She’ll insist. She always does. You know what she got your cousin last year? A hand-knitted tea cosy.

Right, so then the seagull – and I swear it was  massive , like a proper, prehistoric-looking thing – swoops down and just  snatches  the chips right out of little Timmy’s hand. No way! Little Timmy? Proper bawling, was he? Bawling is an understatement! Full meltdown. Screaming, kicking, the lot. His mum was mortified, trying to explain it was just a bird. Like Timmy gives a toss it's “just a bird” when his chips are gone! Serves him right for being a show-off with his massive portion. You know he was bragging about how much ketchup he’d gotten? Oh, classic Timmy. Always gotta one-up everyone. Reminds me of when we were kids, trying to build the biggest sandcastle… And Liam always had to make his the tallest, even if it meant risking collapse. Remember the tide coming in and washing it away just as he was adding the final turret? Ha! He was fuming. Absolutely fuming. Head went down, stomped off like a little moody teenager. He was about eight! Oh God, the tantrums. We were monsters. But honestly, Blackpool was chaos. It’s just…peak holiday vibes. Sticky floors, screaming kids, overpriced arcades. It's the best though, isn’t it? Like, intentionally awful. You  expect  it to be a bit rubbish but you still have a laugh. Totally. I think my highlight was the donkey rides. They looked so miserable. Like they were actively plotting their revenge. They probably were. I saw one trying to bite a kid. Gently, but still. A warning. Don’t get me started on the arcade games. Spent about twenty quid trying to win a fluffy unicorn for my little cousin and came away with a plastic ring and a sense of utter failure. Oh, the claw machines are rigged. Absolute con. They just  taunt  you. Like, “Oh, you almost got it! Try again! Lose more money!” My mum is convinced she's a master of the claw machine. She'll spend ages studying the technique, trying to calculate the perfect angle...and still come away empty-handed. She’s dedicated, though! You gotta admire the commitment. Speaking of commitment, did anyone see that bloke trying to eat a whole pizza on the promenade? No way! Was he winning? Barely. He was sweating, struggling, trying not to drop a slice. It was a spectacle. Honestly, I think he regretted it halfway through.

…and honestly, the silence. You wouldn’t believe the silence. Not a mechanical hum, not a car engine, not a distant lawnmower. Just…nothing. Except the wind, of course. That’s always  something  in the Highlands in January. Sounds… intense. I mean, I enjoy a bit of peace and quiet as much as the next person, but completely cut off? Doesn’t it get a bit… lonely? It’s a different kind of lonely, Mum. It’s not the lonely you get sitting in your flat on a Saturday night. It’s a sort of… expansive loneliness. You feel incredibly small, in the best possible way. Connected to something much bigger. Exactly, Hamish. It recalibrates you. Everything feels… unnecessary. All the worries and the to-do lists just sort of fade away when you’re battling hypothermia and trying to get a fire going. Puts things in perspective, doesn’t it? Hypothermia? Good heavens, George! That sounds actively dangerous. Is it even  legal  to just… camp anywhere in the winter? Legal, yes. Sensible, debatable. Scotland has fantastic access rights, you know. “Right to Roam.” As long as you’re responsible - leave no trace, respect the land - you can camp pretty much anywhere. We’ve got a pretty robust system for responsible wild camping, aye. It’s ingrained in the culture. But Dad’s downplaying the challenge a bit. It's not just battling hypothermia, it’s the sheer planning involved. Gear selection is crucial. You need a tent that can withstand seventy-mile-an-hour winds, a sleeping bag rated to -20, and enough food to fuel a small army. Seventy mile an hour winds! My goodness. And you  enjoy  this? What’s the appeal? Besides proving you’re tougher than everyone else, George? It’s not about toughness, Elsie. It’s about simplicity. Stripping everything back to the basics. It's about being self-reliant. Relying on your skills, your knowledge, your equipment… and a good head for navigation. And it’s stunningly beautiful. The winter landscape up there is breathtaking. The snow-covered mountains, the frozen lochs… It’s a different world. And there's something deeply meditative about it. It forces you to be present. You’re completely focused on the task at hand – staying warm, finding water, making camp. There’s no room for multitasking or dwelling on things you can't control. I suppose I can see that.

Aye, honestly, the pacing was just…off. Like, it started strong, really strong, but then it just  meandered  for a good hour. And for a two-and-a-half-hour film, you can't afford to meander. I get what you mean. It felt like they had a really good concept, and then just didn't quite know what to  do  with it. Too many subplots, maybe? I thought the cinematography was excellent, though. Really moody. Oh, the visuals were stunning, definitely. But pretty pictures don't save a rubbish story, do they? It reminded me a bit of… have you ever read ‘The Name of the Rose’ by Umberto Eco? Eco? Vaguely. Isn't that the medieval mystery one? Aye, that’s the one. It’s brilliant, proper head-scratcher. But the film adaptation was… like, they took all the atmosphere and intellectual heft out of it and just left the basic plot. This film felt similar. All style, no substance. That's a good analogy, actually. I can see that. It felt like they were trying to be clever, but ended up just being… convoluted. You know? Exactly! It’s like they were showing off, saying “Look how artsy we are!” instead of, you know, telling a good story. And then the ending. Don’t even get me started on the ending. I thought the ending was… anticlimactic, shall we say? Like, after all that build-up, it just fizzled out. Fizzled is a good word. Like a damp squib. It was meant to be this big, profound revelation, and it was just… nothing. Actually, it made me fancy a curry. All this talk of disappointment’s making me hungry. Curry? Now  that’s  a good idea. I’m starving. Do you fancy Indian or Thai? Ooh, difficult. Indian. Definitely Indian. Proper, spicy, vindaloo kind of Indian. None of this korma nonsense. Agreed. Vindaloo it is. There’s that place near the station, ‘Spice Delight’… they do a pretty decent one. Aye, Spice Delight. Solid choice. Gets the job done. It’s just… sometimes I wish they’d have a bit more, you know, imagination with their presentation. It's always just plonked on the plate. Ha! You're applying the ‘film ending’ critique to curry presentation now? Well, why not? Everything deserves a bit of artistry, doesn’t it? Even a vindaloo. I hope this captures the requested tone and context!

Right, so then the giant… he didn’t actually  eat  anyone, did he, in the story? He just… stomped around a lot and made everyone really cross? He stomped on their houses! And then the little girl… she had to trick him! With the beans! Magic beans! Exactly! Magic beans. Now, do you remember what the Brownie promise is? We talked about it last night. To do a good turn every day! And to be truthful! And… and… helpful! Brilliant! You’re both amazing. See, stories are full of promises, aren't they? Like the giant  should  have promised not to stomp on houses… but he didn't. He was a naughty giant. Can I play PlayStation now? Pleeeease? After a little bit more chat, maybe. I was thinking about work today, and it’s funny how much everything is like a giant computer now. Even just… making a list. Remember when people used to use typewriters? What’s a typewriter? It’s… well, it’s like a very old computer keyboard. You hit the letters and it prints them onto paper. No screens, no deleting. You had to be  really  careful. Sounds boring. Can you delete things on a PlayStation? Oh, absolutely. You can delete whole worlds if you want to! That's the beauty of computers. Everything is changeable. I had to use Excel all day at work, making spreadsheets. It’s… well, it’s a bit like building with Lego, actually. Little blocks of information. I built a spaceship with my Lego today! It had lasers! Pew pew! Mine’s a car! A really fast car! It can go vroom vroom! That sounds amazing. Excel isn’t quite as exciting as Lego spaceships or fast cars, though. It’s more… organising things. Like when you organise your toys. I don't  like  organising my toys. No, me neither. It’s a bit like that. It’s much more fun to build spaceships. You know, sometimes I wonder if stories are a bit like spreadsheets too. You have characters – those are your little blocks of information, and the plot is how you organise them to make something interesting. That’s a really weird way to think about stories. Can we play now? Please? Alright, alright. Ten more minutes of talking, then PlayStation time. Let’s just finish talking about the giant. What do you think happened to him after the little girl tricked him?

Honestly, look at you. You look like you’ve slept in your clothes. Not that I’m one to talk, I’ve probably got a jam stain somewhere, but… Well, I got up early to avoid the worst of the roadworks on the way over. Didn’t have time for proper presentation. Besides, it’s just you. And I’m comfortable. Though I did nearly trip over the cat in the dark trying to find my slippers. Roadworks, aye. They’re a permanent feature of Bradford life, aren’t they? Seems like they’re always digging something up. I swear they just put a road down then decide it needs ‘improving’ a week later. More like a permanent obstruction. Did you have a good breakfast? I made the porridge, though it’s not quite as good as Mum used to make. Porridge was lovely, thank you. Much needed after that near-disaster with Winston. Though I’m a bit of a fruit and yoghurt man myself, usually. Reminds me, we passed a really decent fruit farm on the way, just outside Ilkley. Proper pick-your-own strawberries and raspberries. We should go sometime. Oh, now that sounds nice. Fresh raspberries… Mmm. Though I’m reading this fascinating article about deserted medieval villages in Yorkshire. Did you know there are hundreds of them? Entire communities just… vanished. Apparently, some were due to the Black Death, others to economic hardship. Extraordinary, isn't it? It makes you think about how fragile things are. Speaking of things disappearing, any news on the house sale? Still getting bombarded with junk mail addressed to the previous owners, I bet. Oh, don't even  start  me on the junk mail. It’s relentless. And yes, the sale is… progressing. Slow progress. The solicitor is dragging her heels, apparently. Says there's a query with the land registry. Honestly, it feels like it's been on the market for years. But the estate agent is optimistic. Which, considering they get paid commission, is reassuring… slightly. Optimistic estate agents – a classic combination. Still, good to hear it’s moving forward. I’ve been meaning to ask, how are your herbs doing? You were saying you were trying to grow basil and rosemary. They're… surviving. The basil’s a bit temperamental. I think I overwatered it. The rosemary seems happy enough, though. I’m hoping to make some pesto later.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from Christmas. The sheer volume of chocolate… I think my blood is mostly cocoa now. Tell me about it. I’m pretty sure I gained half a stone just from Quality Street. Though your sister's homemade fudge was worth every single calorie, mind you. Oh, the fudge  was  incredible! I was trying to be good, but… hopeless. Did anyone else get bombarded with Christmas photos on Facebook? My feed was just a relentless stream of posed families and perfectly decorated trees. Ugh, don’t even. I briefly scrolled through, then just muted everyone for a week. It’s exhausting. My aunt Brenda posted seventeen photos of her new cat wearing a Santa hat. Brenda and her cat. Always a highlight. Speaking of animals, how’s Winston doing? Still convinced he's a lapdog the size of a small pony? He is! He tries to sit on your lap, honestly. You’d need a structural engineer to assess the load-bearing capacity of the sofa. He’s been shedding like crazy, though. I’m thinking of investing in a hazmat suit just to vacuum the living room. Sounds about right. I swear, owning a dog is just constant fur maintenance. It’s a full-time job in itself. Reminds me of old Barnaby, the Labrador we had when I was a kid. Shedded enough fur to knit another dog. Still, worth it for the companionship. Absolutely. So, New Year’s Eve? Did you two manage to stay awake until midnight? We gave it a go. I think we made it to about ten past eleven, then succumbed to the lure of the comfy chairs and a documentary about penguins. Penguins sound far more appealing than a crowded pub, to be honest. I went to a little gathering at a friend’s place. It was nice, but my phone died halfway through, so I spent the rest of the evening feeling utterly disconnected. Oh, the horror! It's like being stranded without a map. Speaking of maps, are you still going to Spain in March? I’m trying to remember which village you were saying you wanted to visit. It had a terribly unpronounceable name. Ronda, it’s called Ronda. Beautiful place. It's up in the mountains. And yes, the plan is still on, thankfully. I’ve been trying to brush up on my Spanish, though I'm pretty sure I’ll just end up pointing and miming my way through everything.

Honestly, the commute was  brutal  this morning. Packed like sardines, and someone was playing incredibly loud music from their phone. No headphones, obviously. Ugh, the worst. I’m so glad I can mostly work from home now. Though honestly, even that's been a bit stressful lately. This survey programming is… a special kind of headache. Oh yeah? What’s going on with it? Still having issues with the coding? No, the coding’s okay, it’s more the  questions . They keep asking me to re-word things because the initial results are… skewed. Apparently, asking people 'Do you feel safe walking alone at night?' yields different results than 'How concerned are you about your personal safety when walking alone at night?' It's infuriating! Like, people know what you're getting at. That’s… ridiculous. Bureaucracy at its finest. Sounds like classic survey stuff, though. I’m dealing with a different kind of headache. My boss wants me to write copy for this new energy drink, and it’s just… awful. Like, aggressively marketed towards teenage boys awful. I feel so slimy even thinking about it. Oh no. What's so bad about it? Everything! The tagline is “Unleash Your Beast,” and the whole campaign is built around this idea of… primal energy. It’s just so… performative masculinity. And they want me to make it sound  cool . Ugh. That sounds awful. You should just refuse. I wish I could! I need the money, you know? Rent’s ridiculous, even with sharing. How are you managing, being a student and all? Your parents still helping much? They’re helping a bit, but I’m trying to be as independent as possible. Part-time work and a loan, mostly. But it’s tight. I keep looking at flatshares further out, but then the commute nightmare looms again. Did you see that article about house prices in London? Apparently, the average deposit is now… something obscene. Don’t even get me started! I swear, owning a place here is just a pipe dream. My mum keeps saying we should all move back to Kent, but… no thanks. I love being in London, even with all its flaws. Plus, my nan would never forgive me if I left. She’s convinced I’m living the glamorous city life. Haha! My mum’s the same. She thinks I’m constantly at swanky parties and debating philosophy with intellectuals.

Honestly, I’m feeling so sluggish. I really need to get back into a routine with the walking. It’s just… getting started is the hardest bit, isn’t it? Especially when it’s grey and drizzly. Tell me about it. I keep  saying  I’ll go for a run, but then I look out the window and convince myself the washing machine needs emptying instead. It's a classic avoidance tactic. You two are hopeless! You need to just force yourselves. I went for a decent hike on Saturday, up near Box Hill. Felt amazing afterwards. Though my knees did complain a bit on the way down. Box Hill! That’s… ambitious. I'm aiming for a gentle stroll around the park to begin with. Honestly, I think I've forgotten how to properly exercise. It's all been sitting at this desk, transcribing legal jargon for the last year. Speaking of desks and sitting, I was looking at house prices again last night. Don't ask me why. It’s a terrible habit. Oh, don't start. It'll just depress us all. I know, I know. But seriously, even a tiny little terrace house in Guildford now is… ridiculous. It’s gotten so out of hand. Remember when you could get a decent place for under two hundred thousand? Vaguely. That feels like a different lifetime. Even around here, everything is just astronomical. You’d need a lottery win to afford anything decent. It’s the London commuter belt effect, isn't it? Everyone wants to be within reach of the city. Drives the prices up everywhere. I was reading an article about people moving to… well, practically Wales, to afford a house. Wales sounds nice, actually. Though a long commute. Maybe I should just commit to becoming a tiny house enthusiast. Now there’s an idea. Though wouldn’t that get cramped? Especially with all your books. It would. Speaking of cramped, I'm trying a new recipe tonight. Moroccan tagine. I hope I've got enough space in my biggest pot. It's a bit of a faff, lots of ingredients. Ooh, that sounds lovely! I’ve been sticking to really simple stuff lately – pasta, stir-fries. I just can’t be bothered with complicated cooking when I’m tired. I’m on pasta duty tonight too. Just a quick tomato and basil sauce. Can’t beat a classic, right?

Honestly, this weather is a blessing. Last week I was convinced Cambridge was permanently grey. Needed a bit of sunshine after that Budget announcement, mind you. Tell me about it. It was… underwhelming, wasn’t it? All a bit of rearranging the deckchairs, wasn't it? I was hoping for something a bit more substantial for young professionals, you know, maybe some help with… well, everything. Houses, student loan repayments… Exactly! Felt like they were patting us on the head and saying "there there, things will  eventually  get better." Still, it’s Corpus life, isn’t it? Surrounded by centuries of financial stability, slightly detached from the real world. How’s the engineering world treating you, anyway? Still battling with concrete and…bridges? Sadly, yes. Currently wrestling with a drainage scheme in Peterborough. It's… exhilarating. Mostly it’s just a lot of paperwork and trying to convince people that slightly more expensive materials are a good investment. It's horrifying the amount of money they try to save on stuff that's going to cause problems down the line. Sounds stressful. Better than dealing with academics and their grant applications, though. Seriously, the hoops they make you jump through… You’d think they were applying to NASA. I can imagine. So, any interesting dramas at Corpus lately? Spill the tea. Oh, there's always something. Old Professor Armitage is still convinced the students are deliberately sabotaging his research. He’s blaming it on a poltergeist. A poltergeist? Really? Swears it. Says books are falling off shelves and his tea goes cold prematurely. Honestly, I think he just forgets where he puts things. But, on a lighter note, did you catch Wicked in London last month? Wicked! Yes! Absolutely loved it. The staging was incredible, wasn't it? And the music… I had ‘Defying Gravity’ stuck in my head for a week. Same! It's just  such  a good show. I’m tempted to go again. I've always been a sucker for a good musical. Although, my last theatre trip was a disaster. Went to see a modern adaptation of Hamlet and it involved interpretive dance… a lot of interpretive dance. Oh, dear. That sounds… challenging. Sometimes sticking to the classics is the best bet. Are you thinking of seeing anything else soon? They've got Hamilton touring again, haven’t they? Oh, Hamilton… Tempting. But the prices are ridiculous.

Right, that’s the fence done. Feels a bit… brighter, doesn’t it? Less depressing grey. Definitely. Needed doin', that. Been lookin’ at it for months, you have. I tell ya, you’re a proper artist with a brush, lad. Not bad for a lecturer, eh? Well, I’ve had practice. My grandfather was a painter, back in Germany. Proper landscapes, all oil paints and the works. I tried it once, couldn’t get the hang of it. Too much patience required, I think. Give me a good novel anyday. See, I always fancied learnin’ to paint. Just little things, y'know? Like the docks at sunset. Always thought that’d make a good picture. Never got round to it though. Too busy drivin’ around, pickin’ people up and droppin’ ‘em off. You should. It’s good for the soul, creative stuff. Though I imagine your job provides enough stories. You must see everything from the front seat of that cab. Oh, unbelievable stuff. Last night, picked up a bloke dressed as Batman. Proper suit and everything. Said he was goin’ to a kids’ party. Now  that  was a sight. Thinkin’ about tryin’ to get a picture, but didn’t want to be rude. No, better not. Though ironically, I was just talking about films with one of my students. We were discussing method acting. Apparently, some actors really  become  their characters. Method actin’, eh? Sounds a bit mental to me. I mean, you’re gettin’ paid to pretend, aren’t ya? No need to actually  be  someone else. Unless you’re one o’ them proper Hollywood types, I suppose. Exactly. Though it can be quite effective, I suppose. Speaking of which, did you ever see that local production of ‘Hamlet’ down at the Everyman a few years back? Proper good, it was. That fella, Liam, he was brilliant. Liam… aye, the one who used to work at the chippy? Didn’t know he could act. Good on him. Still, I’d rather spend me tenner on a decent second-hand record than a theatre ticket. Found a mint condition Elvis album last week at the car boot sale. Bargain. Nice one! I’m always on the lookout for old books. Found a first edition of ‘Wuthering Heights’ a while ago. Cost a pretty penny, but worth it. See, I’m trying to get me a shed. Back garden’s lookin’ a right mess.

Honestly, this scenery is just… relentless. Beautiful, obviously, but just field after field of… well, fields. Reminds me a bit of Norfolk, actually, just a bit more…Polish. Relentless is a good word for it. Though I’m starting to appreciate the sheer scale of it all. It’s so different from back home, isn’t it? Everything feels…bigger. And flatter, generally. Definitely flatter. Although the bit near Zakopane was stunning. Really stunning. Makes you feel tiny, those mountains. Speaking of which, are we still on track for Tarnow this evening? I checked the satnav, but it’s always good to double check. Yep, still aiming for Tarnow. Should get there around six, give or take. I booked us a spot at that campsite near the Old Town, the one with the decent reviews. Hopefully, it’s not too busy. Good thinking. And have you been keeping a rough tally of the expenses? I’m a bit rubbish with the finances, you know that. I just…lose track. Yeah, I’ve got a spreadsheet going. Fuel's not been too bad, actually, surprisingly. It’s the tolls that are adding up. And the pierogi. We’ve definitely had a lot of pierogi. One cannot  have  too much pierogi! Seriously though, thanks for managing all that. It’s really taken the stress off. No worries at all. That’s what friends are for, isn’t it? So, any news from back home? Has Sarah sorted out her house move yet? She’s still battling with the estate agent, apparently. It’s a nightmare, honestly. She’s trying to declutter, which, knowing Sarah, is a Herculean task. She keeps finding “sentimental” things from uni. Sounds about right. I’m trying to get better at that myself, you know? This trip is actually forcing me to. You can't really travel light when you’re living in a campervan, so you have to be ruthless. It’s surprisingly liberating, though. I can imagine. I’m a terrible hoarder. I’ve got boxes of old papers and books… things I  might  need someday. It's ridiculous. Oh, I completely get that. My mum's the same. Attics full of “just in case” items. Have you seen any hitchhikers? I was thinking about it earlier, it feels like you don’t see them anymore. Not yet, thankfully. I’m not sure I’d be brave enough to pick anyone up, to be honest.

Right, just off the M55 at Junction 1 then, yeah? Should be straightforward enough. Though Preston traffic can be a nightmare, even on a Tuesday. Ugh, tell me about it. Honestly, I’m stressing about getting to the library before it closes. Need to hand in that English essay. It’s… not great. You’ll be fine, darling. You always worry too much. Remember that story you wrote last term, the one about the girl and the lighthouse? That was beautiful. That was ages ago. This one’s about  Othello  and… I just don’t get it. It’s all jealousy and manipulation. Depressing. Shakespeare, eh? Always a tough one. I never understood half of it when I was at school. Still don't, probably. More of a football man meself. Speaking of depressing, did you see the news about the train strikes again? Honestly, it’s making everything so difficult. I wanted to visit my sister in London next month, but… Don't even get me started on the trains. They’re a joke, an absolute joke. Used to be able to rely on them, now it’s a lottery. Costs a fortune too. Yeah, and it's awful for people who actually  need  to travel. Like, for work. Or exams! Actually, that reminds me - how are your revision going, sweetie? Any idea what you want to do after your A-Levels? I think I want to apply for Lancaster. It's not too far, and they have a good creative writing course. But it depends. My history grade is… questionable. Lancaster’s a good shout. Nice place. Though a bit pricey, if I remember right when we were looking for places for your cousin, wasn't it? It was. But a good education is worth investing in, isn’t it? We can worry about the finances later. Oh! Look, a Sainsbury’s. Do we need anything? I’m almost out of almond milk. Oh yeah, can we get some of those chocolate digestives too? The fancy ones, with the dark chocolate? I need brain food. Chocolate digestives? Always. Can't go wrong with a digestive. Though I prefer a good ginger nut, meself. You and your ginger nuts, George. They’re your lifeline. Remember when you were trying to stop smoking, you replaced every cigarette with a ginger nut? Don’t remind me! Put a stone on, I did.

Honestly, I thought you'd forgotten about us entirely! Didn’t realise you were even back in the country. Oh, don’t be daft, love. I wouldn’t forget you two. Just… a little spontaneous, that's all. Needed a bit of a change of scenery after dealing with that solicitor, and Thirsk seemed… peaceful. Plus, I knew young’un here would be thrilled. Didn't want to give you too much warning - you’d start fussing. Grandma! You’re actually here! Did you bring any sweets? Now, now, young man. Straight to the point, are we? There  might  be a tin of biscuits in my bag. But first, tell me how school is going. Still glued to that… that glowing rectangle? It's a phone, Grandma. And yeah, kinda. We’re doing this project on coding, it's actually pretty cool. Coding? That’s good. It’s the future, isn’t it? Though I still struggle to work the telly remote sometimes. Honestly, all this technology…it’s a bit overwhelming. Overwhelming is putting it mildly. All this ‘AI’ they’re going on about. Reminds me of that dreadful comedian, Jimmy Tarbuck, always going on about robots. Harmless enough, but the youngsters seem to think it's some kind of threat now. It’s not a  threat , Grandma, it’s just…powerful. It can write essays and everything. It's tempting, isn't it? Though I suspect Mr. Henderson would see right through it if I handed in an essay written by a computer. He’s got a nose for these things. Speaking of which, are you alright, Mum? You seem…quiet. Just thinking, love. About your Auntie Margaret, mainly. I was clearing out some old things this morning, and came across a box of her letters. Awful sad, really. Always such a bright spark and then… well. It's just a reminder, isn't it, how easily things can unravel? I know. It's horrible. She was such a lovely woman. It’s good you’re talking about it, though. Bottling it up won’t help. Was she ill? Like, really ill? Not physically, dear. It was…in her head. A darkness. They called it depression. It's dreadful to watch someone you love just…fade away. It makes you realise how fragile the mind is. It does. And it's important to remember that it  is  an illness, like any other.

Right, so, what do you reckon? Feels pretty snappy, doesn’t it? This Ryzen 7 is actually doing something for once. It’s…a laptop. It’s black. It turns on. Progress. Seriously though, yeah, it feels quick. Much better than that dinosaur you were lugging around before, the one that sounded like a jet engine taking off. You’re not wrong there. Remember when you tried to run that old racing game on it? Nearly melted the desk. Don’t remind me. That was a disaster. This one actually runs it on medium settings, no problem. I’ve also got all my photo editing software downloaded. No more waiting ten minutes to export a single image. Good. 'Cause your patience wearing thin is not a pretty sight. Speaking of software, have you done a full virus scan yet? You’re always downloading stuff from… questionable sources. I’ve got a good ad blocker and antivirus, alright? Relax. I'm not just clicking on everything that pops up offering free VPNs. Though, I did find this amazing YouTube channel dedicated to building PCs out of Lego… Lego? Seriously? You and your YouTube rabbit holes. You’ll be trying to build a fully functioning server farm out of Duplo next. Hey, don't knock it 'til you try it! It's actually pretty impressive engineering. Anyway, I was thinking - you two should both give it a go. What are you both up to this weekend? Maybe a hike up Dunstable Downs? I might be on tutor duty Saturday morning, prepping some lessons. Then… probably just collapsing into a heap. Teaching twelve-year-olds takes it out of you, you know? They’ve got unlimited energy and zero filter. Dunstable Downs sounds good to me though. Need to get some fresh air. Been stuck grafting in the garden all week, prepping Mrs. Henderson’s rose bushes. She wants them looking pristine for the village fete. Village fete… right. Sounds charming. I've been trying to get back into a bit of training, actually. Found this MMA gym over near the train station. It's…intense. MMA? You? Aren't you the guy who tripped over a rug last week? It was a particularly aggressive rug! And it’s good for fitness, okay? Plus, it’s a good way to de-stress. Better than, say, endlessly scrolling through TikTok. Speaking of endlessly scrolling... I saw on Facebook that Old Man Hemmings' cat went missing again.

Honestly, this place is lovely, isn’t it? Such a nice change from… well, everything else in Tarnow’s centre square. It was a bit grim before, wasn't it? Just that chipped statue and that slightly threatening souvenir stall. It  is  good. Really good. And the Pierogi are amazing. Seriously, best I’ve had since… well, since Grandma’s, probably. Though she’d kill me for saying that. She thinks hers are the only proper ones. Oh, well, that's grandmothers for you. Always the best cooks in the world, according to themselves. I’m just glad we found somewhere decent to sit and actually  talk . I feel like all our chats lately have been rushed phone calls whilst I’m trying to prep for some online lesson or you're rushing to catch a tram. Tell me about it. This teaching gig is…intense. The hours are crazy and the kids, bless 'em, are exhausting. Especially the ones who genuinely believe English is just a series of random sounds. It's rewarding, but… draining. It sounds it. Still, you're brilliant at it. You always were a natural with languages. Remember that summer we spent in Spain? You were practically fluent after a week. I was still struggling to ask for the bill. That’s because you were too busy trying to perfect your paella-ordering technique. You were determined to be a culinary expert even then! And it’s not fluency, honestly. It's just…picking things up. I think I’m better at mimicking sounds than actually  understanding  grammar. Don't sell yourself short. Anyway, how’s Mark? Still obsessing over his running? Last I heard, he was aiming for a sub-three-hour marathon. Oh,  always . It’s his life now, I swear. He's currently in a phase of meticulously tracking his electrolytes and complaining about shin splints. It’s… a lot. He’s really good at it though. Properly dedicated. I just wish he’d dedicate a bit of that energy to, I don't know, doing the washing up. Men and their hobbies. It’s a universal constant, I think. Speaking of dedication… I finally started that online course on addiction counselling. It's… heavy. Oh, wow. That's… a big step. Are you alright? That must be really triggering, thinking about… everything. It is. It’s definitely forcing me to confront a lot of stuff I’ve been actively avoiding for years.

Right, so I’ve been looking at tickets for the Dorset Steam Fair. They’re quite pricey, aren’t they? Especially for all of us. Pricey? It’s daylight robbery, that’s what it is! Used to be you could get in for a fiver, now it’s… what, nearly forty quid each? They’re taking the mickey. Still, it’s a good day out if the weather holds. It  is  a lot, but Dad really wants to go. And honestly, it’s nice to do something all together. Do they still have all those vintage tractors? Yeah, loads. And the showmen’s guild stuff. I was looking on their website, and they’ve apparently made a real effort with accessibility this year. Better pathways, disabled viewing platforms… About time too. Last time we went, I nearly broke my ankle trying to navigate that mud pit. They need to think about people with bad legs, you know? It’s not all young lads running around. That’s good to hear. Mum would really appreciate that. Remember when we tried to get her wheelchair onto that hill at the county show? Disaster. Absolutely. Speaking of things needing consideration… getting tickets sorted is one thing, but actually  getting  Mum and her chair there and around… it’s a logistical nightmare. We could ask Kevin to help. He’s got that big van, right? And he’s fairly strong, could lift the wheelchair if we need to. Good idea. I’ll give him a ring. It’s just… I’m starting to worry about Mum being further away from her routine. She gets so anxious when things change. I know, but a day out would do her good. Change of scenery, you know? We just need to be really careful and make sure she’s comfortable. She'll be alright. Honestly, she’s tougher than she looks. Remember when she chased that estate agent off the drive when he was trying to undervalue the house? Oh, don’t remind me! She was fierce! That estate agent never came back. It did make me think though… property prices around here are crazy, aren't they? Tell me about it. I was looking at flats in Bournemouth the other day, just to get an idea, and you’d need to win the lottery to afford anything decent. Bournemouth is a rip-off. Overpriced and overcrowded. Still, at least it’s near the sea.

Honestly, this weather is dreadful, isn’t it? Didn’t think we’d be back to this so quickly in April. Feels like February again. It’s a bit grim, isn't it? Though better than snow, I suppose. Remember that blizzard we had a few years back, just before Christmas? We were stranded for days. Were you really? That sounds cool! Did you build a snowman? Cool isn’t quite the word I’d use, lad. More… inconvenient. We were rationing biscuits and Dad was attempting to dig a path with a plastic spade. It wasn’t a pretty sight. Your father always was a bit optimistic with a spade. So, are we all settled for this evening? I was hoping we might go to that new artisan bakery in Northallerton. I hear they do a lovely sourdough. That sounds nice, Mum. Though young Thomas here has been moaning about needing to finish some project for school. Something involving Shakespeare, wasn't it? It’s a presentation on  Macbeth . It’s due tomorrow and I haven’t even started writing it! It’s so boring. All those witches and daggers… Now, now. Shakespeare isn’t boring. He’s timeless. Though I will concede  Macbeth  is a bit bleak. Have you thought about focusing on the psychological aspects, Thomas? The ambition, the guilt… I dunno. It just feels like a waste of time when nobody even reads it properly. Miss Davison will just skim it and give me a B. Oh, nonsense. You’re a bright boy, Thomas. You can do better than a B. Maybe a little encouragement is needed. Have you told your father about your worries? He’s been glued to Twitter all afternoon, complaining about some politician or other. Probably wouldn’t notice if you recited the entire play to him. It's a dangerous echo chamber, that Twitter. I try to avoid it whenever possible. Though, I must admit, it’s a good place to keep up with what’s happening locally. Did you hear about old Mr. Henderson shutting up shop? His haberdashery has been going for generations. Oh, no! That’s dreadful. Such a lovely man. And where will people go for decent buttons now? Everything’s online these days. It’s a disgrace. It feels like we’re losing all our little independent businesses. It's the same with the church, Mum. Attendance is dwindling.

Right, so dentist appointment for Cindy is booked for next Tuesday afternoon. Not ideal with school, but it was the only slot they had before half term. Oh. Can I still go to Ashaad’s party? We'll see, darling. We’ll have to see how long the appointment takes, and if you're feeling okay afterwards. It’s a long party isn’t it? Ashaad’s mum makes really good pizza. She does, doesn’t she? Very generous. Anyway, did you both remember to book in for your hearing tests? The school sent the letters home. Oh yeah! I did it online. It was really easy. I haven’t done it yet. Okay, you need to do that tonight, please Leo. It’s important. They just check everything is alright. It's not scary. Is it like at school? When we had to listen to the beeps? Exactly like that. Just a slightly more thorough version. Now, about your birthdays…it’s a bit mad having them so close together isn't it? Such a busy time. It’s good though! We get to have loads of cake. I want a Lego spaceship for my birthday. A really big one. A really big one, huh? We’ll see. We need to start thinking about what Cindy wants too. Any ideas? She likes Monet. All those paintings with the water lilies. She does. Perhaps a print would be nice. Or we could go somewhere that has a Monet exhibition? Can we have a party? A really big one with loads of friends? We’ll discuss that. Let’s focus on getting through this dentist appointment first. And then there's the school trip to the museum. Sounds good though, doesn’t it? Learning about history. Will there be a gift shop? Probably. Which always leads to requests for things you definitely don’t need! Now, I’m going to attempt to make a salad. Though I’m not sure Leo will approve. He’s not a big fan of vegetables. Radishes are disgusting. You don’t  have  to eat the radishes. But a little bit of green is good for you. Speaking of good for you, have you both finished your maths homework? Almost. Just a few more sums to do. I did mine! It was easy. Except the bit about… well, it was a bit tricky but I did it.

Honestly, I’ve been living off pesto pasta for three days. It’s a crisis. A genuine culinary crisis. You and your pesto pasta! You said the same thing last month. Just… go to the shop? Or, you know, let me cook for you? I made a massive chilli last week, there’s loads left. You are an angel. But the thought of  going  to the shop… it’s just…effort. Especially after work. And the chilli smells amazing, genuinely. I feel bad always letting you do all the cooking when I come round. Don’t be silly! I actually enjoy it. And honestly, your contribution is moral support and excellent gossip. Speaking of which, how’s the copywriting going? Still churning out ads for… what was it? Organic dog biscuits? Sadly, yes. Organic dog biscuits. It's creatively bankrupting me. Though, I did manage to sneak in a slightly subversive line about the biscuits being “paw-sitively delightful” which my boss loved, naturally. You wouldn't believe the meetings we have about dog biscuit slogans. Oh my god. I'm picturing it. Intense brainstorming sessions. My hospital is…insane right now. We’ve had a huge influx of stroke patients. It's emotionally draining, you know? Trying to help people re-learn how to speak…it's tough. That sounds incredibly hard. You’re amazing for doing it, honestly. It’s proper, important work. I just write about biscuits. Hey, someone’s gotta do it! And it funds our wine nights. Besides, you're good at it. Remember when we were kids and you wrote that whole play about the garden gnomes? Oh god, don’t remind me. It was horrific. Mrs. Peterson's gnome army taking over Ashford. Such drama. Mum still has photos, I think. It was peak cringe. No way! I remember! And old Mr. Henderson played the king gnome, didn't he? He was brilliant. He took it  so  seriously. He did! He had a full beard and everything. It was…ambitious. How are Mum and Dad doing? I haven’t spoken to them properly in ages. They're good. Mum’s started a pottery class. Apparently, she’s making some truly terrifying garden ornaments now. Revenge of the gnomes, maybe? Dad’s still obsessed with the allotment. He’s convinced he’s going to win the village show this year with his marrows. He’s been saying that for twenty years.

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of it! He just rocked up with a suitcase full of francs, handed it over, and the farmer just… accepted! No solicitors, no surveys, nothing. Just a handshake and a suitcase full of cash. Can you imagine trying that now? Absolutely not! You’d be arrested, probably. Though, it does sound rather… idyllic, doesn’t it? A bit like something out of a film. Speaking of films, have any of you been to the cinema lately? I tried to get tickets for that new Bergman retrospective, but it was completely sold out. Sold out? These things always are. I’ve found that if you just turn up an hour before, looking confident, they usually find you a seat. Works every time. It’s a sort of gentle…assertiveness, you see. Works for me too, old boy. Though, as a dentist, I was always rather good at getting my way with people. They weren’t exactly thrilled to be in my chair, but they tended to cooperate! Remember the old NHS perks? Sailing trips, for a start! Oh, the sailing! Goodness me, those were the days. Remember Dr. Henderson? Lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon! It sounded rather glamorous at the time, though I suspect it was mostly seasickness and lukewarm tea. Glamorous is one word for it. I’ve been looking at some rather more affordable trips, actually.
