Prague, for instance. Apparently, it’s remarkably cheap. Beautiful architecture, apparently. Though I wouldn't know, haven't been. Prague is lovely, yes. Though overrun with tourists, of course. It’s a shame what’s happened to some of these places. It’s much the same here, really, with the town. It used to be a thriving market town, remember? Thriving is an understatement! We had two proper butchers, a baker who made everything on the premises, and a haberdashery with a window display that put Harrods to shame. Then came the supermarket, and the ring road, and… well, you know the story. It was ruined, quite simply. And now they're trying to 'rebrand' it! As if a new logo and some hanging baskets will magically restore its former glory. Honestly! Though I do think the new plans for the barn are rather good. The jive event! Yes, I’m rather looking forward to that. Old Man Hemmings has really done wonders with the place.

Right, so we’re agreed – the gap in the market is definitely short-form video explainers. Specifically, aimed at undergrads struggling with core concepts. Absolutely. And not just ‘talking head’ style. I’m thinking animated, whiteboard style, maybe even some stop-motion. Something visually engaging. More TikTok than lecture capture. Exactly! The attention span…it’s diminishing exponentially. I was reading an article the other day about how the average TikTok video is now… what was it… eight seconds long? We need to grab them  fast . Eight seconds. Good grief. That’s less than the time it takes to explain the Krebs cycle. Which, incidentally, could be our first module. Biology 101. Universally painful. Perfect. And we focus on that initial impact – the ‘hook’. Punchy visuals, a question, a startling statistic. Then deliver the core concept in a digestible way. We could even gamify it – little quizzes at the end of each video. Ooh, gamification is good. We need to think about a brand though. Something approachable, not too academic. Not ‘LearnWithProfessorBoring’. Something…snappier. ‘ConceptCracked’? Too cheesy? A little. Hmm… ‘Unboxed Concepts’? ‘Core Clarity’? We could run some polls on Instagram. See what resonates. Honestly, social media is going to be key. We’ll need a strong presence. Consistent posting, engagement… I’m happy to manage the posting schedule and content calendar. You’re the content queen, though. You’ve got the teaching background, the curriculum expertise… I’m more the ideas guy, the ‘big picture’ strategist. Plus, I’m fairly adept at the editing side of things. I’ve been messing around with DaVinci Resolve during this house-sitting downtime. That’s brilliant! I can storyboard, write scripts, and actually explain the stuff in a way that doesn’t induce comas. But I’m hopeless with tech and I definitely don't have time to learn video editing on top of everything else. Have you thought about music licensing? That can be a nightmare. Yeah, figured we’d stick with royalty-free tracks to begin with. Epidemic Sound is pretty good. Or Artlist. We’ll have to budget for that, obviously. And consider the legal aspects – copyright, disclaimers… We should probably consult with someone on that. My cousin, David, he’s a solicitor specialising in intellectual property. I could ask him for a quick chat. That would be fantastic. Also, thinking about learning materials… it’s not just the videos, is it?

It’s just…remember when we all went to Brighton with Chloe and Mark? And Chloe was  convinced  she’d seen a mermaid? Oh god, yes. She was absolutely adamant. Said it had long, flowing red hair and a shimmering tail. She drew a whole sketch on a napkin. A very detailed sketch, I might add. Mark just kept trying to tell her it was probably a seal, but she wouldn’t have it. She said seals don’t wear tiaras. That’s classic Chloe. Always adding the fantastical element. I think she genuinely wanted to believe. It’s probably something to do with her grandmother’s stories, all those tales of selkies and sea spirits. You’re probably right. She was utterly captivated by the sea as a kid. Used to spend hours collecting shells on the Norfolk coast. Remember those awful holidays to Great Yarmouth? Awful is a strong word. Nostalgic, perhaps. Slightly sticky-floored arcades and questionable fish and chips, yes. But we had some good times. Remember trying to build that sandcastle that kept getting washed away by the tide? And then arguing about whose fault it was that it kept collapsing? You blamed me for building too close to the water’s edge. Well, you  were  ignoring my perfectly reasonable warnings. It was basic coastal engineering, really. You just wouldn’t listen. Basic? You were being a control freak! Honestly, everything’s a lesson with you. I just like things to be…structurally sound. Like our relationship. Needs a solid foundation, you know? Oh, you. Flattery will get you everywhere. Though, thinking about the sea…it’s funny how much it changes, isn’t it? From calm and glassy to wild and stormy. Reminds me a bit of…well, life. That’s… surprisingly profound. Coming from the queen of sarcastic comments. Hey! I have moments of deep introspection. It's just usually hidden beneath layers of cynicism. It’s probably a defence mechanism. Probably. You know, I wonder if Ethan and Sarah will ever get down to the coast. They're always so busy with work. They need a break. They’re both completely stressed. Ethan’s been talking about burnout for months. Maybe we should suggest a weekend away somewhere by the sea? Somewhere quiet. Good idea. Somewhere with no internet access. Force them to actually  talk  to each other. And maybe even  see  a mermaid.

Oh, honestly, look at what she’s wearing. That dress is… a choice. You’re being harsh! It’s a bit… bold, maybe, but it’s clearly intentional. It’s got that whole, like, maximalist vibe going on. I think it’s a bit much for daytime TV. It looks like she’s off to a premiere, not discussing gardening. Exactly! Who dresses like that to talk about begonias? And those shoes! They look like they’re made of plastic. They  are  plastic, I think. It’s that designer, Melissas, isn't it? They do all those quirky plastic shoes. They're surprisingly comfy, actually. I had a pair of red ones once. Comfy or not, they just look… cheap. I don’t get the appeal. Give me a good leather boot any day. I’m a sandal girl, myself. Though I’m definitely feeling a boot vibe for autumn. I saw these really nice Chelsea boots in John Lewis last week. A lovely dark burgundy. Ooh, burgundy’s good. Classy. I’ve been after a good trench coat for ages. Everything’s either too expensive or looks like something my grandma would wear. Oh, I know the feeling. I was looking for one last year, and it’s a nightmare. Everything’s either too short, too oversized, or the wrong colour. Have you tried vintage shops? You can sometimes find a really good one. I have, actually! No luck so far. I keep finding ones that are amazing material but the fit is all wrong. It’s like they were designed for someone completely different. That’s the problem with vintage, isn’t it? Sizing is all over the place. I’m thinking of just biting the bullet and getting a new one, even if it’s a bit pricey. Totally. Sometimes you just have to. You get what you pay for, right? Speaking of pricey, did you see that Dior show? The dresses were insane. Oh my god, yes! Absolutely stunning, but…completely impractical. Like, where are you even  wearing  those? To a gala? A fashion show? They’re art, aren't they? Pure escapism. I love seeing the creativity, even if I’d never actually wear anything like that. Me too. It's good for a bit of inspiration, though. I saw a really nice tailored blazer in a similar colour to one they used, I might try and find something similar on the high street.

So, how was college today? Anything interesting happen? You’ve been a bit quiet since you got in. It was… okay. We started a new photography project, which is good. Black and white landscapes. I’m thinking of going down to the beach at Camber Sands. It looks really dramatic on a grey day, you know? Lovely! That’s a brilliant idea. You always had an eye for that sort of thing. Remember when you were tiny and insisted on taking pictures of every single pebble on the beach? Drove your father mad. Oh god, yeah! I thought they were all special. I still kind of do. It’s just… there’s this boy in my class, Leo, and he’s  really  good. Like, properly amazing. And he was looking at my ideas and just… sort of dismissed them. Said they were “a bit cliché.” Oh, Leo. Sounds delightful. Honestly, darling, don’t let him get to you. People are just threatened by talent, or maybe he's just a bit of a know-it-all. You’ve got a fantastic eye, and your pictures are always so… evocative. Don’t let some boy crush that. I know, I know. It’s just… it made me doubt myself. It’s stupid, isn’t it? I get so anxious about people judging my work. It’s not stupid, sweetie. It's perfectly normal. Everyone feels that way sometimes. I get terrified before presentations at work. You wouldn't believe the amount of deep breathing I have to do! Apparently, Mrs. Henderson in accounts thinks I’m meditating. Oh, bless her. How was your day at the reception? Any interesting callers? Usual chaos. Old Mr. Davies called again, convinced someone had stolen his parking space. Turned out he’d just forgotten where he’d parked. Honestly, the things I put up with. It’s not exactly challenging, but it pays the bills. And the office gossip is surprisingly good. Have you read anything good lately? I need a new book. I finished that thriller last week, the one you recommended, and it was brilliant. Really kept me guessing. Oh, I’m so glad you enjoyed it! I've just started a biography of Joan Rivers. She’s fascinating, completely fearless. Although, her life was quite… tumultuous. I saw a documentary about her recently. She was absolutely hilarious, but also incredibly vulnerable. I love Joan Rivers!

Right, well, that's the blooming application form finished. Took me long enough. All those boxes… honestly. Oh, good for you, Arthur. What application, dear? The one for the… the assistance with the heating? That's the one. Says I need to declare every single penny I've ever had. Feels a bit intrusive, doesn’t it? You’d think they’d have enough information on you already, considering. It's the modern world, isn’t it? All data, all the time. Tell me about it. And then there was a question about 'dependants'. I put you down, Margaret, naturally. Oh, Arthur, that’s sweet. Although, I manage perfectly well, thank you very much. Still, it's the thought that counts. Speaking of managing, young Timmy from next door… a dreadful child. Absolutely dreadful. Oh? Still causing havoc? I thought his parents were finally getting a grip. Grip? They’re letting him run wild! Yesterday, he was throwing stones at the bird’s nest in the apple tree. Poor little things. I had to go out there and give him a piece of my mind. Stones at birds? Disgraceful. That cockerel of ours wouldn’t take kindly to that, would he? Gives  me  a right telling off if I get too close to his hens. He’s a feisty one, that bird. Nearly took my ear off last time I was round. He does have a personality, I’ll give him that. It's his crowing at five in the morning that’s the problem. Honestly, it’s enough to drive a person mad. And I haven't had a decent night’s sleep in weeks. You and me both, Margaret. Tossin’ and turnin’ all night. It’s this house, I reckon. It’s getting colder and draftier with every passing year. You two really should consider moving, you know. A nice bungalow, somewhere manageable. Manageable… it’s the finances, dear. Things aren't exactly flush. And frankly, the workmanship these days is appalling. Remember old Mr. Henderson? He could build a house with his eyes closed. Now, everyone just rushes things and cuts corners. Aye, shoddy work. We had a bloke come round to look at the guttering. Said it needed replacing. Quoted me a ridiculous price. I ended up fixing it myself with a bit of sealant and a prayer. Sounds about right. Speaking of fixing things… I’ve been getting into 3D printing.

So, she’s actually looking at flats now, can you believe it? After all this time talking about it, it’s… happening. That’s wonderful, Margaret. Truly. It must be a relief, for both of you. Though, you always did seem fairly resolute about it, didn’t you? I remember you saying years ago, once she’d finished university, you wanted her closer. Well, resolute and terrified are two sides of the same coin, aren't they? It's a huge upheaval. For  her , more than anyone. Leaving everything she knows in Barcelona. Her friends, her job… even the sunshine. She's a Mediterranean girl at heart, you know. She adapted well when she first went, though. She’s always been a resourceful one, your daughter. Remember when she was little and lost her favourite teddy bear at the pier? She organised a full-scale search party! Oh, God, yes. A tiny dictator, demanding ice cream as payment for information. She gets that from her father, I suspect. But this is…different. It’s not a lost teddy bear. It’s a life. I keep asking myself if I’m doing the right thing, encouraging this. Is it selfish? Am I just craving having her near? Don’t be silly, Margaret. It’s not selfish at all. You're a mother. It’s natural to want your children close. And she’s an adult. She’s made this decision. You're just supporting her. I know, I know. It's just…the practicalities are starting to sink in. Finding a flat she can afford in Brighton. The housing market is ridiculous. And helping her with visas, and finding a job… oh, it's a list as long as my arm. Have you spoken to David about it? He's good with paperwork, isn't he? He might be able to help with the visa side of things. David's being brilliantly supportive, of course. He's already started researching solicitor's who specialize in immigration. He’s said he'll help with the deposit, too. Honestly, I don’t know what I'd do without him. He’s the practical one. I'm the worrier. Well, you balance each other out, don’t you? That’s what makes a good partnership. And, truly, Brighton is a lovely place for her to settle. It's vibrant, there's a good arts scene… she’ll love it.

So, did you catch any of the Scottish referendum coverage last night? Absolute nail-biter, wasn’t it? Just bits and pieces, to be honest. I was helping my daughter move some furniture. Turns out a three-piece suite is a lot heavier than it looks. Back’s been complaining ever since. No, but seriously, it's a relief, isn't it? Though I suspect it’ll open a whole new can of worms with devolution and things. Absolutely. A lot of unanswered questions still. Feels like everyone’s holding their breath a little. Still, good on Scotland for having a proper debate about it, you know? Unlike some of the… shall we say, less nuanced discussions we have here. You’re not wrong. Speaking of nuanced discussions, did you hear back about that job interview at King’s? The one in London? Oh, that. Yeah, I did. Didn’t get it. Oh, damn. Sorry to hear that. What did they say? The usual. “Highly competitive field,” “strong candidates,” “we’ve decided to go with someone whose profile more closely matched the requirements.” You know the script. The infuriating script. They all sound the same. Was it someone internal, do you think? Probably. Heard through the grapevine that Professor Davies' son was also applying. Bit of a nepotism situation, I reckon. Ugh, that’s just… frustrating. Well, you're far too good to let that get you down. There'll be something else. Plenty of opportunities. And honestly, London’s a bit of a hassle anyway. Brighton suits you. That’s what I keep telling myself. And you’re right about Brighton. I just… I was hoping for a bit of a change, you know? Something a little more… prestigious, perhaps. Stupid, I know. Not stupid. It’s perfectly natural to want to advance your career. But don’t undervalue what you have here. You're well-respected, you’re good at what you do. And you're close enough to London to pop up for conferences and whatnot. True. How’s work been for you? Anything exciting happening with the sixth formers? It’s…the usual teenage drama, really. One’s convinced he's going to be the next Shakespeare, another is currently going through a particularly angst-ridden breakup. Thankfully, I’ve seen it all before. I’m mostly focused on getting them prepped for their mocks at the moment.

Honestly, this mousetrap game is going to be the death of me. Where  does  this little arm go? It’s like advanced engineering. Let me have a look. You’re trying to attach it to the… the flipper bit, aren’t you? It goes underneath, see? There’s a little slot. It’s remarkably satisfying when it actually works, though, isn’t it? That little chain reaction. It's like Rube Goldberg machines. We did one in physics. It was epic. Speaking of epic, remember that time David went to work in America? That was a bit of a Rube Goldberg situation in itself, trying to sort out his visa. Don’t remind me. The paperwork was… soul-destroying. And the questions! "Have you ever been a communist?" Seriously? Oh, the Americans and their assumptions! I remember when we visited your sister, Sarah, in Boston. The kids were fascinated by how…loud American children were. Loud? Yes! So much more vocal. And confident. Not in a bad way, just… assertive. They’d just come up and  tell  you what they were thinking. No British politeness. Sounds good, actually. They’re direct, that's for sure. I think it's a cultural thing. Everything is bigger in America, including the volume. And the portions! My goodness, the portions. I swear everything came with a side of butter and a gallon of sugar. I've heard that. I’m thinking of doing a year abroad next year, maybe somewhere in the States. Just to experience it. That sounds lovely, dear. But be prepared for a shock. It’s very different from here. The healthcare system, for a start… Don’t even get me started on the healthcare system. It's terrifyingly expensive. You need travel insurance that covers absolutely everything. And don't get sick. Is it like, if you break your leg, you're bankrupt? Not necessarily bankrupt, but a broken leg could certainly lead to significant debt. It's a very different approach to social welfare. Oh, look! The mousetrap is actually… working! Oh, praise be! Finally. Now, who wants to set it up again? I'll give it a go. Maybe we can make it even more complicated this time. Add some dominoes. Just promise you won't add anything involving springs. I've had enough of springs for one evening. My head’s spinning. Can we at least booby-trap it with some of Mum’s knitting?

Right, okay, so… operation wardrobe expansion has commenced. Oh really? Already? Didn’t think you’d be hitting the shops so soon after getting back. Jet lag and all that. Jet lag is a lie. A conspiracy created by shopkeepers to prevent people from buying things. No, honestly, I needed a distraction. And… well, there was a sale. A  very  good sale. A very good sale. That's always dangerous. Let me guess, Taobao? You know me too well. It was irresistible. I got… a few things. A few? That sounds ominous. How many is 'a few'? Is it the 'a few' that resulted in the delivery guy looking at our apartment with suspicion? It’s… manageable. Okay, it’s four dresses, a jumpsuit, and a pair of boots. Four dresses? Alright. What kind of dresses? Don’t tell me you went full floral again. Remember what happened last time? You couldn't walk down the street without looking like a walking garden. No, no florals! I learned my lesson. Two are sort of… midi-length, quite simple, dark colours. Good for lectures, you know, professional-ish. Then one is a really lovely silk slip dress, emerald green. Emerald green? That sounds… you. Very elegant. And the fourth? The fourth is a bit more… ambitious. It’s a bright orange, patterned thing. Very 70s. I saw it and just thought, “I  need  this in my life.” It might be terrible. Bright orange? Right. That’s a bold choice. Are you planning on teaching a seminar on psychedelic fashion? Maybe! No, I just thought it would be fun. It's a change. Everything I own is navy, grey, or black. I need a bit of… zest. Fair enough. Zest is good. What about the jumpsuit? Oh, it’s amazing! Wide-legged, navy blue, very comfortable. I can definitely see myself wearing that for evenings out. And the boots… they’re ankle boots, leather, a sort of burgundy colour. Very autumn-y. Burgundy boots, sounds good. Sensible, practical, yet stylish. You’re covering all the bases. When is all this arriving? Apparently, tomorrow. And the day after. And possibly the day after that. They’re splitting the delivery into three parcels. Three parcels! You really did go wild, didn’t you? We’re going to be tripping over boxes for a week. It’ll be worth it. Trust me. You’ll see. And you can help me decide what to wear!

Jaysus, that was a match alright. Absolutely brutal towards the end. Thought for a minute they’d blown it there. Yeah, it was tense! Mr. Davies was going mental in history. He kept shouting ‘Come on Ireland!’ and then the teacher had to tell him off. Oh, typical Mr. Davies! He's a bit of a wildcard. Still, nice to see the lads pull through. Did you enjoy it, Gran? Oh, I did indeed. Though I confess, I get more excited about the camaraderie than the actual rugby nowadays. All that running about… my knees ache just watching it! Ah now, you're a hard woman. Sure you used to run rings around those wee bairns in primary school. That was a long time ago, Liam. A very long time ago. Though, I did have a particularly competitive netball team. Netball? Is that like basketball? A bit, darling. But you can’t bounce the ball, and it’s played with a different ball… It’s a bit… less rough and tumble, shall we say? Now, speaking of rough and tumble, Oisin’s birthday is fast approaching. We need to get the cards sorted. I’ve got one here, but it needs signing. Oh, good point. I’ve got mine too. We could all write something special tonight? It’s not every day he's turning eight. Eight! That’s a proper age. Are we still doing the pirate theme? Aye, he’s obsessed. Wants a full pirate ship cake. I’m hoping your mother is up to the challenge, love. Mum’s already on it. She’s been muttering about marzipan sails and edible treasure chests for weeks. She's in her element. Sounds wonderful. You know, when I was a teacher, we always did stargazing parties for birthdays. A little telescope and a talk about constellations. Wonderful memories. Stargazing? Cool! Can we do that? I’m learning about space at school. We did the planets this week. If the clouds cooperate, maybe. It's supposed to be clear tonight. But first, young man, you need to be thinking about bed. It’s a school night. Aw, but I wanna stay up! Maybe just one more chapter of your book, then straight to bed? Okay… deal. Good lad. Right, so, after Oisin’s tucked in, are we sticking with the plan for Saturday? Trip to Kinsale? Yep. I’ve booked a table at that seafood restaurant you liked.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like all anyone talks about is babies these days. Chloe announced  another  one this morning. Three kids under five! Oh, Chloe. She always did like a challenge. It's a bit of a baby boom in our friend group, isn’t it? Makes me feel… surprisingly detached. I know, right? I think it’s because it feels so far off for me. And then when people ask, and I say “not yet” it feels like I’m giving a really long explanation about my PhD and needing to finish that first. It's exhausting. You don’t need to explain yourself to anyone! It's perfectly valid to want to focus on your career. Speaking of big life changes, how’s the house hunt going? Did you view that one in Grantchester? Oh, Grantchester was… nice. Very quaint. A bit  too  quaint, if that makes sense? All roses and thatched roofs. It felt like a film set. And honestly, the garden was tiny. We need space for the dog, you know? Absolutely. A dog needs room to zoom! Have you seen anything else you like then? A couple. There’s one in Milton, which is a bit further out, but it has a huge garden and a decent kitchen. It needs a bit of work, but it's got potential. It’s also… incredibly beige inside. Beige is a blank canvas! It just needs your touch. You have such good taste. You could totally transform it. I could help, if you wanted. I’m secretly obsessed with interior design. Oh, that would be amazing, actually! I’m hopeless at visualizing things. You’re the creative one. Also, practical. I’d probably just end up buying everything in shades of grey. You  do  have a thing for grey. Hey, on a completely different note, remember that blue dress I wore to Sarah’s birthday? The silk one? Vaguely? Was that the one you said you regretted buying because it was dry clean only? That’s the one! I’ve worn it, like, twice. It’s just sitting in my wardrobe. You could totally rock that. You have way better accessorizing skills than me. Do you want to borrow it? Really? That’s so kind of you! I’d love to. I’ve been trying to be better about not just living in jeans and jumpers. It’s a good excuse to dress up.

Honestly, hearing you two talk… it’s weird, innit? Like, you’re both from Bedford but sound totally different. You've got that proper Bedford twang, Ben, almost… posh. Posh? Mate, I just… speak normally. You're the one sounding like you've swallowed a gravel pit, Liam. All that East Anglian drawl. It’s proper rural. Proper rural is putting it mildly. Sounds like he's trying to charm a sheep. Charming sheep is a perfectly valid skill! Especially if you’re a gardener, Kai. You need to be able to negotiate with livestock. Negotiate? They just eat everything in sight. My nan used to say… actually, never mind. It’s a bit grim. Go on, spill. Grim stories are the best. She used to say old Man Hemmings, down the lane, used to ‘dispose’ of sick sheep by just… leaving them in the woods. Said foxes took care of the rest. Brutal. Absolutely brutal. You don’t get that in town, do you? That’s proper countryside stuff. Speaking of brutal, anyone see that MMA fight last night? McGregor’s back, apparently. Saw a few highlights. Proper showboating, as usual. Honestly, I prefer linguistics. Much less… blood. Although, dissecting grammar can feel pretty violent sometimes. Violent grammar? You're a weirdo, Ben. Speaking of weird, I think my mum’s trying to sell her old guitar online again. She keeps buying them and then deciding she ‘doesn’t have the fingers for it’ anymore. What kind is it? Maybe I could take a look. I’ve been meaning to get something to mess around with. Always fancied learning. Some acoustic thing. She thinks it’s a Martin, but knowing her, it’s probably a knock-off from Argos. She keeps saying she’s going to travel the world with it, become a folk singer… It’s a bit sad, actually. It’s the dream, though, isn’t it? Ditching the nine to five, wandering around with a guitar. Though I'd settle for just finishing marking this batch of essays. Seriously, the grammar… it's a massacre. Honestly, you guys have proper jobs. I spend all day wrestling with weeds and being judged by snails. Though, someone tried to buy a patch of land off me yesterday. Apparently, they want to build a block of flats. Really? Where? Near your allotment? Yeah. Said it was a ‘good investment.’ I told him it was my grandad’s land, been in the family for ages.

Right, so onions are going on… you’re being awfully quiet over there, are you alright? Just mentally calculating spreadsheets again? Nah, just… thinking about the car, actually. It’s due a service next month, and I’m dreading it. The quote they gave me last time was ridiculous. Oh, no. How much? Nearly four hundred quid. Four hundred! For an oil change, a filter, and them poking around for ten minutes. It’s daylight robbery. I swear they inflate the prices knowing people rely on their cars. It  is  mental. I’m so glad I cycle to work. Saves a fortune, even with the rain sometimes. Although, honestly, the state of the roads after all this wet weather… it’s terrifying. Tell me about it. I splashed through a pothole yesterday that felt like driving over a small mountain. I’m worried about the suspension, to be honest. That’s probably another few hundred quid just waiting to happen. You really need to get it checked out then. Before it’s something  major . Saves more in the long run, even if it stings now. I know, I know. It’s just… trying to save for a deposit on a house, and then the car needs constant attention. It feels like all my money just disappears. It does, doesn't it? Everyone says owning a car is expensive, but you don’t really  feel  it until you’re staring down the barrel of a huge bill. Have you looked into getting quotes from other garages? Maybe a smaller independent one? I had a quick look a while ago. The main dealers are always the most expensive, obviously. Found a couple of independents, but the reviews were a bit…mixed. Some said they were brilliant, cheap, honest. Others said they’d been ripped off. It’s always a gamble, isn’t it? It is. Honestly, sometimes I think it would be cheaper to just get the bus. If the bus went anywhere near my work, maybe! It’s a good hour and a half each way on public transport. I’d never get anything done. It’s the commute that kills you, really. All that wasted time. True. Although, you could read, listen to podcasts… make it productive? In theory, yes. In practice, I just end up scrolling through TikTok like a zombie. It’s terrible. We’ve all been there. Right, garlic’s in.

Right, now then, love, you’ve had a good brew, haven’t you? And a biscuit. Grandad, more tea? You look like you could do with another one. Aye, lass, I wouldn't say no. A bit weak, mind, last time. Like dishwater. Oh, don't start, Harold! It wasn’t weak, you just like to complain. I made it exactly how you usually have it. Two sugars, a splash of milk… Leave him be, Dorothy. He's just enjoying himself being grumpy. It’s a Yorkshire tradition, you know. Now, this cake’s lovely. Did you bake it yourself? I did, Nana. Victoria sponge. Thought it’d be a nice treat for your visit. Liam, have you thanked your grandparents for the chocolate biscuits? Yeah, ages ago. They're good. Better than the ones at school. That’s good to hear. Now, Liam, your room’s looking a bit of a state. You promised you'd tidy it up before they came. I will, I will. Just… after playing this level. It’s really hard. Level? What’s this level? Something to do with that… glowing box you’re always staring at? It's a game, Grandad. It's a spaceship one. Spaceships! In my day, we had skipping ropes and hopscotch. Much healthier, if you ask me. You wouldn't get a sore bottom from hopscotch. That's true, Nana. Although I distinctly remember  you  falling over during hopscotch once and scraping your knee. Oh, don’t bring that up! That was years ago, and it was a particularly slippery pavement! Blame the council, I say. They never grit properly. Aye, the council. Always been useless. Remember when they tried to put a roundabout on Hessle Road? Caused chaos, that did. Absolute chaos. Goodness me, I'd forgotten about that. It was a disaster, wasn’t it? They had to take it out again after a week. What's a roundabout? Oh, it's… it's a circle of road, Liam, where everyone drives around in a circle and gives way to the people already on it. Sounds complicated. Reckon they should just stick to traffic lights. Less confusing. Oh, Harold, you’d complain if they gave you a free cup of tea. Now, Dorothy, are you taking us to Bridlington next week like you promised? I want to smell the sea air. Yes, of course, Nana. I’ve booked the car, and the little tea room you like is still open.

Right, so pirates tomorrow then? Everyone excited for pirate day at school? Yes! I’m wearing my sparkly eye patch and a stripy top! And I'm bringing my hook! I wanna be a pirate too… a scary pirate! With a big sword! You can be a scary pirate, darling. I think we’ve got a cardboard sword somewhere, haven’t we? We’ll find it in the morning. Now, eat your beans. You need pirate strength! But they’re… beany. They are beany, but they’re good for you. And pirates need good food to sail the seas! Speaking of good food, did you two remember to tell me what you wanted for dinner tonight? Pizza! With pepperoni! And chips! And… and a little bit of broccoli, maybe. Right, pizza, chips, and a tiny bit of broccoli. Deal. Now, after pirate day, next week is Shakespeare week at school, isn’t it? Yes! We’re learning about  A Midsummer Night’s Dream ! What’s that? Is it about fairies? It is! It's a play with fairies and magic and lots of silly stuff. We might even try and go to Stratford-upon-Avon if the weather’s nice. It’s where Shakespeare was born, you know. Wow! Can we see his house? We can try! It might be a bit busy, but we can definitely visit Shakespeare’s Birthplace. And maybe see a performance. I want to be in a play! You might get your chance! Now, remember last week when we talked about the circus workshop? The one in a  real  circus? Oh yes! It’s on Saturday! I’m going to learn how to juggle! And I'm going to learn how to walk on a tightrope! Very ambitious! It’ll be fun, though. They said it's a proper circus tent, and you'll be learning from real circus performers. Can we take pictures? Of course! Speaking of pictures, did you two finish looking at the Easter egg hunt photos? The ones Grandma sent? Yes! I found the most eggs! That’s what Grandma said! She said you were a very clever Easter bunny hunter. And… oh! I almost forgot. I signed you both up for that little stop-motion animation workshop next month. Stop-motion… what? It’s where you make little films using toys and taking lots of pictures. Like Wallace and Gromit! Oh!

…and honestly, the whole thing was utterly ridiculous. I mean,  arrested ! For trying to sail to Cyprus. From Jeddah? Good Lord, Margaret! That’s… ambitious. And illegal, clearly. Ambitious is one word for it. Foolhardy springs to mind, if I’m being blunt. What possessed you? Well, you have to understand, it was the early 80s. I was teaching English in Jeddah – a rather… isolated experience, let me tell you. And I’d met this chap, a Norwegian, absolutely brimming with confidence. He’d sailed all over, apparently. Said it was a perfectly feasible trip. Feasible, perhaps, for a seasoned sailor with a proper vessel. Not, one imagines, a converted fishing boat and a vague idea of navigation. It wasn't  vague ! We had charts. And the boat… well, it  had  been a fishing boat. But we’d fitted it out! Sort of. It wasn’t exactly luxurious, I’ll grant you. Anyway, we set off, convinced we’d be sipping ouzo in Cyprus within a week. And the authorities didn’t take kindly to your unscheduled departure? Didn’t even let us get past the harbor. We were barely a mile out when this patrol boat came roaring alongside. Honestly, it was terrifying. They hauled us aboard, questioned us for hours - mostly because we couldn’t explain anything in Arabic, naturally. It turned out you need quite a lot of permits to leave Saudi Arabia by sea. I can imagine. A rather closed society, even now. Were you concerned about… the availability of, shall we say, refreshments along the way? Oh, absolutely. That was a major factor in the Norwegian’s enthusiasm. Alcohol is, needless to say, strictly forbidden. We’d stocked up, shall we say, rather liberally. That’s likely what raised suspicions in the first place. A boat suspiciously full of tinned peaches and… other things. Tinned peaches! A classic smuggling disguise. Ingenious, really. Though I suspect they weren’t fooled for a moment. So, what happened then? Did they confiscate the peaches? They confiscated everything! The boat, the "supplies", even my passport. We spent three days in a rather grim jail, then were eventually deported. I had to explain to the college principal why I’d abandoned my teaching post and ended up in international incident. Goodness me. You’ve lived a life, Margaret. Indeed. Speaking of boats, reminds me of a story… back when I was a young dental student, I decided I needed a sailing dinghy.

Honestly, the state of that bathroom this morning… I don’t know what goes on in there. It looked like a bomb had hit it. Oh, tell me about it. Boys, eh? It’s like living with a herd of… well, I won’t say what. Just messy. Absolutely messy. Is Leo still sulking about not being allowed to go to Millie’s party? You know he is. Dramatic sighs, slamming doors, the whole nine yards. I tried to explain, “Leo, it’s a 13th birthday, it's girls only, it’s not a personal rejection.” He just rolled his eyes. It  is  a personal rejection. Did he say that? Honestly! He's got the world at his feet, that boy. Opportunities galore. Have you seen the work experience placements the school are offering this year? A bit. There’s that engineering one, isn’t there? Matthew’s mum was saying how good it is. Leo wouldn’t be interested in engineering, though. He’s still obsessed with those explorers, you know, Bear Grylls and all that. Wants to live in a tent in the Amazon. I would! It’d be awesome! Well, maybe not the Amazon. Bit too many spiders for my liking. But he needs to think about his future. He's got good GCSE results coming up, he needs to use them. It wouldn't hurt him to earn a bit of pocket money either. I'm looking for someone to babysit for Mrs. Henderson next week, Thursdays and Fridays. Could he be persuaded? Hmm. He’d hate it. Too “uncool.” He’d rather spend all day on that computer playing… whatever it is he plays. Though, actually, maybe if it was used to fund a more realistic adventure? Like, say, a camping trip with his mates? A proper one? With a campfire and everything? Maybe. If you promised to clean the bathroom for a month afterwards. And maybe a little babysitting to  earn  the funds. No way! Babysitting is torture. Come on, Leo. It’s a few hours of your time. It’s good money, and you can save up. Plus, you’d be doing Mrs. Henderson a favour. She’s really sweet. Actually, she mentioned her grandson's football team needs a referee. Refereeing? Seriously? I play football! I can’t be refereeing! Everyone will think I'm a traitor. Well, you won’t be playing  and  refereeing, will you?

Honestly, this bread is amazing. Like, genuinely amazing. I could eat a whole loaf myself. It is lovely, isn’t it? They do a fantastic job with the local ingredients here. You wouldn’t get bread like this in Tesco's, would you? No way. Tesco’s bread is… sad. Sad is a good description. Though, I will say, they do a reasonable sourdough these days. It’s improved. Still not Croatian sourdough though, is it? Speaking of ingredients, did you see the price of truffles in that little shop in Rovinj? Astronomical! Oh, don’t even get me started. A tiny jar for the price of a new pair of shoes. And everyone’s obsessed with them. I had a patient last week who was convinced truffle oil would cure her heartburn. Seriously? Honestly. People will believe anything. She’d been watching some chef on the telly, apparently. All these celebrity chefs, they’re all the same, aren't they? Shouting and waving knives. A bit dramatic, perhaps. But they do inspire people to cook, which is a good thing. Remember that Jamie Oliver phase? Everyone was making proper meals. Yeah, but Jamie Oliver’s practically off-grid now, isn’t he? Living on a farm, raising pigs. I saw an article. He’s gone full country bumpkin. Well, he always had a bit of that about him. Still, the food here is wonderful. Remember when we were in America last year? It was… underwhelming. Everything was huge and covered in cheese. Oh, God, yes. And the portions! I felt ill after every meal. And everyone smokes. Even when it’s clearly not allowed. It’s a different culture. Still doesn’t make it right, though. Especially considering all the research on stem cells and lung cancer. Speaking of which, I was reading an interesting article about advances in regenerative medicine… Oh, here we go. A medical lecture on a family holiday. I can't help it! It's fascinating. They're growing organs in labs now! Imagine the possibilities. That’s a bit scary actually. Like, Frankenstein’s monster. It  is  a bit dodgy. What about education, though? I’m stressing about uni applications. It feels like everyone’s got a plan and I’m just…winging it. Don't worry about having a plan at 18. It’s perfectly acceptable to change your mind. I thought I wanted to be an accountant, ended up a management consultant.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience. I think that’s supposed to be pasta bake? It’s…beige. Very beige. Though, to be fair, it's a step up from yesterday's 'mystery meat' situation. I’m pretty sure it involved a lot of offal. You’re braver than me. I just stuck to the salad. It’s mostly lettuce, but at least I  know  what it is. Plus, I needed something green after staring at spreadsheets all morning. Spreadsheets, the bane of modern existence. I’m drowning in transcripts at the moment. Seriously, people say the  strangest  things when they think a recorder isn’t really picking up all the nuance. Oh, tell me about it. I'm trying to A/B test tagline variations for a new book series and the click-through rates are… perplexing. Apparently, “Medieval Mayhem!” doesn’t resonate with the target audience as much as we thought. Medieval Mayhem  should  resonate! That's… pretty good. What were the alternatives? “Historical Intrigue” and “A Tale of Two Kingdoms.” Apparently, sophisticated is the way to go? Teens these days. Maybe they're tired of the alliteration? Or maybe ‘mayhem’ feels a bit… immature. It's fascinating, isn’t it? How much subconscious stuff goes into even the simplest choices. It's practically what my entire research project is based on. That's cool. What are you researching, exactly? If you don't mind me asking. I always feel a bit weird asking. No, not at all! I'm looking at how linguistic markers of uncertainty – like ‘sort of’ and ‘kind of’ – are used differently across various age groups and social contexts. It’s surprisingly complex. Sounds intense. Digital marketing is all about certainty. Trying to  create  certainty. "Buy this! You need this! It will change your life!" It's exhausting. The pressure to create that manufactured certainty must be huge. We just try to observe what actually  is . Although, even observing feels… subjective, you know? Definitely. Especially when people are aware they’re being observed. It changes the data. I had to do a user experience test last week and everyone was behaving so perfectly, it was useless. The Hawthorne effect in action! It’s the classic research pitfall. Exactly! It’s constantly making me question everything. I spent three hours yesterday debating whether a slightly prolonged pause actually  means  anything, or if the speaker was just thinking.

Right, so are we definitely heading straight to Kasia’s then? No last-minute detour to find pierogi? Tempting, very tempting, but no. We promised Kasia we’d be there for tea. She’s making that apple cake, remember? The one with the… what is it, the poppy seeds? Oh, yes! That  is  a good cake. Worth resisting pierogi for, almost. Are you sure you’ve got everything? Passport, wallet, the little tin of biscuits you insisted on bringing? Everything’s here, darling. I’ve checked three times. Honestly, you’d think I was attempting an expedition to the Antarctic, not a two-hour drive. Though, navigating Tarnow’s one-way system  can  feel that challenging. You’re not wrong there! Kasia tried to explain it to me on video call, and my brain just short-circuited. It’s like someone designed it purely to confuse outsiders. She's a saint, trying. And she’s been so kind, putting us up for the week. Honestly, I feel a bit bad, dumping ourselves on her like this. Don’t be silly. She practically begged us to come! And think of all the sightseeing we can do. We can finally see that medieval castle she was raving about. Oh, yes! The one with the… dragons? Or was that just Kasia being Kasia? A bit of both, probably. She does enjoy a good story. Speaking of which, are you still planning on attempting to speak Polish? Remember that phrasebook you bought? Oh, don’t even ask. It’s mostly just verbs conjugated in a way that makes absolutely no sense to me. I’ll stick to “dziekuje” and hoping for the best, I think. Sounds sensible. I’ve brushed up on a few basics, but I’m terrified of accidentally saying something incredibly rude. The tones are so different, aren't they? Absolutely. Although, I suspect Kasia will be lenient with us. She speaks perfect English, bless her. She's just keen for us to experience a bit of Poland. Which is lovely. And honestly, it’s good to get away, isn’t it? Even if it’s just for a week. It's good to have something to look forward to. It is. It really is. And this campervan is surprisingly comfortable, isn’t it? I was dreading the drive, but it’s actually rather… relaxing. It is! It’s like being in a little mobile living room.

Honestly, that Adidas sponsorship with Man U is just…lazy. It’s the same template every year. Just change the colour and slap a different logo on. Yeah, it’s lacking imagination, isn’t it? Remember when Umbro were doing their stuff with them? Proper designs, a bit different. More…flair. Flair! Exactly. And I’m not even a Man U fan, but even I notice. It feels like they’re just cashing in on the name at this point. It’s the same with loads of sponsorships, though, isn’t it? Just a financial transaction. Totally. It's all about visibility now, not necessarily a genuine connection to the sport. Although, I do think some sponsorships work well. The Premier League and Barclays, for example. Seems to fit. Yeah, that one feels…natural. Though even that’s just down to the money, isn’t it? Speaking of which, have you seen the new Leicester kit? That purple one? Oh god, yeah. Bold choice. A bit…much, even for me. It's like someone spilled grape juice all over it. Seriously! It’s like they were intentionally trying to make something divisive. And they succeeded. My brother reckons it’s amazing, naturally. He's a die-hard. Brothers, eh? Always on the opposite end of the spectrum. Mine thinks anything remotely stylish is “pretentious”. Sounds familiar. Honestly, sometimes I just want everything to go back to the classic designs. Simple stripes, solid colours. Remember when Sheffield Wednesday had that striped one with the little owl on the chest? Iconic. Now  that  was a kit. Proper retro vibes. Although, I’m getting hungry now. All this football talk is making me crave…something bad. Oh no, don’t tell me you’re thinking about… McDonalds. I’m thinking about McDonalds. A Quarter Pounder meal, large fries, the works. You’re a lost cause. We literally had a really nice meal an hour ago. A  healthy  meal. There's a difference. And watching this muted football is strangely triggering a need for processed goodness. It's a psychological phenomenon, I'm telling you! Football and fast food – a dangerous combination. Although… those curly fries  do  look good on Instagram… See? You're weakening. We could walk there. It’s not  that  far. Don't tempt me. Let's just finish this cuppa and then  maybe  we'll discuss the merits of a McFlurry.

Honestly, it’s just… draining. Every single day. What is, babe? Still the Job Centre? Yeah, well that too. But mainly it’s just… people. Old mates from school getting all… smug. Posting pictures of their new kitchens, holidays, you know. Like they’ve won the lottery or something. Oh, massively. It’s the Instagram effect. Everyone’s living their best life online. It's more than that though. It’s Colin, right? Colin from school. His nan left him a fortune. A  fortune . Apparently, she was secretly a property tycoon. And he’s just… flaunting it. New car, all that. He didn’t even  work  for it. Ugh, that's so annoying. It feels… unfair, doesn’t it? Especially when you’re putting in the effort. Exactly! And he acts like he’s sympathetic. “Oh, tough times, mate.” Like he’s down with the struggle. He wouldn’t know struggle if it slapped him in the face. Men. Honestly. Remember when Darren mistook that Indian bloke at the station for someone else? Awful. Oh God, don’t even. I was mortified. He was apologising profusely afterwards, but still. The initial assumption… It's just… a lack of awareness, I think. Anyway, focus on you, not Colin’s inherited riches. How’s the Job Centre been? Any luck? Same old. They keep sending me on these courses. “Digital Skills for the Modern Workplace.” Like that’s going to magically land me a job. I told them I don’t have childcare for a full-time role, and they just shrugged. Seriously? That's ridiculous. You  need  childcare to apply for most jobs, and they just shrug? Apparently, it’s my responsibility to “find a solution.” Like it grows on trees. I’m just about managing on the Job Seekers Allowance, but with the gas and electric going up… I'm sweating it. It's a nightmare, isn't it? Mum and Dad were saying theirs doubled. Have you looked into any help schemes? I’ve tried. It’s a long process, lots of paperwork, and proving everything. And honestly, sometimes I just feel… ashamed. Claiming benefits. It's not what I wanted. Don't be ashamed. It’s a safety net for a reason. You’re doing what you need to do. Plus, you were always the one who said Uncle Barry shouldn't have spent his inheritance on that boat.

Honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t believe the traffic getting back from Cambridge yesterday. Absolute standstill on the A1. Oh, that road. Always was a nightmare. Used to be lovely countryside, now it's just… cars. Proper nose-to-tail. My daughter said the same. She works just off the A1, says it's getting worse every week. That sat nav of hers sends her all sorts of ways to avoid it, but sometimes it just adds extra time on. Exactly! Mine tried to send me through a tiny village the other day, single track road, tractors everywhere. I just ignored it in the end. You know the road better than a computer, don't you? Oh, I do. Always have. Used to drive my husband all over the place, before his eyesight went. Never trusted those newfangled things. Give me a map any day. Speaking of eyesight, I saw Old Mr. Henderson down the shops yesterday, and he’s got a new wart on his nose. A proper one. Thought it was a bit of fluff at first! Oh dear! He's always picking at things, isn't he? Probably irritated an old one. Poor man. Have you eaten already, Doreen? I made a quiche, there's plenty left. Oh, I had a bit of toast, dear, but a slice of quiche would be lovely. Thank you. It’s been a funny week for eating. I tried that new supermarket, the big one out by the industrial estate… Oh, Barton's? It  is  enormous, isn't it? Vast! And so impersonal. I couldn’t find a decent marrow for anything. And the checkout girl looked like she hadn’t slept in a week. I much prefer Mr Patel’s shop down the road. He always has a good selection, and a smile. It’s all about convenience, isn't it? But you lose something when everything's so… big. I was cleaning out the kitchen of a lady in Orton Longueville yesterday, said she'd stopped going to the market because it was a 'faff'. Said she just orders everything online. That’s sad! The market's lovely. Though I did read something awful in the paper this morning... about a plane crash. Somewhere over in Europe. Oh no, not another one. It's terrifying isn't it? Makes you think twice about flying. My nephew’s flying to Spain next month for his stag do.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is the  worst . He keeps saying “right, so…” before every single sentence. It’s so annoying! Ugh, tell me about it. He's so… repetitive. I swear he said “right, so…” at least twenty times in one lesson today. Was it Science with you? Yeah, Science. He was trying to explain photosynthesis which, like, I already understand, but he was going on and on. And Ms. Chen keeps calling us “lovelies.” It’s so patronising. “Lovelies”?! Oh my god, that’s awful! She’s a trainee teacher, isn't she? I think that’s why she's doing it. Trying to be all…friendly. It just comes across as really weird. Exactly! It feels like she’s talking to toddlers. And then there’s Ben Carter. He keeps trying to copy my art homework. Seriously? Again? What was it this time? The charcoal shading. I spent ages getting the light and shadow right, and he just… copied it almost exactly. He showed it to Miss Ainsworth, and she was all impressed. It’s so unfair! Ugh, Ben. He’s such a…a leech. You should tell Miss Ainsworth. I thought about it, but it just feels… awkward, you know? Like I’m snitching. I get it. But it's your work! You deserve the credit. Speaking of art, I think I’m actually going to enjoy the sculpture project. Apparently, we get to use clay. Oh, really? That sounds decent. Although, knowing our luck, we’ll have to make something historically accurate. Like a Roman bust or something. Maybe! I’m hoping for something more…abstract. Anyway, how did you find the English test? I thought it was really hard. Especially the poetry section. Nightmare. I completely blanked on the analysis of “Ozymandias”. I knew the poem, but I couldn’t write a coherent essay to save my life. I think I just rambled about sand and broken statues. Oh no! That’s rough. I managed to scrape something together, but I’m definitely expecting a C at best. Did you understand the question about the symbolism in “The Raven”? Sort of. I think I got the “nevermore” part, but I couldn’t link it back to the overall themes properly. Honestly, Ms. Bell is so intense about poetry. She makes it seem like the end of the world if you don't get every single nuance. She does!

Honestly, the things Mrs. O’Malley told us about the nuns when we were little… terrifying! All that talk of eternal fire and… well, you know. It stuck with you. Eternal fire? Seriously? That sounds… intense. Did she actually  believe  all that? I think so. She was very devout. It's just… a bit much, isn't it? Especially for kids. Makes you wonder what actually goes on behind those convent walls. Mama! More peas! Coming, sweetheart. See, this is a much simpler belief system: more peas = happy baby. Yeah, definitely less… apocalyptic. It's weird to think about, though, all these different beliefs. Like, Mr. Henderson at school was talking about Scientology yesterday. Oh,  Scientology ? Oh dear. That's… a whole other level of weird. I read something about that a while back. All about Xenu and space opera… honestly, it sounds like something out of a sci-fi film. That's what I thought! He was trying to explain it, and I was just picturing The Matrix, you know? Like, are we all just living in a simulation controlled by aliens? Don’t start with The Matrix now, I’ll be questioning reality all night! Though, honestly, sometimes looking at the state of the world… it wouldn’t surprise me. I know, right? It's just… I don't get why people need all these complicated rules and beliefs. Can't we just be nice to each other? Oh, if only it were that simple. I think it's about finding meaning, a sense of belonging, something to explain the unexplainable. But sometimes, it feels like it just causes more trouble than it's worth. Like with Sarah and Emily arguing about which church is the ‘right’ one? It was so awkward at the park. Exactly. They were both so convinced they had the truth… it’s exhausting. Remember old Mr. Davies? He used to say no matter what you believe, as long as you’re kind, it’s alright. Mama! Biscuit? Not until you finish your peas, little man. See, even he understands the rules. A simple system. Perhaps we should all adopt that. Peas, then biscuits. Maybe. It's definitely less stressful than trying to figure out if you're a chosen one destined to save the universe. Precisely. Now, eat your dinner. And let’s not delve too deeply into existentialism before bedtime. It’s bad enough trying to get a toddler to sleep as it is!

Right, so if we go this way, we completely avoid that awful roundabout near… what’s it called? Oldfield’s farm? Yeah, that one’s a nightmare. Always backed up. This route’s a bit longer, but honestly, it’ll be less stressful. Are you sure you’re alright to drive after… all that dancing last night? I’m grand! A bit achy, maybe. Honestly, I feel like I’ve aged ten years. All those quicksteps and waltzes… it’s exhausting! I’m starting to think ballroom’s not for me. Oh, come on! You were a natural. Remember when Mrs. Henderson said you had ‘a lovely frame’? She says that to everyone, I reckon. She's basically a professional flatterer. Though, it  is  funny seeing Mr. Henderson trying to keep up. He looks like he’s auditioning for a Laurel and Hardy remake. He does, doesn’t he? Speaking of aging, did you see that article about ageism in Hollywood? Apparently, they’re saying anyone over 40 is ‘unmarketable.’ Ridiculous. It’s utter nonsense. Look at Helen Mirren, she’s incredible! And Meryl Streep…they're both still killing it. It’s just… sexist and ageist, all rolled into one. Exactly! And even for men, it’s the same. They want shiny young things. Remember when they tried to recast Indiana Jones? Disaster. Total disaster. Harrison Ford  is  Indiana Jones. It's like trying to replace… well, it’s like trying to replace Old English with Klingon. Just doesn’t work. A very specific comparison. You and your medieval lit, eh? Speaking of things that don’t work, how’s your thesis coming along? Still wrestling with Chaucer’s symbolism? Don't even get me started. It’s like he deliberately made everything obscure just to torment future academics. I'm stuck on this bit about the knight’s tale and…oh, it’s a mess. Honestly, sometimes I wish I’d just done something sensible, like engineering. Now look, you are brilliant at what you do. And considerably less likely to be covered in scaffolding and mud. Did you manage to catch the latest episode of ‘Succession’ then? Oh my god, yes! Shiv's face when… you know. It was brilliant. Absolutely brutal. I'm completely hooked. Right? It's the writing, isn’t it? So sharp. It’s been ages since a show has had me so invested. Are we stopping for petrol soon?

Honestly, this scenery is just… unreal. I mean, Bolton’s lovely, but it doesn’t quite do rolling hills and vineyards, does it? It doesn’t. Can we put some music on? I’m getting a bit bored. Yeah, good shout. What are you fancying, Leo? I've got everything downloaded. Anything but Mum’s eighties playlist. Please. Hey! There’s nothing wrong with a bit of Madonna or Wham! It’s  classic . Let the boy have his music, dear. What have you got, Leo? Um… Arctic Monkeys? Or maybe some Aitch? Sorted. Alright, Arctic Monkeys it is. Ooh, look at that little olive grove! We  have  to stop at one of those markets later and get some proper olive oil. Not that supermarket stuff. Absolutely. And some of that truffle oil. I read the Istrian truffles are some of the best in the world. We’ll need some pasta to go with it. Speaking of food, I saw a little Konoba – that’s what they call the tavernas here – a few miles back, looked really authentic. We could try that tonight. I’m craving some proper Croatian food. Yes, definitely. Somewhere with a view, ideally. Oh, and Dad, you’re doing brilliantly driving on these roads, they're… interesting. They’re a bit narrow, aren’t they? And winding like a snake. Thankfully, I'm used to city driving, so this is a bit of a holiday for my nerves. Although, I wouldn’t fancy doing this in a caravan. Caravans are awful. Auntie Carol and Uncle Dave are always going on about their caravan holidays. They’re so… beige. Beige is a good word for it, Leo. Honestly, they spend their summers in Center Parcs or a caravan and think they’re living the dream. I’d much rather be doing this – exploring somewhere new. Remember that festival we went to last summer? Would actually be good to find a festival here. Perhaps, but let’s focus on the scenery and the food for now. We've got a whole week. Though, I did read about a small jazz festival near Pula… we could look into that. Jazz? No way. Now Leo, be polite! It might be nice. Oh look! Another vineyard! This one looks fancier. Maybe they do wine tasting. I don’t mind a bit of wine tasting. Though I’ll be the designated driver, obviously. You’re a good man, you are.

Right, so then Chloe was proper going off on one about Liam, said he’d been looking at other girls on TikTok. Honestly, the drama. Oh,  please . TikTok is basically designed for that sort of thing. Everyone's showing off. It's a minefield. More drama than EastEnders, honestly. She needs to chill. Did she actually…see him interacting with them, or just assume? Probably assumed. Chloe jumps to conclusions faster than anyone I know. Remember last month with Ben and the barista? Turns out she just misread the situation entirely. Aye, that was a disaster. She was texting him all sorts, proper accusatory. It turned out Ben was just asking the barista about the coffee blend! She was mortified. Speaking of mortifying… Did anyone hear about what happened at Jess’s party last night? Apparently, someone was… recording things. Oh god, don't tell me. What, like, videos? Yeah. Apparently there’s a whole group chat going around. It's… bad. Really bad. Apparently, someone was trying to get footage of people… you know… Oh,  no . No way. Seriously? Who would  do  that? That’s disgusting. I heard it was one of Mark’s friends. That bloke's always been a bit… creepy, hasn't he? Ugh, Mark needs to sort that out. Honestly, the audacity. This is why I hate parties. It's awful, isn't it? People have no respect for boundaries. And the thought of it being shared around… Absolutely vile. What even  is  wrong with people? Jess is fuming, apparently. Rightly so. It’s just…invasive. Like, you can't just go around recording people without their consent. It’s illegal, isn’t it? It is. And even if it wasn’t, it’s just horrible. It’s just…ugh. It makes me feel sick. Honestly. I’m avoiding Mark for a bit. I can't even look at him right now. I’m thinking we all need a games night. A proper, safe, non-recording, non-TikTok-stalking games night. We can play Monopoly and get properly competitive. Ooh, yes! Actually, that sounds perfect. Monopoly or maybe Cluedo? I'm surprisingly good at Cluedo. Cluedo, definitely. I love being Miss Scarlet, plotting murders. It's a great stress reliever. I’m in. And no phones allowed! We’re all leaving them in the kitchen. Operation: No Scandals. Brilliant. We’ll make a pact right now.

Right, I’m officially flagging. This caffeine isn’t doing what it used to. Tell me about it. I swear the library coffee is actively  removing  energy. It’s like drinking sadness. You two are moaning. I think it’s alright. Though, I did bring a backup Hobnob, just in case. A wise move, Gareth. A  very  wise move. Hobnobs are essential library survival kit. Speaking of survival, did anyone manage to find somewhere decent to grab lunch yesterday after the Cisco course? Honestly? It was a disaster. I ended up in that Pret. Overpriced and the sandwich was mostly air. I think the lettuce had seen better days. Pret’s always a gamble. I risked a wander towards MediaCityUK. There’s that new Vietnamese place – Pho. It was actually pretty good. Big portions, loads of flavour. Pho, eh? I’ve heard good things. Is it… spicy? I’m a bit of a lightweight when it comes to heat. They’ve got different levels. You can go mild, medium, or ‘burn your face off’. I went medium. It had a bit of a kick but wasn’t overwhelming. Ooh, I might have to check that out. I’m seriously craving something that isn’t a sad, beige sandwich. I had a really good Pad Thai last week, ironically, over in Didsbury. Didsbury? That’s a trek though, isn’t it? Especially on a lunch break. I was thinking something a bit closer to campus. There's that little Italian place on Chapel Street. Mario’s? Does decent pasta, quick service. Though, you’ll probably spend half your lunch queueing. Oh yeah, Mario’s. It used to be good, but it’s gotten really busy since that student discount started. You’re right, the queue stretches out the door. See, this is why lunchtime is such a stressful event. It’s a minefield of disappointing sandwiches and endless queues. I'm seriously considering just bringing in a packed lunch every day. That’s dedication, Paul. That’s true dedication. Though, a packed lunch can get a bit… repetitive. True. Unless you’re a seriously amazing packed lunch maker. I’m more of a ‘slightly squashed banana and a dry cracker’ kind of person. Sounds about right. Right, I’m off to wrestle with the vending machine for a biscuit. Wish me luck. It usually takes a tenner and a stern talking-to to get anything out of it.

Right, so I was explaining to me mum about TikTok yesterday. Honestly, it was like trying to explain quantum physics to a goldfish. Oh, bless her. My dad thinks Facebook  is  the internet. Any mention of anything else… blank face. “Is that on the Facebook?” is his default question. It's fascinating, isn’t it? How differently generations adopt these platforms. I was reading an article about how even within Millennials, there’s a pretty big split in social media usage. Some are almost entirely on Instagram, others are drifting back to Facebook for the groups… it’s a constantly shifting landscape. Shifting is an understatement! I downloaded BeReal on a whim the other day, purely because everyone at my daughter’s school is rabbiting on about it. It's just… pictures of what you’re doing, simultaneously taken, no filters. Supposedly authentic. Right, the anti-Instagram. Feels a bit performative  being  authentic, though, doesn't it? Like, “Oh look, I'm just casually sorting through the washing up, totally unplanned!” Exactly! And the timing is a nightmare. Beep goes off at a random moment, and you scramble to take a picture of something vaguely interesting. Last time it went off while I was on the toilet. Didn't post  that  one. Oh, dear! That's a story for another day, I suppose. I mostly use LinkedIn, professionally speaking. It’s handy for networking, keeping up with industry trends… and silently judging people’s profile pictures. Oh, the LinkedIn headshots! The posing! It’s a whole genre. The slightly-too-serious stare, leaning forward slightly… it's like they're all auditioning for a role as a very competent accountant. You know what’s brilliant though? Seeing librarians on TikTok. Proper, serious librarians doing book recommendations, little dances with books, debunking library myths. It's… unexpectedly charming. I've come across a few. They're doing fantastic work, actually. Reaching a whole new audience. It challenges the stereotype, doesn’t it? The shushing, cardigans-and-sensible-shoes librarian… Though, to be fair, some of us  do  wear cardigans and sensible shoes. Comfort is key when you’re shelving books all day. Fair point. But it’s good to see the profession evolving, embracing these new tools. My mum still thinks the library is just full of dusty books and silence. She hasn’t been in one for twenty years. We need to get her in for a workshop.

Right, so we’ve got the broad strokes of the business case down, haven’t we? The projected patient numbers, the catchment area… it all seems fairly robust. It's just… what  do  we do with the tape? The tape? Ah, you mean the demographic data from the consultation process? Aye, good point. We need to make sure it’s properly summarised. Not just raw figures. A narrative, really. Show the unmet need. The distance people are having to travel currently for end-of-life care. Exactly. People are driving to Maidstone, even further. And the southern end of the catchment… they’re completely reliant on the hospice in Guildford. That’s… that’s not right, is it? Especially considering the traffic on the A21. No, it's not. Which is precisely why Tunbridge Wells makes sense. Geographically, it’s a central point. Easier access for the majority. Though, I’ll be honest, I did have old Manvers on the phone again last night. Oh dear. Still on about Rotherham, is he? You know him. Reminded me, for the tenth time, that he built a perfectly good hospital there in '88. Says we should’ve looked at re-purposing existing buildings. Completely missing the point about the specialised care a hospice provides. Honestly, some people… It's about creating a  home , isn't it? Not just four walls and a roof. And that brings us back to the site selection. Have you spoken to any estate agents about plot sizes, the potential for garden space? Done a preliminary trawl. There’s a decent plot just off the Pembury Road. Good access, relatively flat, and it’s not overlooked. Though, getting planning permission might be tricky - it's green belt. But it’s worth pursuing. We need light, air, space for families. And crucially, peace. Peace is paramount. And we need to think about how we integrate with the existing local health services. The GPs, the community nurses… it can’t be a silo. We need seamless referrals, shared care plans. Agreed. I've already had a preliminary chat with the Clinical Commissioning Group. They’re cautiously supportive. It's the money, of course. The health budgets are stretched to breaking point. We need to demonstrate value. We will. The demand is there. And we can highlight the cost savings - preventing unnecessary hospital admissions, providing palliative care that reduces pressure on A&E… it’s a strong argument.

Oh, look at this one! Us at Sarah’s wedding. God, we were young. And look at her hair! What  was  that all about? The early nineties. Big hair was mandatory. She thought she looked like Kylie Minogue. We all did, probably. Remember how uncomfortable those dresses were? Seriously. Corsets and layers of netting. I can’t believe we willingly subjected ourselves to that. It looks… sticky, just looking at the photo. Sticky is the word. And look at old Mr. Henderson, trying to dance. Bless him. He nearly took out the cake table. He always did enjoy a good boogie, didn’t he? Used to say dancing kept him young. Speaking of which, are you still going to Ascot next year? I think so. It's a bit of a splurge, but it's fun. You should come with me, darling. Me? In a hat? I think I’ll leave the glamour to you two. I’d probably just end up looking like a beetroot. You’d rock a fedora, Dad. Embrace the unconventional. Speaking of unconventional, I saw Chloe Matthews at the supermarket today. Remember her? From school. She looked… different. Lots of tattoos, very brightly coloured hair. Chloe Matthews? Really? Gosh, she was such a quiet girl. Always buried in a book. Goes to show, you never know what people get up to, do you? People change. It's good she’s found something that makes her happy, though. Absolutely. Oh, this reminds me, did you order that new phone case, love? Mine's cracked to bits. I did. Should be here tomorrow. I got you that floral one you were looking at. And a pop socket, because you keep dropping your phone. You’re the best. Honestly. I'm such a klutz. It’s probably genetic, from your side of the family. I bet your grandfather was dropping things all the time. Apparently Great-Grandpa George was a terrible sailor. Kept falling overboard. Mum told me he was the reason they invented life jackets. That’s a slight exaggeration, I think. But he  was  rather accident-prone. Actually, talking of family history, I had a really interesting conversation with Carol at work today. Oh? About what? Her husband’s been researching our family tree. Apparently, we had a distant relative who was a… smuggler! Down on the coast. A smuggler? Seriously? That’s amazing! I can totally see it, though.

Right, so we are definitely watching ‘The Descent’ tonight then? Are you sure you're alright with it? You know it’s proper scary, like, genuinely unsettling. Yeah, yeah, I’m good. Honestly. I’ve been wanting to watch it for ages. Everyone says it’s amazing, properly freaky. Don't chicken out on me now though, you’re the one who suggested it! I didn’t  suggest  it exactly. I said it was the scariest film I’d ever seen and you immediately went “We HAVE to watch that.” There’s a difference. And I maintain, it’s less jump scares and more… creeping dread. That’s worse, y'know? Creeping dread is good! It gets under your skin. Jump scares are just cheap. Though I do appreciate a good, well-timed one. Remember that bit in ‘The Ring’ with the… Oh god, don’t. Don’t even  think  about Samara. I had nightmares about that woman for weeks. Proper weeks! I used to check behind the curtains. You did? Seriously? That’s brilliant! You were checking behind the curtains for a ghostly child coming out of a telly? Don’t laugh! It was terrifying! And it wasn’t just the telly, it was the… the way she  moved . All jerky and creepy. God. And those seven days… Okay, okay, point taken. ‘The Ring’ is horrific. But ‘The Descent’ is different, isn't it? It's claustrophobic. It's cave monsters. It's… realistic. That’s what makes it scary. People actually get lost in caves. That's exactly what makes it scary! People  do  get lost in caves! And then they get eaten by… whatever those things are. I don't even want to think about what they are. They aren’t even properly explained, are they? I think it's deliberately ambiguous. They're just… creatures born of the darkness. It adds to the atmosphere. It adds to the nightmares! Honestly, I’m already regretting this. I should’ve stuck with ‘Bridesmaids’ or something. Much safer. Come on, don't be such a scaredy cat! We’ve got snacks, we’ve got blankets, we’ve got each other to hide behind. It’ll be fine. It’ll be  fun . Hide  behind  you? You're about five foot nothing! That's not much protection against subterranean monsters! It’s the principle of the thing! We can scream together! Misery loves company.

Right, well, I'm just going to put the kettle on one last time. You sure you don't want a biscuit with your cocoa? No dear, thank you. Cocoa's quite enough. Though I do wish they still made those little chocolate wafers. The ones with the orange cream filling. Now  those  were biscuits. Oh, I remember those! Mum used to buy them. Everything seems to have disappeared, doesn't it? It’s all different now. Speaking of disappearing, have you seen that little tablet I bought? The iPad? I left it on the side, and now it’s… vanished. An iPad? What do you want one of those for? All these gadgets. Honestly, when I was a young man all we had was the wireless. And a good book, of course. It’s for work, mostly. Lesson planning, marking… and a little bit of Netflix, if I’m honest. But I need it for tomorrow. I was checking emails just before I came down. Emails. Another thing I don’t understand. Why can’t people just write a letter? A proper letter, with a stamp. You can  feel  a letter, you know? And it’s a nice keepsake. All these emails just disappear into the ether. I know, it’s different. But it’s so much quicker. Honestly, I'm convinced half the emails I get are scams anyway. Did you remember to look at that Airbnb listing for Aunt Carol’s trip? She’s coming down next month. Carol? Yes, the one who always wants a feather bed? I had a look. A bit pricey, wasn’t it? That cottage near the moor. It has good reviews. And a proper kitchen. She wants to make her pizza from scratch. Don’t ask. It's a whole  thing  with Carol and her pizza. Pizza? In Devon? Shouldn’t she be eating a nice cream tea? You’d think so! Look, I'll just have a quick search for the iPad again. It’s probably under a cushion or something. I’m going to rearrange the living room furniture tomorrow, actually. It's been the same for far too long. Oh, be careful with the old armchair. Your grandfather was very fond of that one. He used to sit there every evening, reading his newspaper. I will. I promise. It's just feeling a bit… cluttered. Right, no iPad. I’ll check upstairs.

Aye, honestly, the sheer scale of it, ye ken? I’d read about Patagonia, seen the photos, but nothing prepares ye for actually bein’  there . The mountains just… rise up out of the steppe. It’s brutal and beautiful all at once. Absolutely. It’s that sense of isolation, isn’t it? I felt that in Iceland, too. Standing there, under the Northern Lights, and knowing the next landmass is Greenland… makes you feel pretty small. Though I imagine Patagonia has a different kind of stillness to Iceland. More… ancient? Aye, ancient is a good word for it. And the wind! Constant. They say it’s the strongest consistent wind on the planet. Not the kind of wind that rips through a Scottish glen in a ten-minute squall, but a relentless, steady push. It shapes everything. You can see it in the trees, bent over permanently. Reminds me a bit of the Outer Hebrides, that constant exposure. But on a… grander scale, obviously. Did ye get much reading done out there? I always pack a decent stack, hoping for those long flights and quiet evenings. I tried, I tried. Brought a couple of Robert Macfarlane essays, thinking they’d fit the landscape, ye ken?  Landmarks  and a few others. But honestly, I was too busy just… looking. Genuinely, I’d sit and stare for hours, just at a mountain range. Couldn't bring myself to bury my nose in a book. Felt almost disrespectful. I know exactly what you mean. Sometimes a place is too immersive. I had that in Kyoto. I’d planned to plough through a pile of Murakami, but I just ended up wandering the temples, taking photos, and trying to absorb the atmosphere. Ended up reading more  about  Kyoto when I got home than  in  Kyoto. That's the thing, isn't it? Sometimes the reading comes after, as a way to process it all. Did ye ever get around to reading that Hilary Mantel novel I lent ye?  Wolf Hall ? Oh, aye! Just finished it last week. Brilliant. Absolute brilliant. The way she gets inside Thomas Cromwell's head… phenomenal. I'd been putting it off, thinking it'd be a bit dense, but I was hooked from the first page. Told ye! She’s a master. Makes history feel so…immediate. I’m thinking of tackling her latest one,  The Mirror & the Light . It’s a beast of a book, though.

So, I sent off the application for the Bartlett summer school. Oh, lovely! That’s good, darling. Which one was it, the design one? Yeah, the ‘Experimental Architecture’ one. It sounds…intense. Proper hands-on, building stuff, coding, all that. Sounds right up your street, doesn’t it? You always were better with your hands than your head, even when you were little. Remember building that ridiculous fort in the garden? Took over the whole lawn. Mum! It was a masterpiece. And it  was  structurally sound, mostly. Anyway, I’m a bit worried. It’s… competitive. Really competitive. Well, of course it is. It’s the Bartlett. But you’re brilliant, love. You got into the postgraduate course, didn’t you? That’s more than most people manage. That feels different. That was just… me getting a place on a course. This is a selective summer school. It’s like proving I  deserve  to be where I am. Stupid, I know. No, it's not stupid. It's perfectly normal to feel that way. Especially in architecture, it’s all about impressing people, isn’t it? Still. Don’t let imposter syndrome get to you. You're a talented girl, you really are. I’m terribly proud of you, you know. Thanks, Mum. It means a lot. It’s just…work’s been stressful too. Mr. Henderson keeps breathing down my neck about the community centre designs. That awful man. Still nitpicking, is he? Honestly, he sounds like a right misery. He always struck me as someone who peaked in university. Pretty much. He keeps saying it’s ‘not innovative enough’.
