But it’s a community centre, Mum! It needs to be practical and accessible, not a spaceship. Exactly! Sensible shoes and a good roof. That’s what people want. Not flashing lights and moving parts. Have you tried explaining that to him? I have. Several times. It’s like talking to a brick wall. I ended up staying late two nights this week just to redo the elevations based on his feedback. It felt… pointless. Oh dear. That’s not good for your well-being. Don’t burn yourself out, darling. Remember what Dr. Patel said about managing stress. I know, I know. Easier said than done. Look, I’m sorry I’m moaning. I just needed to vent. No apologies needed, sweetheart. That’s what mothers are for. Vent away.

So, you remember old man Hemmings down the lane? Sold his house last week, apparently. For a tidy sum, they say. Hemmings? Oh, aye. Lived there donkey's years, didn't he? Always complaining about the youngsters speeding past. Good riddance, if you ask me. Though, a tidy sum, you say? Everything's gone up these days. Can't buy a decent shed for under five hundred quid now. Five hundred for a shed! Honestly! It’s daylight robbery. When our David wanted one, Arthur built it for him. From scratch. Used some reclaimed timber and everything. Cost next to nothing. You can't get that kind of skill anymore. No, you can't. Everything’s throwaway now. And those new builds… dreadful. All boxes. No character. They pack ‘em in like sardines, too. I was reading in the paper the other day about the housing situation in London. Absolutely scandalous. London! Don't even get me started on London. My niece, Sarah, she’s been trying to get on the property ladder down there for years. Impossible, she says. Rents are astronomical. She’s got a good job, mind, but it’s still not enough. It’s heartbreaking, isn't it? They call it progress, but it feels like we’re going backwards. My granddaughter, Emily, she's saving up for a deposit, too. She works hard, but it’s a losing battle. They should build more council houses, that's what they should do. Like they used to. Proper houses, built to last. Not these flimsy things they put up now. Remember when everything was built to last? My dad’s Ford Anglia, he had that for twenty years. Never a day’s trouble with it. Ah, the Anglias. Solid little cars. I had a Cortina, back in the sixties. Teal blue. Now  that  was a car. You didn’t need a computer to drive it! Just a steering wheel and a bit of common sense. These new cars with all the gadgets… it’s just showing off. It’s all about image these days, isn't it? And the politicians… don’t even mention them. Promises, promises, and not a single one kept. Remember when they said Brexit would free up money for the NHS? Lies, all lies. Don't I just. They're all the same. Looking after themselves. It's a sorry state of affairs, I tell you.

Right, so I was chatting with Old Man Hemmings from the community garden this morning, and he's really keen on running some sort of bird-watching workshop in the converted space. Apparently, he’s quite the local expert. Bird watching? In there? I thought we were aiming for more… practical skills workshops? Pottery, maybe? Something that generates a bit more income than peering at pigeons. Well, he’s offering to do it for free, which is a huge bonus. And it  would  bring people in. We need to think about diversifying. Plus, he mentioned he knows a bloke who can get us a good deal on some binoculars for participants. Free is good, obviously. But the space isn’t really set up for… twitching. It's got that big window overlooking Coldharbour Lane, not exactly a feathered paradise. And where would they put their coats and bags? We’re still using that corner for storage, aren't we? We could clear some of that storage, yes. Mrs. Davies is still hoarding boxes of old newsletters from 2018. I keep asking her to sort through them, but… you know Mrs. Davies. It's like asking a dragon to give up its gold. She’s a character, that one. Look, about the conversion… has the electrician finished the new lighting yet? Because the yoga class on Thursday is going to be relying on that, and I don’t want another incident like last week with the flickering fluorescent tubes. He promised it’d be done by today. I’ll give him a nudge. I also need to chase up the furniture quotes. I’m leaning towards those stackable chairs, rather than the fancy upholstered ones. More practical for multi-use, and cheaper, naturally. Sensible. Though we do need to create a welcoming atmosphere, don’t we? A few plants, maybe some nicer artwork than the ‘Protect Our Planet’ posters we’ve had since day one. Agreed. I was thinking about approaching that art student from Lambeth College. She did some lovely work for the food bank last year and offered to do some pro bono pieces for us. Good thinking. And what about the fire escape audit? I haven’t seen any paperwork on that. I remember last year's inspector was a bit… particular. That’s on my list for tomorrow. I’ve also got to finalise the holiday cover. Amelia's off for two weeks in August, and I’m trying to juggle things so we don't have a complete meltdown.

Honestly, this is incredible, Rhys. This roast chicken is… phenomenal. Seriously. Glad you think so. Bit of a secret marinade, that. My nan’s recipe, tweaked a little. She’d kill me for saying tweaked, though. “Don’t you  dare  change a thing!” Nan’s recipes are sacred, aren’t they? My Nain had this… this unbelievable bara brith. Never tasted anything like it. Tried to get the recipe off her, but she was infuriatingly vague. “A pinch of this, a handful of that…” Oh, bara brith. Now  that’s  a proper Welsh treat. I haven’t had a good one in ages. This is a good treat, though. A very good treat. You’ve outdone yourself, chef. Flattery will get you seconds. Though I suspect you’re already planning them. It’s the gravy, isn’t it? A good gravy makes or breaks a roast. This is… exemplary. David, you always were a whizz in the kitchen. Even back in Cardiff, you were whipping up amazing things. Remember that paella you made for the fundraiser? Oh god, the paella. That was a disaster waiting to happen. Nearly set the kitchen alight. Too much sherry, I think. Oh no! See, Rhys? You’re a much more controlled chef now. A mature chef. I learned my lesson. No more impromptu paella-making. Although… I did experiment with a Moroccan tagine last week… Oh, I love a good tagine! Lamb, with apricots and almonds? Precisely. It was… acceptable. Not quite nan’s roast chicken standard, obviously. We need to see a menu for tomorrow, Rhys. What culinary delights are we expecting? Tomorrow… hmm. I was thinking a simple pasta dish. Nothing too ambitious after this. Maybe a carbonara? Ooh, yes! Carbonara sounds lovely. Though if you’re feeling inspired, a little garlic bread wouldn’t go amiss. And have you managed to find any decent Welsh cheese around here? I’m craving some Caerphilly. I spotted a farm shop on the way here, I'm pretty sure they had a selection. We could pop back after dinner if anyone's interested. Oh, yes, please! A good bit of Welsh cheese with a glass of wine… perfect end to the day. Alright, alright. Farm shop it is. And I’ll see what I can rustle up with some garlic bread. But no pressure, okay? It won’t be nan-level perfection. Just delicious, Rhys.

…and then she just went full circle, started talking about her auntie Brenda again. Honestly, you'd think Auntie Brenda single-handedly invented the microwave, the way she goes on. Sounds about right. Family gatherings, eh? A minefield of anecdotes and questionable opinions. Exactly! And everyone trying to one-up each other with holiday stories. “Oh,  we  went to Barbados, darling, it was  absolutely  divine.” Like, alright, settle down, Brenda. It’s competitive holidaying. It’s a thing. Remember when your cousin…what’s his name…Mark? Tried to claim his trip to Skegness was ‘culturally enriching’? Oh, god, yes! He’d taken a picture of the donkey rides and was going on about the “local equestrian traditions.” Honestly! Skegness. Right? Speaking of places, have you ever been to Bristol? I was down there last week for a site visit. It’s… surprisingly cool. A bit gritty, but loads of character. Bristol? Not really, no. Always seemed a bit…far. Is it good for food? I’m always on the lookout for decent food places. Yeah, really good. Loads of independent restaurants. I had this amazing Korean fried chicken. And there’s a whole harbour area, really lively. Apparently, Banksy’s from there originally - still has stuff dotted around the city, you can go on a 'Banksy tour'. Oh really? I didn't know that! We should go sometime. Maybe next year? After…you know. After the caravan debacle. We absolutely should. Although, admittedly, I’m still slightly traumatized by the thought of navigating those country lanes in that monstrosity. Tell me about it! Honestly, I’ve never driven anything so wide in my life. I felt like I was piloting a small boat. And the advert for it? "Effortless touring!" It was  anything  but. "Effortless touring," my foot. They should rename it “Stressful Steering”. Did you see that new advert for the electric car, though? The one with the sheep? Oh! The one where they’re all just...staring at it? Really weird. I don’t get it. It’s like they’re saying “sheep approve of sustainable transport”. Exactly! It's baffling. Although, it did make me think about getting an electric car. They’re getting more affordable, aren't they? They are, a bit. But then you have to worry about charging points and range anxiety. I don’t want to be stranded in the middle of nowhere with a flat battery and a herd of judging sheep.

Honestly, the hospital… it’s just a conveyor belt, isn’t it? In, examined, out. Barely a word said. I felt like a number, not a person. Oh, you get used to it, don’t you? I mean, they’re busy, they’ve got a lot on. Though that don’t make it any easier when you’re the one sat there, waitin’ for bad news. How’d your appointment go then, with the specialist? It’s…well, it’s not great. They want to do a biopsy. Said it’s precautionary, but…you know. It’s the ‘but’ that gets you. And trying to explain it all to Mum. She’s convinced it’s the worst possible thing. She started crying, naturally. Oh, bless her. Mothers will be mothers, won’t they? Always catastrophisin’. My Nan was the same, always thinkin’ the worst. Losing my Uncle George… that just floored her. Still hasn’t really recovered, I don’t think. Exactly. And Dad… well, Dad just goes quiet. Bottles everything up. Which is worse, in a way. He just sits there with this grim look on his face and pretends nothing’s wrong. It’s exhausting trying to get him to talk. Men, eh? They’re all the same. My Barry, he’s… well, he’s just not the expressin’ type. When his mum died, he barely said a word at the funeral. Just stood there, stone-faced. I had to hold it all together, really. It’s awful, isn’t it? Grief affects everyone differently. And then you’ve got to organise everything… the funeral, the will, all the paperwork. My Auntie Margaret left everything to the cats, can you believe it? No! Seriously? Seriously! Apparently, she loved those Persians more than any living soul. It’s caused all sorts of family drama. My cousin’s furious, she was expecting some money to help with the mortgage. Oh, that’s a pickle. Family fallin’ out over money… it’s always the way, isn’t it? Though, bless your aunt, at least she went out doin’ what she loved, lookin’ after her pets. I suppose so. It’s just… exhausting. And I haven't even started thinking about what  I’m  going to do if this biopsy comes back… well, you know. Don’t borrow trouble, love. Wait and see what they say. Easier said than done, I know. Fancy another biscuit?

Honestly, this Merlot is  lovely . Much better than the one we had last week. Remind me where you got it from again, David? It’s from a little vineyard just outside Lichfield, actually. They do a delivery, which is handy. Apparently, they used to just supply restaurants, but they started doing direct to consumer during lockdown and it took off. Can I go back to gaming now? Just a minute, Leo. We’re having a grown-up conversation. How was school today? Did you manage to finish that history project? Yeah, it’s done. Mr. Henderson said it was… adequate. "Adequate." That's high praise coming from Henderson. Shut up, Liam. Sounds like a typical teacher response. They rarely give out outright compliments, do they? No, they don’t. It’s always ‘could be better’ or ‘room for improvement’. Still, at least it's finished. David, you were saying about work? How’s the new project going? The one with the automotive supplier? It’s… challenging. They’re incredibly resistant to change. I'm trying to streamline their logistics, get them onto a better inventory system. They’ve been doing things the same way for twenty years and think their current method is perfect. It’s like trying to push water uphill. Oh, I know that feeling. Some people just hate admitting they could be doing something more efficiently. Remember old Mr. Peterson, the solicitor I used to work for? Absolutely wouldn’t touch a computer. Exactly! It’s the same principle. They’re scared of investing the time - and a little bit of money – to actually improve. I was suggesting a new software package, it would save them at least fifteen percent a year, and he just stared at me like I'd suggested he sell all his vintage cars. Fifteen percent? That's a lot of money. It is. But they're obsessed with the upfront cost. Honestly, sometimes I wonder why I bother. Speaking of cars, did you see that new Audi R8? It's insane. Leo, please! We’re talking about serious work issues. Although, yes, I did see it. Very nice, but completely impractical. Practicality isn’t really the point with an R8, is it? Though, I’m planning a ski trip with the boys in January. That's a bit more practical, I suppose. Have you ever been skiing, Emily? Years ago! Italy, with my parents.

Right, okay, this one… this is absolutely dreadful. Look at this haircut. What  was  I thinking? Oh my god! It's… enthusiastic. Very early 2000s. Is that… a fringe attempting to be a wave? It is! It's a failed experiment. I thought I was being all edgy. This was taken in Tokyo, remember? That little side street near Shibuya crossing. Oh yeah! With all the vending machines. You were obsessed with the vending machines. Did you bring back any weird flavoured drinks? Several. One tasted exclusively of sadness and melon. Seriously. And another one… I think it was corn? Corn-flavoured soda. Oh, that sounds awful. Still, Tokyo looks incredible in the background. You were always so good at capturing the atmosphere, even with questionable hair. Well, the city  was  incredible. I’d go back in a heartbeat. Remember the tiny ramen shop we found? The one where you had to order from a machine and then hand the ticket over? Yes! And the guy practically shoved the ramen at you – no smiles, no "enjoy your meal", just… ramen. It was brilliant. So efficient. Exactly! No messing. Okay, next one… oh, this is a good one. This is… wait for it… me attempting to photograph a badger. Oh no. Seriously? You tried to photograph a badger? Where was this? Down in Norfolk, obviously. Near Holt. I saw it rooting around in the woods and I thought, “Right, National Geographic moment!” I crept through the undergrowth for ages, trying to get a good angle… And the badger…? The badger looked at me like I was insane, snorted, and waddled off. This photo is just a blurry mess of leaves and a tiny, indignant badger bottom. That is amazing! That's going on the fridge. It’s a perfect encapsulation of your photographic ambition versus reality. Harsh! But fair. It  was  a bit ambitious. I think I scared it half to death. Though, to be fair, I was wearing that bright orange jacket. I practically glowed in the dark. You did love that jacket. You wore it everywhere. It was your “adventure jacket.” It was! It felt… appropriate. Although, perhaps not appropriate for badger stalking. Right, let’s see… this one’s from Kyoto. Look at the temple… it’s breathtaking. And look at my pose! Utterly ridiculous. You were always posing. Are you doing a ‘contemplative wanderer’ thing? Absolutely. I was trying to look deeply philosophical.

Right so then we got to this pub in Galway and it was FULL of hens. Like, offensively full. Feather boas everywhere. Oh god, the worst. Did anyone try to make you wear a sash? Thankfully no, but I did get offered a shot of something bright blue. Declined, obviously. It looked… questionable. Ireland’s good for a hen do, isn’t it? Loads of castles to pose in front of. Did you actually  do  anything scenic, or just pub crawl? Scenic? Mate, Ireland’s just a really green pub crawl. You’re basically moving the pub to a different landscape every few hours. Pretty much. There was a cliff walk, but it was mostly just trying not to blow into the Atlantic. And then finding the nearest pub. Did anyone go skinny dipping? You know, standard travel tradition. No way. It was freezing! And honestly, too many potential hen parties to witness that horrifying sight. Sensible. I once went skinny dipping in the arveron river. Mistake. It was like swimming in liquid ice. Speaking of cold… remember that time we went camping in the Peak District and you, Liam, snored so loud the sheep started running away? Hey! That was a particularly good night of snoring. I was achieving levels I didn’t know were possible. You sounded like a walrus giving birth. Seriously. Alright, alright, let’s not re-traumatise everyone. So, how’s work, Jess? Still wrestling with sourdough starters? You know it. I'm trying to perfect this rye bread recipe, but it’s a pain. It needs like, 48 hours of proving. It's almost not worth it. Then Mrs. Goldberg keeps requesting specifically Jewish recipes– Mrs. Goldberg? Is she Jewish? Yes! She’s amazing. But she expects authenticity and I'm like, I'm a baker, not a culinary historian. She keeps asking about Claudia Roden. Claudia Roden’s the queen, though. Her books are amazing. My gran used to make her lemon and almond cake. Killer. Ooh, sounds good. You know my nan makes a killer brisket. It takes like, eight hours, but it’s worth it. Then she always tells terrible Jewish jokes afterwards. Do tell. I’m a sucker for a good terrible joke. Oh god, where do I start? Okay, okay… Why don't Jews play poker? Too many shuffles. That’s… bad. Really bad. You’re banned from telling jokes.

Honestly, I could eat my weight in these peanuts. They’re doing a good job here. Proper roasted, not those pale things you get everywhere else. They  are  decent, yeah. Though I’m starting to feel a bit…salty. It's a good job we’re walking back, needs washing down with a pint or two. Speaking of washing things down, did you see that clip of someone trying to smuggle live goldfish into Australia in their hollowed-out books? No way! Really? Goldfish? That’s… dedicated. And incredibly impractical. What was the point? Apparently, they were going to use them in some sort of… competitive fish show. Don't ask. Border security were having none of it though. The look on the officer’s face was priceless. That sounds like something out of a film. Have you seen anything good lately? I feel like I’ve been in a movie drought. Everything feels…predictable. I just finished watching ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’. It’s completely bonkers, but brilliant. Michelle Yeoh is incredible. It's not predictable, I can promise you that. It messes with your head in the best way. Ooh, I’ve heard about that one. It’s been on my list for ages. I need something to occupy myself while I’m marking those dissertations. It's soul-destroying. Everyone thinks research is all intellectual excitement, it’s mostly just proofreading badly punctuated sentences. Tell me about it. I’m in the weeds with coding at the moment. It feels like I'm banging my head against a brick wall. It's not  intellectual excitement  when you’ve been staring at the same error message for three hours. You need a distraction. We should go to a theme park. Alton Towers? When was the last time we did something properly silly? Alton Towers? That’s a commitment. It’s basically a day dedicated to queuing and feeling mildly terrified. But… actually… that sounds kind of good. Though I’m more of a roller coaster man myself, you're more of a…gentle log flume sort of person, aren't you? Hey! I’m perfectly capable of handling Nemesis. I just… prefer not to have my internal organs rearranged if possible. Have you been playing anything good on the computer lately? Maybe that’s a less physically demanding distraction. Been completely hooked on ‘Baldur’s Gate 3’. It's ridiculously complex.

Honestly, this haddock is  perfect . Lightly battered, not greasy at all. You have to try a bit of mine. Oh, go on then. Just a little corner. Mmm, you’re right. Really good. Though I still think I made the right choice with the cod. It’s flakier, don’t you think? It is nice. Though I'm still aching from yesterday. I thought learning to row would be… more graceful. It wasn’t. It was mostly splashing and almost capsizing. Oh dear! Did you manage to stay upright at all? I’ve done a bit of kayaking, and even that can be tricky. I nearly ended up in the River Cam, fully clothed, last summer. A rogue swan decided my kayak was a personal enemy. A swan! Seriously? That sounds terrifying. I was mostly fighting the oars. And the instructor kept shouting things like, “Feather your oars!” which sounded like some ancient rowing code I wasn’t privy to. It  is  a bit of a strange phrase when you think about it. Though I suppose it makes sense. You need to angle them right. Speaking of getting wet, I really need a new waterproof jacket. Mine’s seen better days. Everything I own gets soaked when I’m even vaguely near water. Oh, I was looking at some in Cotswold Outdoors last week. They’ve got some good stuff, but it’s eye-wateringly expensive. I ended up getting one from Mountain Warehouse, hoping for the best. It’ll probably fall apart after the first downpour. That’s the risk you take, isn’t it? Oh, you wouldn’t believe who I bumped into last month. My cousin, Eleanor, on the train to London. I hadn’t seen her since we were children. Her mother, my aunt Margaret, basically cut her off after she married…well, never mind that. Anyway, there she was, looking exactly as I remembered. It was a really strange reunion. Wow. That  is  a long time. It’s funny how family relationships can be so complicated. Did she seem…happy? She seemed…resilient. Definitely. She’s a successful architect now, living in Australia. It was a bit overwhelming, catching up on thirty years in three hours. It also brought back a lot of memories of my grandmother, you know? She adored Aunt Margaret. It was a terrible shock when she died so suddenly, remember? I do.

Honestly Dad, it’s just… everything’s so fast now, isn’t it? Like, Grandad used to talk about Morse code, actually  sending  messages that way. Can you imagine? Now it’s just… tap, tap, tap on a screen and it's there. Aye, your Grandad was a dab hand at that, Morse code. Used to say it kept his mind sharp. A bit like those Sudoku things you do, I suppose. Though, it’s a world away from texting each other “Where are you?”. Exactly! And it’s results day next week, which is stressing me out. I keep checking UCAS, refreshing the page every five minutes like it’s gonna magically update. Don’t do that, lass. You’ll wear your phone out. And you'll only fret yourself more. Remember what I said, whatever happens, we’ll sort it. It's not the be-all and end-all. I know, I know. It's just... university, you know? Moving away, student finance… it’s a lot. Did you ever worry about money that much when you were my age? Always. Always worried about money. Different worries though. Back then it was about affording a decent pair of shoes, not tuition fees. Speaking of shoes, did you get those ones you were looking at on eBay? Not yet. There were a couple, but they kept getting snatched up. And honestly, trying to compare prices between eBay and Amazon and Sports Direct… it's exhausting. Amazon Prime delivery is a curse, makes you expect everything instantly. Tell me about it. I ordered a new cable for the TV and it arrived before I’d even finished making a cuppa. It’s madness. Though, I’m still waiting on that glass water bottle I ordered last week. Vodafone said it delivered, but it's not here. Vodafone are always rubbish with deliveries. Remember when you were waiting for that new phone? Took them a week, and then it turned up at next door's. Don’t remind me! Honestly, I swear they employ pigeons to deliver stuff. Now, are we still going to your Auntie Brenda's for dinner? I need to remember the directions. It’s that new estate, isn’t it? Yeah, still on. It’s just off the A56. I can put it on Google Maps for you, and send you a pin. That’s alright, I'll try to remember.

Man, it’s good to actually chill, yeah? Feels like ages since we properly just…sat. Tell me about it. Uni’s been a proper madness, innit? Exams looming, lectures piling up… feels like I'm living on caffeine and stress at this point. Seriously. I'm drowning in dissertations. Mine’s on the impact of online communities on political discourse, which sounds cool, but actually involves sifting through endless Reddit threads full of… well, you can imagine. My computer’s about to give up the ghost, honestly. Ah, the classic student computer struggle. Mine’s been giving me grief too. Keeps freezing mid-essay. I swear it’s got a personal vendetta against me. You thinking of upgrading? Or just patching it up 'til you're done? Thinking upgrading. But the cost, man. It’s ridiculous. Been looking at building my own, but even  that  feels expensive. Speaking of expensive, have you seen flight prices to Japan? Japan?! Woah, hang on. You finally planning that trip? I remember you talking about Tokyo for ages. Yeah, man! I’m serious. Thinking of going straight after exams. A friend of a friend’s got a contact who can get us cheap accommodation. Still gotta save up, obvs, but it feels…possible. Think you’d be up for it? Possible is good! Tokyo… yeah man, that'd be sick. Always wanted to go. The food alone! Have you seen those ramen places? Forget everything we eat here, it'll be a whole different level. Exactly! I’ve been watching videos, reading blogs… apparently, there’s this tiny little restaurant in Shinjuku, serves the most insane tonkotsu ramen. We  have  to find it. Consider it a mission. But seriously, after exams, that sounds amazing. What about long term, though? Got any plans post-uni? You sticking around London? I’m pretty sure I wanna live abroad for a bit. Maybe South America. Learn some Spanish, escape the grey. What about you? Still thinking about going into coding? That’s the plan. Found a scheme, a graduate programme with a tech firm in Canary Wharf. It’s competitive, but… y’know. Gotta try. Mum keeps saying I’m wasting my degree if I don’t go into finance, but I’m just not feeling it. Nah, gotta do what  you  want to do, right? Mum’s gonna mum. So, coding, then? That's serious graft.

Oh, look at this one, Granddad! Remember this? Us at the beach in Cornwall, must be… oh, 2010? Hmm… Cornwall… lovely place. Though a bit windy, as I recall. You were a little nipper then, weren’t you? Little legs paddling in the sea. It was a blustery day, definitely. But the ice cream made up for it. And you built the most incredible sandcastle, Granddad. A proper fortress. Well, a man's gotta have a hobby, doesn’t he? Even in retirement. Speaking of hobbies, have you seen what Brenda’s been posting on Facebook? She's taken up macrame. Macrame! Can you imagine? No way! Brenda? That’s…unexpected. I saw she’d been to Buckfast Abbey. Posted loads of photos. Oh yes, she went with Carol. Said it was very peaceful. Tried the Buckfast Tonic Wine, naturally. Said it tasted like medicine and regret. Buckfast! Good stuff. Used to be a favourite of mine, back in the day. Though I wouldn’t recommend a full bottle! Now, about this trip you were talking about... where are you thinking of going? We were looking at a cruise, actually. Maybe the Mediterranean? Or the Caribbean. Somewhere warm. It’s just an idea at the moment. It’s the insurance that worries me. It’s getting so expensive, especially with…well, with everything. Insurance is a rip-off. Pure and simple. They’re all in cahoots, the lot of them! Just look at what that David Cameron was up to, hiding his money… scandalous. Tax avoidance, they call it. Robbing the country blind! It  is  frustrating. And it feels like nobody’s held accountable. Speaking of frustrating, my car’s making a funny noise. Sounds like a dying walrus. I’m taking it to the garage tomorrow, but I’m bracing myself for a huge bill. Cars are trouble. Always have been. Never trust a machine, I say. Remember old Mrs. Higgins? She voted Conservative for fifty years, then her Ford Anglia broke down on the M5 and she switched to Labour immediately! Said it was divine intervention. That's a good story, Granddad. You always have the best stories. It is true! What are your thoughts on the upcoming election, Granddad? Are you still a staunch Labour voter? Voting… Waste of time, most of it. They all say the same things. Promises, promises. Still, I suppose you have to try.

Honestly though, Dad, you and Mum navigating Belgium with a sat nav… I was picturing utter chaos. Chaos is a strong word, darling. A little… spirited, perhaps. Your mother insisted on reading the paper map  as well . Just in case, she said. Like the sat nav was going to suddenly sprout legs and wander off. It was helpful, actually. Just to have something to cross-reference. Though, admittedly, it did lead to a few… disagreements. Especially when the sat nav tried to take us down a pedestrian zone in Bruges. Oh, no! Did you get told off? A very stern-looking gentleman in a beret certainly made his feelings known. Lots of waving of arms and rapid-fire Flemish. I understood precisely none of it, but the tone was quite clear. He thought we were completely mad, trying to drive a car down there. And the roads! So narrow. You’ve barely got room to breathe. Sounds horrifying! Was the food good, though? You said you were excited about the chocolate and waffles. Oh, the food was  excellent . The chocolate, as expected, was divine. And the waffles… well, they were a religious experience. Though I did make the mistake of ordering a waffle with everything on it. Everything. Everything? What does ‘everything’ even  mean  on a Belgian waffle? Strawberries, bananas, whipped cream, chocolate sauce, speculoos crumbs… it was a mountain of sugar. Your father barely touched his afterwards. It was a bit much, even for him. It was… a learning experience. I’ve learned my limits when it comes to waffle toppings. But the markets were wonderful, darling. Bruges has a beautiful market square. We got some lovely cheeses and little trinkets. Oh, nice! Did you cycle at all? I know Mum was keen to hire bikes. We did! Just along the canals in Ghent. It was lovely, very flat and easy cycling. Though your father nearly ran over a small child. I did  not  nearly run over a small child! I braked in plenty of time. It was the child who ran into my path. Right. Of course. Anyway, I’ve just gotten a new mobile phone. A fancy one. One of those with the really good camera. I’m still trying to figure out how it all works. Oh, nice! What did you get? A Samsung. Apparently, it’s very good for taking pictures of the cats. Essential, obviously.

Right, so I’ve got the chicken marinating, that needs at least an hour, ideally two. Do you want me to start on the roast potatoes then? Sounds good. Though honestly, the smell of that marinade is already making my mouth water. What did you put in it, again? Oh, the usual. Lemon juice, garlic, a bit of rosemary, paprika… and a sneaky dash of chili flakes. Don’t tell the kids. My lips are sealed. You’re getting very clever with your marinades, you know. Remember when we just used…soy sauce and a bit of ginger? Don’t remind me! Those were the dark days of culinary experimentation. Speaking of experiments, have you seen what Sarah’s done with her hair? On Facebook, I mean. It’s… bright purple. Oh, Sarah. Always one for a statement. Is it a good purple? Or one of those shades that makes you question reality? Somewhere in between, I think. A kind of… lavender meets electric plum. I commented, said it looked ‘bold’. Tactful, I thought. Very diplomatic. She’ll take that as a compliment. Right, potatoes it is then. Are you going to get the fireplace going tonight? It’s a bit chilly, even with the heating on. I was thinking about it. I’ll need to get some logs down from the shed, though. It’s a bit of a trek. You wouldn’t fancy braving the garden, would you? Not particularly, no. I’m quite happy stirring these beans. Though I did notice old Mrs. Higgins was putting out her winter bedding plants this morning. Impressive dedication. She’s always ahead of the game, isn't she? She’s got the most beautiful roses, too. I wish I had her touch with flowers. Everything I plant looks…sad. You’re being modest. Your hydrangeas were lovely this summer. Though, to be fair, everything looks good next to her garden. It's like something out of a magazine. Perhaps I should just buy cut flowers. Less effort. Speaking of less effort, did you remember to order that new perfume I mentioned? The one with the…bergamot? Almost. It’s in my online basket, ready to go. I was just checking the reviews. Apparently, it smells amazing, but fades really quickly. Oh, that’s annoying. I hate perfumes that disappear after five minutes. It’s such a waste of money. I quite like the one Auntie Maureen wears, though, even if it does smell slightly… mothball-ish.

So you were in Queensland, you said? Lovely part of the world, I hear. Never been myself. Aye, Queensland. Spent a good six months out there, back in ‘87. Business trip, mostly. Though I did manage to sneak in a bit of fishing. Beautiful coastline. Different world, really. Six months! That's a decent stretch. I only ever had a short holiday in Sydney. Beautiful, of course, but felt…remote. Did you find the business culture very different? Oh, vastly. Much more relaxed. Less…sharp elbows, if you know what I mean? Though the suits were still sharp enough, mind. A lot of lightweight linen, thankfully. Couldn’t imagine those heavy worsteds in that heat. Back home, every businessman looks like he’s going to a funeral. You’re not wrong there! My husband always said they looked terribly uncomfortable. All that stiffness. Did you find it easy, adjusting to the pace of things? Took a bit of getting used to. I’m a Northern lad, born and bred in Manchester. We’re used to getting straight to the point. Australians, they like a bit of chat first. A lot of “G’day” and “No worries”. Had to learn to slow down. Needed a bit of a bank loan to fund the trip. It was a good earner, but expensive. Bank loans are always a pain. I had to get one for my house, years ago. Still paying it off! Speaking of accents, I was once mistaken for an Australian in America. Apparently, my Yorkshire dialect bears a surprising resemblance to some of their regional twangs. Oh really? That’s fascinating! I’m from Bristol, and people often struggle with our accent, even other Brits. We have a bit of a…melody to our speech, apparently. A sort of West Country lilt. Some people think we sound a bit like pirates! Now, I’ve heard about the Bristol accent. Apparently, you folks drop your ‘h’s like they’re going out of fashion. We do have a tendency! It’s just…how we speak. I taught English as a foreign language for years, and I had students from all over the world. They’d often ask me to say things slowly, and try to decipher what I was saying. It was always amusing. Teaching’s a noble profession. I’m a lecturer myself, at the university. Though I'm nearing retirement now.

Honestly, this pierogi is amazing. I didn't realise vegan pierogi could even  exist , let alone be this good. Rzeszow is a surprisingly good shout for vegan food, isn’t it? It really is! I did a bit of research before I came, and there were loads of options. Much better than some places in England, actually. So, how are you finding Poland in general? Properly settled in now? Settled is…a strong word. Let's say I’m acclimatising. The language is still a hurdle, obviously. I'm trying Duolingo, but it’s slow going. And the sheer number of consonants! It’s brutal. More importantly, I’m utterly addicted to Polish social media now. Oh really? What platforms are you using? Instagram? TikTok? TikTok mostly, surprisingly. It’s a rabbit hole. I keep finding these incredibly bizarre, niche accounts. Like, one guy who just films himself meticulously cleaning rusty tools. And he has, like, half a million followers. It’s fascinating. That  is  bizarre. I get sucked into the language learning side of TikTok. So many people giving tips and tricks. It’s a lot more helpful than my old university textbooks. Though, I did get sucked into a whole drama about a British influencer who went to Bali and tried to open a ‘spiritual retreat’…it was…messy. Oh, those are the worst. The ‘digital nomad’ dramas are always so cringe. I’ve been trying to wean myself off Instagram, actually. It’s just…noise. I've started listening to podcasts instead. Oh, what kind? Any recommendations? I’m always looking for new ones. I’m currently obsessed with this true crime podcast, “Root of Evil”. It's about this incredibly complex family history and a series of murders. Ooh, that sounds intense. I’ve gone a bit more…whimsical. I found one called “Off Menu” – it’s two comedians interviewing people about their dream meal. Utterly ridiculous, but it’s perfect background noise while I’m attempting to decipher Polish grammar. That sounds lovely! I need something a bit lighter. I’ve been watching a bit too much bleak Scandi-noir on Netflix lately. It's good, but it’s draining. Are you watching anything good on TV? Honestly, British TV feels so…tired at the moment. I'm not really watching much TV, surprisingly. Partly because I don’t have a proper aerial setup here, but mostly because I'm so easily distracted by my phone.

Right, so swimming tomorrow morning, then… what about Pippy? Are you two excited to see Pippy? Yessss! She said she’d bring her juggling balls! And her sparkly dress! She promised! That’s lovely. She's a good babysitter, isn’t she? I feel much happier leaving you two when she's here. She lets us build really big dens! And she told us a story about a travelling circus. Oh really? Did she? What was it about? It had a lion and a clown and… and people flying through the air! And a strongman! He could lift a car! Wow! Sounds amazing. You know, Pippy’s trying to get a Blue Peter badge. A Blue Peter badge?! What for? She sent in a picture of the amazing things she can do with juggling. But they need a photograph  of  her, for the badge. And she’s a bit shy about being photographed. We could take a picture of her! That’s a brilliant idea! We could ask her nicely, and then she'd have a photo for Blue Peter. But we need to make sure it’s a good one, a really special one. Can we decorate her with glitter? Hmm, maybe not  too  much glitter. We don't want her looking like a disco ball! What about when we go on holiday? Do we need passports? Good question! Yes, we do. I need to dig them out. They’re probably tucked away somewhere safe… which means I’ll never find them. How old is Pippy? Oh, she's… a grown-up. Older than me! She’s… twenty-something. Why does she like juggling? She told me she used to watch her grandpa juggle when she was little. He was a really good juggler too. It's a family thing, I think. Oh, you won’t believe what she told me… What? Apparently, in some parts of China, they eat eggs that are… really, really old. Like, months old! Ewwww! Yucky! Do they smell? She said they smell  very  strong. And they turn a funny colour. She said it's a delicacy, but I don’t think I’d try one! I wouldn't either. Right, back to more exciting things. Maybe after swimming, we can practise our own circus skills? We could build a little stage in the garden. Yes! Can we be the strong people? I want to be the lion!

Right, so then she was goin’ on about how her lad, like, never seems bothered, y’know? Oh, god. That sounds… awkward. Awkward is an understatement! She was proper stressed. Said he’s lost all interest, and she’s worried somethin’s up with ‘im. Well, I mean, life  is  stressful. Could be anything, right? Work, uni… just general life stuff. Aye, she said that, but she kept goin’ on about… well, about it bein’ somethin’ physical. Like, she was whisperin’ about erectile dysfunction. Woah. That’s… a lot. She just straight up said that to you? Not straight up, not at first. It was all hints and worried looks, then eventually she just blurted it out. Said she’d been readin’ online and, well, you can imagine. Ugh, the internet is the worst. Self-diagnosing is a nightmare. Honestly, it's probably just a phase. Happens to everyone sometimes. Stress can do a lot. She was convinced it was more than that. She was talkin’ about tablets and doctors and all sorts. It sounded right scary, honestly. Poor lass. I can see why she’d be worried. But, like, there are so many reasons it could happen. And it’s not exactly something people talk about, is it? Must be awful feelin’ like you can’t even discuss it. Exactly! She was mortified even talkin’ to  me  about it. Said she couldn’t tell anyone else. God, that’s rough. It’s such a taboo subject. Makes it even harder to deal with, doesn't it? Maybe she should push him to see a doctor, just to rule things out. She said she’d tried, but he’s stubborn as an old mule. Wouldn't even entertain the idea. Said he's just “tired”. “Tired” is a convenient excuse. Honestly, men can be so… obtuse sometimes. Tell me about it. She’s feelin’ really rejected, as well. She said he doesn’t seem to want her anymore. It’s not just the physical thing; it’s the emotional side of it too. That’s what’s really heartbreaking, isn’t it? It's not about performance; it’s about feeling desired. Absolutely. It's like, she understands there can be issues, but the lack of communication is killin’ her. It’s the silence, she said. The lack of affection. That’s brutal. She’s in a really tough spot. I don't even know what to say to her, really.

Right, so I was thinking, for tonight, we could do the chilli with the rice, but like,  really  load up on the speed vegetables in it, yeah? So we get, like, three of our five a day just in the chilli. Ooh, good shout. Chilli sounds good. And we’ve got loads of that frozen mixed pepper stuff, haven’t we? That counts, right? Like, properly counts towards your five a day? It does, yeah! It definitely does. And I was thinking, if we do the rice as a Healthy Extra ‘b’… because I’ve been properly good today. Only had fruit for breakfast, and then that massive salad at lunch. Proud of you! I’ve been a bit… shaky. Had a biscuit with my tea, which is never a good sign. It just happened. It called to me. Oh, those biscuits are dangerous. They really are. Speaking of tea, fancy a peppermint? I found a new one, it's got proper mint leaves in, not just flavouring. Oh yes, please! Anything involving actual mint is a win. I’m so over artificial sweeteners and flavourings. Seriously, what  is  in those 0 calorie syrups? It just tastes… wrong. I know! It’s creepy, isn’t it? And it makes you want more. Like, your brain doesn't register it as sweet properly, so you just keep adding more and more. Anyway, chilli it is. I’ll get the mince browning. Oh, and I found that spice mix in the cupboard – the one with the smoky paprika? That would be perfect. Perfect! Oh, and did you see they’ve got double peas in the freezer now? Double peas! Like, seriously? Who needs that much pea? Haha, I know! It’s excessive. But good for us, I suppose. We can freeze half and save it for another time. It’s cheaper than buying two bags, right? Always gotta be thinking about saving money, especially with tax coming up. Ugh, don't even  mention  tax. It's the bane of my existence as a freelance illustrator. So many forms, so little actual money going in. You’re lucky with your fixed pay as a pharmacy dispenser. Yeah, it’s… stable, at least. Though they’re always changing our targets now, which is irritating. ‘Dispense ten more prescriptions an hour!’ Like, I'm not a robot! Seriously! People need things dispensed  correctly  and safely, not just quickly.

So, have you actually  looked  at villas in Italy, or are you still just… vaguely dreaming of Tuscany? I’ve looked, alright? It's just… intimidating. So much choice. And everything looks amazing in the pictures, doesn’t it? Then you read the reviews and it’s all, “Thin walls, aggressive wasps, local cats using the pool as a toilet.” Oh, don't start with the cat toilet situation. Honestly. We need a pool, though. That’s non-negotiable. Otherwise, what’s the point? Agreed. Pool is essential. And a decent kitchen. I want to actually  cook  when we’re away, not just survive on panini and gelato. Although, a lot of gelato is definitely part of the plan. You and your cooking. Honestly, you make a mean carbonara, but I suspect the main aim is to find a suitably large wine selection to pair with it. That’s just good planning! Speaking of plans… I was thinking, after Italy, maybe we finally tackle Scotland? I’ve always wanted to do the North Coast 500. Oh, that sounds… bracing. Lots of driving. And midges. I’ve heard terrifying things about the midges. I’d rather get a tattoo, honestly. You and your threats of tattoos. You've been saying you'll get one for years. What would you even get? A miniature version of Buster? Very funny. No. I was thinking… maybe some wildflowers. Around my wrist. Relatively small. Not a full sleeve, you know. I don’t want to scare the neighbours. You wouldn’t scare the neighbours. They’re more worried about Mrs. Henderson’s increasingly elaborate garden gnomes. Though, wildflowers are lovely. A bit… bohemian for you, though, aren’t they? Oh, stop. I have hidden depths. What about… if we won the lottery? What’s the first thing  you'd  do? Besides buying a lifetime supply of single malt. Hmm. Good question. I’d probably pay off the mortgage, obviously. Then I’d set up a trust fund for the kids. After that… I’d build a proper home office. This spare bedroom is driving me mad. Too cramped. And the Wi-Fi is terrible. Of course you would. Always practical. I'd buy a small cottage by the sea. Somewhere ridiculously picturesque. And I’d spend my days writing. Still on that novel, then? Always. It’s slow progress. I’m stuck on chapter twelve. The protagonist is facing a moral dilemma, and I just can’t decide which way she should go.

Right, so, the 18th is definitely free then? For the… well, for  a  celebration, at least. Aye, the 18th is good. Though I still think a proper knees-up needs to wait 'til after Sarah's back from Spain. She’d be proper miffed missing her own… well, approaching the big five-oh. She wouldn't miss it, she'd just… grumble about the timing. And honestly, leaving it another three weeks feels like an age. I’ve already ordered the cake. A rather splendid chocolate one, actually, with… miniature historical figures on top. Historical figures? You and your little hobbies. What figures? Romans? Tudors? Is there a tiny Oliver Cromwell glaring at the icing? Mostly Victorians. A little nod to the era. Though there  is  a rather determined-looking Boudicca. I thought it was fitting. Anyway, back to the 18th. We should probably ring Mrs. Higgins and see if she’s still up for doing the catering. She’s brilliant with canapés. Good shout. I’ll give her a bell tomorrow. Speaking of ringing people, did you get that postcard I sent from Skye? The one with the Old Man of Storr? Ah, yes! It arrived. Very dramatic. Though the postmark was… smudged. Made it look like it had been wrestled from a particularly grumpy postman. It was a lovely trip, though, wasn’t it? Very bracing. Aye, bracing is one word for it. I nearly blew away twice. Still, the scenery’s worth it. Saw a golden eagle, did you know? Majestic creature. Remarkable. And you managed all that walking despite your knee? Managed. With a considerable amount of grumbling and a walking stick that’s now practically an extension of my arm. Though it got me thinking… all this talk of independence up there… it's a proper mess, isn't it? It is rather… complicated. I was reading an article in the  Times  about it this morning. Apparently the latest polls suggest… Polls suggest all sorts. They were saying Labour were going to win in ‘97, weren’t they? And look what happened. The whole thing is fuelled by emotion, I reckon. A lot of ancient grievances. There is a historical element to it, certainly. Though the economic arguments are equally potent, it seems. And the young people… they seem quite keen on the idea. Aye, they do. They haven't lived through a lifetime of… well, of being British, I suppose.

Right, so we’re drawing pictures for the Syrian refugees, aren’t we? And Mrs. Davies said they’re sending them to a charity that distributes them to families who’ve had to leave their homes. I’m drawing a princess! She’s going to give them a sparkly crown! I’m making a…a super-robot! He’s going to protect them from monsters. That’s lovely. Both of you. It's very thoughtful. I was thinking… maybe we could draw them pictures of comfy chairs? Chairs? Why chairs? Well, imagine having to leave everything behind. Everything! Your bed, your toys, your favourite chair… it must be so hard not having a comfortable place to sit. So a picture of a nice comfy chair might remind them of home. Like my beanbag? Exactly like your beanbag! Or the armchair in here. What kind of chair would you draw? A pink one with fluffy cushions! And a little table for my dolls. That sounds wonderful! What about you, Leo? A racing car chair! With fire coming out the back! It’s a super-chair! A super-chair! That's brilliant. You know, there are all sorts of chairs, aren't there? Rocking chairs, office chairs… even those really hard wooden chairs they have at school. I hate the school chairs! They make my bottom hurt! They’re not very comfortable, are they? That’s why it’s nice to have a comfy chair at home. It’s somewhere safe and cosy. Like a hug. I like the chair with the arms. I can build a fort around it. See? Chairs can be lots of things. And for people who don’t  have  a chair right now, even a picture of one can be a happy thing. Will they like my princess? I’m sure they will! A sparkly crown is a brilliant idea. And Leo, a super-robot protector is exactly what everyone needs sometimes. I bet they'll have the pictures on their walls. Are we having tests at school next week? Miss Jones said something about tests. Yes, dear. You've got your spelling test on Tuesday, and a maths one on Friday. I’m good at spelling! I know all the tricky words. I don’t like maths tests. They’re hard. I know they can be tricky, but you’re both very clever. And remember, it's not about getting everything right, it's about trying your best.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from Sarah’s announcement. A second one? So soon? I know, right? It was a bit of a shock. Though, knowing Sarah, she probably started planning it the minute Leo turned six months old. She’s always wanted a big family. She is, isn't she? It's lovely, genuinely. But massively overwhelming when you think about it. Two under two... I don't know how she’ll cope. Remember how stressed she was with just Leo and the return to work? Vaguely. I think I was deep in marking hell at that point. But yes, she did seem perpetually exhausted. Though she hides it well. She always puts on a brave face. She does. And she’ll probably insist on homemade everything again. Organic purees, cloth nappies, the whole nine yards. Bless her. I admire the dedication, truly. It's a lot of work. A  lot . Makes my marking deadlines seem rather trivial, doesn’t it? Still, I’m glad for her. And for Mark. He seemed genuinely thrilled when she told him, even if his face did briefly betray a flicker of absolute terror. Oh, Mark. He’ll be brilliant. He’s so patient. He’ll be the one doing the night feeds while Sarah perfects miniature knitted outfits. Probably! Though, with both of us being lecturers, we should be sympathetic to the sleep deprivation. We know what it’s like to function on minimal hours! Just… different reasons. Ha! True. Though I suspect a crying baby is a slightly more pressing concern than a looming essay deadline. Speaking of which, did you manage to get through all of Miller’s papers? He sent a ridiculously long reading list. Nearly. I skimmed a couple. Don't tell anyone. I’m hoping I can get away with it in the seminar. He’s so easily distracted by tangents anyway. You rogue! You’re braver than I am. I read every single page, and I still feel like I haven’t absorbed a thing. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I’m actually cut out for this lecturing business. Don’t be silly. You're amazing with the students. They adore you. And you have a knack for explaining things clearly, even the really complicated stuff. Remember how flustered poor Emily was about post-structuralism? You sorted her out in five minutes flat. She was a sweet girl.

Honestly, that was the worst comedian I’ve ever seen. Absolutely dreadful. All those jokes about mothers-in-law…so predictable. Harsh, Lottie, harsh. He wasn’t  that  bad. Just…beige. Like a biscuit. Beige and offensively reliant on tired tropes! You know, my grandmother, she always said you could tell a bad omen if a comedian told a joke about a wife being a bad driver. Utterly superstitious, she was. Your grandmother and her omens. Did she have one for encountering policemen in the countryside? Because we’ve seen a surprising number today. Probably involving bad harvests and disgruntled fairies. No, actually, she was quite fond of policemen. She’d bake them cakes. Said they deserved a bit of kindness. Remember that time old Mr. Henderson – the village bobby – got stuck in the duck pond trying to retrieve a rogue football? How could I forget? He was absolutely furious, but your grandmother just kept offering him tea and biscuits. He looked like he wanted the earth to swallow him whole. Exactly! She was brilliant. Though, thinking about publicity…that whole incident got in the local paper. "Policeman Rescued From Pond by Cake-Wielding Widow!" The headline was glorious. Glorious and probably the reason he transferred to a different beat. Speaking of publicity, I’m still slightly mortified about that interview I did for the university website. They made me sound like some sort of eccentric genius. You  are  an eccentric genius! Just a modest one. Seriously, though, they completely misquoted you about the semiotics of garden gnomes. They said I believed garden gnomes were “powerful symbols of post-modern alienation.” I just said they were a bit kitsch! Honestly, the things they do. It’s all about boosting student numbers, isn’t it? Pretty much. It’s all branding. Makes you think about how we spend our holidays, though. Remember that remote cottage in Cornwall? No phone signal, no internet…pure bliss. No chance of being misquoted there. Blissful isolation. Although, I do vaguely recall you spending half the week trying to build a signal booster out of tin foil and coat hangers. It was a legitimate scientific experiment! And it almost worked! This countryside is lovely, though. It's good to get away from all that…academic noise. It really is. And much easier on the feet than those cobbled streets in Norwich. Though I do miss a decent curry.

Honestly, Dad, you wouldn’t  believe  the signal in my room. It's like living in a black hole. I tried to FaceTime Grandma yesterday, and it just kept cutting out. Ah, that mobile reception's always been dodgy around the back. They promised to put a mast up years ago, down by the old orchard, but never did. Waste of time, those promises. It's frustrating! I need to send this essay off tonight, and I’m worried about uploading it. Do you think I could use your hotspot? Hotspot? What's that now? Another one of your… gadgets. It’s just sharing the Wi-Fi from your phone, Dad. It’ll give me a better connection. Oh. Right. Well, I suppose. As long as it doesn’t use all my data. That bill’s enough as it is, even though I don’t use the thing much. Mostly just for the grandkids ringing. It won't, promise! We'll keep it brief. Speaking of things needing moving, are you still planning on having a clearout of the shed? I might be able to help this weekend. That shed’s a disaster zone, love. Been meaning to do it for months. All sorts of junk in there. Old fishing gear, bits of wood, your grandfather’s tools… I’m thinking of getting rid of the boat too, actually. Haven’t been out fishing properly in years. Knee’s not up to it anymore. Oh, really? The boat? That's a shame. I remember you taking me out on that when I was little. Good memories, eh? But it’s just sitting there, rotting. I might hire a van to take everything to the tip. Do you know anyone? I think Mark’s mate, Dave, does van hire. I can ask him for a quote. How much stuff are we talking about? A whole shed full? Pretty much. And then there's the attic... don’t even get me started on the attic. Thinking of having a bit of a sort through up there too. Maybe find some of those old antiques your grandmother collected. Oh! Really? I didn’t know she collected antiques. That could be fun! Have you been to the Great Dorset Steam Fair this year? Not yet, no. Been meaning to, but the weather's been awful. Your Auntie Carol keeps going on about it, though. She loves all that old machinery.

Honestly, the thought of them actually demolishing the library…it just feels wrong, doesn’t it? It’s been there forever. It does. And apparently, the council’s justification is…what was it? “Underutilised community space”? I saw Mrs. Henderson down at the shops, and she was absolutely fuming. She uses it every week for the reading group. Underutilised! It’s always busy! At least, when I’ve popped in. And it’s not just books, is it? They do those computer classes for older people. My aunt went to one last year, said it was brilliant. Where are they supposed to go then? Exactly. They’ve suggested moving everything into the community centre, but that’s miles away and hardly accessible for those without a car. Plus, it's always booked up with other things. It’s a proper short-sighted decision. Typical council, though, isn’t it? Always looking at the short-term cost, never the long-term benefit to the community. I saw an article online, a petition's started. I signed it, of course. Good. I'll have a look. Speaking of online… I spent ages last night looking at fabrics for the armchair. It’s surprisingly difficult to choose! Oh yes? Trying to match something to the curtains? A bit, but it’s more… getting a feel for what will actually  work . Everything looks different on a screen. I thought I wanted something floral, but when I looked at the swatches, it was just too much. I know what you mean. I ordered paint samples that looked completely different in real life. Ended up going for something totally unexpected. Have you seen those textured weaves? They look quite nice and hardwearing. I have, but I’m worried they’ll show every bit of fluff and cat hair. And Winston does love to shed. Good point. He's a fluffy one. Did you read that article in the paper about the old Victorian building they’re restoring down on Elm Street? They're keeping the original facade but doing everything else up. I did skim it. It's a shame they’re not preserving the whole thing. It's beautiful architecture. It's expensive though, isn’t it, maintaining those old buildings? That’s what they said. Apparently, it's cheaper to knock them down and build something new. Which is just ridiculous. It’s losing all our history.

Right, so are we all agreed? No more eighties power ballads on this trip? Seriously, last time it was non-stop Bon Jovi. Oh, come  on ! Bon Jovi's classic! And it was only for like, an hour. An hour that felt like an eternity, honestly. I think my eardrums are still recovering. Can we at least agree on a playlist everyone contributes to? That sounds sensible. A bit of variety is good. I’m happy to put some stuff on. I’ve been listening to a lot of that new Phoebe Bridgers album, actually. Phoebe Bridgers? Is that…sad girl music? A little bit, yeah. But it’s really good. Very atmospheric. I can add some to the playlist. Ooh, can we have some Dua Lipa? I’ve been properly obsessed with her new single. Dua Lipa is acceptable. As long as it's not  too  upbeat. My blood pressure thanks you in advance. What about presents? Have you two managed to get anything for Aunt Carol? I got her one of those… what are they called? Those paint-by-numbers kits? Floral ones. She’s always going on about wanting to get back into painting. Good thinking. She’ll love that. I got her a ridiculously expensive hand cream. She’s obsessed with hand cream. Oh, nice! I was stuck. I couldn’t think of anything. She already  has  everything. I ended up getting her a fancy tea towel. A tea towel is perfectly lovely! Don’t underestimate a good tea towel. What are you doing this weekend, by the way, Mark? Aside from subjecting us to your questionable musical tastes. Trying to finish building that bloody model railway. It's a disaster. I keep losing tiny little pieces. Honestly, it’s infuriating. I thought it would be relaxing. You and your hobbies. Always ambitious. I'm attempting to finally tidy the garden shed. It’s been a disaster zone since last summer. Oh god, sheds. They are magnets for junk. My dad’s shed is full of…well, I don’t even know  what  it's full of. Probably spiders. Speaking of disaster zones, have you guys been watching that new show, ‘Hoarders: Next Generation’? It's absolutely horrifying. ‘Hoarders’? No. I can’t cope with that sort of thing. Too stressful. I prefer something a bit lighter. Like…garden makeover shows. Garden makeover shows are the worst!

Right, so you’re seriously thinking about getting a car then? At sixteen? Yeah, well, a lot of lads at school are starting to learn, and Ben’s already passed. It’d be good to be able to get to football practice without relying on Dad all the time. It’s a big responsibility, lad. A very big responsibility. Not just the driving, but everything that comes with it. Have you even started to think about the cost? Sort of. Ben was saying his Dad got him a little Fiat, something cheap. A Fiat? Good start, I suppose. Though even a little Fiat needs insuring. And that, my love, is where the real pain begins. How much is insurance? Oh, don't even ask. It depends on so many things. Your age, your driving experience – which you haven’t got much of, let’s be honest – the car itself, where you live… Malton isn’t the worst, but it's not exactly rural, you see. More chance of accidents. So, it’s loads then? Loads is an understatement. Because you're a new driver, and a young one at that, you’re statistically the most likely to crash. Insurance companies  love  that. They practically print money off young drivers. But Ben said his insurance was only… like, eight hundred quid. Eight hundred? Bless him. Either his Dad’s paying a hefty premium under his name, or he’s been very lucky. Or, and this is often the case, he’s not telling you the full story. Is that including black box insurance? What’s a black box? It’s a telematics device. They fit a little box in the car that monitors everything you do – your speed, your braking, the time of day you drive. If you drive safely, your premium can come down. But if you speed, or drive aggressively… it goes  up . That sounds… annoying. Like Big Brother’s watching you. It is a bit, but it can save you money. It’s something to consider. We’d need to get quotes, of course. Lots and lots of quotes. And compare them. And remember, it’s not just the insurance. It’s the road tax, the MOT, the petrol, maintenance… cars are money pits, honestly. Right. Okay. So, it’s not as simple as just getting a car, then. Not at all. It’s a serious financial commitment, and something you need to think carefully about.

Honestly, the week… the week was something else. They’re talking about restructuring again, you know? Another “efficiency drive.” It’s just code for making everyone do the work of two people. Ugh, sounds awful. Like when they made Mr. Henderson teach both Year 9 Maths  and  Science when Mr. Davies left? He was so stressed, kept losing his pen. Poor Mr. Henderson. It’s terrible though, isn’t it? That pressure. I was reading something about measuring stress levels – apparently, they can tell how stressed you are by looking at the frequency of certain words you use in everyday conversation. You’re having me on. What, like if I say “deadline” a lot, they know I’m about to have a coronary? Apparently! And things like "should" and "must." Lots of obligation words. They feed it into a computer and it spits out a stress score. Creepy, isn’t it? Seriously creepy. Like Big Brother. Are you being recorded at work then? Not consciously, but who knows what they’re doing with the network traffic. They're always "monitoring performance" or whatever. Speaking of which, did you lot see that Ireland’s finally getting around to… well, I’m sure you know what I mean about allowing young ‘uns to get a present at a certain age? Oh, the age of consent thing? It’s absolutely ridiculous it’s taken this long. It's a mess, honestly. And everything with the equality vote back then… I remember how tense everything was. It was a huge deal. It felt like the whole country was holding its breath. So… anyone fancy Chinese tonight? I'm starving. That sounds lovely. Though, honestly, the chicken in their curry has gone downhill. It's all gristle these days. You’re not wrong. They’re scrimping on everything. It's the same with everything, isn’t it? They'll cut corners anywhere they can. I was listening to a podcast about that – how companies try to manipulate language to make things sound better than they are. Oh, the power of spin! It’s amazing how they can reframe something awful into a “positive opportunity for growth.” Exactly. And the importance of how you  say  things. Actually, I was trying to explain the concept of a windpipe to young Saoirse earlier. It’s a tricky one for a four-year-old. A windpipe? Eww. Sounds… medical. It is!

Honestly, Mum, you wouldn't  believe  the traffic getting out of town. It was backed up all the way to Westhoughton. Oh, aye? Probably someone having a nosey at the birds again down at the reservoirs. You know folk round here, they get obsessed. Him and his binoculars. More interested in watching the buzzards than the lorries, I reckon. Buzzards are cool. They just hang in the air. Did you see that plane earlier? It was massive! That’ll have been coming from Manchester. Probably headed to somewhere in Europe. Shame about Brexit, really. Made things a bit more complicated for travel, didn’t it? Though, I suppose we always managed before the EU, didn’t we? It's just a faff, isn’t it? All the extra forms. And Dad keeps going on about needing a vignette for Italy again. He loves driving, your dad. Always has. Says it’s the only way to see the real countryside. That’s why he fancies those hilltop villages in Tuscany. Me, I'm happy on a beach with a good book. Can we go to Italy this summer? Can we? Please? We’ll see, son. We’ll see. Depends on a lot of things. Like whether your sister finishes her law conversion course alright. Speaking of which, how’s that going, love? Stressful, I imagine? It’s… a lot. Honestly, it’s just endless reading and trying to remember case law. It's a different way of thinking than I'm used to. Plus, converting to Scots law is a nightmare. Everything’s slightly different. You’ll be fine, pet. You always were a bright spark. You just need to remember everything's in kilograms over there, not stones and pounds. And multiply everything by 1.6 to get the kilometers from miles. Honestly, it’s a nightmare trying to follow all that! Kilograms? That's loads. Why can't everything be in grams? Because grams are tiny, son! You wouldn't measure a car in grams, would you? It’s all about scale. Which reminds me… remember that time we were arguing about the weight of those bags at the airport? Oh, don’t even start, Arthur! Honestly, you were convinced you could smuggle a whole wardrobe through security. Thought you were Bear Grylls or something! Dad's always got a plan. It usually involves bending the rules slightly. I just like to be prepared!

Honestly, this lentil shepherd’s pie is hitting the spot. I was craving something proper comforting. It  is  good. Though, I still think you could’ve used a bit more smoked paprika. Just to give it a little…oomph. She's right, a little paprika would've been good. But it's great either way. It’s just…weird still thinking about where meat  comes  from. Even when it’s, like, lentils pretending to be mince. Exactly! That’s why I’m so fascinated by the whole ‘cultured meat’ thing. Like, growing actual meat in a lab. No animal suffering, less environmental impact…it sounds perfect. It does sound a bit…dystopian though, doesn’t it? “Shmeat” as they call it. Like something out of a sci-fi film. I don't know, I’m kinda with El on this. If it means animals don’t have to go through…well, everything. I’m in. Abattoirs are horrific. I saw a documentary once…I had to turn it off. Oh god, don’t even. I avoid those documentaries like the plague. It’s just too upsetting. And people are like, “But hunting is natural!” Natural doesn’t equal ethical. It’s just a different kind of suffering. It’s tricky, isn’t it? Because even growing vegetables has an impact on the environment. It’s not a zero-sum game. But at least with plants, they don’t  feel  pain. As far as we know. That's the big question. Do plants feel pain? Maybe they’re screaming silently as we munch on their leaves. We’ll never know. Don’t even go there! I’m trying to enjoy my shepherd’s pie! Maybe I should just start taking vitamin B12 supplements, just to be extra safe. I read that can be a problem with a vegetarian diet. Good idea. Though, honestly, I’m terrible at remembering to take vitamins. I bought a load ages ago, and they’re still sitting in the cupboard. Probably expired. Me too. They're just gathering dust. It's like, you have the best of intentions, y’know? Be healthier. But then…life happens. It’s like Larry David. He  knows  he's being socially awkward, he  knows  he shouldn't say that thing, but he does it anyway. It’s just…compulsive. Have you seen the latest season of Curb Your Enthusiasm? Oh my god, yes!

Right, that was a belter of an advert, wasn't it? For what even  was  that for? Some kind of… cleaning product? Nah, I think it was for that new streaming service. ‘StreamLife’ or something daft. They're everywhere now, aren't they? More than you can shake a stick at. Honestly. I’m still paying for Netflix and Disney+, and I barely watch anything on either. It’s a waste of money, really. Though, I did enjoy that new Marvel thing… what was it called? ‘Eternals’? It was alright. Bit long though, wasn’t it? Nearly three hours! I nearly fell asleep halfway through. Three hours for superheroes? Madness. I'd rather just re-watch ‘Shawshank’ for the tenth time. Never gets old. Oh, good shout. That's a classic. Have you seen, Liam's been ordering everything online again. Like,  everything . Is he still obsessed with those miniature figurines? The Warhammer ones? Worse. He’s got into collecting vintage board games. Apparently, he got a ‘Monopoly’ from 1935 for £80. Eighty quid! For a board game! He’s mental, that lad. Honestly. He'll be bankrupt before he knows it. Still, better than spending it on… well, never mind. What’s he saying about Christmas then? Has he finally admitted he’s doing nothing? He's trying to organise a massive Christmas game night. Says everyone's gotta bring a board game. And snacks. Oh, brilliant. So,  I'm  expected to spend forty quid on a board game and a mountain of crisps? Lovely. He's relying on the fact we’ll all feel guilty and end up doing it. It’s his tactic. Spot on. Speaking of Christmas, have you guys got any plans yet? Anything beyond hiding from family and consuming chocolate? I was thinking about… maybe trying to get up to Edinburgh for a few days? Just get away from it all. Edinburgh? That sounds good. A bit cold maybe, but good. How are you getting there? Train? Yeah, probably train. It’s cheaper than driving, and less stressful. Plus, I can read on the way. Though, the signal is supposed to be awful up there. My Uncle Barry lives near Edinburgh. Maybe you could look him up? He's a bit of a character. Always has a story to tell. Oh, Barry. He's the one who tried to convince us the Loch Ness Monster was real, wasn't he?

Honestly, this free buffet is a lifesaver. I skipped breakfast this morning, thinking ‘Alumni Day will provide!’ And it has. Classic you, always optimising for free food. I had a proper breakfast, but I’m already eyeing up those mini quiches. It’s good to be back, though, isn’t it? Feels… different. Less pressure, definitely. Completely. Remember stressing about mooting? I honestly thought Professor Davies was going to single-handedly dismantle my entire legal argument. Oh god, Davies! He  loved  to dismantle arguments. Though, looking back, it was good practice. Ruthless practice. Speaking of practice, how’s the job going? Still decoding the mysteries of teenage slang? You have no idea. Apparently, “rizz” is now a crucial term. I had to Google it. Multiple times. And then explain it to a visiting professor from Germany. It was… a moment. Oh, that’s brilliant. I’m mostly just scheduling interviews and wrangling spreadsheets. Exciting stuff. But it pays the bills, right? And it leaves me energy for actually  living . Which is what I plan to do this summer. Ooh, plans? Tell me everything. Last I heard, you were eyeing up Italy. Italy is happening! Two weeks in Tuscany with my sister, followed by a week in Rome. We’ve booked a cooking class in Florence – apparently, I'm going to become a pasta-making expert. Or at least, hopeful. That sounds incredible! I’m so jealous. I’m… still deciding. I’ve been toying with the idea of backpacking through Southeast Asia. But then I remember how much I hate hostels. Hostels  are  a special kind of hell. Maybe somewhere a little more… comfortable? You deserve a relaxing holiday, after all that linguistic heavy lifting. You’re right. I’m just… I feel like I should be doing something ‘productive’ with my time off. Like, research or volunteer work. It’s terrible, I know. No, it’s not terrible. It’s just… you. You’ve always been a bit of a workaholic. Remember when we stayed up all night finishing that dissertation, fuelled by instant coffee and sheer panic? Don’t remind me. I think I still have nightmares about footnotes. How's your mum doing, by the way? I haven’t spoken to her in ages. She’s good! She's just got back from a cruise around the Mediterranean. Apparently, she learned to salsa. Sent me a video. It was… terrifyingly enthusiastic.

Ugh, honestly, this essay is killing me. I’ve been staring at this screen for hours. What’s the problem? Still stuck on the intro? Worse. I’ve  got  an intro, I’ve got a whole load of points, it’s just…writing it all out feels impossible. It's about post-structuralism, honestly, it just feels like making stuff up. Right, the one Ms. Davies set? She does love a good bit of Derrida. Loves it! She practically breathes it. It’s just… so abstract. I miss things like history, where there’s actual  facts . Yeah, I get that. It's a big shift. Have you tried breaking it down into smaller chunks? Like, just focus on one point at a time? I’ve tried. I really have. It just ends up sounding like babble. I’m convinced she’s going to read it and think I haven’t even read any of the required texts. Don't be daft. You're too clever for that. You always were. Want me to read over the intro when you’ve finished a draft? Fresh eyes and all that. Actually, yes, please. That would be amazing. You always know how to make it sound…less like a GCSE student wrote it. Haha, experience, my dear. Years of suffering through postgrad seminars. Speaking of suffering, I’m knackered. That lecture on econometrics this morning nearly sent me to sleep. Ooh, sounds thrilling. What did you do afterwards? Did you at least get a decent coffee? Attempted to. The queue at the cafe was ridiculous. Ended up grabbing a biscuit and surviving on willpower. I’m seriously considering booking a massage. My shoulders are like rocks. Oh, you  should ! You deserve it. I saw a really good offer at that place near the library. The one with the lavender smell? Oh, the aromatherapy place? Yeah, that sounds heaven. Is it expensive? I'm currently running on a student budget... sort of. Not too bad. I think it was like, thirty-five quid for an hour. I had one a couple of weeks ago and honestly, it was life-changing. Felt like a new person. Hmm. Tempting. Very tempting. Maybe I’ll sneak a look online later. Though, knowing my luck, they'll be fully booked for the next month. Don't be so pessimistic! You deserve a bit of pampering after a day of econometrics torture.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Mum. You’ve really outdone yourself. Oh, don’t be silly, love. It’s just a bit of mince and mash. Though, I did find a really good lamb at the butcher’s this week. Proper quality. It  is  lovely, though. And the gravy… perfectly seasoned. You using that new stock cube I got you? Actually, yes! The Knorr one with the proper beef flavour? It makes all the difference. Though I still think my own gravy from scratch is superior, really. Of course, Dad. Whatever you say. Did you see that report on the news this morning? About Calais? Briefly. Another load of trouble, I presume? Those poor people… though honestly, it’s getting beyond a joke now, isn’t it? This constant stream… It's dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. But sending boats back isn't the answer. Where are they supposed to go? They’re desperate. Exactly! It's a complex situation. And the rhetoric is just… awful. Anyway, let's not ruin lunch talking about it. How are your plans coming along for the summer, Mum? Still thinking of that cruise? Yes, well, I’ve had a look at a few. They are surprisingly expensive. And the one I liked, the Mediterranean one, is already nearly fully booked. Money’s always the problem, isn’t it? Still, you deserve a bit of sunshine. You work too hard. You should come with her, Dad! It would be good for you. A bit of a change. Oh, I don’t know about that. Cruises aren’t really my thing. Too much… enforced fun. I’d rather stay here, potter in the garden, read a book. We could look at something a bit different then, perhaps? Somewhere quieter. Or even just a week in Cornwall? Cornwall would be lovely. We could all go! Maybe next year? We haven’t had a proper family holiday in ages. Now  that  sounds nice. We could get a cottage… near the sea. Remind me, how are your school holidays looking, love? Do you know when you're off yet? I think it’s the usual, six weeks in August. Although, there's talk of changing things next year, spreading them out. It's all a bit up in the air at the moment. Goodness, changes again. They never leave things well alone, do they? No, never. It’s just… constant upheaval.
