…and honestly, the tiling is just…wrong. Utterly wrong. I specifically said,  specifically  said, slate effect, not shiny, glossy tiles that look like they belong in a public swimming pool. Ah, the joys of tradespeople, eh? You’d think ‘slate effect’ wasn’t exactly rocket science. I’m still battling with mine over the bathroom. Promised it’d be finished two weeks ago. Two weeks? Good heavens. Mine’s been going on for a month. The bathroom's been out of action for a month, I’m having to sneak downstairs at ungodly hours to brush my teeth in the downstairs loo. It feels like camping! I know the feeling. It's the disruption more than anything, isn't it? And the dust. Honestly, I find dust in places I didn’t even  know  existed. They’ve promised me,  this week , the new shower screen. I’m not holding my breath. You’re a braver man than I am. I’m half tempted to just rip the tiles up myself and start again. Though frankly, I haven’t the faintest idea how. And my back… well, let’s just say it’s seen better days. Don't do anything rash, old boy. You’ll end up doing more damage. Remember what happened to old Professor Davies and his attempt to fix the leaky gutter? Oh, don’t remind me! Nearly took out Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses, didn't he? A rather spectacular fall as well, if I recall. Spectacular. He was lecturing on the fallibility of man that afternoon, ironically enough. Speaking of disasters, have you heard from Margaret? She’s redoing her kitchen. Apparently, it’s a nightmare. Not recently. She mentioned something about a granite worktop arriving with a rather sizeable chip in it. Sounded…stressed. Stressed is an understatement. Apparently, her husband, Arthur, attempted to 'sort it' with some sort of epoxy resin. It looked like something out of a science fiction film. She called a specialist, naturally, who said it was beyond repair. Now she's facing a new worktop and a hefty bill. Oh dear. Arthur’s a good man, but…practical skills aren’t exactly his forte. Reminds me of my brother-in-law. Tried to rewire a lamp once. Nearly set the house on fire. Men and DIY, eh? It’s a dangerous combination. I'm thinking of just getting a pre-built kitchen, you know?

Right, so who wants more curry? It’s a mild one, I promise, even for delicate palates. Mmmph, more please! It’s actually really good, Dad. Not spicy at all. It  is  lovely, thank you. Though, honestly, anything tastes good when you haven't cooked all day. Little Leo here nearly ate a bolt earlier. A bolt? What bolt? Found it under the table. Apparently, it looked “shiny and interesting”. Thankfully, I wrestled it out of his grasp before he could… well, you know. Shiny! Good! Eating metal? Seriously? That's… a superpower waiting to happen. Like Wolverine! More like a trip to the emergency room. Don't encourage him, Liam. Though, Wolverine  is  cool. You know, I used to think as a kid that night deposit boxes were like secret superhero entrances to the bank. You’d slip in unseen… Oh my god, that’s brilliant! You and your imagination. I always thought they were just for lazy bankers. Lazy bankers who don’t want to count money after dark! Speaking of dark, Liam, have you thought about what you want to do for your birthday? It's creeping up, you know. I dunno. Maybe just hang out with mates? There’s that park event next weekend, the one with the science stuff? Oh, the one with the horrible histories bit? You were saying something about wanting to go to that. They do a really good dissection thing, apparently. All fake, of course, but… Ugh, dissection. Sounds a bit… yuck. Though, the horrible histories bit sounds cool. They used to have a really good one on Victorian medicine, all about leeches and stuff. Leeches. Now  that’s  horrible history. You and your fascination with grim details. I was reading a bit about biology the other day, actually. The human body is an amazing thing. And it’s all built on… well, a lot of surprisingly disgusting stuff. You and your late-night Wikipedia spirals. Honestly, I thought you were asleep hours ago. Couldn’t sleep. Thinking about birthday plans, actually. And wondering if Leo’s developing a taste for ferrous metals. It's worrying. Honestly, you wouldn't think a little fella would go for anything that wasn't edible. Spoon! Good! Right. Spoon retrieved. Perhaps we should stick to the curry, everyone. And maybe hide all small, shiny objects? Yeah, good call. More curry then. And maybe we can talk about superhero entrances  after  dinner.

So, how was Halloween, then? Did you get absolutely inundated with trick-or-treaters, Margaret? Oh, it was a good turnout! Not as crazy as some years, thankfully. Mostly little ones, all very polite. Though one little boy was dressed as a… a giant Brussel sprout. A Brussel sprout, you say? Now, that’s original. Reminds me of the time young Timmy down the road went as a dustbin. His mum spent weeks making it! That’s so funny! We had loads! One girl was dressed as a unicorn, and another was a vampire. I got loads of chocolate though! Good stuff! More important than any fancy dress, really. How’s school going, sweetheart? Still enjoying it? It's alright. History is a bit boring, but art is good. We're doing pottery at the moment. Oh, lovely! You always were good with your hands. Remember that little horse you made out of clay, Arthur? It was brilliant! Indeed! Though I suspect it looked more like a donkey, if I’m honest. A rather lumpy donkey. But she was proud of it. Speaking of horses, has Bethany been riding much lately? I haven't seen her mention it. She’s been a bit quiet about it, actually. I think she’s losing a bit of interest. It’s expensive, you know, and it's getting colder. She's talking about joining the drama club instead. Drama club, eh? A bit more suited to her, perhaps. Always did have a flair for theatrics, that one. Drama club sounds fun! Are you going to watch her, Grandma? Oh, absolutely. I wouldn't miss it for the world. Though I’ll probably be hiding behind my hands most of the time, too nervous to watch! You always were a worrier, Margaret. Still, it’s good she's finding something she enjoys. This area’s good for that, isn't it? Lots of opportunities. Norwich is a nice little city. It is. Never thought I’d come to like it as much as I do, mind you. Grew up in Costessey, always thought Norwich was a bit… grand. But it’s grown on me. Plenty of pubs, at least. That's always a good sign, Arthur. And some lovely countryside nearby. Remember that trip we took to Blakeney Point years ago? The seals! Ooh, I want to go to Blakeney Point! I’ve seen pictures of the seals.

Honestly, this traffic is ridiculous. I thought we’d be there by now. It's just… stationary. Again. Well, what did you expect, love? It’s the Steam Fair. Everyone and their dog comes to this. Remember last time? Took us nearly three hours to get from the A31 roundabout. Three hours! And then trying to  find  a parking space was another nightmare. Especially with your Dad’s dodgy knee. Are we even sure there'll be accessible parking this year? Last time they said there was, but it was all taken up by people who just didn’t have badges. That's what I’m worried about. I emailed ahead, they said they've increased the number of disabled bays but… knowing our luck. It’ll be right at the back of the field, miles from the entrance. They always say that, don't they? ‘Increased the number’. Probably added five spaces and expect everyone to be grateful. It's just the same old story. You know, reminds me of my old neighbour, Mrs. Higgins. She was waiting years for council housing, proper bungalow suited for her arthritis. Kept getting put on waiting lists, told there was nothing available. It’s awful, isn’t it? And now they’re building all these fancy retirement villages, but they’re so expensive. Who can afford those? It's all very well for people with a bit of money tucked away, but what about the rest of us? I’m already worried about Mum and Dad. They won't want to leave their house, but it’s getting harder for them to manage the stairs. I know. And that house is huge. So much wasted space. It would be perfect for a young family, but they're just clinging on to it. They say it’s ‘sentimental’ but… it’s just not practical anymore. Sentimentality, that’s all it is. My mother was the same. Wouldn’t sell the house after Dad died, even though she could barely manage the garden. Said it was full of memories. Ended up falling down the steps one day, broke her hip. That's when we finally had to sort something out. That’s awful. Makes you think, doesn't it? You want your parents to be safe and comfortable, but you also have to respect their wishes. It’s a tricky balance. Oh, look, it's moving, finally!

Honestly, I’ve been spending hours online looking at allotment layouts. It’s a total rabbit hole. Do you realise how many different ways you can arrange raised beds? Oh, I can imagine. Pinterest is dangerous like that. I've been mostly looking at what actually  grows  well in this climate, to be honest. I don't want to put all that effort in and then everything just…fails. Good point. I got a bit carried away with the aesthetic side of things. Like, I want a little gravel path and a mini greenhouse, but realistically, I need to focus on the veg. What are you thinking of growing? Definitely tomatoes. I’m a sucker for a homegrown tomato. And courgettes, obviously. They’re so prolific, you end up giving them away to everyone you know. I was thinking maybe some beans – runner beans or French beans? And definitely herbs. Ooh, herbs are a good shout. I'm planning a whole herb garden near the kitchen door, for easy access. Mint, rosemary, thyme…the usual. I’m a bit ambitious and want to try growing some pumpkins. Pumpkins! That’s brave. They take up so much room. And you need to start them off indoors, don’t you? It sounds like a lot of work. Yeah, I know. It's a long-term project. But imagine the Halloween carvings! And pumpkin soup… It'll be worth it. What about potatoes? Are you a potato person? I am! But I’m a bit worried about blight. Is it a big problem around here? Apparently, there are early and late blight, and they can wipe out a whole crop. I’ve heard about it. My nan used to grow potatoes, and she always said to “earth them up” to protect them. I’m not entirely sure what that means, but it sounds important. We should look into it. We definitely should. And what about soil? Have you thought about that? Apparently, the soil on allotments can be pretty rubbish. I’ve been reading about soil improvement. Loads of compost, obviously. And manure, if we can get hold of some. I was thinking of getting a compost bin, but they take up quite a bit of space. Good idea about the compost bin. Maybe we could share one? I have a small garden, but not enough space for a full-sized bin. And I have a friend who works at a stables, she might be able to get us some manure.

Right, so are we still on for going into town tomorrow then? I need to get, like, actual clothes for this Uni open day. Everything I own is either pyjamas or stuff I wore in Year 11. Yeah, definitely! I was thinking we could meet up around eleven? Gives us time to wander, mooch about, maybe grab a coffee… preemptively stress about my future? You know, the usual. Eleven sounds good. Actually, I was speaking to Chloe earlier, and she said she  might  be free to join us. She's being a bit vague, though. Apparently, her flatmate’s having a bit of a crisis about a boyfriend. Ooh, drama. Chloe always ends up in the middle of someone else’s drama. Is it… Liam again? The one who collects ceramic frogs? No, thankfully not. It’s Ben, the one she met at that party last month. Apparently, he’s been “ignoring her texts” which, let’s be honest, is basically relationship code for “I’m seeing someone else.” Ugh, men. Honestly, it’s exhausting even  hearing  about other people’s relationship problems. I’m glad things are… steady with Alex. Boringly steady, maybe, but steady. Steady is good! Especially at our age. No need for the heartache. Speaking of Alex, are you still going to his dad’s band’s gig on Friday? Oh god, yes. It’s a commitment now, isn't it? His dad is so excited. He keeps sending me links to their music, which is… enthusiastically 80s. Think synth, big hair, and questionable lyrics. Sounds… unique. You’re a good girlfriend for going. I couldn’t do it. I'd probably spend the whole time trying not to make eye contact. I'm bracing myself. I'm bringing earplugs, just in case. What about you? Any plans for the weekend other than the Open Day? Just chillin’ mostly, I think. Mum’s trying to get me to go to Grandma’s, but I'm avoiding that like the plague. She'll just bombard me with questions about my future and try to set me up with some farmer’s son. Oh, the Grandma interrogation! Classic. You’re right to avoid it. It’s self-preservation. Exactly. Honestly, she thinks I haven’t thought about anything beyond next Tuesday. It’s exhausting. So, town tomorrow, eleven then? And maybe Chloe if she manages to escape the Ben-induced chaos?

Right, who’s going first then? I reckon I’m warmed up after that last round. Absolute carnage. Oh, you were good, honestly. That flanking manoeuvre was… sneaky. I was completely caught off guard. Still blaming the lag though, honestly. Lag is a myth. You’re just deflecting, Chloe. I saw you staring at your phone halfway through. I was  not ! I was checking the football scores! It’s important research, okay? Needed to know if Barrow were actually winning for once. Hold on, hold on… almost… yes! Headshot! Take that, camper. Nathan, are you ever  not  camping? Seriously? You’re like a human turret. Hey, it’s a valid strategy! Someone’s gotta defend the objective. And it’s fun! Plus, it really winds people up. Like you, apparently. He’s not wrong, it is kinda hilarious watching people rage. Speaking of winding people up, remember that time Liam tried to convince everyone he was a professional eSports player? Oh god,  that  was a good one. He kept talking about ‘optimal APM’ and ‘macro gameplay’. We were all just playing Mario Kart! And the outfit! He borrowed Josh’s gaming headset and tried to look all serious. It had little cat ears on it. Cat ears? No way! I missed that. Genuine article. He insisted they improved his audio clarity. He ended up losing every single race. It was glorious. Actually, speaking of outfits, has anyone seen that new streetwear collection at Urban Outfitters? The hoodies look banging. I need a new one for campus. Urban Outfitters? Seriously? You’ll be broke within a week. Everything’s massively overpriced. But it’s  aesthetics , Tom! You wouldn’t understand. Gotta look the part, you know? Especially when I'm trying to network at the careers fair. Networking in a hoodie? Bold strategy. I’m thinking of just wearing my best shirt and hoping for the best. I'm just gonna rock up in whatever I can find that doesn't have stains. Priorities, right? So, anyone fancy another round? I’m feeling pretty good now. Alright, alright, another round it is. But Nathan, no camping. I’m serious. I'm reporting you. Fine, fine. I'll try to be more… dynamic. But no promises. Oh, before we start, I saw a weird little chihuahua on campus today. It was wearing a tiny raincoat. A  tiny  raincoat. A chihuahua in a raincoat?

Honestly, Doreen from bingo called me yesterday, you won’t believe it. Complaining about Brenda. Apparently, Brenda’s been winning  every  week, and Doreen reckons she’s cheating. Oh, no way! Brenda? Little Brenda from the post office? She seems so sweet. Sweet as pie, apparently a shark when it comes to bingo. Doreen said she saw Brenda subtly switching her dabber mid-game. Swearin’ it were a different colour ink! Oh, that’s brilliant. A bingo scandal! Sounds like something out of a film. Have you seen anything good lately? I’m completely wiped after work, just want to veg out with something mindless. Oh, I tried to watch one of those superhero films with your father last week. Dreadful. All explosions and people flying about. Couldn't follow a word of it. Gave me a headache. He loved it, of course. Says it's 'escapism'. Dad loves anything with a big explosion, doesn’t he? I’m trying to get him into something a bit more…subtle. I recommended ‘Past Lives’ the other day. Have you heard of it? ‘Past Lives’… no, doesn’t ring a bell. Is it one of those foreign ones? I do like a good romance, but it has to be a proper one, not all…confusing. I watched a French film once, oh, it was awful! Subtitles, you know, you’re reading all the time instead of watching. It's Korean, actually. But it's subtitled, yeah. It's really beautiful though, very emotional. About reconnecting with someone from your childhood. It’s not overly dramatic, more…melancholy. Melancholy… sounds a bit depressing to me. I need somethin’ cheerful! Reminds me, Mabel was on about that old Cary Grant film, ‘Bringing Up Baby’. Have you seen that one? Now  that  is a film. Proper funny and romantic. Oh, yes! I’ve seen that. It’s a classic. Katharine Hepburn is amazing in it. We should watch it together sometime. That’d be lovely, dear. Perhaps next week? Though I'm supposed to be helping Doreen with the village fete. She’s roped me into running the tombola, naturally. Honestly, that woman. Always needs a bit of help. Sounds like you’ll be busy. I’m free most evenings, though. What about Friday? I can swing by after work, we could order a takeaway, watch ‘Bringing Up Baby’, and you can tell me all about Brenda’s bingo malarkey.

Honestly, the interview was… a lot. Like, genuinely draining. Not because it was  hard , just because of the sheer amount of… enthusiasm. Oh god, tell me about it. Was it the sort where they ask you to ‘tell them about a time you failed’? Because I  hate  those. Worse. They asked me to describe myself as a vegetable. No! You are joking. A  vegetable ? I am entirely serious! And then, after I’d stumbled through something about being a resilient root vegetable, they asked what kind of spice I’d be and why. Sounds utterly bizarre! Is everything alright in here? Lots of laughter. Everything’s fine, just El’s describing her interview. Apparently, she had to embody a vegetable. Oh,  that’s  awful. These recruitment things just get weirder and weirder. Tell me about it! I think they're trying to see how you react under pressure, but it just feels… absurd. Anyway, enough about my existential crisis as a parsnip. How was your week? Did you manage to schedule that spa thing? I did! Booked it for next Saturday. Massages, the whole shebang. Need it desperately, after dealing with the chaos that is editing that magazine this week. Honestly, the deadlines are insane. And the articles… some of them are just… baffling. Oh, the magazines? Is it still full of 'manifest your dream life' and ‘glow up’ guides? Pretty much. Although, there was one article about competitive dog grooming. That was a new level of niche. Competitive dog grooming? Seriously? Apparently, it’s a huge thing! The dogs are dyed, sculpted… it’s intense. Anyway, are you and Finn still planning on that board game night? Yeah! He's bringing 'Ticket to Ride'. I'm hoping to win this time. He always obliterates me. He  is  good at those strategy games. I’m rubbish. I get distracted by the little train pieces. Ha! You have the attention span of a goldfish sometimes. Have you been watching ‘The Undateables’ again? Don't judge me! It's strangely comforting. They're all so lovely. Plus, it makes you feel better about your own disastrous dating life. It's a genuinely heartwarming show, actually. It's nice to see people being genuinely  kind . True. It's a nice change from… well, everything else. Did you manage to watch all of those DVDs I lent you, by the way? Not all of them, I’m embarrassed to say.

Right, so the washing machine’s decided it’s having a mid-life crisis, hasn’t it? Just sits there beeping at me. Beeping? What does that  mean ? Machines shouldn’t just beep menacingly. Is it error code related? I haven’t a clue. It’s just… beep. Pause. Beep. Like it’s judging my laundry choices. I tried turning it off and on again, obviously. Standard procedure. Didn't work. Classic. It’s probably something trivial. Is the drain hose kinked? Did you check that? No, I just stared at it, hoping it would sort itself out. I'm a researcher, not a plumber! Honestly, I’m starting to think we need to just outsource all our domestic chores. We could. Although, the cost… I was looking at meal prep services the other day, actually, because I’m seriously failing at adulting this week. All I’ve eaten is instant noodles and slightly stale biscuits. Oh, don't even. I opened the fridge earlier and it was just…sad. A lone yogurt and half a jar of pickles. I think my mam would be horrified. She always says, “A tidy house, a tidy mind.” Mine’s both a mess, clearly. Your mam’s a wise woman. Mine just sends passive-aggressive texts about how much weight I've lost. Apparently, I look ‘peaky.’ Oh, God. That's…a unique form of concern. Still, better than being told off for a messy house, I suppose. Speaking of family, did you manage to speak to your brother about his wedding plans? Briefly. He’s still agonising over the seating plan. Apparently, Uncle Barry and Auntie Carol have had a falling out over a garden gnome. A garden gnome?! Seriously? That’s… peak family drama. It’s like a real-life soap opera with more floral arrangements. Exactly. I offered to mediate, but he just said, “Don't get involved, it’s a minefield.” I think he’s enjoying the chaos a little bit. Probably. He always did thrive on a bit of conflict. Have you seen that new Wes Anderson film yet? The one with the quirky colour palette and the overly symmetrical shots? Not yet. I’ve been meaning to. I’m buried under journal articles at the moment. It's supposed to be really good though, isn’t it? Margot Robbie’s in it, right? Yeah, and Jason Schwartzman. It’s wonderfully absurd.

Honestly, the prices around here are just… scandalous. You’d think being so far out, it'd be cheaper, wouldn’t you? But everyone from down south is snapping things up as second homes. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? Even little villages that used to be completely overlooked are suddenly ‘desirable’. Drives up the cost for locals, makes it impossible for young people to get on the ladder. It’s that VW scandal all over again, really. They lied, cheated, and now everyone’s paying the price. Not literally, with cars crashing, but the principle… It’s a ripple effect. Confidence shaken, markets distorted. That money flowing  somewhere … definitely inflating property values. VW scandal. That was a mess. Still makes me furious when I think about it. Liam – my brother, you remember him? – he traded his Golf in just a few months after it all came out. Lost a fortune. Said he couldn’t trust the brand anymore, and frankly, who could? It was a huge breach of trust. I remember reading articles at the time about how they deliberately programmed the cars to cheat emissions tests. It’s not just about the money, it's the sheer dishonesty of it all. And it’s not isolated, is it? You look at the banking crisis, the PPI mis-selling… It feels like there’s always someone getting away with something. Pushing the boundaries, exploiting loopholes. And the ordinary person always ends up footing the bill. This housing market… it feels like one big loophole being exploited. It absolutely does. Remember when we were looking in Penrith? Little cottage, lovely garden… asked for £200,000. Boom! Within a week, another one went on the market for £220,000, same size, same condition. Just because it had a ‘southern appeal’, apparently. “Southern appeal.” Sounds like a marketing term invented to justify inflated prices. What exactly does that even  mean ? A slightly nicer kitchen? A magnolia wall? It’s perception, isn’t it? They think everything north of… well, Birmingham, frankly, is cheaper and cheerful. They come up here, slap on an extra fifty grand, and assume someone will pay it just because they’ve got a London postcode. It's infuriating! I was talking to old Mrs. Henderson down at the shop, and she was telling me her granddaughter can’t afford to live in the village she grew up in.

Honestly, Arthur, you've got a knack for upsetting people, haven’t you? Even on the phone. Now, now, Harold. I weren't trying to upset anyone. Just stating a fact. Young Timothy said the council were thinking of putting houses up by the old orchard. A fact, Harold, a fact! He probably didn’t appreciate you then telling him it was a terrible idea and they hadn’t a clue what they were doing. Timothy’s a nice lad, trying to do his job. Well, it  is  a terrible idea, isn’t it? Another housing development. Where will everyone park? And it’ll ruin the view. Beautiful orchard that was, full of apples. It’s change, Arthur. Everything changes. You can’t stop it. Though, I agree, another lot of houses… it’s a bit much. Still, we’re alright. Got our little bungalow, pension’s… well, it’s enough. Aren’t complaining, are we? Enough to keep the lights on and the telly going. But it doesn’t stretch to much else, does it? Remember when pensions were decent? You could actually  live  on them. Oh, don’t start on the pensions again, Arthur. It won't do your blood pressure any good. And honestly, the telly is enough entertainment for you, you watch it all day. He's got his routines, hasn’t he? Morning telly, afternoon telly, evening telly. It’s a wonder he even remembers to eat. Speaking of which, have you seen young Emily lately? It's been ages. Not since Christmas. She said something about taking the little ones to Weston-super-Mare for a week. Staying in one of those…bed and breakfasts. Can’t stand bed and breakfasts, myself. Always smell of stale cooking and damp. Emily loves a bit of seaside air. Good for the children. Though a bed and breakfast…it does sound a bit cramped. I remember when we used to take the children camping. Now  that  was an adventure. Camping. Now  that’s  something I could never get my head around. Lying on the cold, hard ground in a tent! No thank you. Give me a proper bed any day. Though, speaking of proper beds, did you read about old Mr. Henderson? Apparently, he’s having to sell his house. Can’t afford the repairs. Poor old chap. They’re building flats on every scrap of land around here.

Honestly, the physics practical was a disaster. I completely messed up calculating the resistance. Mr. Davies looked  so  disappointed. Tell me about it. I spent like, three hours trying to write up the biology report on natural selection. Honestly, it all feels a bit pointless. Like, what’s the point of knowing how finches’ beaks evolved? It’s not pointless! It's foundational to understanding, like, everything! Evolution is how life  works . Though I agree, writing about it is painful. Did you guys see that TikTok going around about the lady who thinks evolution is just a theory? Oh my god, yes! The comments were…a lot. It’s like, the scientific method exists, you know? Evidence, observation…it’s not just someone’s opinion. People are wild. Speaking of wild, did you see Sarah and Ben broke up? Again. No way! That's, like, the fifth time this year. What happened this time? Apparently, he liked a picture of another girl on Insta. Classic Ben. Honestly, I don’t get why she keeps going back to him. It's a whole dramatic thing. She says he understands her, but he clearly doesn’t respect her boundaries. It’s kind of…toxic, isn’t it? Totally. And it's always the same cycle. He apologises, she takes him back, he does it again. It's exhausting just watching it. It’s weird how different everyone is with relationships, though. Liam and Chloe have been together for, like, forever and they seem genuinely happy. It’s almost suspicious. Maybe they just have good communication? Radical idea, I know. Seriously though, it makes you think about what you want. I’m definitely not looking for drama like Sarah and Ben. Me neither. I’ve been thinking about all that stuff we talked about in PSHE, about sexism and stuff. It's just… everywhere, isn't it? Even in relationships. Yeah, it’s messed up. Like, I saw this thing online about how women are held to a different standard than men when it comes to, like, how many partners they’ve had. It’s not fair. It's double standards all the way down. And then when you try to call it out, you get called a feminist and it's like… being a feminist just means you believe in equality! It shouldn't be a dirty word. Exactly! It’s just basic human decency.

Honestly, the hospital was a nightmare yesterday. The waiting room was packed, absolutely rammed. And you know what it’s like – everyone coughing and spluttering. I’m convinced I’ll pick up some dreadful infection before my actual operation. Oh, you poor thing. You really shouldn’t worry too much, love. Stress won’t help. And you’ve got a good immune system, you always have. Remember when little Timmy next door gave you that awful bug and you bounced back in a day? That Timmy was a little terror. Always covered in muck. But she’s right, dear. You’re a strong one. Though hospitals  are  breeding grounds. I swear, every time your father went in for something, he’d come out with something else. Aye, that's the truth. Used to say he went into hospital for a broken leg and came out with the plague! Though, mind, he always moaned about the food. Said it was fit for pigs, he did. It’s just… it’s a big operation, isn't it? And then all the tablets afterwards. So many! I’ve made a spreadsheet to keep track. Honestly, it's ridiculous. Three times a day, with food, without food, different dosages... I’ll be rattling like a maraca. Oh, that’s clever, a spreadsheet. I’d be lost without a list. I barely remember what I had for breakfast, let alone a complicated medication schedule. Have you asked about acupuncture? Old Mrs. Higgins swears by it for pain management. Acupuncture? Oh, nonsense. It's all quackery. A waste of money if you ask me. Give me a good cup of tea and a lie-down, that’s what works. Though, to be fair, your Auntie Maureen swears it helped her arthritis... Maureen’d swear anything if you offered her a biscuit. Speaking of which, are those scones I smell? Lovely! Yes, I made scones! They should take your minds off hospitals and needles. Dad, you’re terrible. And Mum, yes, Auntie Maureen… well, she’s enthusiastic. I haven’t looked into acupuncture. It just seems… a bit much. It's worth a look, love. It can't hurt. Though, if it makes you feel better, I’m here to help you with your pills, alright? I can come round every day and make sure you take them properly. That's really kind of you, actually. Thank you. It’s just… I feel like I’m letting everyone down with this.

Right, so we were talking about what we learned at school today, weren’t we? Leo, what did  you  learn about today? We learned about… slavery. It was really, really bad. People were mean. Yeah! And they took people from their families! It’s not fair! No, it absolutely wasn’t fair. It’s hard to imagine, isn’t it? That people thought it was okay to  own  other people. Why did they do it? That’s a really good question. Well, some people wanted to make lots of money growing things like cotton and sugar, and sadly, they used enslaved people to do that work, without paying them, or letting them have any freedom. It was a very selfish and cruel thing to do. Did they get in trouble? Eventually, yes. It took a very long time, and a lot of brave people had to fight for it, but slavery was eventually made illegal. But it caused a lot of pain and suffering for a  long  time. Like in that book we read about the pirates? They were baddies too. Sometimes, yes. Some pirates were very mean, and they did bad things. And you know, sometimes, even people who are fighting for what they believe in can do things that are wrong. Sometimes, when there's a war… We learnt about World War Two! Grandma told me about the bombs! Yes, Grandma did! War is terrible, isn’t it? It’s when countries disagree and fight each other, and it means lots of people get hurt, and sometimes die. Why do they fight? That’s a complicated question, sweetie. Sometimes it’s about land, sometimes it’s about ideas, and sometimes it’s about power. But it always causes so much sadness. And even in war, there are rules, you know? Like, you're not supposed to hurt people who aren’t fighting. But sometimes, those rules get broken. Did soldiers get sad? I think many of them did. It's very scary to be in a war. And it’s important to remember that even soldiers are people, with families and feelings. It’s easy to think of them as just fighting, but they’re also often very young, and they have to deal with very difficult things. It all sounds really horrible. It is horrible. And that’s why it’s so important to learn about it, so we can try to make sure it doesn’t happen again.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from that  Great British Menu  final. What a nail-biter! I thought Mark was a goner when his pudding went wrong. He was lucky, wasn’t he? I thought the Welsh chef had it in the bag. Her menu was just… stunning. Proper artistry. It's so stressful to watch, though. All that pressure! I couldn't cook a decent meal under that kind of scrutiny. I barely manage dinner on a Tuesday. You’re not wrong there. I admire their dedication, but give me a simple roast any day. Speaking of which, Mrs. Higgins next door was telling me her daughter is engaged. Apparently, he proposed at a rugby match. At a rugby match? Loud proposal that one, I reckon. Hope she said yes! Can’t stand a disappointed bride, can you? Reminds me of poor old Doris, back in the day... Oh, not the Doris story again, Dad! We’ve heard it a hundred times. Just saying! Always a cautionary tale. Anyway, did anyone see that article about Dame Judi Dench learning to rap? Yes! It’s incredible! She’s 89! And she’s dropping beats. It’s officially the coolest thing I’ve seen all week. They said it was for a charity single. Good on her. Always willing to help a good cause. It’s refreshing to see that sort of thing. It makes you realize some of these celebrities actually have hearts. It does. Although, I saw a picture of that dreadful Katie Price’s new… renovations. Honestly, it looks like a Barbie dreamhouse exploded. Don’t even mention her. It’s all a bit vulgar, isn’t it? Reminds me, we need to get the gutters cleaned. The squirrels are building a nest up there again. Squirrels are adorable, though! They try so hard. Adorable until they start chewing through the wiring. Remember last year’s Christmas lights debacle? Ah, yes… the blackout. That was a good Christmas, though. Ended up playing charades by candlelight. That  was  fun. We should do that again this year. Oh, and speaking of fun, have you all booked anything for the summer? We’re still dithering. Thinking maybe Cornwall. Cornwall’s lovely. Bit crowded now, though. We’re thinking of trying the Isle of Wight. Never been. Ooh, Isle of Wight! I’ve heard the music festival there is amazing. It is, but it’s also incredibly muddy.

Right, okay, dishwasher duty. Lily, can you unload the cutlery, please? Thomas, you can get the plates. Gently now, those are Mummy’s good ones. But I  always  do the cutlery! It’s boring. You did it last time, yes. But everyone takes turns, remember? It’s fair. And think of it as… a sorting challenge! Like at Hogwarts! Hogwarts? Like Harry Potter? Exactly like Harry Potter! You’re sorting the cutlery into its correct house. Forks are Gryffindor, because they’re brave and pointy. Spoons are Hufflepuff, because they’re reliable and good at scooping. What about knives? Knives are Slytherin. A little bit cunning, aren’t they? And the teaspoons are Ravenclaw – clever and small! Slytherin knives! Now, be careful with those plates, Thomas. You’re doing brilliantly. You know, unloading the dishwasher… it's actually a little bit like what George Stephenson did. Who? Is he in Harry Potter? No, no. George Stephenson was a really important engineer. He built the first public railway line. Imagine trying to move lots and lots of plates… or anything really… from one place to another. Before Stephenson, it was all done by horse and cart. Really slow! So he made trains? He did! He invented things that made trains much faster and more efficient. He was a bit like… sorting everything into the right order so it could travel quickly. Like we’re sorting the dishwasher! But trains are way more exciting than the dishwasher. They are! But he had to start somewhere, didn’t he? He used to mend clocks when he was a boy, can you believe that? Tiny little gears and springs…a really precise job. Clocks? Like Grandad’s cuckoo clock? Exactly like Grandad’s! Stephenson was really good with his hands and worked out how things fitted together. Just like you’re doing with the plates. It’s all engineering, really. This is for Professor Dumbledore! He likes tea. Oh, excellent choice Lily. A very wise professor indeed. Now, is everything out? Double check…there's always one sneaky spoon left hiding at the bottom. I found one! A Hufflepuff spoon! Wonderful! You two are fantastic dishwashers. Now, who wants a biscuit to reward their engineering skills? Speaker_2 & Me! Okay, okay, one each. But after that, it's practicing times tables. No escaping real-world challenges, even for Hogwarts students and future engineers! Aw, Mum. Sorry darling, but it’s important.

Right, I’m officially beat at Words With Friends. She just played ‘quixotic’ for like, eighty points. Eighty! Ouch. That's brutal. She’s ruthless, isn’t she? Is it still Sarah? Yeah, Sarah. She’s on a roll. I think she’s secretly a Scrabble champion in disguise. Honestly, the vocabulary. Speaking of rolls… these garlic knots are nearly ready. Anyone want to test one? I think I nailed the proofing this time. Ooh, absolutely! Garlic knots are my weakness. Though, honestly, anything you bake, Liv, is gold. Seriously, you should be running a full-blown bakery, not just a side hustle. Tell me about it. The sourdough alone is worth queuing for. You know, I was thinking… we should actually  do  a proper supper club. Like, a themed one. Oh, that’s a good idea! What theme? Medieval banquet? Futuristic food? I was thinking something simpler. Maybe Italian night? I could do a proper pasta-making demonstration, antipasto platter, the whole nine yards. Sounds amazing. Though… remember Mark’s attempt at a supper club? The legal issues were a nightmare. Something about needing licenses for serving alcohol and food publicly. Oh god, yeah. He got shut down by the council halfway through. It was chaos. Exactly! We’d need to be careful. Maybe just BYOB and stick to strictly food. Or, we could find a café that’d let us rent the space for an evening. That'd be easier. Like, maybe yours, Charlie? Hmm, tempting, but I’m already stretched as it is. And the insurance… ugh. Don’t even get me started. Things have been  crazy  busy since Old Man Hemmings started complaining about the latte art. Said it was "too modern." Honestly. Too modern?! What does that even mean? Classic Hemmings. He’s a dinosaur. Remember when he tried to get me to stop making flat whites because they weren’t “proper coffee”? Oh, I remember! You told him they were basically just a smaller cappuccino. He wasn’t having it. Right, well, while you’re all reminiscing about grumpy customers, I’m getting these knots in the oven. Ben, can you chop the parsley? It's on the counter. Sorted. So, back to Sarah and Words With Friends… I need a strategy. Maybe I should start just randomly throwing letters at the board and hoping for the best. That's... not a strategy. Maybe try looking up some high-scoring two and three-letter words?

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think I’ll stick to a sandwich tomorrow. Yes, it is…interesting. I brought some borscht from home today. Would you like to try? My grandmother's recipe. Oh, that sounds lovely, actually! I’ve always wanted to try proper borscht. Is it…beetroot-y? Very beetroot-y! And a little sour cream on top. It’s quite filling, perfect for a cold day like today. Sounds perfect. How are things with little Leo? Is he enjoying nursery? He is! He’s finally starting to talk a bit more. He repeats everything you say, it’s hilarious. Though mostly it’s “no!” and “more!” right now. Very challenging. Oh, that’s the age, isn't it? My Ben was exactly the same. Testing boundaries from the moment he could speak. He’s thirteen now, you wouldn’t believe it. Still tests boundaries, to be fair. I can imagine. It never really stops, does it? Do you have any hobbies to help cope with the teenage years? I’ve taken up pottery. Sounds terribly middle-class, I know, but it’s really therapeutic. Getting your hands dirty, creating something… it’s a good release. What about you? Still doing your photography? Yes! I’m actually taking a course next month, a landscape photography workshop. I’m hoping to improve my composition. I’m obsessed with capturing the fens. It’s so atmospheric. Oh, that’s fantastic! The fens  are  beautiful. Very stark, but beautiful. You’ve got a good eye for it, I’ve seen your photos. Thank you! Speaking of work…have you heard anything more about the new IT system they’re rolling out? I’m a bit worried about the extra workload. Oh,  don’t  get me started. They announced another training session today. On a Saturday. Honestly, the organisation of this is a shambles. They haven’t thought it through at all. That’s awful! A Saturday? That's ridiculous. It feels like they just expect us to absorb it all. Exactly! I’ve mentioned to Mrs. Davies that they need to stagger the training, give us time to actually implement what we've learned without being swamped. She said she’d raise it, but… I know how that goes. “I’ll raise it” usually means “I’ll add it to a very long list that will never be seen again.”

Right, so are we definitely going the right way? Because this doesn’t look like… Mothercare way. It looks like we’re going towards… Ribbleton. Aye, I’m sure I’m right. Just trust yer Dad, love. I know Preston like the back o’ me hand. We just need to swing left at the next roundabout, then it’s dead straight. Are you  sure , darling? Because the satnav said to turn right back there, near that Tesco. Maybe we missed a turn? Satnav! Pah. Waste of time, those things. Always sendin’ ya the long way round. I’ve been drivin’ in Preston for fifty years, I think I can manage a trip to Mothercare. Fifty years… that’s before mobile phones even existed, isn’t it? Imagine navigatin’ without Google Maps. We used maps, lass! Actual paper maps! And a bit of common sense. Which seems to be in short supply these days. Alright, alright. Let’s just see where this takes us. Did you get everything on the list, Emilia? The little blankets? The… the thing for the bottles? Yeah, I got the blankets. They’re so soft! And the bottle steriliser, and the… oh, wait. Did you want the ones with the little bears on, or the plain white ones? I got the bears because they were cuter. The bears are lovely! Perfect. They’ll look so sweet. Everything is so expensive though, isn't it? This baby is going to cost a fortune. It’s worth every penny, though. Isn’t it? A little grandkid… best investment you’ll ever make. Yeah. It’s just… weird, thinking about having a little tiny human. I mean, I was a tiny human once, obviously, but… it all feels so far away. Like when I was still at college. You weren’t  that  young, Emilia. Just a few years ago. Feels like a lifetime! I remember sneaking out to go to the pictures with Chloe, pretendin' we were going to the library… remember that, Dad? I remember gettin’ a phone call from yer Head of Year! "Young Emilia and Chloe seen at the Odeon, sir!" Nearly had a heart attack. Thought you’d both been kidnapped. Oh, Dad! It was just  Mean Girls . Speaking of jobs… did you hear back from the university about that internship, Emilia? They said they’re still reviewing applications. It’s probably a no. Everyone wants to do marketing, apparently.

Ugh, I’m so stuck on this level of ‘Starlight Kingdoms’. It’s impossible! Starlight Kingdoms? Is that still a thing? Thought you’d have moved on to something else by now, love. You've been on that for months. Yeah, it’s a bit addictive. She's been grinding for ages trying to get the Sunstone Amulet. Apparently, it unlocks a whole new map. It  does ! And it’s the final thing I need to beat the Crimson King. But this puzzle… it’s really messing with my head. It's like, psychological warfare or something. Psychological warfare in a computer game? Oh, the youth of today. Back in my day, we had to  go outside  to get frustrated. Mum! It's a complex strategic challenge! It requires spatial reasoning and… and… a good internet connection. She’s right, actually. Some of those puzzles are pretty clever. Have you tried looking up a walkthrough online? I have! But everyone's doing it differently, and none of them work! It’s so annoying. I’m starting to feel… defeated. Defeated? Over a game? Honestly. It's nearly Christmas, you should be feeling festive, not defeated by pixellated dragons. Have you thought about presents yet? I’m still trying to figure out what to get your father. He’s impossible. He said he wanted a telescope, didn’t he? To look at the stars. Bit ironic, considering you’re stuck in ‘Starlight Kingdoms’. A telescope… yes, but he also said something about a new gardening trowel. Men! Always changing their minds. What about you two? Any Christmas travel plans? I was thinking maybe we could go to Brighton for the day? We haven’t been in ages. Although, uni applications are stressing me out. I haven’t even finished my personal statement. Brighton sounds good. I've got a couple of interviews lined up in January, so I need to crack on with some revision. It’s just… finding the motivation is hard. I feel like all I do is apply for jobs or study. It's exhausting. It will all be worth it in the end, darling. You’re a bright lad, you'll be fine. Remember when you were little and you were obsessed with taking things apart to see how they worked? Science was always your thing. Yeah, well, sometimes I wonder if I should have just stuck with dismantling toasters instead of aiming for astrophysics.

Right, so I was explaining to Mrs. Higgins today about different metals, because we were talking about armour in history. And I realised… do you two even know the difference between, like, iron and steel? Is steel shiny? Iron is… rusty? Well, iron  can  be rusty, yes. That's what happens when it oxidises. But steel is iron  with  carbon added, which makes it stronger. And shinier, generally. It's a whole chemical process. Ooooh. Like Minecraft! You need iron to make iron tools, but you need diamonds to make diamond tools! And netherite! Netherite is the best! It floats in lava! Yes, yes, you’re both Minecraft experts. Though I’m not sure Minecraft is the best source of metallurgical information. Speaking of valuable resources, apparently, amethyst is really good now, isn't it? For…spectral arrows? Yeah! You can see through walls with them! I built a whole amethyst farm. Impressive. You’re far more dedicated than I am. Anyway, this all got me thinking… remember Old Man Hemlock and his story about the Silverwood? The Silverwood? Was that the tree that grew coins? No, that was the Goldengrove! The Silverwood was supposed to be a tree with leaves of pure silver, guarded by a griffin. He swore his grandfather saw it when he was a boy, somewhere near the old quarry. A griffin! Like a lion with wings? Exactly. Apparently, the silver leaves could cure any illness. It was a completely invented legend, of course, but Old Man Hemlock told it with  such  conviction. I always wondered if he truly believed it. Maybe he did! Maybe it’s still there! We could go look! It’s probably just a very shiny birch tree now, darling. Speaking of believing things… have you both been taking your vitamins? I left them on the side this morning. I had the fizzy ones! They tasted like oranges. I didn’t want mine. They smell funny. They’re important! Especially with everything going around at school. And besides, you need to grow big and strong like… like steel! Stronger than iron! Can I go back to Minecraft now? I'm building a portal to the end. Okay, okay. Just promise me you won’t try to smelt amethyst into a sword. Can I watch? Of course. Just finish your milk first. And maybe, just maybe, we’ll check out Old Man Hemlock’s quarry next weekend.

Honestly, I’m proper knackered. That seminar this morning was a right slog. Three hours on Victorian poetry… honestly. Tell me about it. Mine was on the French Revolution. Sounds interesting, aye? It wasn’t. Just endless dates and names. Proper boring. Fancy another drink? Go on then, why not. Same again? Lager shandy? Aye, sounds good. You know, I was thinking about getting back into playing guitar. Haven't touched it in ages. Oh yeah? That's a good shout! You were really good, weren’t you? Remember when we tried to start a band in year ten? Don't remind me. “The Misfits”, was it? Absolute disaster. Me trying to be the cool singer, you on bass looking miserable, and Liam trying to drum on anything he could get his hands on. He  was  terrible on the drums. But we had fun, didn’t we? Before everything got… weird. Yeah. It's just… makes you think, doesn't it? About people. Like, remember Mark from school? Ugh. Don't even. He was always a bit… off, wasn’t he? I heard stuff, years later, after we left. Really horrible stuff. Honestly scares me sometimes, thinking about it. Don't. Honestly, don’t go there. It’s… it's awful. It makes my skin crawl. You hear stories now and then, and it just makes you sick. I know, I know. It’s just. You try to remember people as they were, but then you hear something like that and it colours everything. It’s vile. Like, how can someone  be  like that? Don't think about it. Seriously. We're all just trying to get through uni, have a laugh. Let's try and keep things happy, yeah? Right. You're right. Sorry. Didn’t mean to bring the mood down. What about hobbies then? Anything else you've been up to besides suffering in seminars? I’ve started knitting. Knitting? You? Yeah! Don’t laugh. It’s surprisingly relaxing. Keeps my hands busy when I'm supposed to be reading. I'm making a scarf. It's… progressing slowly. It looks a bit wonky. I can imagine. You're not exactly known for your precision. But hey, at least you're being productive! I might actually pick up the guitar again. Need something to distract myself from all the history textbooks. Maybe we can jam, if you promise not to laugh at my questionable musical talent.

Seriously though, have you even  started  your EPQ? Mr. Davies is gonna kill us all if we haven’t got a decent proposal by next week. Dude, don’t even remind me. I’m doing mine on the history of skateboarding, but it's just…so much research. Like, where do you even  begin  with the history of a plank of wood with wheels? That actually sounds kinda cool. I’m stuck on veganism and ethical consumerism. It feels really preachy, even to me, and I’m the one doing it! Plus, everyone just assumes you’re judging their burger choices. Oh god, yeah. You get  that  look. Mine's on the impact of social media on political polarization. Super edgy, right? But it's mostly just me scrolling through Twitter getting more depressed. Sounds about right. At least skateboarding has some fun visuals. I’ve been watching old Tony Hawk videos for “research.” Mostly just an excuse to watch skateboarding, tbh. Speaking of fun… remember that Montenegro trip we were talking about last year? Has anyone actually looked at flights? Briefly. They’re… not cheap. And my mum keeps hinting that she’d rather I saved the money for uni. Which, fair enough, but Montenegro! My parents would probably say ‘no’ just on principle. “Too far away, too many unknowns, what about your A-Levels?” the usual. Ugh, parents. Mine are slightly more chill, but they’re still hovering. I was thinking maybe we could all chip in, like a little travel fund? That’s a good idea. I could probably get a shift or two at the cinema. The pay’s awful, but it’s something. What about you, Liam? I’m trying to convince my uncle to let me help him with some gardening over the holidays. Pays a bit better, and it’s outdoors. Less… soul-crushing than the cinema. That actually sounds pretty nice. Okay, travel fund is a go then? We could even start a little spreadsheet. I’m getting  very  organised for this. You and spreadsheets… a match made in heaven. Right, so Montenegro... what do we even  do  there? Aside from, you know, failing our A-Levels. I saw some pictures, it's got like, amazing mountains and coastlines. Apparently the food's good too. Lots of seafood. Oh, brilliant. More seafood for you two. I’ll be over here with a sad plate of chips.

Honestly, this kitchen is a disaster zone. Like, who leaves dirty dishes for  days ? It's grim. Tell me about it. I walked in earlier and nearly slipped on something… questionable. Honestly, I’m starting to think living in halls was cleaner. And that’s saying something. You both make it sound like a biohazard zone. It’s not  that  bad. Though I do agree, the passive-aggressive notes about washing up are getting a bit much. Yeah, the notes are just… intense. Someone wrote “Are you incapable of basic hygiene?” on a post-it stuck to the microwave. The microwave! Oh my god, that’s brutal! Seriously, who raised these people? It's just a plate, wash it! My nan would have a fit. She'd say, “A clean house is a sign of a clear mind!” Mine would just shout. Loudly. She’d be horrified I’m paying this much money to live somewhere that looks like a student squat. Rent’s insane, isn’t it? I swear, half my student loan just vanishes into the landlord’s pocket. You’re telling me. I’m working part-time just to cover it, and even then, I’m having to be really careful with money. My parents aren’t exactly rolling in it, so I can’t ask them for help. Same. Mum keeps sending me these links to budget recipes, bless her. Like I haven't heard of beans on toast before. It's sweet, but… it feels a bit demoralising, you know? Like I should be out enjoying being at uni, not meticulously calculating the cost of every meal. My mum’s the same. Constantly asking if I’m “managing” and sending me care packages full of biscuits. Which is nice, but I’m trying to eat less sugar! Oh, speaking of mums, did you hear Sarah’s mum apparently booked a weekend visit for her… without even  asking  her? No way! Seriously? Swear to God. Sarah was saying she’s dreading it. Her mum’s planning a sightseeing tour and has already booked them into a fancy afternoon tea place. Apparently, Sarah just wanted a quiet weekend to catch up on work. That’s… a bit much. Some parents just don’t get it, do they? They think uni is some sort of extended holiday. It's awkward, isn’t it? My parents are pretty chill, thankfully.

Honestly, Mum, the kids are already driving me round the bend about Christmas. Leo’s written a list as long as his arm, mostly Lego, naturally. And Freya’s decided she  needs  a unicorn. A real one, apparently. Oh, children. They never change, do they? I remember your brother, Rhys, convinced he could train a seagull to deliver presents. He spent weeks building it a harness! Your father nearly had a fit. Oh god, Rhys. That sounds… classic. He always was a bit of a dreamer. Still is, I suppose. Did you manage to get everything sorted for Christmas at yours? Are Gareth and Sarah coming down? Yes, they are! They’re bringing little Amelia with them. She’s grown so much since last Christmas, it’s lovely. I’m attempting a full Christmas dinner, but honestly, I’m slightly dreading it. It's a logistical nightmare, isn't it? Trying to please everyone. Tell me about it! I’m thinking of just ordering a takeaway and pretending I slaved over a hot stove. Saves a lot of stress, you know? You wouldn’t! Your grandmother would haunt you. She’d be turning in her grave. She was a phenomenal cook. Remember her mince pies? How could I forget? They were legendary. I think I tried to recreate them once and… well, let’s just say they didn't quite live up to Nana’s standard. They were slightly burnt and tasted vaguely of cinnamon and regret. Oh, darling. That sounds about right. Speaking of regret, how’s the teaching going? Still enjoying it? Are you still in Vietnam, or have you moved on? Still in Vietnam, actually. It’s… interesting. It’s definitely not Torquay, that’s for sure! The culture is amazing, and the kids are lovely, but sometimes it’s just… exhausting. Trying to explain things when the language barrier is so big. And the heat! It’s stifling. I can imagine. You always did prefer a good British drizzle. Are you planning to come home for Christmas, then? Or stay put over there? I’m trying to save up to come home next year, maybe for a proper summer holiday. Christmas is just too expensive with the flights, you know? I’ll have to settle for a slightly surreal Christmas in Vietnam, with a plastic Christmas tree and a very confused Santa. Well, that sounds… memorable, at least.

So, new phone then? Looks fancy. Is it one of those foldable ones? Nah, just a regular… well, relatively regular. Got a Pixel 8 Pro. Needed an upgrade, mine was on its last legs. Battery life was atrocious. Seriously, I could watch the percentage drop in real-time. You still got that old… brick? Hey! It works. Does what I need it to do. Calls, texts, Spotify. What more could a man want? Though, yeah, the camera is… functional. It’s seen better days. It's a testament to British engineering, really. Surviving this long. British engineering? That thing’s probably Chinese made, let’s be honest. Speaking of which…Have you noticed how much  everything  has changed around Crayford? It's all flats now. Used to be fields, you know? Fields! Yeah, it’s the same everywhere. They’re building on every bit of green space they can find. Profit margins, innit? Though, I heard they’re putting in more speed cameras around there. Oh, brilliant. More revenue generation. They’re just waiting for people to slip up. Thinking about getting my license renewed actually. Been putting it off. It’s the eye test I’m worried about. Shouldn't be a problem, Dad. You've got 20/20 vision… of sarcasm. Seriously though, how’s work? Still dealing with angry callers all day? You have no idea. It’s been mental lately. Everyone's got an opinion and they’re all very keen to share it with me, usually involving shouting. And I was down with the flu last week. Knocked me for six. Couldn't move for three days. Ouch. Get well soon-ish. Any progress on the Brighton move? Still thinking about it? Still thinking. Your mum’s not keen, you know. Says it’s too ‘young people-y’. Wants to stay closer to everything here, her friends, the shops… she’s got her routines. But I'm thinking… it’d be nice, a fresh start. Remember that trip to Tanzania we were planning? Tanzania! God, that feels like a lifetime ago. Before… everything. Remember how excited we all were? Yeah, and then your mum’s back went, and the whole thing fell through. Shame really. I've put on weight though, haven’t I? Feel like I’m expanding exponentially. You're looking good, Dad. Really. It's… a comfortable look. We should definitely try and do something like that again though, a proper trip.

Honestly, the supermarket was  heaving . I just wanted milk and bread, ended up spending forty quid. Forty! Forty? What happened? Did you succumb to the biscuit aisle again? Don't even. No, it was fruit and veg, actually. Apparently, everyone decided they needed organic kale today. And then I got suckered into a meal deal for lunch…it’s a vicious cycle. The meal deal is the downfall of us all. Though, to be fair, forty quid isn’t  terrible  these days. Everything’s gone up. It is, isn’t it? It's just… frustrating. It felt like a tiny little shopping trip turned into a major expedition. How was your day? Any interesting PR disasters to report? Thankfully, no disasters. Mostly just fielding questions about the new branding. Everyone’s got an opinion, naturally. It’s like trying to herd cats, honestly. I spent half the morning reassuring people it wasn’t “too modern” and the other half explaining why we couldn't use Comic Sans. Oh, Comic Sans. The bane of your existence. Seriously though, branding is such a minefield. Everyone thinks they're a design expert. Tell me about it. I swear, my auntie emailed me a PowerPoint presentation with alternative logo ideas. She works in accounts. No way! That’s amazing. And terrifying. Did you… acknowledge the PowerPoint? Politely. I thanked her for her “enthusiasm” and gently steered the conversation back to her tax returns. Speaking of enthusiasm, have you seen the gig listings for next month? The Blue Notes are playing down at The Waterfront. Oh, really? The Blue Notes! I haven’t seen them live in ages. They were brilliant when we were students. I know! I was thinking we could get tickets. It'd be a good shout, a bit of nostalgia. That sounds fantastic. Let me just check my calendar… Mid-week or weekend? It’s a Friday night. Perfect end to a long week of quelling branding rebellions. Perfect. Yes, definitely. Let’s book something tomorrow then, before they sell out. You're a lifesaver suggesting something fun. I was starting to feel overwhelmed by the kale and the Comic Sans. Anytime. We need a regular dose of live music to maintain our sanity. Besides, I need someone to roll their eyes at my terrible dancing. Oh, that’s guaranteed. You know I will. Now, about that forty-pound supermarket bill… We  are  having soup for dinner, right?

Right, so onions are softening nicely. Are you sure you don’t want a bit more garlic in this? It needs a little…oomph, I think. No, no, I’m good. Garlic overpowers everything. Honestly. It’s like a bully in a flavour profile. Besides, you know I’m not keen if it’s too strong before bed. Dramatic, as ever. It’s just garlic. Speaking of things needing oomph…have you made any progress on that bean bag? Oh, don’t even. I’ve unravelled three rows already. It’s…challenging. I thought knitting a simple square would be simpler. It’s not. It’s actively mocking me. It sounds like it. Are you using those chunky needles? Maybe thinner ones would help? I am. And the wool is massive. It's supposed to be quick, but it's just…bulky. I’m starting to think I should just buy one. Waste of money. You’re practically halfway there! Plus, think of the satisfaction when it’s finished. Remind me again why you decided to knit a bean bag in the first place? Elara wants one. A bright pink one. Apparently, all her friends have them. And I thought, “Oh, yes, I’ll just  knit  one.” Apparently, I overestimated my abilities. You underestimate them all the time. It'll be lovely. Oh, and I was thinking about the bathroom… Oh dear. What now? Is the shower curtain offensive? It's… dated. And it’s slightly mildewy. I was looking at some online – a nice teal one with a geometric pattern. And maybe a new bath mat? As long as it’s not one of those fluffy ones that hold onto all the water. I hate those. They’re a breeding ground for bacteria. Definitely not fluffy. More of a quick-drying microfibre. And I was thinking, maybe a little shelf above the toilet for candles and…things? A shelf. Hmm. As long as it doesn’t involve me drilling anything into the tiles. I’m perfectly happy with the status quo, honestly. It’s functional. It’s…functional. It could be  nice , though. A little bit of colour. A little bit of… zen. Zen. Right. Well, as long as the zen doesn’t require power tools. Or involves pink wool. This sauce needs stirring. Maybe we should talk about something less…domestic improving. How was your day of transcribing? Any particularly thrilling dictations?

Right then, finished that crossword, mostly. Stuck on 23 down, "A small coastal resort". Six letters. Oh dear. Is it… Bognor? Nah, tried that. Doesn't fit the crossing letters. It's a tricky one, this. Always are in The Times, aren't they? They’re designed to be tricky, Dad. That’s the point. Keeps the brain ticking. Are you having your tea now? Near enough. Just finishing the crossword first. Don’t want to start eating and then get distracted by a revelation. Though I could murder a biscuit with me tea. I made some shortbread yesterday. There's a tin in the kitchen. Bit crumbly, mind you, but perfectly edible. Crumbly’s good! Means they melt in the mouth. Right, lets see… small coastal resort… could be… Margate? No. Southend? Too long. Have you thought about a place in Cornwall? Lots of small coastal resorts down there. St Ives, maybe? Cornwall… hmm. Could be. Does St Ives have six letters? Yes it does! But no, doesn't fit the letters I’ve already got. Blast it all. Don't get yourself all worked up about it, Arthur. It’s just a crossword. Easy for you to say, Doris. You're not the one trying to solve it! It's a matter of principle, you see. Can’t be beaten by a crossword. Remember that one last month, Dad, when you spent three days on one clue? The one about the… antique bedpost? That was different! That was a deliberately obscure clue. This one’s just… stubbornly elusive. Oh, hang on a minute... what about… Whitby? Whitby? Yes! Whitby! Six letters. And… yes! It fits! Finally. Took me long enough. See? Persistence pays off. Although, I suspect you just got lucky. Lucky? No, no, it's skill, pure skill! Years of crossword solving experience. Now, where's those biscuits? Doris, are those biscuits still there? They are, Arthur. Though I suspect your skill might have attracted the attention of the neighbourhood cats. I saw Tibbles looking longingly at the kitchen window earlier. That little rascal. Always sniffing around for crumbs. Right, tea and a biscuit. That’s the life. You two want one? No thank you, Dad, I’m alright. Just finishing up some emails. Oh go on, Arthur. Just the one. They  are  rather nice, even if they are a bit crumbly. I’ll have one too then.

Honestly, I’m absolutely shattered. That shift was… something else. Mrs. Henderson decided today was the day to simultaneously demand two pain killers  and  insist she didn’t want any medication at all. Sounds about right for her. She's a character, that one. Did you manage to navigate that particular conundrum? Eventually. A lot of gentle redirection and promising to check with the doctor. It’s just… draining. And then Ms. Davies was convinced her slippers had been stolen. Slippers? Seriously? Yes! Utterly convinced. Spent twenty minutes searching under beds and in cupboards. They were on her feet. Oh, bless her. They really do start to lose it, don’t they? It’s sad, but you have to find the humour sometimes. Absolutely. Speaking of losing things, has anyone seen the shopping list? I swore I left it on the kitchen counter. I think I saw it under a pile of mail, Dad. By the fruit bowl? Ah, right. Thanks, love. We need to get organised. Christmas is looming, and I haven't even started thinking about presents. Don’t even mention Christmas! I’m still recovering from last year's chaos. Remember Aunt Carol and her insistence on ‘helping’ in the kitchen? Oh god, yes. And the burnt Yorkshire puddings. She’s lovely, but a culinary disaster zone. Have you booked the train tickets to Mum’s, Dad? Not yet. I was hoping to wait for the price to drop a bit, but it doesn’t seem to be budging. It’s ridiculous how expensive it is these days. It is. We’re thinking of driving this year, actually. It'll take longer, but it works out cheaper and we can pack more presents. That's a good idea. Are you still planning on going to the Christmas market in Strasbourg, though? Oh, I’d love to! I've always wanted to go to a proper German Christmas market. Everything looks so magical in the photos. We talked about it. It's just...money's a bit tight this year. Work hasn’t been brilliant, and with the price of everything going up… We'll see. It's early days yet. Maybe if we cut back a little on some things. I'm already dreading the January sales, though. It's all just… consumption, isn't it? True. I’ve been trying to be more mindful of what I buy.

This coffee is lovely, isn’t it? Much stronger than what I’m used to back home. Aye, it’s good stuff. They don't mess about with it here. Been drinking it every morning since I arrived, couldn't start the day without it now. You enjoying your time here so far? Oh, tremendously, thank you. It’s just… different. In a good way, mostly. Though it took me a good three days to adjust to the driving! Oh, the driving. Don’t even get me started. I’ve been coming here for near ten years now, winter months mostly, and I  still  haven’t mastered it. They have a certain… enthusiasm, shall we say? Enthusiasm is one word for it! I had someone overtake me on a blind bend yesterday. I nearly ended up in a field of olive trees. Oh, that’s nothing. Happened to me last year. Ended up face-to-face with a donkey. A donkey, I tell you! Stared me right in the eye like I was the one in the wrong. A donkey! That’s brilliant. I’m still trying to get used to the roundabouts too. They seem to operate on a ‘first one in wins’ basis, rather than any sense of priority. That's it exactly! No one gives way. It’s every man for himself. You just have to commit, really. Just barge your way in and hope for the best. Though, I wouldn't recommend that to a new driver. I think I’ll stick to the buses, to be honest. Have you ventured much inland? Beyond Kyrenia? A bit. I did a trip to Famagusta a few years back. Quite sobering, really. Seeing Varosha, all those abandoned hotels… it’s like stepping back in time. A ghost town. I’ve heard it's very moving. I’m hoping to go next week. A friend recommended a restaurant there, said the seafood is exceptional. The seafood  is  good here. You’ll get a good meal wherever you go, honestly. Although, be careful with the meze. They bring you everything  and  the kitchen sink. You’ll be rolling home. That sounds perfect, actually. I’m on holiday, after all. I need to indulge. Have you tried the halloumi here? It’s incredible. Oh, halloumi! They do it so well. Grilled, fried, in salads… I had it with honey and sesame seeds the other day, absolutely delicious.

Honestly, the students were dreadful today. Just absolutely dreadful. Didn’t read the assigned chapters, kept asking questions we’d already covered… it was relentless. Oh, tough day then? Mine weren't  bad , just… distracted. Lots of chatting, a couple of phones out. Standard Friday afternoon stuff, really. I think they’re all just mentally checked out, anticipating the weekend. I wish I could get away with that level of leniency. It feels like if I let anything slide, the whole class descends into chaos. Dr. Albright keeps hinting about student evaluations being tied to funding… it’s stressful. Ugh, don’t even get me started on institutional pressures. It feels like we spend more time worrying about metrics than actually  teaching . Did you hear anything more from Ben about his funding application? He said he had a meeting with the head of department this morning. Didn't sound optimistic, though. He’s really counting on that grant to continue his research. He was saying the competition is brutal this year. It always is, isn't it? He's brilliant, though. He deserves it. We should invite him and Chloe over for dinner next week. It’ll take his mind off things, at least for a few hours. That’s a good idea. I’ll text Chloe and see what evening suits them. It’s just… I feel like we only ever see people at these incredibly stressful academic events. It’s nice to just have a relaxed evening with friends. Exactly. And we need to catch up properly. It feels like ages since we’ve had a proper chat. It does. Oh, goodness. Look at the haze. It’s particularly bad tonight, isn’t it? Awful. You can actually taste it. It’s getting worse, isn’t it? I saw an article this morning about the increased particulate matter levels. They’re blaming it on the factories further upriver. It’s depressing. I try to cycle to work whenever I can, but days like this… I’m tempted to just take the metro. Though that’s hardly better, is it? Packed like sardines, breathing in everyone else's germs. No, but at least it's a slightly different kind of pollution. We're practically living in a smog bubble here. Still, better than being stuck in traffic, I suppose. True. Small mercies. Actually, speaking of the metro, Sarah was saying she’s thinking of moving back to London.

Right, so onions are chopped, garlic’s minced… anyone fancy helping with the peppers, Chloe? Sure, Mum. Just let me quickly upload these photos from the gallery opening last night. Honestly, the canapés were tiny. Like, one bite and gone. Gallery opening, eh? Sounds fancy. Hope you weren't expected to  buy  anything. I swear, half those places are just setups to extract money from people who look like they might have it. No pressure to buy, thankfully. Mostly just networking. Though there was this one sculpture… shaped like a giant banana. Very thought-provoking. A banana? Right. Well, thought-provoking or not, it doesn’t sound very filling. Speaking of filling, what does everyone fancy with this stir-fry? Rice, noodles…? Noodles for me, please. I’m trying to cut back on the carbs a little. Though looking at this, I suspect ‘a little’ won’t be happening tonight. Smells lovely, Sarah. Thanks, love. Chloe, noodles or rice? Rice, please. So, Dad, what did  you  get up to today? Apart from critiquing the art world, of course. Oh, the usual chaos at the Department. Had a meeting about the new budget which, predictably, involves doing more with less. Then young Thomas forgot to file a crucial report, so spent an hour untangling  that  mess. Honestly, sometimes I wonder why I bother. Oh, Thomas. Bless him. Still learning the ropes, I suppose. You're too kind to cover for everyone. I had a rather stressful day myself. Mrs. Higgins was convinced her oxygen levels were dropping, turned out she’d just been hyperventilating after watching  Bargain Hunt . Oh,  Bargain Hunt ! The drama! Sounds exhausting, Sarah. You nurses deserve medals. Seriously. We manage. It’s the quiet moments, like this, that keep me going. This is nice. Just… chopping vegetables, chatting. Did anyone catch that new detective show on last night? The one everyone's talking about? Oh,  Shadows of Doubt ? Yeah, I did! It's really good, quite twisty. Although I figured out the killer halfway through. I tried to watch it, but fell asleep. Honestly, I think I'm getting too old for all these whodunnits. My attention span isn’t what it used to be. You and me both, dear. Maybe we should stick to  Gardeners’ World . Less stressful. Right, peppers are done. Anyone need a taste-test? Mmm, perfect! You’re a natural, Mum. This is going to be a great stir-fry.

Honestly, this new bus route is a joke. It adds like twenty minutes onto my commute. Twenty! Really? I hadn’t noticed. I haven’t taken the bus in ages, thankfully. Cycling’s still winning out. Though it  was  pouring this morning. Well, you work closer to the city centre. I'm out at the West Cambridge site, it's a nightmare. They’ve rerouted it all through Milton Road, it’s just…chaos. Milton Road is always chaos. It’s a permanent state of being for that road. Did you pop into the Cambridge University Press bookshop yesterday? They had a sale on. No, I didn't, was too knackered after work. Was there anything good? I’ve been meaning to get some new fiction. A few things, mostly academic stuff, to be honest. Though they had a lovely collection of illustrated editions of classic children's books. Thought of your niece. There was a student protesting outside, though. Oh yeah? What about? Cambridge students are always protesting about  something . Something about tuition fees again, I think. With a megaphone and everything. Sounded very passionate. He was stood right outside the bookshop, it was quite a scene. Classic. Proper student behaviour. Reminds me a bit of being at Northumbria, honestly. We were always at it. Though our protests were usually over the quality of the VKs in the student union. Very different priorities. You wouldn’t get that at Cambridge, would you? Everything's rather…refined. It's so different to Newcastle, isn't it? Like night and day. The campus at Northumbria was all brutalist concrete, and everything was a bit rough around the edges. Here it’s all ancient buildings and perfectly manicured lawns. It is. My old college, St John’s, looks like something out of Hogwarts. Although, it can feel a bit… isolating, sometimes. The whole collegiate system. You're very much stuck within your college bubble. Yeah, I can imagine. We just all sort of mingled wherever, in the city centre mostly. Everything was right there. You had the Quayside with all the bars, the Bigg Market...it was proper lively. Sounds… chaotic. Compared to punting on the Cam, it's a world away. How did you find the workload at Northumbria compared to what I remember of Cambridge applicants stressing about? Honestly? It was intense. But in a different way. There was a lot more practical work, a lot more application.

Honestly, this soup is amazing. You’d think after all these years, The Chester Arms would get complacent, but it’s consistently good. It is lovely. Though I’m starting to feel a bit stuffed. Portions are huge. Maybe I shouldn’t have had the bread roll. Oh, go on! You deserve a bread roll. You work too hard, dear. Always running around, solving everyone else’s problems at work. It’s alright, Mum. It keeps me busy. Better than dwelling, you know? Speaking of busy, how are the preparations going for Leo’s visit? Are you nearly ready? Nearly. I’ve managed to clear out the spare room, finally. It was becoming a dumping ground for everything. Though I’m still not sure what to make for him. He's such a fussy eater. He’s a grown man, Mum! He can tell you what he wants. I know, I know. It’s just… I want to make a good impression. It’s the first time he’s properly visiting since… well, you know. Since everything. He’ll be thrilled just to spend time with you, honestly. He talks about you all the time. Says you were the one who taught him to love maths. Oh, he exaggerates. I just tried not to scare him off too much with long division. He was a bright lad, though. Always questioning things. Reminded me of your father. I remember Dad trying to explain fractions to me using biscuits. It never worked. I just ate the biscuits. Sounds about right! Speaking of things not working, I was trying to explain the subjunctive to a client yesterday - a marketing manager, of all people – and it completely went over his head. The subjunctive? Oh, that’s a tricky one. Even  I  had trouble with that when I was teaching. The English language is so… inconsistent. It is! It’s a glorious mess. All these weird rules and exceptions. I was explaining it to little Alfie yesterday actually, he was asking why you say “If I  were  king…” instead of “If I  was  king…” Oh, bless him! He's a bright spark. How’s he doing with his reading? Flying. He’s obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. Wants to be a paleontologist. That’s lovely. A good, solid profession. Not like these… influencers, or whatever they call themselves these days. Do you know what they  do , exactly?

Honestly, it’s just… look at it. All that glass. It feels so… disconnected from everything else, doesn’t it? The O2? Yeah, it’s a bit… brash. A bit much, really.
