Especially alongside all this history. You’ve got the Cutty Sark down there, and then  that . It's like someone plonked a spaceship down. Exactly! And the traffic around it is always horrendous. Honestly, I'm so glad we don't have a car. It’d be a nightmare trying to get anywhere near here on a weekend. Tell me about it. Remember Aunt Carol trying to visit us when we lived in Richmond? She spent two hours circling the roundabout. Ended up parking miles away and walking. Oh, God yes. She was fuming. Still mentions it occasionally. Makes me glad we rely on public transport. Even if it's sometimes… questionable. Questionable is a polite word. Though, it does force you to walk more, doesn’t it? Which is good. Look, we’re almost at Greenwich now. Fancy popping into the market for a coffee? Yes, please! I could murder a coffee. And a pastry. Maybe we should start thinking about the holiday, though. Have you had a chance to look at those cottages in Cornwall? I have. They're nice. A bit… cosy. I’m worried about squeezing all of us in. Especially with the amount of stuff the kids seem to need to take on holiday. It’s ridiculous. Don't even get me started. Apparently, Leo needs three different pairs of swimming trunks, a snorkel, and a bodyboard. He’s eight! Exactly! And Lily insists on bringing her entire collection of stuffed animals. It's a logistical nightmare. I swear, we need a removals van just for their holiday belongings. It’s all a bit mad, isn’t it? All this…  stuff . What do people actually  need  to be happy? That's a proper philosophical question. Deep thoughts by the Thames. That's a new one. Probably a good coffee and a pastry, to start with. Look, there’s that boat trip place. Remember when we did that years ago? Vaguely. I think it was raining. And I ended up getting seasick. Ah, yes. You turned a rather alarming shade of green. Maybe we’ll stick to solid ground this time. And coffee. Definitely coffee. Oh, and speaking of measurements... I was trying to convert a baking recipe from an American website, and it's just  impossible .

Honestly, this rain is relentless. It’s been chucking it down since this morning. Ruined any plans of actually  doing  anything today. Tell me about it! I’m soaked just walking from the car to the house, and that’s with an umbrella. At least it’s good for the garden, I suppose. Though, honestly, everything’s already soggy. My phone’s playing up again. Keeps freezing. I swear, it’s on its last legs. I need a new one, but they’re so expensive! Ugh, phones. They just don't make them to last anymore, do they? It’s planned obsolescence, I’m convinced. Mine's alright, thankfully. Though I dropped it last week, and I was convinced the screen was going to shatter. Remember when phones just…worked? You could drop them, bash them about, and they'd still call someone. Now, you breathe on them wrong, and they’re bricked! Speaking of things that need replacing... little Leo’s sports day is next week and I've lost his sports shoes. Oh no! Where did you last see them? Leo will be gutted. He was so excited about the egg and spoon race. That’s the thing! I have no idea. They were by the back door, I think? I've turned the house upside down. He’s already asking about them, poor lamb. Maybe they're under the sofa? Things always end up under the sofa. Speaking of things disappearing…have you seen Barnaby? Barnaby? The bear? No. Little Maisie had him last. She takes him  everywhere . Honestly, that bear has been to more places than I have. She's obsessed with that bear. Remember when we took her to Build-a-Bear? The drama when she couldn't decide what stuffing to pick. Took us a good hour just to choose the right fluff! Oh, the memories! She wanted the sparkly stuffing, didn't she? Absolutely insisted. It’s funny, isn’t it? The bond they have with those cuddly toys. It is. Although, I’m secretly hoping she starts showing some interest in other things soon. I’m trying to get her potty-trained, and it’s a battle of wills. She’d rather spend her time chatting to Barnaby, apparently. Potty training, hmm. Fun times ahead. My friend’s just started with her little one. Apparently, she’s found glitter in the potty. Oh, no!

Right, so I was thinking… seriously thinking, about the whole consultancy thing. Not just dipping a toe in, but  really  going for it. Oh? That’s… bigger than you let on usually. I thought you were just enjoying the freedom of a few freelance projects. Yeah, well, I am. But the response to that website I threw together has been… surprising. People are actually  reaching out . And not just for quick fixes. Proper strategic stuff. The kind of work I actually enjoyed before the endless meetings and powerpoint presentations. That’s fantastic, really. But are you sure about leaving the security of… well, of having a ‘proper’ job? Especially now. Security is an illusion, love. We’ve talked about this. And honestly, the stress was killing me. I was waking up with anxiety every Sunday night. This… this feels exciting. And lets be real, the earning potential is significantly higher. I know, I know. It’s just…it feels like a big jump. Have you thought about partnering up with Ben and Chloe? They’ve been talking about doing something similar with their marketing skills. You’d complement each other really well. That’s… a very good idea. Actually, a  really  good idea. I mentioned it to Ben briefly when we video-called last week. He seemed pretty keen. We need to hash out the details though – equity, roles, that sort of thing. Definitely. Get that nailed down from the start. I’ve seen too many collaborations fall apart over those kinds of ambiguities. Absolutely. I’m thinking we could meet up with them in Bali next month? They were talking about heading that way anyway. Sort of a working holiday – a bit of sunshine and a lot of brainstorming. Bali… Hmm. That sounds… tempting. But what about the house? We've got another three weeks here house-sitting for Mark and Sarah. And then what? We talked about maybe looking at something a bit more permanent when we got back to the UK. That’s where it gets tricky. I’m not sure I want to go back to the UK full-time just yet. Maybe a longer-term house-sitting gig somewhere else? Or… and this is a bit of a wild thought… what about finally looking into that property we saw in Portugal? The little farmhouse near Lagos? Portugal… You’re serious? We haven’t talked about that in ages!

Honestly, I still can't believe you’ve never played Pokémon. Not even once? Nah, never got into it. Always seemed a bit… childish, init? Plus, all that catching and battling, just seemed like a faff. Childish?! It's a global phenomenon, Liam! And the strategy is surprisingly complex. You clearly haven't seen a competitive battle. It  is  a bit nerdy, though. Remember when Ben tried to trade Pokémon on the bus and nearly started a fight? Oh god, yeah! He was offering a Charizard for a… a Pidgey, I think? The kid was  fuming . Proper little scuffle. Ben was always a bit… optimistic about value. Optimistic is a polite way of putting it. He'd try to sell you a broken biscuit for a fiver. Speaking of optimistic, how’s your mum, Liam? Still trying to set you up with every girl she meets? Don't even. She cornered me at Grandad's last week and started listing off names. Said she knows a girl who works at Costa, "Lovely girl, makes a good latte." As if that’s a personality trait. Oh, mums are the worst for that. Mine’s convinced I’ll end up with a doctor. Like, where am I going to meet a doctor who also enjoys going to gigs and getting chips at midnight? Probably one who’s really into Pokémon… Alright, alright. Easy now. Anyone fancy sending a quick trip to the shop? I'm craving After Eights. I'll go. I need a break from listening to you all argue about pocket monsters and dating dilemmas. Plus, my Fitbit’s telling me I haven’t done enough steps today. You and that Fitbit. Obsessed. It's motivational! Anyway, how long ago was that festival we all went to? The one where it rained for three days straight and we nearly lost the tent? That was… 2018, wasn't it? Absolute disaster. Remember Sarah trying to camp in a ditch because her tent pole snapped? Oh, that was hilarious. She looked so miserable. And then a sheep came and ate her sandwich. Classic Sarah. Always attracting chaos. Speaking of chaos, did anyone see old Mr. Henderson trying to parallel park outside the pub earlier? It was like watching a slow-motion train wreck. No way! I missed that. He's a menace. Honestly, sometimes I think he does it on purpose just to wind people up.

Honestly, that Rashford… all show, isn’t he? Diving around like a salmon. Oh, now, don't be like that, Arthur. He's a good player when he’s on form. Though I did see him go down rather dramatically yesterday. It’s a bit of both, I think. Defenders are certainly quick to make contact these days, but he exaggerates it. You’ve got to give them  something  to call a penalty, haven't you? It's the way the game's gone. Referees are under so much pressure with VAR… they're looking for anything. It’s a bit frustrating to watch, honestly. Frustrating? It's a disgrace! Back in my day, you’d get knocked to next Tuesday and just get up and carry on. No whining. Oh, Arthur, those were different times. They didn’t have the same level of scrutiny. And health and safety… imagine the lawsuits now if they played like that! Speaking of lawsuits… did you all see that story about the celebrity chef and the dodgy scallops? Apparently, they weren’t what they claimed to be. Oh yes! Some sort of imposter scallop situation. Honestly, you can’t trust anyone these days. Still, dodgy scallops are a bit different from Rashford diving. That's true enough. Though both are a bit of a con, if you ask me. What are we having for pudding, by the way? I've been leaving room. I made a trifle! Your favourite, Arthur. With proper custard, not that instant stuff. And strawberries from Farmer Giles’ stall. Strawberries from Giles? Now  that’s  what I’m talking about! He grows a good strawberry, that man. Better than any of this foreign stuff. I need to get some jam from him soon. My students keep asking me about Norfolk produce for their projects… I promised to bring some in. It's good you're incorporating local things into your lectures. Makes it more engaging, I imagine. How are the new courses going? Still swamped with marking? Always swamped with marking! It's the nature of the beast. I'm trying to get the students to debate more, rather than just write long essays. It’s exhausting facilitating, but more rewarding when it works. Oh, you lecturers all work so hard. I don’t know  how  you do it. I was quite happy just looking after little ones and letting their parents deal with the education!

Honestly, I’m starting to think this wasn’t the right move, y’know? Lancaster. Uni in general, maybe. What d’ya mean? You were buzzing for it back in September. All about ‘independence’ and ‘finding yourself’… remember all that? Yeah, well, that was before three weeks of lectures, a dodgy flatmate and realising I actually hate essays on Victorian poetry. It just feels… pointless. Right. The existential crisis has hit. Welcome to the club. Honestly, half the people I know are quietly contemplating dropping out. What about your parents? They’ll be proper gutted. That’s the thing, isn’t it? My mum's already planning my graduation party. She’s got Pinterest boards and everything. She'd be devastated. But staying here, pretending I’m enjoying this… that feels worse. Look, don’t make any rash decisions, yeah? Maybe talk to your personal tutor first? See what options there are? A change of course, maybe? I’ve thought about that. But even the other courses…nothing really grabs me. It’s weird, isn’t it? I always thought I’d  know  what I wanted to do. Nah, most people don’t. My grandad always says I’m too busy thinking about the ‘big picture’ and not enough about the now. He used to be a docker, proper down-to-earth bloke. Says I get it from my mum. A docker? That’s cool. My grandad was a fisherman. Spent his whole life on boats around Falmouth. Smelt permanently of salt and diesel. Mine just smelled of roll-ups and the docks, a truly potent combination. Speaking of potent smells… what  are  those? Your shoes? Oh god. They’re awful, aren’t they? I walked through a muddy field after that party last night. Didn’t even think. You look like you’ve been digging for treasure in a swamp. Honestly, you’re bringing the whole room down. Sorry! I’ll clean them later. It’s just…everything feels a bit overwhelming at the minute. I get it. Just breathe. And clean your shoes. Seriously. Hey, did you ever wonder where your name comes from? Saoirse? It's such a beautiful name, but kinda unusual. My mum’s obsessed with Irish culture. She went on a trip to Ireland when she was younger and just… fell in love with it. She said ‘Saoirse’ means ‘freedom’ or ‘liberty’. A bit ironic maybe, considering how trapped I feel right now.

Honestly, this risotto is  divine . You were right to recommend this place. It's exactly what I needed after that week at work. Told ya! Oxford does a good risotto. And you looked like you needed it. You've been glued to your laptop for weeks, according to your mum. She sends regular ‘rescue reports’, you know. Mum's a menace, but she’s right. Project’s finally wrapped up though. Honestly, the amount of back-and-forth with stakeholders… it was relentless. I think I aged about ten years. Oof, sounds brutal. What was it actually  about  this time? Another system implementation? You’re the queen of seemingly impossible deadlines. Pretty much. New CRM system for the marketing team. Apparently, the old one was held together with sticky tape and prayer. Everyone had different ideas of what they wanted, and nobody could agree. Classic. Sounds… delightful. My job’s comparatively stress-free, thankfully. Pearson's pretty good at, you know,  not  creating artificial crises. Though persuading people that educational materials can be exciting is a challenge in itself. Oh, I can imagine! Trying to make textbooks cool. A noble, but potentially futile, mission. So, how’s work going otherwise? Still loving the marketing side of things? Yeah, mostly. It's good, really good. We’re launching a new series of digital resources for GCSEs, that's taking up a lot of my time. It's just… the office politics are starting to get a bit much. There's this one guy, Darren, who thinks he's the marketing guru, constantly undermining everyone else’s ideas. Ugh, Darren sounds… charming. Every office has one, doesn’t it? The self-proclaimed expert. Exactly! He just steamrolls meetings, and then takes credit for everything. I'm starting to actively dread Monday mornings. Anyway, enough work moaning. How’s the love life? Still seeing… what was his name, Alex? Oh, Alex. That was a… short-lived experiment. Let’s just say he was  very  into CrossFit and talking about his macros. And not much else. Oh no! The macros! That's a red flag if ever I saw one. A huge red flag. It turns out, I'm not particularly interested in the precise protein content of my dinner. We went our separate ways. I swear, dating in your twenties is exhausting. Tell me about it. I haven't even  started  dating. Too busy with work and… avoiding Darren.

Right, now, have you actually  looked  at the postage on this, love? It's adding another ten quid on. Ten quid! For a little bag of Lego. But it's the specific minifigure I want, Mam. It's a limited edition space guy! They don't make them anymore. Limited edition, my foot. They just charge more because they  say  it's limited edition. Honestly, eBay is bandit country. It’s not bandit country! I found a good deal. It’s only twenty-five quid for the minifigure and a little baseplate. Twenty-five quid  plus  ten for postage is thirty-five quid for a plastic man! You could get a whole box of Lego for thirty-five quid. A proper box, with instructions and everything. But I don’t  want  a box. I just want him! He’s going to complete my space battle scene. Space battle scene? You’ve got hundreds of Lego already, you do. Is it greed, is it? Pure greed. It's not greed! It’s collecting! It’s different. And anyway, Lewis has got three of the new Star Wars guys, and I don’t have  any . Oh, here we go. Comparing yourself to Lewis. Right. Well, Lewis's dad works for Amazon, doesn’t he? He probably gets them for free. That's not a fair comparison. He doesn’t get everything for free! He just gets a discount, I think. Discount or free, it’s not the same. Look, let’s just look on Amazon. Sometimes they have the same things, and often the postage is a bit better. Though they're getting sneaky with that now, aren't they? Always trying to get you to pay extra for ‘Prime’ or whatever it is. I don’t want Prime. It's just a waste of money. Exactly. It's a swizz. Right, let’s see… “Limited Edition Space Minifigure”… Oh, look at this one. Looks exactly the same. Is it cheaper? It is. It's… eighteen ninety-nine. And free postage if you spend over twenty quid. But is it  exactly  the same? Does it have the right helmet and everything? Some of them are knock-offs. It says ‘Genuine Lego’. And look, the seller has 99% positive feedback. Seems alright. Ninety-nine percent? What about the one percent? Oh, don’t be daft. It’s probably someone who just changed their mind or something.

So, how was the train up? Dreadful, I expect? Always a nightmare getting out of London on a Friday. Actually, it was surprisingly okay. A bit crowded, obviously, but nothing like the usual chaos. Managed to get a seat, even. And it wasn't delayed, which is a miracle these days. Lucky you. I remember when you could practically  walk  on the lines during Friday evening. No trains at all. Used to hitchhike back to Mum and Dad’s in Mordern, you know. Back in the… well, a long time ago. Seems a different world now. Hitchhiking! Seriously? That sounds terrifying. It wasn’t so bad. People were more trusting then, I suppose. Or maybe just daft. Mostly lorry drivers, bless ‘em. Always happy to give a lift. Used to get some right characters, though. One fella tried to convince me he was a secret agent, heading to a top-secret mission. Oh, wow. You’ve got some stories, Grandad. Stories, eh? I’ve got a lifetime of ‘em, love. What about you? How’s work been? Still keeping those production lines running smoothly? It’s... hectic. We're launching a new product next month, so it's all hands on deck. Lots of late nights and stressed-out colleagues. Honestly, I'm living on coffee and willpower at the moment. Sounds familiar. Though my ‘production line’ was usually just trying to get dinner on the table without burning it. Remember your Nana? She could burn water. I do. She was wonderful, though. Always made a fuss. The best. Always had a biscuit for you, didn’t she? Even if you’d just had a full meal. You’ve put on weight since I last saw you, haven’t you? Grandad! That's a bit rude! It's muscle. From all the… frantic production line supervising. Muscle, eh? Alright, alright. You look well, though. That’s the main thing. Are you seeing anyone nice? Oh, not at the moment. Work's keeping me too busy. Maybe sometime next year. Though honestly, the thought of dating feels… exhausting. It does at our age, believe me. Still, don't rush into anything. There's plenty of time. Now, shall I top up your coffee? And perhaps find some of those biscuits your Nana used to love. Though I can't promise they won't be slightly burnt. It’s in the genes, you know.

Right, so we’re actually tentatively looking at flying out Christmas Day morning. It’s insane, I know. Christmas  Day ? Seriously? That sounds… stressful. Like, airport chaos stressed. Oh, blimey. That’s dedication. Where are you heading anyway? Is it worth the Christmas Day travel trauma? Mum’s in Sydney. She's been on about it for months, and the flights were surprisingly cheap, if you don't mind being up at 3am. Plus, it means we get a longer time with her. Crikey. Flying on Christmas Day. That's a new one. I spent one Christmas working in a servo, watching everyone else rush around. Not glamorous. Honestly, I’m already dreading the food situation. My mum is insisting on making a goose this year. A  goose , guys. It's so much effort, and honestly, a bit much. A goose! Good grief! You’ll be peeling sprouts until Boxing Day. I’m sticking with turkey, traditional as that is. Though I’m thinking of getting a pre-prepared one this year, just for sanity. Pre-prepared is the way to go. I tried to be all ambitious last year and carve the turkey myself… it was a disaster. Looked like a crime scene. Tell me about it. I once tried to deep-fry a turkey. Don’t recommend that, ever. Thankfully, no one was hurt. Just a smoky backyard and a very unhappy insurance company. Speaking of disasters… did you guys hear about Old Man Hemmings down the lane? Apparently he hit a deer on the way back from the pub last night. No way! Was he alright? And the deer…? He’s fine, a bit shaken up. But the deer… wasn’t. Apparently, it was a big stag. Poor thing. They found bits of it all over the road. Blimey. That’s awful. You see so many deer wandering about around here, especially this time of year. It's a wonder it doesn't happen more often. Plenty of wildlife around, alright. I saw a fox in your garden the other night, Jess. Bold as brass, just strolling about like he owned the place. They’re getting braver, aren’t they? I had one trying to get into my bin last week. Little bandit. They're probably wishing for a bit of goose, actually. Though I doubt they’d appreciate the cranberry sauce. So, are we still doing Secret Santa this year?

Honestly, I still can't place where your accent is from. It’s…not quite anywhere specific, is it? That’s what everyone says! I think it’s just a mishmash of everywhere I’ve lived, really. A bit of Hampshire from childhood, a load of London from uni, and then just…general floating about. It probably sounds awful. No, it's nice! Just…unidentifiable. Like a linguistic chameleon. It’s much more interesting than my Brummie drone, honestly. Hey! There's nothing wrong with a Brummie accent. It’s distinctive. Besides, you can tone it down when you need to. I've seen you do it in job interviews. That's survival, mate. Pure survival. They look at you differently if you sound like you've spent your life battling Peaky Blinders. Speaking of different, this car is  smooth . Seriously, it’s like gliding. What is it, a Volvo? Yep. My dad insisted. “Safe, reliable, practical” were his exact words. Apparently, a bright red sports car isn't “sensible” for a newly qualified engineer. Sensible is overrated. Though, I’m grateful for the legroom. I'm starting to regret accepting this lift after that enormous Sunday roast. Tell me about it. I’m officially in a food coma. Still, better than trying to navigate Cambridge traffic on the bus. Did you check the route, Liam? There’s always that weird roundabout near the science park that throws everyone. Yeah, I’ve got it all mapped out. Avoiding the science park roundabout. It’s a black hole of lane discipline. Plus, I’ve got the music sorted. Hopefully, something vaguely palatable for everyone. As long as it's not more 80s power ballads, I’m good. Last time, I genuinely thought my ears were going to bleed. No promises. I’m on playlist duty, you know I can’t resist a bit of Bon Jovi. Although, I did throw in some stuff I thought you’d both like. Some indie, a bit of…slightly embarrassing guilty pleasure pop. Oh god, what constitutes 'embarrassing' for you? That's the real question. Let’s just say it involves a boy band, a lot of synchronized dancing, and a questionable amount of hair gel. Excellent. This promises to be a truly harrowing journey. Are we stopping for coffee at least? I think I need caffeine just to process the thought of 90s boy bands. Definitely coffee.

Right, honestly, that physics lesson was brutal. I swear Mr. Harrison deliberately tries to confuse us with all the jargon. Tell me about it! I spent the whole time just nodding along, hoping I didn’t look  completely  lost. What was even with the wave-particle duality thing? My brain just shut down. It's alright, I think I kinda got it. But honestly, I'd rather be listening to music all day than thinking about photons and electrons. Have you guys heard the new Arctic Monkeys track? Oh yeah! 'Body Paint'. It’s…different, isn't it? Like, less guitar-driven than usual. Different is an understatement. It's almost…disco? I don’t know. It's growing on me though, Alex Turner's lyrics are still top tier. Yeah, the lyrics are brilliant. It's a bit of a departure, but I like that they're experimenting. It’s not like they just keep churning out the same album over and over. True. Speaking of music, did you see that new Dune trailer? The soundtrack is Hans Zimmer, right? Yeah! Zimmer is a god. Everything he touches turns to gold. The first Dune film already had an incredible score, so I’ve got high expectations. Proper cinematic vibes. I'm more excited about the film itself, to be honest. I read the book last year, it’s absolutely massive. It's like, a whole universe in a book. I tried to read it, but I got bogged down in all the political stuff. Too much spice and warring houses for me, I think. I’m more of a visual person, anyway. Yeah, it can be a bit dense. You need a flowchart just to keep track of all the characters! But the world-building is amazing. It’s like, a desert planet where the most valuable resource is a drug that gives you psychic powers. What's not to love? Exactly! And Timothée Chalamet is perfect as Paul Atreides. He just  looks  like someone who's destined for greatness…or doom, depending on how you look at it. He's alright, I guess. I'm more of a Zendaya fan. She seems really cool. Zendaya  is  cool. She’s got that whole effortlessly chic vibe going on. Have you seen Euphoria? That's a pretty intense show. I've heard of it. Isn't it super gritty? My mum would kill me if I started watching something like that.

Right, so how was Balanceability today? Did you two have fun? It was  so  good! I didn’t fall off once! I fell off a little bit…but I got back on! That’s brilliant, both of you! Even falling and getting back on is amazing. It’s all about building confidence, isn’t it? Miss Jones said I was a superstar! She said I was really good at balancing. Wow, a superstar! I’m really proud of you. And you, [Speaker_3’s name], getting back on shows real bravery. It’s hard when you wobble, but you didn’t give up. It was wobbly. But then I just…held on tight. Exactly! You problem-solved. That’s what we talk about at school, isn’t it? Finding ways to overcome challenges. At school today, Leo said he can already ride a bike without stabilisers! But I told him Balanceability helps you learn better. That’s a very good point! It’s a different way of learning, and it sets you up for success. It’s not about who gets there first, it’s about  how  you get there. Remind me to tell you about something similar that happened with an assessment I was doing at work… it’s a long story. Can we have pizza tonight? Maybe. We’ll see how well you both eat your dinner. Speaking of dinners, I was talking to Sarah today - you know, from my school days. She’s having her house completely renovated. Is she getting a swimming pool? Actually, yes! She's building one in the garden. And get this, a manmade waterfall! A waterfall?! Cool! Can you dive into it? That’s a good question. You absolutely  cannot  dive into a swimming pool unless it’s really, really deep. It’s so dangerous. Even then, you have to be super careful. We’ll have to talk about water safety. It's important. Mrs. Peterson was talking about safety too. She said we have to listen to grown-ups. That’s very wise, darling. Grown-ups usually have a good reason for telling you to do things. Have you been having interesting conversations at school? We talked about cats! Oh really? What about cats? It’s National Cat Day in Japan! We learned about it. It’s very silly. They give the cats special treats! That  is  silly and lovely! Our cats would definitely approve.

Honestly, I’m shattered. That spin class nearly killed me. I thought my legs were going to fall off. Oh, no way! I tried one of those once. Nearly threw up in the instructor’s face. Not a good look. Seriously though, you  enjoy  those? Enjoy is a strong word. But it feels…productive, y’know? Like I’ve actually  done  something with my Sunday. Unlike binge-watching terrible reality TV. Which, let’s be honest, is also tempting. I feel that on a spiritual level. I spent the last two hours down a rabbit hole of home renovation videos on YouTube. Now I’m convinced I can tile a bathroom. I absolutely cannot tile a bathroom. Oh, bless you. You’ll end up with wonky tiles and a lot of grout in your hair. Speaking of projects… how’s things with Ben going? Still… nebulous? Nebulous is a good word for it, actually. It's…comfortable. Which is nice. But also slightly terrifying. We've been 'seeing each other' for three months and it feels like we're still just politely circling each other. Like two very polite sharks. Ooh, polite sharks. That’s a good one. Is he just… cautious? Or is he deliberately keeping you at arm’s length? I think cautious. He’s been hurt before, apparently. A proper messy breakup involving a cat and a stolen saxophone. A stolen saxophone?! That's a whole other level of drama. I thought my ex was bad, he just left his socks everywhere. Honestly! The cat was apparently a neutral party, just a witness to the entire debacle. Anyway, he seems scared to fully commit. He's always got a 'busy week' or a 'prior engagement' when I suggest something more concrete. Sounds frustrating. You deserve someone who’s excited to spend time with you, not someone who treats you like a dentist appointment. Have you… actually  told  him how you’re feeling? Like, laid it all out there? I’ve dropped a few hints. Said things like, “It would be nice to maybe, potentially, at some point, do something that isn’t just grabbing a quick coffee.” It’s very subtle. Subtle? Honey, you’re basically sending smoke signals. You need to be direct. Men are shockingly oblivious sometimes. Trust me, I’ve dated my fair share. You think so? I always worry about coming on too strong. Scaring him off.

Right, that was a good dominoes drive, eh? Didn’t half take old Mrs. Patterson down a peg or two this week. She thought she had me cornered, did she? Yeah, you were proper good, Uncle Geoff. She looked  fuming  when you played that double six. Fuming is an understatement, Geoff. She nearly knocked over Old Man Hemmings’ tea! Honestly, some people have no grace in defeat. More pizza, anyone? I made garlic bread too. Aye, I’ll have a slice of that garlic bread, thanks, love. This pizza's good, though. Better than that Italian place we went to last month. Remember, the portions were tiny! Paid a fortune for a few mouthfuls. That's what I said! I was still hungry afterwards. It was all fancy and… small. This pizza is proper filling. That’s because I don’t believe in scrimping on portions, that's why. You want a meal, you  have  a meal. Speaking of which, did you two decide what you wanted for Easter yet? I was thinking about that new football kit. The one Newcastle’s got? It’s really expensive though. Expensive? Everything's expensive these days, lad. Used to be able to get a decent kit for twenty quid. Now it’s nearly a hundred. Daylight robbery, it is. Perhaps you should save up a bit and get it yourself? Shows you appreciate it more. Your Grandad’s right, you know. A bit of effort means more than just being handed things. Although... I might slip you a tenner towards it. Don’t tell your Grandad. You're the best, Mam! Thanks. Maybe I'll ask for some new trainers too. Mine are falling apart. Trainers, eh? Getting through them like water, you are. I remember when a good pair of boots lasted you years. None of this flimsy stuff. Times change, Geoff. They’re all about fashion now. Honestly, I’m going to get my hair cut next week. It’s getting to  here . I feel like a sheep. You? Get your hair cut? It's always looked the same to me! Short and sensible. Sensible? I’d like to try something different for once! Maybe some layers. Though Mrs. Higgins at the salon always looks at me like I’ve asked her to shear a cow. Maybe you could get it dyed a wild colour! Like blue or green. Now there’s a thought!

Right, so milk first, or tea first? It’s a debate for the ages, isn’t it? Tea first, always. Absolutely always. It’s just… the correct way. Milk first dilutes it, makes it all… sad. Sad tea? You’re dramatic, you know that? Though, I did see that article about how posh people put milk in first. Posh people can get away with anything. They probably have special tea-making protocols passed down through generations. Like, “One clockwise stir, using only a silver spoon.” Oh, imagine! Speaking of posh, did you see that Gordon Ramsay’s opened a new pub in London? Apparently, it’s ridiculously expensive. Seriously? Another one? He’s taking over the whole pub scene. Bet you couldn't get a decent pint for under a tenner. Probably not. Though, remember that pub we went to in York? The one with the massive beer garden? That was proper good. Oh yeah, The Golden Fleece, wasn't it? Good shout. They did a cracking Sunday roast as well, if I recall. Although… the Yorkshire puddings could have been bigger. They always could be bigger, couldn’t they? It's a national tragedy, the consistently undersized Yorkshire pudding. Right, tea’s brewing. What are we having for dinner? I’m thinking something… green. Green? As in… vegetables? Yeah. I feel like we haven't had a proper veg haul in ages. I was thinking maybe broccoli and… oh, I don’t know. Something adventurous. Adventurous vegetables? What constitutes an adventurous vegetable these days? Kale? Brussels sprouts? Don't even  mention  Brussels sprouts. They’re the enemy. Maybe… pak choi? I’ve never actually cooked with pak choi before. Ooh, that’s actually a good shout. Stir-fry it with some ginger and garlic, bit of soy sauce… yeah, I'm on board with that. Better than risking a sprout-induced trauma. Perfect. And maybe some chicken. Oh, and you won’t believe who I saw on the train this morning. Go on… spill the tea. It was… Richard Ayoade! Proper starstruck, I was. He was reading a book, all serious and intense. I didn’t want to bother him. No way! Richard Ayoade? That  is  a good sighting. He always seems so… permanently bewildered. Do you think he genuinely  doesn’t  understand how things work? I genuinely think he might not. But that’s part of the charm, isn't it?

Right, okay, my turn. Ugh, this is awful. “Philosophical.” No describing, no saying ‘thinking’… oh brilliant. Go on, give it a go. You’ve got a minute! This is going to be good. Philosophical… relax, Bethan, relax. Right, okay… um… “Deep thoughts… about… everything.” No, no, worse. “Old men with beards!” No! Oh, this is impossible. You’re getting there! Think about what it  means , not just what it looks like. Just wave your hands dramatically and hope for the best, love! That’s usually my tactic. Abstract concepts! Existential crises! The meaning of life! Is that… too much? A little! A little too dramatic. Think simpler. Is it related to… teachers? Because you’re always going on about pedagogy and stuff. Oh! Maybe…“Questioning everything?” No, still too broad. Oh, I’m going to fail. Think about famous philosophers. That might give you a clue. Socrates! Is… is that allowed? Is saying “Socrates” allowed? No! No names! Right, okay. “Ancient Greek thinkers!” No! Still referencing names… This is agonizing! Just shout something vaguely intellectual. “Big questions!” Time’s up! Oh, Bethan. That was… a struggle. I hate this game. It’s designed to make you feel inadequate. It’s brilliant! It's hilarious watching you squirm. It's good for the brain, you know. Keeps the grey matter moving. Now, my turn! “Symbiotic.” Right… let’s see. Oh, this one’s tricky! Symbiotic? Oh, I know this one. Don't tell me, though… let’s see how Dad does! Hmm… “Living together…” No. “Mutual benefit…” Close, but too…literal. "Tiny creatures helping big creatures!" You're thinking of remoras and sharks again, aren't you? Maybe! It's a good example! "Working together…" Oh, this is a nightmare! It’s something to do with nature, isn’t it? Yes! But don’t give it away! "Two things… needing each other…” Argh! It’s on the tip of my tongue. Think of bees! Bees and flowers! Yes! "Bees and flowers!" Yes! Good one, Dad! Although, a little obvious with your bee obsession. Hey! Bees are fascinating creatures! And vital for the ecosystem! It’s… symbiotic! See? Alright, alright, settle down. My turn. "Ephemeral". Oh, lovely. This will be a disaster. Anyone got any good ideas to get me started...? Is that even a real word? Sounds like something you'd find in a very fancy dictionary. It is a real word!

Right, okay, so I’m going to lay down… Seven of hearts. And… discard a four of clubs. Someone’s got to take that four, it’s practically begging to be taken. Begging, is it? Alright, alright. I’ll take the four. Lay down a five of clubs. And…discard a two of diamonds. I’m trying to get rid of these pesky diamonds, honestly. Pesky is an understatement. I've got a hand full of them. Right, I’ll take the four, adding a six of clubs. Discarding a… oh, this is awful. A queen of spades. Someone is going to be furious. Oh, you fiend! I’m already dreading this queen. I’ll take it, reluctantly. Seven of spades. Discarding… a three of hearts. I’m just throwing things at the wall hoping something sticks, at this point. You’re a brave woman, taking that queen. Honestly, I was hoping someone else would pick it up. Reminds me of old Mrs. Davies from my school, always volunteering for the worst jobs. She once single-handedly scrubbed the entire school hall floor! Oh, now  that’s  dedication. My Nain used to say, “If a job’s worth doing, it’s worth doing properly, even if it kills ya!” Sounds about right. She’d be the one volunteering to clear up after everyone else at the village fete. Still, the queen is a killer. I'm starting to suspect someone's deliberately stocking up on spades. Don’t look at me! I swear, it’s pure coincidence. Though, I  do  remember Uncle Bryn hoarding all the wild cards at Christmas last year… nearly caused a riot during Monopoly. Oh, Bryn! He’s incapable of playing a board game without turning it into a strategic war. Remember the time he tried to bribe little Rhys with sweets to give him Park Lane? Absolutely scandalous! Rhys was only eight! I think that’s when Mum implemented the “Bryn-proof Monopoly rules”. No bribery, no trading until you're ten. Speaking of rules… are we still adhering to the ‘no complaining about your hand’ rule? Because honestly, this is bordering on cruel and unusual punishment. Oh, hush now. A little bit of hardship builds character. Besides, it’s just a game. Though I am planning my revenge already, I have a sneaky feeling about this seven of spades. It’s all about the long game, isn’t it?

Honestly, I’m still recovering from finishing those applications. UCAS is a  nightmare . It's just… endless personal statements. Tell me about it! I remember when I applied. It feels like a lifetime ago now. Though, admittedly, my stress was less about the statement and more about figuring out what I even  wanted  to do. Still kinda figuring it out, to be fair. How are you feeling about your choices, Liv? I think I’ve narrowed it down to three. Bristol, Exeter, and Leeds. All for History. Bristol’s my top choice, but everyone says it’s so competitive. Bristol  is  competitive. But definitely worth a shot. I've got a friend there studying Law, she loves it. The city's amazing, too. Though, be warned, it's basically all hills. Oh great. Just what I need. More walking! You’ll build up a tolerance. It's good practice for naval life, honestly. All that scrambling around on ships. You’re always finding a way to relate everything back to the Navy, aren’t you, Sam? Hey, it's a very relevant skill set! Anyway, how’s work, Chloe? Still surviving the retail madness? Trying to! It's… intense. Honestly, I'm exhausted most of the time. But it pays for new shoes, so… Speaking of exhausting, I had the worst cold last week. Honestly, I thought I was dying. Mr. Henderson, at the accountancy firm, just told me to drink Lemsip and get on with it. Charming. Ugh, bosses. Mine just stare at you expectantly if you even  look  slightly ill. Same. My manager just asked if I'd finished stocktake yet, even though I was practically green. You lot are all getting sick. I've been locked away in a lab with sophisticated equipment, so I'm immune to all the peasant diseases. Oh, be quiet! You’re just lucky you’re not dealing with the public. Honestly, the things people say… Last week someone tried to return a used face mask. A  used  face mask! No way! People are wild. Honestly. Have you guys started thinking about Christmas presents yet? I am so behind. I’ve got a list started, but I’m skint, so it’s mostly handmade stuff. Trying to make bath bombs, but they just keep crumbling. I can offer to cover the ingredients, if you like. My salary is slightly more generous these days.

Honestly, this programme is dreadful. Absolute rubbish. I don’t know why we bother sometimes. It’s alright, Nan. A bit slow, yeah, but it’s easy watching. Good for after dinner. Easy watching is right. Requires zero brain cells. You know, back in my day, telly was… well, it was different. Different how, dear? You’ve said that five times already this evening. Just… better. More effort put in. Everything’s so…glossy now. Well, technology’s moved on, hasn’t it? Speaking of moving on… I’m starting to think I should just sell the car. It’s sitting there, doing nothing. Sell it? But you only got it last year! I know, I know. But I barely drive anymore. I can get everything I need delivered, and if I want to go anywhere, I can get the bus. It’s just another expense really. Insurance, tax, the MOT… it all adds up. Good idea, Mum. You’re much better off walking or cycling. Keeps you fit. Speaking of cycling, did you fix that puncture on your bike? Oh, don't remind me! No, it's still leaning against the shed. Honestly, I'm hopeless with anything mechanical. I keep meaning to ask Mr. Henderson next door, but I always forget. I could take a look if you want, Nan. I'm pretty good with a bike pump and a patch kit. Used to fix all Leo's punctures when we were at uni. Oh, would you darling? That would be lovely. You’re a lifesaver. Though, Leo’s punctures were usually self-inflicted, weren’t they? Trying to do tricks he shouldn’t. That’s putting it mildly. He was a menace on two wheels. I remember. Near broke his neck once trying to jump that ramp at the recreation ground. Honestly! It gave me palpitations just watching him. You two were always so adventurous. I was more of a… cautious child. Well, that's why you were sensible enough to have us! Mum always walked everywhere when we were kids. Rain or shine. “Good for the constitution,” she used to say. It is! And it's free. Although, I do miss driving to the coast sometimes. That sea air… We could all go to Brighton next weekend? Train’s easy, and we don’t have to worry about parking. That sounds nice. Though it’ll be rammed, won’t it?

Oh, this is a lovely space, isn’t it? I don’t think I’ve been in the Law Faculty since… well, since graduating, actually. Feels very different seeing it like this, all set up for alumni. It is nice. I work here now, so I’m used to it, but even I think it looks a bit special today. Are you from around Cambridge originally? I don't think I recognise you from my time studying here. No, I’m from Aylesbury. Bit of a trek, but worth it for a day catching up with everything. I’m working as a Language Research Coordinator now. Fascinating stuff, though quite different from tort law! And you? Lincoln, originally. I stayed on after graduating, working as a Research Administrator here. It’s… steady. Keeps me busy. What kind of language research? Mostly sociolinguistics, looking at language variation and change. At the moment, I’m focused on dialectal differences across the UK, but a previous project involved looking at language contact in Spain. Have you been? Spain, you say? Wonderful country. Spent a summer cycling through the Basque country years ago. Absolutely stunning. Though the language… now  that’s  a challenge. Nothing like anything I’ve ever encountered. Oh, really? I’ve always wanted to go to the Basque country. I’ve done a bit of Spanish, but nothing beyond the basics. Basque is completely isolated, you see. No relation to any other European language. It's a linguistic puzzle. Reminds me a bit of trying to understand the intricacies of Mandarin, actually. Spent a few weeks in China with the university a while back. Utterly bewildering. That’s incredible. I’ve done a little bit of Mandarin, just for fun, but I can barely string a sentence together. It’s so tonal. It feels a world away from Indo-European languages. I tried learning Japanese once, got as far as the Hiragana and Katakana scripts, then just… gave up. Too much! I think I prefer sticking with languages a bit closer to home. Sensible girl. Though you miss out on some truly fascinating linguistic complexities. Tell me, what brought you both back to Cambridge today? Just reminiscing? A bit of both. It’s good to see what everyone’s been up to. Plus, there was a talk scheduled about funding opportunities for research. Always useful. I was hoping to catch up with a few of my old professors.

Honestly, two years! It feels like ages since we all last properly sat down like this. How’s work, Sarah? Still wrestling with spreadsheets at the dentist? You know it. Though Mr. Henderson decided he wanted a new filing system last week. Apparently, alphabetical wasn't 'dynamic' enough. Dynamic filing! Honestly, the things people come up with. It took me three days to re-sort everything. Oh, Mr. Henderson. He sounds…special. I had a candidate today who genuinely asked if our office had a nap room. A nap room! For a recruitment agency. No way! What did you say? I tried to keep a straight face and explained the concept of commission. She wasn’t impressed. It’s exhausting, honestly. People's expectations are just… wild. Did anyone see Aunt Carol posted another one of those vaguely political things on Facebook? Oh, don't even. I had to mute her again. Last week it was something about the price of tomatoes. This week it’s… I honestly didn’t even read it. Too much effort. Remember when everyone was doing the ice bucket challenge? That was a simpler time. Ha! Simpler indeed. I think I still have ice shivers thinking about it. I’m surprised Mum didn’t make us all do it for charity. She was always keen on a good cause. She’s got a good heart, Mum does. Though that bake sale she organised for the animal shelter… half the cakes were burnt. Don't remind me. Remember little Tommy Jenkins trying to sneak a second slice of the charcoal cake? Poor kid. Speaking of kids, how’s little Leo doing, Sophie? He must be getting so big. He’s a whirlwind. Just turned four. He’s started asking about where babies come from, which is…fun. We’re trying to keep it age-appropriate, but he’s a bright spark. It's a whole different level of exhaustion than recruitment. Oh, the questions! It’ll be worth it, though. Hey, has anyone heard anything from Uncle David lately? It's been ages since he called. He mentioned something about a cruise with Brenda. Somewhere in the Mediterranean, I think. He keeps promising to teach me Italian, but he always gets distracted by… well, Brenda. Honestly, they're like teenagers. They've always been a bit of a whirlwind. Remember when he proposed to Brenda for the  third  time on that rollercoaster?

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me mad. It makes a perfectly good cup, when it  deigns  to make one, but half the time it just gurgles and spits and then says ‘descale’. Descale! I descaled it last week! Sounds familiar. Ours went through a phase of that. Did you check the filter? Sometimes they block, even if they’re relatively new. It’s the water, I reckon. Hunsonby water. It's… robust. Too much iron in it. That’ll clog anything. Well, it’s not robust enough to get a decent signal for the telly, that's for sure. Still waiting on BT to send someone out, the cheek of it! We’ve been without proper news for a week. Speaking of news, did you see what Keir Starmer said about… well, everything? It felt a bit… bland, didn't it? Bland is an understatement. He’s trying to be everything to everyone, which means he's appealing to nobody. A true politician, I suppose. Remember when Labour actually  stood  for something? Oh, don’t get me started. It’s all so… pragmatic now. No fire. No ideals. It's depressing. I remember when people actually believed in changing the world. It’s hard to hold onto those ideals, isn’t it? Especially when you're facing things like… removal costs. I finally got a quote back for storing some of the furniture. It’s eye-watering. Ouch. Seriously? What are they charging? Fifteen pounds a week for a small container. And that’s before petrol, insurance, and the sheer agony of deciding what to keep and what to ditch. Fifteen pounds! Robbery! We paid half that when we moved things to storage after your father… well, you know. Everything is up. Everything. It’s scandalous. And the council tax here… I’m still reeling. Don’t even. I’ve been going through the paperwork and trying to understand it. It’s a labyrinth! Honestly, I miss teaching. At least then, things made logical sense. You’d think with a maths background you’d be good at deciphering council tax bills! Oh, dear girl, council tax is not mathematics. It's… dark magic. Honestly, I think they just make the numbers up. It's a deliberate obfuscation tactic. Keep the voters confused, and they won't question anything. It’s the same with these energy bills. It's exhausting. You try to be informed, you try to do the right thing, and then you get hit with a bill for fifteen pounds a week just to store a few chairs.

Honestly, Mum, the thought of Christmas already fills me with dread. Not the actual day, but  getting  to the actual day. It's the sheer logistical nightmare. Oh, don't start, darling. It's not  that  bad. Just a bit of planning, that's all. Remember when you were little? You loved it, even the chaos. I loved the  receiving  of presents, Mum. Not the frantic wrapping, the endless shopping, and trying to coordinate everyone's schedules. And Dad’s insistence on doing the turkey – honestly, it’s still traumatising thinking about that slightly pink bird from ‘18. He meant well! He wanted to contribute. And it wasn't  that  pink. A little pinkness never hurt anyone. Anyway, have you started thinking about where you're spending it this year? Are you coming down to Devon? That's what I'm wrestling with. I'd love to, truly. But if I come down, that means taking time off work, and then I’m battling the Christmas traffic… plus, your brother will inevitably ask about my ‘life plan’ again. Oh, don’t worry about David. He just wants what’s best for you. And honestly, you  should  have a life plan, dear. Teaching English online is all well and good, but is that really what you want to be doing in five years? It pays the bills, Mum! And it gives me flexibility. I'm thinking of doing a TEFL course specialising in business English. That might open up some better-paid opportunities. I saw one advertised online the other day, fully remote. Well, that sounds sensible. And potentially lucrative. That’s a good idea. But you can’t live your life glued to a screen, can you? You need… social interaction. Are you still seeing that nice Mark? We're “seeing each other.” It’s very casual. He’s a musician, so his schedule is… erratic. He's playing a gig in Brighton Boxing Day, wants me to come. But I said I'd tentatively offer to help Sarah with her Christmas decorations. Sarah? Oh, Sarah from your book club? Is she still with that dreadful man? I always thought he was a bit shifty. They broke up, actually. It was messy. Hence the decoration help. She's feeling a bit lost, apparently. Actually, she mentioned wanting to come to Totnes for New Year. She’s always admired the area. Oh, how lovely!

Honestly, I thought Nan was gonna kill him last night. The snoring! Oh,  god . Was he at it again? Proper saw-milling, was he? It wasn’t just snoring, it was… a symphony of snorts and wheezes. I genuinely thought something was wrong. A symphony! That’s brilliant. Though I can imagine why Nan was fuming. She needs her sleep. He said he had a cold, but I reckon it’s just his default setting. He's always been a snorer. Remember when we went camping and he kept everyone awake? Don’t even  mention  that camping trip. I was practically catnapping standing up all weekend. It was awful. Anyway, did you lot get yourselves sorted with bread for the week? Waterfields was rammed this morning. Managed to get a loaf of their white farmhouse, thankfully. Nearly didn't though. Old Mrs. Higgins was holding up the whole queue, arguing over the price of a bap. She’s a nightmare, that woman. Always trying to get a discount. Honestly, it's a loaf of bread! They do a lovely batch loaf, don’t they? Though it’s a bit rich for everyday, isn’t it? I just went for a couple of rolls. I got some of their sausage rolls. Proper good, especially when they're still warm. Ooh, good shout. I nearly got some of those Richmond sausages they do. They're a bit pricey, but they're worth it, aren’t they? Especially with mash and gravy. Definitely. Though me nan reckons you can’t beat a good Cumberland sausage. Says they’ve got more flavour. It’s all about proper seasoning, isn’t it? I made a sausage casserole last night, and it was a disaster. No flavour at all. You need a good dash of smoked paprika, and a pinch of nutmeg. That's the secret. My grandad always used to carry a handkerchief with him, stuffed with herbs and spices. Said it was 'for flavouring'. Oh, that's... interesting. A bit much, maybe? A bit eccentric, even for your grandad! Honestly, he's a character. Does he still wear those ridiculous tweed jackets? Always. And those flat caps. He looks like he’s stepped straight out of a film. He's a classic. Speaking of classics, anyone else think Sarah’s been a bit quiet lately? I haven’t seen her properly in ages. She mentioned something about being swamped with uni work.

Honestly, that was… a weekend. A  weekend . Sounds dramatic. Rough one then? Rough is an understatement! Mum insisted on redecorating the spare room while I was there. The entire weekend was dominated by magnolia. Magnolia, Dad attempting to hang wallpaper, and the general chaos that ensues when they try DIY. Oh, lord. Your dad and wallpaper never ends well, does it? Remember the kitchen incident? Don't even  mention  the kitchen. It’s still a family legend. He managed to get more paste on himself than on the wall. But this was worse. The sheer volume of magnolia… it’s oppressive. I’m pretty sure my soul is now beige. Right, a beige soul. I can see it. So no relaxing family time then? Very little. I tried to escape into a book a couple of times, but Mum kept asking me to ‘hold this’ or ‘tell me if this shade is okay’. It was relentless. What about you? Any drama on the farm? Thankfully, no magnolia-related incidents here. Bit of a headache with a broken slurry pump, but nothing I haven't dealt with before. Managed to get it fixed by Saturday afternoon, so spent most of Sunday pottering around in the garden. Pruned the apple trees, which is always satisfying. Sounds idyllic, actually. I’m officially requesting a weekend escape to the countryside next time. Somewhere with no paint charts and minimal parental supervision. You’re always welcome. We’ve got the spare room, although I can't promise it’s magnolia-free. It's more of a… muted olive. Muted olive is significantly better. Anything exciting happening at work this week? You mentioned a potential new contract? Yeah, should be hearing back from those folks at Hanson’s on Monday. Looks promising, all going well, it will keep us busy for a good six months. More paperwork, more meetings, the usual joy. That's good news though! More stability is always a bonus. I'm just… drowning in spreadsheets at the moment. Honestly, I'm starting to dream in formulas. That’s the project coordinator life for you. I remember when I was trying to sort out the funding for the new barn, I felt exactly the same. It's soul-destroying. It is. Hey, are you free next Saturday? There's that new Italian place that opened downtown, I thought we could try it out. A proper celebration of surviving the weekend, and escaping the magnolia.

Honestly, the kids are driving me round the bend with their French pronunciation. It’s like they actively  avoid  making the ‘u’ sound correctly. It’s all ‘too’ instead of ‘tu’! Oh, bless them. It's so hard isn’t it? Especially that ‘u’ sound, it's just not something we naturally make in English. Still, they’re lucky you’re so patient. How are you finding the new curriculum changes, though? More grammar focused, right? Nightmare. Absolutely a nightmare. They’ve piled on so much grammar, and they expect Year 7s to grasp subjunctive moods! It’s brutal. I feel like I’m just drilling them with rules rather than getting them to  speak  the language. I miss the old days when we could actually focus on cultural stuff and making it fun. I know what you mean. We’re the same. It feels so… sterile now. Though, I’m not teaching French, thankfully. Just Spanish. Which, apparently, is 'easier.' Don’t even get me started on the regional accents  within  Spain! Oh, Spanish is a minefield! I tried to pick some up while travelling, but every time I thought I was getting the hang of it, someone would start speaking so fast I felt like I’d gone back to being a Year 7 myself. Exactly! It's humbling, isn't it? Anyway, enough about work. How’s everything else? Still enjoying Hitchin life? It’s good, really good. Quiet, definitely quieter than Birmingham. Though, I do miss the buzz sometimes. And having friends just a short train ride away. How’s little Leo doing? He must be… what, almost a year old now? He’s just turned ten months! It’s flown by. He’s crawling everywhere, destroying everything, and starting to say ‘dada.’ It’s a whirlwind, honestly. Exhausting, but amazing. Oh, that's lovely! I’m still on the fence about the whole baby thing. Part of me desperately wants one, but then I think about my job… and the lack of sleep… and the sheer expense of it all! I get it. It's a massive decision. And it  is  expensive. We're constantly buying things, and then he grows out of them within weeks! But honestly? It’s worth it. It's just… different to anything I've ever experienced. Though, my Spanish is definitely suffering. I barely have time to string a sentence together these days.

Right, well, that's a proper good show of nesting activity this year, isn't it? More than last, I reckon. Seems that way. Though, truth be told, I don't pay  that  much attention. Just glad they're not building in the guttering again. Had a right mess last time. Oh, don’t remind me! Took Arthur three days to clean all that out. Though, bless him, he did find a little blue feather. Kept it for weeks. He’s a sentimental soul, that boy. Speaking of finding things, I saw Mrs. Higgins struggling with her shopping yesterday. Said her hip was playing up something awful. Poor soul. She’s getting on a bit, isn't she? Eighty-something, I reckon? It's just what happens, isn’t it? Things start to fall apart. Don't be morbid, George! It's a beautiful afternoon. Look at the birds flitting about the feeder. Though, I must say, I'm starting to think we need to fill it up again. They’re emptying it remarkably quickly. I'll do it later. After a slice of this cake, mind. Doreen, this is lovely. What did you put in it? Seems a bit… moist. Just a touch of apricot jam. And a splash of orange juice. Thought it needed a little something. Though I was worried it might be a bit too sweet, with your diabetes and all. Oh, don’t fuss. A little treat won’t hurt. Doctor said I need to enjoy myself. It’s just… sometimes I feel a bit sluggish afterwards. That’s just old age, Norman. You’re past it, lad. Face facts. Easy for  you  to say, you haven’t got a dodgy pancreas! Now, now, you two. Behave yourselves. Remember what happened last week when you started arguing about the pigeons? That wasn't my fault! He said pigeons were intelligent. Intelligent! They're flying rats, I tell you. They recognise faces, George! I read it in a magazine. Honestly. It's a wonder I put up with you both. Oh, look! There’s a robin building a nest in the climbing rose. It’s almost finished. Good spot, Doreen. Actually, I was thinking… remember those little puppet shows Arthur used to put on for the grandkids? Oh, aye. Terrible things. All that squeaking. Gave me a headache. They loved them! And you secretly enjoyed them, George.

Right, I think I'm going to go for the grilled halloumi with the salad. It smells lovely. Are you having the kebab again, David? You know me too well, Sarah. Can't resist a good kebab, especially out here. And the bread… oh, the bread is just divine. Though, I did see old Mrs. Higgins from number 42 eyeing up my plate last time. She gave me the  look , you know the one. The one that says, “You’re having far too much enjoyment.” Oh, Mrs. Higgins! She gives everyone the look. Remember when she told me off for letting Winston sniff her roses? Said he’d ruin the blooms! He just wanted a friendly sniff! Winston was a good lad. I still miss that scruffy terrier. You’ve not replaced him, have you? No, not yet. It doesn’t feel right. It’s only been a couple of years. Though, my sister’s trying to convince me to get a rescue greyhound. Says they're very laid-back. A greyhound, eh? Bold choice. Bit different from Winston. Speaking of bold choices, look at that couple over there. He’s practically serenading her with a rendition of… is that ‘She’ll Be Coming Round the Mountain’? Oh, goodness me. It is! And she looks mortified. Poor woman. You’d think a romantic getaway wouldn’t involve public outbursts of song. You'd think. Reminds me of my brother, Barry. Proposed to Margaret with a kazoo solo. A  kazoo , Sarah! She nearly walked out. Oh, Barry! He always was…unique. How  is  Margaret, by the way? I haven’t spoken to her since Uncle George passed. She’s… coping. It hit her hard, George’s illness. Especially as it was that awful creeping dementia. She says the worst part was watching him disappear bit by bit. It's a cruel disease, Sarah. Cruel. It is. Mum’s worried about it, you know. She’s been getting forgetful lately. Nothing serious, but she keeps misplacing things and asking the same questions. It’s just age, I expect. Though, you’ve got to be vigilant. Have you convinced her to get her hearing checked? She’s been struggling to hear me these last few visits. I have. She’s booked an appointment for when we get back. She's dreading it, wants to avoid getting a hearing aid if at all possible. Says they make her feel old.

Honestly, the commute is just… draining. An hour and a half each way. It's eating into everything. Oh, love, you poor thing. That  is  awful. I thought your new role would be closer? It’s supposed to be! They said twenty minutes on the train. Lies, all lies. It's a roundabout route, and then the bus… honestly, it’s a nightmare. Well, you’ve always been a good traveller, haven’t you? Remember that trip to Italy? Packed like sardines, and you didn’t complain once. Dad, that was fifteen years ago, and I was fuelled by gelato and the excitement of being in a new country! This is just… grey and damp and delayed trains. Are you still liking the work itself, though? Is it interesting? Yeah, the project is good. It's challenging, and I'm learning a lot. It’s just… getting  to  the project is the problem. I’m thinking about asking if I can work from home a couple of days a week. Worth a shot, love. Can't hurt to ask. Speaking of work, this new agricultural scheme is a right palaver. So much paperwork. It’s like they deliberately try to make it complicated. Always does feel that way, doesn’t it? Everything’s forms and regulations now. Remember when you used to just…  do  things? Exactly! Now you need permission for everything. Oh, and old Mrs. Higgins called today, asking if I could help her sort out her prize-winning marrow for the village show. Said it’s looking rather… lopsided. A lopsided marrow? Seriously? Dead serious. Apparently, it’s crucial to position it just so for maximum impact. She always did take that show very seriously. Remember when she accused Mr. Peterson of sabotaging her dahlias? Oh, the drama! Anyway, are you two sorted for Christmas? Have you started thinking about presents yet? I’ve got a few ideas. Your Auntie Carol keeps dropping hints about a new set of gardening tools. And your father… well, he’ll probably be happy with a new pair of socks. Hey! I appreciate good socks. They’re an essential! I was thinking, with the renovations you’re planning, maybe we could contribute towards the kitchen? Oh, Dad, that’s incredibly generous! But we really don’t want to put you to any expense. Nonsense! We’re perfectly alright. We want to see you two get the house just how you want it.

Honestly, I was scrolling through TikTok last night, and you won’t BELIEVE the catfish situation I stumbled upon. Oh, go on then! I love a good catfish story. It's a guilty pleasure, isn't it? Like watching Jeremy Kyle. You  know  it's awful, but you just can't look away. Oh my god, Jeremy Kyle... don't even get me STARTED. The absolute state of some of those people. The lie detector! It was brutal. Right? But this TikTok was insane. This girl thought she was dating this really fit builder, like, proper ripped. Sending pics, chatting every day for months… Months?! Oh, the poor thing. I know! And then another girl messaged her saying, “Uh, that’s my dad?” Apparently, her dad had been using a load of old photos he found on the internet and pretending to be, like, twenty years younger. No way! That's mental! That’s…actually quite sad too, when you think about it. What was the dad playing at? Seriously! Like, what’s the motivation? Was he just lonely? Or trying to relive his youth through someone else? It’s proper creepy. That's what everyone was saying in the comments. Apparently, he’d been doing it with multiple girls! Apparently, this TikToker’s been getting messages from loads of other girls now. Blimey. That’s…a lot of effort for a lie. You'd think he'd get bored eventually. Remember that one on Jeremy Kyle where the bloke had been pretending to be a pilot? Oh, God yes! The fake uniform, the dodgy accent… It was all falling apart live on TV! The guests were ripping him to shreds. It was glorious. See, it's that public humiliation that gets me. But with this TikTok thing, it’s happening behind closed doors, and it’s so much more insidious. This girl was genuinely falling for someone who wasn’t even real. Or, well, real but…not who she thought. It's awful. It makes you wonder who you can trust online, doesn’t it? Everyone puts on a front. I saw a post the other day about how easily you can create deepfakes now. It’s scary. It really is. You'd think people would be more careful, but I guess when you  want  to believe something, you kind of ignore the red flags. It's like those people on Jeremy Kyle who refuse to believe their partner’s been cheating, even with all the evidence staring them in the face!

Honestly, the amount of times my laptop’s crashed this week is ridiculous. I swear it's actively trying to sabotage my dissertation. Oh, those machines! They have a life of their own, don’t they? It's always the crucial moment, isn’t it? Right before you save. I remember when I was doing my sculpture, I had a digital component, and… disaster. Lost an entire week’s work. Digital is no replacement for a good sketchbook, believe me. Tell me about it. I'm seriously considering going old school. Pen and paper it is. Though, my handwriting’s atrocious. Speaking of things going wrong, did you ever manage to get to Paris this year? You were talking about it ages ago. I did! Finally. It was lovely. Though, I felt terribly guilty leaving the bees for so long. Old Man Tiberius, the largest one, gave me  the look  when I got back. You know the one. Like I’d personally offended the entire hive. Tiberius sounds like a character. Did you at least get some good sketching done? Paris is a sketcher’s paradise. Darling, I sketched until my fingers ached! The light is just… exquisite. And I remembered enough French to stumble through most conversations. I’ve been trying to brush up, although my German is far better, naturally. Funny, isn't it? Born in Vienna, better at German than French. It is a bit ironic. You’re multilingual, though, aren't you? How many languages do you know properly? Oh, properly? That’s a strong word. I’m fluent in German and Italian. My French is… serviceable. I can get by. And I had a year of Classics at university, so I can mangle a bit of Latin and Greek. Mainly, I can recognise it. It’s all a bit rusty now, sadly. Classics! That’s mental. It’s so different to what I’m doing. I’m just drowning in theories about postcolonial literature. Though, it's fascinating, in a headachy sort of way. It sounds exhausting. What will you do after you finish, then? Any ideas? Your father was asking the other day. I honestly have no clue. Maybe some sort of teaching. Or something in publishing. Honestly, it feels like everyone in my year is either starting a band, backpacking through Southeast Asia, or having an existential crisis. It’s the age for existential crises.

Honestly, the way that van just pulled out! No indicator, just  pulled  out. It's a miracle we didn’t have an accident. Ugh, seriously! Some people just don’t think. Makes my heart race every time. Are we sure this is the quickest route, Dad? This traffic is already building. The Sat Nav says it’s the fastest, dear. Though, knowing Sat Navs, it’ll probably send us down a single-track lane in five minutes. Remember that time it took us to that garden centre near Colchester? Oh, don’t remind me. Through three villages, backing up when a tractor came the other way… I nearly lost the plot. Still, better than the A303, I suppose. Used to be a nightmare on that road. It is getting busy now, isn’t it? Everyone and their dog is heading to the coast. I’m supposed to be doing essays this weekend, but honestly, I can’t concentrate with all this stress. What are you studying now, love? Still the history thing? Yeah, finishing my masters. Looking at social mobility in Victorian England. Fascinating, but a lot of reading. And endless referencing. Sounds… involved. Remember when computers were simple? You just switched them on and they  worked . Now you need a degree to understand Windows 8, or whatever number they’re on now. Don’t even get me started on technology. I spent half an hour on the phone to my sister yesterday trying to explain how to send a photo. She keeps saying she can't ‘attach’ it. It's like speaking a foreign language. It is frustrating, isn’t it? Especially when you’re trying to help someone and they just… don’t get it. Speaking of frustrating, I need to call that solicitor again. Still waiting for them to sort out the paperwork from Mum’s house. Honestly, the amount they charge… it’s daylight robbery. They always are, aren't they? It’s like they know you’re vulnerable and they just take advantage. I’ve got a day off next week, I might finally get around to clearing out the spare room. It's full of… well, everything. Old furniture, boxes of things… Mum always did like to keep everything, didn’t she? I remember her having a whole room dedicated to ‘Mantiques’, as she called them. Just old bits and bobs. That’s a good one.

Right then. What’s that dear? Just thinking. Thinking about…the telly. Oh aye? What were you watching earlier? That police programme again? No, no. Not that one. That’s on tomorrow. It was… that one with the houses. You know. The ones they renovate. Oh,  that  one. The one where they all get terribly stressed? That’s the one. It’s daft, innit? All that fuss over a bit of wallpaper. It is, isn't it? They act like their lives depend on getting a nice kitchen. Exactly! A kitchen! As if a kitchen’s going to solve all their problems. Though I do look, you know. See what they come up with. I like to see what they do with the space. I suppose. I just find it…bizarre. All that money thrown around. Well, they’ve usually bought a right fixer-upper, haven’t they? They need to spend something. Fixer-upper! Ha! Some of them are falling down! They are a bit rough around the edges, aren't they? Still, it’s good to see people trying to make something nice. Hmm. Suppose so. Still prefer a bit of nature myself. More peaceful. Oh, you and your nature. Always wanting to be out in the garden. Well, it's better than watching people argue about tiles, isn't it? It is, yes. Though it’s a bit chilly out there at the moment, isn’t it? It is a bit. Maybe tomorrow. If the sun comes out. That’d be nice. Perhaps we could have a cuppa in the garden. Now you're talking. A cuppa in the sun. Can't beat that. No, you can't. Are you wanting another biscuit? There’s still a few left. Don't mind if I do. Not one of those ginger ones though, they’re a bit strong for me. Alright, alright. A chocolate one it is. Here you go. Ta. Thank you, love. These are nice. These are proper biscuits. Not like some of the rubbish they sell now. They are good, aren’t they? Old-fashioned. Just how we like them. Exactly. They don’t make ‘em like they used to. No, they don’t. No, they really don’t. Is there anything else I can help you with? Do you want me to continue this conversation, perhaps adding another speaker or steering it towards a specific topic?

This pasta’s lovely, honestly. You’ve really outdone yourself. What did you put in the sauce? Just a bit of everything, really. Roasted peppers, some cherry tomatoes I managed to salvage from the garden before the rain, garlic… the usual. Honestly, the garden’s a disaster though. Everything’s looking a bit bedraggled after that downpour yesterday. Oh aye, it was biblical, wasn't it? Proper lashed it down. I was thinking about getting some lavender for the window boxes, but I’m worried it'll just get flattened. Lavender’s pretty resilient, actually. It’ll bounce back. You need to get some of those little plant supports though, especially if you’re going to put them outside. Speaking of which, have you heard back from Sarah and Mark about coming down next weekend? Not yet. I texted Sarah this morning but she just sent back a thumbs up emoji. Standard Sarah. I’m hoping they can make it. It feels like ages since we’ve all been together. Me too. Mark was going on about wanting to see the college gardens, remember? He’s obsessed with anything remotely historical. He is, isn’t he? A proper history buff. He’d love it here, honestly. It's a bit quieter than Birmingham, mind. Though maybe that’s a good thing for him. Definitely. A bit of peace and quiet is what we all need, really. I’m starting to think I should just give up on having a garden and replace it with gravel. Less work, less disappointment. Don’t be daft! It's lovely when it’s actually  nice  weather. Remember those tomatoes you grew last year? They were gorgeous. And you were so proud. True, true. Though I think half of them got eaten by slugs. Anyway, I was listening to that new Fontaines D.C. album on the way home today. Have you heard it? Oh aye, I’ve got it saved on Spotify. Haven’t really given it a proper listen yet, though. I've been stuck on that old Arctic Monkeys album again. Don’t judge. No judgement here!  Whatever People Say I Am, That’s What I’m Not  is a classic. Gets me every time. It’s just… sometimes I need something a bit less shouty, you know? Something a bit more mellow. I get you. Sometimes you just need a bit of background noise.

Honestly, hearing about Ben losing his job… it’s just awful, isn’t it? Especially after he’d only just finished that training course. It is rough. It’s that constant feeling of instability now, isn't it? Like you can do everything ‘right’ – get the qualifications, upskill, be reliable – and still just…get let go. Makes you wonder what the point is sometimes. Exactly! He was saying the company just decided to restructure. Classic corporate speak for “we don’t need you anymore”. He’s properly stressing about the mortgage and everything. Poor bloke. I keep thinking about that, actually. I mean, I’m lucky, obviously. PhD funding covers things, but the thought of having to actually  apply  for jobs properly after this… it’s terrifying. Remember how much everyone was panicking about getting a ‘graduate job’ back in the day? Oh god, yeah! The pressure! And then the internships that paid less than minimum wage just to get ‘experience’. It’s a scam, the whole thing. My sister was telling me about how much university fees have gone up  again . Seriously? They just keep hiking them up. It’s making higher education completely inaccessible for so many people. It’s already such a debt burden to take on, and it’s only getting worse. She’s worried about her youngest going to uni in a few years. Says she’ll have to help him with the fees even if they can barely afford it. It's a mess. It is. It really is. Hey, speaking of messes… Remember Sarah’s disaster of a rendition of ‘Defying Gravity’ at karaoke last month? Oh,  please ! Don’t remind me! Her key changes were… ambitious. And the high note? It was more of a strangled yelp. A strangled yelp is putting it mildly! I think she genuinely thought she was Idina Menzel. It was glorious. I was trying so hard not to laugh, but tears were streaming down my face. She even tried to do the dramatic arm movements! Honestly, it's why I love her. No self-awareness whatsoever. Do you fancy actually going to see a musical properly sometime? There’s a new production of  Wicked  on in London, apparently. Oh, that sounds amazing! I’ve always wanted to see that. And we could make a whole day of it, maybe go for a nice lunch beforehand? Definitely. We should check dates and book something.

Oh, that’s a lovely illustration, isn’t it? Really captures the mischievousness. Do you think Leo would understand the joke on this page though? He's still a bit literal sometimes. He’d get it. Honestly, he understands way more than you give him credit for. Remember when he explained irony to Gran? She was baffled. Ach, I remember! I thought  I  was losing it for a minute. He’s a bright lad, that one. Like his Uncle Hamish, always questioning everything. Hamish…that’s a name I haven’t heard in ages. How  is  Hamish? Last I heard he’d moved to…Australia, was it? Yeah, Australia. He’s good. Still doing the wildlife photography. Sends postcards, mostly pictures of kangaroos. He's got a little boy now, Finn. Amazing kid. Looks just like Dad did, apparently. Oh, good. I always worried about Hamish drifting so far away. Though, to be fair, your father wasn't the easiest to be around. Always had a different woman on his arm, didn’t he? Don’t remind me. It was…complicated. It’s probably why I’m so hesitant about…well, you know. Trying again. With someone new. You deserve someone brilliant, Mum. Someone who actually appreciates you.
