Mark was…not that. Aye, that Mark was a blunder. Never understood a word you said. Always talking about himself. Different to your stepfather, of course. A good man, though a quiet one. David was. He was solid. And good with you both, even though he wasn’t your biological father. It’s just…seeing how well Leo gets on with his dad, even with everything…it makes me wonder if I’ve messed things up. You haven’t messed anything up. Things are just…different. Leo’s happy, and that’s the main thing. You've created a lovely family, even if it doesn't look like the traditional one. Traditional! Ha! What  is  traditional anymore? I come from a family of ten, raised in a tiny tenement in Glasgow. My mother worked herself to the bone. That's traditional. This…this is just living! True. And speaking of family, I've been trying to sort out that family tree. It's proving a nightmare. Do you know anything about Great-Grandad Angus on your side, Gran? Dad barely spoke about him. Angus? Vaguely. I think Dad said he was a bit of a rogue.

Honestly, this shift is killing me. Like, absolutely draining. Oh no, really? Still at the cafe, yeah? Yeah, still at the cafe. It's just… constant. Constant customers, constant orders, constant cleaning. And old Mr. Henderson keeps trying to pay with loose change, like, handfuls of pennies. Oh, bless him. But that sounds exhausting. Are you managing to save any money though? A little bit, yeah. Enough for a takeaway at least. I’m thinking Chinese on Friday. Fancy it? Ooh, yes! Definitely. I’ve been craving a good chow mein all week. I’m just… bored of uni work, honestly. Endless essays. Tell me about it. I’m avoiding mine like the plague. It’s on Victorian literature, can you believe it? Ugh, sounds dreadful. At least your job is  doing  something. I feel like I just sit and read and read and read… Speaking of doing things, I finally shaved my legs properly yesterday. Oh, good for you! I haven’t done mine in ages. It’s getting ridiculous. Like a proper Yorkshire lass now. Haha! It’s just… I feel so much more presentable if I do. And winter is coming, you know? Trousers only go so far. True. Though I'm thinking just embracing the fuzz. Saves so much time and money on razors and shaving foam. Plus, it’s warmer. Hmm, a valid point. I just get self-conscious, I think. My mum always used to be really insistent on being smooth. Mine weren't bothered either way, honestly. Just as long as I was clean. Though, Dad did once comment on my “leg wool” when I was about fifteen. Mortifying. Oh my god, no! That’s awful. Dads are the worst sometimes. He thought he was being funny. I just glared at him. It’s just…effort, isn’t it? All that shaving… it’s a chore. Maybe I’ll just invest in some really thick tights. Problem solved. That's a good plan! Practical and warm. And less prickly. Exactly. Less prickly is always good. Right, I'm going to go and brace myself for another wave of pensioners wanting to pay with pennies. Chat later? Definitely. Good luck surviving! And let me know when you’re ordering the Chinese. I’ll get the prawn crackers. Is there anything else you’d like me to do? Perhaps you would like me to expand on the conversation, add another speaker, or change the context?

Right, so ‘V’ is for… vodka, obviously. Though honestly, after three pints of this, vodka feels a bit… aggressive. Aggressive is a good way to put it. I’m switching to Guinness, myself. Less likely to punch someone after a Guinness, you know? More likely to just… contemplate the meaning of life, very slowly. True. Though contemplating the meaning of life IS a dangerous game after enough alcohol. Remember Liam at uni? Ended up trying to explain quantum physics to a lamppost. Oh god, Liam. The man was a legendarily bad influence. Speaking of bad influences… ‘W’ has  got  to be whiskey. And associated stories of incredibly poor decisions. Definitely whiskey. Though my 'W' story isn't  my  poor decision. It was my cousin, Kevin. He decided, after a particularly potent single malt, he was a professional boxer. No way! Kevin? The one who cries during sad adverts? The very same. He challenged a bloke twice his size in a pub car park. Lasted approximately seven seconds. Honestly, it was less a boxing match and more a very swift, humiliating takedown. That’s brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. It's amazing what alcohol makes people think they can do. Which, slightly darker territory, makes me think about… the stuff that  isn’t  legal. 'X' - Xanax. Too many stories there, unfortunately. Yeah, a bit grim for alphabet games, isn’t it? Let’s swiftly move on. ‘Y’… honestly, I’m drawing a blank. Yogurt. Yogurt?! What? Hear me out. 'Y' is for yearning. Yearning for a probiotic snack after all this… indulgence. Plus, it subtly undermines the whole boozy theme. Subversive yogurt. You are ridiculous. But okay, I’ll allow it. Subversive yogurt. Right, last one. 'Z'… this is hard. Hmm… this is tough. You know what always springs to mind with ‘Z’? Zero tolerance. Which, sadly, brings me to thinking about the racism still prevalent in football. It’s just… appalling. It is. That incident with the England players last year… absolutely disgusting. The vitriol online was horrifying. Zero tolerance is exactly what's needed, but it's clearly not enough, is it? They need to find a way to stop it  before  it happens, not just punish people afterwards. Exactly. And it's not just football. It's everywhere, isn't it? It just… flares up in the public eye more with high-profile events. It’s exhausting. It is. God, this alphabet game took a turn.

…and the planning officer, bless her, was adamant. Absolutely adamant. No modern insulation, period. Said it would ‘compromise the breathability’ of the walls. Breathability! Honestly, you’d think we were building spaceships, not restoring a cottage. Oh, they’re a nightmare for that, aren’t they? The ‘breathability’ argument. It’s always breathability. I had a similar issue with the Old Rectory in Marsh Gibbon. Wanted to put in double glazing, beautiful, sympathetic timber frames, and they wouldn’t budge. Said it would trap moisture. Exactly! And then they wonder why damp is such a problem in these old buildings. It's a Catch-22, isn’t it? You’re trying to preserve them, but you’re limited in what you can actually  do  to preserve them. Have you looked at the lime plaster quotes yet? I sent you a few. I have, yes. A bit… daunting, to be honest. Mrs. Higgins’ quote is, predictably, the highest. But she does do exquisite work. I had her on the Tithe Barn back in ’08, and it still looks fantastic. Such a delicate touch. She’s worth it, though. It’s not just about the plaster, it’s about understanding the building. She understands the nuances. The cheaper quotes… well, I'm not convinced they've even  seen  a building like this before. That’s my worry. I’m leaning towards Mrs. Higgins, but the budget… It's a tightrope walk, isn't it? We really need to bolster that Heritage Lottery Fund application. Did you manage to get those additional photographs of the original fireplace? Yes, I did. I spent a good hour wrestling with the scaffolding yesterday, but I got them. They clearly show the original tooling, the detail. It’s a strong visual argument for retaining as much original fabric as possible. I’ve put them in a separate folder on the shared drive, labelled ‘Fireplace – Historic Detail’. Excellent. That’s exactly what we need. We need to emphasise the significance of that fireplace. It’s a unique example of… well, you know. It’s practically a signature piece of the local craftsman. Absolutely. And have you started drafting the section on community engagement? They always want to see community involvement, don’t they? I’ve got a rough outline. I was thinking maybe a series of workshops, showing traditional building techniques. Get locals involved in the restoration, make them feel ownership of the project.

Right, so I was explaining to my team today about the initial findings from the phonetics data, and honestly, half of them just glazed over. Like, I was talking about vowel shifts in Sunderland and they were looking at me like I’d sprouted a second head. Oh, the joys of explaining complex linguistic stuff to people who haven't dedicated their lives to it. It’s like trying to explain the intricacies of quantum physics to a cat. Exactly! And it’s not even  that  niche, is it? Everyone  has  an accent! Everyone speaks with regional variations! It's fascinating! They were more interested in the demographics section, naturally. Numbers are easier. Predictable. Though, to be fair, demographics  are  important. It’s easy to fall into the trap of assuming linguistic features are just random, when they're so intricately tied to social factors. Which, I suppose, is what my PhD is trying to unravel. You’re doing amazing work, you know. That stuff on second-generation Brummie accents… genuinely brilliant. It’s properly insightful. Thanks. It’s slow going, though. Trying to quantify subtle shifts in pronunciation… it's a rabbit hole. How’s your research progressing? Still wrestling with the Newcastle dialect’s influence on Sunderland speech? Yeah, pretty much. It's proving… complicated. There's a lot of intermingling, obviously, being so close. But trying to isolate distinct features… it's a nightmare. Plus, everyone’s code-switching all the time, depending on who they’re talking to. That's the beauty of it, isn’t it? People aren’t these rigid linguistic boxes. It’s fluid, adaptable. Speaking of adaptable… any thoughts on where we should go on holiday this year? I was idly scrolling through stuff last night. Ooh, good question. I was thinking maybe somewhere completely different. Somewhere with a totally alien soundscape. Iceland, maybe? Or even Georgia? Georgia? That sounds… intense. And probably involves a lot of consonants I can't pronounce. Iceland is good though. Imagine the fieldwork possibilities for  you . All those vowel sounds. You're awful! I'm trying to have a holiday, not collect data! Though… you’re right. It  would  be interesting. Maybe a compromise? Somewhere warm, but with a fascinating linguistic history? Morocco, perhaps? Morocco! I like that. We could wander around the souks, listen to the Arabic dialects… and eat loads of tagine. It's settled then.

Right, so I need to sort out the money for the school tennis tournament. They need £15 per child, and it’s next Friday. Oh. Can I take some sweets to school then? Well, you've had enough sweets recently, haven’t you? We talked about that. And no sweets for the tennis. It’s a sports event. Is it going to be sunny? Hopefully! Let’s look at the weather forecast later. Now, £15 each… that’s £30 total. I’ll get it sorted online tonight. How were school dinners today? They were… okay. I had chips and a sausage. I had pasta and chicken nuggets. And peas. Good. Did you eat all your vegetables? I ate some of the peas. I ate mine. Excellent. You know, Granny always makes sure you get lots of vegetables when you’re at her house. She’s very good at that. Granny’s food is the best. Especially her roast chicken. And her chocolate biscuits! Yes, she does make lovely biscuits. Though perhaps not quite as good as your midnight feast last night, was it? Maybe. So, the tennis. Do you both need new tennis socks? I think yours are probably getting a bit small, William. I don’t think so. They’re okay. Mine are fine too. Alright. Just checking. Right, anything else for school I need to know about? Any letters I’ve missed? Actually, Amelia said her mum said if she was a clown, she’d join the circus. Oh, really? That’s an interesting thought. I’d be an acrobat! I’d swing on the aerial hoop! Oh, you would, would you? That’s ambitious! It takes a lot of training to be an acrobat. I think I’d be the ringmaster. I’d tell everyone what to do. That suits you, William. Very bossy. I'm not bossy! No, no, I’m just joking. You’re a very decisive young man. Maybe someday you'll run your  own  circus! Now, back to serious things... the tennis money... and perhaps we can discuss a slightly more sensible topic. Have you finished your homework? Nearly. Yeah. I finished mine. Good. That’s good to hear. Mummy can I have a drink of juice? Yes, of course, darling. Just a small one. Rest your feet while you drink it. I want juice too. Okay, okay. Juice for everyone.

Honestly, that film was… exhausting. All that bleakness. Beautifully shot, of course, but emotionally draining. Bleakness is good for the soul, you know. Reminds you to appreciate the sunshine. Though I must confess, I found the pacing rather slow. Needed more explosions, frankly. Explosions? Dad! It was a character study, not a Michael Bay film. Though I agree with you, Sarah, it was heavy. Did anyone actually  like  the main character? He was utterly reprehensible. That’s the point, wasn’t it? To show how people can be driven to awful things by circumstance. It’s what they were debating at that Cambridge history event I went to last week, actually. How much responsibility do we assign to individuals versus societal forces? Oh, that sounds frightfully intellectual. All this modern history teaching… it’s not like when I was at school. Straightforward dates, kings and queens, battles. None of this ‘deconstructing narratives’ nonsense. They were arguing about that, specifically. About whether the national curriculum still prioritizes memorization over critical thinking. Apparently, there’s a push to get students to examine multiple perspectives, question sources… the usual. Which is good, isn’t it? Though it’s a difficult balance. You don’t want to end up with everyone claiming history is just ‘their truth’ and denying objective facts. Exactly! And these politicians… always meddling. Remember when they tried to make us all learn French? Utter waste of time. I never used a single phrase of French after leaving school. That was a disaster. And now they’re tinkering with the curriculum again. Honestly, it feels like they change it every five minutes, making it impossible for teachers to get their heads around it. It does. And it’s frustrating because we all  want  kids to have a robust education, but the constant shifting of priorities makes it so hard. It’s all about league tables and test results now, isn't it? That's the problem. It’s lost its focus on actually  teaching  and more about performance metrics. I’ve been talking to a few university departments about internships for some of our junior creatives. They’re finding graduates are technically proficient – they can use the software, they have the qualifications - but they lack the critical thinking skills and real-world application. That's a common complaint. I think part of it is the way degrees are structured. Too much theoretical study, not enough practical experience.

Terrible weather isn’t it? Keeps going and coming. Didn’t think we’d see rain like this in July. No, you wouldn’t. Reminds me of November, honestly. Could be sat with a fire going, couldn't you? Proper dreary. Well, it’s good for the garden, I suppose. Everything was starting to look a bit parched. Though, I suppose it’ll be slugs next. Always slugs. It's a bit unsettling, this weather. Makes you think about… well, everything that's going on in the world. Ukraine, that conflict in Sudan… It feels like things are getting more unstable. Always been unstable, hasn’t it? I remember when I was a lad, the Suez Crisis. That was a worry. Didn't know if we were all going to be bombed to smithereens. Though, it felt a long way off then, didn’t it? Being a kid in Norfolk. Oh, yes. I remember hearing my mother talking about it, saving coupons for everything. We didn’t have much, you know. Hard work, it was. Not like today. Speaking of hard work, I was looking through some old family documents the other day. Found out my great-grandfather was a bricklayer. Built half of Harrow, apparently. Really? That's fascinating. Mine were… well, mine were a bit more… bureaucratic. Civil servants, mostly. Very steady, very reliable. Not much excitement. My grandfather, he worked at the shoe factory in Norwich. Ernest Woods. Lovely man. He used to tell me stories about the war. Had a shrapnel wound in his leg, he did. Never complained, though. Just got on with it. They didn’t complain, did they? That generation. They’d seen too much. My uncle was a policeman, during the Blitz. Terrible things he saw. He never really talked about it. Just… blanked. It’s amazing to think about the lives our ancestors led, isn't it? So different from ours. I was having a clear out of the attic and found this old rocking chair. Must be Victorian. It’s solid as a rock, but covered in dust. Is it that one we were talking about, the one you thought might be worth something? Possibly. I’ve had a look online, and similar ones are going for a decent price. Though, it'll need a bit of restoration. Restoration? You can’t restore things properly these days. They don’t make the wood like they used to.

Right, so just to be clear, you’ve got the keys to Mum’s, yeah? And the forwarding address is all set up with the bank and everything? Yes, yes. All done. Honestly, feels…weird, doesn't it? Last trip from her place. Feels like the end of an era, really. It does. It’s massively bittersweet. I keep expecting to turn around and see her pottering in the garden. Are you alright driving? You seemed a bit…off this morning. Just a bit of a sniffle, that’s all. Old age catching up, I suppose. Nothing a hot toddy won’t fix tonight. Don’t fuss. You've been doing the bulk of the lifting with all this moving, I appreciate it. It’s no bother, honestly. It's just…I worry. Especially with you catching things. Remember that time you had the flu, and thought you’d broken your leg? Oh, don’t remind me. I was convinced I was dying. Your mother fussed over me for a week straight. Speaking of your mother, have you managed to sort out her broadband at the new place? She'll have a fit if she can’t watch  Bargain Hunt . I called them yesterday. They’re sending an engineer on Tuesday. Apparently, it's a slightly different setup, so it needs a bit of fiddling. She was mostly concerned about whether they'd understand her accent. Oh, she’s a character, your mother. Reminds me of old Mrs. Higgins from down the road. Always complaining but with a heart of gold. Right. Are we nearly there? My stomach’s rumbling. I skipped breakfast this morning, being all emotional about leaving Mum. About twenty minutes. I was thinking we could grab some fish and chips in Northampton? It's been ages. That sounds lovely, actually. Proper chippy chips, not that frozen rubbish. Speaking of things being ages, remember that holiday we took to Cornwall when you were about eight? The one where I lost all my money on the arcade machines? How could I forget? You were  furious . You swore you'd never play a fruit machine again. And I haven’t! Mostly. It was a fortune, it was. Enough for a decent deposit on a small house, probably. Which brings me to…have you looked at remortgaging? Your rates must be going up. I’ve started looking, yeah. It’s a nightmare.

Right, so we’re thinking roast beef, yeah? Nan always loved a good roast beef. It feels… fitting. Definitely. And Yorkshire puddings, obviously. Huge ones. Remember last year when Uncle Barry ate like, four? Oh, Barry. Always the showman. Okay, roast beef, Yorkshire puds, roast potatoes…what about veg? She used to adore those little steamed carrots with a knob of butter. Oh, yes! And peas. She always insisted on mushy peas. Drives everyone else mad, but it's Nan. We have to. Mushy peas it is. Now, the seating plan… This is where it gets tricky. Auntie Carol and Uncle David  have  to be separated. You know how they get going about politics. Oh, lord, yes. Total disaster waiting to happen. Put Uncle David next to me, maybe? I can deflect. He just likes talking  at  people anyway. Good thinking. And your Mum and Dad… they’re alright together, aren't they? I'll put them near Nan, so she can easily chat. Yeah, they’re fine. They’ll probably just talk about the garden. Have you got the photo board sorted? The one with all the baby pictures and stuff? Almost. I was trying to find that one of her and Grandad on their honeymoon… the one in Blackpool. It’s vanished. Honestly, I’ve been rearranging cupboards all afternoon trying to find it! It’s like things just… disappear these days. It's a bit worrying, honestly. It is, isn’t it. It’s like when she started forgetting where she put her spectacles, then the TV remote… It's scary. Don’t. Don’t start, darling. We’re celebrating, not dwelling. Though, you're right. It's getting harder. It was only last week she asked me who I was. Oh, Mum. That must've been awful. It was. But she smiled afterwards, and said I looked familiar. That’s something, isn’t it? Anyway. Focus. Candles? I was thinking those lavender-scented ones she likes. Perfect. And maybe a little bouquet for the table? Nothing too flashy. Yes, just something cheerful. I was at the fishmongers earlier, trying to find a nice salmon fillet for a starter, but they'd sold out. Apparently, everyone’s having fish on Friday. Of course they are! You’d think they’d  expect  it. Fancy some bread and butter pudding for dessert? I saw a recipe on Great British Bake Off the other night that looked amazing.

Right, honestly, my mouth is killing me. Proper killing me. Oh no, what’s up? Still with the wisdom teeth? Aye, still with ‘em. They finally decided to properly come through, but it's not… nice. Like, there's these holes on both sides now, and everything gets stuck. It's awful. Ugh, that sounds properly grim. Have you seen a dentist out here, or are you waiting ‘til we get back? Waiting ‘til we get back. I’m not trying to navigate French dental insurance, thank you very much. My mum was going on about how I should've had them out ages ago. "Should've, could've, would've," honestly. Mums are good at that, aren't they? Mine’s already grilling me about getting my dissertation started again. Like I haven't even had a proper break yet! Oh god, dissertations. Don't even remind me. I’m dreading going back. Honestly, this has been the best distraction. Though I’m starting to feel a bit guilty about putting everything off. Same. But a week in the sun is a pretty good excuse, I reckon. Besides, we need this. Especially after… everything with your folks. Don't. Don't go there. It's still… a lot. The move, and everything. Sorry, I didn’t mean to. It just feels proper weird knowing they’re already settled in that new place. Is it… nice? I haven't seen any pictures. It’s… small. Apparently. Mum sent a quick text saying it’s “cosy.” Which, knowing my mum, means you can practically touch all four walls at once. Dad seems alright about it, but he misses the garden. He’s always going on about his roses. He does love his roses. Right, well, try not to think about it too much. We've got, what, three more days of not thinking about dissertations and family drama? Sounds like a plan. We going back to that little patisserie tomorrow? I need another one of those pain au chocolat. It's the only thing that's relieving the pain in my mouth, honestly. Definitely. And maybe we can check out that market everyone keeps talking about. Apparently, they've got amazing cheese. Ooh, cheese. Now you’re talking. Though, I’m a bit worried about how I’m gonna get all me stuff back to uni when we get back. I think I’ve bought way too much.

Right, so we need to think of some good acts of kindness for this week. Mrs. Peterson said it could be anything, big or small. Can we bake cookies for Old Man Hemmings? He always waves! But… cookies have milk in them, don’t they? Grandma gets tummy aches if she has milk. Good point, sweetheart. We could make lactose-free ones! There are some really good recipes online. Or maybe we could make him a card? A card with sparkly bits! And a picture of a dragon! It’s nearly Chinese New Year, dragons are lucky! I want to learn to write ‘Happy New Year’ in Chinese! It looks like squiggles! That’s a brilliant idea! We can look that up later. It's the Year of the Dragon this year, isn’t it? I was reading about it – apparently, dragons symbolize power and good fortune. Can we get red envelopes too? Like in the pictures? Absolutely! We can get some and fill them with… hmm. What should we put in them? Money! But… we don’t have any real money. Well, we could use our chess pieces! Remember when we pretended the pawns were pennies and the queen was a pound? Ooh, yeah! I can give Old Man Hemmings three pawns and a knight! That's…a lot! I want to give him a rook! They’re the castle pieces, and castles are important! That’s very generous of you both. Okay, cookies or cards for Mr. Hemmings, Chinese New Year envelopes with chess piece money… what else? I was thinking maybe we could help Mrs. Davies with her shopping. She struggles with the heavy bags. But she always smells funny. Well, we can wave and smile at her then. Kindness doesn’t always mean getting close, does it? Sometimes it just means being friendly. Can I dye my hair red like a dragon for Chinese New Year? Please? Oh no, absolutely not! Red hair dye stains  everything ! Plus, your dad would have a fit. I want purple hair! Like a magical dragon princess! We can talk about temporary hair spray maybe. Nothing permanent! Let’s focus on the acts of kindness first. Now, about that Chinese writing… I’ll get my laptop. And we need to check if we have enough lactose-free flour for the cookies. Does this meet your requirements? Let me know if you’d like me to continue the conversation or adjust anything!

So, did you see that dent in the car? Dad’s absolutely fuming. Oh, yes! He told me. What  happened  exactly? He just said someone reversed into you at the supermarket. Yeah, basically. I was walking back to the car with the shopping and this silver van just…backed right into the back bumper! It wasn’t going massively fast, but still. A proper thump. The lady was  so  apologetic though. Kept saying she hadn’t seen me. Oh dear. Are you okay? Not shaken up or anything? I’m fine, honestly. Just a bit startled. It was more annoying than anything. Dad's just worried about the cost of the repair, I think. It looks worse than it is, though, honestly. Still. Not a nice experience. It reminds me a bit of that time I cycled into Mrs. Higgins’ rose bush when I was your age. Completely demolished it. Oh, Mum! You’ve told me that story a million times. Well, it’s a good story! So, what else has been happening? Anything exciting at school? Still enjoying English? Yeah, it’s good. We’re doing  Alice in Wonderland  at the moment, and it’s actually really weird, but in a good way. I didn’t realise how bonkers it was before. All those talking animals… It  is  bonkers, isn’t it? Very clever though. Have you seen any of the stage adaptations? They can be incredible. Not yet. I’d like to, though. There’s one touring next year, apparently. I was looking at it online. Oh, lovely! We should see if we can go. Speaking of online, what have you been listening to lately? Still obsessed with that band, ‘Static Bloom’? They’ve released a new single! It’s really good. I got the lyrics downloaded, and I’m trying to learn the guitar part. It’s hard. You're determined, that’s for sure! Your grandfather was very musical, you know. Played the piano beautifully. He’d be proud. I know. I wish I'd asked him to teach me. Have you started thinking about Christmas presents yet? A little bit. I'm completely stumped for your dad, as usual. He says he doesn't  need  anything. Tell me about it! He’s impossible to buy for. Maybe a new gardening tool? He's been going on about needing a better trowel. Hmm, not a bad idea.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork they had to wade through! I was telling them last night, it’s not enough to just  feel  strongly about it, you have to be absolutely meticulous. Every objection, backed up with evidence. Absolutely. It's the same with these solar farms, you know? They're proposing a huge one just outside Ramsgate, taking up prime agricultural land. Beautiful countryside. People are furious, but fury alone won't stop it. They need to be armed with facts. Facts and money, that’s what they need. That’s the really nasty bit, isn’t it? These energy companies, they’ve got bottomless pockets. They can afford to fight tooth and nail, hire the best lawyers… it’s David and Goliath. Exactly! And the council… well, let’s just say their Development Control Committee isn’t always the most…robust. I sat on that committee for a brief, regrettable period. Too many councillors are swayed by promises of ‘investment’ and ‘jobs’. They don’t think about the long-term consequences. It's all about ticking boxes for them, isn’t it? Meeting their green targets, whatever the cost to the local environment. They don’t care about losing valuable farmland or spoiling the landscape. It’s just numbers on a spreadsheet. They should be looking at the bigger picture. Honestly, all this money being thrown at subsidies for wind and solar… it's peanuts compared to the investment needed for proper research. Energy storage, for instance! That’s the real bottleneck. You can generate all the green energy you like, but if you can’t store it effectively, what’s the point? Precisely! I read an article the other day about some breakthrough with flow batteries… apparently, they’re far more efficient and environmentally friendly than lithium-ion. But it’s still in the early stages. Needs funding. They say there’s a new type of hydrogen storage being explored, using some sort of metal alloy… but again, it needs significant investment. It’s just frustrating. So much potential, stifled by short-sighted policies. It's the politics of it all, isn't it? The lobbying, the backroom deals… it’s a murky business. These planners, they're not always acting in the public interest. Sometimes, you have to wonder where their loyalties lie. Oh, definitely. And you have to look at who’s  funding  all these studies that supposedly prove these developments are ‘sustainable’.

So, have you booked those driving lessons then, love? Your mother’s been going on about it for weeks. I have! First one is next Tuesday. Bit nervous, actually. It’s been… a while since I even thought about it. Nervous? Good! A bit of healthy nervousness keeps you alert. Your Grandad Albert, bless him, thought he was Fangio before he even started lessons. Nearly drove Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses into the canal! That’s a slight exaggeration, Mary. He stalled, and it rolled a bit. Didn’t  quite  reach the canal. Still, the roses weren’t thrilled. You’ll be fine, though. It’s a sensible thing to do. I hope so. The instructor seemed nice on the phone, but I’m worried about the parallel parking. Everyone says that’s the killer. Oh, it is a devil. But practice makes perfect. Though, mind you, these modern cars with all their sensors… takes the skill out of it, doesn’t it? We had to rely on mirrors and instinct back in my day. Speaking of cars, we need to sort out insurance quotes for you. I’ve had a look, and it’s… surprisingly expensive. Especially for a new driver. I was expecting that. I’ve been saving, though. I’m hoping I can find something reasonable, especially if I start with a smaller engine. Good thinking. And make sure you declare everything properly. Don’t try to be clever, eh? Little fibs come back to haunt you with insurance companies. Absolutely. Right, what about holidays? Any firm plans for the summer? Not yet, but I’m thinking maybe Cornwall. I’ve always wanted to go to the Eden Project. Cornwall is lovely. Though it can get awfully crowded in the summer. We went a few years back, and it was like Piccadilly Circus down there. We had a lovely time in Dorset last year. Quite peaceful. Perhaps we could all go somewhere together this year? A cottage by the sea… That sounds lovely, Dad! I’d be up for that. We could take Buster, too. Oh, yes! Buster would love that. He practically lives for a good beach romp. Though we need to make sure wherever we go is dog-friendly, of course. I'll start looking. And Mary, perhaps you could check on your Auntie Beatrice this week? I spoke to her on Friday, and she sounded a little down.

Honestly, Dad, the parking in Brighton is a nightmare. I spent twenty minutes circling yesterday just to drop off groceries. Twenty minutes? Back in our day, you just parked where you wanted. No yellow lines, no meters, no bother. Though Old Man Hemmings would get a bit cross if you blocked his drive, mind you. He was a proper grump, Hemmings. Things were different then, weren’t they? It’s just… everything’s so crammed now. And expensive. I saw a parking space advertised for £250 a month! £250? Crikey. You could’ve bought a horse for that money back then. Remember old Bess? Your Grandad bought her for fifty quid at the market. Best horse he ever had. Always a winner at the races, Bess was. Though he did nearly bankrupt us all a couple of times betting on her. Oh, you and your horse racing. Still glued to the telly for it, are you? Can’t help it, love. It’s in the blood. Got a little bet on this afternoon, actually. A fiver each way on ‘Lucky Star’. Don’t tell your mother. I won’t. Speaking of things I shouldn’t tell Mum, have you seen what Facebook is doing now? Another update. Constant notifications. It's driving me mad. Facebook? What's Facebook? Some sort of newfangled contraption? I wouldn’t know, I stick to my crossword and the racing post. These newfangled things, they're all just a waste of time, if you ask me. It’s… complicated. It’s how everyone stays in touch. But honestly, sometimes I wish I could just turn it off. It's just noise. Noise is what it is. You kids always need something buzzing in your ear. We survived alright without all this… whatchamacallit… technology. We made our own fun. I know, I know. Though, honestly, I’m starting to think I need to learn to cook properly. I’m living on pasta and pesto at the moment. It’s not exactly healthy. Pasta and pesto? Good grief. When I was your age, your mother had me making proper meals. Roast dinners, shepherd’s pie… She’d have your hide if she knew you were living on that muck. Though she was a good cook. Always made sure we had fresh produce. Remember that allotment we had? Vaguely. I remember helping you pick runner beans. And being eaten alive by mosquitoes.

Honestly, the level of Shakespearean drama in the student union debate society is…intense. Like, full-on hand-wringing and soliloquies about lost library books. You’re kidding. Is someone trying to be Hamlet over a late fee? Pretty much. This guy, Alistair – complete with velvet waistcoat, naturally – was going on about the injustice of it all. “To pay, or not to pay, that is the question!” It was brilliant, but also… exhausting. He’s got a surname like ‘Thornthwaite’ or something equally ridiculous. Thornthwaite?! That’s perfect. Sounds like a character  from  Shakespeare. They should just call him Thorn. Everyone shortens surnames, right? My Nan always called old Mr. Davies “Daff” – because he apparently looked like a daffodil. Daff Davies! Oh, that’s magnificent. We call old Professor Eldridge ‘El’. Mostly because his lectures are… lethargic. It feels rude, but it’s become a thing. Fair enough. Speaking of things becoming a thing, I tried golf again yesterday. Absolute disaster. I genuinely think the ball actively  avoided  hitting the hole. You and golf. It’s a doomed romance. I still maintain it’s just an excuse to walk around a field and get aggressively frustrated. It’s the competitive angle, I think. I  need  to win. It’s a deep-seated issue, probably stemming from childhood board game losses. It's a flaw, I know. I take it way too seriously. It's endearing. Well, slightly. It's more amusing to watch you seethe internally whilst politely congratulating someone on their par. You’re a master of passive-aggressive golf. Exactly! I’m a specialist. Though, I’m starting to think I’d have more success learning to yodel. At least then the frustration would be… audible. Now  that  I’d pay to see. Imagine you, mid-yodel, following a particularly bad shot. Don’t encourage me. Anyway, how's work going at the bookshop? Still dealing with demanding literary snobs? Oh, you know. Yesterday, someone demanded a first edition of  Ulysses  without knowing what  Ulysses  even  is . I just stared at them. Then subtly directed them to the Mills & Boon section. You legend. You’re openly sabotaging their reading choices? It’s a public service, really. Preventing cultural contamination. Plus, it’s incredibly satisfying. And honestly, that guy had an air of someone who’d complain about the font size. You're a menace. A delightful menace. Right, another coffee?

Honestly, this week has been  mental  at work. Like, back-to-back meetings, everyone wanting everything yesterday. You wouldn’t believe the demands. Tell me about it. Bricklaying in this heat is… a special kind of torture. At least you’re indoors with air con, yeah? Air con that’s permanently set to ‘arctic’ by the IT department. I’m sat here in a cardigan, honestly. It’s a bit ridiculous. How’s the new build going, then? Are you actually making progress? Slowly but surely. Foreman’s on my back about speed, naturally. Says I need to “crack on”. Like I’m not trying! But hey, a job’s a job, innit? Pays the bills. Speaking of which… anyone fancy ordering another pizza? I’m starving. Ooh, tempting. I’m trying to be good though. Started one of those juice cleanses. A juice cleanse? Seriously, Chloe? You and your fads. How long will that last? Two days, tops. Hey! I’m on day three! It’s… challenging. Mostly challenging because everything smells amazing and I can’t eat it. Honestly, even your wine smells tempting. You can have a sip, if you like. Loosen you up a bit. Being all healthy isn't worth missing out on good times. Maybe just a tiny sip. It wouldn't hurt, would it? What about you, Amelia? How's work? Still trying to wrangle those production deadlines? You have  no  idea. We’re launching the new range next month, and everything is a disaster. The packaging factory messed up the design, half the stock is delayed, and my boss is breathing down my neck. Honestly, I think I'm developing a stress rash. Sounds glamorous. Oh, it  is . Particularly when I’m checking spreadsheets at midnight. I'm considering moving back in with my parents, just to save some money and escape the chaos. Oh, no! Don’t do that! That’s… backwards progress. You’ve got that lovely flat! I know, I know. But the rent is ridiculous. And honestly, having a bit of family support while I get this launch sorted would be amazing. What about you two? Any changes on the living front? Nah, still crammed into that tiny flat with Dave. It’s cozy… in a claustrophobic sort of way. We’re trying to save for a deposit, but Cambridge property prices are insane. Seriously. It’s a joke.

Right, well, you can just about see the whole garden from here, can’t you? Bit of a mess, admittedly. Been meaning to get out there with the shears. Looks alright to me, Harold. Gardens always look a bit…lived-in, don’t they? Especially after a bit of weather. Still, seems a lot smaller on this screen, doesn't it, Margaret? It does, Arthur. Though it’s lovely to see it. You’ve got a right jungle growing on there, Harold. Is that bamboo still taking over? Oh, the bamboo. Don't even get me started. Tried digging it up, but it just keeps coming back. It’s evil stuff, that, honestly. Like it  wants  to take over the world. Remember Old Man Hemmings next door? He had a right battle with bamboo years ago. Ended up using some sort of chemical, I think. Didn't do the roses much good, mind. I’m loathe to use chemicals, you know. Bad for the bees. And I've got the owl box up in the oak, need to keep that area safe for them. Speaking of which, haven’t seen the tawny owl for a few weeks now. Hope she’s alright. Oh dear. They are beautiful birds, aren’t they? I used to have one frequent my garden when I was childminding. Fascinated the little ones. It's that time of year, isn’t it? They’re probably busy nesting somewhere. Though, talking of nesting, Mrs. Peterson is at it again about the fence. Says I’ve let it get too wonky. Oh, not that fence! What does she want, a straight line all the way down? It’s a fence, Arthur, not the Taj Mahal! Honestly, some people! Always something, isn’t there? Sounds like a typical neighbourly dispute. More than a dispute, it’s a war of attrition. She's forever complaining about something. Last week it was the height of my lavender. Said it was blocking her sunlight. Honestly! She’s a difficult woman. Always has been. Remember when she reported us for having a television that wasn’t covered by a license? Don’t remind me. It was a complete waste of time. They came out, checked, and of course, everything was perfectly legal. She just likes to cause trouble. Speaking of television, did you catch that David Attenborough programme last night? The one about black holes?

Right, so if we go this way, we completely avoid that roundabout near the retail park. Absolute chaos it was last time, honestly. Sounds good to me. Though, I still maintain that roundabout isn't  that  bad. People just don’t understand priority, that’s all. Priority? They don’t understand how to merge, love! It’s just a free-for-all. Anyway, are we still thinking Italian tonight? I was looking at that place, ‘Bella Notte’, near the cathedral. Bella Notte… hmm. Seems a bit… touristy, doesn’t it? All red checked tablecloths and opera music. Well, the reviews are decent, and I fancy pasta. We could go to that new Thai place, but you said you weren't feeling it last week. I wasn’t, no. Too spicy. And it's a bit out of the way, isn't it? All the way up near Bishop Auckland? It feels like a proper trek. It’s not  that  far! It's, like, twenty minutes. And Bishop Auckland's alright, actually. They've done a lot of work on the town centre. I don’t know. Remember when we tried going to that pub near Durham, ‘The Old Mill’? Thought it’d be all cosy and historic, ended up being freezing and smelling of damp. Oh,  don’t  remind me. It was like stepping back in time…to a very cold, unhappy time. That was a mistake. At least Durham Cathedral is lovely, even if the pub was a disaster. It is stunning, though. Makes you feel quite small, doesn't it? All that history. I saw some photos online of the interior - the vaulted ceilings are incredible. Absolutely. It's a shame the bus routes are so rubbish around there. Getting there without a car is a nightmare. I remember trying when I was at uni… took me nearly two hours! Two hours! Seriously? That's ridiculous. I suppose that's why everyone drives. Speaking of drives, are you sure you’re happy doing all the navigating? You've been brilliant so far, but my phone's running low on battery. Aye, I'm happy enough. I've got the offline maps downloaded. Plus, I’m a Geordie, we're born with an internal compass. Actually, I was looking at houses near York train station the other day. Houses? What’s this about? Are you thinking of moving? Just browsing, you know.

…and then I realised, it wasn’t a robin at all! It was a dunnock. Honestly, they sound almost identical, don’t they? But a dunnock’s song is a bit… flatter, less cheerful. Oh, I struggle with those little brown jobs. Robins, blackbirds, chaffinches, easy. But all the smaller ones… they all just blend into a general birdsong chorus for me. Though, I did get a new bird feeder, you know, the one with the cages around it. Oh, the squirrel-proof ones? Good thinking. They're relentless, aren't they? Little acrobats. They are! And greedy. I was watching one the other day, practically dismantling the feeder trying to get at the sunflower hearts. It’s stopped them mostly, though. Keeps the starlings out too, which is a bonus. They’re lovely to watch, but they clear the feeder in minutes. I find the birdsong wakes me up now, rather than the alarm. Which is nice, until it’s a particularly insistent blackbird at half past five! Still, better than that jarring beep, isn’t it? Oh, miles better. I’ve had alarm clocks that’ve driven me to distraction. Though, you know, I had a bit of a scare the other day. Woke up with a nosebleed. Right in the middle of the night. Oh dear! Are you alright? Yes, yes, perfectly fine now. Just… a bit alarming, you know? Happened once years ago, but not since. I think it was just the dry air. And I’d been gardening earlier, bending over a lot. That’ll do it. Gardening’s good for the soul, though. I’m trying to get some lavender established. It’s proving difficult. Keep getting slugs. Slugs! They’re the bane of my existence. Old Mrs. Higgins down the road, she swears by beer traps. Apparently, they drown in them. That’s… rather gruesome, isn’t it? I might just stick to the pellets. Speaking of Mrs. Higgins, have you seen her lately? She hasn’t been to the WI for a couple of months. No, I haven't. I heard… well, Doreen told me, and you know how Doreen’s gossip is, but apparently, her daughter mentioned she was having some tests done. Something with her throat. Oh, no. That’s awful. She’s such a lovely woman. Isn’t she? Always cheerful, always baking. Doreen said it  might  be throat cancer, but it’s early days.

Honestly, it’s just… exhausting, isn’t it? The constant updates. Everyone presenting this utterly  perfect  version of their lives. Tell me about it! I was scrolling through Instagram last night, and it’s just endless holiday photos, perfect families… it's all performative. You know it’s not real life. Exactly! I’ve started limiting myself to, like, fifteen minutes a day. It just sucks the joy out of everything. Though, I did see Sarah Millington posted photos from Italy. Looks lovely, but honestly, I'm pretty sure she's heavily in debt after that trip. Oh, Sarah. Always one for appearances. How  is  she, anyway? Haven’t spoken to her in ages. She's… okay. Still clinging to the dream of a perfect life, I think. She’s been talking about another round of IVF. It's her third attempt, and I feel so bad for her, but she’s just pinning all her happiness on it. Oh, poor thing. That must be incredibly stressful. I remember when Lisa was going through it. It took such a toll on her, physically and emotionally. She ended up deciding to go down the single parent route, you know? Adoption. That’s lovely. Is she happy? Absolutely thriving. Little Leo is the apple of her eye, and honestly, she’s said it’s the best thing she ever did. She’s found a real community through the adoption agency, too. It's really changed her life. It makes you think, doesn't it? About what truly makes a family. It does. I’ve been doing a lot of thinking lately, actually. About everything. Work, life… I’m starting to feel… restless. Like I need a change. Oh? What kind of change? Still teaching? Still teaching, for now. But I’ve started writing again. Remember I used to write short stories? Of course! You were brilliant! You always had such a knack for character development. What are you working on? I’ve started a novel. It’s… ambitious. It’s set in Dorset, obviously. A bit of a family saga, with a bit of mystery thrown in. It's early days, but it's keeping me sane, honestly. A good distraction from the chaos of social media and the relentless pressure to be ‘perfect’. Actually, it's therapeutic. That's fantastic! You absolutely should. You need a creative outlet. It's so important.

Honestly, this tea is a lifesaver. The kids were  full  of beans this morning. Year 9s, you know? Just… relentless. Ah, yes. I remember those days. Though my battlefield was more… Shakespearean insults than TikTok trends. It’s a different world, isn't it? Completely different. It’s amazing how quickly things change. They were asking me about influencers today, honestly. Influencers! Instead of poets. Times change, young lady. Though I suspect human nature doesn't. Still the same desire for attention, just a different platform. How’s the French going? Still battling with subjunctive moods? Oh, don't even  start  me on the subjunctive. It's a constant struggle. I feel like I spend half my life explaining why it exists. But it’s good, genuinely. I love seeing them get that ‘aha!’ moment when it finally clicks. Makes the headaches worthwhile. It does, doesn't it? That little spark of understanding. That’s why I did it for so long. Though, truth be told, I miss the peace and quiet sometimes. Retirement is lovely, don't get me wrong, but… a bit too much time with one’s own thoughts. I can imagine. Do you still do much gardening then? I remember you talking about your roses. I do. Though the slugs have been having a field day this year. Absolute bandits, they are. It’s a constant war, honestly. And my knees aren’t what they used to be, bending down all the time. Getting old is… well, it's not for the faint-hearted. Tell me about it! I swear I pulled a muscle just reaching for a biscuit earlier. Speaking of which… more tea? Don’t mind if I do. You know, there was a bit of bother down the street last night. Young lads trying to break into Mr. Henderson's shed. Oh no! Really? That’s awful. Poor Mr. Henderson. He’s such a lovely man. Lovely, but a bit naive. Left the shed unlocked, apparently. They didn't get much, thankfully. Just a few garden tools. Police were round this morning, taking statements. Makes you think, doesn't it? It's getting worse around here. It is. It’s quite worrying. I try to keep the kids aware of their surroundings, you know? Things were so different when we were growing up. Different indeed. My Margaret – she’s a nurse down at the City Hospital – she says they’re seeing more and more stabbings, even young ones.

Right, so I’m officially declaring it’s pizza night. I’ve had a day. A  day . Like, spreadsheets actively tried to fight me. Oh, tell me about it. My inbox is currently a disaster zone. Found an email from July still lurking in there. July! Sounds rough. Though, to be fair, my day mostly involved arguing with software that insists my calculations are wrong when they demonstrably aren’t. It’s a personality clash, honestly. You lot are having stressful days, huh? Mine was… underwhelmingly average. Which, after a week of fire-fighting on site, is a win. Pizza sounds fantastic though. What kind are we thinking? I was leaning towards a proper Yorkshire Pepperoni. Loads of it. None of this fancy stuff. Just…meat and cheese. Ooh, good shout. I’m down. Though, can we at least  consider  having some of those garlic bread things on the side? They just elevate the whole experience. I'm easy, pepperoni is good. Though I did discover this insane Spotify playlist last night – all 80s synthwave. It’s unbelievably cheesy. Perfect pizza-eating music. I can send you the link? Yes, please do! I’ve been stuck in a bit of a musical rut lately. Need something new. Speaking of cheesy, has anyone seen that new Adam Sandler film? The one where he’s a talking hamster? You are taking the Mickey, aren’t you? No, thankfully, I’ve avoided that particular cinematic low point. I heard it’s… a choice. Apparently his daughter insisted he do it. The internet said it’s so bad it’s almost good. Like a train wreck. But honestly, I’d rather listen to 80s synthwave on repeat. Sounds about right. Anyway, pizza is a solid plan. What about after? Anyone fancy a board game? I brought ‘Ticket to Ride’ with me. Ooh, yeah! I’m always up for ‘Ticket to Ride’. Though, fair warning, I’m fiercely competitive. I will cut you all off at the pass. Bring it on! I’m surprisingly ruthless when it comes to train routes. Oh dear, this sounds like it’s escalating quickly. I'll just… quietly try to build my routes and hope for the best. Excellent. So, pizza, synthwave, then world domination via railway networks. Sounds like a perfect evening to me. Right, who's ordering? I’m terrible at phone calls. I'll do it. Unless anyone wants to attempt to navigate the website?

Honestly, the gym was rammed this morning. Like, shoulder-to-shoulder rammed. Couldn't get near the squat rack. Oh, no way! It's usually pretty quiet when I go, which is around six-ish. Everyone's still asleep, I guess. Or avoiding leg day. Leg day is the worst. Pure suffering. I tried doing a circuit yesterday and I swear my quads are still screaming. You guys are dedicated. I haven't stepped foot in a gym since… well, since before the pandemic, probably. I’m more of a ‘walk to the shops’ kind of fitness enthusiast. You need to get back into it, man! It's good for the brain, too. Speaking of needing a break, I’m seriously thinking about a little trip somewhere. Somewhere warm. Ooh, where were you thinking? Anywhere specific? I've been scrolling through Airbnb, fantasizing about Greek islands. I was looking at Portugal, actually. Algarve area. Seems pretty reasonable, decent weather, good food. Not too far to travel. Portugal sounds nice. So much better than the weather we’re having here. It’s been drizzling on and off all day. Proper miserable. Makes you want to hibernate. Tell me about it. I walked to get coffee earlier and nearly got blown away. It's like autumn decided to skip straight to November. Did anyone ever end up getting tickets for that festival? The one we were talking about last week? The electronic one in London? I did! Managed to snag a couple. It's ages away though, like, next July. Good excuse to start planning. Nice! What kind of music are they playing? I'm not very up on my electronic stuff. It’s all pretty varied, actually. Some proper techno, some house, a bit of drum and bass. Should be a good vibe. I'm thinking about volunteering at my niece's kids’ camp this summer. It's a bit chaotic, but it’s good fun. Oh, that's sweet of you! What sort of activities do they do? The usual, I guess. Arts and crafts, sports, a lot of running around. They have a themed week, this year it’s pirates. Apparently, I need to learn how to tie nautical knots. Pirates? That sounds amazing! I'd be rubbish at nautical knots though. I can barely tie my shoelaces properly. Haha! Maybe you can be the pirate who trips over everything.

Honestly, the refereeing in this game is absolutely shocking. Shocking. Aye, it’s a bit ropey, isn’t it? Gave that away far too easily. Should’ve held their ground. Held their ground? They were practically inviting a tackle! It’s like they  wanted  a free kick for the other team. You’re harsh. They were trying to be clever, a bit of a feint. Didn’t come off. Clever? It was amateur hour. Reminds me of when I tried to learn karate as a kid. All flailing limbs and no coordination. You, doing karate? I’m picturing it now. Don't you dare! I was dedicated. For about a week. Until I realised falling over gracefully wasn’t one of my talents. Right, they’ve got a corner. This could be interesting. Depends if they can actually deliver a decent ball. Their crossing’s been… optimistic, to say the least. Optimistic is one word for it. Airshot city is another. Remember that film we watched last week? The one with… what was his name? The guy who played the footballer? Pelé? You mean  Escape to Victory ? That's the one! Honestly, it’s a bit cheesy but still brilliant. Especially the bit with the helicopter… Ah, a classic. Though their football skills looked a  lot  better than what we're seeing on screen right now. A low bar, admittedly. Oh! Good header! But the keeper saved it. Of course he did. He had no chance, actually. Right on the line. Still, should’ve been more accurate. Speaking of accuracy, have you thought about what we’re doing for Easter? My mum’s already asking. Easter? Is it already that time? Feels like Christmas was yesterday. Tell me about it. She wants to know if we’re coming home. And if we bring chocolate. Specifically, Cadbury’s Creme Eggs. It’s a non-negotiable requirement. Creme Eggs, huh? A worthy demand. I’m happy to acquire a substantial quantity for the mission. Plus, you know your mum’s roast dinner is legendary. It is. It really is. Though she does make me help peel the potatoes. Traitorous potatoes. A small price to pay for culinary brilliance. Although, I'm not sure my digestive system can handle a  full  roast dinner these days. PhD life has been kind to my waistline… said no one ever. You’ve been living off instant noodles and despair, haven't you?

Ah, look at this one! Little Leo, absolutely covered in chocolate. Must have been… what, four years old? At that funfair in Tralee. Whoa! He  is  a mess. Did he fall into a chocolate fountain or something? No, he won a game. One of those where you try to knock down the milk bottles with a ball. And the prize was a huge chocolate bar. He just… demolished it. Right there and then. Face, hands, clothes – everything. Boys will be boys! Reminds me of your Uncle Hamish. At the Glasgow fair, he managed to get stuck on one of those rotating teacups. Couldn’t stop laughing! Eventually, a strong man had to lift him out. Oh, Hamish. Always a character. You know, looking at these pictures… it feels like yesterday he was a tiny babbling thing. And now he’s almost taller than me. He’s growing so fast. He’s already talking about wanting to run the London Marathon one day. Says he wants to raise money for… penguins? Penguins! Bless him. He’s got a good heart. Though I do worry about him already setting such ambitious goals. He’s only twelve. Let him dream, dear. It's good for him. Being ambitious isn’t a bad thing. Though I must say, all this talk of marathons… reminds me of that trip we took to Iceland. Iceland? Oh, the glaciers! And the Blue Lagoon. That was a magical trip. And freezing! Remember how we had to wrap up in about five layers just to walk to the car? And the Northern Lights! That was truly breathtaking. Though Leo was more interested in finding a volcano. He was obsessed with volcanoes at that age. I think he still is, actually. He’s building a model one for his science project. It's…messy. Lots of paper mache and red paint. Sounds about right. He always did like getting his hands dirty. Remember that time he tried to recreate the eruption of Vesuvius in the kitchen? Don’t remind me! The bicarbonate of soda and vinegar everywhere…It took days to clean up. It’s good to have memories like this. Keeps us grounded. Speaking of which, is anyone up for going to the cinema later? They're showing that new historical drama. Ooh, yeah! That sounds good. Can I choose the snacks? As long as it doesn't involve a chocolate fountain, you can choose anything you like.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Mum. You’ve really outdone yourself. It tastes just like…well, like being about ten again. It  is  lovely, isn’t it? I always remember your mum making this when we came round after school. It was a treat. Though, I’m pretty sure she used to sneak a load of extra veg in, hoping we wouldn’t notice. Oh, I did. Gotta get those five-a-day in somehow, even if they  are  disguised in mashed potato. Your father refused to eat anything green, you know. Said it was ‘rabbit food’. Dad and his rabbit food. Honestly. He'd happily polish off a sausage roll, but a pea was the enemy. Speaking of things he wouldn’t eat…do you remember that time he tried black pudding in Whitby? Oh, goodness! How could I forget? He went absolutely puce. Said it tasted like rusty nails. He was moaning for a good hour. He  did  have a sensitive stomach, your father. Though he’d never admit it. Always thought showing any weakness was a terrible thing. Remember when he tried to fix the garden shed roof himself? And ended up needing a trip to A&E? Yes, vividly. He was so determined, though. “I can do it myself!” he’d say. Stubborn as a mule, that man. He was, wasn’t he? But underneath it all, a big softie. Oh, this reminds me - did I tell you I’ve started learning to crochet? Apparently, it’s very therapeutic. Crochet? That’s…unexpected! You always struck me as more of a speed-reading, multi-tasking kind of person. Well, I’m trying to slow down a little! My friend, Carol, does it, and she convinced me. I’ve made a rather wonky scarf so far. It looks…rustic. I used to knit. Years ago. Used to make cardigans for you girls. Though I haven't picked up the needles in ages. My eyesight isn't what it used to be. I do read, though. I’ve got one of those Kindle things. It's marvellous. They are brilliant, aren’t they? I’ve got a few eBooks, but I still prefer the feel of a real book. The smell, you know? Oh, absolutely. There’s nothing like curling up with a good book. Though, the convenience of an eBook is hard to beat, especially when travelling.

Lovely bit of bread this, isn’t it? Proper crusty. It is nice. From that little bakery down the road, wasn’t it? The one near the post office? That’s the one. Old Mrs. Higgins still makes a good loaf, despite her age. More than I can say for some youngsters, eh? All fancy sourdough and whatnot. Give me a white bloomer any day. Well, you like what you’re used to, don’t you? I do like a bit of granary myself. Bit more… substantial. Substantial? It’s just full of bits! Seeds and husks and who knows what else. Makes yer teeth feel like they’re scrubbing the floor. Oh, don’t be like that. It’s good for you. Fibre and all that. Doctor says… well,  used  to say, I should eat more fibre. Doctors always say that. They’d have us living on bran flakes and sprouts. Not much enjoyment in that, is there? No, I suppose not. Though a little sprout now and then doesn’t hurt. Want another cup of tea? I just made a fresh pot. Don’t mind if I do. Lovely. Though it’s gone a bit lukewarm, hasn’t it? Always happens. Should’ve put a cosy on it, I suppose. I did! It's right there… oh, you're right. It's slipped off. Silly me. Old age, creeping in, you know? Don’t talk like that. You’re not  old . Just… experienced. And slightly forgetful. Like me. That’s kind of you to say. Though I do forget things more than I used to. Where I put my glasses, what I went into the kitchen for… I went upstairs earlier to get my slippers, and completely forgot why I was going upstairs. Stood there for a good minute, just… blank. Happens to the best of us. It’s just… life, I suppose. Slowing down a bit. Slowing down? I feel like I’m grinding to a halt sometimes! Still, better than the alternative, eh? Definitely. So, did you hear from young David today? How was his driving lesson? He rang. Said it went alright, but the instructor kept shouting. Apparently, he nearly stalled in the middle of a roundabout. Oh dear. Roundabouts are tricky. So many things to think about. He says he’s getting the hang of it though. Wants to pass his test before his eighteenth birthday.

Honestly, the kids were  wild  today. Year twos are just… a different breed, aren’t they? One of them tried to convince me that a badger lives in the staff room. A badger, Chloe! Oh my god, seriously? That’s amazing. Mine were arguing over who gets to be the unicorn in their role play. It escalated. Full-on glitter and tears. Sounds about right. Kids and glitter - a dangerous combination. Speaking of dangerous, you will  not  believe the day I’ve had. My car decided it didn’t want to be a car anymore. Just… died on the A2. No way! You just got that car, didn't you? I did! Six months. Apparently, it's something to do with the fuel pump. The AA guy was lovely, but it’s just… typical, isn’t it? Right when I was actually, you know, trying to be a functioning adult. Oh, that's awful, Liv. So frustrating. Is it going to be expensive to fix? Potentially. He said it could be a couple of hundred, but honestly, who knows? Everything is expensive these days. It’s cheaper to fly to Spain than it is to get a car fixed here. You’re not wrong. Have you booked that holiday yet, by the way? You were talking about going to Portugal? I have! Finally. We're going to the Algarve in September. Just a week, but it’ll be nice to get some sun. I desperately need it after this week. What about you two? Any holiday plans? Not yet. We’re thinking maybe Cornwall? Somewhere fairly low-key. Just a bit of sea air and pasties. Ooh, Cornwall is lovely! We went last year. You have to try the Cornish ice cream. It’s a religious experience. I’ve heard! Okay, officially adding that to the itinerary. Speaking of itineraries, have you guys got any ideas for Sarah’s birthday present yet? It's next month. I’ve been racking my brain! She's so hard to buy for. She always says she doesn't want anything. She said she was thinking of doing a pottery class, maybe we could get her a voucher for that? Ooh, good shout! She’d love that. She's always going on about wanting to be more creative. Yeah, that's a brilliant idea. I'm in. What about Ben? Heard anything more from him?

Right, so Old Man Hemmings’ daughter’s finally moved out, eh? About time, she was drivin’ everyone mad with the music. Bass thumpin’ ‘til all hours. Aye, good riddance to her, honestly. Though you’d think he’d be delighted, finally havin’ the house to himself. He just seems… worse, somehow. More grumpy. Maybe he’s missin’ the noise? Sounds daft, doesn’t it? But some folk get used to a certain level of chaos. Is he the one who always complains about footballs in his garden? That’s him. Proper stickler. Says it’ll damage his prize-winning roses. Though, let’s be honest, they look a bit sad, those roses. You know, remember Mrs. O’Malley? She was sayin’ her grandson’s joined the army. Poor lad, goin’ off to… well, you know. It’s horrifying, what’s happenin’ over there with ISIS and everything. It’s terrifying. I saw something on Instagram, a news report… you can’t escape it, even online. Makes you feel helpless. It does. And it’s not just them, is it? The world feels… brittle, lately. Like anything could snap. I was talkin’ to Dieter – my brother, you know, in Germany – and he’s sayin’ they’re worried about things escalating there too. It’s a strange time. Can we talk about Harry Potter instead? I finished the fourth book last night! It was brilliant! Oh, lovely! Which bit was your favourite? When Hermione uses the time-turner! It’s so cool she can go back and do loads of lessons. I wish we had those at school! I was obsessed with that book when I first read it. Still am, a bit, if I'm honest. I’ve started re-reading the series. It’s just… comforting, you know? A bit of escapism. Aye, escapism’s good. Actually, speaking of escapism, I’m startin’ to think I need a new project. This house… it’s lovely, don’t get me wrong. But it needs  so  much work. The damp’s comin’ back in the cellar. Oh, not again! Thought you’d finally got that sorted. That damp’s a nightmare. Always smells like old pennies down there. It's a constant battle. And with the price of everything goin’ up, it’s getting harder and harder to afford the repairs. I been lookin’ at a couple of places over towards Aigburth, near the park.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork has increased tenfold with this new free school meals system. It's not just ticking a box anymore, is it? We have to know  everything  – every allergy, every dietary requirement, gluten-free, dairy-free… It’s a minefield. Oh, you’re telling me! Little Timmy can’t have anything green, apparently. Anything. Green. A perfectly good pea is off limits. Honestly, you’d think we were dealing with royalty, not seven-year-olds. It's the parents, isn’t it? Overprotective, some of them. Though, I suppose it’s better than the old days, when it was just a soggy biscuit and a glass of milk. Remember those? Just about. My mother used to talk about wartime food, of course. Nothing wasted, everything rationed. She used to make these… well, approximations of sausages. Mostly breadcrumbs and whatever scraps of meat she could get hold of. Goodness me. My mother-in-law, now  she  had a story. Escaped Siberia as a child, unbelievable journey all the way to Africa. Came here after the war, of course. Always said the food was the biggest shock – so much choice! She’d lived on practically nothing for years. Incredible. My grandmother practically lived on potatoes and carrots. She’d boast about making a meal out of nothing. I remember her making a sort of ‘mock apple pie’ with biscuits and spices… tasted nothing like apple but we all pretended it did! Oh, that’s clever! Speaking of food, have you been to the Farm Shop lately? They’ve got some lovely gluten-free bread now. Sarah – you know, with the allergies? - she’d be thrilled. I popped in yesterday. It's getting awfully expensive, though. The Village Shop is cheaper for basics, but the Farm Shop has such lovely produce. Though, honestly, I still prefer a proper butcher for my sausages. You just can’t beat a good pork sausage. You're right about the sausages. Though I’m trying to cut down on red meat… it’s all this talk of Iron Man, really. My daughter's training for it, you know. Oh, wow! That’s serious dedication. She's always been sporty, hasn't she? Always. Keeps me on my toes, just watching her. She's been cycling all over the place. Actually, the Tour of Britain is coming through our village next week. It’s going to be chaos!

Right, honestly, this week at work’s been a proper shambles. You wouldn't  believe  the drama. Oh god, lay it on me. I need a bit of a vent after today. Production’s been a nightmare – everything’s running behind, suppliers are late… the usual. Sounds stressful. Mine’s been…well, mine’s been beige. Just admin, admin, admin. Spreadsheet central. At least it’s not  actively  awful, you know? Beige sounds amazing right now. Mine’s been a delegate who decided mid-conference they’d booked the wrong one, demanding a full refund. Then another one who lost their luggage  and  their phone. And then, the icing on the cake, a speaker cancelled five minutes before they were due on stage. Five minutes! Oof. That’s…a lot. Did you manage to salvage it? Eventually, yeah. Found someone to fill in, but it involved a frantic search through the attendee list for anyone with vaguely relevant expertise. Turns out a marketing manager from a tech firm was a closet expert on sustainable energy. Who knew? That's lucky! Seriously. You’re a magician, you are. Not a magician, just stressed. It just makes you wonder, doesn't it? Like, people just don't  think  before they book things, or pack properly, or…anything. Tell me about it. It's like people assume everything just magically happens. They don't see all the behind-the-scenes stuff to make it work. I had someone complain  to my manager  that their reports weren't automatically being updated. Like, hello? I literally send you a spreadsheet template and instructions every month! It’s the entitlement, isn't it? Like everything’s just  owed  to them. Speaking of owed, I need to chase up Sarah about that money she borrowed for the weekend trip to Brighton. It's been… a while. Oh, good luck with that. Sarah’s legendary for “forgetting” to pay people back. Remember when she ‘forgot’ to chip in for the birthday meal last year? Oh no, don’t remind me! It took three months and a very pointed email to get that sorted. It's just…awkward, isn't it? Ruining a friendship over twenty quid? Exactly! But it’s the principle of the thing. I'm skint as it is. And I need to book train tickets for visiting my parents next month. You should just be straight with her.

Honestly, the council are just… unbelievable. Demolishing the library? It’s the heart of the community! I know, it’s a disgrace. They’re saying it's structurally unsound, but I heard Old Man Hemmings – you remember him, used to volunteer there? – saying it just needs some repairs. They want to build another block of flats, of course. Of  course  they do. That’s all they ever want to do. Right, I’ve started drafting a petition. I’ve got a basic outline on my laptop, but I’m really rubbish at the wording. It needs to sound… urgent, but not hysterical, you know? I’m happy to look it over. I’m fairly good at that sort of thing, being an administrator and all. Endless reports to proofread. Though honestly, sometimes I think the people  writing  the reports deliberately try to make them incomprehensible. Tell me about it. My transcription work is similar. People rambling, awful audio quality... it’s a nightmare. Anyway, petition first. I was thinking something about the library being a vital resource for education and community engagement… too cliché? Maybe. How about focusing on what  specifically  will be lost? The children’s story time, the access to computers for people without internet at home, the local history collection? Make it tangible. Good point, good point. I’ll add that. I was also thinking about getting flyers printed and putting them up in local shops. Definitely. And social media. Everyone’s on Facebook these days, even the pensioners. I can share it on the Plumstead Community Group. Gets a lot of traffic. Brilliant. You’re a lifesaver. Honestly, if we don’t fight this, what’s next? They’ll be closing the park, then the community centre… Don't even go there. It’s all part of their plan, isn’t it? Slowly eroding everything that makes Plumstead, Plumstead. Speaking of eroding things, I'm on late shifts all next week. Dreadful. Seven till three. Oh, no! That’s awful. You’ll be exhausted. I know. And I always get stuck with the enquiries about parking permits. People are so aggressive about those things. It’s like I personally denied them the right to park outside their house. People are awful. I heard Doreen's been trying to learn mnemonics to help her remember things. Apparently, her memory's not what it used to be. Doreen? Really?

…and then young Derek, bless ‘im, he comes round with those Jehovah’s Witnesses leaflets again. Honestly, you’d think after ten years he’d realise we’re not interested. Polite as pie, mind you, can’t fault him for that. Just persistent. They’re a dedicated bunch, alright. Remember old Mrs. Hedges, down the lane? She got right involved with them, years ago. Changed her completely. Stopped going to the Women’s Institute, wouldn’t have a gin and tonic at Christmas. Goodness me. That's a bit drastic, isn’t it? Though I suppose if it gives people comfort… Still, a gin and tonic at Christmas is a tradition! Speaking of which, are we still on for The Crown next Friday? I fancy a nice bit of fish and chips, and a glass of something bubbly. Sounds lovely, Mary. Though I’m still grumbling about the price of everything these days. Fifteen pound for fish and chips! Back in my day… Don’t start on that, Arthur. Everything’s gone up. Even the blooming tax. I swear, they just invent new ways to take our money. I still don’t understand half of it, even after all these years. They certainly do. It’s a nightmare. Though I’m glad they’re finally doing something about potholes. Did you see the state of the road going into Dereham? It’s like driving over the moon. Potholes are the least of our worries. Have you seen the parking situation at Cromer these days? Absolute chaos. Tried to take Millie and George last week, and spent half an hour driving around in circles, looking for a spot. In the end, we parked miles away and walked. That’s nothing new. Always been a nightmare at the coast, especially in summer. Used to be worse though, before they built that new car park near the pier. Still not enough, though, is it? And all those people just abandoning cars on double yellows. You get some right characters. Speaking of characters, did you hear about old Mr. Peterson and his pigeons? Oh, don’t get me started on Peterson! That man could talk to those birds for hours. Says they tell him things. He’s a bit…eccentric. Though harmless enough. He’s been feeding them in the square for years. It’s just a bit messy, all the droppings and feathers.

Honestly, the amount of logs we’ve got stacked up now is ridiculous. I thought we’d be burning through them faster with the weather being so… well, still quite chilly for June. We didn’t really use the log burner much in May, did we? Too mild. Good job you got a good deal on them, though. Though, stacking them was  your  penance for buying so many, remember? Don’t remind me. My back still hasn’t forgiven me. Mum, you were admiring the new upholstery on the chairs earlier, weren’t you? Did you think I’d done a good job? It’s lovely, dear. Really brightens up the room. Though I do still maintain a more traditional fabric would have suited the style of the house better. But that's just my opinion. It looks very comfortable, at least. Comfortable is the key, isn't it? Style follows function. Though I must say, I still prefer a good wingback chair. A proper wingback. They don’t  make  them like they used to. Dad, you say that about  everything . Remember when we were talking about the new Japanese restaurant in town? You said they didn’t make sushi like they used to in… well, I’m not even sure where you were imagining sushi was better! Honestly, the stories I’ve heard about travelling from Tokyo… the hustle and bustle. It’s not for me, not anymore. Give me a quiet evening by the fire any day. Speaking of which, are we having mashed potato tonight? I do enjoy your mashed potato, dear. Yes, Dad, mashed potato. And yes, Mum, I know you prefer a more muted colour scheme. It’s my house, though! Don’t be impertinent, darling. I was merely observing. Honestly, the price of potatoes these days! Have you seen the budget? It’s scandalous. How are young families supposed to manage? It's frightening. Everything's going up. I was talking to Sarah at work – they're seriously considering outsourcing more of our admin to India just to cut costs. Apparently, it's cheaper to have someone doing the work halfway around the world. That’s awful. Where does that leave everyone here? The quality of work will suffer too, surely. They’re turning everything into academies now, aren’t they? It’s all about efficiency and cutting corners. Mrs. Henderson next door was saying… Oh, Mrs. Henderson!

Honestly, the council tax this year… it’s gone up again. I swear, they just pluck figures out of thin air. Do you two feel the same? Oh, you’re telling me. Mine’s crept up too. Thought being on a fixed pension would offer  some  protection, but no. It’s all going up, isn’t it? Everything. It’s criminal, absolutely criminal. They say it’s for services, but what services? The roads are full of potholes, the bins get collected when they feel like it… and don't even get me started on the state of the library. They’re building that new estate out by Old Catton, aren’t they? That’ll be more demand on everything. More people, more taxes, but will anything actually  improve ? I doubt it. Remember when they promised that new roundabout would solve the congestion on the A47? Still a nightmare. Roundabouts. Don't talk to me about roundabouts! Tried to drive to Cromer last week, Sat Nav sent me round three of ‘em, going backwards half the time. Thing’s got a mind of its own, that Sat Nav. Nearly ended up in a field! Oh, technology. I tried to record something the other day on the telly, a documentary about remote Scottish islands, fascinating place. Spent half an hour trying to figure out the new remote, ended up missing the whole thing. Honestly, it's designed to confuse us. Remote places… that's a thought. I was reading about someone who bought a cottage in the Outer Hebrides. No phone signal, no internet, just… peace and quiet. Seems appealing, doesn’t it? After all the fuss and bustle. Sounds a bit too isolated for my liking. I’d go stir-crazy. I need my telly, and a shop within reasonable distance for a paper. Though, I did see a nice little bungalow for sale in Attleborough.
