Not exactly the Hebrides, but… Attleborough? Oh, it's nice enough, but a bit… bland. They’re building houses everywhere around there though. It's losing it’s character. Remember when it was just a little market town? That’s the problem with progress, isn’t it? Everything changes. Still, a new house might be nice. Lower energy bills, less maintenance. This old place is starting to feel its age, and so am I, come to that. Though, the garden's lovely in the summer.

Right, so the motherboard's definitely gone. Completely fried. I’ve tested everything else, power supply’s good, RAM’s good, even tried a different graphics card just to be sure. Nothing. So you can't fix it? Is it proper broken broken? Absolutely proper broken. It’s beyond repair, lad. We’re talking replacement. Oh dear. That’s not good. Was it still under warranty? That’s the frustrating part. It  was , but it expired last month. One month! I swear, these warranties are designed to run out the second something goes wrong. So we have to  buy  a new one? A whole new computer? Not necessarily a whole new computer. We can just replace the motherboard. But they’re not cheap, especially a decent one. I’ll have a look tonight, see what's available. Sauce! Fajita sauce! Alright, darling, just a minute. We're talking about computers. Honestly, you'd think he could sense we were discussing something expensive. He's a smart one, that one. He understands more than we give him credit for. Speaking of, did you confirm with Liam’s Dad about the rugby on Saturday? Yes, everything's sorted. Pick up at nine, drop off after training. He's really excited. Apparently, they're practicing tackling this week. Cool. I’m hoping I get to play scrum-half. Mrs. O’Malley says I’m quick enough. You are a quick lad, alright. Now, back to this computer… I really should have renewed that warranty. I was putting it off, thinking it was a waste of money. Famous last words. Well, you couldn’t have known. And honestly, you’ve spent hours trying to fix it. You’re a wizard with these things. I appreciate that. It's just annoying. Okay, after I look at motherboards tonight, maybe we could all go swimming? I think we all need a good swim. Yeah! Swimming would be great! Can I take my goggles? Of course, you can. That sounds lovely. Though, I might just stay here with… this little sauce monster. Someone's clearly lobbying for more fajitas. More sauce! Sticky ears! What did he say about his ears? He keeps poking them and saying they’re "sticky out ears.” It’s adorable, but slightly worrying. All the better to hear you with, my boy. Right, let’s finish dinner then. I’ll tackle the motherboard research later.

Right, pizza’s almost ready! Who wants extra pepperoni? Me! Me! Lots and lots! Like, a whole pizza of pepperoni! No fair! I want pepperoni too! But not  all  of it. Just… six pieces. Six pieces, okay. We’ll see. Now, remember what we talked about? No shouting, okay? We use our inside voices. It’s much nicer to listen to inside voices. But if I shout, you  hear  me better! That's not always true, sweetheart. Sometimes, shouting just makes it hard to understand what you’re saying. It’s like when you’re trying to tell me about your amazing handstand, but you’re tumbling around yelling at the same time. I miss the important bits! I did a handstand for  ten  seconds today! Wow! Ten seconds is fantastic! That’s a really long time. You’re getting so strong. Did you tell your teacher about that? No. She was busy talking about…about… Nessie! Nessie? The Loch Ness Monster? What about her? Nessie! Is she real? Does she eat pizza? That's a good question! Some people think she’s real, some people don't. It’s a big mystery. And I highly doubt she eats pepperoni pizza – probably more fish, I imagine. It wouldn't be very polite to throw pizza in the loch, would it? No! It would pollute the water! Exactly! Good thinking. Right. Pizza’s ready. Now, are you both excited for Lily’s birthday party on Saturday? Have you decided what you’re wearing? I want to wear my sparkly dress! The one with the unicorns! But I want to wear my superhero cape! Hmm… well, perhaps we can think about that later. We need to talk about being good guests, okay? Using our manners, saying thank you… and not shouting over everyone when Lily's opening her presents. Remember? Inside voices. Inside voices… and lots of cake? And lots of cake! Now, who can tell me – if I have three slices of pizza, and you have two, how many slices do we have altogether? Five! Fantastic! You’re brilliant. Okay, pizza time! And after, we can start planning that fairy garden we talked about. We can use all the pretty stones we collected last weekend. Ooh! And we can make a little pizza for the fairies! With one pepperoni! One pepperoni for the fairies. Perfect. Now, dig in! This IS good pizza!

Honestly, this Peka is incredible. I’ve never tasted anything quite like it. It's just… falling apart. Isn’t it lovely? It's proper slow cooking, isn’t it? They bury it in embers for hours. You won't get that in Bolton, love. Though, mind you, Mrs. Higginbottom did make a pretty decent slow-cooked beef when I was on the ward… she always said the secret was a splash of Worcestershire sauce. Worcestershire sauce? Sounds grim. This is much better. Can I have another potato? Grim? It's a classic! Though, I must say, the potatoes  are  rather good. Not the waxy kind, are they? More of a… floury, Maris Piper sort. Definitely floury. You can tell they’ve been grown properly. This whole region is just… beautiful. Rovinj was lovely, wasn't it? Though  packed  with tourists. Rovinj was gorgeous, but yes, a bit of a scrum. Pula was better, more spacious. I preferred the Roman amphitheatre to anything back home, even though I've delivered hundreds of babies in the maternity unit at the Royal Bolton… you’d think I’d be used to grand structures! Mum! You always bring it back to babies. Well, someone's got to! And it's a fascinating world, you know. Though these Croatian doctors… apparently, they're very keen on natural births. Very different approach than some of the London hospitals, I heard from a colleague who visited. It's amazing how much healthcare varies. The wife and I were talking about it on the flight – the level of scrutiny you get from immigration officers these days is just… intense. They grilled me about my consultancy work for twenty minutes! Oh, tell me about it. They gave me the side-eye because I was a student and travelling alone. Like I was planning a marijuana farm or something. Which, admittedly, would be pretty lucrative here, considering… Marijuana farm?! Olivia! Don’t fill his head with nonsense. Honestly. I’m just saying! It's legal-ish here. I read an article about it... anyway. Where were we? Oh, the food. It just reminds me, Ben, your food tech class. Are you still making those weird edible spheres? They're not weird! It’s molecular gastronomy! Mr. Davies says I’m a natural. He said I could be the next Heston Blumenthal. Heston Blumenthal… now  there's  an innovator. Similar vein to Steve Jobs, really.

Right then, finished that up, didn’t we? Good bit of ham, that was. Though I say, this new bread… a bit dry, isn’t it? Not like what Mrs. Higgins used to bake down the lane. Oh, you always say that, Arthur! It’s perfectly good bread. You're just stuck in the past, you are. Still, it’s nice to have everyone together again for lunch, isn't it? Indeed. It's a rare treat these days. Though young David did mention something about debt collectors knocking on doors in his street… Apparently, a rather aggressive lot. Oh, don’t get me started on those. They’re the scourge of the earth. PPI claims, mostly. Preying on people who barely understand what they’re signing up for. I was reading an article about it in  The Week  – absolutely scandalous. PPI? Fancy that. Always thought it was something for fancy city folk. Never bothered me none. Though I did get a letter once, said I was owed a few quid. Filled it in, never heard a thing back. They’re very good at taking, aren't they? And not so good at giving back. Speaking of taking… are we still planning on having that little party next month, for Emily’s birthday? Yes, we booked the hall down by the church, remember? Small one, but perfectly adequate. I’m thinking maybe a bit of a sing-song afterwards? Emily always loved a good croon. A sing-song in the church hall? Bit ambitious, isn’t it? Though I suppose as long as we don't disturb the Abbey… They’re quite sensitive about noise over there. Remember old Mr. Peterson complaining about the carol singers? Oh, I remember that! He was a right grumpy old thing. Always moaning about something. But I used to enjoy singing in the choir, back in the day. Though my voice isn’t what it used to be… sounds more like a rusty gate these days. Don't be silly, Arthur. You still have a lovely voice. Although perhaps we should leave the solos to Emily. She’s the talented one. Absolutely. Speaking of talents, have you started your seeds yet, Arthur? I know you were talking about growing tomatoes this year. Not yet, no. Been meaning to, but then I got distracted trying to figure out this computer. That David gave me. It's a devilish machine, I tell you.

Right, another day done. Honestly, the stories you hear… Tell me about it, dear. You get used to it, but it never stops being… sobering. Though today was mostly benefit fraud, thankfully. Less drama than the shoplifting cases. Benefit fraud is… frustrating, isn’t it? Especially when you hear the justifications. I had one woman today, claiming hardship, but she was talking about a holiday to Tenerife next month. Oh, the cheek of it! You wouldn’t believe some of the excuses people come up with. Though, I suppose everyone's got a story, haven't they? Doesn’t make it right, though. It's just… difficult sometimes, seeing people in such difficult situations. And then others just taking the mickey. Absolutely. It's a real mixed bag. Makes you think about the whole justice system, really. Is it fair? Is it effective? Do people actually  learn  from it? A question for the ages, that is. I’ve been doing this nearly ten years now, and I still don't know the answer. Seems to me like it’s more about ticking boxes than actually rehabilitating anyone. They go round and round, don't they? They do. And the funding cuts… it’s impacting everything. Schools, the NHS, the courts… it all feels a bit precarious. Precarious is a good word for it. My grandson, little Jamie, he's trying to get extra tutoring for his GCSEs, but it's just so expensive. Everything is so expensive these days, isn't it? Used to be able to put a bit aside, now… it all goes on bills. It’s awful, isn’t it? I’m a language teacher, and even  I’m  struggling. Private tuition is booming, but it’s mostly for kids whose parents can afford it. Creates such a disparity. It does. It really does. Makes you wonder what the world’s coming to. Speaking of coming to… did you see the weather forecast? More rain. It’s like Scotland here, honestly! I did! Honestly, it's relentless. I was hoping to get a weekend trip to the coast, but I think that's out the window. Perhaps a train trip somewhere instead? Though the train fares are… well, you know. Don't even start me on the trains! Daylight robbery, that's what it is. I went up to see my sister in Aberdeen last month, and it cost me a fortune.

Right, so we were talking about what makes people happy, weren’t we? What makes  you  happy, Lily? Um… ponies! And chocolate! And… and when you read me stories! Lovely! Those are all brilliant things. And what about you, Leo? What makes  you  feel happy? Dinosaurs! Roar! And building really tall towers. And… and when I beat you at Connect Four! Oh, you  do  love beating me at Connect Four, don’t you? It’s good to have things that make you smile. It doesn’t always need to be something big or expensive, does it? Does it mean you need lots of money to be happy? That’s a really good question, Lily. Not at all, sweetie. Not at all. Lots of people  think  money will make them happy, but it doesn’t always work like that. If I had lots of money, I’d buy a  massive  dinosaur! A really, really BIG one! You would, wouldn’t you? But even if you didn’t have lots of money, you could still imagine a massive dinosaur, couldn’t you? You could draw one, or build one out of blocks… And I could pretend to ride a pony! Even if it’s just a pretend pony! Exactly! See? It's about using your imagination and enjoying the little things. Like sunshine, or having a cuddle, or… hmm… can you think of a rhyme for 'happy'? Snappy! Like a crocodile! That’s a good start! But maybe something that  sounds  a bit more like 'happy'? Pappy! Like… Grandpa! Clever girl! Pappy rhymes with happy. And you know what makes  me  happy? Seeing you two having fun and being kind to each other. That makes me the happiest person in the world. I like being kind! I shared my stickers with Lily today. And I let Leo have a turn with the red car! See? That’s wonderful. That’s  much  more important than having lots of money or lots of toys. That’s what true happiness is all about. Can we build a tower now? A really, really tall one? Yes! And then we can pretend it's a castle for the pony and the dinosaur! Sounds like a fantastic plan! Let’s go build the tallest tower Comberton has ever seen! Right, what did you say rhymes with happy? Pappy! That’s right, pappy! Now, what rhymes with blue? Shoe! Perfect!

Seriously though, have you thought about what you’re doing after sixth form? Like,  really  thought about it? Everyone else seems to have a five-year plan already. Five-year plan? Mate, I’m struggling to plan what I’m having for dinner tonight. Uni’s the vague idea, yeah, but beyond that… nothing. What about you, Mr. Future CEO? I’m thinking of trying to patent something. Seriously. I had this idea for a self-cleaning dog bowl. Like, automatic scraper and water filter. People would buy it. Dogs are messy. A self-cleaning dog bowl? That’s… niche. But actually, not terrible. You'd need loads of funding though, right? Patents aren’t cheap. Exactly! And that's where it gets tricky. I was reading about this guy who invented a better mousetrap, patented it, but then couldn’t afford to  market  it. Sat on the invention for years. Harsh. That’s rubbish. So, what, you’d need investors? Like… Dragons’ Den stuff? Possibly. Or maybe crowdfunding. But then you have to give away equity, and what if it’s a massive success? You want to keep the bulk of the profit. I’ve been looking into investment, actually. Trying to understand it. Investment? You’re going deep, aren’t you? I barely understand my pocket money, let alone shares and stocks. It’s not  that  hard. It’s all about risk, and potential return. Like, China's growing so fast, right? Investing in Chinese tech companies now could be huge in ten years. China, eh? My dad said something about that. Said they’re basically taking over the world. Everything’s made in China. Not taking over, but definitely becoming a superpower. And that means economic opportunities. You could, like, put a little bit of money into a tech fund, and just… watch it grow. It's like planting a seed. Sounds… boring. I’d rather just spend the money on a new graphics card for my computer. That’s a valid use of funds. But think bigger! This is about future financial security. Becoming independent. Not having to work nine-to-five for someone else. Okay, okay, you’ve convinced me to… think about it. But I'm not promising anything. My priorities are currently beating level seven on  Elden Ring . And then maybe finally finishing that history coursework. Fair enough. But seriously, keep it in the back of your mind.

Honestly, I think my thighs are burning already, and we’ve barely done two runs. I’m officially unfit. Don’t be silly, you're fine! It’s just the altitude, and it’s been ages since we’ve skied. Remember that time in Austria, after Mum and Dad’s anniversary? We hadn't skied for, what, five years? Vaguely. Mostly I remember Dad complaining about his knees the entire time. And you being brilliant, naturally. You always picked it up so much faster than me. Well, I did a season once, you know? It’s completely different when you’re  living  it. Anyway, are you sure you’ve got enough layers on? You were shivering at the top of the lift. I think so. Base layer, fleece, waterproof… it’s just a cold kind of cold, isn’t it? Like it seeps into your bones. Right, are you still up for trying that red run off the Platto peak this afternoon? Ooh, the one everyone’s been talking about? The view from up there is supposed to be incredible. But…are you sure? We can always stick to blues if you prefer. No shame in it! No, I want to try it. I feel like I need a challenge. Though, if I end up faceplanting into a snowdrift, you’re not allowed to laugh. Oh, I make no promises. I’ll film it, at least. For posterity. You are awful. Speaking of awful, have you heard from Sarah and Mark? They were meant to be meeting us for lunch. I texted Mark earlier, he said they were still getting sorted. Apparently, little Leo decided to have a meltdown because his ski boots felt ‘funny’. You know Leo. Oh, bless him. Sounds like a typical toddler ski trip experience. It’s amazing they even attempted it. Do you think they'll manage a full day on the slopes? Hmm, I’m not sure. They might end up just pottering around the beginner area. But hey, at least they’re giving it a go. It’s good to see them, isn’t it? It feels like ages since we all last properly hung out. It does. Life just gets in the way, doesn’t it? Work, kids… it’s hard to carve out time. Maybe we should try and do this more often. A yearly ski trip? I’d love that. Maybe next year we can convince Mum and Dad to come along?

Honestly, Roger, you're wobbling. Just… hold still. I’m trying for a nice even trim, not a Picasso. It’s just… the thought of you wielding those scissors so close to my ear. Remember what happened with Brenda’s fringe? That was  one  time! And she requested a dramatic side-swept look. Besides, this is much more practical. Speaking of practical, have you thought any more about the stringing method? The cable ties are a bit… clunky, aren’t they? They work, though! And they’re cheap. We’re talking pence per racket, Margaret. Less than a packet of biscuits. The whole point is affordability, remember? We’re aiming for the ‘repair, don’t replace’ market. I know, I know. But aesthetically… it doesn’t scream ‘professional’. I was thinking maybe a braided nylon cord? Something thinner, more streamlined. And we could offer different colours. Braided nylon... that’ll add to the cost, won't it? We need to keep the material cost down. What about the gauge? Too thin, and it’ll snap. Too thick, and we're back to cable ties territory. Dimensions are crucial. And the weight… a heavier string adds to the strain on the frame. Right, weight. Good point. We need to do some testing. I’ve got that old battered racket of Thomas’s – the one with the cracked frame. We can experiment on that. Excellent. And we need to figure out the pricing. I was thinking £5 for a basic restring, £8 if they want a colour change. That sounds reasonable. But how do we market this? “The Racket Rescue Service”? It sounds a bit… desperate. Hmm. Maybe something like “StringThings”? Catchy, memorable. It implies we’re all about the strings. StringThings… it’s… okay. A bit twee, perhaps. We could pitch it on Dragons’ Den! Imagine! Peter Jones asking about our projections… Oh, please. They’d tear us apart. “A niche market with minimal scalability!” I can hear Deborah Meaden already. Well, it's something to aspire to. Though, speaking of aspiring... I think I just… oh dear. What is it? What have you done?! I… I think I’ve snipped a little bit off your earlobe. WHAT?! Margaret! You've actually  cut  my ear! It stings! It’s tiny! Honestly, it’s barely noticeable. And look, it’s created this… interesting stripe in your hair. It’s… avant-garde.

Lovely cuppa, isn't it, love? Always makes things better. Even a gloomy Tuesday. It is, Arthur. Just what I needed. Though I still think you put too much milk in mine. Just a wee bit. Now, now, Elsie. Been doing it this way for sixty years, haven't I? You'd think you'd be used to it by now. It’s good tea, Grandpa. Though I do take mine plain, if you don’t mind. I’m trying to cut back on the dairy. Yeah, good stuff. So, you were telling me about that exhibition you went to in Cambridge, Sarah? Contemporary art, was it? Yes, at the Kettle’s Yard. It was… interesting. A lot of installation work. Lots of found objects. One piece was literally just a pile of bricks. A pile of bricks? They call  that  art these days? Back in my day, art was proper pictures. Landscapes, portraits, you could  recognise  something. Oh, Arthur, you and your landscapes. Reminds me of old Mr. Peterson down the lane, always painting sunsets. Very nice they were, truthfully. But a pile of bricks… that  is  a bit much, isn’t it? It’s meant to be about deconstruction, challenging perceptions, the inherent beauty in the mundane… all that sort of thing. The artist’s statement was quite lengthy. Oh, the artist’s statement. Always the clever bit, isn't it? Often more impressive than the artwork itself. Sounds like a lot of hot air to me. I remember when art was about skill. Look at Turner, now  he  could paint. The way he captured the light… masterful. You couldn’t just throw a few bricks together and call it a masterpiece. But isn’t ‘skill’ subjective, Grandpa? What one generation considers skillful, another might dismiss as…conventional. It’s about pushing boundaries, isn’t it? She’s got a point, Arthur. It’s about context, too. What's considered art changes over time. Think about the Impressionists, they were ridiculed when they first started showing their work. True enough. Though I still think a nice watercolour of some flowers is perfectly acceptable art. Doesn't need to be a pile of bricks, does it? I just don't get it. It all feels a bit…pretentious to me. Give me Constable any day. Now  there  was a man who knew how to paint a field. I think it's good to be open to different things, though.

Honestly, Chloe was  so  passive aggressive at yoga today. Like, genuinely. I said I was trying a new studio next week and she just went… “Oh, that’s…nice.” With the biggest emphasis on the ‘nice’ like it was a coded insult. Ugh, Chloe. She's a professional subtle digger, isn’t she? I swear she practices in front of a mirror. How are you still friends with her? I don’t know! We’ve known each other since school. It's just… comfortable? But comfortable and infuriating are apparently very close beds fellows. I need to seriously reassess. On a scale of one to ten, how much do you think I should ghost her after that? Oh, dramatic. Ghosting's a bit harsh, maybe? Though, honestly, a temporary social media mute might be a good starting point. Speaking of infuriating people, old Mrs. Henderson tried to tell me  how  to administer medication today. Like, after years of training,  she  knows better. Oh my god, the nerve! People are so… presumptuous. It’s like they think watching a bit of “24 Hours in A&E” qualifies them to be medical professionals. Exactly! I just smiled sweetly and said, “That’s a really interesting perspective, Mrs. Henderson, but I’ll stick to the protocols, thanks.” It's exhausting, though, constantly having to explain yourself to people. I’m knackered. You deserve a medal, seriously. I’ve just been battling spreadsheets all week. They’ve decided we need a completely new project management system and I'm the designated person to learn it and then teach everyone else. It’s a nightmare. Oh, don’t even. New systems are the bane of my existence too. It’s always "Oh, it’ll be  so  efficient!" And then it’s just more work and endless glitches. Precisely. And the language they use in the training manuals! It’s like they’re deliberately trying to confuse you. “Leveraging synergistic opportunities through dynamic cross-functional collaboration…” What does that even  mean ?! Oh god, corporate speak. It's a virus. Remember that team meeting last month where Brian kept saying ‘circle back’ like it was a revolutionary concept? Oh god, yes! I nearly lost it. Right, I'm officially procrastinating on this training now. I was supposed to have finished the first module an hour ago. Join the club. I was supposed to write up my reflective practice report. It's just… staring into the abyss of paperwork.

Honestly, the day just disappears. Emails, diary management, answering the phone every five minutes… it’s relentless. And then Sarah wants a full briefing on everything,  everything , before she makes a decision. It’s exhausting. Sounds it. Still, at least it's a job. Remember when you were convinced you'd be a journalist? That seemed… less stressful, somehow. Oh, don't even. The reality of journalism is probably a lot more frantic than being a PA. At least I’m well-fed as a PA. And I’m still writing, just… memos and reports, not hard-hitting investigative pieces. You could always start a blog. Get back into it. Maybe. Or maybe I’ll just sink into the sofa with another glass of wine. You know, compensate. Speaking of which, have you had a cigarette today? Not yet. Trying, really trying. It’s just… after work, with a coffee? It feels like a ritual. I get it. We're both creatures of habit. Bad habits, admittedly. I’m aiming for one bottle of wine a week, but it’s looking shaky. One bottle? That’s ambitious. I think I’d need a detailed spreadsheet to track that. You always were the organised one. Which begs the question... is it intelligence or common sense that gets you through life? Oh, that’s a good one. I think it's more common sense. All the degrees in the world don’t help you when you have to deal with a crisis at work or a flooded bathroom. Exactly! I meet people in IT with incredible technical brains, but they can’t, for the life of them, figure out how to book a train ticket or understand why their neighbour is upset. It’s true. And it’s fascinating watching different cultures navigate things. My friend Priya was telling me about how her mother handles family dramas. It’s so different from how British women do it. Less direct, more… strategic. Strategic. I like that. British women tend to passive-aggressively simmer for a week before unleashing hell. Precisely! And there’s the whole feminist debate wrapped up in that, isn’t there? The expectations of how we  should  behave, the pressure to be polite, even when we’re furious. It’s exhausting being a woman sometimes, isn’t it? Just constantly calibrating. And then being judged no matter what you do. Too loud, too quiet, too ambitious, not ambitious enough… You’re telling me.

Right, so, farm day. Overall, a success? Or a chaotic mess? Be honest. It was good! The piglets were really fluffy. But Leo kept trying to  feed  them his biscuit. I wanted to feed them! They looked hungry. They have special food, sweethearts. You can’t just give them your biscuit. It’s not good for them. Did you both enjoy the tractor ride? The tractor ride was the best bit! It was bumpy! And I waved at all the cows. I liked the chickens. They were chasing each other. And one pecked my wellington. Oh dear! Not nice. Did you tell the farmer? No. It didn’t hurt. Just surprised me. Good. Now, how was school today? Isla, you first. Anything interesting happen? Mrs. Davison said I was a super star at painting. I painted a rainbow with glitter! Oh, wonderful! I’m sure it was beautiful. Leo? How about you? Um… I got a yellow card. A yellow card? What happened? I was building a massive tower with the blocks, and Jamie knocked it down. And I told him he was being silly. And then I shouted. You shouted? A little bit. Shouting isn’t very kind, Leo. Remember what we talked about? Using your words? I know. But he  wrecked  my tower! It took ages! I understand you were frustrated, but shouting doesn’t solve the problem. You could have told a teacher, or asked him to help you rebuild it. Yeah, you could've told Miss Evans! She always helps. Okay. Good. Now, before I start making dinner, anyone fancy picking a DVD for tonight? We have that new animal one, or we could re-watch 'Paddington'. Paddington! Please! No, the animals! With the lions and the zebras! Hmm. We'll have to compromise. Maybe we can watch Paddington  tomorrow  if you’re both good at bedtime? Okay. But can we have popcorn with the animal one? Absolutely. But not too much, okay? Remember what happened last time… You cleaned it all up! I did indeed. Right, farm talk over, school talk over, DVD sorted… time to make some dinner! Anyone want to help me chop vegetables? Maybe… just the soft ones? Isla, perhaps? Does this meet your requirements? Let me know if you would like any adjustments! . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . Right, so, farm day. Overall, a success? Or a chaotic mess? Be honest. It was good! The piglets were really fluffy.

Right, so I was thinking, Easter’s… looming, isn’t it? And I haven't even  thought  about eggs. Like, actual chocolate eggs. You’re a bit late to the party, love. Sainsbury’s had an Easter aisle the size of a small flat two weeks ago. No way! I’ve been buried in this funding application. Honestly, it's worse than writing a dissertation. All the justification... blah. Still, I think I’ll just get a little selection box. Not bothering with the hunt this year. Too much effort. Sensible. I’m more bothered about what to do with all the mini eggs people will inevitably give us. I swear, we’re drowning in them by Monday. Strategic deployment. Offer them to anyone who admires the… abstract art you’ve been making. Oh, you’ve seen that monstrosity? It’s… an exploration of the human condition through acrylic and questionable colour choices. Honestly, I think even Tracey Emin would raise an eyebrow. It’s… bold. Reminds me a bit of that Jackson Pollock stuff, but with more glitter. Speaking of things people make, I’m actually starting to get into knitting. Knitting? Seriously? You? I thought your crafting skills peaked at ‘basic origami swan’. Hey! That swan was a masterpiece. But yeah, knitting. My grandma sent me a whole load of wool and needles, and a YouTube tutorial link. It’s surprisingly relaxing. It's a scarf at the moment, a very wonky scarf. That's… wholesome. Very Cambridge. You’ll be joining a yarn bombing collective next. Don’t tempt me. Though, imagine if we yarn-bombed the Cavendish Laboratory. A giant, brightly coloured wool DNA helix. They’d have a fit. Actually, speaking of things happening around here… did you see they’re having those Olympic trials thing at the University Parks next month? Track and field? Oh, really? That's good. I might pop down and have a look. It’s inspiring seeing people actually  doing  sport, you know? I’ve been a bit of a couch potato since… well, since forever. I know the feeling. I’ve been trying to run, but I think my legs have forgotten what running  is . I'm pretty sure I saw Claudia Schiffer at the supermarket yesterday though. Claudia Schiffer?! No way! In Cambridge? What was she doing? Stocking up on organic kale? I don't know! I tried to be cool and not stare, but she was definitely her.

Right, well that was… a lot. My feet are killin’ me, honestly. Tell me about it. I thought my knees were going to give way about five times on that bus journey back. Honestly, the 24 is a  nightmare  on a Sunday. Packed like sardines. Sardines have more room, I’d wager. I’m tellin’ ya, they need to put more buses on. All that money they’re makin’ from the congestion charge… you’d think they could afford it. You'd think so, wouldn’t you? Still, we got there and back. And the British Museum  was  impressive, I’ll give it that. Oh, it was lovely. Though, all those glass cases… you can’t really  see  things properly, can you? All that glare. I much prefer museums where you can get up close. True. But you can’t exactly wander around touching ancient Egyptian artefacts, can you? They’d have a fit. Still, the Rosetta Stone… that was something. I spent ages trying to decipher it. So did I! Though, I suspect I didn’t get much further than ‘bird’ and ‘sun’. Honestly, they need to have a little translation guide beside it for people like me. They probably do. You just didn’t see it. You were too busy dodging school children and tourists with selfie sticks. Fair enough. It was busy, wasn’t it? And then that IMAX cinema… Honestly, that was a mistake. What? You didn't like it? I thought the visuals were stunning. All those underwater scenes. Oh, the visuals were alright, I suppose. But that 3D… gave me a headache. A proper, proper headache. I felt like everything was wobbling. Oh. I didn't notice that. I quite liked the 3D effect. Made it more immersive, I thought. Immersive headache, more like! I kept wanting to take the glasses off, but I didn't want to look like the only one. You could have. No one would have minded. Oh, I couldn’t have. I'm too polite for that! Besides, I’d already paid for the ticket. Waste of money, that was. We should've just gone to a normal cinema. Well, we can’t all get what we want, can we? It was your idea to go to the IMAX in the first place! You said you wanted the “full cinematic experience”. I said no such thing! I said I was open to suggestions.

Right, Christmas dinner. Operation Festive Feast needs a plan. Are we still doing it at my place? The flat’s… cosy, let's say. Cosy is a polite way of putting it, mate. It'll be like sardines in a tin. But yeah, yours makes sense. My apartment is smaller, and frankly, your kitchen is a bit more… equipped for a proper roast. Equipped is another polite word. It has a functional oven. So, who are we thinking? Definite yeses? Definitely Anna and Ben. They’re already buzzing about it. Said they’ve been practicing their Christmas jumper game. Then there’s Liam, probably. He’s always a maybe until the last minute, depends on whether he’s got a particularly compelling board game night scheduled. Liam. Always a wild card. And what about Sarah and Mark? They were saying something about possibly going back to the UK for Christmas, weren't they? That’s the rumour, yeah. Sarah sent me a slightly cryptic message about “family obligations”. Which, knowing Sarah, probably means her mum is trying to guilt-trip her into spending Christmas with her sixth husband. Sounds about right. Okay, so tentatively eight, potentially six if Sarah and Mark bail. We need a menu, then. Last year’s goose was…ambitious. Ambitious is an understatement. Remember how long it took to cook? And the grease! I think I’m still finding goose fat in the corners of my flat. Let’s go turkey. Classic, reliable, less likely to set off the smoke alarm. Good call. Turkey it is. And what about starters? I was thinking maybe a nice soup? Something fairly straightforward. Soup’s good. You make a brilliant butternut squash soup. Though, knowing our friends, half of them will just fill up on bread rolls and canapés before the main course even arrives. True. They're remarkably efficient at pre-dinner snacking. Speaking of efficient… have you seen “Elf” yet? I finally caved and watched it. "Elf"? Seriously? You’ve never seen “Elf”? It's a Christmas staple! I know, I know! I've been deliberately avoiding it for years. It seemed… overly saccharine. But it was actually brilliant! Will Ferrell is a genius. Honestly, I was laughing so hard I nearly choked on my noodles. See! Told you. It’s the perfect antidote to the cynicism of December. We  have  to watch it on Christmas Eve. It's the law.

Honestly, Twitter is a cesspit. I’ve just been scrolling and it’s just… relentless negativity. People genuinely get off on being awful. Tell me about it. I had someone leave a one-star review for the bakery today because the sourdough was ‘too tangy’.  Too  tangy. Like, that’s literally the point of sourdough! Oh, don't even get me started on reviews. I got one this week saying my avocado on toast was ‘an insult to avocados’. An  insult ! What does that even mean? People think they're food critics now because they have a phone. It’s the anonymity, isn't it? They wouldn’t say that to your face, would they? They hide behind a keyboard and just unleash. Exactly! And it's always the most ridiculous things. I had someone complain the croissants weren’t flaky  enough . Flaky enough! They’re, like, eighty layers of butter and pastry. What more do they want? You just have to ignore them, right? I try to. But it still stings. Especially when you’ve poured your heart and soul into something. This one guy actually said my café "lacked ambition." Lacked ambition! I’m running a small business practically on my own, mate. Proper cheek. Speaking of ambition, are you still thinking about that Margate place, then? The little art gallery/cafe hybrid? Yeah, still noodling on it. Found a potential space, a tiny shop front just off the old town. It needs a  lot  of work, though. Seriously, the interior is… questionable. Like, floral wallpaper questionable. Ooh, Margate is cool though, isn't it? It's had a real resurgence. You could do really well there. Design-wise, you've got a good eye. Thanks. That’s the thing, I’ve got all these ideas, but then the practicalities hit. Like, permits, refitting, and the sheer volume of cleaning required. It's daunting. It always is. But you’d be brilliant at it. You just need a good designer to tackle that floral wallpaper situation. It sounds tragic. I could do a mood board! I've been playing with some colour palettes for some new cake designs and they might work for a café. Think muted tones, lots of natural textures… That would be amazing, actually. Seriously. You’re a lifesaver. I keep getting bogged down in logistics and forgetting the fun part – making it  look  good. Speaking of fun, I'm officially logging off for the night.

Honestly, Oisin, you’ve barely touched your peas. They’re lovely peas, honestly. Fresh from the garden. They’re green and…round. I don’t  like  round. Everything’s round, Lily. The table’s round-ish. Your plate’s round. No, it’s not! It’s…mostly square. It’s a bit of both, sweetie. Just try one pea. For Grandma. No! Peas are yucky. Can I have more raspberries instead? We’ll have raspberries for pudding if you eat  some  of your dinner. A few peas. Just five. Five peas is a pretty easy deal. I had to eat, like, ten broccoli florets to get dessert last night. Oh, don’t remind me. He wouldn’t touch it. Said it looked like tiny trees. He’s just being dramatic. Honestly, he’ll eat anything covered in ketchup. It’s true. Ketchup solves everything. Want some ketchup, Lily? No! Ketchup’s red. And sticky. Right, okay. No ketchup. Maybe if you finish your chicken...though your brother ate most of his already. Leo, honestly, you were like a little vacuum cleaner. It was good chicken! Dad made it. He did indeed. Though he did spend half an hour trying to identify a bird’s egg he found in the garden before he started marinating it. Oh, don’t even  mention  that egg. I nearly stepped on it. Thought it was a discarded ping pong ball. It was a robin’s egg, apparently. He was very careful moving it. Said it was a scientific investigation. Did it hatch? No, sadly not. Something happened. A badger, I think. Or maybe one of the cats. Well, that’s nature, isn’t it? Speaking of nature, how was your bike ride this morning, darling? It was lovely, actually. Went down by the river. Saw a heron fishing. Though I definitely need to get back into it – I was completely breathless going up that hill. You should get an electric bike. Then you can fly up hills. An electric bike! That defeats the object, doesn’t it? It's supposed to be exercise. I know, I know. But it’s tempting. And then we could all go for rides together. Even Lily! I want chocolate ice cream. After your dinner, Lily. Now, back to the peas…What about a little walk after dinner? Maybe we can spot some birds? Can we get ice cream afterwards? Specifically, chocolate ice cream?

Honestly, the supermarket was chaos this morning. Absolute chaos. Everyone seemed to be doing a massive shop. Oh, don't even. I went yesterday and it was rammed. Needed just a loaf of bread and ended up buying half the biscuit aisle because I couldn't move for people! You two are terrible. I haven’t been to a proper supermarket in months. Far too much hustle and bustle for me. Just little shops, you see. Get what I need and be done with it. That sounds idyllic, honestly. Though I do like the convenience of getting everything in one go. I need to get some more spinach, I’m trying that recipe from that healthy eating blog. Oh, the one with all the kale and things? Looks a bit… rabbit food to me. It’s not  all  kale! There’s quinoa and… well, a bit of kale. I need to be healthier. My cholesterol’s been creeping up. Cholesterol! Fancy that. In my day, we just ate what we liked and got on with it. Though I did give up smoking when I was seventy-five. That was a shock to the system. Seventy-five! Good for you, Mum. That’s fantastic. It’s never too late, is it? No, it isn’t. My sister's trying to quit, she’s on those patches. Says they make her dream about cigarettes! Oh, dear! They need to try hypnotherapy. Old Mr. Henderson down the road, he gave it up that way. Said he just suddenly didn’t want one anymore. That’s amazing. Speaking of wanting things, my eyebrows are a disaster. They’ve gone completely wild. I need to book an appointment with Sarah. Ooh, go for it! She does a brilliant job. Though I’ve been meaning to ask, have you had your hair cut yet? You said you were going to the new salon in town. Not yet, I’m still working up the courage. I heard they're a bit scissor-happy. I’m terrified of ending up with a bob when I specifically asked for layers. Oh, that's awful! You need a reliable hairdresser. I’ve been going to Doreen since… well, since before you were born, dear! She knows exactly what I like. Doreen's brilliant. Though she’s getting on a bit, isn’t she? I worry she won’t be able to do it forever.

Honestly, this weaning is… a whole thing, isn’t it? I feel like I'm constantly covered in pureed sweet potato. Oh, Mum, it's the classic first-time mum experience! Honestly, it gets easier. Though, you’ll find yourself assessing every public surface for ‘splatter potential’ for months. Splatter potential! That’s exactly it! And the faces! The absolute disgust when she tries something new. You’d think I was poisoning her. It’s hilarious, though, isn’t it? Remember when Leo did that with the broccoli? Completely launched it across the highchair. Oh god, yes! Covered the cat in it! She wasn’t impressed. Anyway, enough about baby food warfare. What are you up to this week? Any plans with… well, anyone? Not much planned, actually. Just work, mostly. Though, Sarah mentioned a pub quiz on Wednesday. Said she’d ask if Mark and Chloe were free. Would you fancy joining us, if they are? Oh, that sounds nice. Quiet, though, isn’t it? Just the four of you? I was hoping we could maybe get a bigger group together? Perhaps next weekend? Maybe. I'll see what people say about Wednesday. Everyone’s so busy. Speaking of busy, I’ve finally booked myself onto that baby sign language course! Oh, brilliant! That’s a good idea. I was thinking about doing that. Does it actually work, though? Apparently! I spoke to another teacher at school whose little one did it, and she said it really helped with frustration as they get older. It’s just a few basic signs to start with - ‘milk’, ‘more’, ‘tired’ - stuff like that. That sounds really useful, actually. Less screaming, potentially? I'm in. Maybe we could do it together? They probably have another course starting soon. I’ll check! It’s at the community centre, Tuesdays after work. It’s a bit of a trek from school, but worth it, I think. Oh! And Auntie Brenda is coming down on Friday. She’s promised to bring her famous lemon drizzle cake. Brenda and her cake... a lethal combination! The whole house will smell of lemons for days. She’ll want to see the little one, of course. Are you ready for the interrogation about how I'm coping? Prepare for the 'are you getting enough sleep?' and ‘are you sure you’re eating properly?’ routine. She means well, you know she does.

It’s funny isn't it? How even a tiny incline feels like a mountain when you’re not used to it. London is…well, it’s just flat. Utterly pancake-like. I genuinely forgot hills  existed  for a while there. It’s nice though, isn’t it? To have a bit of undulation. Makes you feel like you’re actually  going  somewhere, even if you’re just walking in a circle. Exactly! And the views. You can actually  see  things. Not just brick walls and the tops of buses. Look, you can see St. Mary’s tower from here, can’t you? Just about. Through those trees. It’s a lovely little village, Little Barningham. Properly…Norfolk. Properly Norfolk? What does that even  mean ? You know. Quiet. Stone cottages. A pub that serves adnams. A general sense of…not being in a hurry. You’re being awfully romantic about it. It’s a village with a shop that closes at four and probably a lot of gossip. All the best places have a lot of gossip. It’s the social glue. Think about it. It's how people connect, how they understand their community. I suppose. It’s still a far cry from the constant hustle and bustle of university life, though. Being here… it’s a good antidote. Definitely. It makes you realise how much headspace the city takes up. I feel like I can breathe properly out here. And think. Not just…react. I know what you mean. It’s funny, isn’t it? To spend so long studying the human condition, and then realise you need to occasionally escape the humans to actually understand it. Precisely. Sometimes you just need to look at fields. And sheep. And appreciate the subtle curve of a hill. You’re sounding increasingly like a postcard. I’m embracing the Norfolk vibe! Honestly, I think we should come back more often. It’s good for us. Good for the soul. Even if it  is  a bit hilly. I have to admit, I'm starting to agree. It’s just…a lot quieter than we're used to. That's the point though, isn't it? Just quiet. And space. And not having to worry about dodging cyclists on the pavement. Good point. Let's make a plan, then. A proper, regular escape to the countryside. It’s just… what will we do if it rains?

…and honestly, the CGI was just… dodgy. Like, really dodgy. It pulled me right out of it. Which film was that again? You were mid-rant when I got in.  Rebellion Rising . Saw it last night with Chloe. Honestly, hyped it up for weeks, and it was just… a mess. The plot was okay, but visually it was just appalling. Looked like a Playstation 2 game at times. Oh dear. Harsh. I’ve heard mixed things. Chloe’s usually pretty good with her film recommendations though. She was gutted, honestly. Said she’d been completely sucked in by the trailers. They clearly spent all the budget on the marketing and none on the actual effects. Classic. It happens. So, how’s work? Still drowning in corpus data? You have  no  idea. Old Professor Davies keeps finding ‘errors’ which just turn out to be him not understanding how the system works. He emailed me at eleven last night asking why a particular word count was different from his handwritten notes. Handwritten! In 2024! Oh, Davies. He sounds… delightful. "Delightful" is one word for it. More like a particularly grumpy badger. Speaking of work, how’s the new project going? The one with the wind turbines? It's… challenging. Lots of stakeholder meetings. Everyone has an opinion on where these things should go, naturally. And a surprising amount of opposition from… cyclists. Cyclists? Really? What’s their problem? Apparently, the shadow flicker. When the blades turn, it casts a moving shadow that they find incredibly distracting. And also, they’re worried about birds. Which, fair enough, is a legitimate concern, but they're focusing on the shadow flicker thing. That's… specific. I mean, I get being annoyed by things, but shadow flicker? Seriously? Tell me about it. Spent an hour and a half yesterday explaining to a group of very passionate cyclists why the calculations showed the flicker wouldn’t actually impact any major cycle routes. They weren’t convinced. Sounds exhausting. You'd think they’d have bigger things to worry about. Like cars. Or those electric scooters that just appear out of nowhere. Exactly! Honestly, the scooters are more dangerous. Honestly, have you seen some of the places people are riding those things? On pavements, going the wrong way… it's chaos. It is! My auntie nearly got knocked over by one last week. Nearly gave the lad a piece of her mind, she did.

It’s just…look at that field of oilseed rape. It’s breathtaking, isn’t it? That bright yellow. It is pretty spectacular. Though, knowing what I know about agricultural subsidies, it probably shouldn't be. All that cash crop nonsense. Cash crops? You’re bringing economics into a lovely walk? I can’t help it! It’s ingrained. Thinking about the market forces behind pretty flowers. It’s a curse, really. Though, this is arguably more functional than pretty, I suppose. Oilseed rape isn't grown for aesthetics. No, no. It's for…biodiesel or something? I always forget. It feels a bit odd, though, doesn’t it? To have something so visually striking be driven entirely by economic factors. Like it's only beautiful because it’s profitable. Exactly! It's a manufactured aesthetic. And the impact on bee populations isn't great, is it? It's a whole complicated system. Still, it  is  yellow. Very yellow. Look, there are some orchids over there, by that hedge. White ones. Do you know what kind? Hmm…hard to tell from here. Maybe common spotted orchids? Though the conditions don’t look quite right. Too dry, perhaps. You’re the botanist. I'm a linguist, remember. I just… appreciate plants. I can tell them apart, mostly. It's a useful skill for fieldwork, actually. Trying to describe environments to students who’ve never been anywhere rural. The vocabulary gets quite specific. Fair enough. I suppose describing the nuances of a landscape requires a pretty detailed lexicon. It’s not all ‘green and pleasant land,’ is it? Definitely not. There's a whole spectrum of greens, and then you get into the textures, the smells… it's surprisingly complex. It’s like analysing a particularly difficult poem, really. Finding all the layers of meaning. Speaking of layers of meaning, have you seen that research paper on the linguistic relativity of colour perception? The one I sent you? Oh, the one about how different languages categorize colour differently? I skimmed it. It was…dense. Dense, yes, but fascinating! The idea that the way we perceive the world is shaped by the language we speak. It’s pretty mind-blowing. Makes you think about how much we miss when we try to translate. It does. Makes you think about how much we miss even  within  a language. So many subtleties get lost. Just like the nuances of this countryside, I suppose.

Right, so are we still on for Saturday then? Your mam’s birthday? Yeah, absolutely. I’ve booked a table at The Black Horse for seven. Thought that was sensible, somewhere a bit… less chaotic than the pub in town. Good shout. She’ll appreciate that, she hates all the noise. Are you driving, or shall I? It’s not far for either of us, really. I’ll drive. My car needs a run-out, truth be told. Been parked up most of the week. Plus, you’ve been doing all the driving lately, fair’s fair. True, true. Though I do enjoy a good drive, actually. Especially when the football’s on the radio. Did you see the match last night? Bits and pieces. Was stuck on a Zoom call until late. Heard Sunderland got a good result though? They absolutely smashed it! Three-nil against Sheffield Wednesday. Honestly, the atmosphere at the Stadium of Light must’ve been mental. I wish I’d been there. Sounds like it. You get properly invested in your football, don’t you? It’s a different level to what I experience following Watford. It’s just… polite applause most of the time. Polite applause! That’s Watford summed up. Speaking of cars, yours is looking good, by the way. Still loving the new wheels? Yeah, they’ve grown on me. Still a bit gutted I couldn’t get the one with the heated seats, but it’ll do. Parking’s a nightmare though, isn’t it? Even just getting to work. Tell me about it! I swear, trying to find a space near the office is a full-time job. People just park anywhere. It’s like the Wild West. Seriously! I saw someone park right across someone’s dropped kerb the other day. Honestly. Anyway, we should probably talk about presents for my mam. Have you got anything sorted? I’ve got her a little something. A new scarf. She always complains she’s cold. And I was thinking of taking her to see the Angel of the North when we’re up there. Have you taken her before? No, actually. She's always said she wanted to go, but never got around to it. That’s a lovely idea. Might be a bit windy up there though, mind. Oh yeah, good point. We’ll need to wrap up warm then. Also, been thinking about flats again.

Honestly, this Fred Sirieix trial is absolutely gripping, isn’t it? I can't believe he’s doing so well. Never pegged him as a dancer. Ooh, is it on tonight? I missed it last week, had a right bad headache. My Elsie – that’s my sister, you know – she’s proper hooked. Says he’s a dark horse. It is! Saturday night, BBC One. You absolutely must catch it. It’s a good bit of escapism, isn’t it? Something a bit silly. Escapism! You young ‘uns need a bit of that, always rushing about. Back in my day, escapism was a good book and a cup of tea. No television until the 60s, you know. Times have changed, haven't they, Margaret? Though I do still love a good book. Speaking of things changing… have you noticed the geese are already gathering down by the river? Feels earlier this year. Oh, they are, aren't they? I saw a huge flock yesterday, heading south. Proper noisy bunch, too. Bit intimidating when they come waddling across the road, they do. They know when it’s time. Instinct, pure instinct. Used to watch ‘em with my Arthur - my husband – down at the ‘Nene Washes. Magnificent sight, hundreds of them. Always said they knew more than most folks. It's amazing, isn't it? The distances they travel. I read somewhere that some of those geese migrate all the way to Russia for the winter. Russia! Blimey. Elsie’s son, Darren, he went to Russia on holiday once. Said it was freezing. Wouldn’t fancy a winter there, not for all the tea in China. Always loved watching the smaller birds, though. The robins, especially. Such cheerful little things, even in the bleakest weather. Remember feeding them scraps out of the kitchen window. We get a lot of blue tits in the garden. They’re so quick! And the squirrels are getting bolder. I saw one trying to get into the bird feeder yesterday. Complete menace. Oh, squirrels! They dig up my bulbs! I planted some lovely tulips last autumn, and they were all gone by spring. Little devils. Had to put netting over them this year. Always a battle, nature is. Always a balance. Give and take. My Arthur used to say… …Oh, never mind. Old memories. Is everything alright, Margaret? You seemed to… drift off. Oh, just remembering. Lovely man, Arthur.

Honestly, the interview was… a disaster. I mean, genuinely. Oh no! Really? I thought you were a shoo-in for that role at the language school. You've got loads of experience with their curriculum, haven't you? That's what  I  thought! But the panel… they were so fixated on my experience with, like, phonetics. Which is fine, I’m confident with phonetics, but it was a general French teaching post! They kept asking me about minimal pairs and vowel sounds – I felt like I was back in my Masters, being grilled! Ugh, that sounds awful. So rigid. Some schools are like that though, aren't they? All theory, no practical application. Were they at least nice? Niceness is subjective when you're being interrogated about the intricacies of the French ‘u’ sound for twenty minutes. They were… efficient. Coldly efficient. And one of them kept interrupting me. Honestly, I nearly told him to let me  finish a sentence . Oh, the  nerve ! I hate that. I had a similar thing happen once, years ago, at an interview for a head of department role. This guy just kept talking  over  me, explaining my own experience back to me, but incorrectly. I just wanted to scream. Exactly! It’s so undermining. Anyway, I think I fluffed the lesson observation part too. I completely blanked on a past tense exercise. Blanked! Me, a French teacher. It’s mortifying. Oh, don’t beat yourself up. Everyone has off days. You're brilliant with your students, you always have been. It was just one interview. Easy for you to say, you’re happily teaching Year 5 and completely content. I'm apparently incapable of securing a proper job. Hey! It's not always easy with Year 5, believe me. Especially when half of them have decided that glitter is a food group. But seriously, you'll find something. Have you thought about supply work again, just to tide you over? I'm so over supply work. The constant traveling, the last-minute phone calls… it’s exhausting. Plus, half the schools don't even provide a proper staff room. You're expected to eat your lunch in a classroom surrounded by ten-year-olds and half-finished art projects. True, that does sound… chaotic. Speaking of chaos, have you tried weaning little Leo onto anything other than purees yet? It's a battlefield over here.

Honestly, I’m starting to freak out a little bit about… everything. Like, proper adulting is looming. Oh, tell me about it. I feel like I’ve been ‘almost an adult’ for about five years now, and it’s still not sinking in. What’s specifically freaking you out? Is it the job? The job’s…fine. It’s stable, which is good, but I don’t know if “stable” is enough, you know? Like, am I just going to be a Production Controller forever? It doesn't feel  wrong , it just feels… small. I get that. I keep having these moments where I think, “Is this it?” Filing, answering emails… it’s not exactly setting the world on fire. But then I remember the rent needs paying, and a decent oat latte is not cheap. Exactly! The financial reality is so depressing. I mean, I’ve got student loans still hanging over me, then I want to eventually save for a deposit on a flat… it feels impossible. My mum keeps saying “just get on the property ladder!” Like it’s that easy. Oh, mothers. Mine’s the same. She keeps sending me links to little cottages in the countryside, assuming I’m secretly yearning for a life of baking and tending to a vegetable patch. Which, honestly, sounds idyllic, but also… unrealistic. Seriously. I saw a tiny flat in Finsbury Park advertised for £1,800 a month.  A month!  It was basically a glorified cupboard. London is insane. Cambridge is bad enough, honestly. I’m starting to think I’ll be living with housemates until I’m 40. That’s… probably realistic. Have you thought any more about that masters you were considering? The one in Environmental Policy? Yeah, I’ve been looking at courses. It feels a bit terrifying though, going back to studying. Especially with work. And the cost… it's another huge financial undertaking. I know, it's a big decision. But you’re really good at that stuff, you care about it. Sometimes I think we get so bogged down in the practicalities that we forget what we actually  want  to do. You’re right. I was talking to Sarah the other day, and she just quit her marketing job to travel around South America. Completely on a whim. Wow, that's brave! Or maybe incredibly reckless. Maybe a bit of both! But it made me think… what's the worst that could happen if I just took a leap?

Honestly, I’m starting to think Liam’s just… a bit of a knob, you know? Oh, go on then. What’s he done  now ? Is it the football again? He promised he'd text you during the match, didn’t he? No, not the football, surprisingly. It's just… he was talking about Chloe last night. Properly talking about her. Like, detailing how nice her new jacket was. Chloe? Chloe from his uni course? The one with the… the really loud laugh? The very same. And he kept saying how ‘easygoing’ she is. Easygoing! As if I’m not. Honestly, it just felt… weird. Like he was trying to make me jealous. Ugh, boys are the worst at that. Little tests, aren’t they? Just to see how you react. Ignore it, honestly. He’s probably just being a bit daft. Easy for you to say, you and Ben are practically joined at the hip. You don't know what it's like when someone's constantly comparing you to other girls. Yeah, that does sound annoying. Is she… attractive, this Chloe? Be honest. Look, she’s alright. I'm not saying she’s some supermodel, but she definitely fits Liam's ‘type’. Long dark hair, always dressed nicely… everything I'm not when I'm trying to revise for exams. Oh, don’t start with the self-deprecating stuff. You look lovely! Remember that dress you wore to Sarah’s birthday? He was going on about  that . That was ages ago! And he was just being polite, probably. Everyone says nice things at parties. He genuinely seemed to like it. I remember thinking it suited you really well. Anyway, maybe you’re reading too much into it. He could just be trying to be friendly. Friendly? Detailing someone’s jacket and personality isn’t ‘friendly,’ it’s actively highlighting why someone else might be better than me! I’m seriously starting to wonder if I’m wasting my time. Don't do that. Don't go down that rabbit hole. You deserve someone who appreciates you for  you , not someone who’s busy analysing other girls’ outfits. Honestly, if he’s making you feel like that, he’s not worth the hassle. Plus, remember what happened with Lucy and Mark? She kept getting jealous over his work colleagues, and in the end, she was right to be suspicious. He  was  messing about.

Honestly, the shepherd’s pie was a bit dry tonight, wasn’t it? I think I need to add a bit more stock next time. It was alright, Mum. I ate mine. It was perfectly acceptable, darling. You always put too much pressure on yourself with the cooking. It’s lovely to have a proper home-cooked meal, though. Beats takeaway any day. Yeah, it was better than pizza. Though pizza  is  good. Don’t even start with the pizza requests, Jamie. You had pizza three times last week! So, Ethan, how was the hockey match this afternoon? Did you win? We smashed them, actually! 5-2. I scored one! Oh, brilliant! That’s fantastic, love. Which position did you play? Left wing. I got a really good pass from Ben and just…whacked it in. Excellent! Your coach must have been impressed. Did Mrs. Davies come to watch? She's always so supportive. Yeah, she was there. She was yelling really loud. It was a bit embarrassing. Haha! My mum does that at my football matches too. It’s mortifying. Mothers will be mothers, won’t they? They’re so proud. Speaking of proud, your cousin, Chloe, landed a new client today. A really big one. She’s absolutely buzzing. That’s amazing news! Good for her. She’s been working so hard on building her business. It must be a relief to get such a substantial contract. Absolutely. She’s thinking of going to Barcelona for a conference next month, to network. It’s a bit pricey, but she thinks it’ll be a good investment. Barcelona? Wow! I want to go to Barcelona. Well, perhaps one day we can all go. How are your summer plans shaping up, both of you? Any ideas yet? I was talking to Ben about maybe going camping. Just the two of us. His dad said he could take us somewhere near the Peak District. That sounds… adventurous. Make sure you pack appropriately, and tell us exactly where you’re going. Camping in the Peaks can be quite chilly even in summer. I’m going to France with Grandad. We’re visiting his friends in Normandy. He lived there when he was a kid. Oh, that’s lovely! He’ll enjoy that so much. Normandy is beautiful. You'll have to practice your French, Jamie.  Groans . I hate French. It’s a useful language to know, though.

Honestly, the size of these trees is just… mind-blowing. I keep expecting to see a dinosaur wander past. Seriously! It feels prehistoric. Though I’m starting to regret that extra slice of pie last night. My jeans are definitely feeling a bit snug after all this driving. Oh, don't even! I’m avoiding mirrors. We've been eating so much comfort food since we landed. It's a holiday, right? Gotta embrace it. Speaking of embracing things...have you heard anything from Sarah since she got back from Italy? Not really. She posted a few photos on Instagram, looking very glamorous in Rome, but I haven't actually  spoken  to her. Just a quick 'liked' on a photo of the Colosseum. She’s always terrible at keeping in touch when she's travelling. She is, isn’t she? It's the ‘I’m having too much fun to bother with phones!’ mentality. I sometimes wonder if she even remembers we exist when she’s on one of her adventures. I know! It's a little frustrating. Especially after she spent ages moaning about needing a holiday, and then completely disappears into a travel bubble. Remember that time in Thailand? We tried to video call and she was halfway up a mountain, covered in mud, trying to explain something about sustainable farming. Oh god, yes! And the connection was dreadful. All we could see was blurry green and hear snippets of her yelling at a water buffalo. Honestly, it was like watching a really bad nature documentary. Exactly! It's like she actively seeks out experiences that make it impossible to have a normal conversation. And then gets offended when we don’t know all the details. It’s her thing. Still, I hope she's okay. She was pretty stressed before she left with that whole mess at work, wasn't she? Yeah, with Mark being…Mark. Honestly, I don’t know how she puts up with him. He’s just constantly undermining her, even when she's succeeding. It's exhausting just  hearing  about it. It’s awful. She deserves someone who celebrates her achievements, not downplays them. Perhaps Italy will give her some much-needed clarity. She needs to realise she can do better. Hopefully. Maybe she’ll come back with a newfound sense of self-worth and dump him. That would be the best souvenir.

Honestly, that Kiev was…industrial. I’ve never encountered a Kiev so…firm. It felt like chewing on a bouncy castle. It’s alright. Garlic sauce helps. Don't talk with your mouth full, please, Leo. And yes, it  was  a bit…dense. I think they’d frozen it and then refrozen it, then maybe refrozen it again. It tasted like it had been on a long journey. Speaking of journeys, did you two finalise plans for Granny on Saturday? I’m still on call for work, unfortunately. There’s this system migration… Yes, I’ve booked the train tickets. We're leaving at ten, which gives us plenty of time to get to her before lunch. She was very excited to hear we were coming. She asked if I was bringing biscuits. Of course she did. Always the biscuits. She thinks I’m a biscuit denial machine. Can I have another biscuit? After you finish your chicken, Leo. Honestly, the backchat! You get that from your father. Hey! I resent that. I’m a paragon of politeness. You called Mrs. Higgins a Wallie last week for parking over your drive. Technically, it  was  a Wallie move. Blocking someone's drive. Anyway, Granny. Are you sure you’ve remembered everything? Her medication? The new slippers? Yes, yes, the list is exhaustive. I’ve even backed up all the photos from my phone to Dropbox  and  Flickr. You know how she likes to see pictures of everything. Especially Leo causing mayhem. I don’t cause mayhem! I'm a reasonable person. Reasonable? You tried to build a den inside the washing machine last Tuesday. See? What did I tell you? Speaking of mayhem, did you see the rugby yesterday? That drop goal at the end! Absolutely brilliant. I missed it! I was… wrestling with servers. Honestly, the IT world is a constant battle against entropy. Was it a good match? Phenomenal. A proper nail-biter. We really need to get you into rugby, Leo. It’s a far superior sport to… football, obviously. Hold on a minute. My head is starting to throb. I think I need a lie down after this. All the planning, the Kiev… it's too much. Oh dear. Do you want me to make you a cup of tea? And maybe a biscuit? For medicinal purposes, of course. Can I have one too? Please? And maybe another garlic sauce?

Right, so I’ve put the potatoes on to boil. Are you chopping the onions or shall I? I can do the onions. How’s the transcription going? Still drowning in legal jargon? You have no idea. Seriously, I think I’m starting to speak legalese in my sleep. It’s a massive case, apparently, something to do with… honestly, I’ve stopped trying to understand. Just type, type, type. Though, I did spot a misspelling of “heretofore” earlier. Felt very superior correcting  that . Good for you. Standing up to the lawyers. Speaking of things arriving, my latest eBay obsession turned up today. Oh, no! Not more vintage cups and saucers? How many  do  you need? It’s never enough, obviously. This one’s a Shelley Dainty Blue. It was a bargain! Apparently, it’s from the 1920s. It’s just… exquisite. I’ve already got it displayed with the others. You  have  to see it. I’ll have to admire it from a distance, lest I accidentally break one. You know how clumsy I am. Did you manage to get any of that buckwheat bread from the market on Saturday? I’ve been craving it all week. Oh, yes! They’d just brought a fresh batch out. I got two loaves, figuring we’d get through it. It’s lovely toasted with a bit of butter and jam. Perfect. That’ll do nicely with the sausages. Ooh, and I almost forgot! They’re having a proper leaving do for Brenda on Friday. At The Red Lion. Brenda! Oh, that’s lovely. She deserves a good send-off. She's been there forever. Are we going? I think we should, don’t you? She’s always been really kind to me, even though we don't really socialise outside of work. And it'll be nice to see everyone. Definitely. I’ll book a table, just in case. It gets rammed in there on a Friday. What time did you say it starts? Seven-thirty, I think. It's supposed to be a bit of a buffet. Good. I’m starving just thinking about it. This community market is amazing. They had a stall selling homemade chilli oils too, really hot ones. I got a couple for your brother, he'll love them. Oh, brilliant! He’s obsessed with anything spicy. You’re a lifesaver. Right, onions are chopped. What next?

…and honestly, the amount of paperwork is just… insane. It’s not even the work  doing  the accounts, it’s proving where everything came from, all the time. Right. Because you’re dealing with a lot of cash, aren’t you? With the shop? Yeah, and even card payments. They want to know everything. I’ve started wondering if I should just… you know, funnel some through a different account. Woah, hold on. Funnel? Like… how? Just… a business account, maybe? One I don’t use as much. Spread the load, make it look less suspicious. That sounds… dodgy, babe. Seriously. It  is  dodgy, love. That’s what they call ‘structuring’ and it’s a red flag as anything. They’re specifically looking for that. You’re basically asking for a visit from financial crime. But it just feels like they’re deliberately making it difficult! I’m a legitimate business, I pay my taxes… why do I have to jump through so many hoops? Because criminals use businesses to launder money, obviously. Sorry to state the bleeding obvious. Exactly. And unfortunately, because of that, every legitimate business gets caught in the net. What sort of amounts are we talking about, roughly? Well, a good month can be… eight, maybe ten thousand through the till. And then another five or six on card. Ten thousand cash?! That  is  a lot, isn't it? It's busy! It’s a summer tourist spot, people like to pay with cash! Maybe you need a better card reader system or something? One that integrates better? That might help with the traceability, yes. Look, the best thing you can do is be scrupulously honest and keep impeccable records. Every. Single. Transaction. Think about getting a proper forensic accountant to just check everything over, one off cost but worthwhile. Forensic accountant… that sounds expensive. It is, but a fine from HMRC, or worse, is a lot more expensive. Trust me, I've had a client go through that. Nightmare. Remember Uncle Barry? He thought he was being clever with his tax. Ended up owing more in penalties than the actual tax! Oh god, don't even. He's still moaning about that. So, no 'funnelling' then? Fine, no funnelling. It just feels like I’m constantly bracing for a problem. It’s exhausting. It makes me wonder if starting a business was actually a good idea.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s chucking it down. Makes planning anything impossible. Tell me about it. I had a garden fete scheduled for Saturday, raising money for the hospice, and it looks like it’s going to be a washout. We're having to move everything into the village hall, which is a bit of a squeeze. Oh no, that’s a shame! Hopefully it won't impact attendance too much. People are pretty dedicated to a good cause, aren’t they? I’m still buzzing from work, though. Little Leo finally managed to write his name today! It was wobbly, but it was definitely a ‘Leo’. Aww, that’s brilliant! Must be a proud moment. I’m drowning in spreadsheets at work. New stock arrives next week, and the delivery is a nightmare to organise. Honestly, sometimes I think about chucking it all in and opening a little bakery. A bakery! You'd be amazing at that, love. Remember those lemon drizzle cakes you used to make for every birthday? They were legendary. Thanks, Mum! But realistically, it's a pipe dream. Too much risk. Speaking of which, has anyone heard anything about the sign language class? I signed up ages ago, and I haven’t had a confirmation email. I think I saw a poster about that at the community centre. They moved the start date back a week, apparently. Something about the instructor being unwell. Let me check online when I get home. Good idea. I'm really looking forward to that. I think it'll be so useful in the classroom, especially with some of our non-verbal students. It’s lovely you’re thinking about that. And how are  you  feeling, darling? Still a bit tired? Yeah, a little. This first trimester is exhausting. But I’m trying to keep busy and stay positive. The scan went well, and everything seems to be normal. That's the main thing. You look glowing, actually! It really suits you. Are you still getting cravings for weird things? Last time you were obsessed with pickled onions and chocolate biscuits. Don't remind me! It's moved onto grapefruit and cheese now. It’s a truly bizarre combination, but I can’t get enough of it. Oh dear. Sounds… interesting. Listen, I need to dash. Got a meeting with the hospice committee to finalise the fete arrangements.

Honestly, this canteen pasta is…an experience. Not necessarily a  good  one. Tell me about it. It's consistently…beige. Like, aggressively beige. I think they just boil pasta and then add sadness. You two are brutal. I actually don’t mind it, it fills a hole. Though, I did bring a banana, just in case. Smart move, Maya. I wish I’d thought of that. I’m already feeling that 2pm slump creeping in. This morning’s proofreading session was…intense. So many commas in the wrong place. Oh god, commas. My nemesis. I spent half of yesterday trying to explain the nuances of the Oxford comma to someone. It was like talking to a brick wall. Was that Ben from Marketing? He once asked me if ‘affect’ and ‘effect’ were interchangeable. I almost choked on my tea. Oh, Ben. He means well. He just…doesn’t have a natural flair for linguistics, does he? You’re so patient, Elara. It’s a professional hazard, I think, being surrounded by words all day. You just assume everyone understands the basic rules. It’s like expecting everyone to know the capital of France. True. Though, working in publishing, you quickly learn that assumptions are the mother of all mistakes. Remember the whole debacle with the mislabelled map in the geography textbook last year? Don’t remind me! That was a Monday morning I’d rather forget. The editor nearly had a heart attack. Apparently, Greenland was significantly smaller. And situated somewhere near Spain, as I recall. It was a geographical disaster! It’s all fun and games until someone’s international relations are offended by a misplaced island. Speaking of which, how's that manuscript going, Astrid? The one about the Swedish folklore? It’s…challenging. The author insists on using these incredibly archaic turns of phrase. It’s beautiful, but ensuring it translates understandably for a modern audience is proving difficult. I'm spending a lot of time with a Swedish-English dictionary. Sounds fascinating though. I always think folklore is so rich. It says so much about a culture. Absolutely. And the translation process is so interesting. You’re not just converting words, you're conveying a whole cultural context. Which, you know, is basically what we  do  every day, just in a slightly less…mythical way. Exactly! It’s all about bridging gaps, isn't it? Between author and reader, between cultures, even between poorly placed commas and grammatical sanity.

Right, so the visa's the biggest headache, innit? I’ve been reading online, some people get knocked back for the smallest thing. Tell me about it. I’m stressing already. Did you manage to find that checklist someone posted on the Mongol Rally forum? The one that’s, like, twenty pages long? Aye, found it. It’s mental. Apparently, they’re really picky about passport photos. Like, if your ears aren’t showing properly, they’ll send it back. Seriously? Ears? That's ridiculous. I'll need to get some done professionally then, won't I? Last time I tried to do them myself, they looked like I'd been in a fight. Yeah, best to be safe. I think I’ll bite the bullet and go to Boots. It's a fiver a pop, but it's better than the hassle of re-applying. Speaking of which, have you sorted your passport renewal? Mine just came through, thankfully. Nearly. I’ve got the application form filled in, just need to get the supporting documents together. And obviously, the photos. Ugh. It’s a right pain. It is. Right, let’s talk donations. We’re a bit behind where we want to be, aren’t we? I put a post on Facebook, but it wasn't exactly setting the world alight. Same. Mum sent a tenner, which is nice, but we need more than that. I was thinking, maybe we could put an ad on Gumtree? Like, "Two lads driving to Mongolia for charity, please sponsor us!" Gumtree? Is that a bit desperate? Maybe, but it’s worth a shot, innit? It’s free advertising. We could put a link to our JustGiving page. Plus, it might attract some weirdos who want to join us. I can see that happening. Alright, you handle the Gumtree ad. I’ll harass more people on social media. And I’ll start researching mechanics in… well, wherever the first breakdown happens. Good thinking. That car is held together with duct tape and dreams, let’s be honest. Have you found that spare part we were talking about? The one for the alternator? I did! Found a bloke in Bolton selling one for twenty quid. Says it's practically brand new. Going to pick it up next week. Brilliant. That's one less thing to worry about. What about the route? Have you had a look at the best way to go through, like, Kazakhstan and stuff?

Right, honestly, I still can’t believe you ended up in A&E. Over an arm. I  told  you it hurt, didn’t I? It wasn’t just an arm ache, it felt…wrong. Like properly wrong.
