And then I couldn’t move my fingers. Morning, sleepyheads. Or, well, morning to some of you. What’s all the commotion? Someone finally discover the joys of a 9am lecture? Worse. Seren here had a dramatic night. Attempted arm dismemberment, apparently. Dramatic is a bit strong. And it wasn't  attempted  dismemberment, it was a potential fracture! They x-rayed it, everything. Turns out it’s just…badly sprained. Oh, bless. No broken bones, at least. Still, A&E is not a fun place to spend a Saturday night. You have  no  idea. It was full of lads who’d fallen over. And one guy who'd tried to fight a lamppost. Honestly. Did anyone ask what  you  were doing to hurt your arm so badly? I just said I tripped. Didn’t want to explain the whole ‘attempting a handstand and failing miserably’ situation. Too embarrassing. Wise move. So, are you alright now? Feeling less…arm-challenged? Yeah, it’s sore, but the nurse gave me some painkillers. I think I just need to sleep. I'm absolutely knackered. All that waiting around… You should have let me come with you! I didn't want to wake you! And honestly, it was quicker just to get a taxi. Plus, you were already planning on going out. True. Speaking of going out, how was Liam last night? You two seemed pretty cosy at pre-drinks. He's…nice. He's really funny. We just chatted, mostly. He’s doing History, so he was going on about some Roman emperor. Sounds riveting. Is he one of those history boys who tries to work Roman references into every conversation? No, not yet. He was actually pretty normal. Though he did ask me if I’d seen that meme about Boudicca on TikTok. Oh god. They’re all the same. So, is this a  thing  then? You and Liam? I don't know! It's literally one conversation. One slightly-too-long conversation. It’s not a ‘thing’. Relax, Seren. It’s university, everything’s a ‘thing’ for five minutes. You'll figure it out. Come on, let’s get some breakfast. I'm starving. Good idea. Maybe some toast will revive me.

So, did you have a good time at Gran and Grandad’s yesterday? Honestly, it was a bit chaotic, wasn’t it? Yeah, it was alright. A bit crowded though. Could barely move in the kitchen. Tell me about it! Auntie Brenda was right in the doorway, holding court with everyone about her prize-winning dahlias. I swear she didn’t move for a solid hour. Haha! Yeah, I saw. Did you talk to Cousin Liam? He was wearing that weird hat again. Oh,  that  hat. The one that looks like a pineapple? Yes, briefly. He asked me if I was still marking GCSE papers. Honestly, the man thinks maths is some sort of mystical art form. He’s a bit clueless, isn't he? Did you try the buffet? The sausage rolls were good. Oh, the buffet was…substantial. A bit too much potato salad for my liking, but the sausage rolls were decent, you’re right. Your Uncle David made a right mess of the trifle, though. I think he got a bit enthusiastic with the sherry. He always does! Remember last Christmas when he…? Oh, don’t even start. We’re still finding glitter. Honestly, I don’t know how your Grandma lets him near anything remotely festive. She loves him, though. She says he’s ‘full of life’. That's one way to put it! Did you get chance to speak to old Mrs. Higgins from next door? She was asking after you. Said she’d seen you cycling down the high street last week. Oh, yeah. She’s nice. She always gives me sweets if I help her with her bins. That’s lovely. It's good you're helpful to the neighbours. It was nice to see everyone together though, wasn't it? Even with the chaos. It's been ages since we’ve all been in the same room. Yeah, it was okay. It’s just…everyone talks so loudly. It was hard to hear anyone properly. That  is  a family trait, isn’t it? We're all a bit…vocal. Did you feel overwhelmed at all? Not really. It was just a bit tiring, you know? All the talking. And having to say hello to everyone. I understand. It can be a bit much. Still, it was a lovely anniversary, and it was good to celebrate Gran and Grandad. They were really touched.

Honestly, Dad, are you  sure  you packed enough water? We’ve barely left Manchester and I’m already thirsty. It’s gonna be a long drive. Aye, I’m sure, love. There's a full two-litre bottle in the footwell, plus your own little one. And if that runs out, we’ll stop, won't we? Don't you worry. Speaking of which, did you grab a pen? I need someone to write down the mileage every couple of hours, just to keep track. Pen? Ugh. I thought we were past needing to write stuff down. Isn’t that what phones are for? Phones run out of battery, lass. And sometimes the signal's patchy. Old-fashioned methods are the best, remember? Plus, it'll keep your hands busy. You always fidget on long journeys. Anyway, what about lunch? Fancy a pasty when we get down to Cornwall, or something else? A pasty would be good, actually. Or maybe some fish and chips. I saw Holland & Barrett in town yesterday… I was thinking of getting some of those digestive enzyme tablets, you know, for… stuff. Oh, not again. Your mum keeps telling you about that Irritable Bowel Syndrome, doesn’t she? Honestly, you're too young to be worrying about all that. Just eat sensible. Speaking of worrying, I’m still stressed about the house move. It’s just… endless boxes. I know, but it'll be worth it, won’t it? A garden big enough for a proper trampoline! And a spare room for my art stuff. That's true. Though unpacking all those books will be a nightmare. And trying to get the furniture arranged how your mum wants it. She’s got a very specific vision, you know. She’s already planned where all the pictures are going. She always does. Remember that chocolate orange she hid in the biscuit tin for a week? Said it was ‘for guests’. Aye, that was a good one. She’s a crafty one, your mum. Did you see that documentary about manor houses last night? Some of them were absolutely enormous. Imagine living in a place like that! It's ridiculous, isn't it? All that space. It must cost a fortune to heat. Actually, have you seen how much petrol is now? This trip is gonna bankrupt us. Don't say that! We budgeted for it. We'll be alright.

Honestly, the state of the garden is appalling. I keep meaning to get out there, but… well, you know. Life just gets in the way. Tell me about it. I spent the weekend battling spreadsheets. Thought I'd finally get on top of things, ended up further behind. At least you  have  a garden to neglect. My balcony is currently sporting a single, rather sad-looking geranium. Neglect is a strong word, dear. It simply needs attention. A bit of weeding, a trim here and there. It’s like anything, really. Requires consistent effort. Though I must confess, even I found keeping the school grounds pristine exhausting after a while. The children were… enthusiastic diggers. Enthusiastic diggers, eh? Sounds familiar. My grandson thinks my workshop is his personal excavation site. Found a half-eaten biscuit in the biscuit tin the other day, wedged amongst the chisels. Oh, bless him. They are little horrors, aren’t they? But you wouldn't trade it. My niece is at that age where everything is covered in glitter.  Everything . Glitter is the herpes of the craft world. It gets  everywhere . You’re still finding it years later. I’m convinced it’s self-replicating. A rather dramatic analogy, Jonathan. But I see your point. It's remarkably persistent. Now, has anyone heard from Eleanor? She promised to bring the photographs from her trip to Italy. Not a peep. She said she was having trouble with the digital camera, something about the memory card being full. Said she'd try and get it sorted, but she’s notoriously… disorganized. That sounds like Eleanor. She sent me a postcard, though. Very flowery language about Tuscan sunsets and delicious pasta. Didn't mention a single logistical problem. Maybe she’s pretending everything’s perfect for our benefit. It’s what I do on social media. A carefully curated illusion. That’s a rather cynical view, isn't it? I prefer to think she’s simply enjoying herself and doesn’t want to burden us with her troubles. Could be either, really. She's always been a bit of a mystery, Eleanor. Though a lovely one. Anyone fancy another cup of tea? I can put the kettle on. Oh, yes, please. That would be lovely. I think I need something strong. This week is already shaping up to be… challenging. I’ve got three particularly dense interviews to transcribe.

Right, Operation Mother’s Day is a go! What do you two think? We need a plan. Gran’s expecting a visit, of course, but what are we  doing  for her? Can we make her a card? A really sparkly one? With glitter! Glitter gets  everywhere . Remember last time? It was in my toast. He’s got a point. We can definitely make a card, but maybe a slightly less…explosive glitter situation. How about painting? We could do handprints? Ooh! Handprints! Like butterflies? Exactly! Beautiful handprint butterflies. And what about breakfast in bed? We could make toast, and… well, I can handle the coffee. Can I help with the toast? I’m good at putting the bread in. You are  excellent  at putting the bread in. You’re my official toaster operator. Now, Gran loves those little pastries from the bakery, don’t you think? I could pop down and get a couple. And a flower! She likes daffodils! Wonderful idea! We can get some daffodils too. Right, so card-making, handprint butterflies, toast prepared by the official toaster operator, pastries, and daffodils. Sounds like a good start. Is this going to take all day? I was hoping to go to Forest School tomorrow. It won't take  all  day, sweetheart. We’ll get everything done this morning, and then you're free for Forest School. It's good to be organised! Like, you know what they say - "a stitch in time saves nine!" What does  that  mean? Is someone sewing? It’s an idiom, darling. It means if you fix something right away, it’s easier than letting it become a bigger problem. Like if my Lego tower is wobbly, I should fix it before it falls down? Exactly! You're a little idiom expert already! See, learning is everywhere. Mummy, can we tell Gran a joke? I know a good one. Oh, please do! Let’s hear it. What do you call a lazy kangaroo? Hmm… I have no idea! What  do  you call a lazy kangaroo? Pouch potato! Oh, that's brilliant! Gran  will  love that one. Right, let’s get started on those cards then. And remember, gentle glitter application, please! I’ll be extra careful. And maybe I can draw a kangaroo on Gran’s card? A pouch potato kangaroo! That sounds perfect! Let's make this the best Mother's Day ever. Yes! The best ever!

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, you know? Knowing she wasn’t herself for so long. We just…we just assumed it was age. Mum always was a bit forgetful, but it escalated so quickly. It's the speed, isn't it? That’s what gets you. With Dad, it was…slow. We had years, awful years, but years to prepare. To say things. Cancer’s a bastard like that, just sneaks up and then…bang. Exactly. And she was  fierce . She’d tell you exactly what she thought, Mum would. Even when she was confused, she still had that spark. I miss that already. I find myself wanting to call her just to…argue about something silly. Oh, I totally get that. I still reach for the phone to tell my Dad something, a ridiculous work thing or a funny story about Ben. Then I remember. It's like a phantom limb, isn't it? You still  feel  the need, but it’s not there anymore. Phantom limb is a perfect way to put it. And David's not coping well, he’s really shutting down. He keeps saying he’s fine, but he barely touches his food and he’s just…distant. Oh, poor David. He was so close to your Mum. It's a different kind of grief when it's not a parent. It’s harder to know how to support them, I think, because you don’t want to invalidate their feelings by comparing it to your own. Have you tried just…sitting with him? Not talking, just being there? I’ve tried, yeah. He just gets agitated. Says he needs to be strong for us all, which is classic David. He’s always been the strong one. It’s exhausting trying to get him to talk. He's not strong by  not  feeling, though, is he? That’s what we tell Ben, all the time. It's okay to be sad, it's okay to be angry. Bottling it up just makes it worse. Has he considered…you know…talking to someone? A counsellor? I’ve suggested it, but he’s adamant he doesn’t need it. Says it's 'nonsense'. Honestly, his stubbornness can be infuriating even at the best of times. It just feels like I'm failing him somehow. You’re not failing him. You're trying. And sometimes trying is all you  can  do.

Right, so I think I’ve finally cracked the dissertation timetable. Monday is solely literature review, Tuesday is data analysis, Wednesday… well, Wednesday is damage control from Monday and Tuesday, realistically. And then Thursday and Friday are writing days. Sounds…intense. Are you actually sticking to that? You said that last week about the poetry analysis and ended up re-watching all of  Buffy . Okay, fair point. But this is different! This is the final stretch. Plus, Professor Davies actually gave me some really useful feedback on the methodology. He thinks my approach to the Korean politeness strategies is… innovative, apparently. Ooh, ‘innovative’! That’s good. Bet he says that to all the boys though, doesn’t he? He always seemed a bit… patronising. Maybe. But still, it's encouraging. Anyway, speaking of Korea… did you see that article about the debate around gender roles there? It's fascinating. Apparently, younger Korean men are increasingly reluctant to date because they worry about the expectations around providing financially. Oh yeah, I skimmed something about that. Sounds stressful. It’s weird, isn’t it? The pressure on men to be the breadwinner is still so strong in some cultures, even while everything else is changing. Exactly. It’s a really complex issue. And it feeds back into the whole language thing, you know? The different levels of formality, the honorifics… it’s all tied up with societal power structures. It’s amazing how much language reflects everything else. It is. Reminds me of that lecture last term on how linguistic sexism is perpetuated. Horrifying, really. Right, food. What are we doing for dinner? I’m starving. That sandwich at lunch was… inadequate. I was thinking a veggie stir-fry? I bought loads of stuff from Waitrose yesterday. Proper posh veg. Ooh, nice! You’re going all out. But Waitrose… seriously? You know they got criticised for their animal welfare standards, right? I… I thought they were better than that? Apparently not. Something about the chicken farms. It’s grim. I'm trying to be more mindful about where I get my food from. Good point. Maybe we should go to the co-op tomorrow then. They’re generally more ethical, aren't they? Although, their fruit is always looking a bit sad. Actually, I’ve got that game I was telling you about,  Stardew Valley , on the computer. I’m thinking of selling it.

Honestly, this pizza is saving my life. I swear, that physics problem set nearly broke me. Tell me about it! I was staring at that equation for a solid hour and then just…gave up. It’s like they  want  us to fail, isn’t it? You lot are stressing about physics? I'm just trying to remember if I’ve actually submitted anything for my history module this week. It's all a blur. Oh god, don’t even. I haven't even  started  my essay on… what even  is  it? Something about post-structuralism and… pigeons? I don’t know. Pigeons?! Seriously? Is that a real thing? Apparently. Professor Davies is obsessed. Says they’re a metaphor for… something. Honestly, I zoned out after ‘pigeon’. Right, let's not talk about coursework. Distract me. Anyone got plans for the weekend? Sugarhouse is doing that cheesy night, isn’t it? Ooh, I'm tempted. Though, remembering last time… I spent the entire night talking to a guy who was convinced he was a time traveller. No way! What did he say about the future? Mostly complaining about the airport scanners. Said they ‘disrupt the temporal flow’. Honestly, he was a trip. Classic Lancaster. Speaking of weird nights, remember that Rocky Horror screening we went to? The one where everyone was  really  committed? Oh my god, don't remind me! I’m still having nightmares about the pelvic thrusts. And that guy dressed as Riff Raff… terrifying. It was iconic though, wasn't it? A proper Lancaster experience. Speaking of experiences, anyone else remember when the whole of Lancaster flooded a couple of years ago? We were practically stranded in this house. Traumatising. Trying to wade through knee-deep water to get to campus… I lost a shoe. A perfectly good shoe. I think I still have a slightly damp sports kit top from that. It just…never fully recovered. That reminds me, I need to buy new boxers. Mine are all holey. I swear, doing laundry in this house is a team sport. It is! Plus, you always end up accidentally taking someone else’s. Remember last secret Santa? When you got that… thing. Don’t. It was a knitted toilet roll cover.  A knitted toilet roll cover.  It was… thoughtful. Seriously though, who buys a knitted toilet roll cover? Unless it's your grandma, there’s no excuse. And speaking of awful gifts, remember when Chloe got us all copies of  City of Bones  for Christmas?

…and honestly, the state of the place, you wouldn’t believe it. Like, full bins everywhere, crisp packets blowing about, half a kebab just…stuck to the pavement. It was grim, man, proper grim. Right, sounds charming. Was it busy though? Like, did you actually  get  a good look at the chips? That's the real metric. Aye, it was rammed. Loads of students, obviously. Proper queue stretching down the street. I was there for about forty minutes just to get a portion. Forty minutes for chips. You know how I feel about chips. I do. It’s a borderline religious experience for you. So, were they worth the wait? Be honest. Don't let your chip devotion cloud your judgement. They were…okay. Honestly, a bit disappointing. Not enough salt. And the batter wasn’t  crisp  crisp, y’know? More like… gently warmed. I’ve had better from Greggs, and that’s saying something. Greggs? Now  that’s  a low blow. You’ve officially downgraded the entire chip-eating experience. I’m just being realistic! I had built it up in my head, this legendary chippy everyone raves about. It just didn’t live up to the hype. Right. So, the rumour is busted. The myth debunked. Still better than a motorway service station chip though, right? That's the baseline. Oh, aye, definitely better than a service station chip. No competition there. Although, I did have a surprisingly decent one at…what’s that place near Cambridge, with the weird sculptures? The American diner? The one shaped like a giant dinosaur? That’s the one! I was starving, to be fair, and it was like 2am. Their chips were actually pretty good. And the milkshakes were…dangerous. Dangerous in a good way or a ‘need a lie down afterwards’ way? Both, honestly. Like, sugar rush-induced existential crisis good. I swear I saw a cartoon giraffe for a bit. You are making that up. I swear! It might have been the lack of sleep. Or the sheer quantity of sugar. Anyway, it was a bizarre night. We ended up singing karaoke with a truck driver. Oh my god. You’re always getting into these situations. It's a gift. I'm just wishing I had been there to witness the cartoon giraffe and the karaoke truck driver. Did you manage to get a decent coffee then, after that ordeal?

This weather, eh? Proper miserable. Been like it all week. Not a drop of sun. It is a bit grey, isn’t it? Makes you feel a bit sluggish, doesn’t it? I swear my joints ache more when it’s damp. You’re telling me! My vitamin D levels must be plummeting. I feel like a bear needing hibernation already. Though, lecturing online in a dimly lit room doesn’t exactly help. Tell me about it. Had a student fall asleep mid-sentence today. Not ideal. Probably the weather though, honestly. Everyone’s a bit…deflated. My knees are playing up again. Doctor says it’s the arthritis. Just getting old, I suppose. She’s put me on some new tablets though. Says they’ll help with the pain. Oh, good. Anything that eases it is worth a go. You were struggling, weren't you, getting up the stairs? Couldn’t do it without clinging onto the banister, I tell you. Like a mountain climber. These new pills… they make me a bit sleepy though. That's often the side effect, isn’t it? Trade one problem for another. Still, better to be sleepy than in pain, I guess. Yeah, although being sleepy and trying to explain post-structuralism to undergraduates is… challenging. Oh dear. You have my sympathy. Speaking of challenging, young Thomas next door showed me his new television. Massive thing. All curved screen and flashing lights. I can’t even work the remote on ours, let alone something like that! They’re all getting too clever for their own good, those things. All smart this, smart that. I just want to watch the football. And even  that’s  complicated now. All these different channels, different times… Dad, you’re sounding like a proper curmudgeon. But I do get it. It’s overwhelming. I spend half an hour just trying to navigate streaming services. It's the algorithms, isn't it? Designed to keep you scrolling indefinitely. It's a conspiracy. Conspiracy, eh? That’s what they want you to think! I tell you what’s a conspiracy - Norwich losing to Millwall last weekend. Absolute robbery! The referee was blind as a bat. Oh, don’t start on the football, dear. It’ll only raise your blood pressure. You need to relax. Relax? With my team getting cheated out of a win? Never! Still, maybe these tablets will help.

Honestly, the wedding planning is… a lot. I thought I was organised, but then you start looking at flowers and suddenly you’re questioning all your life choices. Oh, tell me about it. Even picking a bloody colour scheme feels monumental. Are you sticking with the rustic vibe? Rustic is  so  last year, isn't it? Everything's boho now. Loads of pampas grass, macrame... Seriously? I thought rustic was having a moment. Though, to be fair, I’m mostly living in sweatpants and haven’t paid attention to wedding trends since… well, ever. I don’t want  all  pampas grass, it'll look like a hay bale exploded. But I get the vibe. It’s just…expensive. And Mark keeps saying "as long as you're happy" which is sweet, but also unhelpful when I'm debating the merits of hydrangeas versus peonies. Men. Bless them. Leo just offered to 'help' with the seating plan. Apparently, he thinks sorting people by height is a good idea. Oh my god. That's… a choice. Is he still seeing Chloe? I haven’t heard anything. Nope. It fizzled out. Something about him “needing space”. Which, let’s be real, means he got bored and found someone else to “need space” with. Ugh, boys. Honestly, are any of them capable of actual commitment? Don’t even get me started. My cousin, Sarah, just announced she’s pregnant. They’ve been together six months. Six! I’m happy for her, obviously, but I’m also slightly terrified for her. Wow. That’s… fast. Is she working? She was, but she’s had to quit. She was a teacher, actually. Said the morning sickness was awful. Oh, poor thing. That must be so stressful. Are you still on for dinner on Friday? I managed to get a table at that new Italian place, "Bella Notte". Ooh, yes! I’ve heard good things. I’m in. Need to escape the world of colour corrections and resolution nightmares for a few hours. Work is driving me insane. Count me in too. I need a proper catch-up. I haven't seen you both properly in ages. Have you seen what Amy's been posting on Instagram? She's in Bali. No way! I thought she said she couldn’t afford a holiday? She was complaining about her boiler last week! Amy and her ‘broke but travelling’ lifestyle.

Honestly, this new telly… it’s got more buttons than a spaceship. I swear, I spend more time trying to find a programme than actually watching it. Oh, I know the feeling, Arthur. My granddaughter tried to set up one of those streaming things for me, all those Netflixes and Amazons… My head spun! Ended up sticking to the radio, much simpler. It  is  a bit much, isn’t it? The kids at school are all fluent in this stuff, though. They’re teaching  me  new shortcuts sometimes! Though, frankly, I just want to know how to show a historical documentary without navigating five menus. Shortcuts! Ha! I just wish it'd remember what channel I last watched. It always goes back to news, and I’ve had enough of that doom and gloom, thank you very much. Reminds me of young Daniel, always getting into mischief. He’d change all the channels when I was trying to watch the racing. Daniel’s a lovely boy, though, isn't he? Grown into such a fine young man. Though I still remember when he convinced your poor Bessie the horse he could fly. Oh, don’t remind me! Bessie nearly had a heart attack. He was running around the field flapping his arms, shouting about being a superhero. She just looked at him like he'd lost his marbles. Horses, eh? They see it all. They do have a way of looking right through you. My wife’s sister has a couple, she's always talking about the expense. Hay, vets, shoes… it all adds up. I’m glad I stuck to books. Less feeding required. Speaking of expense… young Sarah sent me a message. Wants money for her daughter’s school trip. France, it is. Fancy! When I was a lad, a school trip was a bus ride to Great Yarmouth. It’s hard, isn't it? They all want the best for their children, of course, but everything is so expensive. I used to help out with the childminding fund, but even that's stretched now. It’s a worry, honestly. Tell me about it. Education funding's a nightmare at school. Trying to get resources for the kids... it's constantly battling. And the paperwork! Honestly, it rivals your telly for button overload. I used to love the teaching, but the administrative side is… draining. You always were a hard worker, lad.

Honestly, the kids were driving me round the bend today. Year nine are… a special breed, aren't they? Full of energy, mostly directed at disrupting my attempts to explain the subjunctive. Oh, teenagers. Always have been, always will be. I remember my son, Alan, at that age. Thought he knew everything. Wouldn't listen to a word I said. Though, I suspect he knew more about electronics than I ever would! He was always tinkering with something. It's the constant need to test boundaries, I think. It’s exhausting! Still, some of them are lovely. I’ve got a few who are really enthusiastic about languages. One girl is already planning to learn Japanese after GCSEs. Good for her! It's good to have ambition. What languages do you teach, anyway? French and Spanish, I presume? French and German, actually. I did a year abroad in Berlin, and it completely changed my perspective. Although, German grammar still haunts my dreams. I can imagine! I never had much head for languages myself. Tried a little French on holiday once, resulted in a rather embarrassing order at a restaurant. Ended up with a plateful of snails when I thought I was asking for chicken. Oh dear! That’s a classic mistake. You have to be careful with those false friends. Have you been on holiday recently, by the way? I remember you and Margaret used to go to Spain every year. We did for years, but not for a while now. Margaret isn’t quite up to the travel these days, sadly. We’ve been doing more little trips around the country. Went to Stratford-upon-Avon last month, lovely little town. I’ve taken up sketching again, you know. Trying to recapture my youth, I suppose. Oh, that’s lovely! I used to dabble in painting, but haven’t had much time for hobbies since starting my Masters. Which reminds me, I'm still wading through research papers on sociolinguistics. It's fascinating, but also… a lot. Sounds demanding. What are your weekend plans? Anything exciting? Not particularly. Just catching up on marking, I think. And maybe a long walk with the dog if the weather holds up. What about you? Alan’s coming round with the grandchildren on Saturday. Always a lively affair. Little Emily’s just started learning to play the piano, so we'll be subjected to a recital, I expect.

Honestly, that was the most… underwhelming Valentine’s Day ever. Like, seriously. Tell me about it! I was expecting… something. Anything. Even a cheesy card would’ve been nice. Instead, it was just… normal. Normal?! Mine was actively worse than normal. My flatmate’s boyfriend got her roses, chocolates, the whole shebang. And then  my  boyfriend just… suggested we order pizza and watch a documentary about pigeons. Pigeons?! Really? I’m not even joking! I tried to subtly hint that maybe, just maybe, going to the cinema or even a slightly nicer restaurant than the uni canteen might be good. But no. Pigeons. Oh my god. That  is  bad. I mean, what's wrong with pigeons? They're just… birds. But on Valentine’s Day? A firm no. Did you at least like the pizza? It was alright. But it just felt like a regular Friday night, which is kind of the point, isn’t it? It’s supposed to be  special . We were talking about going to see that new horror film, ‘The Shadow Watchers’ this weekend, though. That’s something, at least. Ooh, I’ve heard good things about that one! Properly scary, apparently. I’m more of a rom-com girl, myself, but I’ll make an exception. What about you, any weekend plans besides terrifying yourself at the cinema? Just a bit of shopping, I think. Need a new pair of jeans. Everything I own is either falling apart or has a stain on it. The life of a student. What about you? My mum's making me go with her to that new Vietnamese place downtown. She’s obsessed. Apparently, it’s “authentic.” I’m worried it’s going to be really spicy. My spice tolerance is… minimal. Oh no. That's a genuine problem. My sister took me to this Indian restaurant once, and I genuinely cried. The waiter thought I was having an existential crisis. Oh gosh! See, this is why I’m anxious. My mum will be all, "Oh, you're not embracing the culture!" and I'll be secretly chugging water. Honestly, just order something bland. Noodle soup is usually a safe bet. And hey, at least you're being treated to dinner. My boyfriend would probably suggest we make instant ramen. Oh,  lovely . Instant ramen with a side of pigeons. You deserve better, honestly! Although, I do love your accent, it's so…London.

Honestly, the audacity of that MP to say… honestly. It’s just… breathtaking, isn’t it? Breathtakingly awful, you mean. Right? Like, the complete disconnect. He was talking about ‘cultural integration’ as if it’s a one-way street. As if people arriving  here  are the ones who need to change, and not… well, not look at the systemic racism baked into everything. Exactly! And the way he framed it, it wasn’t even a dog whistle, it was a full-on foghorn. I mean, I’m trying to enjoy these dan dan noodles – and they  are  good, by the way, did you ask for extra chilli? – but it’s just… grinding. Yeah, extra chilli. Needed it. And I know what you mean. It’s hard to switch off. It’s like, you’re trying to have a nice evening and then BAM, you’re reminded that half the country thinks like that. It just makes you want to shout into the void. It does! And it bleeds into everything, doesn’t it? Even work. I was in a meeting today, and one of the senior partners was going on about “preserving the character of the neighbourhood” when we’re talking about a redevelopment project in Brixton. Like, “character” is code for “keeping it gentrified”. Ugh, the architecture world is rife with that, isn’t it? It’s always ‘heritage’ or ‘character’ but it never really acknowledges  whose  heritage,  whose  character is being erased in the process. It’s all so… performative. It is! And it’s exhausting constantly having to navigate that. Like, I genuinely want to create beautiful spaces, but I don’t want to contribute to displacing communities. It feels impossible sometimes. What about you? Any workplace dramas? Oh, always. I’m pitching a piece on the housing crisis, specifically focusing on social cleansing in Southwark. And my editor keeps pushing back, saying it’s “too politically charged”. Too politically charged! It’s literally people being forced out of their homes! Seriously? What a joke. It's all about who owns the land and who benefits, isn't it? This whole system… I swear, sometimes I think capitalism is just a sophisticated pyramid scheme. Entirely. It’s designed to concentrate wealth at the top, and then pretend it’s all about meritocracy. And the housing market is just the most blatant example. I was looking at places in Kensal Rise the other day – just out of morbid curiosity – and a one-bed flat is going for nearly two grand a month.

Right, so nursery starts Monday. Honestly, I’m a wreck. Oh Mum, you’ll be fine! He’ll love it. Remember how much he loved the taster sessions? That was different, wasn't it? I was  there . Him being completely left with strangers… it's just a bit much. And what if he cries all day? They said they’ll ring, but… They understand. They’re used to it. And honestly, he's such a sociable little thing, he’ll be fine. It's  you  who needs to get used to the idea. Easy for you to say, you’re not the one facing going back to work! I feel like all my brain cells have turned to mush in the last year. It won’t be that bad! You’re brilliant at your job, you’ll fall straight back into it. Plus, it'll be good for you, won't it? To have something for  you  again. Hmm, maybe. Still feels… daunting. Especially with sorting out childcare and everything. Speaking of which, have you any plans for summer? With uni finishing and all? Not really concrete plans, no. I was thinking maybe a little trip somewhere. Somewhere hot. I'm desperate for some sun. Oh, that sounds lovely! We were talking about maybe a week in Cornwall, but with nursery starting it feels like there's no money left. Cornwall’s nice! A bit… chill, maybe? I was thinking something a bit more exciting. Maybe Croatia? Or Greece? Croatia! Ooh, that’s a bit ambitious isn’t it? Why? I can save up a bit before then. I’ve been picking up extra shifts at the pub. That's good, love. Just don't overdo it. You need to focus on your dissertation too. Anyway, we’ll see. First, we need to get through Monday. Right, let's talk about food. He’s been a bit… fussy lately. I'm thinking of pushing the weaning a bit further. Oh yeah? What were you thinking? He’s still mostly squishing everything, isn’t he? Yeah, but he’s starting to actually  swallow  some of it. I was thinking of introducing some slightly lumpier textures. Maybe mashed sweet potato with a bit of chicken. Sounds good. As long as it’s not too much at once. You don’t want him choking. Absolutely not. Small steps. And speaking of small steps, I need to actually choose what to wear tomorrow.

Honestly, the day has been… a lot. I swear, every time I think I’ve finished one thing, another three pop up. Tell me about it. Though, I’m not sure mine qualifies as ‘a lot’ compared to potentially… you know. The police station. Oh, right, how did that go? Dreadful, I imagine? I was thinking about you all afternoon. It wasn’t as bad as I feared, actually. Just a formal statement, really. They were very polite. Though the questions… going over it all again and again. It’s exhausting. Did they get anywhere with it then? Do they have any leads? Not that they let on. Said they’re following up a few things, but nothing concrete. Apparently, the CCTV wasn't brilliant. Figures. Standard, isn’t it? CCTV always seems to be pointing the wrong way, or blurry, or conveniently ‘having a technical difficulty’. Exactly! It’s just… infuriating. At least you got it over with, though. Anything else stressful happen today? Aside from the obvious. Just the EE bill. They’ve charged me for data I didn’t use! Again. Honestly, it’s a monthly battle. I swear they just make stuff up. Oh, they're notorious for that! You have to really scrutinise it and call them up and argue. It’s such a waste of time. It is. They rely on people just not bothering. I had a similar issue with British Gas last month. It's a con, frankly. It’s designed to be opaque, isn’t it? To confuse people and get away with overcharging. It’s infuriating. Right, who’s thinking about plans for the week? I feel like we haven’t properly caught up in ages. I’m fairly booked, work-wise. Big project deadline on Friday. But I might be able to sneak out Wednesday evening. Wednesday’s good for me. I promised I'd help Mrs. Davies with her garden, but I can reschedule. I’m on a late shift Wednesday, unfortunately. But Thursday I’m free! Thursday works. We could go to that new Italian place in town? I heard it’s really good. Ooh, yes! That sounds lovely. I’ve been craving pasta. Italian sounds fantastic. Though, I’m still on a mission to find a decent fish and chip shop around here. It’s a struggle, I tell you. You’re not wrong. Lichfield’s chip shops are… lacking.

Honestly, the wedding was… a lot. Beautiful, obviously, she looked incredible, but  a lot . Aunt Carol cornered me for a solid forty minutes about the best way to grow runner beans. No way! Aunt Carol and her runner beans. That's classic. She’s a force of nature, that one. Still, glad it went well, even with botanical interrogations. How’s married life treating you so far? It’s… adjusting. It’s mostly just remembering I have to consult another human being before making decisions. Like, “Can I buy that ridiculously oversized Star Wars Lego set?” Used to be a given. Now it’s a negotiation. The trials and tribulations of matrimony. Speaking of ridiculously large things, have you seen the new season of  House of the Dragon ? They’ve really gone to town on the dragons this time. I’ve been meaning to! Been a bit swamped. But I caught a trailer. It looked… intense. Still, nothing beats a good historical epic. I’ve been re-watching some documentaries on the Roman Empire. Did you know they used chickpea flour as a cheap substitute for wheat flour during shortages? No way! Seriously? That’s mental. Makes you think differently about hummus, doesn’t it? It was a survival food. I was reading about the logistical nightmares of keeping armies fed back then. Must have needed a constant supply of, well, everything. Like trying to keep my van stocked with different composts. Exactly! And the sanitation. Can you imagine the sea lice problems the soldiers had if they were travelling by sea? And malarial mosquitoes. It’s a wonder anyone lived to a decent age back then. Although, honestly, thinking about some of the rock stars who check out young… seems like not much has changed. True. Hendrix, Joplin, Morrison… gone way too soon. Speaking of checking out, have you seen what’s happened with that bloke, what’s his name… the one who played Spartacus? Andy Whitfield, wasn’t it? Apparently, he died pretty young, some kind of cancer. Oh, that's awful. I remember him being brilliant in that show. It’s depressing when someone so physically vital… goes. Makes you appreciate every cup of tea, I suppose. You making any interesting brews lately? Actually, yeah! I’ve been experimenting with different herbs and spices. Got a fantastic mix with cardamom, cloves, and a bit of cinnamon. Makes a really warming brew.

Ugh, honestly, English was  brutal  today. Mrs. Davies is obsessed with metaphors. Like, everything is a metaphor to her! Tell me about it! I completely blanked on the question about the symbolism in “The Raven”. I wrote something about… a black bird being sad? I don’t even know. Oh, no! That’s… not great. I think I managed to scrape by, but I spent the whole time trying to figure out if a cloud was a metaphor for sadness or just… a cloud. Seriously! And it’s like, can’t we just analyze the story without dissecting every single detail? It's exhausting. Exactly! Although, Art was actually really good today. We’re starting a new project – painting landscapes. I’m thinking of doing one of Grantchester Meadows. Ooh, nice! I’m doing the Botanic Garden, I think. It’s got so many interesting colours. Mr. Henderson said we can use watercolour  and  acrylics. Fancy! We're just watercolour. He said acrylics are "too messy for Year 9s". Honestly, he treats us like babies. He does, doesn’t he? Speaking of treating us like babies, French is just… pointless. Madame Dubois keeps trying to make us role-play ordering croissants. Who even  does  that?! I know! And her pronunciation is so fast! It’s like trying to understand a swarm of bees. Did you hear Sophie Thompson actually understood everything today? No way! Sophie? She's usually the one asking what ‘Bonjour’ means. I know, right?! She was suddenly fluent. I swear she’s been secretly taking lessons. It’s so unfair. Maybe. Or maybe she just crammed really hard. Anyway, what about wind band rehearsal on Thursday? Are you still up for it? Definitely! I’m actually really excited about the new piece Mr. Peterson chose. It’s got a really cool flute part. Oh good! I'm a bit worried about the trumpet section, though. Liam keeps messing up the high notes, and it sounds like a strangled goose.  laughs  Oh, Liam. He tries so hard. But yeah, it’s… rough. Have you seen Emily Carter lately? She’s been really quiet. Yeah, I haven't really. I think she's upset about something. Apparently, she and Ben had a massive argument after the history lesson on Tuesday. Oh, no! Really? What happened? I think it was about him liking Chloe Miller’s Instagram post. Apparently, it was a really flirty one.

Honestly, Doreen, this latte is lukewarm. Lukewarm! For nearly four quid, you'd think they could manage a bit of heat, wouldn't you? Mmm? Oh, yeah, fair enough. It is a bit…beige. Beige is a good word for it, actually. It’s the colour of disappointment, that is. And four quid! Daylight robbery, that is. Remember when you could get a decent brew for fifty pence? Aye, and a biscuit with it! Now, you're looking well, lad. Still playing rugby? I saw young Thomas Thompson down at the pub last week; he says you're like a whirlwind on the pitch. Yeah, still going. We lost on Saturday, though. Terrible ref. Said I was offside about twenty times. Honestly, I was miles onside. Referees! Always have been a law unto themselves. Your grandad used to say they were paid to make the wrong decisions. Your grandad said a lot of things, Margaret. Half of them involved a fishing story and exaggerating the size of the catch. He did love a good tale, didn’t he? Now, what about this new school of yours, Liam? Is it any good? They say it’s all tablets and interactive whiteboards. It’s alright. The tablets are…okay. Mostly just use them for research. Miss Davies keeps going on about ‘digital literacy’ and ‘future-proofing’. It’s a bit boring, to be honest. I’d rather just have a textbook. Digital literacy! Honestly. They’ll be teaching them to code before they can spell their own names. It’s all a fad, mark my words. Don’t be so sure, Brenda. It’s the way the world’s going. Though, I still can’t get my head around TikTok. All that dancing. It’s not  all  dancing, Mum. There's, like, funny stuff and…life hacks. Life hacks? What on earth are life hacks? Just little tips and tricks. Like, how to peel a mango perfectly, or how to tie your shoelaces really fast. So, basically, things people have known for centuries? Honestly, the branding. That’s what gets me. ‘Life hacks’. Marketing, pure and simple. Speaking of branding, did you see that new flag they designed for the local council? An absolute disaster. Looked like a toddler had been let loose with a paintbrush. Oh yeah, saw that on Facebook. Everyone was having a go. Apparently, it cost them fifteen grand!

Honestly, Dad, you drive like a maniac. I swear every time I’m in the car with you, I’m convinced I’m going to end up in a ditch. Now, don’t be daft, love. I’m a perfectly competent driver. Been driving for fifty years, haven’t I? A few… adjustments to my speed, perhaps, but perfectly capable. He’s getting a bit reckless in his old age, isn’t he? And he insists on taking those country lanes like he’s competing in a rally. It's a wonder he hasn’t had a prang, honestly. Though, I suppose a bit of speed keeps him young. Speaking of which, Mum, you’ve made a lovely roast. Though maybe a  little  much gravy? Oh, don’t start on the gravy, David. People need to enjoy their food. It’s not like anyone here is worrying about their weight. That’s a bit of a generalization, Mum. Some of us are mindful. It’s just… the obesity crisis is real, isn’t it? And portion sizes are a huge part of the problem. Obesity? Rubbish. People just aren’t as active anymore. All this sitting around glued to screens. In my day, we were outside playing football until dark. Built up a proper appetite that way. It’s a little more complex than that, Dad. Genetics play a role, metabolic rates… it’s not just about being lazy. Your Uncle Bernard, bless him, was always a big man. Ate everything in sight. And he lived to be eighty-five, fit as a fiddle. Didn’t seem to harm him at all. Though, he was a very religious man, you know. Went to church every Sunday. Believed it kept him healthy. I’m not convinced religion has much to do with physical health, Mum. Though, a strong community can definitely contribute to wellbeing. Always thought it was a load of old… well, never mind. Talking about health, I’m still waiting to hear about that biopsy result. Bit worried, I am. They said it could take a few weeks, didn’t they? Try not to fret, Dad. You’re a tough old bird. It’s just… the waiting is the worst part. It’s like a dark cloud hanging over everything. I was telling one of my students about it, and she was saying she’s severely allergic to nuts. Absolutely terrifying.

Right, so I’ve been battling with Moodle all morning. Honestly, it’s like it actively  wants  me to fail. Oh no, what’s up? Is it the assignment submission bit again? That always seems to be a problem. Worse, actually. It’s the grade release. I uploaded all the feedback, everything’s marked, and now it’s refusing to properly release the grades to the students. It’s showing some as ‘not submitted’ even though they definitely submitted, and others are just…blank. That’s infuriating. Did you check the override settings? Sometimes it gets stuck in override mode and ignores the actual submissions. Yes! Checked that first thing. Multiple times. I’ve gone through the manual, watched three YouTube tutorials, and even contacted IT, who were predictably unhelpful. “Have you tried refreshing the page?” was the height of their technical expertise. Ugh, classic. They always say that. It's just...it feels deliberately obtuse, doesn’t it? Like the designers were actively trying to make it as user-unfriendly as possible. Exactly! It's not intuitive at all. I spent an hour trying to figure out how to bulk release grades, and it turned out you have to release them individually. Individually! For a class of eighty students! Seriously? That's…bizarre. You'd think they’d have a ‘release all’ function. Did you try exporting the grades to a spreadsheet and then re-importing them? Sometimes that forces it to recognize everything. I did. Twice. Both times it messed up the formatting and created even  more  errors. Honestly, I’m starting to think I’m cursed by Moodle. Don’t say that! You're a perfectly competent lecturer, it’s just a terrible piece of software. Look, I had a similar issue last semester with the quiz functionality. It kept marking answers wrong that were perfectly correct. Turns out there was a hidden character in one of the answer options. A hidden character? How does that even happen? No idea! It was a rogue space or something. It took me ages to find. It’s just… you have to be so meticulous with everything. One tiny little error and the whole thing falls apart. I wish they’d just invest in something decent. Something that doesn’t feel like it was built in the 90s. Blackboard seems so much more streamlined. I’ve heard. But, you know, universities and their legacy systems.

Honestly, I still feel like I’m on Californian time. Woke up at five this morning feeling properly alert. Useless. Oh, bless you. It’ll pass. Though you were impressively functional in that faculty meeting. I was bracing for complete jetlag-induced rambling. I think the adrenaline of having to defend my module changes helped. Did you catch Professor Davies’ face when I said we were incorporating TikTok analysis? Priceless. Absolutely priceless. He looked like you’d suggested teaching ancient history via interpretive dance. Speaking of which, have you booked tickets for the Mill Theatre?  A Midsummer Night’s Dream ? Nearly! I was just about to. They had a couple of decent seats left in the front row, but they’re a bit pricey. Do you think it’s worth it? Or should we go for something further back? Front row sounds amazing! It's a small theatre, even further back won’t feel  that  far. Plus, you know how Mrs. Higgins loves to wave at the actors. True. She’s a dedicated theatregoer. So, front row it is. Thursday or Friday evening? Let’s do Friday. I have that grant application deadline on Thursday, so I’ll be a bit of a stress-head. Friday feels… lighter. Good plan. And we can grab a bite beforehand at The Old Mill? Perfect. Right, let’s get it booked. Though, honestly, having a quiet evening in is starting to sound tempting after the conference. I know, right? It was good, genuinely insightful, but a week of networking and forced cheerfulness is exhausting. Tell me about it. And all the talk about ‘work-life balance’ while everyone’s glued to their phones until midnight. Hypocritical, much? Terribly. Still, I did pick up some interesting ideas for the new curriculum. And I met a professor from UCLA who’s doing amazing things with digital humanities. Oh, that’s good! Maybe a collaboration? Possibly. It’s early days. Everything feels… surreal still. It feels like ages since we were discussing baby names and hideous nursery wallpaper. Feels like another lifetime. Though, if we’re honest, baby names are still a minefield. Honestly, Mabel? I know! Your mum's suggestion. Bless her. Though, I did quietly veto Barnaby. Good. Absolutely good. Barnaby is… a lot. It's all a bit overwhelming when you start thinking about it properly, isn’t it? It’s very different to preparing a lecture on post-structuralism.

…and honestly, the whole thing with Omar’s visa has been a complete nightmare. He's been waiting six months now just for an interview. Six months! You’d think with his background, being a qualified engineer… Six months? That’s…that’s ridiculous. Is it the UK visa, or to go somewhere else? To come  here . To visit. He wants to see his niece, little Layla. She’s just started walking. You know, he FaceTimes her every day, but it’s not the same. Bureaucracy, eh? It's infuriating. I’ve written to my MP, everything. It is. It’s always the same story. Red tape. I’m still trying to sort out my cousin’s paperwork. His wife is stuck in Dohuk. It’s not easy. Especially with… well, everything going on. Everything  is  going on, isn’t it? It’s hard to know where to even begin sometimes. Still, it’s good you're helping him. Family's important. Absolutely. And my cousin… he's a good man. He was working with an NGO, helping rebuild schools after the fighting. It’s complicated though. A lot of the money… it gets diverted. You know, the politics of oil, the Wahabi influence… it's a tangled web. Oh, don’t even get me started on the Wahabi influence. I was reading a piece about Libya the other day, and it’s utterly bleak. The youth, especially, have so few opportunities. Radicalization is almost inevitable when you’re offering them nothing but poverty and despair. That’s true. That’s a big part of it. And young people, they’re very easily influenced. Especially when they see corruption everywhere. They lose faith in everything. It's why so many are trying to leave, risk everything to get to Europe. Exactly. It's heartbreaking. Speaking of leaving, we’re actually thinking of moving. Oh? Really? Where to? We’re looking at… well, it’s a bit out there, but we’ve seen a place near Formby. It’s a bit more space for the kids, a slightly bigger garden. And closer to the coast. We’re spending so much time driving now, ferrying them around to different clubs and activities, it's exhausting. Formby, nice. It’s a bit of a trek for me, though. I usually meet people in town for coffee. Yeah, it is a bit further out. But we’ll still have to see each other, of course.

This lamb is absolutely lovely, honestly. You’ve outdone yourself. Glad you think so. It’s a shoulder, you know, a bit more flavour than the leg, I find. And a bargain. It  is  delicious. Though I do think a roast needs a proper Yorkshire pudding. You haven’t made one in ages, have you? I haven't, no. I just…can’t be bothered, to be honest. It's so much effort for something that gets devoured in five minutes. True. Though a really good Yorkshire pudding… It elevates everything! We always had them, naturally. My mother would have considered it a sacrilege to serve a roast without them. Times change, eh? Speaking of changing things… still thinking about getting a telly for the dining room? I am. Just a small one, for watching the news with dinner. Makes it feel a bit more…civilised. A television in the  dining room ? Good heavens! What has the world come to? It’ll completely ruin any conversation. Oh, come on, Mum. We’re perfectly capable of talking  and  watching the news. Hmmph. I still think it's dreadful. Though I must say, your brother sent me some Scottish tablet the other day. Now  that  was a treat. Truly authentic. Not like the stuff you get in the shops. He's a good lad, your brother. Sending tablet all the way from Edinburgh. Reminds me, have you two started looking at cruises again? You mentioned wanting to go somewhere warm. We’ve been browsing, yes. Nothing concrete yet. The Caribbean is appealing, but it seems terribly…touristy. We were looking at a Mediterranean one. Italy, Greece, all that lovely history. Though I need to get my stamina up first. I’ve started doing those chair-based workouts again. Good for you! Keep moving, that's the key. I'm trying to walk the dog more, but he’s a lazy old thing. Refuses to go further than the end of the garden some days. Old age, I suppose. It catches up with us all. Speaking of catching up… have you heard anything more from the landlord about fixing the leaky roof? Nothing. I’ve texted him twice this week. He just ignores me. Honestly, the man's a nightmare. I'm starting to think we should just move. Rented accommodation is such a lottery, isn't it? You're at the mercy of these people.

Right, so I genuinely think I could live off pasta forever. It’s the perfect food, innit? Cheap, easy… practically a full nutritional profile. You say that now, Liam, but you'll be craving a proper meal in a week. You’ve been on pasta on a budget since, like, September. It’s… a choice. Though honestly, my Mum’s Sunday dinners are a major source of motivation for going home. Aye, Brenda’s roasts are legendary. Seriously, she could open a restaurant. Though, knowing her, she’d just offer everyone a free pudding. She’s a gem, that woman. But back to the pasta situation. I’m considering adding tinned tuna. Elevate the experience, you know? You’re descending into madness. You need to expand your culinary horizons. Have you even  considered  frozen veg? Frozen veg… a radical concept. It would require freezer space, wouldn’t it? This flat is already a logistical nightmare. Speaking of which, how’s the hunt for a new place going, Chloe? Slow. Ridiculously slow. Everything is either tiny, expensive, or both. And landlords? Don’t even get me started. One tried to tell me a damp patch was “character”. Oh, that’s awful. They always try and pull something. Have you looked further out, like towards Cleator Moor? I have. It's a bit…distant. And everything feels so isolated. It's hard to get to Uni from there. Plus, I kinda like being able to walk into town, even if it’s just to look at Boots. Fair enough. The buses are a joke anyway. Remember when we were kids and you could get anywhere for a quid? Golden age of public transport, that was. Speaking of golden ages… anyone hear from Ben lately? Haven’t seen him since… well, ages. He messaged me last week. He's swamped with work at the pub. Apparently, it's mad busy with tourists at the moment. He’s thinking about doing an extra shift to save up for a new guitar. Good for him. He's always wanted a Fender Strat. He's a good lad, Ben. Always willing to lend a hand. Unlike some people I know, who've been “meaning to” help me fix my car for three months now.  Looks pointedly at Liam  Hey! I’ve been busy! Existential dread is a demanding taskmaster, alright? Besides, I don’t even  own  any tools.

Right, so I was thinking, for the lesson on Friday, we could actually  make  the biscuits. Rather than just talking about recipes. Ooh, yes! Can I decorate them? With sprinkles?  Lots  of sprinkles? And icing! Can we have icing too? Like on the ones Grandma makes? Sprinkles and icing are a definite yes. But, it’s a Year 3 class, remember? We need to keep it vaguely educational. So, we can talk about weighing things, measuring, following instructions… That sounds… boring. It’s not boring! It's science! And maths! And…domestic goddess training! Look, we can make animal biscuits. Elephants, lions… Can we make dinosaurs? Hmm. Perhaps. If we have time. It’s a bit tricky to get dinosaur shapes. What did you get up to today, you two? Anything exciting? I levelled up my apartment in Tomodachi Life! My Mii character got a bigger bed. I got a new dinosaur figure! A Triceratops! It’s  massive . Lovely! Did you manage to find that book I asked you to look for in Morrisons, darling? The one about the little bear? Oh! Yes! It was right at the bottom, behind all the cookery books. It was a bit dusty. Oh, brilliant! Thank you. Year 3 are obsessed with bears at the moment. Speaking of which, did you see that leaflet for the half-birthday party at the community centre? Half-birthday? What’s that? Well, it’s a party to celebrate being halfway through the year. You know, because birthdays are only once a year. It's a bit silly, really. But they’re doing face painting. Ooh! Can we go? Can we, can we? We’ll see. It’s next Saturday. We might be visiting Nana and Grandad. I promised. Have you read any good books lately? I’m trying to get back into reading, but I keep falling asleep. I’m reading about space! It's got pictures of planets and rockets. I’m reading a chapter book! All by myself! About a girl who finds a magic unicorn. It's got glitter on the cover. Actually, it's a really good book, even if it  does  have glitter. That sounds lovely. Maybe we can visit the library this weekend. They've got loads of new books in, I saw. And I need to return this one. It's about… oh, what  is  this one about? It’s about a detective who solves crimes with his pet hamster.

Honestly, the state of Facebook now. It’s just… endless political arguments and people sharing those infuriating chain letters. Tell me about it. I nearly unfriended Aunt Carol last week. She shared one about how 5G causes… well, you know. The usual. Oh,  no . Luckily my family mostly stick to pictures of grandchildren and aggressively enthusiastic holiday snaps. Keeps it relatively sane. Though Dad did share a meme about Boris Johnson once. I had to intervene. It's a minefield. I mostly use it to stalk old school friends and see who's having a mid-life crisis and buying a sports car. Speaking of sports cars… Did you see Mark from Accounts has got a new one? A bright red Mustang. It's… a choice. A Mustang? In Norwich? Where’s he going to  drive  it, the bypass? Seriously though, that’s a bit… showy, isn’t it? Especially for someone who still brings packed lunches in Tupperware. Exactly! It’s like he’s trying to compensate for something. Probably feels undervalued in the department. Or maybe he just won the lottery and is determined to live his best cliché life. Maybe both. He always did have a penchant for American excess. Remember when he tried to order a supersized portion of everything at that diner in London? Oh god, yes! The waitress looked genuinely terrified. He ended up leaving most of it. It was a logistical nightmare. Speaking of things that are a logistical nightmare, have you tried getting decent internet out here? I spent half an hour just loading a simple email this morning. Don’t even  start  me. It’s atrocious. For a supposedly rural idyll, the broadband is shockingly slow. It's almost enough to make me long for the London tube. Almost. I know, right? I tried to join a Zoom meeting with a colleague yesterday and it just kept cutting out. He thought I was speaking in code. Oh, dear. This area really needs an infrastructure upgrade. Although, I suspect they're too busy arguing about parking restrictions to worry about something as important as reliable internet access. Probably. It’s Norfolk. Progress comes at a glacial pace. Still, at least we have good pubs. And reasonably priced gin. That’s the spirit. Cheers to glacial progress and reasonably priced gin! Let’s just hope Mark doesn’t turn up in his Mustang.

Right, pass us the remote will you, Liv? Honestly, this thing is a mystery. Three hundred buttons and I still can’t just…turn the volume up. Just the red one, then the plus. Unless you want to go onto the guide. The guide? Why would I want the guide? I just want it  slightly  louder. You’re a whiz with these things. Seriously, you were operating a DVD player before you were ten. It’s logical. Red for power, plus and minus for volume. It’s not rocket science, Ben. Easy for you to say. Anyway, this film is…interesting. “Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs”. Honestly. It’s classic! Remember when we watched this on repeat when we were little? Vaguely. I mostly remember being desperate for a sandwich. And feeling slightly disturbed by the giant spaghetti tornado. It’s about unchecked ambition, Ben. And consumerism. Don’t dismiss it. Oh, here we go. A deep dive into the metaphorical significance of airborne spaghetti. You’ve been reading too much for uni. No, I’m just saying! It's a cautionary tale! He just wanted to make people happy, but he didn’t think about the consequences. Like, what happens when it  never  stops raining food? Probably a lot of obesity. And angry farmers. Speaking of consequences, I had a right nightmare at work today. Old Mrs. Higgins was complaining about the price of biscuits  again . Honestly, you’d think the end of the world was nigh. Seriously? Biscuits? Seriously. And then Gary spilled a whole display of fizzy drinks. It was chaos. I’m starting to think retail isn’t for me. Well, no one said it was glamorous. At least you're earning money. I'm just living off student loans and the occasional handout. Don’t sell yourself short. You’re smashing it at uni. And you’re getting loads of interesting stuff done in your art projects. Speaking of art, did you finish that piece you were working on? The…feminist one? I’m still working on it. It’s complicated. I’m trying to get the message across without being…preachy. Just trying to sound out the topics for our assignment. It’s about the male gaze, basically. How women are often depicted in art through a male perspective. And how  that  affects perceptions. Right. Sounds…heavy. It is! But important. It’s weird though, isn’t it, how different conversations are now?

So, you reckon they'll actually pull it off then? With the new regulations? Pull what off, lad? You’re flitting about like a bleedin’ bluebottle. The regulations for what? The football club, you know. Everton. With the new points deduction, and the stadium funding, the whole carry-on. Will they stay up? I’ve been reading all sorts of pessimistic punditry. Stay up? Aye, they'll stay up. They always do, don't they? Bit of a wobble every now and then, keeps things interesting. But they've got grit, Everton. Unlike some of these soft southern sides. Grit? I'm not so sure. It feels…different this time. It's not just on-pitch performance, it's all the financial turmoil. Reminds me a bit of the late nineties, actually. When everything felt a bit unstable. The nineties? You mean when Major was stumbling about, trying to keep the Tories together? That was a right mess. Thought Blair was a breath of fresh air at the time, didn’t we all? New Labour, promise of a new dawn… turned out to be a bit more complicated than that didn’t it. Complicated is putting it mildly. He was… persuasive, let's say. And the Iraq war… that casts a long shadow. Though, honestly, looking back, I’m not sure anyone had a good answer for Saddam Hussein. Aye, but did we need to go sticking our noses into everything? America calling the shots, like always. The government then, thought they were invincible, didn’t they. Thought they could sell us anything. That’s the danger of power, isn't it? And the spin. The constant spin. Remember ‘stakeholder society’? That was a brilliant bit of marketing, really. Sounded all inclusive, but basically meant everyone had a vested interest in propping up the system. Stakeholder… aye, sounds posh. More like ‘stakeholder in the problem’ to me. Used to pick up MPs in my cab back then. All flash suits and promises. Never saw any of it filter down to the fellas working on the docks, you know? That’s the rub, isn't it? The disconnect. It’s still there, really. Look at the cost of living now. While they’re arguing about tax cuts for the wealthy, people are choosing between heating and eating. Aye, you’re right there. And they wonder why people are getting fed up. They need to spend a day driving a cab, listening to what people are  actually  worried about.

Honestly, I spent like, three hours yesterday just trawling through BNC recordings trying to find examples of specific discourse markers. It's… draining. Three hours? Oh, no. That sounds genuinely awful. What markers were you after, specifically? Still the ‘like’ and ‘you know’ obsession? It started with ‘like’, naturally. But then it spiralled into trying to quantify the use of ‘so’ at the beginning of clauses. It’s a rabbit hole, I tell you. A linguistic rabbit hole. Sounds riveting. Are you two still on about work on a Sunday? Sorry, Mum! No, we're just… commiserating. I’m complaining, mostly. How was your walk? Lovely, thank you. Saw a very handsome pug in Victoria Park. Honestly, I’m considering getting one. Though your father would have a fit. Oh, good luck convincing him! He's firmly a 'big dog' kind of man. Speaking of fits, I’m starting to think I need to seriously revamp my LinkedIn profile. Everyone seems to be landing amazing jobs, and mine feels… pathetic. Don’t! You’re brilliant at what you do. LinkedIn is just a highlight reel, remember? People only post the good stuff. And you’ve been nailing the editing, haven’t you? I have, yeah. It’s just… seeing everyone jetting off to conferences in the Maldives, or posting about their promotions… makes me feel a bit stuck. I really want to live abroad for a bit, you know? Like, Spain maybe. Oh, Spain would be amazing! You’d love it. The food, the people… you’d fit right in. Though, you’d have to learn to embrace the siesta. I could manage a siesta. It's just…the flying. I absolutely  hate  flying. It genuinely terrifies me. You and your father. He practically needs sedating before every flight. Though he’d never admit it. It's irrational, I know. I just… imagine everything that could go wrong. It's awful. Do you ever feel like that, Chloe? A little. But I'm mostly just scared of turbulence. It feels so… uncontrollable. I was reading an article about someone who’s started a whole social media account dedicated to debunking flying myths. Apparently, turbulence is rarely dangerous. Oh, interesting! Maybe I need to follow that. I'm spiralling already just thinking about booking a flight to Barcelona. Do you think Wales is nice? I’ve not really spent much time there.

Right, so I was thinking, maybe a bit more chilli in this? It feels a little…flat. A little flat is putting it mildly, darling. It tastes like tomato soup someone forgot to season. Definitely chilli. And maybe a squeeze of lime? Lime’s good. You always know what this needs. Seriously, you should be a chef. Don’t be silly. I just appreciate flavour. Speaking of flavour, did you ever get that tattoo you were talking about? The little fox? Oh, yeah! Got it done last week. On my inner forearm. It's…surprisingly painful. Oh, you poor thing! But worth it, I presume? Let me see… Here. Be gentle, it's still a bit tender. Oh, it’s  beautiful . Really delicate. Clever choice. You’ve gone for proper artist then? Not one of those backstreet places? Nah, proper studio in Shoreditch. Recommended by Maisie, actually. She had one done there a while back.  A knock at the door.  That’ll be Chloe. Right on time. She said she was escaping the chaos of Christmas planning.    Chloe, darling! Come in, come in. We’re attempting dinner, but it’s currently lacking…oomph. Chloe: Sounds about right. Smells delicious regardless. What’s the Christmas situation looking like? My mother is already asking about guest lists and whether Aunt Mildred is bringing her questionable fruitcake. Oh God, the fruitcake. That thing is a weapon. I’ve told my sister I’m handling the turkey this year. It's a risk, I haven't done a turkey in ages, but at least I can control the seasoning. Unlike this chilli, apparently. Hey! I’m adding the chilli now! It'll be perfect. So, Chloe, how’s work? Still drowning in submissions? Chloe: You have  no  idea. The interns are…enthusiastic, let's say. One sent me a manuscript entirely in Comic Sans.  Comic Sans.  I nearly lost it. Oh, the horror! You’re a saint, Chloe, you really are. Seriously? Comic Sans? That's…criminal. Is it a particularly terrible manuscript, at least? Chloe: It was a vampire romance, written entirely from the vampire’s perspective, detailing his struggles with online dating. It was… something. The cover was even worse. It looked like it was designed in MS Paint. Oh dear. Sounds like you need a very large glass of wine. Speaking of, I'm going to raid the wine rack. Anyone want a glass?

Honestly, this butternut squash risotto is taking  ages . I think I underestimated how long it would actually take to properly toast the rice. Oh, you’ll be fine. It smells lovely though. Much more ambitious than my usual ‘throw some leaves together’ effort. Though, on that note, I did find a really good little Italian deli near work. They do these amazing pre-made salads with proper mozzarella and roasted vegetables. It’s a lifesaver when I’m on deadline. Ooh, tell me more! I’m always looking for quick lunch options. Especially now I’m trying to be…well, less reliant on Pret. It’s a black hole for my bank account. It’s called ‘Bella Italia’ - slightly unimaginative name, I’ll grant you. But seriously, it’s proper good. They do pasta boxes too, if you’re really desperate. Speaking of desperate, how  was  that pilates class you tried? You looked…determined on Instagram? Determined is one word for it. Tortured is another. I genuinely thought my core was stronger than that. Everyone else was gracefully flowing through the exercises and I was… flapping. Like a stranded fish. Oh no! I’m imagining the scene. I’m thinking of joining a barre class. Apparently, it's good for posture, which after hours hunched over a laptop, is probably vital for my survival. Barre sounds terrifyingly elegant. I’m more of a ‘sweaty and vaguely in control’ kind of exerciser. Did you manage to book that weekend away to Lisbon then? You were talking about it ages ago. I did! Finally. Flights are booked, and I’ve got a little Airbnb in Alfama. It’s supposed to be really vibrant. I’m proper excited. I was thinking of dragging Sarah along, but she’s got that conference in Barcelona. Lisbon is amazing. You have to try the pastel de nata. Seriously, prepare to become addicted. And wander up to the São Jorge Castle, the views are incredible. Oh! And I bought this really ridiculous floaty dress when I was there last time. It’s completely impractical for everyday life, but it makes me feel like I'm in a film. A film? What film? I don’t know! A… romantic comedy? Something with a soundtrack and a lot of sunshine. I have a problem with buying clothes based on the  feeling  they give me, not whether they’ll actually fit into my wardrobe.

Honestly, the things they come up with. I had a student today genuinely ask me if Plato was a real person. A  real  person! You’re kidding. After a whole semester of reading him? I wish I was. Said he thought it was a pen name, like, a collective of philosophers. I just… stared. It’s exhausting, isn’t it? Trying to build up from absolute zero with some of them. It is. Though I had one who thought Machiavelli invented the word ‘Machiavellian’. Said he’d looked it up, and the etymology led straight back to him. Oh, that’s good. That's a lovely little circle of misinformation. We’re fighting a losing battle, aren't we? Against the internet. Probably. But at least it gives us something to talk about. Speaking of exhausting things… have you seen Sarah lately? She sounded completely frazzled on the phone. No, not since… oh gosh, was it Ben’s birthday? She was complaining about her mum then, wasn't she? Yes, the mum saga continues. Apparently, her mum’s decided she needs to ‘find herself’ and has booked a silent retreat in the Himalayas. No way! That’s… ambitious. And Sarah’s stuck picking up the pieces with her dad. Exactly. She said she hasn't slept properly in weeks. It’s amazing how one person can generate so much chaos. It really is. And then she feels guilty for feeling stressed about it! It's a vicious cycle. Poor thing. We should probably invite her over for dinner soon, force-feed her carbs and wine. Good idea. How about next week? Tuesday? We could try that new Sichuan place down the road. Perfect. And maybe we can get her to talk about something other than her mother. Although honestly, that could be a full-time job in itself. True. Oh, speaking of things needing attention… I think I need to cut my toenails. They’re starting to tap against my shoes. Oh, please, don’t. Not now. I’ve just managed to compartmentalise all thoughts of podiatric maintenance. Sorry, sorry. Just a random thought. Occupational hazard of wearing uncomfortable shoes all day, I suppose. You and your shoes. You'd choose comfort over style every single time. Hey, practicality is key! Especially when trekking across Beijing. Besides, a man must be able to walk without fearing impalement by his own toenails.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just  exhausting . Three hours of polite conversation about pottery. Pottery, David! Right, your mother-in-law's pottery appreciation evening. You warned me. Still, gotta keep the peace, eh? Peace? It was a hostage situation. And she kept referring to her latest…creation…as ‘organic’. It looked like a lopsided ashtray. Seriously. Organic lopsided ashtray. Sounds… rustic. Did your husband ride to the rescue at any point? He was being strategically charming to Uncle Bernard about the cricket. A full-scale tactical retreat. Left me to fend for myself against the earthenware onslaught. Speaking of strategic retreats, have you seen the new Bond film? Not yet! Been completely swamped at work. Apparently, someone in accounts thought it was a brilliant idea to switch software mid-financial quarter. Chaos. Absolute chaos. Is it any good? It’s… fine. A bit predictable, honestly. The villain was trying to take over the world by controlling the global supply of sustainably sourced quinoa. Quinoa? Seriously? I’m not making it up! And the love interest spent most of the film explaining the ethical implications of drone warfare. It felt less like a Bond film and more like a particularly tense university debate. Sounds… woke. They’re really trying to update the franchise, aren’t they? They are. And I’m not sure it’s working. Anyway, enough about culturally significant cinema. How’s Sarah? Still obsessed with that true crime podcast? Oh, relentlessly. She’s convinced the local baker is a secret art thief. Apparently, he has a ‘shifty’ look and buys a suspicious amount of canvas. A baker? Using canvas? Apparently, he’s using it to… line his bread tins? It's a whole thing. She's spent hours researching the art world and the price of flour. She even tried to get me to go undercover and buy a loaf of sourdough. That’s… dedicated. You didn’t, I hope? Absolutely not. I have a company to run. Although, thinking about it, his sourdough  is  suspiciously good. Don’t encourage her, David! She'll be staking out the bakery with night vision goggles next. It's like that Flat Earth thing my brother got into a few years ago. Completely unshakeable belief in the ridiculous. Oh god, the Flat Earth thing. That was a fun Christmas. Trying to explain the concept of gravity to someone who genuinely believes the world is a pancake.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? Seriously, my legs are going numb. Nearly, love, nearly. Still a good few hours to go yet, though. Cornwall's a long way from Manchester, you know. Look out the window, isn’t the scenery lovely? All these fields… It's… green. And fields. I’ve seen fields before, Dad. Are we going past Jamaica Inn at any point? I read that book for English and it sounded really creepy. We should do, yeah. It’s a bit further down, near Bodmin Moor. Spooky place, supposedly. Your Grandma always said there were smugglers running around there back in the day. She used to tell us stories. Did she? Grandma’s stories are always… exaggerated. Remember when she said she once met the Queen? Oh, she did love a good story, your Grandma. Speaking of colours, have you noticed how grey everything is? The roads, the houses… It’s all just fifty shades of grey. Like that book you were reading. It’s not  just  grey, Dad! Look, there’s a yellow gorse bush. And those wildflowers are purple. It’s not all depressing. It reminds me a bit of the Wizard of Oz going from black and white to colour. Good point, love. A good point. It does brighten up a bit when you look for it. You know, it’s amazing how much things have changed since I was a lad. Remember when you were learning about the telegraph? And Morse code? Yeah, in History. It's like, why did people even bother? Just send a text! It’s so much easier. Easier now, yes. But back then, it was revolutionary! Instant communication, even if it was just dots and dashes. Before that, it was telegrams, delivered by hand. Imagine waiting days for a message. Sounds… awful. Though, I guess they didn't have their phones constantly buzzing. True enough. It's a trade-off. Did you finish that Sherlock Holmes story for school? Almost. It's good, but a bit… long-winded. And the language is really old-fashioned. Like Lewis Carroll. Why did they write like that? They did things differently then. More descriptive. Building the atmosphere. It’s a skill, really. Like those old fairy tales. They're dark, aren't they? Not like Disney. Really dark. But interesting. Hey, Dad, can we stop for chocolate when we fill up with fuel?

Honestly, this cake is amazing, Gran. Did you make it yourself? Aye, lass. Old family recipe. Victoria sponge, it is. Though, truth be told, I had a little help with the jam. Betty down the road makes a proper set, you see. Mine tended to be a bit… runny. It’s fantastic. Seriously. So much better than anything you buy in a shop.
