Although, speaking of shops, did either of you see the price of petrol at the station near the M5? Robbery, I tell you. Don't even  start  on petrol prices, Liam. It's criminal. I nearly choked when I filled up yesterday. It feels like I'm funding a small nation just to get to work. Petrol, eh? In my day, you could get a full tank for a few shillings. Though, of course, we didn't drive much during the war. Everything was rationed, you know. Fuel, food… even sweets! Wow, that’s… intense. My grandad used to talk about the rationing. Didn’t he grow his own vegetables in the garden? He did! And my wife, bless her soul, she’d preserve everything. Pickles, jams, fruit… the pantry was always full. Though, she worried endlessly about bombing raids. We lived near the Manchester ship canal, you see, a potential target. That must have been terrifying. It’s hard to imagine living with that constant fear. I mean, the closest I get to danger is potentially losing a dataset at work, and that’s hardly comparable! A dataset is serious business, though, isn’t it, Chloe? All that linguistic data… Tell me about it. Right now, I'm trying to get a corpus of northern slang compiled. Trying to get people to actually  write  it down is the hard part. Everyone just  says  it, and then it's just… lost. Northern slang, you say? Back in Timperley, we had some right colourful expressions. “Nowt” for nothing, “Ey up” for hello… though I suppose that’s pretty common. I remember hearing “Ey up” on a documentary about Yorkshire. Sounds very friendly. It is! It's a proper greeting. Oh, speaking of places, have you guys booked your holiday yet? You were talking about going to Cornwall, weren't you, Liam? We are! Just finalised it last week. A week in St Ives. Hopefully get some surfing in, if the weather holds. Surf, eh? When I was a lad, we went to Blackpool.

Right, so I’ve made a start on the list for stuff to take when I move. It's… longer than I thought it would be. Oh, darling, moving always is. You underestimate how much  stuff  accumulates, don't you? Especially books. You’ve always been a bookworm. Have you got the good saucepan? The one I gave you for your birthday, the heavy-bottomed one? Yep, it’s on the ‘definitely take’ list. Honestly, I use it all the time. Can’t believe how much better it is than everything else. Did you manage to get hold of Auntie Maureen? I wanted to tell her properly about everything before she hears it second-hand from Brenda. I spoke to her this morning. She was thrilled, absolutely thrilled. Said she's already looking at train tickets to come down for the wedding. Though she did ask if you were  sure  about Sarah. Oh, here we go. Well, she just wants you to be happy, love. She remembers what happened with… well, you know. Mum, please. That was ancient history. And Sarah’s different. She’s… grounded. And she makes me laugh. And she understands the whole teaching thing. Unlike… well, never mind. Alright, alright. No need to get defensive. I just relay messages. I’m a messenger, not a judge. Did you sleep okay last night? You looked a bit peaky at breakfast. Jet lag finally catching up with you? A bit, yeah. It's weird, I felt completely fine on the plane, but then as soon as I got here, boom. Exhausted. And I keep forgetting things. Like, I walked into the living room and couldn’t remember why I was there. It’s a bit worrying. Oh, darling, don't fret. It’s just the jet lag, honestly. It does that. Makes your brain all fuzzy. Drink plenty of water, and I’ve got some lavender oil, you can put a few drops on your pillow. Helps with relaxation. Good idea. Lavender sounds nice. Speaking of nice, this roast smells amazing. What kind of fish is that? It's not something I've seen before. Weaver fish. Old Mr. Henderson at the market had some fresh in. It’s a bit fiddly to fillet, but the flavour is wonderful. Your father used to love it. Reminds me of that holiday we took to Cornwall, oh, must be thirty years ago now.

Honestly, that documentary is stressing me out. All this talk about waiting lists… it’s just relentless. Aye, it’s a mess, isn’t it? The NHS is on its knees. They’re understaffed, underfunded… you hear stories all the time. Old Mrs. Henderson down the street was waiting six months for a hip replacement, six months! It’s criminal. You’d think, being a wealthy nation, we could manage to look after people properly. They keep talking about efficiency savings, but it just feels like cutting corners. Well, they’ve been tinkering with things for years, haven’t they? Remember all the restructuring under Blair? It’s just one thing after another. Speaking of things changing… have you seen Sarah’s new hair? She’s gone all pixie cut. Oh, aye! I saw a photo on Facebook. Looks a bit harsh, doesn't it? She always suited longer hair. I know, right? A bit too severe for her, I think. Reminds me of that woman from ‘Line of Duty’… AC-12. Bit intimidating. Haha, aye! You're right! But each to their own, eh? She looks confident enough, and that’s the main thing. Though I’m glad I booked my hair appointment for next week. I'm thinking just a trim. Nothing drastic. Sensible. I need to book one too. It's getting ridiculous. Speaking of ridiculous… did you see the petrol queues yesterday? Ooh, don't even get me started! It was insane! People panic buying like it’s the apocalypse. Exactly! It’s the same every time there’s a whisper of a shortage. People are so quick to jump to conclusions. Reminds me of the toilet paper hoarding at the start of lockdown. Honestly! And now they’re talking about A-Level reforms… making them more vocational, less academic. I read about that. Seems like a good idea in theory, preparing students for work. But what about those who want to go to university? Will it narrow their options? That’s what I'm worried about. It'll just create another tier system, won't it? The kids who are steered towards vocational training might not have the same opportunities. It's always the unintended consequences, isn't it? They try to fix one problem and end up creating two more. Exactly. Look at these plants. I’ve been trying to keep this fern alive for weeks, and it’s still looking a bit droopy.

Right, so I genuinely think I’m gonna have to get a job over Christmas. Like,  actually  get a job. Not just a few shifts here and there. Oof, that’s rough. Why? Are things seriously that tight? I thought you were okay with savings from summer. I was! But then, like, impulsive Amazon purchases happened. And that weekend trip to York wasn’t exactly free, was it? Plus, I’m predicting a festive spending spree. My niece and nephew are expecting  a lot . Tell me about it. My little cousin already has a list for Santa that’s approximately the length of a dissertation. And expensive. Very expensive. Honestly, kids are just miniature financial black holes. Speaking of black holes…did anyone actually read that article I sent about the economic impact of the Black Death? Proper grim stuff. I skimmed it! It was a bit… intense, even for me. All that stuff about labour shortages and wage increases. Kind of a messed up silver lining, though, innit? Yeah, but at the cost of, like, a third of the population. Not exactly a win. It makes you think about the fragility of everything, doesn’t it? Especially now, with everything going on. Fragility is a good word. Like, I’m genuinely stressing about uni applications. What if I don't get into any of the ones I want? Then what? Stuck doing something I hate? You'll get in somewhere, love. You’re brilliant. Besides, it's not the be-all and end-all. Plenty of people take gap years and end up doing amazing things. True. Although, honestly, the thought of another year at home fills me with dread. Mum’s already started dropping hints about ‘helping out’ more. Translation: doing all the housework. Ugh, parents. Always finding ways to guilt trip you. My mum wants me to come home every weekend, even when I’m properly settled in at uni. The pressure! Mine just wants to know if I’m ‘meeting nice boys’. Honestly! I’m trying to study for a degree, not find a husband. It’s exhausting. It’s that whole societal expectation thing, isn’t it? Like, you have to tick all the boxes: successful career, marriage, 2.4 children… It’s all a bit… patriarchal. Totally. It's why I'm trying to get more involved with the feminist society at college. They’re doing some really interesting stuff, like campaigning for better representation in the curriculum.

Honestly, this coastline is breathtaking. Makes you forget about… everything else. It really is. Although, looking at the ocean does also make me think about how vast everything is, and how small our little dramas are. Which reminds me… I’ve been thinking about Sarah. Oh? What about her? Still going on about Mark? No, no, it’s not even about Mark anymore. It’s just… I think I’m done. Done with the whole friendship, really. Wow. That’s… big. That’s a really big thing to admit, isn’t it? It’s so hard to just… let go of people. I know, right? We’ve been friends since uni, which is, what, fifteen years? But lately, every time I see her, I just feel… drained. It’s always complaints, always negativity. And she always manages to turn the conversation back to herself. Ugh, the conversational narcissists. The worst. I had a similar thing with Chloe a couple of years ago. It was exhausting. Like I was constantly providing emotional labour. Exactly! It’s like I’m her unpaid therapist. And she doesn’t even  want  advice, she just wants to… wallow. I feel awful even saying it, but I dread seeing her name pop up on my phone. You're not a bad person for feeling that way. Seriously. Sometimes friendships just… run their course. It doesn't mean you have to have a massive blow-up. It just means you’ve grown apart. The trick is how to navigate it without causing a huge scene. That’s what I’m struggling with. I don’t want to ghost her, that feels horrible. But I also don’t want to have a big, dramatic confrontation. She’ll just get really upset and then feel victimised. Oof, yeah, Sarah sounds… sensitive. What I did with Chloe was just gradually… lessened contact. I stopped initiating things. I'd respond to texts, but I wouldn’t suggest meet-ups. And if she asked, I’d be “busy” a lot. Eventually, it just sort of… fizzled out. That sounds… sensible. A slow fade. But what if she notices? What if she asks what's going on? You can just be vague. “Things are hectic at work,” “I'm trying to prioritise some self-care,” you know, the usual. You don’t owe her a detailed explanation. And if she  really  presses, you can say something like, "I just feel like we're not connecting as much these days."

So, uni’s… well, it’s uni. Still a lot of reading, honestly. Feels like all I do is read and then write about reading. Ah, the life of a humanities student. Just as it should be, darling. Though, honestly, after all these years, I still can’t believe how much reading they make you do. I thought  I  read a lot during my degree, but it seems to have escalated. It has, definitely. This week it’s all Victorian poetry. Browning, Tennyson, the lot. It's...dense. How’s the painting going? Anything new on the easel? Oh, I’m trying a new series. Inspired, oddly enough, by our trip to Italy last year. Remember those crumbling frescoes in that little church in Assisi? I’m attempting to capture a similar sense of faded grandeur. It’s…challenging. Trying to get the right texture, the right  feeling  of age. Sounds amazing, honestly. You always manage to pull something beautiful out of everything. Have you thought about exhibiting them anywhere? I’ve been considering it. There’s a little gallery in Hampstead I’ve had my eye on. But I’m never quite sure if my work is… ready. You’re always your own harshest critic, aren’t you? You shouldn't be! You're brilliant. Truly. Anyway, have you spoken to Aunt Clara recently? I tried calling yesterday, but it went straight to voicemail. Oh, she's off on one of her cruises, I believe. Apparently, this one’s to the Greek islands. She sends postcards, rather lovely ones actually. Though often they’re full of complaints about the food or the weather. You know Clara. Of course. Classic Clara. Still, at least she's getting out there. Speaking of getting out there, are you still thinking about going to Berlin for that exhibition next month? The one with the Klimt drawings? Oh, absolutely! I’ve already booked the train. It's a slightly mad dash – only a few days – but I  have  to see those drawings. Klimt has always been… a connection, you know? Being from Vienna and all. It feels almost like a pilgrimage. That’s lovely. I’m glad you’re going. I’m drowning in essays at the moment, so Berlin is sadly out of the question for me. Have you read anything good lately? I'm in desperate need of some light reading to escape the Victorian gloom.

Honestly, I still feel a bit sick from that pierogi place last night. Should have maybe just had soup. Though, soup feels… insufficient before a gym session, doesn’t it? Insufficient is putting it mildly. You need fuel, especially after all this driving. You’ve been doing most of it, haven’t you? I feel a bit guilty, just navigating and occasionally pointing out scenic routes. Don’t be silly. I don’t mind. Honestly, I find the driving quite… meditative. Though, these Polish roads are testing my meditative state. It’s just… really quite relentless, isn’t it? Constant little villages. It’s part of the charm! It feels much more  real  than a motorway, all slick and anonymous. How much longer, do you reckon? Google Maps is being particularly unhelpful. Google Maps thinks we’ll be in Tarnow in… fourteen minutes. Which, knowing Google Maps, is probably optimistic. And then we have to find this gym, right? The one you read about online? Is it decent? Apparently, it's got a really good free weights area. And a surprisingly high number of female weightlifters which is… nice. I’m a bit tired of being the only woman near the dumbbells. It’s so frustrating. Oh, I can imagine. It's ridiculous. The whole gym culture is so… gendered. Like women aren’t supposed to be strong. It’s completely archaic. I remember once, years ago, trying to use a machine at a gym and a bloke actually came over and  adjusted  it for me. Like I didn’t know how to operate a lever! Ugh, the mansplaining! It’s infuriating. It’s not even about strength, is it? It’s about control. They feel threatened. It's always the same little power play. Exactly. And it’s exhausting. Although, I wouldn’t mind a little bit of… silence right now. This music is starting to grate. It’s all very upbeat Eastern European dance stuff. It’s a bit much before noon. Okay, a little quieter. You're right. It’s a bit… intense. It's funny, isn't it? How much being English defines us, even when we're miles away from England. We’re always apologising, always craving a quiet cuppa, and always complaining about the weather, even when it’s perfectly pleasant. It’s true. We’re a nation of complainers. And tea drinkers. And… overly polite people.

This mug’s lovely, isn’t it? Proper hand-thrown, you can feel the difference. Not like those mass-produced ones. Aye, it is a nice mug. Though I still miss my old blue one. The one with the little rose on. Oh, that one! The one that chipped when you dropped it trying to reach the biscuit tin? That’s the one. Bit of a clumsy moment that were. Though I blame the biscuits, really. Too tempting. Have you put enough milk in yours? You like it strong, don't you? Just right, thanks. This weather’s been peculiar, though, hasn’t it? Sunshine one minute, then a drizzle the next. Can’t get anything planted properly. It’s been a funny summer. Not a proper summer, not at all. I was saying to Maureen the other day… she’s got a lovely garden, Maureen… but she’s struggling too. Too wet for her roses, she says. I saw a spider in the bathroom this morning. A big one. Nearly gave me a heart attack. Spiders are good luck, you know. Old wives’ tale, but I always believed it. Keeps the flies down, too. Though I wouldn't want one wandering over me while I'm having a bath! No, thank you. I’m quite happy for them to stay outside. I’m trying to get the lavender established, but it's a slow process. It just doesn’t seem to want to thrive. Lavender needs well-drained soil. You’ve got a bit of clay in yours, haven’t you? That might be the trouble. Old Mr. Higgins always said lavender liked a bit of grit. I did add some compost… Maybe I should try some grit. Talking of Mr. Higgins, did I tell you about the power cut last week? No, what happened? Complete darkness. And I was right in the middle of marking essays. Had to light a candle. Felt like being back in Victorian times! Oh dear. That’s a nuisance. We had a power cut a few weeks back. Scared the life out of Agnes, it did. She thought the world was ending. She's getting so frail, Agnes is. It’s awful seeing people get older. Remember when we all used to go to the Bradford Festival? That seems like a lifetime ago. Aye, I do. Good times, them were. Fred always used to get us lost trying to find the folk music tent.

So, are we definitely going to Cornwall this year then? Like,  actually  Cornwall? Yes, darling, we are. Your Grandad’s already booked the cottage. It’s the same one we went to a few years ago, remember? Near Padstow. Oh, yeah! The one with the really bumpy garden? And the seagulls trying to steal your chips? Aye, that’s the one. Those seagulls were bolder than brass, they were. Nearly took a sausage roll right out of my hand. It’s just… Cornwall feels… a bit boring, doesn’t it? Everyone goes to Cornwall. Boring? Cornwall is beautiful! The beaches are lovely, and we can go to the Eden Project again. And your Grandad wants to try and find that little pub with the live music. Oh, the one where he tried to join in with the band, even though he doesn’t play an instrument? Now, that’s a bit harsh, love! I just offered a bit of percussion. Didn’t quite catch the rhythm, maybe. He was enthusiastically clapping, is what he was doing. Anyway, it’s nice and relaxing. A proper family holiday. Are you excited about seeing Auntie Carol and Uncle Dave? They said they might come down for a day. Ugh, Auntie Carol. She always asks me about school, and then tells me I need to "apply myself" more. And Uncle Dave just talks about his garden. Ah, don't be like that, lass. They mean well. And Dave’s got a prize-winning marrow, you know. A marrow? Seriously? He’s very proud of it. It's apparently enormous. Anyway, I was thinking, should we invite Chloe and Sophie to come with us for a day? They’ve been asking about the holiday. Chloe and Sophie? To Cornwall? With  us ? Well, just for one day. It would be nice for you to have some friends to hang out with. We could go to the beach, get ice cream… But… they’re really annoying sometimes. Chloe always copies everything I do, and Sophie keeps talking about that boy, Liam, even though he totally ignores her. Now, now, be a good sport. Sharing your holiday is a good thing. Besides, maybe it’ll tire them out for a week. I guess. But if they embarrass me, I'm blaming you both. Deal. We’ll just have to keep an eye on them. Now, about packing… have you started thinking about what you want to take?

Honestly, Heath Ledger was  so  good in that film. Like, Patrick Verona is the blueprint. I know, right? And Julia Stiles was amazing too! Kat Stratford is such a mood. Though Mr. Stratford was a bit…much. So annoying! Like, let them date! It’s literally the whole plot! Ugh, parents. Speaking of annoying…Mr. Henderson just gave us  another  homework assignment. Seriously?! What is it this time? A five-page essay on the causes of the First World War. Five pages! It’s a Friday after school! I just want to watch Netflix. That is brutal. Mine’s not much better. Mrs. Davies wants us to analyse a poem by Wordsworth. Like, who even  cares  about Wordsworth? Exactly! It's so boring. Maybe we should just…skip it? Nah, my mum would kill me. She’s all about the good grades. Besides, I think it’s worth just getting it done so we can enjoy the weekend. True. Okay, okay, fine. So, are you still up for going to London next month? Definitely! I’ve already started making a list of all the places we need to go. We  have  to go to that vintage shop in Shoreditch. The one with all the Dr. Martens. Yes! And that little cafe with the fairy lights? And we need to see a musical! Oh, which one? Wicked is always good, but it’s a bit pricey. I was thinking maybe Six? I saw a TikTok of it and it looks amazing. All the queens singing! Ooh, good idea! We should check ticket prices. And we need to figure out how we’re actually getting there. Your mum said she might be able to drive us, right? Yeah, she said she'd think about it. But she's worried about the traffic. Maybe the train is better, even if it's a bit more expensive. Probably. Less stressful, at least. And we can bring snacks! We could get those giant cookies from that bakery by the station. Ooh, yes! That's a plan. London is going to be so good. It’ll be way more fun than writing essays about boring old wars and poets. Definitely. Although… maybe we should actually start thinking about that essay now. Just a little bit? Ugh. Fine. But only after we make a proper London itinerary with  all  the snacks. I hope this fits your specifications! Let me know if you’d like me to adjust anything or write more.

Honestly, Facebook is a minefield. I spent an hour last night arguing with someone about… well, I don’t even remember what it was about now. Just endless loops of misinformation. Misinformation? Always was a load of rubbish, that internet thing. Never trusted it. Oh, don’t start, Arthur. You ask me to look up recipes all the time! And weather forecasts. That’s different! That’s practical. It’s all these opinions… everyone’s an expert now. Back in my day, you listened to folks who  knew  things. It’s just… unfiltered, isn’t it? Everyone has a platform. Reminds me a bit of some of the students, actually. It does. And it’s addictive. I keep telling myself I’ll delete it, but then… the photos of friends’ kids, little updates… you get sucked back in. Speaking of kids, did young Thomas ever get his chicken pox? I remember asking ages ago. He did, finally. Dreadful week. Poor little thing was covered head to toe. Luckily, mild as anything, though. Bit of Calpol and lots of cuddles. Chicken pox used to be proper nasty. Nearly lost my cousin, Betsy, to it. They had to call the doctor three times. Different times. It’s amazing how much better medical care is now. Even just simple things like vaccinations… It is. Though I do worry sometimes, all these vaccinations. It feels like they’re injecting them with everything under the sun. Now you're talking like that Elsie! It’s all God’s work, you know. Keeps us healthy or doesn’t, as He sees fit. Shouldn't be messing with it. Oh, here we go… I think there’s a middle ground, Arthur. Science and faith aren’t necessarily mutually exclusive. Humph. You young ‘uns and your science. Always trying to explain things away. Where’s the wonder in that? Sometimes a bit of explaining  is  wonderful, Arthur. It helps you understand things. Remember when you were convinced the washing machine was possessed? That was a faulty motor! A perfectly reasonable explanation! But it sounded like a demon, I tell you. A demon! Were you referring to the clicking noise? Clicking? It was a groaning, a wailing! It sounded like… A possessed washing machine. Classic Arthur. Honestly, sometimes I think he has a touch of the… what’s it called, when you have to check things over and over? OCD? Obsessive-compulsive disorder?

Honestly, the traffic was dreadful getting back from Mum’s. Absolute gridlock all the way from Maidstone. Oh, don't even start me on Maidstone. It's a black hole for traffic. I avoid it like the plague whenever possible. Remember old man Hemmings used to say Maidstone was built on a ley line of perpetual congestion? Hemmings said a lot of things, didn't he? Half of them didn’t make any sense. Still, he was a character. He’d tell you stories about Kemsing in the war, really vivid stuff. I wish I’d asked him more about that. I only really knew him as the grumpy man who shouted at us for playing football too close to his petunias. Oh, the petunias! He lived for those petunias. He’d spend hours watering them. Speaking of the old days, remember when your dad, Speaker_6, tried to teach us all German? He was convinced we’d all be fluent and then we’d go on some grand adventure through Germany. Well, it's a useful language! And I  was  fairly fluent, once. Lost it a bit over the years, though. It’s all about practice. I said to Speaker_1, "You should learn it, it will be useful for your job,” but no, she didn’t listen. I had enough to learn  with  my job, thank you very much! And a lot of my patients don’t speak German. Honestly, learning a language is hard enough without your husband drilling you with verb conjugations! It’s the accents that get me. I went to a conference in Munich a few years ago and I couldn’t understand a word anyone was saying. They were speaking German, obviously, but it was like a different language entirely! All guttural and…well, German. That’s so funny! I’ve always wanted to try and pick up a bit of Italian. I was thinking about doing one of those intensive courses. Oh, Italy! I'd love to go to Italy. We should all go to Italy! Imagine, loads of pasta, sunshine… Sounds good. Though with this lot, we’d probably end up getting lost in Rome within five minutes, arguing over directions. We always argue over directions! Speaker_3, you're the worst. You insist on going "the scenic route" which invariably ends up adding an hour to the journey. It’s more enjoyable! And you see more of the countryside.

So, did you catch that Fontaines D.C. gig last week? The one in Bristol? Nah, man, couldn't make it. Was working a double shift at the pub. Gutted though, I’ve been wanting to see them live for ages. How were they? Absolutely brilliant. Proper energy. Grian Chatten’s stage presence is… something else. Though honestly, the sound was a bit muddy at times. You could barely hear Carlos O’Connor's drumming over the bass. That’s a shame. He's a beast on the drums, isn’t he? I was watching some live footage online and the power he gets is mental. I tried drumming for a bit when I was younger, quickly realised I lacked the coordination. Haha, yeah, it takes dedication. I had a go a while back, just messing around on my brother’s kit. Ended up mostly hitting cymbals and looking like a complete idiot. Sounds about right. Speaking of music, have you heard that new Yard Act album? ‘Night Plays Murmurs’? Yeah! Been obsessed. Proper storytelling, innit? Bit different to their earlier stuff, a bit more…polished maybe? I think so. Still got that spoken word vibe, but it’s definitely more refined. Proper good for driving. What have you been up to apart from gigs and music, though? Still hunting for an internship? Yeah, the internship search is…ongoing. Sent off a few more applications this week, mostly in marketing stuff. It’s so competitive, eh? Everyone seems to want experience but how are you supposed to  get  experience without an internship in the first place. Tell me about it. It’s a catch-22. I’m lucky I got into the kitchen straight out of sixth form. Learned on the job. Hard work, but at least I was  doing  something. How’s your dissertation coming along? Slowly. Very slowly. I'm researching the impact of social media on political discourse, and honestly, it's just a rabbit hole of negativity. Makes you want to delete all your accounts. I’m supposed to be finishing the literature review next week. Ouch. Sounds… intense. I’m glad I’m chopping vegetables for a living. Simplifies things. It does sound simpler! What’s the plan for the weekend? Any exciting chef-related adventures? Just a busy service at the pub, hopefully. Maybe catch up with Liam and Chloe on Sunday, they were saying they were free.

Honestly, this place is rammed, isn’t it? Didn’t realise it’d be this busy for just a coffee. Aye, it’s always like this on a Saturday. Least we got a table, though. It's a bit loud, isn’t it? Hard to hear yerself think. Tell me about it! Right, what’s the plan for today then? You’ve got that friend’s birthday party tonight, haven’t you? Yeah, at Ben’s. He’s turning fourteen. Mum, can you drop me off? It’s a bit of a trek to Walker. Walker? Oh, goodness. Right, I can do that, but you’ll need to be ready for seven sharp. I’ve got that domino drive at the social club after, you know, Mrs. Henderson's leaving do. A domino drive? Seriously? Still going on with those? Don’t knock it ‘til you’ve tried it! It’s a good laugh, and it raises money for charity. Plus, Brenda makes her famous scones. Speaking of which, I need to write a shopping list. Milk, flour, sugar… we’re out of everything. You always say that. We always have loads of stuff. It’s just buried under stuff. Don’t be cheeky! Anyway, about the summer holidays… have you thought any more about what you want to do? We talked about maybe a few days in Durham? Durham’s alright. It's a bit…beige, though, isn't it? Beige?! It’s a historic city with a beautiful cathedral! What’s wrong with a bit of beige? I dunno. Just feels…quiet. I was thinking maybe we could try something a bit more…exciting. Like, Blackpool? Blackpool?! Good grief, no. Too many stag dos and chip shops. We’d need a mortgage just to pay for the arcade games. Plus, I saw something on the news last night about the state of the beach there. Oh. Right. Well, what about camping? We could get some new sleeping bags. Mine’s smelling a bit…ripe. Camping… Now you’re talking. That could be good. We haven’t done that in ages. We’d need to check what’s on at those campsites near Alnwick. Actually, talking of things smelling ripe… did you see old Mr. Peterson in the drive-through at McDonald’s yesterday? No way! What was he doing? Well, he was wearing his pyjamas, for a start! And shouting at the poor girl taking the orders.

Honestly, this flat is… smaller than I remembered you saying. But nice! Really nice. Good light. It’s… cozy. That’s the word. Cozy. It’s a step up from student halls though, yeah? Which is all that mattered. And rent’s surprisingly reasonable down here. More reasonable than Brum, anyway. Definitely reasonable. You’re getting away with murder. So, how’s the new job then? Assurance Analyst. Sounds… intense. It is. It's a lot of spreadsheets. A lot of “are you  sure  this is right?” Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm just paid to be suspicious of numbers. But the salary's good. Really good. Like, actually allowing me to think about, you know, a deposit on a place, and not just instant noodles for a month. Good, good. You deserve it. Remember that summer we both worked at the garden centre? I vividly remember smelling compost for eight hours a day.  Don’t . Don’t even. That was a dark time. I still instinctively flinch when I see a bag of Miracle-Gro. Speaking of dark times, how’s the linguistics recording going? Still trying to document every regional dialect in the South East? It’s… a slog. I’m currently working on a project trying to map the variations in the pronunciation of ‘bath’. Apparently, it’s a linguistic goldmine. ‘Bath’? Seriously? People actually  care  about how you say ‘bath’? Apparently so. Trust me, there are entire Reddit threads devoted to it. And it’s linked to socio-economic factors, historical migration patterns… it's surprisingly complex. But more importantly – big news! Sarah’s pregnant.  No way!  Sarah? Wow. That’s… huge. Congratulations to both of you! When’s she due? February. So, just after Christmas. It’s… a bit mad, to be honest. Suddenly having to think about things like nursery schools and buggies. It'll be amazing, though. Scary, definitely, but amazing. Are you… planning a joint bank account? Facing the financial realities of impending parenthood? We’re talking about it. She's very keen. I’m slightly more hesitant. I still remember the horror stories from uni about shared finances. Yeah, it can be a minefield. But communication is key, right? And a really detailed budget. My mum always said – never spend more than you earn. Revolutionary, I know. Sounds like good advice. Although a bit difficult in Sussex, isn’t it? Everything’s so expensive here.

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, you know? Like, should I have pushed her harder to go to the doctor sooner? She kept saying it was just a cold, just tiredness… but looking back… Oh, Sarah, don't. You can't do that to yourself. You know your mum, she’s fiercely independent. She wouldn't have  wanted  you nagging her. It’s easy to say ‘should have’, ‘could have’ afterwards, but you did what you thought was best at the time. I know, I know. Logically, I do. It’s just…it’s hitting me hard this week, the anniversary is coming up. And little Leo keeps asking where Nana has gone. How do you explain that to a six-year-old? Oh, bless him. It's awful. We had that with Ethan when Grandad went. We kept it simple. Said she was very poorly, and her body stopped working. And that she wouldn’t be feeling any pain anymore, that she was at peace. He asked if she could still see him from heaven and… well, I just said yes. That’s lovely. Maybe I'll try that. I was trying to avoid the ‘she’s in heaven’ thing, worried about getting into theological debates with a six-year-old. Trust me, they’re more pragmatic than you think. Ethan just liked the idea she was somewhere nice, watching over us. It gave him comfort. How’s Mark coping? He was close to your mum, wasn’t he? He’s… quiet. Very quiet. He’s always been the stoic one, bottling things up. I keep trying to get him to talk, but he just says he’s fine. I’m worried he’s internalising everything. It's almost worse than being openly upset, you know? I do. Men are rubbish at that, aren’t they? All that ‘strong, silent’ nonsense. Maybe gently suggest he talk to someone? It doesn't have to be a formal counsellor, just… someone impartial. Your brother, maybe? I’ve thought about that. Maybe. It’s just…everything feels so raw. And then you hear about other people, like Mrs. Higgins down the road… stage four breast cancer. She was practically bouncing with energy last month. It just feels so unfair. It  is  unfair. Absolutely gut-wrenchingly unfair. And it's terrifying, isn’t it? Makes you think about getting every lump and bump checked, even the tiny ones.

So, how was school today, you two? Anything exciting happen? It was alright. History was boring as usual. We’re still on the Tudors. Mine was… okay. I got put on the bench for football practice, though. Mr. Davies said I need to work on my passing. Oh, that’s a bit frustrating, isn’t it? But good he’s giving you specific feedback. That’s a good coach. Remember when you were being a bit grumpy about football last week? Seems you’re back into it now. Yeah, well, being on the bench isn’t great. But I want to get better. Of course, you do. Practice makes perfect. Speaking of practice, how’s the tennis coaching going, Leo? Did you manage to book another session with Mr. Henderson? I was going to ask about that actually. He’s away next week, apparently. Some tournament thing. Oh, right. That’s a shame. Still, good for him! It's nice to see someone local doing well. It reminds me, did you see that article about the local council wanting to invest in the tennis courts down at the park? I did. It’s about time, isn’t it? They’re in a dreadful state. Though, knowing the council, it’ll take years to actually happen. It’s like when they talked about the new roundabout… Don’t even start on the roundabout! Honestly, it's been discussed for five years. It’s the same with everything these days. All talk, no action. Remember the referendum? Endless promises...  Sighs  Let’s not go there, shall we? It’s a family meal. What was a referendum again? It was like a big vote, ages ago, about whether we should leave Europe. It was quite a divisive time. Anyway, moving on… Leo, have you thought any more about what you might want to do after school? Apart from being a professional tennis player, obviously. I don’t know. Everyone's talking about university, but it seems… expensive. And a bit pointless, maybe. It  is  a big commitment. Have you looked into apprenticeships at all? There are some really good ones in engineering around here now. That’s a good idea. Actually, Mrs. Peterson at the library was talking about a new initiative to help young people set up their own businesses. She said there’s funding available for small start-ups. Now  that ’s interesting.

Honestly, I’m so glad we decided to do this. Just getting out of London for a bit is…necessary. Even if it’s just for a weekend. Me too. Work has been…a lot. Though, I'm already stressing about getting back to that mountain of emails on Monday. Did you see Sarah's LinkedIn post? About the redundancies in her department? Oh, no! Seriously? That’s awful. Which department? Marketing. Apparently, they’re restructuring. She seemed pretty gutted, understandably. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Even at a place like that. Definitely. It does. That's terrifying. Anyway, Lancaster! Are you excited to see the university? I’ve only seen pictures, it looks really beautiful. Yeah, I'm really looking forward to that. And hopefully, a proper seaside trip is on the cards too. I need some fresh air, and I’m craving fish and chips. Like,  really  craving them. Oh, you're speaking my language. We  have  to find a good chippy. I read something about Morecambe having some decent ones. Perfect! We could spend a whole afternoon just wandering around the coast. Though, remember that time we tried to get cockles on that beach in Norfolk? Oh god,  don’t  remind me. The cockle disaster! We were convinced we were going to have this amazing picnic and ended up spending the afternoon trying to dig up tiny, inedible things. And covered in mud. Exactly! And the woman at the stall was giving us the dirtiest looks. Like we were ruining her livelihood. Worth it for the story, though, right? Speaking of stories, how’s the dissertation coming? Are you still battling with chapter three? Still battling, unfortunately. I keep rewriting the introduction and then realizing it doesn’t actually connect to anything. It's… frustrating. You’re so far ahead with yours. How’s it going, actually? It's…progressing. I'm on the analysis now, which is good, but I’m hitting a few brick walls. It’s just so much data. It feels like I'm drowning in transcriptions. I can imagine! That sounds awful. Are you thinking about what you want to do afterwards? Any job applications going in? A few. Mostly research-based roles. I’m hoping to stay in academia, if possible. But it’s competitive, isn’t it? You're thinking of sticking with research, aren’t you? Or are you tempted to try something completely different?

Honestly, I can’t believe Liam’s actually gone and joined a climbing club. Liam! Of all people. No way! Seriously? That’s… unexpected, to say the least. He can barely manage the stairs after a night out, never mind a rock face. I know, right? Apparently, Ben from our year at sixth form is in it too. That's how I found out. He was showing off pictures on his Insta story. Liam looked absolutely terrified. Ben? Proper outdoorsy lad, Ben. Always hiking. Makes sense he’d be into climbing. Still, Liam… are you sure it wasn’t a dare? A really elaborate, month-long dare? He said he wants to “challenge himself.” I think he’s having a mid-life crisis, and he’s 21. Honestly, the drama. He’s always been a bit… cautious. Remember when he wouldn’t go on the log flume at Flamingo Land? Oh god, yes! He nearly cried. He said his hair would get wet. The log flume! He’s convinced he’s got some sort of rare hair condition now, hasn’t he? He’s obsessed! He’s already ordered some special vegan, sulfate-free shampoo online. It was like £30. For shampoo. Blimey. He's a special one, that lad. Speaking of special ones, have you seen Maya’s new band are playing at the Leopard next Saturday? No! Really? That’s brilliant! I didn’t know she’d even started a band. What kind of music is it? She said it’s kinda indie-pop, a bit like Wet Leg. I listened to a couple of tracks she sent me, they're actually really good. She’s on vocals, apparently. She always had a good voice. Remember her doing karaoke at your 18th? She absolutely smashed ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’. How could I forget? She grabbed my dad's microphone and wouldn't let go. I think he was secretly enjoying it though. Definitely. He lives for that kind of chaos. So, are we going to the Leopard then? To see Maya? Yeah, definitely. We should get a few others to come with us. Maybe Sarah and Josh? They'd love it. Good shout. I'll text them now. What are you up to this weekend, anyway? Aside from listening to Liam moan about his aching muscles? Nothing much planned yet. Thinking of finally getting round to finishing that Warhammer model I started about six months ago.

Right, okay, so I’m going to use my researcher to… build a research station in Atlanta. Because honestly, the outbreaks are popping up everywhere and we need to get ahead of this! Atlanta? Bold move. Lots of potential for spread from there, though. Are you sure? I was thinking maybe Bangkok, to try and contain the Asian outbreaks. Containment is a strong word, Rhys. We’re basically just delaying the inevitable with this game. Though I agree, Bangkok feels strategically smarter. Atlanta feels... ambitious. I'm with Rhys. Atlanta feels like a gamble. Think about the connections, the airports… it’s a hub! Oh dear. Another potential super-spreader city. Honestly, I’m convinced this game is designed to make us all feel inadequate. It’s a metaphor for life, isn’t it? Constant crisis management. Oh, don’t be so gloomy, Gareth. It’s just a game! Though, you’re right, it is stressful. Anyway, I'm going to use my operations expert to fly to Cairo. We’ve got three cubes there already, and if we don’t deal with it now… Okay, okay, Atlanta it is. I’m going for it. And I'm using my event dispatcher card to remove a cube from São Paulo. That's getting out of hand. Good call on São Paulo. Right, my turn. I’ll use my scientist to treat a disease in Essen. Then I’m going to fly from Bangkok to… hmm… Chicago. I need to get closer to the action in North America. Chicago? Prepare for chaos, my friend. That’s a risky move, right in the heart of everything. I’m going to use my medic to treat three blues in Moscow. Trying to keep that one under control. Three blues in Moscow?! That’s… concerning. I’m going to try and build a research station in London and focus on treating the yellow outbreak. Oh, London’s looking grim. I’m going to help out there. I’ll use my quarantine specialist to… quarantine London. Sacrificing a city to save the world, eh? It’s a tough choice. Very dramatic, Gareth! I’m going to move my senior support worker from Cairo to Algiers. We've got a lot of support there to start treating. Oh no, wait! I just drew an epidemic card! And it’s… Asia! Oh, brilliant. More cubes in Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City, and…  another  one in Jakarta.

Right, so, the CBeebies panto is booked! We’ve got tickets for the Saturday matinee. Are you both excited? Yes! Will Mr Tumble be there? Will they do the twelve days of Christmas song? That’s my favourite! I think so, darling! They usually include all the favourites. It’s going to be brilliant. Now, about your birthdays… Elsie, yours is first, isn't it? Just after the panto. Mummy, can we have a unicorn party? A really sparkly one! A sparkly unicorn party sounds lovely! We'll have to start planning. And Leo, yours isn't far behind. Any thoughts on what  you  want to do? I want a dinosaur party! With a big, big dinosaur cake! And a bouncy castle! A dinosaur party, excellent! A bouncy castle might be tricky in the garden, depending on the weather, but we’ll see what we can do. Honestly, it feels like you two are growing up so fast. It was only yesterday you were obsessed with  In the Night Garden… . Do you remember Upsy Daisy? I remember! She always says ‘Upsy Daisy!’ Exactly! You two have memorized entire episodes. Remember when Leo used to try and copy Makka Pakka's sounds? Oh, you haven’t forgotten! It’s amazing how things stick with you both. Speaking of sticking with you, World Book Day is coming up. Have you started thinking about what you want to dress up as? I want to be Princess Poppy! She's so pretty. I want to be a pirate! With a sword and an eyepatch! Perfect choices! We’ll need to get started on costumes then. And then, right after that… Mother’s Day. You two have got to think of something lovely to make me. We could make you a card! With lots of glitter! I can draw you a picture of a dinosaur  and  a pirate! That would be the best gift ever! Honestly, I feel like we’re constantly juggling birthdays, celebrations, school events… it’s a whirlwind! Mummy, are you tired? A little bit, darling. But it's a happy tired. Having you both makes everything worthwhile. Now, who wants a biscuit? And then we can talk about the guest list for your parties... Me! I want a biscuit! And I want all my friends from school to come to my dinosaur party! Alright, alright, biscuits for everyone! And we’ll work on that guest list.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s biblical rain. Makes planning anything… impossible. Tell me about it. I was going to cycle to that interview down by the river, but then the heavens opened. Ended up sprinting for the bus, looking a right state. Did it go alright, the interview? You were a bit cagey about it earlier. It was… okay. It’s a tiny little local paper, covering mostly council meetings and village fetes. Not exactly Pulitzer Prize material, but it’s a job. And nearish. Better than nothing. You’ve been looking for a while now, haven’t you? Is the commute a killer though? That’s what put me off a place near Richmond. It’s manageable. About forty minutes each way. Though, realistically, closer to an hour with the traffic. The real downside is the pay. It’s… modest. Well, you’ve got to start somewhere, Liv. And it sounds like it would give you some good experience. Remember when I first started teaching? The kids were terrifying! Speaking of terrifying, did you see what Mark put on Facebook? Another picture of his ‘perfect’ sourdough. Honestly, the man thinks he's Paul Hollywood. Oh, god. He's so competitive about baking. Remember that disastrous bake-off at Sarah's birthday? Vaguely. Wasn't there some kind of incident with a collapsed Victoria sponge and a very offended aunt? That was the one! Aunt Mildred hasn’t let him live it down. I’m still trying to figure out if moving to Bristol was a good idea. The job is good, genuinely, but I miss having proper pubs nearby. All they seem to have down there is craft ale bars. Bristol’s lovely, though. Isn’t it a bit… gentrified now though? Everything's getting so expensive. It is. That’s the problem. Rent is insane. I’m starting to think about maybe looking a bit further out, towards somewhere like Clevedon? Clevedon's nice. Bit sleepy, maybe. Have you thought about Taunton? It’s a bit further, but the train links are good. Ooh, Taunton. That’s an idea. What about you, Amelia? Still enjoying the language teaching? Have you had any particularly… interesting students lately? Oh, you know. The usual mix. Couple of really enthusiastic beginners, one student who seems to think he’s fluent already, and a teenager who only signed up because his mum made him.

Honestly, this book…it’s just…fluffy. All this talk about finding yourself through sourdough baking. Really? Like a complex emotional journey requires a perfectly proofed loaf? Oh, come on, Sarah. It’s a bit of escapism. We all need it. Besides, I’ve been meaning to try sourdough. Apparently, it’s all about the starter. My Nan used to have a starter, she called it ‘Bertie’. Bertie? That’s amazing! My grandma just made everything from scratch, but she didn’t give it names. It was all just…practical. Yorkshire puddings the size of dinner plates. That’s her legacy. My mum was a bit the same. Practical. She wasn’t one for hobbies, more for… well, making sure we had clean socks and decent packed lunches. I did have a weird obsession with My Little Pony though. Spent hours braiding their manes. Oh, I had those! Rainbow Dash was my favourite. Remember how they smelled? That slightly plasticky, sweet smell? You can still buy them, apparently. For collectors. Ludicrous prices. Everything’s collectible now, isn’t it? I vaguely remember having some…Stretch Armstrong? Was that a thing? Or am I making that up? He was all gooey, I think. Oh yes! Stretch Armstrong. And the worry when he inevitably split and the goo got  everywhere . My brother had him. He was absolutely furious when Mum binned him. It was a tragic loss in his eight-year-old world. Speaking of tragic losses…work is driving me insane. Old Mr. Henderson is querying  every  expense claim. Even the postage stamps. Honestly, it’s like he thinks I’m personally trying to fleece the company. Oh dear. Sounds familiar. I’ve got a new boss, used to be in finance in London. She’s all about “synergies” and “optimising workflow”. Which basically translates to ‘expect to work longer hours for the same money’. It’s always something, isn't it? I'm dealing with a huge account at the moment, a shipping company. They want me to work miracles to get their costs down. They don’t understand that sometimes, cheap isn’t always best. They never do. It’s the same with everything. You try to explain it logically, and they look at you like you’re speaking a different language. Honestly, sometimes I think people from Peterborough speak a different language. Oh, don't start! I get that with Essex all the time.

So, how was it then? Honestly? Was it as awful as you both made it sound leading up to it? Awful is a strong word, love. Let’s just say it wasn’t  exactly  the idyllic seaside getaway we'd envisioned. Idyllic? Ha! More like a seagull convention with chips. Honestly, they were brazen. Positively brazen. One tried to nick my sandwich right out of my hand! She wasn’t kidding. Brenda was wrestling a gull for a cheese and pickle. It was a sight to behold. No way! You fought a seagull? Mum! I didn’t  fight  it, I… defended my lunch. It was a perfectly good sandwich. And it had Branston pickle, you know how I like it. The B&B wasn’t much better, mind. Right on the main road. Constant traffic. And the landlady… well, she was enthusiastic. About everything. Especially her collection of porcelain thimbles. Oh, Doreen. She gave me a full tour. Each thimble had a story. A  very  long story. I think I aged five years just listening to her describe the history of one little German thimble. A German thimble? That’s… ironic, considering. Don’t start, dear. Yes, I know. Ironic. But at least she wasn’t talking about fishing all the time like Old Man Hemmings down at the harbour. Honestly, you couldn’t get a word in edgeways about cod. Speaking of fishing, Dad did try to go out on a boat trip. That was a disaster. Absolute disaster. The sea was choppy, I’ve got a dodgy back as you know, and the captain smelled strongly of kippers. I was seasick for three hours. Three hours! Oh no, Dad! You and seasickness are not a good mix. He turned green. A very fetching shade of green, I must say. They didn’t even catch anything! Just one tiny little whiting. And a plastic bag. They hauled up a plastic bag. Symbolism, I tell you. Pure symbolism. We did see a lovely beach though, one day, a bit further down the coast. We took Winston – he loved it. Chased the waves for hours. Oh good! At least someone enjoyed themselves. Did you get any pictures? Hundreds. Mostly of Winston looking utterly ridiculous. And Doreen’s thimbles. And a particularly aggressive seagull. I’ve got one of me looking distinctly unwell on the boat. It’s a masterpiece of misery. I want to see them all.

Right, who finished the milk? Seriously? I was going to make a proper coffee, not this… watery stuff. Oh, was that you wanting milk? Sorry! I had a latte this morning. Didn’t even think. I'll grab some on the way back from yoga later, yeah? Yoga already? You’re a morning person, aren’t you, Chloe? I'm operating on about four hours sleep. Deadline looming, you know how it is. I practically  lived  on coffee last week. It's the only way to survive a Saturday deadline! But yeah, downward dog and a green smoothie are my attempt at being a functioning human being. How’s the article coming along? The one about the… dodgy property developer? It’s… well, it's complicated. He’s got  layers . And a very expensive lawyer. I’m trying to get a solid source who isn’t terrified to speak on record. It’s infuriating. Sounds stressful. You need a proper breakfast, at least. I was thinking bacon sandwiches. Unless anyone's vegan-ing it up today? Bacon sounds amazing, actually! I'm not vegan, just… trying to be mindful. But bacon is definitely mindful-worthy. Oh, I'm in. Definitely bacon. Though maybe a slightly smaller portion. Trying to counteract the coffee and general life chaos. Speaking of which, did either of you see that ridiculous article about Harry Styles buying a goat farm? No way! A goat farm? What’s he going to do with a goat farm? Start a boy band for goats? Apparently, it’s for sustainable wool production. Seriously! He’s trying to be all ethical and… fashionable? It’s a whole thing. Ethical wool? That’s a new one. Honestly, celebrities. Anyway, less goats, more bacon. I'll get started. Anyone want brown or white bread? Brown, please. Oh, and Liam keeps texting me about his phone. Apparently, it’s decided it doesn’t  want  to connect to the internet anymore. He’s convinced it’s a conspiracy. Liam and his conspiracy theories! Honestly, he thinks everything is a plot. Probably thinks 5G is controlling his toast. It’s probably just needs a restart. I could take a look later if he's still struggling. I'm pretty good with that sort of thing. Being an engineer and all. Though mostly I just fix robots that weld cars these days. Not exactly cutting-edge stuff.

Honestly though, I still don't trust Satnavs implicitly. Remember when yours sent us down that unmade farm track last summer? Oh, don’t even! I was convinced it was taking us to a shortcut. Nearly lost the suspension on the car, I swear. Google Maps is generally better, though, isn’t it? At least it shows you what the road  looks  like beforehand. Google Maps is alright. Still thinks Old Man Hemmings’ field is a public park. Keeps telling me to turn left into it. Aye, they’re not always right are they? Used to navigate by the stars, we did. Less reliant on batteries and dodgy signal that way. Although, Saudi Arabia was a different story. No stars, just sand. And a lot of very stern men pointing things. Saudi Arabia? You were stationed there, Reg? I didn’t know that. A tour or two. Hot work. But good lads. Got a bit of a soft spot for the place, despite everything. Different world. Anyway, enough about sand. How's the decorating going at yours, Liam? Still haven’t managed to convince Sarah that magnolia isn’t a colour? It’s an ongoing battle. We’ve got the living room done, thankfully. She finally agreed to a muted grey. But she wants bright orange in the spare bedroom. Bright  orange , Reg. I’m fighting it, I really am. Orange? That’s… bold. My Nan had orange wallpaper in the seventies. It was horrific. Oh god, the seventies. I’m trying to avoid all design choices that scream ‘seventies’ at my place. It’s hard enough just finding affordable furniture, let alone stylish furniture. This admin job doesn’t exactly pay a fortune. Tell me about it. Project coordination is alright, pays the bills, but it’s not exactly setting the world alight. You thinking of moving on anytime soon, Chloe? I might look around. It’s just… stable, you know? And the commute’s decent. Plus, it gives me time to do my masters. But yeah, maybe something a bit more… fulfilling. I’m happy enough with the labouring. Keeps me fit, I reckon. And the money's alright. Though my back’s starting to complain a bit now. You gotta look after your back, lad. Years I spent lifting things, marching. Wrecked my knees. Now it’s just a constant ache. Speaking of aches, how’s your mum doing, Liam?

Honestly, I feel like I’ve been fighting off a cold for a week. Just this persistent tickle in the throat. Probably all the recycled air on the flights. Oh, you poor thing. You need to be diligent with the hand sanitiser, you know. Everything goes around on planes. I swear I bring back a new germ with every trip. Are you taking vitamin C? I’ve started chucking a sachet in my water every morning. Are you seriously still doing that, Helen? Vitamin C is basically useless unless you’re already deficient. It’s a marketing ploy. Honestly. Oh, don’t be like that, Sarah! It can’t  hurt , can it? And it feels like I’m doing  something . I’m trying to get loads of sleep, which is hard when you’re constantly shifting time zones. This garden is beautiful, though. Such a calming influence. Do you know what that one is?  points to a sprawling shrub  It looks almost prehistoric. That’s a Rhododendron maximum. Quite invasive, actually. They’re constantly battling to keep them contained here. Apparently, they’re a nightmare in the Pacific Northwest – smothering everything in their path. Invasive, huh? So beautiful, but a bit of a rogue. Sounds a bit like my uncle, actually.  laughs  You’re terrible, David! But true. He’s a charmer, but he’ll walk all over you if you let him. Speaking of walking all over things, have you noticed how meticulously maintained everything is here? The paths, the borders… It's incredible. It's down to a team of incredibly dedicated horticulturalists. And a huge budget, I suspect. The Swedish are very good at investing in green spaces. You see it all over Stockholm. It’s a real point of pride. Makes you think about the council back home, doesn’t it? Half the flowerbeds are just weeds and the grass is knee-high. Don’t even get me started. They keep threatening to cut the library budget. As if books aren’t important enough already! I’m going to write a strongly worded letter. You and a million other people, Helen. It rarely makes a difference. I tell you what  does  make a difference – volunteering. Maybe we should suggest a garden clean-up day with the school? Get the kids involved, teach them a bit about botany. That's a brilliant idea, Sarah. They could learn something, and it gets them off their screens for a few hours.

Honestly, Dad, you've lost  all  your London in the last few years. You sound practically Kentish now. Kentish? What are you on about, love? I've always spoken like this! It's just… people don't talk properly anymore. All mumbly, you know? My ears ache trying to understand some of these youngsters. Oh, don't start on the youngsters, Arthur. It's the sound systems on their phones. They're all shouting into little boxes. My ears are permanently ringing after a shift. It's not their fault the signal's rubbish around here. You try getting a decent connection in Chatham. It’s true though, Dad. You used to have that proper East End drawl. Remember when you'd tell us stories about growing up in London? You sounded like Michael Caine. Michael Caine? I don't sound like Michael Caine! I sounded like my father, that’s who I sounded like. And he sounded like  his  father. It's… diluted, I suppose. Everything gets diluted. Like that washing-up liquid, always ending up too watery. Speaking of watery, did young Daniel finally manage to sort out the custody arrangement with Sarah? I saw her in town, looking absolutely shattered. Sort it out? She's demanding half his benefits, that's what she's doing. And trying to paint him out to be some sort of terrible father because he…well, you know. Because he struggles with a drink? Look, it's not helping anyone, Daniel. You need to get help. Honestly, watching you two is exhausting. Easy for you to say, you're not the one stuck in the middle. She’s threatening to take little Maisie away for good. And she’s using his, you know…problems against him. It’s a sad state of affairs, that. A child needs their father, even if the father's a bit…flawed. Back in my day, you stayed together. You worked at it. Oh, Arthur, don't romanticize the past. You and Mum weren’t exactly a picture of marital bliss. Remember those shouting matches? And him locked in the shed with a bottle of whiskey? That was different. That was stress. The war… losing his job… Okay, can we  please  not revisit the war again? I'm trying to write my dissertation and this is distracting me. Honestly, the stories… it's like living in a soap opera.

Honestly, the Baked Alaska was a disaster. Utterly. Why? What happened? Did it melt? It didn't  melt  exactly. It… slumped. It slumped dramatically. I think the meringue wasn’t stiff enough, and the freezer isn’t quite cold enough. It looked like a sad, sugary island. Haha! A sad sugary island. Did anyone eat it? Your brother demolished most of it. He said it tasted fine, just looked ‘a bit wonky.’ He’s remarkably unfazed by culinary catastrophes. Yeah, he’s like that. He’d eat anything. Did you at least manage to grate the cheese without incident? Surprisingly, yes. The cheese grating was the highlight of the evening, truthfully. No blood was drawn. Though I am convinced my knuckles ache. It’s harder work than it looks. Mum always says you use too much force. Well, someone has to get it done! Anyway, we need to finalise plans for the Halloween party. Are you still inviting everyone from school? Yeah, pretty much. Leo’s bringing his cousin, and I think Ben might bring someone too. Should we get more spooky decorations? Definitely. More cobwebs, definitely more inflatable spiders. And we need to think about music. No really scary stuff, though, some of the younger ones get frightened easily. Okay. What about food? We did pizza last year. We could do pizza again, but maybe also some hot dogs, and those little sausage rolls you like. And I promise to attempt another dessert, though it won’t be a Baked Alaska. Good plan. Speaking of things not going to plan, Mr. Harrison was really weird in history today. Oh? What happened? He kept going on about how young people these days have it too easy, and how when  he  was at school… it was all really old-fashioned stuff. He also kept making comments about what people were wearing. That doesn't sound very appropriate. Was he singling anyone out? Not exactly, but he was just… judging. And it was a really awkward vibe. Hmm. That’s not good. It sounds like he might be exhibiting some… questionable behaviour. Sometimes, people’s own experiences colour their views, and they forget what it’s like to be young. It's not always intentional, but it doesn’t make it okay. It’s important to remember that things have changed, and different generations have different experiences. He just seemed really stuck in the past.

This bacon’s lovely, mind you. Proper back bacon. You don’t get this stuff in Leeds anymore, not consistently anyway. Everything's streaky, all fancy. Mmmph. It  is  good. You’ve outdone yourself, Hilary. Though, to be fair, anything seems good after that flight yesterday. Oh, don’t start on the flight! Honestly, the turbulence… I thought we were coming down. Nearly choked on my miniature gin and tonic. It was a bit hairy, wasn't it? But worth it to have you here. It feels… ages since we've just had a proper natter, without a conference or a deadline looming. It does. Remember that time in Japan, trying to navigate the Tokyo subway? That was properly terrifying. You nearly got us on the wrong line, ended up halfway to… well, somewhere completely the opposite of where we wanted to be. Hey! I was following the pictograms! It’s a different system, okay? And we  eventually  got where we needed to go. Though I’ll admit, I was relying heavily on your Japanese. You and your pictograms. Still, Japan… it feels like another lifetime. Remember old Professor Tanaka, always going on about the benefits of seaweed? Oh, God yes. Honestly, I'm still suspicious of seaweed. Anyway, what are your plans for today? I thought we could wander into town, maybe have a poke around the shops? That sounds lovely. Though I was looking at those introductory flying lessons at the airfield. I saw an advert online. I’ve always fancied learning to fly. Flying lessons? Hilary! You? Seriously? You’re scared of turbulence in a 737! Well, a small plane is different, isn’t it? More control, y’know? And think of the views! Although, I wouldn’t trust myself to land it…perhaps it’s a silly idea. A  very  silly idea. Let’s stick to the shops, shall we? Before you start booking yourself onto a pilot training programme. Afterwards, though, I want to show you this little cafe I found, does the best Welsh cakes. Welsh cakes sound excellent. Oh, look at that! Mrs. Davies is already putting the bins out. That woman is efficient. Our refuse collection in Shipley is a complete shambles. They miss a week, then take everything twice the next. Ours is pretty reliable, thankfully. Though I did see old Mr. Jones trying to explain to the bin men that his garden clippings were “organic recycling material”.

Right, okay, my go. Ugh, seriously? Another vowel. This is hopeless. I’m never going to get rid of these ‘A’s. Just play ‘AEIOU’, make a word. Very funny. It’s not a word, is it? Though, thinking about it, I vaguely remember a lecture on… linguistic origins… where someone argued it  could  be considered a word, if uttered with enough… intention. Sounds like university to me. All theory, no practical application. I’m going for ‘QUIZ’. Twenty-two points. Show off. You always get the good letters. Is ‘QUIZ’ even a real word? Feels… dubious. Of course it’s a real word! It’s a test of knowledge! What are you implying? He’s right, it’s a word. It originates from the 18th century, originally meaning ‘an odd or eccentric person’. Before becoming a challenge. I read that somewhere. Probably on Wikipedia while I should have been doing essays. Fascinating. See, this is why I love a good etymological rabbit hole. Though it doesn’t help me get rid of these vowels. I swear, if I get another ‘E’… You were late again this morning, weren’t you? To the library session. I was not  late  late. I was… fashionably delayed. There’s a difference. Fashionably delayed by an hour? Professor Davies looked actively murderous. Okay, maybe slightly delayed. But my alarm didn’t go off! It’s the phone, I’m convinced it’s actively sabotaging me. It's started prioritising Candy Crush notifications over  actual  alarms. Maybe you should get a real alarm clock. You know, the kind with… hands? Prehistoric. No, I'm considering a full device overhaul. It’s a sign, clearly. A sign I need to disconnect. Although… disconnecting means missing important Candy Crush updates. It’s a dilemma. Speaking of disconnecting, are you still hating your coursework? You look permanently stressed. It’s the reading list! Honestly, it’s like they actively want us to fail. Then there is the writing, have you ever tried writing four thousand words on the post-structuralist implications of… children’s literature? Oh god, I remember that module. Absolute torture. I spent a week arguing that ‘The Very Hungry Caterpillar’ was a metaphor for late-stage capitalism. You did not. I did! And Mrs. Henderson gave me a first! She said it was “surprisingly insightful.” I’m sticking to straight history, thanks very much. Give me battles and dates over caterpillars any day.

Right then, finished that crossword, didn’t I? Took me a good hour. Dreadful clues, honestly. Oh, good for you, Arthur. I haven’t had the patience for crosswords lately. Too much on my mind, I suppose. What’s troubling you then, love? You’ve been a bit quiet this afternoon. Not like you. Just thinking about Brenda, really. She’s not been sounding herself on the phone lately. Keeps saying she’s ‘fine’, but you can  hear  it in her voice, you know? Oh, Brenda. Yes, she always was a bit of a worrier, wasn't she? What's she worried about, do you reckon? I asked her, but she just brushed it off. Something about young David and his new girlfriend. Says she's too young for him. Hmm. Well, young people, eh? Always causing a stir. David’s a good lad though, always polite. He is, but she’s barely out of school herself! Still, it’s their life, isn’t it? We can’t interfere. Though it does sound a bit hasty. It always does sound hasty when you’re our age looking back, doesn't it? Seems like only yesterday  we  were young and making rash decisions. Remember that motorbike, eh? Oh, don’t  start  on that motorbike, Arthur! That was a terrible mistake! Your mother nearly had a fit. She got over it. Eventually. Though she did make me promise to wear a helmet. A rather unflattering one, I might add. It suited you. Gave you a rather serious look. More serious than usual, anyway. Cheeky! Speaking of looking serious, have you seen old Mr. Henderson from next door lately? He’s been looking a bit peaky. Now you mention it, I haven’t. I usually see him pottering about in the garden. Maybe he’s got a cold. It’s been a bit chilly lately. Perhaps. Or maybe he's finally given up on those prize-winning roses. He's always fussing over them. I tell you what, though, they  are  beautiful. They are lovely. He puts a lot of work into them. It's good to have a hobby, isn't it? Keeps you busy. It does that. Keeps the mind active. Though a crossword is enough to keep  my  mind active, thank you very much. You and your crosswords! It’s a good job you enjoy them. Now, are you wanting a cup of tea, love?

This is lovely, honestly. You both always outdo yourselves with these meals. What  is  this amazing sauce with the chicken? It’s got a bit of a…zing. Oh, that's a bit of a cheat, really. It’s a pre-made mango chutney, but I added a teaspoon of harissa paste to it. Gives it a little kick, doesn’t it? I found it in that little farm shop near Crediton. Harissa, eh? Clever girl. I’ve been meaning to experiment with that. It's good with lamb too, you know. We had a lovely lamb tagine last week. Sounds good. I’m trying to be better with spices, you know. Doctor says I need to get more antioxidants. Though, to be fair, he mostly meant more fruit and veg, not necessarily setting my mouth on fire. Well, a little bit of spice  is  good for you, Dad. Besides, you’ve been walking miles every day this week! You’ve certainly earned it. Have you been using that fitness tracker app I downloaded for you? Oh, that thing. Yes, yes. It’s… thorough. Tells me off if I don’t get enough steps. Honestly, it’s like being nagged by a tiny robot. Though, it  did  tell me I climbed the equivalent of three flights of stairs yesterday. Which, considering I mostly wandered around coastal paths, isn't bad. It’s a good app, that one. Very motivating. I use it for my running. Though, to be honest, “motivating” sometimes translates as “making me feel incredibly guilty for having a rest day.” That’s the idea! Speaking of guilt…did you hear anything more about the new train station opening in Tavistock? It's supposed to be happening any week now, after all those delays. I did see something in the paper. Apparently, they’re having another inspection on Friday. Something about signalling issues, I think. Honestly, it’s been “almost open” for about five years now. You'd think building a train station wouldn't be rocket science. It’s the bureaucracy, I reckon. And probably a bit of cost-cutting. They always cut corners. I heard from a colleague whose husband works on the project that they originally wanted to put in a proper covered walkway, but it was deemed “too expensive”. Now people will be queuing in the rain. Honestly! It’s supposed to open up the area for tourism, isn’t it?

Honestly, that burger was…substantial. I’m genuinely worried I’ve entered a food coma. Substantial is one word for it. I think ‘actively trying to kill you’ is another. It was like they built the burger  around  the patty, rather than the other way around. Exactly! And the chips…the chips were clearly pre-frozen, then massively overcooked. I'm pretty sure they were weapon-grade. Did you see old man Hemmings struggling with his? Oh yeah, he looked like he was wrestling an alligator. Poor bloke. Speaking of struggles, I’m dreading Shakespeare on TV tonight. My mum’s making me watch it with her.  Shakespeare  on TV? Seriously? Isn’t that…torture? It is. She insists it's ‘culture.’ Apparently, watching Love Island doesn't count. She keeps trying to get me into it though. “It’s all about the language, darling!” she says. Like, yeah, iambic pentameter is  exactly  what I need after a long day of lectures. Reminds me of my Gran. She tried to get me to read ‘War and Peace’ when I was ten. Said it would “broaden my horizons.” I think it mostly broadened my boredom. Ha! Right? Anyway, about broadening horizons…have you thought any more about where this stag do should be? Mark's still insisting on Prague, but I’m seriously leaning towards Amsterdam. Amsterdam’s a good shout. Prague’s cool, but feels a bit…done, doesn’t it? Everyone goes to Prague. Plus, I’ve heard the beer’s better in Amsterdam. Important research, obviously. Crucially important. Though, knowing Mark, he’ll want some sort of elaborate, themed itinerary involving historical tours and…I don’t know, etiquette classes. Oh God. Let's try and steer him towards the slightly less…refined options. Maybe mention the Escape Rooms? He loves those. Good plan. Although, last time he did an escape room, he spent the entire time arguing with the clues. He claimed they were logically inconsistent. No way! That’s amazing. He's a walking contradiction, that bloke. So, lectures today…how’d yours go? Still hating the European Politics seminar? Utterly. Professor Davies just drones on and on about the intricacies of EU agricultural policy. It’s mind-numbing. I swear I almost fell asleep during a discussion about grain subsidies. Grain subsidies? Seriously? I’m in the wrong course. My ‘Modern Literature’ seminar was actually pretty lively today.

Honestly, this cake is amazing. You  have  to try it. It’s lemon and poppyseed, but it’s… lighter than air. Ooh, go on then. I’m officially stuffed after that panini, but lemon and poppyseed is my weakness.  takes a bite  Oh. My. God. You weren’t kidding. It’s incredible. So, how are things? Properly, properly how are things? It feels like ages since we properly chatted. Things are… hectic. Work is just nonstop at the moment. We're launching this new internal system, and it’s been a disaster trying to get everyone on board. Old habits, you know? People resist change like it’s a personal attack. Tell me about it! It's the same at Pearson. We’re constantly rebranding, trying new marketing strategies. It's exhausting trying to convince people that "dynamic synergy" actually means something other than buzzwords. Exactly! And honestly, I’m just… tired. How’s Oxford treating you? Still loving city life after Cambridge? It's good, yeah. Really good. A bit… slower paced, which is nice. Cambridge was a bit of a bubble, wasn’t it? Everyone so driven, always on. Oxford feels a little more relaxed. Though I do miss having a proper beach nearby. Oh god, me too. Being landlocked is the worst. I keep threatening to move to Brighton just for the sea air. Speaking of…have you heard anything from Liam?  grimaces  Ugh. Don’t even. He messaged last week, trying to be ‘friendly’. Said he “just wanted to check in”. Honestly, the audacity. Seriously? What did you say? I left him on read. And then blocked his number. I’m done with the emotional roller coaster. You’d think after all that time, he’d actually learn something. Good for you! You deserve better than that. He was always… a lot. Remember that time he tried to cook you a romantic dinner and nearly set the kitchen on fire?  laughs  Oh god, please don’t remind me! That was a disaster. Luckily, your flat had a working fire extinguisher! My mum still brings it up whenever she meets him. Mum’s a legend. She’s been asking about you, by the way. She wants to know if you're being properly fed and if I'm looking after you. Aw, that’s sweet. Tell her I’m surviving on lemon and poppyseed cake and the kindness of strangers…and you, obviously.

Right, so I was on the phone to Mam earlier, and you will  not  believe what she's been up to now. Oh dear. Lay it on me. Is it another saga with Uncle Barry and his pigeons? Worse, actually. She’s decided she’s a horticulturalist. Apparently, she’s bought like, thirty different types of begonias. Thirty! Our garden's barely big enough for the washing line. Thirty? That  is  ambitious. Does she even know what begonias  need ? She’s more of a ‘stick it in the ground and hope for the best’ kinda gardener, isn’t she? Exactly! She was asking me for advice, can you believe it? She genuinely wanted to know about 'soil pH levels' and 'deadheading'. I was trying not to laugh down the phone. I told her to just YouTube it. Good tactic. Though YouTube can lead you down some very strange gardening rabbit holes. I once spent three hours watching a man build a self-watering system out of plastic bottles. Oh, I can see that happening to her. Honestly, I reckon most of those begonias are going to end up looking a bit peaky by August. She’s got this idea of winning the village garden competition now. The village garden competition? That's… intense. Honestly, your Mam is a force of nature. She is, isn’t she? Anyway, speaking of things that need nurturing, how’s the basil doing? I swear it looked a bit droopy last time I was over. It’s… hanging in there. I think I overwatered it, then underwatered it, then just generally confused it with my inconsistent attention. It’s a miracle it’s still alive, honestly. Maybe we should get one of those self-watering things you were watching on YouTube. No, no. I think I've learned my lesson. I think the basil just wants to be left alone to quietly perish. I’m more focused on perfecting my sourdough at the moment. Oh, how’s  that  going? Last time you were making it, the kitchen smelled like vinegar for a week. I’ve improved! I think. I’ve been following this recipe from this Italian nonna online. It involves a lot of folding, and a lot of waiting. And apparently, talking to the starter. Talking to the starter? Seriously? Apparently, it encourages the yeast growth. I felt a bit ridiculous doing it, but… it actually seems to be working.

Morning, Gareth. Dreadful weather out there, isn’t it? Though, I suppose it’s good for the garden. Morning, David. Ay, absolutely foul. Needed the wellies just to get from the car park. Garden’s loving it, though, you’re right. Mine’s turned into a bit of a jungle, to be honest. Need a weekend dedicated to battling the bindweed. Bindweed’s the devil’s work. I’ve been trying to get rid of some in the rose garden for… well, years. You’d think with a doctorate in botany, I’d have a better solution. You’d think so, wouldn't you? Though a doctorate doesn’t make you immune to the relentless march of nature, does it? Did you catch any of the football on Saturday? A bit. Turned it off after half an hour. The constant focus on the players’ kids is infuriating. This young lad, son of Bellingham, apparently he's already being scouted. It’s ridiculous! Let the boy  be  a boy. I know what you mean.
