It’s all about exploiting potential before they’ve even had a proper childhood. Remember that snooker player, Ronnie O’Sullivan? Had a rough upbringing, didn't he? Proper talent, though. Always admired that. Absolutely. A genuine prodigy. Speaking of tough childhoods, I had a student telling me about his application to the police force. Said they grilled him relentlessly about his family background. Apparently, they’re particularly wary of applicants with relatives in the armed forces. Really? I’d have thought the armed forces background would be seen as a positive. Discipline, leadership qualities… You’d think so, wouldn’t you? Apparently, there's a concern about potential biases. Bureaucracy gone mad, if you ask me. Still, makes you wonder what kind of people they  are  letting in. A fair point. I’ve got a pile of essays to wade through this afternoon. The usual mix of plagiarism and barely coherent arguments. Honestly, sometimes I think they just throw words at the page and hope for the best. Tell me about it. I’m marking dissertations at the moment. One student seems to think quoting Wikipedia constitutes original research. The audacity! Oh, dear. That’s… optimistic, shall we say? I had one last year who cited his own Facebook posts as evidence. You’re joking! Wish I were. It’s a constant battle, isn't it? Trying to instill some critical thinking skills.

Right, so, Auntie Maureen’s definitely coming for Lily’s christening, then? She confirmed this morning? Yeah, she sent a really long text actually, about how excited she is and how she’s already bought a little outfit. A  very  frilly outfit, apparently. Frilly! Like a princess? Possibly a bit  too  princessy, darling. But it’s the thought that counts. Have you managed to book that photographer yet? The one Sarah recommended? I emailed him, but haven't heard back. I’ll chase him again tomorrow. He’s quite popular, so fingers crossed. It’s just… everything feels a bit chaotic, doesn’t it? The birthday party next week, then the christening the week after… It is a bit full on, I’ll grant you that. But good full on! Everyone’s wanting to celebrate Lily. And your father’s being surprisingly helpful, actually. He offered to sort out the balloons. Balloons! Lots and lots of balloons? Pink ones? Yes, lots and lots of pink balloons, sweetheart. Your Grandad promised. Now, about this work thing… how’s it going with applications? Any luck? It's... frustrating. I sent off three more yesterday, but the silence is deafening. It's like they just vanish into a black hole. I'm starting to wonder if I even  can  do anything other than research. This degree feels… useless sometimes. Don't say that! It's not useless at all. It shows dedication and intelligence. It’s just… the job market is saturated right now. Honestly, it’s awful for everyone. Even people I know who’ve been working for years are suddenly finding themselves redundant. Redundant? What does that mean? It means… sometimes companies have to let people go, darling. It doesn’t mean they’ve done anything wrong. It just means there isn’t enough work for everyone. It’s just… I feel so stuck. I'm living back at home, relying on Mum and Dad... It's not how I envisioned things. Oh, love. You're not a burden. We’re happy to have you here, honestly. And you’re saving money, which is sensible. It won't be forever. Things  will  get better. Have you thought about maybe volunteering somewhere? Just to get some experience and keep you busy? I did look at a couple of things, but everything seemed to require experience  to get  the experience. It’s a catch-22.

Honestly, this weather is dreadful, isn’t it? Rain, rain, rain. Makes you want to just hibernate until spring. Tell me about it! I had to cycle to work this morning and I was soaked through before I even got to the shop. It's not exactly conducive to good customer service when you’re dripping everywhere. Mummy, can we build a fort in the living room? A really, really big one? Maybe later, sweetheart. Mummy needs a coffee first. And we need to talk about New York. Are you still thinking about going in October, Sarah? I am, yeah. I’ve been looking at flights and hotels. It’s… expensive, obviously. But I think we could make it work. I found a really cute little boutique hotel in Greenwich Village. It wasn’t  too  ridiculous in price. Greenwich Village, lovely. Remember when we went to New York with Uncle David and Aunt Carol? Carol lost her purse on the subway. Oh my god, yes! And she was convinced she had been pickpocketed by a professional. Turns out, she’d just left it on the seat! She was furious with herself. What’s a pickpocket? It's someone who tries to steal things from people, darling. Don’t worry about it. Anyway, New York. I’m excited. Have you started thinking about what we’d  do ? I want to see a Broadway show. Definitely. I’ve already been looking at tickets for Wicked. It's a bit touristy, I know, but I’ve always wanted to see it. And we should definitely visit the 9/11 memorial. It’s important. Absolutely. And Central Park, naturally. We need a picnic. Oh! And remember our wedding? It rained on our wedding day, didn’t it? How could I forget? Mum was convinced the whole day was ruined and spent the entire time fretting. But honestly, it made it more memorable. Everyone huddled inside, it was actually quite cozy. Were you a princess at your wedding, Mummy? I was a very happy bride, darling. A bit of a soggy one, but happy! Right, back to New York. What about you, Lucy? Anything you’d like to see? I'm just hoping I can get some time off work. It’s been incredibly busy lately. Old Mr. Henderson keeps changing his mind about the window displays. One minute he wants autumnal, the next he wants Christmas.

Right, so basically, this whole section here, it’s all the raw data from the interviews. Transcribed verbatim, which is… a pain, honestly. They give you this massive document, and you’ve just gotta wade through it. Sounds… fun. How many interviews are we talking? Twelve. Each one averaging about forty-five minutes to an hour. It’s brutal. And the formatting is all over the place. Some are double-spaced, some are single, some have timestamps, some don’t. Seriously? They couldn’t just give you a consistent file? You’d think, wouldn’t you? Apparently consistency is too much to ask. Anyway, the key is, I’ve highlighted all the bits that actually relate to the research question – you know, the stuff about social mobility perceptions in post-industrial towns. Okay, so the highlights are the useful bits. Good system. Yeah. Then, this next part… this is the coding. I’ve gone through and assigned each relevant segment a code. So, like, if someone mentions ‘lack of opportunity,’ that gets coded as ‘OPP-LACK’. If they talk about ‘family background,’ that’s ‘FAM-BACK’ and so on. Right, so it’s like tagging everything for themes? Exactly. It's a thematic analysis, yeah. And this spreadsheet here—it’s a bit messy, I admit—it's where I’ve collated all the codes. Each row is a code, and then in the columns, it’s how many times that code appears across all the interviews. So, that gives you a quick overview of the main themes emerging? Precisely. See here, 'OPP-LACK' comes up, like, twenty-seven times. That’s a big one. ‘FAM-BACK’ is sixteen. ‘EDUC-QUAL’ – education qualifications – is thirteen. It’s starting to paint a picture, you know? Yeah, definitely. That suggests opportunity and family background are huge factors. Makes sense. Is this all you’ve got done then, the coding and the counting? No, next comes the interpretation. I need to write up a proper analysis, drawing out the key patterns and implications. And of course, connect it back to the literature review. That’s the scary part – trying to make it sound intelligent. Yeah, that's always the hard bit. Making it all… cohere. But you've done the heavy lifting, it sounds like. Getting through all that raw data must've been killer. It really was. I think I dreamt in transcripts for a week.

…and then I was trying to build a Lego castle, but all the pieces kept turning into slugs. Like, really realistic slugs. It was terrifying. Oh, that's brilliantly bizarre. Classic dream logic. I had one last night where I was giving a geography lesson… to a class full of badgers. Badgers?! Were they being naughty? Hideously. One kept trying to steal my pointer, another was digging under the desks. It was chaos. Honestly, teaching real eight-year-olds is less stressful. Sounds about right. Did you manage to give the lesson? Eventually. I think I got to the Amazon rainforest before they staged a full-scale revolt. What about you and the slug castle? Did you finish it? No way. It just kept collapsing into increasingly slimy heaps. It felt very symbolic, I don’t know about what though. Maybe my looming workload? Can we get a dog? We’ve talked about this, mate. It's a big responsibility. But I’ll walk it! And feed it! And… and cuddle it! He does have a point. A fluffy friend  would  be nice. Though I'm worried about the slugs. Imagine a slug-dog hybrid. Don’t even. No, still thinking it’s not the right time. The house isn't really set up for it, and we’re both pretty busy. But a doggy! A little puppy! It's a lovely thought. We could look into fostering maybe? Just to see how it goes? We can discuss it. Later. Right now, I need more coffee. Speaking of impossible things… I was thinking about the lottery again this morning. Always a good distraction. What would you do if you won? Honestly? Pay off the mortgage, definitely. And then… maybe a small cottage by the sea. Somewhere ridiculously peaceful. And a professional Lego builder to construct non-slug related things. Can we still get a dog? If you win the lottery? Yes, if we win the lottery, you can pick  any  dog you want. As long as it doesn’t eat the Lego castle. Ooh! A golden retriever! Or a rescue pup. There are so many needing homes. I saw a particularly sweet one at the shelter last week… Alright, alright. Let's not get ahead of ourselves. We haven’t even bought a lottery ticket yet. But… the dream is nice, isn’t it? A little bit of hope in a slug-filled world.

Honestly, the state of A&E last night was… something else. Oh no, what happened? You said you'd had a bit of a tumble on your run? A tumble is putting it mildly. I tripped over a rogue root, went flying, and landed… well, on my face mostly. Luckily, it wasn't broken, I think, but my nose feels like it's been rearranged. Ouch! That sounds awful. Did you hit your head? That's what I always worry about with falls like that. No, thankfully not. I think I tucked my head in instinctively. Mostly just pride and a rapidly swelling nose took a beating. And the wait at A&E… three hours! Ridiculous. Three hours? Seriously? I thought things were bad in London, but that's a joke. What was it like? Packed. Absolute chaos. There was a bloke with a clearly dislocated shoulder screaming, a kid with a head wound, and about a million people coughing. It smelled like disinfectant and desperation. Sounds… pleasant. Did they at least give you something for the pain? Eventually. After two hours, a triage nurse took a look, declared it wasn’t broken, gave me some paracetamol and said to ice it. Paracetamol! As if that’s going to fix a squashed nose. Seriously? That’s rubbish. They barely examined you then? Pretty much. It was just “not broken, off you go.” I think they were just trying to get people through the system. I felt like I was bothering them even  being  there. That’s awful. You should have pushed for a proper assessment. Maybe asked to see a doctor? I probably should have, but honestly, I was just so overwhelmed. And I felt bad taking up more of their time when there were people clearly in a worse state than me. It’s just… frustrating. I can imagine. Still, glad you didn’t break anything. Though a rearranged nose doesn’t sound fun. Have you iced it? Yeah, on and off. It’s still throbbing like mad. I look like Rudolph, honestly. Red and swollen. Oh dear. Well, maybe invest in a good concealer? And if it doesn’t start to improve, you should definitely go back and get it checked out properly. Don’t let them brush you off. I think I will. I'm just wishing I hadn't gone for that run in the first place. Rogue roots, honestly!

…and then young Timmy, bless him, asked if Putin was Father Christmas’s enemy. Honestly, the things they come up with. Had to explain international politics to a seven-year-old this morning. Good grief. That's a tough one. Though, you know, it’s not a bad analogy if you think about it. One delivers presents, the other… well, doesn’t. Ha! You’ve got a point there. It’s just… the news is so relentless, isn’t it? Ukraine, Gaza, the American election looming. Seems like one disaster after another. Makes you wonder what’s going to happen next. It does. And it's all so accessible now, isn't it? Back in our day, you got the evening news, that was it. Now it's a constant barrage. I find myself switching off more and more. Me too. Though, being a teacher, I feel I have a responsibility to be informed. Can’t really explain things to them if I’m in the dark. Anyway, enough doom and gloom. How's the shop doing? Still thinking about expanding the online side of things? Yeah, slowly, slowly. It’s a bit daunting, to be honest. I’m not exactly a digital native, you know? My daughter, Sarah, she keeps telling me I need to get on TikTok, reach a younger audience and all that. TikTok? Good heavens. Seems a long way from selling antique furniture. Exactly! I tried having a look, and it's just… people dancing and doing silly things. I can’t see the connection. I’ve got a young lad helping me with the website, he’s quite good, though a bit pricey. He reckons we can get a decent online presence going, but it'll take time. Well, you’ve built a successful business from scratch, haven't you? You've got a good eye for quality, and you know your stuff. A bit of online presence can only help. Remember old Mr. Henderson, down on the High Street? Refused to adapt, and his shop went under. Don’t remind me. Poor old Herbert. Stubborn as a mule, he was. Though, I tell you what, I miss those days of just chatting with people in the shop. The personal connection. I know what you mean. That's something you lose with online retail. Though, it does free you up to spend more time with the grandchildren, doesn't it?

Honestly, I’m starving. I had such a small lunch, I was too busy trying to get that transcription finished. What are you fancying? They do a decent-looking burger here, don’t they? A burger sounds good, actually. Or maybe that pie of the day? I saw someone with it, looked substantial. Though, thinking about it, I could really go for some fish and chips. It's a Woolwich thing, isn't it? You and your fish and chips! We had it last week. Let’s try something different. This place is nice, really quite cosy actually. I like the old wood panelling. It’s a bit…grand for Woolwich, isn’t it? It is a bit fancier than I expected. It’s a good change from the usual. Though I think it needs more pictures. It feels a bit…bare. Reminds me a bit of the student union bar at uni, actually. All dark wood and a slightly sticky floor. Oh god, university bars. A whole other world. Remember that place, The Phoenix? Always packed. Though I suspect this floor is cleaner. Is your coat warm enough? You seem a little chilly. Yeah, I’m alright. Just thinking. It’s the damp, I think. I’ll be fine once I’ve got some food inside me. Did you catch  Happy Valley  last night? Oh, yes! Brilliant, wasn’t it? Sarah Lancashire is incredible. Utterly terrifying and amazing all at the same time. I’m completely hooked. I’ve been trying to avoid spoilers online. It's so tense! I keep having to look away. I can’t cope with intense scenes, remember? Though I do love a good crime drama. It’s just…stressful. You're such a softie! Speaking of stressful, have you noticed the music in here? It’s…interesting. A bit of a random mix. Yeah, it’s a bit all over the place. They seem to be going for a sort of “classic hits” vibe, but it’s jumping from Elvis to…is that Abba? I think it is. It’s a bit jarring, isn’t it? Still, I could listen to Abba all day. Reminds me of Mum. She always had it playing when I was little. That’s lovely. Have you heard anything from your sister recently? How's Winston the cat doing? I spoke to her on Sunday. Winston is being his usual self: completely aloof and demanding head scratches.

Aye, honestly, the light in Skye was just… unreal. Never seen anything like it. Completely different from around here, even. Oh, I bet. I’ve only ever seen photos, but they’re stunning. You getting some good shots, then? Proper landscape stuff? Trying to, aye. It's tricky, though, isn't it? You think you’ve got the framing right, the exposure perfect, then you get it back on the computer and it just… lacks something. Had a real nightmare with the Old Man of Storr. Kept getting glare off the rocks. Glare can be murder. You using a polarising filter? That helps cut down on reflections. I do, aye, but even with that, it was fighting me. Ended up taking about fifty pictures just to get one I was half happy with. Ended up editing the heck out of it, to be honest. It's not  quite  the reality, but it’s closer. That’s the thing, isn’t it? Capturing the  feeling  of a place, rather than just a straight representation. I tried doing some street photography in Barcelona last year, and it was impossible. The light was just too harsh, too direct. Everything looked flat. Barcelona, eh? I’ve always fancied going. Proper heat, is it? Heard it gets scorchin’. Scorching. July and August are brutal. I went in May, which was much more manageable. Still warm, but not unbearable. The architecture is incredible, though. Gaudi’s stuff is just… bonkers. I’ve seen pictures. Like something out of a fairytale. Right bizarre. So, you take a lot of street photos then? Portraits and that? I try to. It's a challenge. You need to be quick, unobtrusive. And you get some funny looks, obviously. Had an old guy in the Gothic Quarter yell at me once, thought I was trying to steal his soul with my camera. No way! That's mental. You just get on with it then, eh? Ignore the grumpy old men. I’m more of a landscapes man myself, though. Just find it more… peaceful. Less chance of someone giving you grief. Though the midges in Skye were giving  me  grief. Oh, the midges! Don’t even get me started. They were biblical on the Isle of Mull last summer. Smothered in repellent and still got eaten alive. Aye, they’re ruthless. Spend more time swatting them than taking photos, sometimes. Still, worth it for the scenery, don’t you think?

Right, so, the week ahead. Anything massively pressing? Apart from the usual chaos, obviously. Not really, work's… work. Year twos are driving me round the bend with their phonics, honestly. They just refuse to blend. It’s like talking to a brick wall sometimes. Oh, bless you. They'll get there eventually, won’t they? It just feels never-ending when you’re in the thick of it. Are you managing to get any lesson planning done, or is it all just firefighting? Firefighting, definitely firefighting. I’ve got that observation next Friday, which is looming like a dark cloud. I need to at least  pretend  I have a cohesive plan, you know? You always manage to pull it off. You’re brilliant with them, even when they’re being little terrors. Anyway, what about Leo? Has the nursery got back about a space? They said they might have something coming up after Easter, but it’s a waiting list within a waiting list, apparently. Honestly, it's a nightmare. I feel so guilty leaving him with Grandma all the time, she’s amazing, don’t get me wrong, but she deserves a life too! She does. And she’d say it’s no bother, you know she would. But it’s not fair to rely on her constantly. I’ll have another look at those private nurseries, see if I can find anything closer that might have a space. That would be amazing, Mum, thank you. Honestly, it would lift a huge weight off my mind. I just want him to be socialising with other little ones, you know? And maybe get a bit of peace while I’m trying to mark 30 sets of handwriting. Right, well, I'll do some digging. What about us? Are you free Tuesday evening? I was thinking we could finally watch that new series everyone's raving about – ‘The Serpent’ is it? Ooh, yes! I’ve heard good things. Tuesday sounds good. Unless little Leo decides to have a midnight wake-up call and ruin my life… it’s been a bit patchy lately, hasn't it? Oh, that’s rough. Is it teething again? I can bring some teething gel over if you like? That would be brilliant, actually. I think it might be. He’s been chewing on his hand all morning. And he's just generally grumpy. It’s exhausting.

This pasta’s lovely, honestly. You’ve outdone yourself, Anon. It’s alright, innit? Just a bit of pesto and some cherry tomatoes. Nothing special. Though, gotta say, working all day building stuff makes  anything  taste good. You’re telling me! My brain feels completely fried. We had a massive problem with the production line today - a sensor completely packed in, and it took hours to diagnose. Hours! And then Ms. Davies was breathing down my neck the whole time. Ugh, Ms. Davies. Sounds delightful. Honestly, I’m starting to think I need a new job. This conference centre is… draining. It's just endless spreadsheets and complaining delegates. What’s wrong with spreadsheets? Seems alright to me. Easy for you to say! You actually  build  things. I just organise people to talk  about  things. It feels… pointless sometimes. Plus, Brenda from accounts keeps wearing the exact same outfit every Tuesday. It’s a floral dress, and it’s genuinely unsettling. Brenda sounds like a character. Speaking of outfits, you wouldn't believe what Mark wore on our date last night. A beige… suit. Beige! Oh, no. Beige is a crime against fashion. Seriously! He said it was “sophisticated”. Sophisticatedly awful, more like. I tried to steer him towards something a bit more… vibrant, but he’s very attached to his neutral tones. Beige is for old men. Got to have a bit of colour, right? I’ve got this new hi-vis jacket, proper bright orange. Can’t miss me on site. That’s… practical. Definitely a statement piece. So, is this Mark… a keeper, despite the beige? I don’t know. He’s nice, genuinely. Just… a bit safe. And he keeps talking about his stamp collection. Stamps?! Oh, dear. That  is  a bit… intense. I’m seeing someone, actually. Chloe. She's a nurse. Properly funny, and doesn’t mind getting her hands dirty. That’s great! Is she local? No, she's from Manchester. We met at a gig in London a few weeks back. We’re trying to sort out when to see each other again, with both our work schedules. It's proving tricky. Tell me about it. Trying to juggle a relationship and a demanding job is exhausting. You end up prioritising work just to get through the week. It’s true. You lose track of who you are outside of it. I haven’t bought any new clothes in months.

Right then, who’s for another cuppa? Mine’s gone a bit cold, hasn’t it? Oh, go on then, Arthur. I wouldn’t mind one. Though I really shouldn’t, should I? Doctor said… you know. Said you shouldn’t enjoy life, did he? Nonsense. A good cuppa solves most things. I’ll have one too, thank you. Earl Grey if you’ve got it, Margaret? Of course, Bernard. Just brewing a fresh pot now. Though honestly, Arthur, it’s the third you’ve had since lunch! Well, what else is a retired man supposed to do? Sit and count the dust bunnies? Besides, it keeps the circulation going. You know what the doctor says about that. He said you were to moderate your caffeine intake, Arthur, not have a free-for-all. Moderate! That’s a strong word, isn’t it? I’m not a racing driver, am I? Just a simple man enjoying a simple brew. He’s got a point, you know. A bit of tea and a biscuit – what harm can it do? Though I do remember your late wife, Elsie, keeping a close eye on your tea consumption. Elsie was a force of nature, that one. She could silence a room with a single glare. And she had a particular fondness for strong tea herself, ironically enough. She'd say "Arthur, you'll be bouncing off the walls!" Here we are. Earl Grey for Bernard, and… Arthur, I’ve made yours a bit weaker this time, just for peace of mind. Weaker? Oh, now you’re just being cruel, Margaret. It'll taste like coloured water. Oh, don't be silly, Arthur. She's just looking out for you. You know she worries. It’s a thoughtful gesture. And a good brew needs to be appreciated. Though I confess, I’m rather partial to a digestive with mine. Anyone? I’ve got some ginger biscuits, Bernard. They’re a little bit healthier, perhaps? Ginger? Oh no, I can’t abide ginger. Gives me heartburn something terrible. A plain biscuit will do nicely. Honestly, you lot. Arguing about biscuits now. It's a wonder we ever got through a childminding course together, Margaret. Remember little Timmy and the jam? Oh, don't remind me! That was a disaster. Jam everywhere. It took me hours to clean up. And Timmy just sat there, giggling. Children. They’re little agents of chaos, aren’t they?

Honestly, this roast is amazing, Mum. You’ve outdone yourself. Oh, go on! It’s just a bit of effort, isn’t it? Glad you all like it. Rhys, you having enough Yorkshire pudding? Loads, thank you. Best Yorkshire puddings ever. Seriously. Nothing beats a good Norfolk roast. Absolutely. Reminds me of Sunday dinners at my Nan’s. Though hers were… considerably less refined. More gravy, less finesse. Less finesse is putting it mildly, darling. Remember the time she put a whole clove of garlic in the custard? How could I forget? I nearly choked! She insisted it was “for the flavour”. She was a character, your Nan. Speaking of characters, did you lot see that protest in London on the news? The one outside the art gallery? Oh, vaguely. Something about… funding cuts? Yeah, apparently they're trying to shut down a really important community art space. Always happens, doesn't it? First the libraries, now the art centres. It’s depressing. London’s losing its soul a bit, I think. Everything’s becoming too polished, too expensive. I was down there last week for a conference and the hotel was… astronomical. Honestly, five hundred quid a night for a room the size of a shoebox. Five hundred! You're joking! I wouldn’t pay that for a week in the Bahamas. Speaking of which, are we still on for Cornwall this year? I think so. We need to look at somewhere that’s dog-friendly, though. And not too far from a decent pub. That’s crucial. You and your pubs! Though, I can’t blame you. Finding a good pub in Norfolk is easy, but elsewhere can be a nightmare. It’s a skill, honestly. A highly refined skill. Did anyone hear back about those CRB checks for volunteering at the school, by the way? I’m supposed to be helping with the art club next week. I got mine through yesterday. Everything seemed okay. They were surprisingly quick. I’m still waiting. Honestly, the bureaucracy is ridiculous sometimes. It's not as if I've been up to no good. You? Never! You’re the most organised person I know. That’s kind of you to say. Though, I did once accidentally hotwire a go-kart when I was eight… long story.  Hotwire  a go-kart? Now  that’s  a story. We need to hear this. Oh, Mum, please!

Right so spill. How was Italy? Honestly, give me all the details. Did you eat ALL the pasta? Oh my god, it was incredible. Honestly, the best. And yes, I ate approximately my body weight in pasta. Carbonara, cacio e pepe, you name it, I devoured it. Seriously, I'm going to need to live on salad for a month. Worth it though, right? Did you do much sightseeing or was it mostly just… food-focused? A bit of both actually. Rome was amazing, obviously – Colosseum, Vatican City, all that jazz. But honestly, some of the best bits were just wandering around little towns, finding hidden restaurants, and people-watching. Oh, and the gelato. Don't even get me started on the gelato. Sounds idyllic. Did you meet anyone interesting? Apart from all the handsome Italian chefs, obviously. Haha! Well, there was this guy at a wine tasting… very charming, spoke terrible English, but we managed to communicate through gestures and a lot of laughter. It didn’t go anywhere, but it was fun. How was work while I was gone? Did everything implode without me? It was… chaotic. Old man Hemmings decided to completely overhaul the project schedule on the Tuesday, then complained when no one could implement it immediately. Classic Hemmings. And Sarah keeps asking about Daniel. Ugh,  still  going on about Daniel? Seriously? It’s been, what, two years? I know! It's exhausting. She keeps hinting that maybe they were meant to be and I'm like, ‘Sarah, he cheated on you with his personal trainer. Move on!’ Honestly, some people just love wallowing. Speaking of exes, have you heard anything from Leo? He messaged me a couple of weeks ago asking about you. Oh god, no. Please tell me he didn’t try to get your number for ulterior motives. No, no, it was just a genuine ‘how are you?’ message. I didn’t reply, obviously. I forwarded it to you, remember? Oh yeah! Right! I completely forgot. I probably ignored it. Good. He’s a menace. Anyway, let’s not talk about awful people. What are you doing tonight? Fancy ordering a takeaway and having a proper catch-up? I’ve got that new true crime documentary everyone’s been talking about. Ooh, yes! Perfect. I’m starving after all that healthy airport food. What kind of takeaway are we thinking? Indian? Thai? Hmm, leaning towards Indian.

Did you speak to Sarah today? How’s she doing? Yeah, I gave her a call this morning. She sounded… tired. Really tired. Said the chemo’s hit her hard this week. Mostly just nausea, apparently, but it's knocking her for six. Oh, poor thing. It’s awful isn’t it? Seeing her go through all of this. I keep wanting to  do  something, but she’s so resolute about just getting on with it, you know? Doesn’t want a fuss. Exactly. And she’s really good at putting on a brave face. She was mostly asking about the kids, actually. Wanted to know how Leo’s doing in football practice. She didn’t want to talk about herself for long. She’s incredible. It just feels so… unfair. I keep thinking about that holiday we all took to Cornwall last year. She was so vibrant, full of energy. It feels like a lifetime ago. It does. It really does. Anyway, shifting gears slightly, I was having another look at Rightmove this evening. Anything new pop up in the village? Just the old Miller place. Still ridiculously overpriced, even after that price drop. And the description is full of estate agent waffle. “Charming character property…” it's basically a crumbling cottage with a damp patch. Right? It's taking the mickey. I’m starting to think we’re just going to be stuck here for the foreseeable. There's literally nothing coming up that ticks all the boxes. Four bedrooms, garden big enough for the dog, and not needing a complete gut renovation. It’s a tall order. And affordable! Let’s not forget affordable. We need to think about the planning permission too, don't we? If we did manage to find something that needed work, getting permission for an extension could be a nightmare. Old Mrs. Henderson next door would object to anything. You’re right. She'd probably argue it blocked her sunlight. Honestly, I sometimes think she just enjoys complaining. I saw her glaring at Mr. Davies for mowing his lawn before 9 am last week. Oh,  please . It's a lawn. It's not a sacred ritual. But you know what she's like. I think we need to lower our expectations. Maybe look at places a little further out, even if it’s a longer commute? I’m reluctant to do that. I like being close to everything, the school, the shops… And I’m already spending enough time on the train as it is.

Honestly, I’m starting to dread coming in on a Monday. Not because of the work, but because of  them . Oh, don't even get me started. Who’s set you off this time? Is it the overflowing bins again? Because I swear, some of them think the communal kitchen is their personal dumping ground. Worse, actually. It’s the music. Always the music. Boom, boom, boom, rattling the windows. And it’s always the same three songs on repeat. Like, do they not  own  headphones? Ugh, the bass. It travels, doesn't it? I can feel it in my flat sometimes, and I’m two floors up. It's inconsiderate, plain and simple. I had a complaint last week about a student playing acoustic guitar at 11 pm. Acoustic guitar! Can you believe it? Seriously? An acoustic guitar is hardly a rave. They're focusing on the wrong things. It’s the thumping bass I can’t stand. Makes my teeth ache. And it’s always when I'm trying to read. Oh, reading. Don’t even. I tried to mark essays in the common room yesterday. Impossible. Between the music and the constant chatter, it was like trying to concentrate in a nightclub. Right? And the leaving dirty dishes everywhere. I genuinely don’t understand how some people can live like that. It’s not hard to rinse a plate! It’s a complete lack of respect, that’s what it is. For the building, for other residents, for  us  who have to clean up after them. I spent half an hour this morning clearing a mountain of pizza boxes. Pizza boxes, yeah. That's a classic. It’s always pizza. Or instant noodles. Honestly, it’s like they’ve never seen a proper kitchen. And the smell. The lingering smell of stale food… it’s disgusting. I've started carrying air freshener with me just to survive. Good shout. I’ve considered industrial-strength bleach, but I suspect that would get me in trouble. It’s just… exhausting, isn’t it? Dealing with all this nonsense day in, day out. It is. And the worst part is, you try to politely ask them to be considerate, and they just look at you like you’re the unreasonable one. “It’s a student hall,” they say. “It’s meant to be lively.” Lively is one thing, a complete free-for-all is another.

Honestly, seeing those people in Bruges pretending they’d  discovered  Belgium was hilarious. Like, you're on a package tour, Sheila, it's not an archaeological dig! Package tours aren’t so bad, love. Keeps things… organised. Though I did overhear a bloke complaining the beer wasn’t ‘British enough’. British enough! In Belgium! Oh, don’t get me started. My sister Doreen went on one to Germany last year. Came back moaning the sausages weren't Cumberland. Honestly. You can’t take some people anywhere. Exactly! And they all flock to the Christmas markets. It's just a load of overpriced trinkets and gluhwein, isn't it? Though, I did get a lovely hand-painted bauble in Antwerp… Antwerp’s nice. Bit busy, though. Reminds me of Brighton on a Bank Holiday. Traffic’s murder. Though, Brighton's traffic is always murder, isn't it? Even  walking  along the seafront is a contact sport these days. Tell me about it. I had to fight my way through a gaggle of stag-dos just to get to the pier yesterday. Honestly. And then a swarm of pigeons descended on my ice cream. Oh, no! That’s dreadful! I'm trying to learn Dutch, actually. Figured if I’m going to be traipsing around the Low Countries, I should at least be able to order a waffle without sounding like a complete idiot. Dutch, eh? Good luck with that. Sounds like someone gargling pebbles. I tried a bit of Spanish once, when we were thinking of retiring to… somewhere warm. Didn’t get very far. Speaking of retiring, how’s your neighbour, Mr. Henderson, coping? He seemed dreadfully lost when he finished work. He's alright, I think. Mostly potters about in the garden now. Says he’s taken up birdwatching. Apparently, there’s a rare spotted flycatcher visiting his apple tree. Can't say I've ever noticed a flycatcher. That sounds…peaceful. It’s just, I’m already dreading the thought of finishing my degree and then… what? The ‘real world’ seems terrifying. You'll be fine, love. You're a bright girl. Remember my Terry? Always said university was the best thing he ever did. Though his boys were his pride and joy. Raising boys is… a different kettle of fish. It is that. All mud and noise. Mine were always covered in something or other. Though they turned out alright.

Seriously though, this Ireland thing is huge, isn't it? All that stuff about legalising same-sex marriage… it's mad to think it wasn't already. It  is  massive. And genuinely moving. My auntie Maureen was over there for a bit, visiting her friend, and she said the atmosphere was electric. Everyone just…happy. It’s just… basic equality, isn’t it? Like, why even  have  a vote on that? Should just be a given. Makes you think about all the other stuff that's still messed up. Exactly! And it's not like Ireland’s some super-progressive place, historically. That makes it even more impressive. It shows things  can  change, you know? Even quickly. Yeah. Mr. Henderson was talking about it in history today, saying it showed a real shift in societal values. He went on a bit, as he does. Oh, Mr. Henderson. Always one for a lecture. Did he mention anything about how much the Catholic church opposed it? Yeah, he did. Apparently, they were throwing everything at it, trying to scare people. Didn’t work, though. No! Good. Honestly, some of the things my mum says… you wouldn’t believe it. She was going on about ‘the sanctity of marriage’ and I was like, “Mum, you've been married three times!” Oh, that's brilliant! My mum wouldn’t say anything like that, she’s too… embarrassing in other ways. Like, she tries to be cool and ‘down with the kids’ but it just never works. Oh, we all have those mums. Mine tried to use a TikTok dance at my cousin’s wedding. It did not go well. No way! Oh god. That's amazing. Traumatic, actually. Anyway, back to Ireland. It’s just… uplifting. It gives you a bit of hope, doesn't it? It does. It’s a lot better than listening to the news about everything else going on. Speaking of which, have you seen what old man Peterson is saying now? He’s claiming that… Oh, don't even get me started on Peterson. That man lives in a bubble of his own making. Honestly, it's like he’s deliberately trying to provoke people. Exactly! It's just… tiring. It is. Right, enough politics. It’s nearly your birthday, isn't it? Are you thinking about a party? I don’t know. Maybe just a few mates. Don't want anything too big.

Right well, that was a good bit of sausage, that was. Not quite Doreen’s, mind you. She could make a sausage sing, Doreen could. She could indeed. Remember that time she entered that sausage competition at the village fete? Proper Norfolk sausage, it was. Oh, I remember. Old Mr. Henderson nearly had a fit when he found out she’d used his secret spice blend. Thought she’d stolen it! Aye, a right kerfuffle that was. But Doreen, she just batted her eyelashes and said it was a tribute. Worked a treat, it did. Won her a blue ribbon, it did. She always was a charmer. Though, speaking of…Have you seen young Timmy’s hamster? I can’t find Mr. Nibbles anywhere. Now that  is  odd. He usually squeaks like a rusty gate whenever you’re about. Good heavens, don't tell me… did anyone leave the microwave door open again? Oh, don’t even  say  that, David! Little Alfie did it last year with his goldfish! We didn’t speak to him for a week. A goldfish? In the microwave? Good Lord. They don’t learn, do they? Remember when I was an apprentice, old Mr. Finch…he had a lad, just starting out, put a lathe tool in the grinder? Oh dear. Not a good idea. No, not a good idea at all! Thing exploded, sent sparks flying everywhere. Nearly took his eyebrows off. Mr. Finch went absolutely purple. Said something about ruining a perfectly good tool and a perfectly good Friday afternoon. Lathe tools are serious business. Precision engineering, and all that. You wouldn't put one in a microwave, would you? Wouldn’t dream of it! Though, I reckon a bit of steel would probably do more damage to a microwave than a hamster. Right, I’m going to have a look. This is giving me palpitations. Honestly, these children… it’s a wonder anything survives. I’m checking the microwave  first . Just be prepared for the worst, Margaret. It’s probably just hiding, though. Hamsters are notoriously sneaky. Sneaky little blighters, they are. Give me a good piece of sausage any day. Less stress involved. More flavour, too. Oh… my… goodness. You are  never  going to believe this. What is it? What’s happened? Oh dear. Here we go. Well, don’t leave us in suspense, Margaret! It's not  in  the microwave... it's  on  top of it… wearing Alfie’s little cowboy hat.

Honestly, the state of things… I saw a headline today about a cat who’d apparently ordered things online using its owner’s Amazon account. Just… pawing at the screen! You’re kidding! A cat? Ordering what, cat food? More scratching posts? It's a sign of the times, isn't it? Everything online, everything automated. Reminds me of those stories about mirror writing. Did you know Leonardo Da Vinci was a prolific mirror writer? Though I suspect this cat wasn't making a grand artistic statement. No, I think it was… Christmas decorations, apparently. The owner woke up to a dozen inflatable Santas arriving. It’s just utterly bizarre. Speaking of bizarre, did you see the latest figures on house prices? They’re absolutely ludicrous. Don’t even  start  me on house prices. We’re effectively priced out of moving anywhere remotely decent. It's discouraging. I was looking at a tiny terraced place near the park, and it’s gone up £30,000 in six months. It's madness. You'd think they’d want people to  be able  to buy houses. It all feels so… unfair. And the banks aren’t helping, are they? Still offering ridiculously small interest rates on savings, while simultaneously making a fortune off mortgages. Banks have always been… opportunists. I remember back in the 80s, the building societies… even then, they weren’t known for their generosity. Though, things were simpler then. Less reliance on technology, less debt, less… everything. Simpler, maybe. Not necessarily better. Remember when you had to actually  go  to the bank to pay bills? Queuing for ages? I do. And now we’re all worrying about online security, passwords, phishing scams… it's exhausting. I’m trying to do that cryptic crossword, but even  that  feels tech-influenced. Clues about algorithms and social media influencers! Cryptic crosswords are a dying art. They require a certain… lateral thinking. Something I fear is diminishing in the younger generation. Although, perhaps I’m just being a grumpy old woman. You’re not grumpy! Just… discerning. Have you been following the American political scene at all? It’s like watching a train wreck in slow motion. Don't even mention it. I try to avoid it. It’s all so… draining. It feels like the world is perpetually on the brink of some sort of disaster. Exactly. It's best not to dwell.

Right, books away. Tablets away. It’s nearly bedtime, and we’ve talked about this. No screen time thirty minutes before bed. But Mummy! I was  just  about to finish building the Ninja temple in Lego Ninjago Tower! It’s almost done! Yeah, and I was about to fight the End Dragon in Minecraft! I needed one more diamond!  One  more! I know, I know. It’s frustrating, isn't it? But your eyes need to rest. All that glowing… it makes it harder to fall asleep. But Kai has a new spinjitzu master technique! I haven’t even tried it yet! And the End Dragon has a new armour! It's super strong! Look, you can both come back to it first thing in the morning. Promise. We can even set a timer so you have a good, long, uninterrupted session. But right now? Books. Or… we could read  together . But Ninjago is way more exciting than books. Minecraft has more adventures! You can build anything! I understand that. They  are  very exciting. But books are adventures too! And reading helps your brain grow. It helps you with your spelling, and your writing, and… well, everything really. But in Minecraft, I’m a builder  and  a fighter! And that’s wonderful! You’re very creative in Minecraft. But you can be a builder and a fighter in books too! There are books about knights, and explorers, and… even ninjas! Are there Minecraft books? There are, actually. Although, I do think creating your own worlds is a bit more special, don’t you? More imaginative? But let’s not get sidetracked. How about this: if you both read for half an hour, we can try and build something  together  tomorrow – out of… actual Lego! Not just the game. Hmm… what could we build? A bigger Ninja temple? A castle! A really massive castle, with a secret dungeon! And a dragon! Those sound like excellent ideas. Now, show me those books. And maybe, just maybe, we can find a story with a dragon in it. Deal? Deal. But I'm finishing the spinjitzu master technique  tomorrow  first thing. And I’m getting that diamond! Absolutely. You both deserve a good diamond-hunting, dragon-slaying session. Now, books please. And quiet voices. Mummy needs a cup of tea after all this negotiating. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

Honestly, that week in Cornwall was just what I needed. Didn’t realise how stressed I was until I was actually  there , you know? Just… sea air and pasties. It sounded amazing, Mum! All your photos were gorgeous. Did you manage to get down to St Ives? I’ve always wanted to go. We did, love, but it was  packed . Properly rammed. We went on a Tuesday hoping it wouldn’t be quite so bad, but still, you could barely move. Still, had a lovely cream tea overlooking the harbour. Sounds really nice. I’m just glad you managed to get away, honestly. You deserve a break. You’ve been running around after everyone for ages. Oh, don’t be silly. It’s what mums do. Speaking of running around, what are your plans for today, you two? Anything exciting? Not hugely, to be fair. I’ve got a stock take at work later, which is going to be  fun  - said no one ever. But before that, I was thinking we could maybe go into Lichfield, do a bit of window shopping? Yeah, that sounds good. I need to pick up a birthday card for Gran anyway. Her birthday’s next week, isn’t it? It is! The 18th. We need to think about what we’re getting her. She said she didn’t want anything extravagant, just… something thoughtful. She’s so hard to buy for. Maybe a nice photo frame with a picture of the grandkids? She always has loads of photos scattered around. That’s a good idea. Or perhaps one of those little succulent plants? She always admired the one I had in my room at uni. Mmm, both lovely ideas. We can have a proper think later. Right now, more coffee anyone? I’ve just made a fresh pot. Yes, please! I think I need another one after the thought of that stock take. Me too. Oh, and Mum, did you ever manage to find out what happened with Auntie Brenda’s cat? You were saying something about it being missing when you were on the phone last week? Oh, poor little Winston! Yes, she found him. Turns out he’d gotten himself stuck in a neighbour’s shed. Apparently, he’d been lured in by the smell of tuna! Oh, bless him! That’s a relief. Winston’s such a character. Always getting into mischief.

This sandwich is… underwhelming. Seriously, five quid for this? It’s mostly bread. Tell me about it. I got the chicken and bacon and it tastes like sadness. Should’ve gone to Greggs. Honestly, Greggs is a lifesaver. Or we could’ve just gone to that little cafe near the station. Remember, the one where Old Man Hemmings always is? Yeah, but he stares at you the whole time. Makes you feel like you’re doing something wrong just for eating a sausage roll. Fair point. Anyone seen Ben lately? He’s been proper ghosting everyone since the History test. I think he’s still reeling. Mr. Davies absolutely  grilled  him about the Crimean War. Apparently, Ben thought Florence Nightingale just handed out flowers. Seriously? He’s supposed to be one of the smart ones. Though, thinking about it, Davies is a bit harsh. Like, he expects us to know everything about every conflict ever. My Grandad fought in the Falklands, and even  he  doesn’t know everything about it. True. He went on about tactical disadvantage the other day and didn’t even mention logistics. It’s like he thinks war is all glory and no, you know, actual stuff. Speaking of which, did you see that documentary on Channel 4 last night about the Ukrainian conflict? It was… intense. Yeah, I caught bits of it. Proper bleak. Makes you think, doesn’t it? All that stuff happening, and we’re here worrying about sandwich fillings. It does. Although, honestly, I need a distraction. Anyone fancy a game of Magic: The Gathering after this? I finally built my new deck. Ooh, yes! I’m in. I’ve been practicing with my enchantress build. Prepare to be defeated, boys. Oh, it is  on . I’ve got a new rare card I’ve been saving. It’s going to wreck everyone. By the way, did they announce the new Head Boy and Girl yet? Not yet. Apparently, Mrs. Harris is making a whole song and dance about it during assembly on Friday. I heard Lizzie Thompson is a frontrunner. Ugh, Lizzie? Really? She’s so…perfect. Like, suspiciously perfect. I bet she’s got a whole team of people stage-managing her life. Maybe. I'm hoping for Raj. He's actually a decent guy, and not afraid to speak his mind. Although he did get in trouble for pointing out that the school’s Diversity and Inclusion policy felt…a bit tokenistic.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is the  worst  physics teacher ever. He just stands there and drones on and on. You can tell he doesn't even  like  teaching. Seriously! I thought it was just me. He explains everything so… complicatedly. Like, he’s trying to be clever but it just makes it harder to understand. Remember when he was trying to explain momentum? It took him like, fifteen minutes to get to the actual formula. Oh my god, YES! And then when someone finally asked him to simplify it, he just sighed and repeated it louder. As if volume equals comprehension? Exactly! And he keeps using phrases like ‘as we’ve previously established’ when half the class has literally just switched off. It’s so condescending. Ugh, and Mrs. Peterson, our form tutor, is just… absent. She never seems to notice anything. Like, Ben was crying in the corner yesterday and she just walked past! What?! No way! I didn’t even see that. Honestly, she just spends the whole time on her phone. I swear she's playing Candy Crush or something. I think she is! Seriously. She barely makes eye contact. Speaking of eye contact, did you see Chloe trying to flirt with Mr. Harrison in the library today?  No way!  Chloe? Mr. Harrison? That's… ambitious. He's like, ancient. I know, right? It was so awkward. He just sort of stared straight ahead and pretended she wasn’t there. It was glorious. Haha! Oh, did you finish that English reading assignment? The one on  To Kill a Mockingbird ? I’m so behind. Nearly. I’m on chapter… ten, I think? It's actually really good, though. A bit slow at the beginning, but it's picking up. Really? I’m struggling. It just feels… heavy. And Miss Evans keeps asking us really deep questions about symbolism and I just want to scream ‘I don’t know!’ I know what you mean. She’s intense. Oh! Have you seen the trailer for that new film,  17 Again ? Ooh, no! Is it good? It looks hilarious! Like, Matthew Perry goes back to being seventeen? Imagine! It’s totally my fantasy to relive high school, but like, knowing everything I know now. That would be amazing. You could avoid all the embarrassing moments. Oh, speaking of embarrassing moments, did you hear what happened with Liam and the custard in the canteen?

Honestly, the thought of Monday… it’s actively making my stomach churn. Need a plan,  something  to look forward to after this weekend’s done. Tell me about it. Though, work wasn’t  terrible  today. Managed to perfect that sourdough recipe, finally. Old Man Hemmings practically wept with joy when he tasted it. Hemmings cries over everything! Remember when Brenda accidentally put salt instead of sugar in his coffee? Thought the world was ending. Right? Drama king. Anyway, speaking of looking forward to things, still on for Transylvania in October, yeah? I’ve been looking at flights. Transylvania! Absolutely. Still need to book the accommodation properly, though. I was having a nightmare trying to find somewhere that wasn’t… you know, actively advertising vampire hunting tours. Oh my god, that’s awful! You want spooky, not actively encouraging a stake through the heart. I’m good with booking that, actually. I’ve got a knack for weird accommodation. Excellent. You’re a lifesaver, Lou. I’m just trying to figure out the rota for the café while we're gone. Old Man Hemmings will revolt if I’m away for too long. You could get Bruce to cover some shifts? He said he was looking for extra hours. Bruce? Seriously? The Bruce who thinks pineapple on pizza is a culinary masterpiece? I know, I know. It’s a last resort. Honestly, the man’s tastebuds are…questionable. Speaking of questionable decisions, did you hear about Sarah getting laser eye surgery? No! Seriously? Sarah? That’s…brave. She’s terrified of needles. Apparently, she had this whole breakdown convinced they were going to laser  into  her brain. Her boyfriend, Ben, had to talk her down for an hour. Oh, bless him. Ben’s a saint. Though, you know, she always did say she wanted to be able to see “like a hawk.” I think that’s why she did it. Fair enough. Still, sounds a bit full-on. Though, I gotta say, I’ve been thinking about getting my eyes checked. Getting a bit blurry reading the specials board at work, you know? Keeps costing me in mistakes. You’d think being Australian, you'd have hawk vision from all the sunshine. Nah, mate. Sunshine just gives me wrinkles. Besides, down under, we say “sharp as a tack,” not “sharp as a hawk.” Different hemisphere, different metaphors. That’s a good one!

Right, so the playlist for the party… I was thinking a bit of everything? Some 80s, some current stuff, a little bit of… what do you guys like at the moment? ‘Dynamite’ by BTS! And… Taylor Swift! I like that song with the… the beat! The one we heard in the car. Oh, ‘Blinding Lights’? By The Weeknd? Good shout! Okay, definitely those. And I’ll add some stuff my friends like, but I want it to be stuff everyone can dance to. No one wants a party with a rubbish playlist. Can we have the ‘Let It Go’ song from  Frozen ? Just once? Okay, okay, one  Frozen  song. But just one! We don’t want to scare everyone off. Speaking of which, have you two thought about what you want to  wear  to the party? I want to wear my superhero costume! Hmm, maybe not the  full  superhero costume, darling. It might be a bit much for inside. What about your new blue trousers and a t-shirt? Okay… but can I have my mask? We’ll see. And you, sweetie? What are you thinking? I want to wear my sparkly dress! The pink one. Perfect! That’s lovely. Right, that's outfits sorted. Oh! I was thinking, before the party, maybe we could do a little photoshoot? I want some nice family photos. Like posing? Yes! Posing! Maybe dress up a little? I was thinking we could do a bit of an  Alice in Wonderland  theme? I’ve got a white rabbit hat somewhere… I want to be the Queen of Hearts! And shout, “Off with their heads!” We’ll work on the shouting, maybe just a little bit. No real heads off, promise. Okay, photoshoot… and then we need to think about food. I was thinking pizza… and maybe some crisps? And cake! Chocolate cake! And cake, of course. You’re very persuasive. Now, have you two been practicing your aerial hoop? Auntie Sarah said she might be able to give you a little lesson at the party, if you’re good. I can do a spin now! I can almost hold upside down! That's brilliant! Just… maybe not  too  high, okay? Safety first. Oh! And I almost forgot… Dad signed us up for the Muddy obstacle course next month! Muddy?! Woo hoo! Yeah, it sounds… chaotic. But fun. Just promise me no swearing, okay? Even if it’s really,  really  muddy.

Right, well, that was a good bit of pizza, wasn’t it? Not too much garlic, thankfully. Reminds me of when your mother… bless her… tried to make a pizza from scratch. Burned the roof off the kitchen, she did. Oh, don’t start, Arthur. You’ve told that story a thousand times. It wasn’t  that  bad. Just a little… smoky. And she blamed the oven, naturally. It’s amazing how much blame can be apportioned to household appliances. My wife swears the washing machine shrinks everything deliberately. Mmm, this is  really  good. Did you make this, Mark? I did, actually. Found a recipe online. It’s surprisingly easy. Though I nearly set off the smoke alarm trying to melt the chocolate. Seems I share your mother’s talent for near-disasters, Arthur. Can I have another slice? Please? Of course, dear. Help yourself. So, how are the exam results looking, you two? Any nerves settling down? Not really. I think I messed up the history one. I completely blanked on the dates for the French Revolution. Dates, eh? Always the dates. Never could remember dates myself. Pointless information, if you ask me. It’s about understanding the context, Arthur. The  why  things happened, not just  when . Though, admittedly, remembering the dates is helpful for the marks. I think I did alright in maths. Miss Davies said I was ‘showing promise’. Whatever that means. “Showing promise” is excellent, love! That’s a definite compliment. Did you hear back about your driving lessons, darling? Yeah, I’ve got my first one next week. I’m so scared. What if I stall in the middle of a roundabout? Roundabouts are a menace. Absolute menace. All those lanes and arrows. Used to be a perfectly good crossroads, then they go and stick a roundabout there. Arthur’s not a fan of progress. Don't fret, dear. Everyone stalls! It’s part of learning. And your instructor will be patient. Though, speaking of driving, did you see what Bethany tweeted this morning? Photos of her new car. Bright pink, it is! Oh, yeah! It's so cool! She says she’s named it ‘Barbie’. Pink? Good heavens. You wouldn’t catch me dead in a pink car. Gives me a headache just looking at it. It’s a bit… bold, even for Bethany. But she’s always been a bit of a show-off, hasn't she?

Right, your move, love. Don’t think too long, you’ll wrinkle your forehead. It’s just… so many possibilities. It’s quite overwhelming, isn’t it? It's more complex than I initially thought. It is a bit, isn’t it? More than checkers, that’s for sure. Though I did see someone playing a version with, like, cards instead of pieces. Looked a right mess. Oh, don’t even  start  on variations. Stick to the proper rules, that’s what I say. Speaking of rules, are you remembering about the cannon? You were forgetting about the cannon last time. I’m trying! It’s the jumping over pieces, right? And needing another piece to block… It’s all about positioning. Thinking three steps ahead. Like a good politician. Though looking at Westminster these days, maybe that’s not a good example. You’re not wrong there. Did you see that piece about Scotland wanting another independence referendum? Honestly, it’s just back and forth, isn’t it? Never ending. It’s… complicated. A lot of it stems from Brexit, I think. And a feeling of being ignored. I was reading a linguistics paper about how language shifts are tied to political movements. Fascinating, actually. Fascinating, eh? I’m more interested in whether or not it’ll affect the price of petrol. Honestly, everything’s gone up. It's daylight robbery. Tell me about it. I was at Brenda’s yesterday, and she was moaning about the dentist. Apparently, they’re wanting another fifty quid just for a check-up. Fifty quid! That’s ridiculous. Dental care should be free at the point of use. Should be, shouldn’t it? Reminds me of when I was a lad. Old Mr. Harrison, the dentist, used to give us a lollipop after every appointment. Now  that  was good service. Oh, those were the days. Right, stop reminiscing and move a piece. You're letting me get ahead. You know, I had a recording of Winston Churchill I found on an old reel-to-reel. Trying to get it digitised. It’s a nightmare with all this new technology. I could probably help with that. I've got some software that can do audio restoration. It's surprisingly effective. That’s good of you, lad. Always helpful. I’m trying to get the greenhouse sorted. The tomatoes are going mad, but the beans are refusing to sprout.

Honestly, some of the things they come up with… this one student, bless her, tried to tell me that “irregardless” is a real word. I had to gently explain… again. It’s exhausting sometimes. Oh, you get that all the time, don't you? It’s the confidence, isn't it? They’re so sure they’re right, even when demonstrably… not. Reminds me of some politicians, actually. Have you been following the latest debacle? A little. Honestly, I try to tune it out. It's just… draining. It feels like everything is just a bit of a mess at the moment. Makes you grateful to be here, I suppose. Not dealing with all that. Exactly. Though, being here does make me think about pensions, and how utterly terrifying that whole system is. I mean, will there  be  anything left? I haven't paid in properly for years, you know, with not really… working. Ugh, don't even go there. I'm still battling with student loan repayments. It feels like it will follow me to my grave. And the interest rates are ridiculous! They say they're helping young people, but it feels like they’re just trapping us in debt. It’s a joke, isn't it? And then everyone acts surprised that people are choosing to move abroad. I was reading an article about how many qualified teachers are leaving the UK because of all the…stuff. It's a brain drain. It is. I’ve been thinking about it myself, to be honest. Not permanently, but maybe another year or two somewhere different. South Korea, maybe? Or Vietnam. The opportunities are decent, and the money is good. Ooh, Vietnam sounds exciting! You'd be brilliant at that. Though, you’d miss proper tea. And a decent MOT. Remember when the car failed last year? That was a nightmare. Don’t remind me! The exhaust was completely shot. Still, could be worse. At least I'm not stuck doing paperwork all day. How are you passing the time, apart from correcting grammatical errors and contemplating the end of civilisation? Largely Netflix, to be honest. I finished that new series, “The Serpent.” Gripping, but slightly disturbing. And I've been attempting to learn Polish. Duolingo is…challenging. Oh, good luck with that! Polish is supposed to be fiendishly difficult. I’ve picked up a few phrases just from being here, but anything beyond “Dzień dobry” is a struggle.

Right, so you’re still pretty set on Human Sciences then? At Oxford? Yeah, pretty much. It just… feels right, you know? It's broad enough, isn't it? Doesn’t box me in straight away. What about you? Still Maths at Warwick? Yeah, Warwick seems the best place for it, honestly. The course is really good, and I reckon I’ve got a decent shot at getting the grades. It’s just… scary thinking about being that far away from everyone. I get that. Oxford's not  that  far, though, is it? We could still meet up, weekends and stuff. Plus, we've got to learn to be independent eventually, right? Easy for you to say, you’re practically built for independence. Remember that camping trip last year? You were happy to fend for yourself, I was complaining about the bugs after five minutes. Okay, fair enough. But seriously, it’ll be good for us. New experiences, new people… Speaking of new experiences, you finally tried a proper Old Fashioned last night, didn’t you? Not just a sip of my dad’s? Yeah, well… one. And regretted it immediately. That stuff is strong. It tastes nice going down, but then… woah. Told ya! It’s an acquired taste, definitely. You're better off sticking to cider, mate. Less chance of ending up questioning your life choices. Cider's good. Speaking of things I regret, I tried to make pasta carbonara on Tuesday. It was a disaster. No way! You and cooking. Name a more iconic duo. What went wrong? Everything. The sauce was watery, the bacon was burnt, I think I put too much pepper in… It looked nothing like the pictures online. Honestly, I think I need lessons. You definitely do. My mum's always going on about how easy it is, but she makes it look effortless. It's a skill, man. A genuine skill. Listen, I'm going to try and head down to watch the rugby next Saturday, are you in? Hawks are playing away. Yeah, definitely. Gotta support the local team. Although, have you seen their form lately? They’re on a bit of a losing streak, aren’t they? Yeah, it’s been rough. But hopefully, they'll pull it together. It’ll be a good laugh either way. We should grab a pint before the match. Maybe… stick to cider for you.

So, you were asking about National Insurance contributions, weren’t you? Bit of a fiddle, it is. People think it just goes towards their pension, but it's more than that, you see. Yeah, I was a bit confused. I understood the pension part, but what else is it for? Everything feels so… opaque. Opaque is a good word for it. Well, it funds things like the NHS, mostly. And unemployment benefits. Basically, it’s a safety net. Though whether it’s a strong enough one these days is another matter entirely. It's designed to be contributions related, so the more you earn, the more you put in, and the more you get out when you retire, or if you fall on hard times. Right, so it’s not just saving for  my  retirement, it’s contributing to the system for everyone? Exactly. It's a communal pot, more or less. And then you’ve got Income Tax on top of that. Now,  that’s  where things get really complex. Used to be simpler, you know, when I started out. Bands were wider, rates were clearer. Now, it’s all these personal allowances and tax-free thresholds… It’s designed to be progressive, isn’t it? The more you earn, the higher percentage you pay? That's the theory. But it doesn't always work out that way, does it? There are loopholes, tax breaks for certain things… Business investments, for example. Often benefit the wealthier folks more than anyone else. They can legitimately reduce their tax burden, which is their right, of course. It just feels… unfair sometimes. Like the system is rigged. Well, often it is, or appears to be. And this government… they're always tinkering with it. Cutting taxes here, raising them there. All political, you see. Trying to appeal to different demographics. Trying to get re-elected. It’s rarely about what’s truly best for the country, and rarely anything to do with fairness. It’s frustrating. I mean, I understand the need for taxation, I really do. It funds essential services. But it's hard to feel like it’s being used effectively. You're not wrong. And look at the national debt. It's enormous. They keep borrowing and borrowing, and someone has to pay it back eventually. That’ll be you and your generation, I’m afraid. So, what do they do with all the money then?

Honestly, this project is just… consuming my life. I feel like I’m living at work. Oh, darling, you always say that. But you're good at it, aren't you? Juggling everything. Good at being stressed, maybe! It’s just endless meetings, endless emails, and everyone wants everything  yesterday . Did I tell you about Sarah? Sarah from work? The one with the bright pink hair? The very same. She emailed me at 8 pm last night asking for a report she knew I hadn’t finished! Said it was “urgent.” Urgent for what?! Her weekend plans? Honestly, some people! You need to learn to just… ignore those emails until Monday. Set boundaries. Easier said than done. My boss expects a response within the hour. It’s ridiculous. How was your day at school? Still battling teenagers? You have  no  idea. Exam season is looming, so it’s just a sea of anxiety and last-minute questions. One boy genuinely burst into tears because he couldn’t remember the capital of France. The capital! Oh, bless him. They do crumble under the pressure, don’t they? It’s awful. It is. Though, it does occasionally provide some amusement. Old Mr. Henderson, the history teacher, accidentally called Napoleon “Napoleon Dynamite” during a practice exam briefing. The kids were in hysterics. Oh, no! Mr. Henderson? He's so serious! I know! He was mortified. Completely red in the face. It was brilliant. Anyway, enough about school. How’s your mum doing? I haven’t spoken to her in ages. She's good, she's good. She started a pottery class, can you believe it? She’s always said she’s not artistic, but apparently, she’s a natural. She’s already made a couple of wonky vases. That’s lovely! She’s always needed a hobby. Has she met anyone new in the class? A few people. She keeps talking about this man called George. Apparently, he’s a retired architect and quite the charmer. She's being all coy about it, but I think she likes him. Oh, wonderful! Maybe she’ll finally find some company. It's been a bit lonely for her since Dad… well, you know. I know. It's good to see her smiling again. So, are you still planning on meeting up with Helen next week? Yes! We’re going to that little Italian place in town, the one with the amazing tiramisu.

So, any joy with that application then, lass? The one down south? Not yet, Grandad. Still waiting to hear back. It's a bit frustrating, honestly. Applied weeks ago. Yeah, recruitment processes are glacial these days. I was telling your Grandad just yesterday, it’s all automated screening and personality tests before you even get a chance to speak to a human. Aye, it's a right carry on. Used to be a face-to-face interview, a proper chat. Now it’s algorithms deciding your fate. Still, you've got a good degree, you’ll be alright. What about that friend of yours, Amelia? How’s she getting on with her job hunt? She’s still temping, but she had an interview last week for a permanent role at a publishing house. Fingers crossed for her. She’d be brilliant at it. She knows everything about books. Publishing’s a tough industry though, isn’t it? Lots of competition. It is. Still, better than standing still, eh? Speaking of standing still, I’ve been meaning to ask, did you two manage to get yourselves sorted for Saturday? We’re having that buffet aren’t we? Your Auntie Brenda’s bringing her potato salad, which, let's be honest, is half the reason people turn up. We’re good for Saturday, Grandad. I volunteered to do the veggie options – hummus, crudités, that sort of thing. And I’m on drinks duty. I’ve ordered a couple of bottles of that Italian red you like, and a prosecco for the ladies. Prosecco! Good man. You remember what your grandmother used to say about a celebration without bubbles being a sad occasion? I think I’ve heard that a few times, yeah. It’s a classic. You still got that old iPod, by the way? I was digging around the other day and remembered how good some of those playlists were you made. The iPod?! Aye, it's in the loft somewhere, I reckon. Full of all sorts of nonsense. Used to spend hours downloading music. Back when you actually  owned  the music, not just streamed it. Remember burning CDs? Such a faff. A right faff! And then hoping your computer didn't crash mid-burn. Still, it was more satisfying than just clicking a button. Right, I'm going to put the bins out. This recycling is a nightmare. So many different bins for so little…well, you know.

Honestly, the conference was… a lot. I mean, useful bits, definitely, but mostly just  a lot . Oh, tell me about it. Were you at the one in Bristol last week? I was hoping to catch up with you, but it was chaos. So many people! No, the one in Bournemouth. Though, I heard Bristol was a nightmare. Apparently, the hotel completely messed up the bookings and half the attendees were scrambling for rooms. Oh,  no . That's awful. We had a bit of a queue for coffee each morning, but nothing on that scale. Bournemouth sounds… less dramatic, thankfully. What was the main focus this year? Still all about communicative language teaching, I assume? Pretty much. Though there was a weird tangent about using TikTok for grammar practice. Which, honestly, felt incredibly forced. Like, I appreciate trying to be relevant, but my students barely use TikTok, and the ones who do aren't looking for verb conjugations. Oh, bless. They always try to chase the trends, don’t they? I had a session on incorporating AI into lesson planning. It was… underwhelming. So much hype, but most of the tools felt clunky and not particularly helpful. I mean, ChatGPT is alright for brainstorming, but it’s not replacing me just yet. Definitely not! I tried one of those AI lesson plan generators. It produced something… technically correct, I guess, but utterly devoid of any spark. It was like a robot had attempted to understand what makes a lesson engaging and failed spectacularly. Exactly! It missed all the nuance, all the little things you add to tailor it to your students. It's just… soulless. And then they want us to spend hours 'adapting' it, which just feels like extra work for something that’s inherently bad. Precisely! I spent half the session mentally rewriting the lesson plan they’d put together. And the presenter was all, "Oh, but AI will free up your time!" Like, no, it doesn't. It just creates a different kind of work. It’s the same with all this talk about blended learning. “Oh, just flip the classroom!” Easy for them to say when they haven't got seventeen year olds who won’t do pre-reading if their lives depended on it. Oh god, tell me about it. I had a student last week who admitted he hadn’t even  looked  at the assigned reading.

Honestly, this road is… well, it’s a road. Not a particularly  good  road, mind you. Full of potholes. Feels like we’re off-roading sometimes! It’s Poland, love. You weren’t expecting autobahn perfection, were you? It could be worse, we could be on a dirt track. And honestly, I’m just enjoying not being stuck in a classroom. Though, I do miss a decent coffee. This instant stuff… it’s a crime against beans. A crime, honestly. You'd think even in Poland they’d have mastered the art of a proper latte. Speaking of crimes, did you see Brenda’s new profile picture? Heavily filtered, darling. Heavily. She looks… ten years younger. Oh, Brenda? Yeah, I saw it. She’s always been a bit of a filter fiend. It's the London effect, I reckon. Everyone's got to keep up appearances. Makes you wonder what she actually looks like these days. Exactly! It’s exhausting. All that effort… I mean, I'm not against a little smoothing here and there, but it’s become ridiculous. I’ve decided to embrace the wrinkles. They tell a story, don’t you think? Definitely. Though, a little hyaluronic acid doesn't hurt. Just saying. Speaking of stories, I was reading that article about volunteering in Ukraine… Makes you feel a bit useless, doesn’t it? Just… travelling around. It does. But we are supporting the Polish economy, even if it's just through petrol and rather sad instant coffee. And frankly, I’m not cut out for frontline volunteering. I'd be more of a hindrance than a help. Remember my attempts at the soup kitchen back home? Disaster. Oh, don’t remind me! You managed to set off the fire alarm with the lentil soup. It was a classic. A classic disaster. Anyway, are we nearly there yet? My bladder is starting to send out distress signals. And I’m starting to think we might struggle to find a decent parking spot in Rzeszow. All those narrow streets... According to the satnav, about forty minutes. And apparently, there's a campsite just outside the city centre. Should have spaces. Though, judging by the reviews, it’s run by a man who dislikes smiling. Oh, wonderful. Just what we need. A grumpy campsite owner. This trip is full of character, isn’t it? It’s a far cry from my nice, quiet life back in Cambridge.

…and that’s why I think the idea of the pyramids being solely tombs is a bit simplistic, don’t you think? It’s the precision, the sheer engineering… it speaks to a knowledge of mathematics and, frankly, physics that we’re only  now  beginning to fully appreciate. And the alignment with Orion, you know, the whole celestial thing. It’s… a lot to take in, Liam. It  is  impressive, obviously. But sometimes I think people get a bit carried away with the “ancient aliens built them” nonsense. I mean, it was still humans, wasn’t it? Clever humans, granted, but humans. Oh, I'm not saying aliens, definitely not aliens! But a sophisticated, lost understanding. Perhaps relating to harnessing tectonic energy, maybe even…precursors to understanding telomeres and cellular regeneration. It sounds wild, I know. But look at the lifespan of the ancient Egyptians, comparatively. And the elite especially. They weren’t living to 80, but they weren’t dying young either. Well, sanitation wasn’t brilliant back then, was it? The ones who  did  make it past childhood probably had a pretty high chance of succumbing to something nasty. It’s hard to compare life expectancy across millennia. True, true. It’s always a bit of a dodgy comparison, isn’t it? Speaking of dodgy… how’s Leo doing with his speech? Any improvement? Slowly. Still behind, the speech therapist seems to think it might be… a little bit of an autism spectrum thing. Nothing confirmed, obviously. It's just, he doesn't really  respond  to attempts to copy sounds. He’s got all the understanding, he just… doesn’t seem motivated to replicate them. Right, right. Well, early intervention is key, they say. It's brilliant you're getting him seen so quickly. But you know, don't stress too much. He’s a bright little button, that boy. And all kids develop at their own pace. Easier said than done. It’s just… watching other kids his age chatter away, it makes you worry. Anyway, enough about me fretting. What were you saying about anti-ageing? Tectonic energy and telomeres? You're losing me again! Just a thought! The idea that there might be techniques, lost techniques, that allowed for cellular repair… coupled with a sustainable energy source. Imagine that. Forget oil, forget fracking. Imagine tapping into the Earth's natural energy. It's the Vikings, you know?

Honestly, this coffee is amazing. Did you get new beans, Mum? I did! From that little shop on Clifton Drive, the one with all the fancy grinders. They said it’s Ethiopian Yirgacheffe. Quite a mouthful, isn't it? Sounds expensive. It wasn’t  too  bad. I had that voucher from Christmas, remember? The one your Auntie Brenda sent. Oh yeah, that was a good one. I almost used it on those sunglasses I saw in town. The tortoiseshell ones? Don’t be daft, spending a voucher on sunglasses. You’ve got loads. Honestly, you girls and your shopping. I need them for the summer! And those were  really  nice. Anyway, we were talking about coffee… did you manage to sort that baby chair for Leo yet? Grandma keeps asking when she can visit, and he needs somewhere to sit. Almost. I’ve been looking online, and they’re all either ridiculously expensive or look like they'll fall apart after a week. I saw one at that new furniture place near Lytham, but it was £150! £150? For a baby chair? That’s daylight robbery! We got yours for about £30 from Argos. Things are just so pricey now, aren't they? Everything’s going up. It's terrifying. It is. It makes you think about… well, everything. Speaking of things going up, did you see the latest on that referendum? People are still banging on about the EU. Don't get me started on that. Honestly, it’s all a mess. The price of everything’s shot up since we left, and for what? I don’t really get it, to be honest.
