It all sounds really complicated. It is complicated, darling. But it affects everything. Like the price of fruit, for instance. I was talking to Mrs. Henderson next door, she says her greengrocer is having trouble getting things from Europe now. We should just get chickens. That's what we should do. Fresh eggs every day, no relying on imports. Chickens? In our garden? Dad, no! I’m just saying! It’d be practical. Plus, they eat slugs. Keeps the plants nice. Speaking of plants, your mother’s trying to turn the garden into a jungle. It’s not a jungle! It's a carefully curated floral display. And I'm thinking of getting a little apple tree. Or maybe a plum tree. An apple tree!

Honestly, the tree looks lovely, doesn’t it? A bit…full, perhaps, but lovely. Did you get it from Mr. Henderson again this year? Yeah, same place. He remembered me, which was nice. He asked how uni was going, and then immediately asked if I’d met a nice boy. Classic Mr. Henderson. Oh, he’s a sweetheart, isn’t he? Always meddling. Did you tell him about Ben? Briefly. Said he was very… well, he said he hoped Ben appreciated having such a clever daughter. Made me roll my eyes. Men. Honestly. How are things going with Ben, anyway? You've been a bit quiet about it lately. It’s good. Really good. He's been properly busy with his course, a lot of late nights in the library. But we had a really nice weekend last week. He took me to that German Christmas market in Canterbury. Oh, lovely! They do a good Glühwein, don’t they? Always makes me think of Aunt Hilda and her obsession with all things German. It was really festive. He’s trying to learn some German phrases for a project, so he kept practicing on me. It was… endearingly terrible. He sounds sweet. Speaking of things German, have you been reading anything interesting for your work? Anything you can use for new copy? Actually, yes! I’ve been researching the history of Advent calendars for a client. It's surprisingly fascinating, apparently they originated with German Protestants in the 19th century. Little candles on wreaths and stuff. Oh, interesting! You learn something new every day. Did you see Mrs. Peterson putting up her lights this morning? Oh, the full works? Of course. It's like Blackpool illuminations over there. Honestly, it’s a bit much, isn't it? But she seems happy, bless her. I offered to help her get her cat down from the tree last year, she wouldn't let me near it. Said Mittens was supervising. Mittens. She's a character. I saw her staring intently at next door’s goldfish yesterday. I swear she was plotting something. That cat is a menace! Speaking of menaces, I booked that nail appointment for you, the one you wanted for your birthday? Oh, Mum, you shouldn’t have! But thank you. Yes, please! My nails are looking dreadful. All chipped and…nurse-like. You work hard, darling, you deserve a bit of pampering.

Right, so… officially resident. Feels a bit weird, doesn’t it? Still smells… new. It does! Like that plastic-y smell. And paint. It’s actually really nice though, much brighter than your old place. This living room is a good size. Yeah, I’m hoping we can actually, you know,  use  it. Last place was just a corridor with furniture shoved down it. First things first though - internet. Have you got the details from the letting agent? Yep, scribbled them on a bit of paper somewhere…  rummages in bag … here we go. BT. Joy. Expect a three-hour call and being transferred seven times. Oh brilliant. I’ll brace myself. While you do that, I’m going to attempt to unpack the kitchen boxes. We desperately need coffee. And somewhere to actually  make  it. Good call. I can smell potential coffee disasters brewing already. Oh, and we need to find out about rubbish collection. Where’s the bin shed? I think the agent said it's around the back, near the nursery. Which is… cheerful. Little kids screaming at 7am, perfect. Oh lovely. Maybe we can befriend the teachers and get a discount. I’ll check the council website for bin days when I’m on the phone to BT. Right, deep breaths…  dials phone …  opening boxes … Okay, this is a disaster. I forgot how much stuff I actually own. And everything is covered in bubble wrap. Still, at least I brought the coffee grinder. What are you thinking for dinner tonight? I’m completely brain-dead. Honestly? Pizza. We can order one. I’m not tackling cooking in this chaos. Besides, I saw a greengrocer on the way here, a proper one, not just Tesco fruit and veg. We should go tomorrow and see what’s in season. Ooh, good idea. I’m craving some decent tomatoes. Everything tastes like water in winter. Speaking of which, I need to find the kettle. And maybe a cigarette… but only outside. Gotta be a good neighbour.  on the phone … Yes, hello? BT? I’m calling about a new connection at…  trails off muttering details . … No, I don’t know what the Openreach number is! Honestly… Found the kettle! And…surprise surprise… no mugs. Figures. This place is basically a shell.  still on the phone … Look, I just want the internet, is that too much to ask?…  sighs … They’re saying it’s a ‘complex installation’ and could take up to five days.

Honestly, this halloumi and harissa burger is  amazing . You absolutely made the right choice. Oh, it's good! Really good. I was torn between that and the chicken, but the harissa just… called to me. How are you finding it? Is the steak cooked alright? Perfect. Seriously, medium-rare, exactly as requested. It’s just… nice to be out, isn’t it? It feels like ages since uni. It really does. Too long. Life just  happens , doesn't it? Work, settling in… It feels weird being back in Peterborough, though. It suddenly feels so… small. I know! I think moving back home after graduating definitely did that to me. Everything suddenly feels very… contained. How are you finding the placement? Still enjoying it at the council? Yeah, it’s alright. A lot more admin than I anticipated, honestly. I thought I’d be out doing fieldwork, y’know, actually  doing  things. But it’s good experience, and the people are nice. It’s just… not exactly inspiring. What about you? Still battling spreadsheets as a project coordinator? Haha, you know me. Spreadsheet central. It’s actually been really busy lately, which is good. I’m heading up a small project at the moment, so I’m getting a bit more responsibility. It’s stressful, but in a good way, I think. That’s good to hear! Remember that awful group project in second year? The one on sustainable tourism? I swear, if I see another PowerPoint presentation on eco-lodges… Oh god,  don't  remind me! Mark spent the entire time trying to convince us that a cruise ship was a sustainable option! I know! And then Sarah just… disappeared for a week. We had to do her entire section! It feels like a lifetime ago, though. Do you still talk to Sarah? Occasionally. She’s living in Bristol now, working as a yoga instructor. Very… zen. She keeps trying to get me to join her on a retreat, but I just can’t face a week of enforced mindfulness. Sounds intense. My mum keeps trying to get me to do a meditation course. She's convinced it’ll solve all my problems! Speaking of mums, mine’s been asking when I’m going to start ‘thinking seriously’ about settling down. Oh,  that  conversation. My mum’s been on that one for years. It’s exhausting. I know, right? It’s like, I’ve literally just finished uni!

Honestly, this pint is  exactly  what I needed after that commute. Three hours on trains, it's criminal. Tell me about it. Birmingham to Cambridge isn’t exactly a hop, skip and a jump either. Though, admittedly, not quite the North East distances you’re used to. Oh, don't even  start  on the distances. My nan still thinks visiting Newcastle is “going down south.” She’s convinced everything south of Durham is just one big London. That’s brilliant. My mum's the opposite. Everything north of Watford is… well, let’s just say she’s not a fan of wellies. Oh, the stereotypes! It's exhausting. Though, actually, I  do  own a decent pair of wellies. You never know when you'll need them in Sunderland. Especially not during a festival. Sensible. Speaking of festivals, are you still following The Futureheads? I saw they’re doing a small gig in Leeds next month. Thought of you instantly. Are you kidding? Of course! They’re legends. Proper Geordie anthems. I wish I could make it to Leeds, but work is…insane right now. This new research project is eating my life. Oh, the joys of research. What’s it on this time? Still the social impact of digital technologies? God no, thankfully. That was soul-crushing. This one’s on sustainable fashion and consumer behaviour. Surprisingly fascinating, actually. It’s amazing how much guilt people feel about fast fashion, but then still  buy  it. The hypocrisy is strong. I’ve been trying to be more mindful myself, but it’s hard. Everything looks the same now, doesn't it? Like, even ‘ethical’ brands just feel…mass-produced. Exactly! And the price hike is brutal. I saw a 'sustainable' jumper the other day for £180. I’d rather just mend what I’ve got, honestly. Gran taught me to darn, and it’s actually quite therapeutic. I wish I’d learned that. My sewing skills peak at attaching a button. Though, to be fair, button-attaching is a valuable life skill. It is! You'd be surprised. Though, you probably don’t encounter many wardrobe malfunctions during a PhD. Unless, of course, you have a particularly dramatic thesis defence outfit. Don't even joke. I'm aiming for ‘inoffensive tweed’ for that day. Nothing that will distract from the inherent boredom of my research. Which, by the way, is on the socio-political implications of early 20th-century garden cities.

So, did you watch that debate last night, Grandma? The one with… all of ‘em? Oh, aye lad, I did. Though honestly, it all just sounds like a load of shouting to me these days. Never used to be like that, y'know? Back in the day, politicians actually  talked  to each other. Yeah, I thought it was pretty mental. That fella from the Reform party kept going on about boats. Just boats, like it's the solution to everything. Boats, you say? Sounds like a right mess. Politicians always need a scapegoat, don't they? Used to be the Germans, now it's people trying to get a better life. Terrible. It's just… they don't seem to be sayin' anything  useful . Like, what are they actually gonna  do  about the NHS? My mam's been waitin' ages for an appointment. The NHS… that’s been goin’ downhill for years, lad. Started when they started lettin' managers run things instead of doctors and nurses. Always said that was a mistake. They don’t understand what it’s like on the ward floor, do they? All about budgets and targets, not about people. Exactly! It's always about the money, isn't it? And they all promise more money, but then… nothing changes. Promises, promises. Politicians are good at those. Back when Attlee won, they promised us the NHS. Felt like a miracle, that did. Proper change. These days, it feels like they're just promising to make things… slightly less bad. My history teacher was saying that Labour were proper champions of the working class, back then. But now… I dunno. Seems like they’ve all just become the same. There's a bit of truth in that, sadly. They all chase the middle ground now, tryin' to appeal to everyone. Ends up appealin' to no one, really. And the young ‘uns don't even bother votin’, do they? A lot of us don't, no. Feels like it doesn't make a difference. Like whatever happens, it's gonna be rubbish anyway. That's a dangerous attitude, lad. Your generation needs to get involved. My father fought in the war, y'know? Fought for the right to have a say. Don't let that go to waste. Even if you think it won’t change things, you  have  to try. I get what you mean, Grandma. It's just… hard to feel optimistic, y'know?

Now, Liam, put down the fork when you’re talking, will you? It's not a very good look, son. Like you’re stabbing the air with it. Sorry, Dad. It’s just… this pasta's really good. He’s right, it  is  good. Your father makes a fantastic carbonara, doesn’t he? Though maybe a little heavy on the pepper tonight. I like a bit of a kick! Keeps things interesting. And it wasn't  that  heavy. Now, manners. Your Granny’s watching. Och, don’t mind me. I’ve seen worse at the school dinner table, believe you me. Though the principles of polite conversation still hold true, regardless of the meal. Did you ever have really bad school dinners, Granny? Oh, you wouldn't believe. Grey meat, watery vegetables, and something they  called  custard. It was an affront to dairy, I tell you. Thankfully, I always packed a piece of fruit. That sounds dreadful. Remember when we took the kids to Fitzgerald’s Park and they refused to eat their sandwiches? Drama, absolute drama. Ah, Fitzgerald’s Park. A lovely spot. We should go back there when the weather improves. Perhaps take them on the little train. Can we, Dad? That train is cool. We'll see, son. We’ll see. Did you hear about the blood moon tonight? I did! Apparently, it's going to be visible for quite a while. I was hoping to get a good look, but with the little one… I’ll take a look later. Perfect night for it, dark and clear. Hopefully, the clouds stay away. Always loved a good celestial event. Reminds you how small we all are, doesn’t it? Although, I wouldn’t trust those weather forecasts. They said it would be sunny today, and look at it now – grey as a mouse. Is a blood moon like, dangerous? Oh, no, darling. It's just a name. It's when the moon passes into the Earth's shadow and takes on a reddish hue. It's beautiful, actually. Though I remember when I was a boy, old Mrs. O’Malley down the road swore it meant bad luck was coming. Said it was a sign from the fairies. Oh, that Mrs. O’Malley. A character. Always had a story to tell. Speaking of stories, are you two still relying on me to babysit little Aoife next week? We were hoping you would, Mum.

So, did you catch any of that Scottish referendum coverage last night? Absolute chaos, wasn't it? Seems like it’s going to be a long few days, honestly. A bit, yeah. Flicked it on and off. Honestly, I’ve lost track of what they’re arguing about anymore. Just seems to go round and round. More interested in what’s happening with the price of petrol, to be frank. Dreadful, isn’t it? Tell me about it. Filled up this morning and nearly choked. Speaking of stressful things, how did that job interview go on Tuesday? Did you get any feedback yet? No, not a peep. Radio silence. Which, you know, is never a good sign. I thought I actually did alright, though. Chatting to the bloke, Dave, seemed to go well. He’s a bit of a character, Dave is. Used to play cricket with his brother back in the day. Right. Well, don’t write yourself off just yet. Sometimes these things take time. Though, you're right, silence isn't encouraging. How's Brenda coping with you being potentially out of work? She’s… supportive. Which is putting it mildly. More worried about the bills, naturally. But she knows I’m putting the feelers out. It’s just… different, isn’t it? After running my own business for thirty years, the thought of answering to someone else again… feels a bit strange. I can imagine. It's a big shift. Remember old Mr. Henderson, from the school? Tried to retire, then lasted a week before going back part-time. Said he was bored silly. Ha! That sounds like him alright. Still, I've got a few leads. And frankly, a bit of a break might do me good. Been burning the candle at both ends for years. You need to look after yourself. Speaking of family, how’s Sarah doing? How’s university treating her? She’s good. Stressed, obviously. Final year. Endless essays. Keeps moaning about having to do group work. Says she ends up doing all the work herself! Sounds familiar, eh? Oh, absolutely. The joys of group projects. My Emily's just landed a graduate scheme with a marketing company in London. So, she's buzzing. Still trying to work out how she’s going to afford to live there, though. It's ridiculous, the cost of everything. London. Forget it. Robbery. I wouldn’t live there if you paid me.

Right, well that was a bit of a kerfuffle getting out of Sainsbury’s, wasn’t it? Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the parking. Tell me about it. It was like the Hunger Games out there. Everyone just…diving for spaces. Did you manage to get everything, Mum? Mostly. I forgot the oat milk, though. Your father said it wasn’t essential, but  I  think it is for your Auntie Carol’s coffee. She’ll have a fit if it’s cow’s milk. She’ll survive, love. She's a hardy woman, Carol is. Anyway, we’re nearly there. Just past the roundabout and then up the lane. Speaking of surviving, I’m starving. What’s for lunch? I skipped breakfast trying to cram in that extra tutorial this morning. I’ve got those cheese and pickle sandwiches I made. And some crisps. And those little sausage rolls from the bakery. Though your father ate half of them already. I had two! They were very good sausage rolls. Reminded me of the ones my mother used to make. Though, frankly, hers were superior. Classic Dad. Always finding a way to compare everything to your mum. They really were good, though. Speaking of baking, I was looking at this recipe for sourdough online…seems ridiculously complicated. Sourdough! Oh, don’t even go there. I tried that once. It ended up like a brick. A very sour brick. I think it’s one of those things you need a specialist course for. Like that pottery class I did. How did that go? Well, let’s just say my ‘vase’ looked more like a lopsided ashtray. Everyone else made these beautiful things, and mine…well, it’s in the shed. It might be supporting a tomato plant now. You’re modest, love. You've always been creative. Remember that knitted penguin you made Aaron when he was little? Oh god, please don’t remind me. That thing was terrifying. It had one eye and a wonky beak! Sounds…unique. So, how much further, Dad? My phone’s lost signal. I need to tell my students I’m on my way back. About ten minutes. Signal’s patchy around here. Makes you wonder how people managed before mobile phones, doesn’t it? We used to just…wing it. Turn up when we turned up. No one knew where anyone was. It was simpler, in some ways.

Honestly, this traffic is mental, isn’t it? Didn’t realise leaving at six would still be this bad. Aye, it’s a right bother. Used to be able to get across Manchester in fifteen minutes, back in my day. Fifteen minutes! Now look at it. All these cars… and for what? It's mostly the M62, isn't it? Seems to be perpetually jammed. They really need to do something about that stretch. Tell me about it. I swear, I aged about ten years just merging onto it. Did you see that tractor? Honestly, right in the outside lane. A tractor? On the motorway? What’s the world coming to! Back in my day, tractors stayed in the fields where they belonged. Probably heading to market. There’s a lot of farmland around here still, even with all the development. Still, a bit of consideration wouldn't go amiss, eh? Held everyone up something awful. And then, right behind it, a trailer full of sheep! Honestly, a woolly roadblock. Sheep, you say? Now that's interesting. My Auntie Bessie used to raise sheep. Lovely creatures, but a right mess, they are. Always getting into the vegetable patch. I spent a summer on a farm once, helping out a friend. The smell… wasn't exactly pleasant. And the early mornings. 4 am starts, just to milk the cows. Oof, no thank you! I need my sleep. I can barely function before nine, never mind four in the morning. Though, I did see some really cute piglets. Tiny little things, all pink. Piglets are clever, you know. Surprisingly intelligent animals. Cleaner than people give them credit for, too. My Auntie Bessie had pigs as well. Always loved a good belly rub, she said. That’s a new one! I always thought pigs were just…muddy. Apparently not. Everything I thought I knew about farm animals is being challenged right now. Maybe we should have just stayed home and watched a documentary. Nonsense! You wouldn’t get this kind of insight watching a documentary. You need to  experience  it. Besides, I enjoy a good bit of traffic. Gives me time to think. Think about what? The good old days when you could cross Manchester in fifteen minutes? Amongst other things. It reminds me… there was this time, back in ‘58, when I got stuck behind a herd of cows… Oh lord. Here we go…Another story.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is lovely, Margaret. Much better than anything I could manage now I'm retired. My hands aren’t what they used to be for all that mashing. It  is  good, isn't it? You always did make a good one though, Eileen. Remember that one Christmas, you practically lived in the kitchen, perfecting the potato topping? Oh, don’t remind me! The pressure! Your Auntie Bridie used to critique every single layer. Said my seasoning wasn’t ‘robust’ enough. Robust! As if a little nutmeg was a crime against humanity. Bridie. A force of nature, that woman. Always had an opinion, and wasn't shy about sharing it. Speaking of forces of nature, have you been keeping up with your walking, Eileen? I know you were aiming for a couple of miles each day. I have, mostly. Though young Thomas, bless him, insisted on taking me ‘off-road’ last week. Ended up nearly tumbling into a ditch. My ankles haven’t forgiven me. Thomas! Oh, he’s full of beans, that one. He thinks he’s Bear Grylls. Has he decided what he wants to do after sixth form? Still leaning towards engineering? That’s the plan, though he’s been talking about a gap year. Volunteering, he said. Some scheme in South America. I’m trying not to overreact. South America! Goodness. That's a long way to go. A bit ambitious, perhaps? Exactly what I said! I told him there’s plenty to do closer to home. Volunteering at the animal shelter, maybe. Or helping at the village hall. Though, truth be told, I secretly hope he’ll realize how expensive university is and decide to get a job for a year. Well, it  is  expensive. I’m still paying off my student loan, and I finished years ago! You know, my sister was saying they’re thinking of starting a scholarship fund at her old school. To help kids from less well-off families get a decent education. That’s a lovely idea. It’s important to give back, isn’t it? I always meant to do more with the oil money, but… well, life got in the way. Don’t beat yourself up about that, Arthur. You always had a good heart. Though, speaking of being helpful, did Mrs. Higgins ever manage to get the hang of that new telly? I offered to show her last week, but she said she’d ask her grandson.

Right, so, Parent's Evening. Overall, pretty good, wasn’t it? Both of you seemed really happy with your teachers. Yeah. Miss Davies said my writing is… sparkly. Mine said I’m good at art! I drew a dragon. A really,  really  good one. I’m glad to hear it. Finn, Miss Jones did mention you’re having a bit of a wobble with your times tables. We need to keep working on those, okay? But they’re  hard ! Nine times eight is… is… something big! It is a bit tricky, but we can practice. Maybe after dinner? Or before story time? We can make it a game. Can we have dessert if we practice times tables? We'll see. Finish your dinner first. Honestly, you two are like little vacuum cleaners. Did you even taste the chicken? It’s good! It's got gravy! It’s yummy. But I’m really excited about World Book Day next week. I’m going as Hermione Granger! Oh, lovely! That’s a good choice. Are you practicing your spells? Yes! ‘Wingardium Leviosa!’ But I keep saying it wrong. I'm going as… …a knight! With a shiny sword! I need to make a helmet. Fantastic! We can get some cardboard and decorate it tomorrow. Speaking of tomorrow, I’ve booked tickets for the circus! Remember we talked about it? Ooh yes! With the acrobats? And the lions? Acrobats, yes. No lions, though, dear. They don’t usually have lions in circuses anymore. It's mostly amazing people doing amazing things. Will there be clowns? Probably. Do you like clowns? They’re a bit scary. Okay, we can sit further away from the ring then. Right, after school tomorrow… I need to pop into the shops, then we’re heading straight to the circus. And then bath time. Can we get ice cream at the circus? We'll see, let's get through dinner first. Actually, that reminds me. This chicken… it smells a bit funny, doesn’t it? No! It smells like chicken! No, it’s… I was reading this article online… apparently, forensic anthropologists can sometimes tell if something is human flesh just by the smell. It’s really weird. They said it smells… sweet? And smoky? Ewwww! What?! Human flesh?! Oh, don’t worry! This definitely isn't human flesh! I was just… sharing an interesting fact. It's a gross fact, I admit.

So, did young Leo manage to finish that curtain job then? His mother was saying he was working down in O’Connell’s, wasn't he? Oh, aye, he did. Said it was surprisingly hard work, all that measuring and… pinning. Proper knack to it, apparently. He’s earned a few bob, though, which is good. He was hoping to buy that new game. Game! Want game! Always thinking of the games, aren't you, little man? Well, that’s a good bit of responsibility for him, earning his own money. Teaches them the value of a pound, it does. Absolutely. It’s a good lesson. Now, about Oisin’s birthday…have we settled on anything yet? I was thinking maybe the adventure centre? That's what I was thinking. He’d absolutely  love  that. But it’s pricey, isn’t it? It is, but he’s only turning six once. We could keep the guest list tighter, just family and a few close friends. That’s sensible. All this massive parties nowadays! A wee gathering is far more manageable. And less stressful for everyone. I’ve seen it all, you know, teaching wee ones for forty years. Party! Balloons! Cake! He's already obsessed with the cake. He keeps asking if it’s going to have dinosaurs on it. Dinosaurs it is, then. I’ll order it tomorrow. We'll need to send out invites too, that’s a job for me I suppose. I could do that, if you’re busy with work. Though honestly, getting a response from people these days…it’s like pulling teeth. True enough. Speaking of busy, I’ve got a treasurer meeting for the garage owners on Tuesday. It’s a thankless task, honestly. Everyone wants something for nothing. Ah, the garages. Always a source of drama, aren’t they? I remember old Mr. Henderson, down the road… he was forever complaining about someone parking over his space. It's hardly parking disputes, Mother. It’s invoices and accounts and trying to figure out the latest tax regulations on rented houses. The government keeps changing things, it’s a nightmare. Tell me about it. Honestly, the tax on rental properties is ridiculous. It’s like they want to discourage people from letting them out. They do love to make things tricky, don't they? Anyway, back to happier things. Oisin was saying “wanty” again today.

Right, I’m telling you, it’s impossible. Absolutely impossible. I’ve been thinking about it for ages. What’s impossible? You've been muttering about ‘it’ for five minutes now. Is it a particularly difficult Sudoku? No, it’s the word game, the one Liam set us. A word with, like, four different vowels in a row. I just…it’s not happening. Oh, that one! Aye, it's a brutal challenge. I’ve been having a go on and off all evening. I’ve got three vowels, but getting a fourth feels like finding hen’s teeth. See! It  is  hard, right? I thought I was going mental. I've tried everything – queuing, audio, plateau… nothing's working. Queuing? Is that even a word? Well, it is now! I’m inventing words if I have to. I just need any four vowels in a row! Think about it, you’ve got a, e, i, o, u… it's like trying to fit a square peg in a round hole. You’re overthinking it. Think about digraphs, or vowel teams. Sometimes they sneak in where you least expect them. Vowel teams? Like… 'eau'? Is that enough? No, that’s only three vowels. Though it’s a good thought. What about words with diphthongs? 'Au' or 'oi' are technically vowel sounds… Oh, clever. But that still doesn't give me four in a row, does it? It’s just teasing me. Honestly, Liam just likes making us suffer. He does enjoy a good mental workout, doesn't he? I was trying to think of words with ‘iou’ in them – that's a tricky combo. Oh god, ‘iou’? That sounds like something a pigeon would say. A pigeon saying ‘iou’? That’s brilliant. Okay, okay, let’s brainstorm. If we forget about it needing to be a  real  word for a second, could we construct something ridiculous? Like… "beauious"? Beauious? What even  is  that supposed to mean? It doesn’t have to  mean  anything! Liam didn’t say it had to be legitimate English. Exactly. It just needs four vowels in a row. Hmm... you know what? That’s… actually a really good point. Okay, "beauious"— it’s horrific, but it might just work. I’m going to text Liam. Wish me luck. Good luck, you’ll need it. He’ll probably say it doesn't count though. He's a stickler for the rules.

Honestly, I napped for like, four hours solid today. Four. I feel like I've wasted the entire day. No way! Four hours? You must have been  exhausted . What even made you nap for that long? I don't even know! I sat down on the sofa to just check my emails, and next thing I know, it’s nearly seven. My neck is properly stiff. Classic. Happened to me last week. Remember that essay we had to read for Dr. Hayes’ class? Knocked me right out. It was brutal. Oh god, that one. So dry. Speaking of brutal, have you seen what Chloe’s posted on Instagram? Another picture from her holiday in Tenerife. She’s living her best life, while we’re stuck here. Ugh, don’t even. I saw. Another infinity pool photo. Honestly, it’s exhausting looking at her 'perfect' life. It's just... curated, isn't it? Totally. Remember when we were digging through old photos last week? The ones from primary school? Chloe had a full-on tantrum because her hair wasn't "just right" for the picture. Some things never change. Oh my god, yes! And she was wearing that awful sparkly pink jacket. The one her nan made her. The one she swore she'd never be seen in again! Look at her now, posing like she's a model. It’s hilarious. Still, she's got good taste in music, I'll give her that. Have you heard that new Arctic Monkeys track? Oh yeah, it's good. A bit different, though, isn't it? More… orchestral. I was listening to it on repeat earlier. Then I promptly fell asleep. Full circle, I guess. Different, yeah, but still undeniably them. It's growing on me. Hey, have you spoken to Liam recently? Haven’t seen him in ages. Not really. He messaged me a couple of weeks ago asking about the assignment, but that was it. Said he was swamped with work at the pub. He's always working. Yeah, he needs to chill out. He's gonna burn himself out. Remember when we tried to convince him to come to that awful karaoke night with us? He refused, said he had a shift. Oh god, that was a disaster. Ben attempting Bohemian Rhapsody… that'll haunt me forever. Seriously! It was the most painful thing I’ve ever witnessed. You know what, I am starving.

So, did you manage to get a look at the application properly before the council planning committee meeting? It felt a bit rushed, didn’t it? I did, skimmed it mostly on the train. Honestly, it’s a mess. The drawings are…optimistic, to say the least. They’ve conveniently ‘forgotten’ to include the existing trees, haven’t they? Exactly! And the shadow analysis is completely bogus. Old Man Hemmings was right to be furious. The whole thing will overshadow his garden. They’ve tried to downplay it, saying it’s ‘minimal impact’. Minimal! It’ll be like living in permanent twilight. And the access road… it’s already a bottleneck in the mornings. Adding another twenty houses’ worth of traffic will make it absolutely gridlocked. Did you see Councillor Davies trying to justify it? Oh, God, yes. All that talk about ‘sustainable development’ and ‘meeting housing needs’. It’s just a greenfield site, Peter! It’s a lovely field, and they’re just going to slap a housing estate on it. He was clearly siding with the developer, wasn't he? I think there’s more to it than meets the eye. A little bird told me Malcolm at the pub knows Davies’ brother-in-law works for the firm doing the build. No way! Honestly, it's disgusting. You'd think they’d have some kind of ethical obligation. And the structure of the meeting itself was…odd. They rushed through the objections so quickly. They did. And then gave the developer's representative ages to make his presentation, full of carefully curated photographs that made it look like paradise. It was infuriating. I wanted to stand up and just read out the objections properly, but I knew it wouldn't make a difference. They’d already made their minds up. I think they were hoping everyone would just roll over. Which is why Hemmings going in guns blazing was actually quite effective, even if he did come across a bit…forceful. He  was  forceful, but he had a point. It’s his quality of life they’re messing with. Do you think there’s anything we can do now? Appeal, perhaps? Possibly. We'd need to get a solicitor involved. It’s going to be expensive, and there’s no guarantee of success, but…I think it’s worth exploring. Especially if we can gather more evidence about those dodgy drawings.

Honestly, I am  starving . I’ve been surviving on biscuits all day. Did you manage to grab anything decent for dinner after your shift? Ugh, tell me about it. Shifts were…a lot today. I just grabbed a meal deal from Tesco. It's pathetic, I know. Tuna and sweetcorn, the height of culinary excellence. There’s still some chicken in the fridge, though, if you fancy it. I can knock up a quick stir-fry? Oh, you are a lifesaver. Yes please! Chicken stir-fry sounds amazing. I’ll get the rice on. You know, I was thinking about Chloe from school the other day. Chloe? Chloe…Miller? The one who was obsessed with horses? That’s the one! I found her on Instagram. She’s…a lifestyle influencer now, apparently. All avocado toast and yoga poses. It’s wild. No way! Seriously? That’s… peak Chloe, actually. Always had a flair for the dramatic. Remember when she tried to organise a protest about the school uniform? Oh god, yes! So passionate about freedom of expression through clothing. Such a rebel. Speaking of dramatic, have you  seen  Mrs. Henderson’s garden lately? It’s like a jungle. Oh, don't even get me started on Mrs. Henderson. It's overgrown, the gnomes are multiplying, and I’m pretty sure she’s been yelling at the postman again. I swear, she's plotting something. I heard a rumour she's started a birdwatching club as a front for surveillance. I’m not even joking. You are awful! Seriously though, she’s a bit…intense. Change of subject, desperately. Did you catch that new film, “Midnight Bloom”? Everyone’s raving about it. No, not yet. Is it worth braving the crowds for? I saw the trailer and it looked a bit…slow. It  is  slow, but beautifully slow. It's one of those films that stays with you. It’s all about grief and…well, blooming again, I guess. Bit heavy, but good. Though, honestly, after today, I just want something brainless. Like a rom-com where everything goes perfectly. Oh, you need “Set it Up” on Netflix then. It’s pure fluff, but exactly what's needed after a hard day. Speaking of needing things… are you still seeing that guy, Ben? Ben… It's complicated. We're “taking a break.” He just… doesn’t understand what I do, you know? He keeps suggesting I “just relax” when I’m stressed from work.

Right, honestly, the state of this place, eh? I swear, dust breeds in here. It's like a self-replicating organism. You say that every time, Liam. And you’re just as bad as me, you know. You leave your shoes everywhere. That's different! Shoes have a designated… area. Near the door. A strategic placement, really. Though, even then, sometimes they migrate. Speaking of migrating, did you see that advert for the new travel company? The one with the llamas? Llamas? No. Was it on telly or online? I’ve been scrolling through TikTok all evening. It’s a black hole, honestly. On telly, during  Corrie . It was ridiculous. A bloke trying to ride a llama through the Andes. Selling holidays, supposedly. Honestly, the things they come up with. Makes you wonder how advertising execs sleep at night. Probably on a bed of money, thinking about the next llama-based campaign. It’s all manipulation, isn't it? Like that diet ad earlier with the ridiculously toned woman. Oh, aye. She looked like she hadn't eaten a proper meal in her life. Reminds me of Auntie Brenda. Still going on about cabbage soup diets, even after all these years. She started smoking again, you know. No way! After everything she said about it giving her a cough that sounded like a dying walrus? The very same. Apparently, old habits die hard. She says it calms her nerves. I reckon it just makes her cough more. It's grim, that. It is. What are you thinking of doing at the car boot sale on Sunday? Any treasures you’re hoping to unearth? I’m on the lookout for vinyl. Found a couple of decent Beatles records last month. You were brilliant at haggling for those, by the way. You've got a real talent. Years of practice, bartering with market stallholders with my nan. She could get a fiver off a bag of potatoes. It’s a skill, I tell you. Speaking of skills, I was reading about NLP - Neuro-Linguistic Programming - at work today. Fascinating stuff. Apparently, it can help people with all sorts of things, even dyslexia. NLP? Sounds a bit… woo-woo, to be honest. Maybe. But it’s based on understanding how the brain processes information. We had a training session focusing on how it relates to helping patients with trauma. It’s quite clever, actually.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s biblical rain. Makes planning anything impossible. Tell me about it. I was hoping to get the car washed this weekend, but it's looking…optimistic. Speaking of cars, anyone seen those new electric Minis? They look surprisingly good. Yeah, I’ve seen them. Properly smart. Though the price tag is a bit…ouch. Still, better than shelling out for constant petrol, I suppose. It’s a huge investment either way. I’m still saving for a deposit on a house, and it feels like a never-ending task. Especially with interest rates doing…whatever they’re doing. Don’t even  start  me on house prices. I’ve been looking up north, thinking maybe Leeds is more affordable, but it’s still mental. I saw a two-bed terrace going for nearly three hundred thousand! Three hundred thousand?! You’re joking! Even in Hitchin, that’s…significant. It's the same down here. My mate just bought a place in Bournville, tiny garden, needs a full refurb, and he remortgaged himself to the hilt. Speaking of stressful things, has anyone tried that new meditation app, Headspace? I downloaded it, figured I need  something  to calm the nerves with the workload I’ve got at the moment. I’ve heard good things. I tried Calm a while back, but I found the voice a bit…patronising, if you know what I mean? Like it was talking to me like I was five. Oh god, yes! That’s exactly it. I need someone to tell me to breathe, not explain  why  I need to breathe. I've started writing again, actually. Short stories. Keeps me sane. That’s brilliant, Sarah! You always had a knack for that. Remember that piece you wrote for the university magazine? The one about the…what was it? The haunted library? Oh, God. Yes! That was awful. Terribly melodramatic. But it did win a prize, which was nice. I’ve been listening to loads of music lately. Discovered this amazing new band, The Mysterines. They’re a bit grungy, bit psychedelic. Perfect for gloomy Birmingham evenings. Anyone heard of them? Nope. Add them to the list. My Spotify is already overflowing with recommendations I’ll never get around to listening to. I’ve been catching up on films. Watched “Everything Everywhere All at Once” last night.

…and honestly, the houses around here were fields! Proper fields. We moved in ‘68, you know, and it was all farmland. Lovely farmland, mind, but nothing like it is now. Remember old Man Hemmings’ place? Where the estate is now? Just cows. Oh yes, Hemmings. Used to deliver milk, didn't he? Lovely man. It was a proper village then, wasn't it? Everyone knew everyone. Quite a shock coming from Ramsgate, I can tell you. Very different pace. You think  that  was a shock? Try coming here from Birmingham in ‘65! I’d secured the dental practice, thankfully, which obviously eased things, but finding somewhere decent to live… that was a trial. Everything was either brand new, horribly expensive, or falling down. Falling down was the norm in Manchester. Though even there, it was getting a bit spruced up by then, early sixties. But you, Brian, a dentist… you’d have been in demand. Must’ve had your pick. Oh, I did alright. Eventually found a little semi near the high street. Needed  everything  doing to it, though. Damp, dodgy wiring, the whole shebang. But it was affordable, and it was mine. I spent the next five years renovating it. Nearly bankrupted me, if I’m honest. We rented for ages, Margaret and I. Couldn’t afford to buy, not on a teacher’s salary back then. Found a little cottage just off the Common. Damp, naturally. Every winter, the wallpaper would peel off. But it was cosy. We bought almost straight away, didn’t we, John? Lucky really. My father helped with the deposit, thank goodness. It was a new build, one of the first on the estate. Bit boxy, but solid. Where did you two meet, actually? Margaret and you? Now that’s a story. A training weekend, down in Bournemouth. Awful weather, freezing cold, and surrounded by trainee teachers. But Margaret… well, she stood out. Even then, she had that… sparkle. Oh, I remember Bournemouth training weekends! Horrible organised fun. John and I met at college. St. Martin’s, in London. He was a bit of a charmer, even then. St. Martin’s! Good college. I was up at Manchester, of course. English Literature. Then did my postgrad at Leeds. Though I did spend a rather… eventful time in Athens. Athens? Oh, do tell! So, I’d secured a place on a post-grad course at the University of Athens.

…and honestly, the dust! You’d think being antiques, they’d be… cared for. But people just didn’t bother. Polish was a rare sight, let me tell you. Mostly just layers and layers of grime. I specialized in small furniture, you see. Boxes, chests, the occasional little table. Not the big, imposing pieces. Too much hassle. Oh, fascinating. That sounds… physically demanding though, doesn’t it? Lifting and shifting things all the time? My work was decidedly less so. Speech therapy. Mostly sitting and listening, and trying to coax sounds out of people. Though, some of the children… they could be quite energetic! Oh, it was! Years of it. Back problems, naturally. But worth it, in a way. I always loved the stories things held, you know? Imagining the lives they'd witnessed. Who’d sat at that table, what secrets were kept inside that box. It’s silly, I suppose, but… Not at all. I think that’s lovely. It’s about connection, isn't it? To the past. My work was about connection too, in a different way. Helping people  make  connections, through language. I spent thirty years working with children who had difficulties communicating. Autistic children, children with Down’s Syndrome, all sorts. Thirty years! Goodness. That must have been… rewarding. And exhausting. I imagine there were some heart-wrenching stories too. Oh, absolutely. It wasn’t always easy. But the little victories… when a child finally said their first word, or strung a sentence together… those were magical. What about your childhood, Marion? Did you grow up around antiques, or was that something you came to later? Oh, no, not at all. Very ordinary childhood, really. Somerset farm. Mud, animals, a lot of fresh air and even more chores. My father was a dairy farmer, a proper old-fashioned one. Roses down the rows, everything perfect. My mother painted, watercolours mostly. Landscapes. She encouraged me, always had paper and brushes about. That’s where it started, I suppose. The art, not the antiques. The antiques came much later, a way to fund the art, really. A Somerset farm… that sounds idyllic. Though I imagine it was hard work. I grew up in Sydney, Australia. Quite different! Sunshine and beaches, and a much more… laid-back lifestyle. My father was a solicitor, quite a respectable profession. My mother was a teacher. They were very keen on me having a ‘sensible’ career.

Right, so onions are caramelising nicely. You sure we’ve got enough balsamic? Last time, it was a bit…understated. I bought two bottles! Relax. It’s in the cupboard next to the paprika. Honestly, you'd think I deliberately sabotaged dinner last time. No, no, it wasn't sabotage, just…a lack of tangy sweetness. Though, remember Old Man Hemmings at the tattoo parlour? He always said balsamic needs to  bite . Oh god, Hemmings. He probably thinks balsamic is a prerequisite for getting a decent dragon. Speaking of, are you still thinking about getting more ink? Maybe. I've been sketching up ideas. Something floral, I think. A bit of a contrast to the…geometric chaos on my arm. It’s just, money is tight, being a ‘highly educated’ unemployed graduate and all that. You'll get there. And honestly, a floral design would suit you. It’s a palate cleanser after all that blackwork. This smells  amazing  by the way. What are we having with this? I was thinking roasted potatoes and some green beans. Simple, but effective. Speaking of effective, how’s the bakery going? Still selling out of those salted caramel brownies? Sell out every. Single. Day. Honestly, I need to hire someone, but finding reliable staff is a nightmare. Plus, I'm thinking about doing Christmas cookie boxes, you know, fancy decorated ones. Thinking of a pre-order system.  Doorbell rings  That’ll be Chloe. Right on time, as always. Prepare for Christmas overload. She starts planning in July.  Chloe enters  Hello, my loves! Something smells divine. What culinary masterpiece are you two concocting? Caramelised onions and impending potato perfection. Chloe, you are officially banned from mentioning Christmas until at least November. Banned? But it's practically here! I’ve already been sketching out decoration schemes. I'm thinking rustic chic this year, lots of pine cones and fairy lights…and I’ve started compiling a spreadsheet of candy cane suppliers. Spreadsheets? For candy canes? Chloe, that's…intense. Resource management, darling! It's a vital business skill, even when applied to peppermint sticks. Speaking of business, how's the bakery, Liv? Are you going to do those Christmas cookie boxes? I’ll take five, minimum. I was just explaining that to Ben. Pre-orders, definitely. I'm also thinking gingerbread houses. Miniature, edible masterpieces. Gingerbread houses? That's ambitious. Remember that time you tried to make macaroons?

Honestly, Cambridge feels… smaller every time I come. Not in a bad way, just…contained. Like a really beautiful snow globe. It is a bit, isn’t it? Everyone’s so focused on their little bubble. Though, leaving it is a relief, I won’t lie. Back to proper London life. Speaking of London life… have you given any more thought to what you’re doing after you finish? Beyond the immediate celebratory pints, of course. Mum, always practical. I’ve been looking at flats with Finn. Nothing concrete yet, obviously. It’s…daunting. The prices are insane. They are. And you’re thinking of staying in the city? Is Finn on board with that? Definitely. He’s already started spreadsheets. You know Finn. He's found a few possibles in Hackney, closer to his work. They're tiny, but… liveable. And good transport links. Hackney’s nice. A bit…rough around the edges, but it’s got character. Better than squeezing into your Aunt Carol’s spare room indefinitely. Though she  does  insist on having a fully stocked biscuit tin. The biscuit tin is both a blessing and a curse. It’s hard to say no to Carol’s shortbread. But yeah, long-term, that’s not a plan. We both need our own space. Plus, I need to properly  focus  on finishing the thesis. Which, by the way, how’s that progressing? Your father is perpetually asking, and I can only give vague, reassuring noises. It’s… it’s getting there. Headed into the final stretch, I think. Chapter five is the killer. It’s just not  clicking . I've been meeting with Professor Davies regularly, and he's helpful, but it’s still a slog. Well, remember what I always say: a slog is just a fancy word for ‘effort’. And effort is what produces results. You've come this far. Don't let chapter five defeat you. Easy for you to say, the literary editor to the masses. You probably breeze through manuscripts no problem. Oh, darling, you have no idea. The things people submit… Honestly, sometimes I think I should just retire and run a small bookshop. Somewhere quiet. Not Oxford, though. Too…stuffy. Oxford’s a bit much, yeah. All spires and tradition. It feels like a theme park version of a university. Precisely. Cambridge is better. More…grounded, somehow. Though, I do wonder if maybe you should have considered applying there for your PhD.

…and then the train just completely stalled outside Peterborough. Honestly, you’d think with all the investment in the lines it’d be better! Oh no! That sounds awful. I drove today, thankfully. Though parking in Cambridge is, as ever, a complete nightmare. Took me about twenty minutes just to find a space. Ah, yes. Cambridge parking. A perpetual struggle. I used to cycle in, back when my knees allowed it. Now, I’m grateful for the Park and Ride. Though even  that  can be a bit chaotic on days like these. Alumni Day always brings them out in force. It’s lovely to see so many people back though, isn't it? I mean, I only graduated a couple of years ago, but it’s nice to see what everyone’s up to. I’m a Language Research Co-ordinator now. Quite niche! That sounds fascinating! I’m an administrator in the same field, actually. Though my focus is a bit more on the practical side of things. Logistics, funding… the less glamorous stuff. Language research, you say? Excellent! I spent a good portion of my career digging up languages, in a rather more literal sense. Archaeological work, mostly. Though it wasn’t all trowels and dust, you know. A lot of linguistic detective work involved. Really? That’s amazing! I’m mostly looking at contemporary usage, but I’ve always been fascinated by historical linguistics. Did you work on any particularly exciting projects? Oh, several. One involved excavating a small village in Norfolk, pre-Roman settlement. We uncovered evidence of a surprisingly sophisticated trading network. And the pottery shards… the markings on them suggested a language link to early Germanic dialects. Quite a breakthrough, really. Wow. That’s incredible. It sounds a million miles away from spreadsheets and grant applications! Indeed! Though even spreadsheets have their story to tell, I suppose. I lectured on Arab culture for many years, of course. Fascinating language, Arabic. The calligraphy alone is a work of art. Although trying to explain the complexities of the verb system to undergraduates could be… challenging. I can imagine! I’ve dabbled in a little bit of Mandarin, purely for personal interest. It's unbelievably difficult. The tones! I’ve heard. My brother did a year abroad in Shanghai and came back completely baffled. Said he couldn't even order coffee without causing offence. The Chinese languages present a unique set of challenges, certainly.

Right, so, genuinely, another shift at the library. Honestly, it’s just…quiet. Like, aggressively quiet. I spent half an hour alphabetising the travel section today. Travel! Who even  uses  travel sections anymore? Everyone just books things online. Sounds… peaceful? Though yeah, alphabetising is a special kind of hell. At least I had a chaotic rush at the bakery today. Someone tried to order a cake with, get this, a picture of their cat wearing a tiny sombrero. No. Way. Honestly, people are wild. We had a guy demand a gluten-free, vegan, sugar-free brownie. Like, at that point, just eat an apple, mate. The requests I get… it’s a different level. A client today wanted a music video shot entirely on a vintage Super 8 camera, but with a modern, hyper-colour-graded aesthetic. It was a logistical nightmare. Basically, expensive and makes no sense. See, that’s the thing, isn’t it? Everyone wants something unique, but nobody wants to pay for it. I'm convinced everyone’s seen too many TikToks and thinks everything should be instantly achievable. Oh god, TikTok. I saw a video the other day of a guy building a fully functional replica of the Starship Enterprise… out of toothpicks.  Toothpicks!  It had, like, millions of views. It’s completely warped our sense of scale. Like, someone’s spending a year building a toothpick spaceship and that’s considered entertainment. Meanwhile, I’m trying to keep a small business afloat and people are arguing over fifty pence. It's the attention economy. The more ridiculous, the more clicks. I was talking to a younger assistant the other day, she was saying she wants to be a “content creator”. I asked what her actual skills were. Blank face. It's genuinely worrying. My little cousin, he’s fifteen, wants to drop out of school and just…stream himself playing video games. He genuinely thinks he can make a living doing that. It’s the dream, isn’t it? The overnight success. But the reality is… grueling. It's a lot of work for very little return. And the pressure! I think there's something about the education system as well, don't you? It just doesn’t prepare people. My mate, Liam, he left sixth form, couldn't hack it, and now he's stuck in a dead-end call centre job. He’s brilliant, proper clever, but he always struggled with the academic side of things.

Honestly, this pint is a lifesaver. That departmental meeting was… draining. Professor Davies just  loves  to hear himself talk, doesn’t he? And about nothing particularly insightful, I might add. Tell me about it. I swear, half of those meetings could be emails. Though, I suppose if they were emails, he wouldn't get to pontificate about post-structuralism for an hour. Precisely! And then he had the audacity to ask  me  to rework the module outlines. After he’d spent twenty minutes telling everyone how brilliant his are. The cheek. You need a raise, love. Seriously. All that extra work and you're still probably underpaid considering how much workload you handle. Have you started looking into that pay review thing the union mentioned? I glanced at the information, yes. But honestly, the forms look so complicated. And the whole thing feels… futile. They always say they’re committed to fair pay, and then it’s just more bureaucratic hoops to jump through. It's like the government with everything. You’re not wrong. Did you see that headline about the NHS waiting lists? Absolutely terrifying. My mum was saying her friend’s been waiting six months for a hip replacement. Six months! It’s appalling. And then they wonder why people are resorting to private healthcare, even if they can barely afford it. It's just… a mess. And the whole thing with the energy bills going up again? Honestly, I feel like we’re constantly robbing Peter to pay Paul. I know. We were looking at our budget last night, trying to figure out how we’re going to afford to put away anything for a deposit on a house. It feels impossible. Especially with interest rates the way they are. Don't even get me started on house prices. Remember when we thought we might be able to afford a little something in Norwich within five years? That feels like a lifetime ago now. Feels like another planet. Speaking of things feeling impossible, have you seen the new series of  The Crown ? I’ve started it! It’s… surprisingly good. I was a bit skeptical at first, but Imelda Staunton is phenomenal as the Queen. Isn't she? It's just so well made. Though it does make me feel slightly guilty enjoying a lavish historical drama when half the country is struggling to heat their homes.

Honestly, this quiche is lovely, Margaret. Did you use that cheddar from the farmers’ market? It makes all the difference. It is really good, Gran! And yes, I did. It was ridiculously expensive, but worth it, I think. Especially with the asparagus. Farmers’ market cheddar  is  a different beast, isn't it? Takes me back to when your grandfather used to bring home a whole wheel from Lincolnshire. He’d insist on grating it himself, much to your mother’s annoyance. Said pre-grated cheddar had no flavour. Oh, he was a stubborn one, your grandfather. But he was right, as usual. Pre-grated just isn't the same. Though honestly, grating all that cheese… a real chore. Speaking of chores, I finally managed to sort out a new TV package. Apparently, you can get everything through the internet now. No more cable boxes, which is amazing. The internet. Remarkable, isn’t it? Still can’t quite wrap my head around it, but you young’uns seem to manage alright. Though I saw something on the news about hacking and data breaches… sounds terribly unsettling. It is a worry. Though I mostly use it to look at pictures of badgers. I’ve joined a badger watching group online, apparently there’s a sett down by the canal. Badgers? Really, Gran? That’s… specific. They’re fascinating creatures! And so misunderstood. We need to protect their habitats, you know. Your grandmother was always rather fond of badgers too, actually. She used to leave out milk for the hedgehogs as well. Said it was a kindness. That’s sweet. Have you guys seen any good films lately? I’m trying to catch up. I was working on a huge manuscript at the publishers last month, utterly consumed by fungal taxonomy. No time for anything else. Fungal taxonomy? Good heavens. Sounds… intense. I saw that one with Meryl Streep, the one about the protests. Quite moving, though a bit long. I’m a bit behind on the films, I’m afraid. Been re-watching some old war documentaries. Reminds me of my time doing National Service. Not that I was ever  in  a war, thankfully. Oh, did you ever tell me about that? Briefly. It was… an experience. Not one I’m particularly eager to relive in detail. It wasn't exactly glorious, despite what the recruitment posters promised. Your Uncle David always said his National Service was a complete waste of time, spent polishing boots and peeling potatoes.

So, what were you up to all day, Leo? Still glued to that… whatever it is you play? It's called ‘Realm of Champions’, Dad! And I wasn’t  glued  to it. I took breaks. Breaks to eat, mostly, I suspect. He practically lives on crisps and orange juice these days. Mum! That's not true! I had a sandwich too. A sandwich consisting of mostly crisps, I imagine. Was anyone else playing with you online? Yeah, Ben and Josh. We were trying to beat Level 7, but it’s seriously hard. There’s this dragon… Oh a dragon! Sounds terrifying. Speaking of terrifying, someone’s decided Mr. Bear needs a bath again. . Look at you, little man, giving Bear a good chewing. Baa! He’s a dedicated bath-giver, alright. Honestly, I don’t know where he gets it from. Maybe from you, Sarah? You’re always cleaning. Someone has to! This house would be chaos otherwise. We went for a little walk earlier, just around the estate. Trying to tire him out. He was fascinated by a pigeon. A  pigeon , can you believe it? Stared at it for a good ten minutes. Pigeons are pretty boring. Unless they're, like, in a game. You can shoot them in Realm of Champions. Not that I  do  shoot them. It’s just… an option. Right. An option. See, Sarah, this is what I’m talking about. It's all dragons and virtual pigeon shooting. When I was his age, we were building dens and skinning our knees. Times change, love. Honestly, I'm just glad he's entertained. And he's good. He's actually very good at building things with Lego. Remember that spaceship he made last week? I helped with the spaceship. A little. A little? I seem to recall you mostly instructing and occasionally adding a single brick. Hey! It's about strategic oversight, okay? I was managing the project. Oh, he’s a project manager now, is he? Little Mr. Efficient. While you're managing projects, perhaps you could manage washing the dishes after dinner? Mum! Not fair! Ah, the age-old battle. Don't worry, Leo. We all had to wash the dishes at your age. Though, I did try to convince your grandmother that playing the bodhrán was a valid excuse… didn’t work. Rest assured, the bodhrán won’t get you out of dish duty here either.

Right then, so Christmas dinner at yours this year, is it? Good luck with all that, eh? Oh, don’t start, George! It's always me. Honestly, I think I’m permanently attached to a roasting tin by now. But it’s nice, isn’t it? Having everyone. It is, Barbara. Lovely to have a proper family Christmas. Though the journey up from Brum is always…character building. Especially on the A14. Character building? That’s a polite way of saying ‘absolutely awful’! Last year we were stuck behind a van full of Christmas trees for like, forever. And Dad kept trying to overtake, even though there was no space! I was so embarrassed. Now, now, I was just trying to make good time. Besides, a man needs a decent view of Christmas trees, doesn't he? Speaking of which, how’s young Tom? Still glued to your daughter, is he? Oh, Tom’s lovely. A good boy, really. Maisie seems very happy. Though she’s been rather secretive lately. Always whispering on the phone, sneaking off… teenager stuff, I suppose. He’s alright, I guess. A bit…intense about horses. He only talks about horses. Like,  only . It’s true! Went to the stables with them last weekend and it was just…horse, horse, horse. Apparently, they're thinking of getting another one? Another one? Goodness me. That’s quite an investment. Still, a healthy hobby, I suppose. Keeps them outdoors. It's better than staring at screens all day. Speaking of investments, I need to get my car serviced before Christmas. The thing’s making a right racket. Sounds like a bag of spanners rattling around in there. Oh, you and that car, George! You’ve had it for…what, thirty years? Forty! Forty years. And she's still going strong. Just needs a little TLC. Reminds me of you, Barbara. Oh, you flatterer! I haven't needed TLC in forty years, George, I assure you. Although a new paintbrush for the watercolour set wouldn't go amiss… I’m thinking of doing a winter scene, you know. All snow and frosty trees. You’re very talented, Barbara. Always have been. Remember that portrait you did of my mum? Still hanging in the hallway, it is. Ooh, yeah! That was amazing. It looked just like her. It did! You should do one of our dog, Alfie. He’s very photogenic.

Honestly, the shift was  mental  today. Old Mr. Henderson decided he was a bird and kept trying to flap his arms. Had to call security. A bird, you say? Sounds delightful. Perhaps he’s finally embracing his true self. Seriously? That’s… a new one. Is he alright though, Mum? Physically, yes. Just… confused. It’s getting harder, you know? Seeing them decline like that. It makes you appreciate a clear head. Speaking of which, how was your day, love? Still battling the marketing jargon? You have no idea. Had a client who wanted ‘synergistic brand narratives’ for…dog biscuits. Dog biscuits, Mum! Synergistic brand narratives for dog biscuits? That’s brilliant. They’re really scraping the barrel, aren’t they? I had a meeting with the finance team about next quarter’s budget. It was…spirited. Let’s leave it at that. ‘Spirited’ usually means someone was shouting. You’ve got that look. Did Brenda try to claim the stationery budget again? Worse. She suggested we re-evaluate the coffee machine. Apparently, it’s ‘unsustainable’ according to her calculations. Oh, Brenda. She’s a menace. Honestly, she’d audit the air we breathe if she could. She would. Anyway, are we still on for dinner with the Millers on Saturday? I promised Sarah I’d try and make that lemon drizzle cake she’s always raving about. Yes, Saturday’s good. Though, if Henderson starts roosting in my garden, I may have to cancel. You’re terrible. Speaking of Saturday, any ideas what you're getting Dad for his birthday? It’s next week, isn’t it? I'm stumped. He says he doesn't  need  anything. Which, knowing him, means he secretly wants a replica Spitfire or something. He did mention wanting to go to that airshow at Biggin Hill again. Remember? He went on about it for weeks after last time. Oh, that’s a good idea! I saw some tickets online last week. Might be a bit pricey though. We could pool our money. It would be a good day out. Unless Brenda decides to audit the airspace above Biggin Hill. Don’t even mention her name. What about you, Millie? Any weekend plans? Besides rescuing brands with biscuit-related narratives? Thinking of going to that new pottery painting place in Tunbridge Wells with Chloe. Apparently, it's really therapeutic. And I need something therapeutic after today’s client meeting.

Well, I saw Doreen at the shops yesterday. You wouldn’t believe what she was saying about Bernard. Oh dear, not another saga with Bernard is there? What’s he done now? Apparently, he’s got himself a… a companion. A lady friend. Doreen was practically spitting feathers. Said she saw him holding hands with her outside the bakery. Bernard? Really? He always struck me as a bit of a one-woman man. Though, you never really know, do you? It's always the quiet ones, isn't it? Though, honestly, at their age… you'd think they’d have enough drama already. It’s awful for Doreen though, isn’t it? After all these years. Still, she's a strong woman. She’ll get through it. Did she say who this… lady friend is? Just that she’s from the bridge club. Apparently, younger than him. Much younger. Bridge club, eh? Well, that explains a lot. Those ladies are a crafty bunch. Speaking of gatherings, are we still on for the little party next Saturday? I’ve ordered a new cheese board, thought we could christen it. Oh lovely! Yes, absolutely. I’m planning on making that chocolate cake you like so much, Arthur. Though, with the price of everything these days… even a simple cake feels like a luxury. It’s the inflation, isn’t it? Everything’s gone up. You go to the shops and come out feeling like you’ve robbed a bank. I had to have a new heating element for the water tank. Nearly £80 just for the part! It’s scandalous. You think back to how things were… you could buy a whole house for what a new washing machine costs now. And then there’s the potential for power cuts this winter. Remember that time we were all without power for two days after the storm? It was like living in the Dark Ages. Oh don't remind me! I couldn't even make a cup of tea! Honestly, what’s the point of civilisation without a kettle? I was watching  Big Brother  the other night, and they simulated a power cut as part of a task. It was fascinating watching them all fall apart. Honestly, people are so reliant on their gadgets. Gadgets! They’re a curse. My grandson spends his entire life glued to that phone. Doesn’t even know how to hold a proper conversation anymore.

Right, so I genuinely think my mum thinks I’m still sixteen. Honestly. She was going on about needing to check what time I was getting the train back up north, and then proceeded to ask if  Dad  was picking me up from Doncaster station. Oh, bless her. Is she alright though? Is she…forgetful, generally? No, not particularly! It’s just…me, I think. She treats me like I haven’t got a brain cell between them. Like I’ll just wander off a platform and get lost. Last time I visited, she packed me a bag with like, three jumpers and a hot water bottle, even though it was July! Oh my god. That’s… peak Mum behaviour. My nan is the same. She still tries to slip me £20 when I see her, convinced I’m a struggling student. I’ve got a  Masters ! Exactly! It’s just… patronising! Still, she means well, I suppose. Speaking of parental units, did your dad ever tell you that story about when he tried to build a shed? Oh god, the shed saga. Don't even get me started. That story’s practically family folklore. It took him six months, involved a near-hospitalisation with a rogue hammer, and the final product leans at a frankly alarming angle. I remember him telling me that! He made it sound like it was a feat of engineering. "It required precision, you see, and a level of commitment..." Meanwhile, it looks like it's about to fall apart in a stiff breeze. The sheer  pride  he took in that wobbly monstrosity. It’s endearing, isn’t it? Right, dinner’s almost ready. Did you want to put the film on now, or after? I was thinking we could watch that new Wes Anderson one. Ooh, yes! Definitely after. I need sustenance first. And maybe another glass of wine. This conference I’m organising is  killing  me. The AV guy keeps cancelling on me, apparently his van broke down. Again. Honestly, the drama with event planning. It’s a whole other level. I’ve got a similar thing happening with a supplier for the new theatre project. They’re threatening to pull out at the last minute because…apparently, they have a dispute with the catering company? It’s ridiculous. It always is ridiculous. It’s like, everyone’s got to have a problem, right?

Aye, well, it's a right pickle, isn't it? This Scottish referendum. Yeah, Dad keeps going on about it. Says it’ll be a disaster if they go. Your Dad's got a point, lad. Though I can understand why they want to, mind. They've always been a bit…different, haven't they? Thinking they're superior and all that. He says it’ll mess up the whole UK, like. Everything's all connected. It will. Absolutely will. Think about the borders, for a start. All that paperwork, the lorries queuing up. It’ll be a right mess at the border crossings. More hassle than crossing the Channel. What about the money, then? He said something about the oil. Oh, the oil. That’s where it gets tricky. They reckon they'll be rolling in it, don't they? But it’s not that simple. The price of oil goes up and down like a yo-yo. And then there's the decommissioning costs…getting rid of all the old rigs. That’s a fortune. So it’s not as easy as just taking the oil and being rich? Not at all, love. It's never that easy, is it? Remember when Maggie Thatcher shut down the mines? Said it'd be better for the economy. Look what happened to those communities. It tore them apart. This could be a bit like that, only on a grander scale. I think Mr. Henderson, our history teacher, said it's about identity, too. That a lot of Scots feel like England tells them what to do. Aye, there's a bit of that in it, I suppose. A lot of history there, you see. Old grievances and all. My grandma used to go on about the Jacobites, always siding with the Scots. Though she couldn’t tell you a thing about politics, just that they were ‘our people.’ Did she have a Scottish accent? Not really. She grew up down south. But she always felt a connection. It’s a complicated thing, identity. More than just a flag and a bit of tartan. So, what do you think will happen? Honestly? I don't know. I think it’ll be close. Very close. People are passionate about it, on both sides. It'll be a nervous night when the results come in, that's for sure. I just hope they think it through properly.

Honestly, this Jeremy Kyle is a car crash, isn’t it? But you can’t look away. Tell me about it! It's awful, but I’m proper hooked. Listen to that fella, though. You can barely understand a word he’s saying. It’s like… is he even  speaking  English? It’s the elision, innit? Dropping all the ‘t’s and ‘h’s. Makes it a right mess. Elision? What’s that then? Basically, like, when people run words together and leave bits out. Like, instead of “want to” they say “wanna”. It’s common, but some people take it to the extreme. Yeah, it's proper common where I'm from. "Gonna," "shoulda," the lot. But that guy… he's on another level. It’s a Scouse thing, isn’t it? The accent generally kinda… swallows things. My auntie Sheila sounds like that when she’s had a few sherries. So does my nan, but she’s always sounded like that, sherry or no sherry. It’s just how she’s always talked. It’s quite endearing, actually. Endearing? He sounds like he’s mumbling into a sock! Honestly, this is why people poke fun at accents. It's not about being superior, it's just... some are harder to decipher. You think our accents are easy to understand, then? Because I get stick for sounding ‘broad’ when I go down South. People ask me to repeat myself all the time. Aye, me too. They think we’re all extras from  Emmerdale . It's a bit insulting, really. It's funny, isn't it? Everyone thinks  their  accent is normal, and everyone else’s is weird. Like when I first came to Chester, everyone thought I was speaking gibberish. They were all like, "What did you  say ?" Oh, it’s the same for me coming down here from Derby. Everyone's like "What are you saying?" and I'm thinking, "I'm speaking English, love!" Just a slightly different flavour. Still, you’ve gotta admit, Jeremy Kyle brings out the best – or worst – in everyone’s accents. It's like the stress makes it even more pronounced. It does, doesn’t it? Listen to that woman now, she sounds like she's about to explode. Ooh, here we go… someone’s about to yell something dramatic. Pass the crisps. This is getting good. Oh, God, she's accusing him of sleeping with her sister...

Honestly, the refereeing in this game is absolutely shocking. Shocking! Aye, it’s a bit ropey, isn’t it? Gave that away far too easily. Should’ve held their ground. Held their ground? They were practically  inviting  a foul! Honestly, I swear some of these refs have never actually  played  football. You’re telling me. It’s all about speed and physicality now, isn't it? No one actually  thinks  about the strategy anymore. Reminds me of when my grandad used to complain about the game changing in the 70s. Said it weren’t proper football without a good old-fashioned tackle. Ha! My Nana’s the same, but she’s more concerned with if the players have “decent haircuts”. She judges the entire team on that. That’s brilliant. You know, it’s funny, you spend all this time doing academically rigorous research, and then you just end up shouting at a telly about twenty-two lads kicking a ball around. Tell me about it. It’s therapeutic, though, isn’t it? A good release. Speaking of therapeutic... how’s the knitting going? Still on that scarf for your mum? Slowly. Very slowly. I’m attempting a cable knit, which, apparently, requires a level of dexterity I simply do not possess. It looks less like a scarf and more like a… a tangled fishing net. Oh, no! Send me a picture, I want to see the carnage. I’ve started a little hat for the… well, for when we potentially have a little one. Oh, seriously? Already thinking about hats? That’s moving fast! Well, I was browsing baby names again last night, and it’s just… happening. I'm deep in the rabbit hole. I found one that means 'star' in Gaelic. That’s nice. We haven't even gotten to names yet. We're still firmly in the 'is this even possible?' stage. Though, I did see someone suggest 'Ragnar' the other day. Ragnar?! Seriously? Where did they even  find  that? Apparently it’s making a comeback. Viking chic, apparently. It's good to have a list ready incase the Olympics are on again. They always get name trends soaring. Oh, good point. Remember when everyone suddenly decided to name their kids after cyclists after London 2012? It was madness. Totally. It's funny how easily influenced people are. Although, Ragnar… I think that might be pushing it a bit.

Honestly, the Bee Movie is… a cinematic masterpiece. Don’t you think? The legal arguments were surprisingly sound. Bees talking! It's so funny when they all fly around! And the bee gets lost in human world! Is it real bees talking, Mummy? Well, not  real  real, darling. It’s a cartoon. But it’s a very clever cartoon. It makes you think. I want to be a bee! I’d collect all the pollen! I want to be King Arthur! With a really big sword! You both want to be… powerful figures, it seems. Speaking of powerful figures… all this talk about the Royal Family. It’s just… odd, isn't it? Paying to go and look at where they live. But they have nice gardens! They  do  have nice gardens. And apparently, they’re very fussy about what fruit they eat. I read an article about how they only have specific varieties of peaches and plums. Royal fruit, apparently. So they don't eat apples? Granny makes the best apple crumble! They probably eat apples, sweetheart. Just… very  particular  apples. It just feels a bit… wrong, doesn’t it? That we’re effectively paying to peek into someone else's life. I’m leaning more and more towards being a Republican, honestly. What’s a Republican? It means you don't think we should have a King or Queen. You think everyone should be equal. It's a bit complicated for now. I want to be King! Then I could have ALL the apples! And a big sword! You would be a very generous King, I suspect. But you know, it does make you think. Would you actually  want  to be royal? All that scrutiny… or a politician, for that matter? No privacy. I don't want people looking at me all the time. Exactly! It sounds exhausting. Now, have you both taken your vitamins this morning? Don't forget, we’re going to the Olympic Stadium on Saturday! For the diving! Can I wear my goggles? Absolutely! But remember, we need to be super quiet. It’s a competition, and we don't want to disturb the divers. Total silence. Like a bee! Quiet flying! Precisely! Very good comparison. Remind me again, did I book that restaurant for after? We  always  struggle taking you two to restaurants. It's either too loud or too boring or… I just want chips!

Honestly, that tip was chaos. Absolute chaos. People hauling furniture, old carpets… you’d think it was a free-for-all. Tell me about it! I saw a woman trying to load a complete bathroom suite into a Mini. A  Mini , Elsie! Sounds… intense. Typical Saturday afternoon. Did you manage to get rid of everything, Mum? Nearly. Just the attic left now. Honestly, the amount of junk accumulated over the years… it’s frightening. Your father, bless him, never threw  anything  away. Said it might be useful. That’s men for you. Mine’s the same. I found a box of screws he’d been saving “just in case” from 1987. 1987! Seriously? What were they even  for ? He couldn’t remember. That was the point! Speaking of useful things, did you see that antique dresser went for a fortune at Thompson’s auction last week? The one Old Man Hemmings had? Oh, I did! I was quite surprised. I always thought it was a bit drab. Though, it was probably good quality. Everything was better made back then, wasn’t it? Not like the flatpack stuff they sell now. Absolutely. We’re redecorating the spare room, trying to go for a sort of… shabby chic look. It’s proving tricky. There's so much  stuff  out there labelled ‘shabby chic’ that’s just… cheap. Shabby chic is just a polite way of saying ‘old and falling apart’, isn’t it? Pretty much. Though a genuinely good antique can look amazing. You wouldn't believe the price of original William Morris wallpaper these days. William Morris… lovely man, wasn’t he? Always thought he was a bit of a socialist though. Remember the debates at university? Oh, don’t get you started on politics! I've got enough to deal with trying to explain the curriculum changes to my Year 9s.
