Honestly, it’s like they're deliberately making it more complicated. Miss, can I get another scone? These are good. Of course, love. Just don't fill up entirely on scones before dinner. Have you heard about Brenda's hen do? Apparently, she’s insisting on a medieval-themed weekend in Thirsk. Thirsk? Oh dear. That sounds… ambitious. What are they planning? Jousting? Something like that, apparently. They’re hiring costumes and trying to find a falconry centre. It's going to be a disaster, I tell you. A complete disaster.

Right, so I was thinking, for your birthday, we could actually go to the museum. Not just wander around town, proper museum. The Walker Art Gallery, maybe? Ooh, that’s nice. I haven't been in ages. But parking's a nightmare around there, isn’t it? Remember last time we tried, we ended up miles away and practically had to take a bus back? Yeah, I do. Nightmare. We could get the train, easy peasy. Though, then we’re limited to what we can bring back if we do any shopping. Speaking of which, have you started thinking about Christmas presents at all? I’m completely behind. A little bit. I've got a few ideas, mostly online shopping. It's less stressful than fighting through Liverpool One. How's work been? Still battling the year sevens? Absolutely. Honestly, some of the things they come out with, you wouldn’t believe. Tried to explain irregular verbs to one lad, and he genuinely thought 'ate' was another animal. Like a type of bird. Oh, you’re kidding! They're brilliant, aren't they? But exhausting. My day was… interesting. Had a really difficult session with one of my patients. He's going through a really rough patch, and it’s hard not to get completely emotionally involved. That sounds tough. You’re too good at your job, you care too much. Need a massive chocolate biscuit to cheer yourself up. Definitely. You know, Sarah and Ben are finally setting a date for the wedding. Apparently, it’s next summer. They’re looking at that venue near Formby, the one with the gardens. Oh, lovely! That’ll be a good one. Hopefully, the weather will be decent. Have they asked us to be ushers or anything yet? Not yet. I think they're still figuring everything out. Listen, about moving… I was looking at places in Allerton again. Found a couple with gardens. Imagine, a garden for a dog! Hold your horses! We haven't even  talked  about a dog! It's a big responsibility. And gardens are expensive to maintain. I know, I know. Just daydreaming. But imagine, a little scruffy thing running around! Anyway, have you heard back about that interview for your Masters? Not yet. I'm trying not to think about it. The waiting is the worst part. I’ve been checking my emails every five minutes. I really want to do it, though.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience. I think that’s supposed to be pasta. It tastes vaguely of sadness. Tell me about it. I swear they just boil everything in the same water. Yesterday’s curry flavour seemed to have permeated the mashed potato. It was… unsettling. Oh god, no! You're right, it  did  taste faintly of spice. I just assumed I was imagining things. Speaking of unsettling, have you seen the new series of ‘Bridgerton’? Oh my god, yes! It's so ridiculous. I’m fully on board though. The costumes are insane, and honestly, I’m living for the drama. Lord Debling is… something. He's  awful ! But you can’t look away, can you? Like a train wreck. Though Daphne and Simon in the first series were on another level. I keep rewatching clips on YouTube when I should be, you know,  studying . Don’t we all? I’ve been down a whole Disney rabbit hole this week. Watched ‘Hercules’ for the first time in ages. Philoctetes is a mood. Oh my god, YES! Phil is the best. He’s so cynical and sarcastic. It’s perfect. I need a Disney rewatch. It’s been way too long. What are you doing this weekend? Anything exciting planned? Not much, actually. My brother's having a football viewing party, but I’m not massively into football. I might just chill, try and finish that assignment for Modern History, and maybe go to that new café, ‘Bloom,’ on Albion Street. Have you heard of it? Ooh, no! What’s it like? Is the coffee good? That’s the important thing. I’m desperate for a decent flat white. This uni coffee is basically coloured water. Apparently, it's amazing. My friend, Priya, went yesterday and said their pistachio croissant is life-changing. Also, they have all these cute fairy lights and plants everywhere. Super Instagrammable. Pistachio croissant… okay, you're selling this. We should go! Saturday? Yeah, Saturday sounds good. We could grab some lunch there, maybe do a bit of window shopping afterwards. I need to browse some new clothes. The temptations of Shein are too strong. Honestly, same. It’s a dangerous website. Speaking of dangerous, have you seen what Liam did on his Instagram story? He got a tattoo! No way! What did he get? Another questionable nautical thing? He's obsessed with anchors, it’s baffling.

Right, so I finally got Charizard. Took ages to evolve him, honestly. It was brutal. Oh, good for you! Is that the really… fiery dragon one? Oisin loves dragons. He keeps pointing at pictures in books, shouting “Drah-gon!” It’s adorable, but mostly just noise. Drah-gon! Nana! Yeah, that's the one. It took like, a million Charizard candies. Honestly, Pokémon Go is taking over my life. It’s good you’re getting out and about though, isn’t it? Instead of just glued to a screen all the time. Speaking of screens, have you Skyped your Dad this week? He was asking about you. Not yet, I was going to tomorrow. He wants to hear about the school trip. Good. He misses you. Listen, I was thinking… we could maybe go for Ramen on Saturday? There’s that new place opened down by the river. Ooh yeah, I’ve heard it's good. Is Oisin coming? Probably. He's been obsessed with noodles lately. Although getting him to  stay  in his seat while eating is another matter entirely. He just wants to chuck them about. Noodles! Up! See? Exactly. Speaking of chucking things, have you seen where you’ve left your skinny jeans? I need to get them in the wash. They’re practically growing legs and walking around on their own. They're probably under my bed. Sorry. I was practicing guitar in them. Guitar in skinny jeans? That sounds… restrictive. It’s fine! It doesn’t hinder my shredding. Much. Hey, do you think we could get ice cream after Ramen? We’ll see. Depends on how well Oisin behaves. Although, honestly, a bribe might be necessary. He’s been saying “more” all day. Just… “More! More! More!” It’s driving me slightly insane. More! Juice! See! More juice now, apparently. Honestly, I swear he understands more than he lets on. He just likes the reaction. He's a clever one, that Oisin. Hey, did you manage to find those fluffy slippers I left here last time? The dinosaur ones? Actually, no. I think he’s hidden them somewhere. He loves carrying them around. It’s a whole thing. We’ll find them eventually. Probably under the sofa, with the remote control and a half-eaten biscuit. Classic Oisin. Right, gotta go finish evolving my Squirtle. It’s a matter of national importance. Alright, alright.

Honestly, this cupboard is a disaster. I’ve unearthed things I’d completely forgotten about. Look at this! Oh my goodness. Is that…? Is that the gardening set? The little green plastic one? The very one! With the tiny watering can and the little trowel. Oh, the hours we spent ‘gardening’ in the garden with that. Mostly just digging holes and then complaining about getting muddy. Mud was inevitable. Mum never understood why we couldn't just  play  with it without getting covered head to toe. She’d always be sending us back inside for a wash. She thought we were deliberately trying to annoy her, didn't she? We weren’t! We were just committed gardeners. Committed mud-makers, more like. I remember trying to grow cress in those little pots, desperately hoping something would actually sprout. It never did. Oh, me too! It always just looked like green dust. And the little plastic strawberries! They were the best. They  were  the best. I think I used to pretend they were poisonous and try to trick you into eating them. You did! You were a menace. You always were. Now, what’s this tucked away at the back… oh! Bako! Bako! Oh, bless. Remember how we used to build the most magnificent, wobbly towers with that? And then inevitably, they’d all come crashing down. Every. Single. Time. And we’d blame each other, even though it was always structurally unsound from the beginning. It was never  my  fault! You’d always put one piece on at a ridiculous angle. I did not! You were the structural engineer, you should have foreseen the problems. Oh, here we go. Still assigning blame after all these years. It’s a wonder we’re still friends. Friends for life, remember? Although, truthfully, I’m starting to think maybe we should just donate everything. This is all just…stuff. It's not just stuff! It’s…memories. It’s a little bit of our childhood. It feels a bit sad to just get rid of it. I know, but where are we going to put it all? We’ve already got boxes of photos and old letters. And honestly, it’s just gathering dust. Perhaps we could keep the gardening set and the Bako. Just those two. Hmm. Maybe. It's just…it feels like letting go of a part of ourselves, doesn’t it?

Honestly, I think that walk did the trick. He’s properly conked out. Good. He was getting a bit… vocal back there. Felt like everyone in the park was judging our parenting. Oh, don’t be silly. Everyone’s too busy trying to manage their own chaos to judge anyone else. Though, did you feel that mosquito bite? I swear, even in October, they’re still lurking. Ugh, yes! Right on my ankle. I’m covered in them. I thought they’d gone for the winter. London’s bad enough, but even here… It's ridiculous. I'm going to have to invest in one of those sonic repellent things. Or just wear long trousers all the time, which defeats the point of living somewhere vaguely pleasant. Good luck with that. You in long trousers? I’d put money on it not happening. Speaking of things that are unpleasant… the traffic on the way back was horrendous. Tell me about it! What normally takes ten minutes took nearly half an hour. I think there was an accident on the A11. Probably. It's always something. Makes you wonder why we bother driving anywhere. Should’ve walked further, really. Though my legs are feeling it. Mine too, actually. Trying to push the buggy up that hill is a workout. Still, better than being stuck in a metal box, listening to LBC. True. Although, I was thinking about that gig next week. The one with… what are they called? 'Static Bloom'? Oh, yeah! They’re playing at the Waterfront, aren’t they? I was hoping we could go. I checked, and it’s on a Tuesday. We could potentially… if your mum’s still happy to have first dibs on babysitting? I’ll ask her. She loves having him over, even if he does put her through the wringer. She says it keeps her young. That's her way of saying 'you're terrible at parenting, let me show you how it's done'. Something like that. But honestly, a Tuesday night gig sounds… blissfully adult. Actual music, not just nursery rhymes. Exactly. And maybe even a pint. Or two. Don’t push it. One pint, max. We still have to drive home, even if the traffic is trying to sabotage us. And I'm not letting  you  drive after a pint. Fair enough, fair enough. One pint it is. Let’s just hope Static Bloom are worth braving the mosquitoes, the traffic, and the potential judgement of fellow parents.

Right, honestly, the day was  brutal . Eight hours on the course, sun beating down, and old man Hemmings complaining about everything. Everything! Oh, no way. Hemmings? He’s always a nightmare, isn't he? What was it this time? The greens too fast? The bunkers too sandy? Both, actually! And then he started going on about my swing needing ‘adjustments’. Like he even knows what he’s talking about. Honestly, if I had a pound for every unsolicited swing tip I’ve gotten… You’d be retired already and sunning yourself on a beach. Speaking of retirement, I spent the entire day trying to wrestle with this application for the grad scheme at… well, it doesn’t matter which one, they all want the same ridiculous things. "Describe a time you demonstrated initiative..." Ugh. Sounds thrilling. You’ve been at it for, what, a month now? Still nothing? Nothing. Sent out, like, twenty applications. Had one automated rejection, and then…radio silence. It's so disheartening. I keep checking my emails every five minutes. It's worse than waiting for exam results at uni. I know it’s tough. Recruitment is a joke, honestly. It's all algorithms and keywords and… nothing about actually being able to do the job. Look, don't give up. Something will come through. You were top of your class, remember? Easy for you to say, you're a professional golfer. You have a tangible skill! I have a degree in…Medieval History. Apparently, there’s limited demand for that in the current job market. Hey! Medieval History is cool. You could write a book! Or be a consultant on  Game of Thrones  - wait, is that still a thing? Not really. Anyway, I did manage to escape the clutches of my laptop for a couple of hours. Went to see that new play at the theatre. Oh yeah? Which one? “The Haunting of Blackwood Manor”. It was…intense. Super creepy. Lots of flickering lights and dramatic organ music. I swear I felt a cold breeze during the ghost scene. You and ghosts. You have a fascination. You believe everything, don't you? Well, my nan always said our house was haunted. She used to leave out biscuits for the resident ghost. Honestly, she was convinced. And the toilets… they’d flush themselves occasionally. Spooky! Probably just a dodgy ballcock. You're such a sceptic! Anyways, what about you?

“A… B… C… D… E… F… G!” Alright, alright, superstar! That’s enough of the alphabet for now, little man. Dinner’s on the table. He’s been at it for a good twenty minutes. It’s…enthusiastic. Bless him. It’s kinda catchy though, isn’t it? Catchy like a particularly persistent cold. Right, who wants more potatoes? I made enough to feed the whole of Ballincollig, I swear. I’m good, thanks. Though, honestly, I’m starving. Been chasing a toddler all afternoon. It’s a workout, you know. Sounds exhausting. Mum's always saying looking after a little one is a full-time job. It absolutely is. More than a full-time job. Speaking of jobs, I’m absolutely buried at work at the minute. This cloud migration is a nightmare. Honestly, I'm starting to dream in server configurations. Oh, don't even  start  on IT problems. I barely know how to turn the TV on. Though, we tried to watch that film you recommended, the one with…what was it, the spaceships?  Arrival . Good film, wasn't it? Bit slow, maybe, but thought-provoking. It was alright. Bit weird. I prefer action stuff. Fair enough. Padraig, are you enjoying your dinner or are you just planning your next rendition of the ABCs? Mmm! Good! He’s a polite little chap, isn’t he? Unlike some people I know… What’s that supposed to mean? Just teasing! You were listing off all your work woes. A bit of a moan, really. I'm allowed a moan! It’s been a long week. Although… I did manage to sneak out for a pint with Declan last night. That helped. Oh yeah? What did you two get up to? Just chatting, catching up. He’s thinking about taking a course in… data analytics, I think it was. Keeps talking about AI. Everyone's talking about AI. It's a bit terrifying, honestly. I read an article about it taking over jobs. It’s a bit of hype, I think. But it's something to keep an eye on, definitely. Padraig, finish your peas! They're good for you. No peas! Yes, peas! You need your greens. Now, what about tomorrow? Any plans? I was thinking we might go to the park. If the weather holds up. A bit of fresh air would do us all good. Yeah, that sounds good.

Honestly, I walked past his room and there he was, fast asleep… in just his pants. It's a new level of comfort, isn’t it? Oh, no! Little man embracing the freedom, I suppose. Is he warm enough? My legs are cold! See? She’s wise beyond her years. She understands the inherent chill of pant-only slumber. He’ll probably wake up shivering and blame us. Pants are silly! Right, well, we can’t have a freezing little boy. I'll sneak in and see if I can wrestle a blanket onto him without fully waking him. It’s a delicate operation. Speaking of operations… I was looking at those extension plans online again. Oh, here we go. The grand design begins. What’s changed this time? Are we building a ballroom, or are we sticking to the utility room ambition? No ballrooms, sadly. Though imagine! Utility room  and  a proper mudroom. That's the dream. I was thinking, if we knocked down that wall between the kitchen and the dining room… and then re-routed the plumbing… Re-routed the plumbing? Darling, you’re going to need more than a YouTube tutorial for that. And honestly, the kitchen's cosy enough. I like bumping into you when I’m making a cup of tea. It’s… domestic. It’s cramped! And someone always ends up with a hot drink spilled on their foot. Plus, we desperately need more storage. Think of all the board games. And my cookbooks! I want a room for all my unicorns! And Lego! A HUGE Lego room! See? They’re with me. They understand the sacred space Lego requires. A dedicated Lego room is far more vital than re-routing plumbing. Okay, okay. A Lego room is a valid point. But think about the flow! Open plan living! Light! Air! Imagine Christmas dinner… not bumping elbows with everyone. We manage Christmas. It’s… chaotic, but we manage. Honestly, I'm picturing the mess a full extension would create. Weeks of dust, builders tracking mud everywhere... It’s too much. It’s an investment! It’ll increase the value of the house, think of the future! I'm thinking about the present. And the present involves not wanting to live in a building site. Besides, imagine explaining to ANON why he woke up in his pants to find half the house missing. It’d be traumatic.

Honestly, this wallpapering is driving me round the bend. Thought it’d be a straightforward weekend job. It’s anything but. Oh, still at it then? I thought you'd have conquered the living room by now. What’s the problem? Bad paper? The paper’s fine, lovely stuff actually. It’s the walls, they’re…characterful. Every angle’s slightly different, every surface has a bump. It’s like trying to apply wallpaper to a landscape. And the paste, honestly, it’s like wallpapering with porridge. Sounds delightful. Reminds me of attempting to fix the damp patch in the downstairs loo. That was a saga. Speaking of sagas, have you heard anything more about the funding bid for the socio-linguistics project? Nothing concrete. Professor Davies is chasing them up, apparently. Said it was ‘under consideration’, which is academic for ‘lost in a filing cabinet’. I’m starting to think we should have gone with the Welsh Language Board. They’re notoriously slow, but at least they understand the value of the work. This feels like throwing a pebble into the ocean with the Research Council. More coffee? I’m putting a fresh pot on. Please. And thank you. I need something strong. Still, if it comes off, think of the data. Years of potential research. Italy, remember? We could be back there interviewing speakers in Sicily. Oh, Sicily… that was a good trip. The food alone was worth the grant money. Though trying to navigate those tiny roads in a rental car was an experience. Remember nearly ending up in the sea? How could I forget? And the driver who just shrugged when we were obviously lost? Right, well, let's hope this funding comes through. It’s either that or I’m going to be spending all my time smoothing out wonky wallpaper. Speaking of things that are infuriating, have you seen what the water company is charging now? Apparently, they need to upgrade the infrastructure. As if we haven't been paying for that for the last twenty years! Daylight robbery. It's the same story wherever you look. They get away with it because no one holds them accountable. It’s almost as baffling as trying to understand what goes on inside the Hadron Collider. Now there’s a topic that’s a bit beyond both our expertise, I think. Though I did watch a documentary about it once.

Right, okay, operation Lego sort is officially underway. Honestly, it’s like a tiny plastic explosion in here. Can I build a castle, Mummy? A really, really big castle with towers? You can, darling,  after  we’ve sorted it all out. We need to get all the little pieces in the right boxes. See? This box is for all the flat bricks. But I wanna build a spaceship! A super-fast spaceship that goes to Mars! We’ll build a spaceship later, sweetheart. This needs doing first. It’s like when we have to tidy up our toys before we can watch The Simpsons. Oh! Like Bart and Lisa! Exactly like Bart and Lisa. Now, what about these… oh, these are all the little window pieces. Leo, can you put these in the window box, please? This is Michelangelo! He’s the best Ninja Turtle! He is pretty cool. But remember, we're not playing  with  the Lego right now, just sorting it. Are you excited about going to see the new Harry Potter film next week? Yes! I want to wear my Gryffindor scarf! I wanna be like Harry Potter and have a magic wand! You both can! We'll get dressed up and get some popcorn. It’ll be fun. It’s just… having everything all over the floor like this is a nightmare. It reminds me of Granny’s house. Granny’s house is messy. It is a little bit messy, isn’t it? She’s having all that work done, all the renovations, and everything’s in piles. She said she found a box of old photos whilst they were taking up the carpets. Did Granny find chocolate? Probably! Knowing your Granny. Have either of you been sneaking Easter chocolate? I swear the eggs are disappearing faster than I can hide them. Maybe. Maybe? Just a little bit. I had a purple one! Oh, you two. Well, as long as you’re enjoying it. Now, back to the Lego. Leo, are you sure you're putting the right bits in the window box? Those look awfully like roof tiles... They  are  roof tiles! For my spaceship! Okay, okay, maybe we can take a five-minute spaceship break. But only five minutes! Yay! Spaceship time! Five minutes… and then it’s  serious  sorting. And maybe another sneaky Easter egg for me. I deserve it. This is exhausting. Mommy, can Michelangelo come to the cinema with us?

Oh my god, you are back! How was Greece? Honestly, fill me  in . Did you actually manage to relax? You looked stressed even  booking  it. It was…good. Relaxing in patches. Honestly, the first couple of days I was still in ‘work mode’, mentally ticking things off, worrying if I’d left anything crucial undone. But then, the sun, the sea…it kinda seeped in eventually. Did you survive a week without me terrorising you? Surprisingly, yes. Things were…quiet. Leo kept asking where you were. He misses your questionable cooking. Apparently, my pasta bake isn't up to standard. Questionable?! My moussaka is a masterpiece! Leo just has unsophisticated tastebuds. Speaking of food, what have you been eating? Don't tell me it's been beans on toast every night. Okay, maybe a  few  nights. I’m not a chef, you know. I did try that new Thai place on Elm Street, though. It was pretty good, actually. You’d like it. We should go next week. Oh, yes! Definitely. I need a proper meal that isn't airplane food. Speaking of next week, are you still on for Sarah’s birthday drinks on Friday? I totally forgot to check if you were free before I RSVP’d. Yeah, I’m in. I already got her a present. It’s…a bit ridiculous, actually. She’s obsessed with those little succulents, so I got her a  massive  one. It's almost as tall as me. Oh my god, that’s perfect. She’ll love it. What’s been happening with Mark, by the way? Have you heard anything? Ugh, don’t even get me started. Apparently, he's now 'finding himself' by backpacking through Southeast Asia. Classic. Saw a picture on Instagram, looking all ‘spiritual’ and wearing a hemp necklace. The audacity. Honestly, some people. It's always finding themselves after they've thoroughly messed things up with someone else. Exactly! Anyway, work’s been…work. Same old, same old. Endless meetings, trying to herd cats. My boss keeps breathing down my neck about this new project, it’s such a mess. Oh, that sounds stressful. How’s the team though? Still functioning as a semi-coherent unit? Just about. Amelia is driving everyone insane with her constant positivity. It’s exhausting. You know, the kind where it feels…forced. And Ben is still obsessively tracking his steps. Seriously, it's a competition.

Right, now then, have you two eaten enough? Don’t want you going home feeling peckish. I made a proper spread, didn't I? I’m stuffed, Grandma. Honestly. That victoria sponge was… amazing. Aye, it were good that. Though, a bit too much jam for my liking. Always a bit stingy with the cream, aren't you, lass? Stingy! I put a good dollop on each slice! You just like to scrape it all to one side, that’s your trouble. She always did like to hoard the best bits, our Doris. Remember that time with the Christmas chocolates? Oh, don’t you start! I only wanted the caramel creams! You two polished off all the Brazils. Sounds like a Christmas battleground. It was a sight to behold, I can tell you. Anyway, enough reminiscing about stolen sweets. Did you manage to get that History essay finished, love? The one on the Tudors? Nearly. Just got the conclusion to write. It’s… a lot about Henry VIII. A  lot . Oh, him. Always a popular choice, that one. A right rogue, weren't he? Rogue is putting it mildly! Chopped off more wives’ heads than a butcher on a busy market day. Aye, and all for a son! Can you imagine, wanting a boy that badly? It’s a bit… extreme, isn’t it? Mrs. Davies says it shows how obsessed he was with power and continuing the dynasty. She's right. Power’s a dangerous thing, it is. Right, are you two set for the weekend? Anything planned? Just gonna hang out with mates, probably. Maybe go into York. You be careful now, York can be a bit lively at night. I will, Grandma. I’m not stupid. Not yet, anyway. Give it time! He'll learn. Now, now, Harold. Don’t fill his head with nonsense. He’s a sensible lad. Speaking of sensible, I need to get the washing on. It’s piling up something awful. Let me help, love. I'm not just for show. Oh, would you? That’d be lovely. You can sort the whites from the colours. Harold, you can… well, you can just sit there and tell us more stories. As long as they don't involve me hoarding sweets. Alright, alright. I have a tale about a sheep and a vicar, if you’re interested… It happened back in the fifties, you wouldn’t believe…

Right, so we’re all agreed, Peter Pan tonight then? After dinner? Yay! The one with Tinkerbell? The  really  sparkly one? That’s the one, sweetheart. Although, you know, it's a bit different from the story, isn’t it? The original Peter Pan is a bit… darker. Darker? What’s darker about it? Does Captain Hook still try to chop his hand off? He does, yes. And well, the Lost Boys aren't always having the best time, and there's a bit more sadness in the story. It’s not all fairies and flying. Oh. Is it scary? Not  scary  scary. A bit… thoughtful. Remember when we talked about Great Ormond Street Hospital? Yeah, the hospital for poorly kids! You said J.M. Barrie gave them the rights to Peter Pan so they could get money. Exactly! He wanted to help them, and the story  does  have a sad bit about children needing help. It makes it even more special knowing that, doesn’t it? So… the hospital gets money from watching the film? Even the sparkly one? They do! Every time someone watches it, or buys it, a little bit of money goes to them. Isn't that lovely? Cool! So, Captain Hook is still bad, even if it helps the hospital? Very bad. But Peter Pan is there to protect everyone, and Tinkerbell helps him. Remember, Tinkerbell is very small, but she’s fierce! She saves Peter. She sprinkles fairy dust! And makes you fly! I want to fly! Well, Tinkerbell's fairy dust is special. We might not all be able to fly like that, but we can all have adventures in our imaginations. Did J.M. Barrie ever go to Great Ormond Street? Did he visit the kids? That's a really good question. I think he did visit quite often. He really cared about the children there. Actually, let's look it up after the movie, shall we? We can see what we can find. Okay! But can we have popcorn while we watch?  Lots  of popcorn? We can definitely have popcorn. But first, let's finish getting dinner ready. Then, adventure awaits in Neverland! I like Neverland! It sounds fun. It is fun! Although, it's also important to remember that home is pretty great too. And we have each other, which is the most important thing. Yeah! And popcorn! And popcorn. Definitely popcorn. Now, who wants to help me set the table?

Honestly, this M5 is just relentless isn’t it? Seems to be permanently gridlocked these days. Used to be able to do this run in… well, not quickly, but without wanting to age visibly. It’s the school holidays, Dad. Everyone's heading for Cornwall. We’re lucky we’re going  against  the flow a bit, taking her to Exeter. Still feels long though, doesn’t it? It does. Especially knowing you’ve got that early flight. You didn’t get much sleep did you, love? You were tossing and turning all night. Not really. Nerves, I think. And probably too much coffee trying to get everything packed. Honestly, the amount of stuff a teenager needs for a gap year… it’s unbelievable. She'll be fine. She’s a sensible girl. Reminds me of your Aunt Margaret, actually. Always so organised. Though Margaret never travelled anywhere further than Torquay, mind you. Happy with her knitting and the WI. Times have changed, haven’t they? Still, Torquay was quite the destination in her day. Remember when we lived near Babbacombe? That was lovely. Such a different pace of life. Babbacombe… now  that  was a nice spot. Far cry from Southend, though! Though I do miss the sea air sometimes. This Devon countryside is beautiful, mind. But different. Remember Taunton? That was a bit of a stopgap, wasn't it? It was. A bit… anonymous. Nothing really felt settled there. Much prefer it here, even with the M5 traffic. It suited us at the time. Close to both our jobs. And Sarah loved her school there. Still, she’s settled brilliantly here now. Completely transformed since starting at the new sixth form. She has. Proud of her, I am. Right, well, we’re getting closer. So, Christmas… have we confirmed what we’re all doing? You two coming to us, I hope? We are, Dad. Unless something completely catastrophic happens at school. Though, I suspect even a school pandemic wouldn’t stop me from having your Christmas dinner. We’re looking forward to it. And we should start thinking about a house-warming for you both, once you’ve fully settled in. A proper one, not just a quick cup of tea while unpacking boxes. Oh, yes! A proper party. We’ll need to get the garden sorted first. Still a bit of a mess after all that building work. Don't worry about that, Dad.

Oh, bless me, this queue is dreadful, isn’t it? Though, I suppose, it's expected on a day like this. Lovely weather for it, all the same. Though a bit too bright for my eyes, really. You’re telling me. I’ve been stood here ten minutes already, just to get a ticket to…well, never mind where to. It’s the principle of the thing, isn’t it? They should have more staff on. Absolutely. Though, I was saying to my neighbour just last week, it’s all about efficiency these days. No one wants to pay for proper service anymore. It’s all self-service and machines. Gives me a headache trying to work them. They expect everyone to be tech-savvy now, don't they? I struggle with the telly remote half the time. My wife, God rest her soul, she was the one who sorted all that out. Always had a knack for gadgets. Oh, I am sorry to hear about your wife. It’s never easy, losing a partner. I lost my husband some years ago. Though, he wasn’t much for gadgets either, thankfully. More interested in his garden. He used to say a garden kept a man honest. That’s a nice thought. Mine was a teacher, you know. Nursery education. Said it was the most important stage. Shaping little minds, she called it. Used to volunteer at the hospice too, after she retired. Incredible woman. That’s wonderful. It’s good to give back, isn’t it? I used to run an art gallery, years ago, before I retired completely. Did a bit of painting myself, though mostly landscapes. Lovely, peaceful thing to do. Though, it never paid the bills, not really. Art’s a difficult game, I imagine. Everything’s about money these days, isn't it? Speaking of which, I was reading in the paper about this ME event next year, the one they're holding…somewhere around here, I think. Oh, you mean the big one? Yes, they're planning it for the field down by the river. I’ve heard a bit about it. Apparently, they’re trying to get more women involved. Which is good, I suppose. Though sometimes I think all this talk of ‘female equality’ becomes a bit… much. It’s like they have to label everything, make a fuss. Women are perfectly capable without being constantly reminded.

Right, so I was looking at flights again, and it’s still looking…optimistic, to get something remotely reasonable. Optimistic as in expensive, or optimistic as in doesn’t actually exist? Both, honestly. Expensive  and  they involve about three layovers in places I’ve never even heard of. Like, Ulan Bator. Why would I be changing planes in Ulan Bator to get to Lisbon? Because the algorithm thinks it’s a good idea, love. Don’t try to apply logic to airline pricing. It's a dark art. Have you tried looking at EasyJet direct from Bristol? That might cut out some of the…exotic connections. Yeah, I did. They’re alright price-wise, but the times are awful. Like, leaving at six am on a Saturday. Ugh. And then getting back at…eleven pm on the Tuesday. I'd have barely any time there. Tuesday? Oh, that’s a bit grim, isn’t it? Is it worth trying to shift the dates even by a day or two? Sometimes just a slight change can knock a load off. I’ve played around with it a bit. It’s just that Mark already has that work thing on the Friday, so we’re trying to fit it around that. And I really wanted five full days, not four, squeezed in with travel. Hmm. Okay. Well, have you thought about…and this might be a bit radical…trains? Trains? Mum, that’s…that’s a long way to go by train! I know, I know. But just think about it. No airport faff, you can actually  see  the country, you can take your time… it’s a different kind of holiday. And you could break it up, stop off in Paris for a night, maybe even Bordeaux. Bordeaux does sound nice…but honestly, the thought of being on a train for two days solid… I’d get so restless. I need a bit of space, you know? Plus, it’d probably work out more expensive, wouldn’t it? Possibly. But I’ve been reading about these Interrail passes. They do deals sometimes. It's worth a look. It might be a bit of an adventure. Maybe. I'll look into it. It just feels like such a fuss getting there. I was picturing just flopping on a beach, not meticulously planning train schedules. Well, you won't flop on a beach if you don't  get  to the beach, will you?

Right, so I checked the bank again, and they’ve actually taken  both  Spotify subscriptions this month. Both mine and Mum’s. Seriously? That’s… inefficient, to say the least. Did you call them about it last time, when it happened with yours? Yeah, and they said it was a glitch, refunded it, and told me it’d be sorted. Apparently not. I’m on hold now, it’s been twenty minutes. The hold music is genuinely criminal. It's like a midi file of a pan flute. Oh, that  is  rough. Banks and their terrible hold music. Honestly, it’s a form of torture. You'll be there all day. Speaking of all day, did you see the cricket yesterday? England absolutely crumbled. Oh man, don’t even. It was painful. Root looked alright for a bit, but then just…gone. They needed him. I was watching it with Ben, he was proper fuming. He’s convinced it’s all down to the pitches being too bowler-friendly. It's a bit of both, I think. The bowlers  were  on fire, but the batting just wasn't up to scratch. No application, you know? Seems like nobody wants to just stick around and build an innings these days. Exactly! It's all slog, slog, slog, and then out. No patience. Remember when Cooky used to just…wear the bowlers down? Solid as a rock. Ah, Alastair Cook. A proper craftsman. Different times. Speaking of different times, how was your Auntie Carol’s birthday weekend? Did everyone make it down to Devon? Yeah, everyone except Uncle Dave. He said his back was playing up again. Mum was proper disappointed. She’d made his favourite lemon drizzle cake. Oh, that’s a shame. He always does appreciate her baking, though, doesn’t he? I remember him smuggling bits of it out to the garden last time. He’s a terrible sneak! But yeah, she was a bit miffed. It was a good weekend overall though. Lots of catching up, a few embarrassing stories about Mum’s youth… the usual. Sounds perfect. Family chaos is the best kind, isn't it? Still on hold, I presume? Honestly, just email them. It'll be quicker. I'm tempted. But I'm stubborn. And I want to  speak  to someone and make them acknowledge their terrible system. Plus, I'm avoiding starting that essay on post-structuralism.

Honestly, this Skype thing is a marvel, isn't it? Seeing your faces like this, feels almost like you’re both here. Though, a proper cuppa and biscuit with you two is always better. Aye, it's alright for a quick catch up. Though I still can't get on with these newfangled contraptions. Always fiddling about with the volume. You can hear everything but what you  want  to hear, eh? Dad, you say that every time. It's probably just your hearing, honestly. Are you managing alright with your leg today? Oh, it's a rum do, this leg. A rum do. On a bad day, it feels like someone's taken a hammer to it. Though, I managed a little potter in the garden earlier. Just deadheading the roses, mind. Can’t be doing any heavy lifting. Good for you, dear. Roses are looking lovely, according to the photos you sent. You always did have a way with the garden. Remember that time you tried to grow pumpkins for Halloween? They were enormous! Ha! Enormous is right. Nearly took out Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning dahlias! She wasn’t best pleased, I can tell you. She gave me a right telling off. Speaking of holidays, I was looking at those globes you sent, David. Lovely things. Reminded me of our trip to Yorkshire, years ago. Yorkshire? That was ages ago! I was still at school, wasn’t I? Mum and Dad took me and…was it Auntie Brenda who came too? It was. A terrible trip! Rain the whole time. We tried to make the best of it, visited those little villages. And you, David, insisted on staying in a youth hostel. It was cheap! And a good experience. Though admittedly, the shared showers weren’t ideal. I had a school project due, remember? Geography, all about the Peak District. That trip really helped. Aye, a proper soaking it was. Remember climbing that hill? Could barely see a thing through the mist. And then you got us lost following a sheep track! Oh, don't start that again, Arthur. It wasn’t a sheep track, it was a public footpath! And we weren't  lost , just…temporarily misplaced. We found our way back eventually. Speaking of being lost – have you been watching that new drama on the television? About the underground system during the war? Oh, yeah! It's brilliant, isn’t it?

Right, so I’ve been looking at flights again, and honestly, it’s just…criminal. Everything’s gone up, hasn't it? Tell me about it. I was checking prices for my mum to come up for Christmas, and it's ridiculous. Even EasyJet are trying it on now. They used to be the budget champions. Exactly! I’m trying to get to Barcelona in November, and it’s almost cheaper to get a train to London and then fly from there. Which defeats the whole object, doesn’t it? That’s mental. Is it… are you going with anyone? Just Chloe, we’re trying to have a little girls’ trip. Sun, sangria, all that jazz. But at this rate, we’ll be staying in and eating pot noodles. Oh, no! Barcelona’s brilliant. You absolutely have to go. Have you tried, like, looking at different airports? Sometimes flying into Girona or Reus can be cheaper. Yeah, I’ve had a look. Adds another couple of hours on the journey though, which kind of negates the saving, doesn’t it? I spent ages yesterday comparing different sites – Skyscanner, Kayak, directly with the airlines… I’m starting to dream in flight numbers. Oh, I know the feeling. When I was booking flights for Italy last year, I was convinced I’d found a glitch. Spent an hour triple-checking, then it turned out I'd just misread the airport code. Oh, classic! I did that with a hotel once. Booked a ‘luxury suite’ thinking it was in the city centre. Turns out it was 20 miles out in the middle of nowhere. Lesson learned: always check the location properly. Definitely. So, what are you having for your tea? I'm starving. This day has just flown by. Three meetings back-to-back, then a crisis with the new supplier… honestly, it’s been a mess. I made a chilli. It's not fancy, but it's easy. And warming. Do you want some? It’ll take your mind off crisis suppliers. Oh, yes, please! That sounds perfect. You're a lifesaver. I think I need a bowl of something spicy and a long sit-down. Plus, you promised we could watch that new true crime documentary. Deal. Chilli, documentary, and hopefully, a flight to Barcelona that doesn't require remortgaging the house. Fingers crossed! Oh, and I brought biscuits. Chocolate digestives. Because every crisis deserves a biscuit.

Honestly, the price of a loaf of bread now… it’s scandalous. Used to be you could get a decent sliced white for… well, less than a pound, certainly. Now? Nearly two fifty. It is awful, isn't it? Everything is going up. I was looking at the cost of cat food the other day… ridiculous. Jasper's getting picky, too. Only wants the salmon flavour, the expensive stuff! Don’t even  start  me on pet food. Honestly, they’ve got you by the short and curlies. You love ‘em, you pay through the nose. It's the same with everything. I was at the supermarket yesterday, and a tin of tomatoes… used to be sixty pence, now it’s nearly a pound twenty. It's daylight robbery, that's what it is. And the banks… don't even get me started on the banks. Charging for everything now. I tried to withdraw some cash yesterday, and they wanted a fee! A  fee ! For using  my  money. I switched mobile phone providers last month, hoping to save a bit. Worst decision ever. The signal is terrible, and the customer service is… nonexistent. I spent an hour on hold yesterday trying to sort out a billing issue. An hour! Oh, customer service. Don’t even ask. I had a problem with a dodgy neighbour last week, had to call the police. Took them nearly three hours to turn up. Three hours! And then the officer just said there wasn't much they could do without further evidence. Honestly, the justice system is falling apart. It's the same everywhere, isn't it? No one seems to care about doing a proper job anymore. Everyone’s just trying to get by. Speaking of getting by, have you seen what’s happened to interest rates? Absolutely crippling. I’ve got a bit of savings, you know, for a rainy day… but earning next to nothing on it. It’s so frustrating. You try to be responsible, save for the future, and then the banks just… swallow all the benefits. I’ve been thinking about investing, but it all seems so risky. Risky is right. Remember Uncle George and that ‘guaranteed’ investment scheme? Lost the lot, he did! Still talking about it, years later. Aye, George was always a bit too trusting. Honestly, it's a minefield. What about you, have you managed to put anything aside, dear?

Right, so we’re doing favourites, yeah? Favourites of everything. I’ll start with holidays. Mine’s gotta be… South Africa. Obvious, innit? Seeing as I practically grew up there. But honestly, the beaches are just… another level. Ooh, good shout! South Africa does sound amazing. Mine’s probably Italy, actually. Florence, specifically. All the art and the pasta… I could live there. Italy’s gorgeous! Though I'm a bit biased towards Ireland, obviously. The Cliffs of Moher are just breathtaking. And the pubs, like, you can’t beat a proper Irish pub. Oh, definitely! I went to Ireland a few years ago, lovely. For me, though, it’s gotta be Greece. The islands are incredible. So much history and the food is just…  chef’s kiss . I’m a bit boring, I think. Mine’s Spain. Benidorm. Don’t judge me! It’s just proper chill, sunshine, sangria… exactly what I need after a stressful semester. Benidorm’s a classic! No judgement here. Right, what about animals? Favourite animal then? Oh, that’s easy. Dogs. 100%. Especially Golden Retrievers. So fluffy and sweet. I’m a cat person, through and through. Always have been. They’re so independent and sassy. Plus, mine absolutely loves a cuddle when  she  decides it's cuddle time, which is the power move. I have a soft spot for elephants. They’re just… majestic. And so intelligent. I watched a documentary about them once and I was sobbing. I love meerkats! They’re just so funny, always standing on their little hind legs, looking around. They proper brighten my day. Meerkats are brilliant! Okay, last one. Food. Favourite food, go! Oh god, that’s the hardest one. Okay… Pizza. Definitely pizza. Any kind, honestly. But especially a good Margherita. Simple perfection. I’m going to go with a full Irish breakfast. Sausage, bacon, black and white pudding, fried egg, the works. It’s a proper cure for everything. Welsh Rarebit! It's a classic, it's cheesy, it's perfect with a side of chutney. You can't beat it. Actually, anything with cheese, really. I'm gonna say… a proper Sunday dinner. Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, gravy… the whole shebang. My nan makes the best. Ooh, a good Sunday dinner is hard to beat. Mine's… Bobotie. It’s a South African dish, minced meat baked with an egg-based topping.

Honestly, I’m starting to freak out a bit about what comes  after  uni. Like, properly freak out. Oh god, same. Feels like everyone else has a ten-year plan mapped out, and I’m just…here. Still figuring out what I want for breakfast. Exactly! And it's not even like, a career thing necessarily. It’s just… what do people  do  when they're old? Like, properly old. Gran used to spend all day knitting, and I’m terrified that’s going to be me. Knitting isn’t  that  bad. It's therapeutic, apparently. My nan does it, but she also does crosswords and judges local flower shows. She's a busy woman. Flower shows… okay, marginally better. But what if I don’t  have  hobbies? What if my only skill is being able to beat level six on Stardew Valley? Hey, that’s a respectable skill! Seriously, commitment like that takes dedication. And you're brilliant at art, remember? You should focus on that. Easier said than done. This essay on the Pre-Raphaelites is killing me. “Discuss the influence of Medievalism on Rossetti’s artistic vision.” It’s just…words. Meaningless, pretentious words. Oh, I feel you. Mine's on Post-Structuralism. I’ve read the same paragraph five times and I  still  don't understand it. It's like they're deliberately trying to sound complicated. Exactly! It's all just intellectual showing-off. I wish I could just paint all day instead of writing about it. Imagine, just losing myself in colour and texture, not worrying about semiotics or whatever. You totally should. Maybe during the break? Actually, proper break. No uni work allowed. Just paint, play Stardew, maybe even attempt a flower arrangement. You know, prepare for old age. You’re awful. But yeah, maybe. I keep thinking about entering some of my stuff into that student exhibition, but I'm too scared it’ll be rubbish. No way! Your work is amazing. Remember that portrait you did of old Mr. Henderson from down the hall? It was incredible. You need to believe in yourself more. Thanks, you’re sweet. You always know what to say. Have you made any progress with your dissertation topic then? Still thinking about video game addiction? Yeah, I think so. I found a really interesting study about dopamine levels and reward mechanisms in MMOs. It's a bit dense, but I think I can make something of it.

Honestly, I’m convinced I live on pesto pasta at this point. It’s just…easy. And I’m rubbish at actually planning meals. You really need to branch out, Liv. It's not healthy. Pesto isn’t a vegetable, you know. Though, I admit, sometimes after a shift, all I want is something beige and minimal effort. Last night was just toast, don't judge. No judgment here! I had a biscuit for dinner on Tuesday. A  single  biscuit. Don’t tell anyone. Oh my god. That’s…depressing. Seriously, though, we should do a proper shop tomorrow? And maybe try that new recipe I saw, the one with the halloumi and the roasted veg? Halloumi sounds good. Expensive, but good. Did you see Sarah’s pictures from her holiday? Greece looked amazing. Ugh, don’t even. Instagram is just a parade of people living their best lives while I’m saving patients from themselves. It's beautiful, though. She deserves a break. Is she still seeing…what’s his name? Ben? Yeah, apparently. They seem okay. Though, she did mention he’s been really into…competitive birdwatching. Competitive  birdwatching ? Is that even a thing?! Apparently! He's got all the gear – binoculars, a special backpack, a notebook for identifying species. She sounded…slightly bewildered by it all. Oh, bless her. I mean, as long as she’s happy. It’s just…a bit niche, isn't it? Reminds me of that guy I dated in uni who was obsessed with collecting miniature spoons. Oh god, Mark. The spoon guy. I’d almost forgotten about him. That was a phase. A prolonged phase. He genuinely expected me to contribute to the collection. I think I escaped with only donating one. Anyway…how are things with Tom? Still radio silence after the ‘misunderstanding’ at your work party? It’s…complicated. He messaged yesterday, just a sort of ‘hope you’re well’ thing. Very non-committal. I replied, equally non-committal. I think both of us are waiting for the other to make the first proper move. Honestly, it's exhausting. That’s awful. You deserve someone who isn't going to make you feel like you’re walking on eggshells. Maybe you should just…not bother? There are plenty of non-competitive birdwatching, non-spoon collecting guys out there. Easier said than done! I am pathologically incapable of letting go of potential. Are you free on Saturday?

Right, so have you both had a chance to look over the speaker consent form? Just want to make sure we’re all clear on what we’re signing up to, especially regarding recording and image rights. Yes, I did. Seems fairly standard, doesn’t it? Though the bit about archiving the presentation indefinitely feels a bit…permanent. I agree. It’s fine for the Uni to store it, but ‘indefinitely’ is a long time. Is that standard practice, do you know, Elspeth? You’ve done more of these than either of us. It is, unfortunately. Apparently, it’s to do with institutional memory and potential reuse for training materials. Not ideal, but we knew the university were pushing for greater recording of events like this. We can push back slightly perhaps, and say we retain copyright over the material? Worth a try. I’m happy to sign, provided we add that clause. Okay, onto the seminar itself. I’ve been sketching out a possible structure. I was thinking we start with a sort of ‘challenges’ overview – the common pitfalls in international business comms, like assumptions about directness, non-verbal cues… Good. And then maybe a couple of case studies? Something that really highlights the misunderstandings that can occur. I’ve got one from my time working with a Japanese firm, where a perfectly polite request was perceived as incredibly rude because of the phrasing. Oh, do share! That’s exactly the kind of thing we need. I was thinking of using a scenario based on a failed negotiation in the Middle East, where assumptions about building rapport completely derailed the process. Excellent. I’ve got a slightly different angle. I was thinking of focusing on the impact of digital communication, and how easily tone can be misconstrued in emails or video calls. Especially with differing expectations around response times. That’s a vital point, actually. We should definitely include that. So, roughly then, intro - challenges, then two or three mini-case studies, one each? And then we finish with practical tips and resources. Maybe a quick Q&A? Sounds good. How long are we allotted, exactly? I keep forgetting. An hour and a half. Which, honestly, doesn't feel like nearly enough to cover the breadth of international business comms. No, it doesn’t. We’ll have to be tightly focused. We need to decide on key takeaways. I think we should all agree to limit ourselves to about twenty minutes each on the case study sections, leaving time for a proper discussion at the end.

Honestly, that seminar was… a lot. Old Man Chen just kept going on about Foucault again. Like we haven’t all read  Discipline and Punish  three times already. Ugh, tell me about it. I swear, he thinks we’re all aspiring Foucauldians. My students were practically glazing over. I had to sneak in a question about Deleuze just to wake someone up. Good tactic. At least Deleuze offers something… different. It's just, sometimes I feel like I'm teaching the same three theorists on repeat. It's exhausting. And the marking! I’m drowning in essays about postcolonialism. You’re lucky. I have a mountain of quantitative data analysis to wade through. Honestly, I sometimes miss just… reading books. Actual, proper books. Not academic articles riddled with jargon. Me too. Remember when we used to just… read for fun? Before it all became "research material?" Vaguely. Feels like another lifetime. Speaking of lifetimes… have you had any luck with sorting out the plumbing yet? The dripping tap is driving me insane. Don’t even  start  me on the plumbing. I called Old Man Wang again. He promised he’d come on Tuesday. Then he didn’t show. Then he said Thursday. Now he’s saying next week. I’m starting to suspect he's deliberately avoiding us. Because he knows we’ll ask him to fix that leak in the bathroom too? The one that’s been there since… well, since we moved in? Precisely. I think he's realized we’re a money pit. Honestly, I’m tempted to just learn to do it myself. YouTube tutorials, here I come. You and plumbing? That’s a terrifying thought. I’d rather live with the dripping. At least it’s a consistent sound. It's not consistent, it's erratic! It's like a Chinese water torture device, slowly driving me to madness. And then there’s the kitchen light… still flickering. Oh god, the kitchen light. I’ve started wearing sunglasses in there. It’s like living inside a strobe. I’m genuinely considering just investing in a whole new lighting system. Just rip everything out and start again. That’s… ambitious. And probably expensive. We should probably just call his son. He seems a bit more reliable. Though, equally, he also charges about twice as much. A necessary evil, perhaps. It's either exorbitant plumbing or a slow descent into madness.

Honestly, this lasagne is… fine. It’s just a bit… beige. And I think you might have used a bit too much béchamel. Beige? It’s a classic lasagne! And I didn't  think  I used too much béchamel. It needed moisture, didn’t it? Otherwise it would've been cardboard. It just lacks… vibrancy. Remember Grandma’s lasagne? That was a masterpiece. Layers of bright red sauce, properly browned cheese… It was a work of art. Grandma had secrets. She’d never tell anyone what she did. Probably a dash of magic, honestly. Speaking of Grandma’s house… are we ever going to actually  do  anything with all that furniture we inherited? It’s just sitting there gathering dust. I know, it’s awful. I feel guilty every time I think about it. But where would we even  put  it? My flat is tiny. And you’ve barely got room as it is, what with all your… robot parts. Hey! Those aren't just 'robot parts'! They're components for potentially revolutionizing… well, something. It’s important work! But yeah, the furniture is a problem. Maybe we should just have a massive clear-out. Donate it all? Probably the sensible thing. Though I do quite like that old dresser. It'd look nice with a coat of paint. We could maybe… decorate it in a funky way? It's just that the whole house reminds me of… well, everything. All the family history. I get it. It's overwhelming. It's like, suddenly you have all these tangible things that represent generations. So, food-related tangent, did you see that documentary about food wastage? It's genuinely horrifying how much perfectly good produce gets thrown away. Oh yeah, the one about supermarkets? Absolutely shocking. It makes you think twice about scraping the plates clean, doesn’t it? Though, honestly, sometimes I just can’t face leftovers. That's fair. I'm trying to get into urban farming, though. Saw a really cool initiative in Brixton. Growing loads of stuff on rooftops. It’s a great way to reduce food miles and waste, you know? That’s brilliant! Very impressive. You're always so keen on the forward-thinking stuff. It's completely different to what they were pushing when  I  was at school, careers-wise. It was all law or medicine, or become a teacher like me. No one mentioned robotics, or… sustainable urban farming.

Right, so I think I’ve got everything chopped for this curry. Just need to start frying it off. How was your day? Absolute chaos, I assume? You have no idea. Honestly, the emails were just…relentless. It was one long fire-fighting exercise. Apparently, several schools hadn’t submitted their data properly, so I spent the morning chasing people up. It’s just… exhausting. Like, I  like  my job, but sometimes it feels like herding cats. Ugh, data. The bane of modern existence. Sounds pretty stressful. I had a surprisingly productive morning actually. Managed to get some solid coding done on the new analysis, which is a win. Though I’m starting to realize this project is way bigger than I initially thought. Realistically, it’s going to take months, not weeks. See, that's the thing with research, isn’t it? It always ends up being more complicated than you anticipate. At least you’re  doing  something concrete, though. I sometimes feel like I’m just… shuffling papers around and sending polite but firm emails. It doesn’t feel concrete when it’s just lines of code staring back at you, trust me. And honestly, sometimes I question the whole point of it. Is this analysis actually going to make a difference to people’s lives, or is it just going to sit in a journal somewhere? Existential crisis, basically. Oh, I know those. I have them weekly. It’s the impact thing, isn't it? Trying to see the bigger picture when you're bogged down in the minutiae. Speaking of bigger pictures, how are your parents doing? I haven’t spoken to them in a while. They’re good, yeah. Mum’s been getting really into gardening, which is… a departure. She's always hated getting her hands dirty. Apparently, it's 'therapeutic'. Dad’s still doing his crosswords and complaining about the government, so business as usual. He keeps asking when we’re going to visit and I feel bad. It's just difficult fitting everything in. I know the feeling. My sister keeps hinting that we should come down to Cornwall, but honestly, the drive is just… daunting. And then you feel guilty for not going. It's a vicious cycle. She sent me pictures of her new puppy though. It’s ridiculously cute. Oh, a puppy! What breed? A little Cockapoo. All fluffy and ridiculous.

It’s funny, isn’t it? How the sea changes. Used to be, you’d go down to Cromer, and it was packed. Families, all sorts. Now, it’s mostly folks with… well, with dogs. And those little campervans. Seems everyone’s living in those now. It’s a different world, George. Everything’s different. Remember when houses weren’t… well,  this  much? Honestly, you could buy a decent little semi in Norwich for a few thousand back then. Now young people can’t even  dream  of getting on the ladder. It’s dreadful. It’s the speculation, isn't it? That’s what’s done it. People buying up properties, not to live in, but to… well, just to make money. Drives the prices through the roof. Makes you wonder where it'll all end. Ends in tears, that’s where it ends. Always does. My Jimmy, he’s struggling something awful. Tried to help him out, lent him a bit, but it’s like pouring water into a sieve. Goes straight through. He says he feels… well, he doesn’t really  say  it, but I can see it in his eyes. He’s a bit down. Oh, poor Jimmy. He’s always been a sensitive soul. Is it the money, you think? Or… something else? It’s easy to get swallowed up, you know. By that darkness. I went through a patch myself, years ago. After Harold… well, everything. It's often a combination, isn't it? Money worries are a huge stressor, that’s for sure. But often there’s something deeper. Relationships, feeling purposeless… It's hard to pinpoint. Have you encouraged Jimmy to talk to someone? A professional, perhaps? Tried, love. He just… clams up. Says he doesn’t want to bother anyone. That’s the trouble with these men, isn’t it? Bottle it all up inside. It’ll eat them alive, it will. They're hopeless, honestly. It's the old-fashioned thinking, I suppose. 'Mustn't show weakness.' It’s a load of rubbish. It takes more courage to ask for help than to suffer in silence. Absolutely. Perhaps you could suggest some volunteering? It can be a good way to get a sense of purpose, to feel needed. There are all sorts of opportunities. Little things can make a big difference. I'm helping out at the school library one afternoon a week now.

Honestly, this new lip liner is a game changer. You  have  to try it. It’s the Charlotte Tilbury Pillow Talk Intense. Ooh, Charlotte Tilbury, fancy! Is it really that good? I've always been a bit wary, it’s so pricey isn’t it? It is, yeah. A bit of a splurge. But honestly, it stays on  forever . And the colour is just… perfect. Like, universally flattering. I wore it on Saturday night and barely had to reapply. Usually, I’m constantly checking. That’s a win. I’m always reapplying. I’ve been trying that Collection lip liner, the one everyone's raving about on TikTok, but it just… fades. Like, within an hour, it's gone. TikTok liners, eh? They look good in the videos, but realistically… I feel like they fall short. Though, I did see one that looked promising. A matte nude one. What about nails? Have you had yours done recently? I did, last week. Went for a dark burgundy. Wintery, you know? Although, I’m already thinking of changing them. I’m gutted, I chipped one already. Just a little one, on my thumb. It’s so annoying. Oh, no! The worst. I’ve been trying to grow mine out, actually. Being a teacher, the hand washing and the constant use of whiteboard pens is  murder  on nails. I’ve been using that strengthening varnish, the OPI one, but it’s slow going. OPI's good. I used to use that ages ago. I got properly into gel polish for a while, but the removal is such a faff, isn’t it? And it’s damaging. So damaging! I tried it once and my nails were paper thin afterwards. I’ve sworn off it. I’d rather a regular polish and just be extra careful. How’s Sarah? I haven't seen her in ages. She's good. She's been doing loads of shopping, actually. Found this amazing boutique in Hanley. Apparently, they do really unique dresses. She sent me a picture of this emerald green one… stunning. Ooh, I love emerald green. You have to go with her sometime! We need a shopping trip. I’ve been meaning to get a new winter coat, but I'm completely overwhelmed by all the choices. Me too! It’s ridiculous. Everything looks the same. I ended up just getting another black one. Predictable, I know.

Honestly, the parking around here is a joke, isn’t it? I circled three times before I found a space, and I’m still convinced I’ll get a ticket. Tell me about it. I had a meeting over near the Walker Art Gallery yesterday, and it was mental. Ended up parking near the docks, and even  that  was busy. Worth it for a coffee with you though, eh? How's the teaching going anyway? Still battling teenagers with questionable grammar? You know it. One lad actually tried to tell me “literally” doesn’t mean what I thought it did. Literally. I nearly lost it. It’s good though, keeps me on my toes. I'm thinking of doing a Masters in Applied Linguistics actually. No way! That's brilliant, lad. What uni are you lookin' at? I’ve got an interview next week at John Moores. Fingers crossed. It’s a part-time one, so I can still work, which is a massive plus, seeing as I'm currently operating on a student budget… again. Good shout. John Moores is sound. Bit of a trek if you’re coming from Birkenhead though, isn’t it? How much are they asking for the course? Is it going to bankrupt you? Nearly. It’s…substantial. I’ve been squirreling away, but I’ll probably need another part-time job. Maybe I can tutor or something. What about you? Still rescuing kids from chaos? Something like that. It's been a tough week, honestly. Got a case involving a family who are being moved to temporary accommodation again. It’s just… frustrating, you know? The system’s broken, and you’re just putting plasters on massive wounds. Yeah, I can imagine. Must be draining. You need a holiday, mate. Have you started thinking about Christmas yet? It’s creeping up on us. Don’t even mention it. My mum's already started asking what I want and she’s hinting about wanting to host again. Absolute chaos every year. Your nan’s still going strong though, right? Making a roast for seventeen people? Still going strong! She’s already planning the seating arrangement. She's threatening to get a new dog this year as well, says she's lonely. Oh no. Not another one. Remember Winston? That thing was a menace. How could I forget? He ate half of Uncle Geoff’s Christmas cake.

Honestly, it’s just… exhausting. The constant negotiation. It’s not even  with  Leo, half the time, it’s with Mark about how to parent Leo. Oh, I know that feeling. It's like you're parenting two children, isn't it? One actual child, and one very large, opinionated one. Exactly! And he means well, I  know  he does. He just… has a very specific idea of how things should be. And it’s always presented as being for Leo’s benefit. Like, “Leo  needs  to be pushed more academically,” or “Leo  needs  more structure.” Right. The classic “it’s for their own good” line. It’s infuriating. How does Leo react to it all? He mostly just shuts down. Which, frankly, I don’t blame him for. It’s like walking on eggshells, constantly. I’m trying to encourage him to be independent, to make mistakes and learn from them, and Mark is just… hovering. Offering solutions before there’s even a problem. It’s hard, isn’t it? Blending families. Everyone has different ways of doing things. And a pre-existing history, of course. That’s the thing. He’s so used to being the sole authority figure. He’s never had to compromise before. I’m used to, you know, collaborative teaching, bouncing ideas off colleagues, letting students take ownership. He sees that as… weakness, I think. Ugh, the patriarchy strikes again. Seriously, it’s 2024, Mark! It’s not about weakness, it’s about fostering a healthy dynamic. You get it. It’s not about undermining him, it’s about building Leo up. Giving him the space to figure things out for himself. I want him to be resilient, not reliant on someone constantly telling him what to do. And you’re right to feel that way. It’s your role as a step-parent too, isn’t it? To be that supportive figure, to offer a different perspective. It’s a difficult balance. It is. And honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m fighting for Leo’s emotional space. It's tiring. And then I feel guilty for feeling resentful towards Mark, because he  is  trying. Guilt is the default setting for mothers, isn’t it? Don’t beat yourself up about it. You’re allowed to be frustrated. It’s completely valid. And remember, you’re trying to navigate something incredibly complex. It takes time.

Honestly, I’ve been scrolling through Pinterest for, like, three hours. It’s a black hole, isn’t it? A proper time suck. Three hours? That's dedication. What were you even looking at? Wedding dresses for your cat? Don’t be daft! Though… that  is  a thing, apparently. No, I was trying to get ideas for Sarah’s birthday. She’s turning the big 3-0, you know? It feels weird. We were just kids messing about at uni. Tell me about it. It felt like yesterday we were all crammed into that tiny student flat, eating instant noodles. Thirty is… significant. What are you thinking of doing for her? I was looking at these DIY gift ideas. Like, making personalised candles or painting mugs. Ridiculous, I know. I’m not exactly artistic. But Pinterest makes it look so  easy . You and half the internet. Pinterest is just a curated fantasy world. You’ll end up with wonky candles and a mug that looks like a toddler decorated it. Probably. Honestly, I'm tempted to just get her a voucher. Less stressful. Speaking of stressful, did you see  The Traitors  last night? Oh, brilliant, isn’t it? Claudia Winkleman is just…  chef's kiss . I'm completely addicted. I’ve been trying to figure out who the traitors are all week. Me too! I was convinced it was Miles. He just had that sneaky look about him. And then he flipped on everyone! I know, right? Total betrayal. Honestly, I’m starting to suspect everyone. It’s brilliant TV. Perfect winter viewing. Although, it’s completely ruined trust for me. I’m looking at everyone sideways now. Same! I nearly accused old Mrs. Higgins at the bakery of being a traitor this morning. She just gave me a very strange look. Oh, no! You didn't! Poor Mrs. Higgins. You're going to have to apologise. I did. I mumbled something about watching too much television. She didn’t seem convinced. Hey, are we still on for drinks with Liam and Chloe next week? It's Liam's birthday soon, isn't it? Yeah, definitely. I think it's the 15th. I've already messaged him. He said he wants to go for that new Thai place on Mill Road. Ooh, good shout! I’ve heard it’s amazing. I’m starving just thinking about it. Fancy another pint? I’m starting to feel a bit… Pinterest-induced anxiety.

Oh, look at this one. It’s a bit… much, isn’t it? All sparkly glass. Reminds me of a ballroom. Hmm? Oh, yeah. A bit gaudy. You know we're aiming for 'tasteful country kitchen', not 'Versailles'. Exactly! Though, it’s only forty quid. Tempting if it’s truly awful and we can get some fun out of it. Forty quid is still forty quid. We’re supposed to be saving for… well, you know. The deposit. Yes. Rightmove is stressing me out. Everything in our price range is either a complete fixer-upper, or the size of a postage stamp. Have you seen that one in Market Harborough? The one with the garden? Oh, the one that looks like it’s leaning precariously towards the road? It’s got character! And it's got potential. Plus, it’s within a reasonable commute for me, even. Reasonable for  you . I'd be facing a two-hour slog every day. And ‘character’ is code for ‘structurally unsound’, isn’t it? Don't be so pessimistic. They said in the listing it just needs ‘minor cosmetic improvements’. Minor cosmetic improvements usually involves replacing the entire foundations. Look, this one… oh, this is grim. Brown carpets, avocado bathroom suite. What were people  thinking ? It's retro! You could do something with it. Think of the before and after photos. Prime Instagram content. Instagram isn't paying the deposit, darling. Seriously, it’s depressing. Every house has something wrong with it. Either the location is awful, or it's falling apart, or they’ve decorated it in a way that suggests zero taste. We just need to be patient. Something will come up. Remember that cottage near Uppingham we viewed last year? It was lovely. And completely out of our budget. Plus, the estate agent said it had a damp problem. Well, you can’t have everything. Right, back to light fittings. Anything catching your eye? Something a little less… ballroom? Oh, this brushed chrome one is nice. Simple. Clean lines. How much is it? … Ooh, seventy-five. Bit pricey. We can look at a few more. Maybe we’ll get lucky. Or, we could just stick with the one we already have. It’s not  that  bad. It just… needs a wipe. It’s covered in dust and looks like something your grandmother had in the 1970s. A wipe won’t solve that.

Honestly, the state of the garden is just… appalling. I really need a weekend to just attack it. Tell me about it. Mine’s looking a bit wild too. Though, to be fair, Millie seems to enjoy exploring the jungle. Found her attempting to ‘bury’ her bone in a pot of petunias yesterday. Oh, Millie! She's a menace, that dog. My nan keeps telling me I need to get a dog, says it'd be good for me. But I just don’t have the time, not with the shifts I’m doing. It  is  a big commitment. And you’re right, the shifts are exhausting. How was your weekend, Chloe? Anything exciting happen? Not really, just worked, did a bit of cleaning. Went to see Mum on Sunday, which was nice. She’s still going on about me needing a “proper” job. Oh, bless her. They always want the best for you, don’t they? What did you say? The usual. I told her I like my job, I like helping people. She just says it’s not ‘secure’ enough. Wants me to go back to college. That’s the generation for you. Security, security, security. It was the same with my dad. He couldn’t understand why I didn't just stay at the hospital forever. It's hard though, isn’t it? Especially seeing you doing amazing work, Chloe, and having to deal with all the…well, everything, for not a lot of money. It's alright, honestly. It’s rewarding, even when it’s tough. Though, Mrs. Higgins was a handful yesterday. Kept trying to feed her biscuits to the radiator. Oh, dear! You have all the stories, don’t you? How’s Sarah doing at the home, Susan? Still struggling with that manager? Oh, it’s worse, actually. She’s taken a personal grudge against Sarah now. Apparently, Sarah accidentally spilled coffee on her new shoes. Honestly, the woman’s a tyrant. She’s making Sarah’s life absolutely miserable. That’s awful. Has Sarah reported it to anyone? She’s trying to. But the agency’s useless, and the home itself just backs the manager up. She’s looking for another job, but everything around here is the same. Low pay, demanding work… it’s relentless. It is. I’ve been looking too, just to see what’s out there. Mostly the same sort of roles, just different locations.

Honestly, the amount of stuff I’ve been reading about sleep lately is…intense. Apparently, it’s not just about  how long  you sleep, it’s about the cycles. And temperature. And light. Oh, don’t start. I feel like I’m constantly being told I’m doing sleep wrong. I just need eight hours, a comfy pillow, and for the cat to not decide my head is the perfect napping spot. But apparently, a degree cooler room is better. And blue light before bed… catastrophic. I’ve downloaded one of those apps that filters it on my phone. It makes everything look orange though. Orange everything? Sounds… cheerful. Look, I appreciate the science, but I’m a teacher. By the time I’ve marked essays and prepped lessons, I’ll sleep anywhere. Honestly, a solid six hours feels like a luxury these days. Fair enough. Speaking of luxuries, are we still on for camping next weekend? Forecast looks…mixed. Mixed is an understatement. ‘Potential for torrential downpour’ is what I saw. But, yes. We need to get out. Remember that time we got completely lost in Rome? Oh god, don’t remind me. We walked for hours, ending up in some backstreet neighborhood. I was convinced we’d stumbled onto a mafia meeting. It was a laundry. A very small, slightly ominous laundry. And you insisted on using that antiquated paper map instead of Google Maps. Hey! It’s about the principle. It's about the adventure! And Google Maps sent us down a one-way street. Besides, getting lost is how you find the  real  Rome. Although, admittedly, that laundry wasn't particularly authentic. You’re incorrigible. Right, so camping. Rain cover essential? Absolutely. And maybe we need to practice getting into that site. Last time, navigating those tiny lanes nearly resulted in a damaged wing mirror. It reminded me of watching old man Hemmings try to land his Cessna. Old man Hemmings? Was he the one who always flew…erratically? That’s putting it politely. He was convinced he was a fighter pilot, even though he hadn't flown anything more advanced than a single-engine plane since the fifties. Every landing was a nail-biter. The whole airfield held its breath. Goodness. That sounds terrifying. Actually, talking of flying, remember that flight we took over the Fiordland National Park in New Zealand? That was properly breathtaking. Oh, absolutely.

Honestly, I’m convinced Hamish thinks he’s a tiny human. The way he stares at you when you’re eating… it's judgemental, I swear. Oh my god, you're right! They  do  have such little judging faces. Mine just tries to stuff everything into his cheek pouches. It's terrifying, the amount he can fit. Mine just runs on his wheel relentlessly. Like, non-stop. I worry he's secretly powering the national grid. That’s nothing. Brenda keeps trying to escape. Last night I found her…inside a cereal box. Just chilling in the Frosties. No way! How did she even  get  in there? I have no idea! She's a master of stealth. I think she’s plotting world domination, honestly. Or at least, cereal domination. They’re such escape artists. I’ve reinforced Reggie’s cage like three times now, and he  still  finds a way. He's currently staring at me like  I’m  the one who's wrong for containing him. It’s funny you say that about judging faces. Speaking of judging… did you see Chloe with that new guy? The one with the bright red hair? Oh,  him . Yeah. Another ginger. They’re multiplying. Don’t say that! That's a bit…harsh? I mean, what's wrong with gingers? Nothing’s  wrong  with them, it’s just… statistically speaking, there’s a lot of them about, isn’t there? Like, a disproportionate amount. It’s a genetic anomaly or something. I read an article about it. Apparently, it's recessive genes, and both parents have to carry it. Still, Chloe has a  type . All her exes have been ginger. It's… a pattern. Maybe she just  likes  gingers! Isn't that allowed? Of course it’s allowed! I’m just saying, it’s an observation. It’s a… fiery obsession. Oh, good one! She definitely goes for the fiery types. He seemed nice enough though, actually. A bit quiet. Quiet is good. Less drama. Unless he’s quietly plotting to replace Hamish as the most judgemental creature in my life. Then not so good. You’re obsessed with that hamster, aren't you? He's my tiny, fluffy overlord. It’s a complicated relationship. Speaking of complicated relationships… have you seen Liam’s Instagram? Oh God, don't even. The thirst trap he posted last night was… something else.  Please  tell me it didn't involve a shirtless gym selfie.

Right, well, that's Australia gone. Completely eradicated. Honestly, I thought I had a stronghold there. Bloody Camilla. She’s ruthless, your sister. Absolutely ruthless.
