She’s built up North America like it's Fort Knox. She always was competitive, that one. Remember when we used to play Monopoly, and she’d… oh, never mind. Too many childhood traumas resurfacing. Don’t start on the Monopoly stories, Maureen. We’ll be here until Christmas. Though, speaking of Christmas, have you started thinking about presents yet? Little Leo is obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. Just starting to browse, actually. It's all so expensive, isn’t it? And they grow out of things so quickly. I swear, last year's dinosaur was obsolete by Boxing Day. You’re telling me. I'm still trying to figure out what to get Dad. He's got everything. Maybe another bottle of that horrifying sherry he likes? Don’t you dare! He’ll be insufferable for a month. Speaking of insufferable, did Aaron ever send you that map he promised? The one showing all the places he’s travelled? He did, actually. I’ve got it somewhere… it’s a bit of a mess, though. He’s not exactly known for his cartographical skills. He keeps mispronouncing place names. Apparently, ‘Worcestershire’ is ‘Wooster-shire’ in his world. Oh, bless him. He does try. Though, I heard he was telling someone last week that Genghis Khan was a famous chocolatier. No! He did not! That’s brilliant. He’s a walking disaster, that boy. A lovable disaster. He's got a good heart. Though, I still can’t believe he tried to record over my favourite album with a lecture on… I think it was the mating rituals of the Peruvian tree frog. Oh, the audacity! Honestly. Remind me to hide all my CDs when he visits. Has anyone seen my glasses? I swear I put them on the table… Check under the Risk board. You were peering at those tiny little armies like a hawk. Oh, here they are. Thank goodness. This game is making my eyes strain. And is it just me, or does it smell faintly of chocolate in here? That’s probably Mum. She’s been stress-eating Quality Street all afternoon. She says it helps her concentrate on… well, I’m not exactly sure what she’s concentrating on. Speaking of stress, this game is doing my head in.

Honestly, I’m starting to think this whole uni thing was a mistake. Like, a really expensive mistake. Oh, here we go. The existential crisis returns. What’s set you off  this  time, Maisie? Is it Professor Davies’ monotone lecturing, or the eternal queue for the library? It’s… everything. I mean, I’m halfway through second year and I still have absolutely no clue what I want to  do . Everyone else seems so certain. Chloe’s already got an internship lined up for the summer, and Liam’s talking about postgrad options. I just feel… lost. Lost is normal, love. Seriously. We’re 19, 20. We’re  supposed  to be lost. Remember when you were convinced you wanted to be a marine biologist and spent all summer building that ridiculous miniature coral reef in a fish tank? Okay, that was a bad one. But that felt… different. That felt passionate. This just feels like drifting. What are  you  even thinking about doing, anyway? You’re studying History, right? Bit vague. Vague, but versatile! I’m toying with the idea of teaching. Or maybe something in museums. I’ve also briefly considered becoming a professional celebrity lookalike. Oh, really? Which celebrity? Florence Pugh. Apparently, there’s a demand. Plus, I wouldn’t even have to change my accent. Though I’d definitely need to work on the cheekbones. You’d be brilliant. Seriously. But yeah, teaching sounds sensible. What about… babies? Have you ever thought about that? Like,  actual  babies? Woah, hold up. Babies? We’re barely capable of keeping house plants alive, let alone tiny humans. And honestly, the thought terrifies me. Don’t even get me started on childbirth. I know, right? Mum keeps dropping hints about grandkids. It’s exhausting. She showed me pictures of her friend’s new baby the other day. All pink and tiny and… overwhelming. Oh, the pressure! My nan's worse. She's already picking out names. And she keeps saying, "You need to find a nice lad, a  steady  lad." Honestly, it's like I'm living in the 1950s. Steady lads are overrated. I'd rather be a chaotic mess with a questionable career path and a flatmate who considers becoming Florence Pugh a viable option. Exactly. And besides, we’ve got each other. We can figure it out. Maybe. Or we can just spend the rest of our lives watching terrible reality TV and eating biscuits.

Honestly, this Geography project is killing me. Like, "Investigate socio-economic disparities within Slough"... who even  asked  for that? Tell me about it. Mrs. Davies is just on one, isn't she? Trying to make us feel guilty about living here, basically. No, but seriously. I went to that part of town, near the Trading Estate, you know? The bit everyone avoids? It's… rough. Proper rough. Ms. Patel said to interview people, but I just felt really awkward. Yeah, I get that. I was talking to old Mr. Singh at the corner shop, and he was saying how much everything's gone up. Rent, food, everything. He's working like crazy, still barely making ends meet. It's not fair, is it? Like, some people are just born with a decent chance and others… it's stacked against them. Everyone goes on about meritocracy, but it’s a load of rubbish. Exactly! My dad was saying the same thing about the government cuts. Libraries closing, youth centres… Where are kids supposed to go? It’s just setting them up to fail. It’s depressing, honestly. Makes you think, what’s the point of even trying sometimes? Don’t say that, man. You’re supposed to be the optimistic one. Remember when we were kids, building forts in the park, thinking we could solve all the world’s problems? Yeah, well, we were ten. Things seem a bit more complicated now, don't they? Remember Jamie? He's… not doing great. Jamie? What happened? I haven’t seen him in ages. Last I heard he was messing around with that dodgy crowd. Yeah, apparently he dropped out of college. His mum lost her job, and he had to get something, anything, to help out. Said he was doing deliveries, but… well, you know. It's not the best sort of work. That’s brutal. His mum always seemed so strong. It just goes to show, anyone can end up in a bad situation. It does. It really does. Speaking of bad situations, have you finished reading that comic I lent you? 'Nova Corps'? Almost! It’s amazing, dude. Honestly, the art style is insane. And the storyline… galactic empires collapsing, philosophical robots… it's way more interesting than socio-economic disparities! Fair enough. Sometimes you just need to escape, you know? Forget about the world falling apart for a few hours and just enjoy some superheroes.

So, how did the recording go yesterday? Did you manage to get everything down you wanted to? It sounded quite ambitious, all those different voices and sound effects. Oh, it was… a process. A  long  process. Honestly, Mum, I think I spent more time fiddling with the microphone and trying to get the levels right than actually speaking. And the cat kept trying to walk across the keyboard. Nearly deleted the whole thing twice. Oh dear. Cats will be cats. But you did get something usable in the end, though? Eventually. It's... rough. Really rough. I’ll need to edit it for hours. And I keep hearing this buzzing sound I can’t get rid of. Maybe it’s the fridge? Probably. Old Mrs. Higgins next door says her fridge makes a right racket. She was complaining to me over the fence this morning about it. Apparently, she thinks it's interfering with her telly. Honestly, the things she finds to complain about. She’s a character, isn't she? Still, a buzzing fridge sounds… less irritating than a cat walking all over your soundscape. How are your joints holding up? You were saying yesterday your knee was giving you gyp. Oh, it’s dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. I had physio this morning, and although the young man was lovely, I doubt it did much good. He had me doing these little leg lifts… honestly, felt like a beached whale. He keeps saying I need to build up the muscle, but it's so painful! Ugh, physio is the worst. I can’t even imagine having to  do  things during it. I just want them to magically fix everything. Are you still trying that new anti-inflammatory cream? I am, but it’s not making a huge difference. I think I’m just getting old, darling. Everything hurts. Speaking of old, have you seen that new dress in Willow’s window? The navy blue one? I was thinking of getting it, but I’m not sure it would suit me. Oh, the one with the ruffles? It's pretty. But… well, you’ve been saying you want to lose a little weight. Maybe something a bit more… streamlined? Don't start. It's so difficult! I tried that cabbage soup diet, you know? Two days in and I was starving. Then I gave in to a chocolate biscuit and it all fell apart.

Right, so I genuinely think I’ve successfully not burnt the garlic this time. It's a personal triumph, honestly. High praise indeed. It smells…garlicky. Which is a good sign. Last time it smelled more like despair. Despair is a strong word, but accurate. I was attempting to be fancy, infusing the oil, and just…lost focus. Blame TikTok. TikTok is always to blame. Seriously though, this smells lovely. What are we watching after? I downloaded that new psychological thriller everyone’s raving about. Oh, the one with… the woman who keeps losing her keys? Sounds brilliantly predictable. I’m up for it. Although, if it’s too scary, I’m blaming  you . Deal. I'll provide the blankets and the moral support. Speaking of support, work was… something today. Oh, go on. Spill. Production Controller problems? Is someone trying to make you magically produce widgets out of thin air? You know me too well. Apparently, there’s a “supply chain issue” with the packaging for the new skincare line. Which translates to “someone forgot to order it six months ago”. And now it’s  my  job to fix it. Classic. They always give the problem to the organised ones. I had a bit of a nightmare with a venue this morning. They’d double-booked the main hall for a dog agility competition and a corporate awards ceremony. Oh my god. That's… a clash of cultures. Imagine the dogs interrupting the CEO's speech. It was a crisis. Honestly, I spent half an hour on the phone trying to appease both parties. Eventually, I managed to get the dog agility competition moved to a smaller hall, but the dog people were  not  happy. Apparently, it impacts their ‘flow’. ‘Flow’ for dog agility? That’s a new one. But I can see it. You handled it though. You always do. Just about. It’s exhausting sometimes, you know? All this constant problem-solving. It’s a far cry from my dissertation on Victorian poetry. You do sometimes wonder where your degree got you, don't you? I remember you saying you were going to be a professor. A wistful thought. Now I’m deciding which shade of beige tablecloth looks more professional. Actually, talking of shades… do you think this sauce needs more paprika? It feels a little…pale. Definitely paprika. And maybe a pinch of chilli flakes. We need something to counteract the beige-ness of everything.

Right, okay, so we’re doing film night next week, yeah? What are we thinking? I’m open to suggestions, honestly, I’ve been watching so much uni stuff I just need  anything  that isn’t economic policy. Ooh, good shout. I was thinking maybe something a bit…scary? It’s almost Halloween, right? We could do a proper jump-scare fest. Ach, scary films are just predictable. Honestly. You know the music will swell, someone will turn around slowly…it’s all a bit done, isn’t it? I’m more into psychological thrillers. Something that messes with your head a bit. Ooh, I'm with Ben on that. Psychological thrillers are  way  better. I saw “The Lighthouse” last month and it was… intense. Properly unsettling. "The Lighthouse"? Is that the one with Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe? I saw trailers for that. Looked weird. Weird good, or weird bad? 'Cause weird bad is a fast track to me falling asleep halfway through. I thought it looked pretty good! Bit artsy, maybe? But Robert Pattinson can do no wrong in my eyes. It  is  weird. Really weird. It's slow burn, a lot of symbolism, and honestly, the accents are… something. But it's brilliant. It’s not a popcorn movie, though. It demands your attention. I've been wanting to watch "Everything Everywhere All at Once" for ages. Has anyone seen that? Everyone keeps raving about it. Apparently it's mental. Oh my  god , Lucy, you absolutely have to. It’s bonkers, genuinely. Martial arts, bagels, existentialism… it's got everything. And Michelle Yeoh is incredible. Bagels? What’s a bagel got to do with anything? Apparently, everything. I’ve seen memes. It's one of those movies you just need to experience, I think. Okay, “Everything Everywhere All at Once” is officially on the list. Anyone vetoing that? Nah, I'm game. Sounds… interesting. As long as there aren’t any jump scares. Perfect. Should we maybe do a double feature? One psychological thriller, and then “Everything Everywhere”? Ooh, good thinking! That could work. Actually, I think I have a copy of "The Babadook" somewhere. It’s pretty psychological, properly creepy. Not  too  scary, though, I promise. "The Babadook"? I don’t think I’ve heard of that one. Is it on Netflix? No, I don’t think so. I think it’s more of an independent film.

Honestly, Mum, Paris was… hectic. And my feet are  killing  me. Oh, darling! Hectic how? Did you have a nice time overall? And what on earth happened to your feet? You were perfectly fine when you left! Nice time yes, but a bit of a whirlwind. We tried to cram everything in. The Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Montmartre… miles and miles of walking. That’s the feet situation, basically. I think I’ve got blisters on top of blisters. Sounds exhausting! Paris is gorgeous, but seriously, you need sensible shoes. I'm just grabbing some water, how was it? Did you manage to avoid all the pickpockets everyone warned you about? I think so! We were pretty vigilant. Mostly just overwhelmed by the amount of people. And the walking. Seriously, the walking. I feel like I’ve completed a marathon. You should have listened to me and taken those supportive trainers! I told you, those fancy boots weren’t going to cut it. Always prioritise comfort, dear. Mum, you said that about every trip I’ve ever taken! I wanted to  look  Parisian, not like a tourist on a hiking expedition. Fair enough. Though, looking like a comfortable tourist is a perfectly valid aesthetic. Did you at least eat some good food? I was picturing croissants and macarons. Oh, the food was amazing. We had this incredible steak frites… and the pastries were heaven. I think I gained about five pounds just from croissants. Well, you needed the energy for all that walking! Did you manage to find a nice little cafe anywhere? I always loved finding a quiet spot to people-watch in Paris. We found one in Montmartre, overlooking the Sacré-Cœur. It was lovely, but absolutely rammed with tourists. Speaking of rammed, remember Sarah’s birthday party on Saturday? Vaguely. I was still recovering from that dodgy curry the night before. I spent most of it hiding in the garden. Was it good? It was… loud. And chaotic. Mark brought a karaoke machine. You would have  loved  it, or hated it. No inbetween with Mark's karaoke choices. Oh, dear. Mark and a karaoke machine. That sounds like a recipe for disaster. Did anyone break anything? Almost. Someone nearly took down the fairy lights. And Liam attempted Oasis. It was… traumatic. Apparently, he’s convinced he’s the next Liam Gallagher. Oh, Liam. He’s a character. He’s still got that bruise from falling off the scooter, hasn't he?

Morning, Chloe! Chaos as usual, I see. You’re practically sprinting towards Falmer House. Morning, Ben! You have  no  idea. Brenda called in sick, so I’m covering her till ten, then I have to run back down to the shop for my shift. It's a gift that keeps on giving, being a supervisor. Ouch. Sounds…fun. Did you at least have a decent weekend to recover from all that? It was alright. Went down to Chichester to see my Mum. It's always a bit of a whirlwind there, she tries to feed me everything in her fridge. Did you do anything exciting? Relatively tame, actually. Spent a lot of time wrestling with the BNC. Trying to get some decent concordances for my lesson on passives. Honestly, linguistics is occasionally beautiful, occasionally infuriating. And then I just…collapsed on the sofa with a large mug of coffee. The BNC. The bane of every linguistics student's existence, right? I remember agonizing over that when I was doing my Master's. Though, to be fair, my thesis was on Malaysian dialects, so it was a different kind of headache. Oh! Really? That sounds fascinating. I’ve always been curious about language variation. Is it completely different to, like, standard British English? Honestly, in some cases, wildly. I was looking at code-switching and influence from Malay and Arabic. It’s…complex. Anyway, enough linguistics rambling. Are you finally getting paid this week? I know you were stressing about the student loan repayment. Hallelujah, yes! Payday is Friday. It'll be a glorious feeling. Though, realistically, 90% of it will disappear into the loan abyss. It’s terrifying how much interest accrues. Tell me about it. I'm still paying off mine from undergrad, even with the Master’s. Although, I’m trying to budget better now. I keep seeing people posting about ‘that girl’ autumn aesthetic and just…no. I refuse to spend £50 on a pumpkin spice latte. Good for you. I saw Liam from the TEFL course last week. He's already booked his flights to Thailand. Apparently, he’s got a private tuition gig lined up. Show off! He always was a bit of a go-getter. Did he mention Sarah? Are they still…a thing? Actually, no. Apparently, they had a pretty messy break-up. Something about a proposal gone wrong and then…well, rumours of cheating.

Right, so you need one part rice to two parts water. It’s really simple, honestly. People make such a fuss about rice. Two parts water? Are you sure? Gran always says one and a half. No, honestly, two. Unless you want it all mushy. We tried one and a half last week, remember? It was… an experience. Stick with two. And a pinch of salt. Not too much, though, you don’t want it tasting like the sea. Okay, okay, two parts. What about the curry sauce? Is that really spicy? I don't really do spicy. It’s a mild korma. I checked the label. It has, like, a tiny little chilli pepper on it, which is a good sign. Though, honestly, anything with jalapenos is a no-go zone for you, isn’t it? Definitely. Remember that time Uncle Dave made nachos with those tiny green things? I was sweating for an hour! Oh, I remember! You were bright red. Anyway, while that’s simmering, let’s get the chicken out. I’m a little worried about this chicken, actually. It was supposed to be used yesterday. Is it going off? I don’t  think  so, but it smells a bit… suspect. Let's have a proper look. You know, sometimes you get those horror stories about food poisoning. It’s scary. Yeah, like that documentary we watched about that bloke who got really sick from eating dodgy chicken? I nearly threw up just watching it. Exactly! Right, it’s a bit… pale. I’m going to be really careful with this. We can always have veggie burgers if this looks truly awful. Don’t want to risk it. You wouldn't believe what they put  in  some of that processed meat, either. Loads of salt and fat, apparently. Everything’s bad for you, innit? Pretty much. Though, honestly, a little bit of what you fancy doesn’t hurt. We're having a treat tonight. Remember that restaurant we went to in Bristol, the one with all the amazing food? Yeah! The one with the really weird art on the walls? That’s the one! We should go back someday. They did amazing curries, but they were so expensive. These vouchers I've got might cover a main course each, though. We could try and go next month. Cool. What about that weird thing you were reading about… the person with the face… you know, the one who couldn’t make facial expressions?

Honestly though, seeing Sarah at the shop today… it just reminded me how much things have changed since school. Aye, she looked… well, she looked proper stressed, didn’t she? Like she hadn’t slept in weeks. Still got that same handbag though. The bright pink one. Is she still with… what’s his name, Mark? The one who was always trying to copy your hair? No, she dumped him ages ago. She’s with Liam now, from a year above. He’s doing a law degree. Apparently, they’re already talking about moving in together. Seriously? They’ve only been going out like six months. And Liam? Bit of a show-off, wasn’t he? Always bragging about his dad’s car. He was alright. Bit too keen on the gym for my liking. Remember when he tried to lift that ridiculously heavy weight and nearly crushed his foot? Oh god, yeah! Mr. Muscle gone wrong. Speaking of gym, I’m knackered. Work was… something else today. Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was a world-class chef and tried to make shepherd’s pie with lentils. Oh no. It was a disaster. The whole place smelled like burnt sadness. I had to pretend to enjoy it while she beamed at me. Honestly, the things you do for minimum wage. Sounds rough. I’m still trying to work out how to be…productive. This job hunting is killing me. Nothing but rejection emails. It's depressing, init? You’ve only been looking properly for a couple of weeks, Liam. Don’t beat yourself up. Have you tried widening your search? Maybe looking further afield? Aye, but getting a job in Whitehaven is hard enough, never mind thinking about moving anywhere. And then there's the money. Or lack of it. Mum’s starting to look at me funny. You could always apply for that barista job at Costa. It's not glamorous, but it’s something. I did! They said I didn’t have enough “customer service experience”. What does that even mean? I’ve served me mam tea for 20 years! It means you need to learn to fake a cheerful disposition while someone is shouting at you about the temperature of their latte. Trust me, I’ve been there. Did you watch that new series on Netflix, the one about the Vikings? No, is it good? It’s amazing!

Right, so then Brenda, bless her, she’s gone and booked a pottery class for us all. A  pottery  class, Liam. Can you imagine? Pottery? Cor, sounds…messy. And a bit slow, innit? Not really my speed. Exactly! I tried to explain to her that I’m not particularly artistic, and I’d probably just end up covered in clay and making something that looks like a collapsed ashtray. But no, she’s convinced it’ll be “therapeutic”. Therapeutic for who, eh? The instructor having to clean up after you? Possibly! She’s always going on about needing a hobby. Says I work too much. Which, honestly, is not wrong. This conference next month is going to be a nightmare. The keynote speaker keeps changing his mind about the AV setup. Oh, the joys. Folks are always right at the last minute. Makes your head spin, doesn’t it? I used to get that a bit with the garden, you know. Deciding what to plant when, then realising you needed something else completely when it didn’t grow right. It sounds…stressful, gardening. All that bending! My back would go into absolute meltdown. I tried yoga once, just once, and pulled a muscle in my shoulder. Yoga’s for the flexible ones, love. You need something a bit more…solid. Walking’s good. Gets you out, you know? Used to walk miles, I did. Before… well, before. Before the retirement life took over? No offence, Liam, but you seem to have perfected the art of doing absolutely nothing. Ain’t no art to it, lass. It comes naturally. Besides, someone’s gotta keep the armchair warm. Though I miss being busy, I won't lie. Used to enjoy a bit of physical graft, actually. Building stuff, fixing things. You always were good with your hands. Remember when you built that birdhouse for Gran? It was wonky as anything, but she loved it. Aye, it was a bit off, that. But the birds didn’t seem to mind. Speaking of Gran, how's she doin'? Haven’t seen her in ages. She’s alright, a bit grumbly as usual. Complaining about the price of biscuits, mostly. She still asks after your mum, though. They used to be thick as thieves, didn’t they? They did. Used to go to bingo together every week. Had some right laughs, apparently. She's a good woman, your Gran.

Right, anyone offering to do the dishes? Seriously, it’s not going to magically happen. Ugh, Mum, do I  have  to? I was just about to start a game. Leave him, love. I’ll do them. Gets me away from listening to you two bicker. Thanks, Dad. Can I help you dry? Sure, mate. Teamwork makes the dream work, eh? Although, honestly, sometimes I think the dream is just a clean kitchen. You say that now… Honestly, the state of your room, though, Noah. It’s a biohazard. You need to clear that up tomorrow. Not ‘sometime next week’,  tomorrow . It's not  that  bad. It is. I nearly tripped over a mountain of dirty socks yesterday. And is that a half-eaten biscuit under your bed? Maybe. Leave him alone, Sarah. He’s a teenager, they live in a perpetual state of mess. Remember when  you  were a teenager? The posters… Oh, the posters. Don’t even  start  on the posters. Bjorn Borg. Honestly. He was gorgeous, though. Remember watching Wimbledon as a kid? It was such an event. Wimbledon’s on now, isn't it? Is Carlos Alcaraz playing? He is, apparently. I caught a bit earlier. He's a bit of a prodigy, isn’t he? Amazing serve. Reminds me a bit of Federer, honestly. Dad, you always say that about anyone good at tennis. Well, Federer  was  the best. Still is, in my eyes. Speaking of amazing, have you seen Ethan’s attempt at a moustache? Oh, don’t. I saw a photo on Instagram. It’s… patchy, to say the least. Looks like a caterpillar died on his upper lip. Hey! It’s growing! It takes time! It looks like you’ve drawn it on with a Biro. Shut up, Leo. Now, now, boys. Be kind. It's all part of the experimental phase. Though, I have to say, historically, facial hair hasn’t always had the best associations. You know… Hitler. Oh, darling, really? That’s… a jump. Just saying. It’s a cautionary tale. Careful with the grooming choices, Ethan. You're so weird, Dad. Have you spoken to Amy lately, Ethan? Still going strong? She posted some pictures with another boy on Instagram, though. Oh dear. Drama! I don’t know... it looked a bit close. Like, holding hands close. Right, well, that’s a conversation you need to have with her, son.

Honestly, the sofa…it’s just  worn . Absolutely worn. I keep saying we need to get a new one, but…it's a whole palaver isn’t it? Getting rid of the old one. Yeah, especially if you can't get anyone to help you shift it. Dad’s good with that stuff, isn't he? Though he’d probably just suggest you keep patching it up with duct tape. He would, bless him. He's a fixer, your father. Though I did see him trying to fix Mrs. Higgins’ bird table with… was it chewing gum? Oh, honestly! He's a character. Anyway, the tip looks like it’s exploded again. I drove past earlier. Mountains of stuff. People just dumping everything. It’s awful. You wouldn’t believe what people try and get rid of. Sarah was telling me about someone who tried to dump a whole kitchen sink at the recycling centre. A  whole  kitchen sink? Seriously? Yeah! Apparently, there was a massive argument. She said the guy just didn't want to pay for bulky waste collection. Oh, the cheek of it! Speaking of Sarah, how are things with her and Mark? Still awful, is it? Yeah, poor love. He's really struggling. Apparently, he had another dizzy spell yesterday. She’s having to practically run his life for him. It’s heartbreaking. It is. She’s so strong, though, isn't she? Managing everything with the kids and then worrying about him. She really is. It reminds me a bit of what happened with Auntie Maureen, you know, slowly… disappearing. It's just awful watching someone you love…fade. It is the worst thing. My mum… forgetting my name. That was hard. Still hard, even now. Did you see that new building they're putting up on the Silk Road? It looks… huge. Hideous. Honestly, it's completely out of character with the town. It’s like someone just plonked a spaceship down. And the traffic…it’s already chaos. They never think things through, do they? Just build, build, build. Don’t care about the consequences. Someone swore at me in the supermarket the other day because I was blocking the aisle. Swearing! Right there! Oh, honestly. Some people have no manners. Remember that Beaver Scout Christmas party last year? Little Timmy swore after losing at pass the parcel. His mum was mortified. Oh, I remember that!

Honestly, Mum, the whole thing at work is just… draining. They’re talking about restructuring  again . Everyone’s on edge. Oh dear, not another one. That's the third time this year isn't it? What are they saying this time? Well, it’s all very ‘streamlining’ and ‘synergies’ and… honestly, corporate jargon nonsense. But basically, my team’s looking at potential redundancies. They haven’t said who yet, but… it’s hanging over everyone. Oh, Poppy, that’s awful! You’ve been working so hard. You’re really good at your job. Don't let it get you down too much, alright? Easier said than done, I know. I’m trying not to. I've updated my CV just in case, which is grim. But realistically, the job market isn’t exactly booming, is it? No, it isn’t. But you’re resourceful. You’ll land on your feet. Have you thought about… well, you’ve always talked about wanting to do something more creative, haven’t you? Maybe this is a sign? Maybe. Though ‘creative’ doesn’t pay the bills, does it? Anyway, enough about work doom and gloom. What are your plans for the weekend? Anything fun? Your Grandad's birthday, remember? We’re going over to his on Saturday for lunch. He's already asked three times if you’re bringing a cake. Oh, right! Completely forgot. I’ll pop to the shops tomorrow and see what I can find. He’ll be thrilled. He loves his little cakes. Are you taking him that new board game he wanted? Yes, I’ve got it wrapped up already. He’s been hinting about it for weeks! He's so excited. Though, honestly, I think he'll just want to talk about his garden. Definitely. He could talk about gardening for hours. You know, I really should try and go to the gym more. I’ve been feeling so sluggish lately. Stress from work, I suppose. You always say that! It’s good for you, dear. Gets you out of the house. I joined a new Pilates class last week. It's surprisingly challenging. Pilates, huh? Maybe I’ll give that a go. Anything’s better than collapsing on the sofa with a tub of ice cream every night. I've been terrible with my eating lately. Oh, don't beat yourself up about it. Everyone indulges now and then.

Right, nearly finished. Nearly dinner ready. Peas and fish fingers, is that alright? Yeah, sounds good. Can I watch Mick after? After you’ve eaten  all  your peas. No arguments. Honestly, you’re worse than Finn sometimes. Finn, darling, stop trying to climb the curtains!  to Speaker_3  No, down! Uh-oh! He's a proper little monkey, isn’t he? You have no idea. Honestly, it’s a full-time job. Now, what are you planning to do tomorrow? It's raining again, isn't it? No good for a park visit. Liam said we might go to his house and build a massive Lego castle. He’s got all the Star Wars sets. Oh, that sounds good. Who’s Liam again? Remind me. From school! We were talking about it on the bus. It’ll take ages, apparently. He's got, like, three different Millennium Falcons. Goodness. Well, as long as you’re having fun. What if it rains all summer? Have you thought about what you’d like to do then? I dunno. Learn more guitar? Mr. Henderson said I'm getting good, but I keep forgetting the chords for ‘Smoke on the Water’. Well, practice makes perfect. Maybe we can find some easy tutorials online? Or, we could try and go to the swimming pool more often. The Quays? It's always busy. And sometimes those older kids splash everyone. We could go early, before it gets too crowded. Or maybe try the one in Midleton? It’s quieter there, I think. We could even pack a picnic. That’d be good. Finn could come too, if he's being good. He’s two. “Good” is a relative term.  to Speaker_3  No, Finn, don't put that in your mouth! It's a sock! What was that you were saying earlier? About…Japan-ease? Oh! Japanese! I was trying to learn a few phrases for a holiday, ages ago. It’s so complicated. All those different writing systems. I got to ‘hello’ and ‘thank you’ and then gave up. I saw a video on YouTube about it. They said it's not that hard if you break it down. Easy for you to say, you’re a quick learner. Right, dinner’s getting cold. Peas first! And no complaining. Are you doing any chores this summer? Mr. O’Malley next door was saying his son helps him with the garden.

Right, that was a bit… much, wasn’t it? All that slow-motion running. Like a music video from 1998. Tell me about it. Could’ve fast-forwarded half of it, honestly. Proper cheese. Though, I’ll give ‘em this, the villain's got style. Proper menacing. Reminds me a bit of that bloke from  Peaky Blinders …Arthur Shelby, yeah? A bit, yeah. Though Arthur’s got a bit more… well, desperation in his eyes, hasn't he? This guy just looks… bored of being evil. Bored of being evil! That's brilliant. You're spot on. Speaking of unsettling, remember old Mr. Henderson, the dentist back in Leicester? Oh  god , Henderson. Don’t even  mention  him. That man was a menace. Always smelled of mint and regret. Regret! Exactly! And the way he'd just…stare. While drilling. Like he was contemplating the existential dread of teeth. And he’d always talk about his holidays. Every single appointment revolved around hearing about his caravan trips to Skegness. “Oh, and the wind was  terrible  this year, you know, awful for the awning.” As if I cared about his awning while he was assaulting my molars! Awning! Oh, that's perfect. It's amazing the things you remember. I’ve got a dentist here, thankfully, who mostly just asks about work. Which leads to me inevitably having to explain what I actually  do  to people. The curse of the English Language Teacher. “So, you… teach people  how  to speak?” Like it's some kind of complex alchemy. What are you working on at the moment, anyway? Any brilliant new lessons brewing? Actually, yeah. Trying to get them to grapple with regional accents. It’s a nightmare. I played a recording of you talking the other day, just a little snippet, and they were  convinced  you were speaking a foreign language. What?! Me? My accent is perfectly reasonable! It's classic Midlands speech! Reasonable to  you , maybe. To a group of eighteen-year-olds from all over Europe, it was utter gibberish. Apparently, the “oo” sounds were particularly perplexing. Oh, they haven't heard me really lay it on thick, then. I can do a Leicester accent that’ll melt your ears. Please, no. My students are easily traumatised enough. So, how's the writing going? Still battling with the novel? Slowly but surely. I’m stuck on chapter twelve. It feels like… like I’ve written myself into a corner and the only way out involves a time-travelling badger.

So, how was the school run this morning? Any little horrors? Honestly, Mum, chaotic. Little Leo decided today was the day to protest wearing shoes. Full-on meltdown in the car park. I swear, I got judging looks from everyone. Oh, Leo. Always a character. Remember when he refused to wear trousers to the supermarket? How could I forget? He insisted he was a mermaid. It’s exhausting, but… mostly wonderful. How was your morning? Did you manage to get to the garden centre? I did, eventually. It was rammed, though. Everyone preparing for Easter, I suppose. I got those little daffodil bulbs you like, and a couple of those iced Easter cakes – the ones with the chicks on. I’ll bring them over later. Oh, you shouldn't have! But thank you. The kids will  love  those cakes. They’re already talking about the Easter egg hunt. Are you free to help me hide them? Of course, love. Any time. It's good to have something to do, now I’m… well, you know. No work to fill my days anymore. Still feels a bit odd. How  are  you feeling about everything, actually? It’s been a few weeks since you finished. It’s a bit of a rollercoaster, to be honest. Some days I feel incredibly liberated - like a weight’s been lifted. Others… I miss the structure, the people. And the pay, let’s not lie. It's a big adjustment. I can imagine. But you've always got us, Mum. And you’ve got loads of things you’ve always wanted to do. That painting course, for example? Yes, I’m looking into that. It starts next month, I think. And I’ve been trying to get back into reading. Though, honestly, I just end up scrolling through Facebook. Old habits die hard. Tell me about it! Anyway, exciting news… I finally got confirmation about the new job! The Head of Year position at Elmwood. Oh, Sarah! That's fantastic! I knew you’d get it. You're brilliant with those children. When do you start? September. Which is good. It gives me time to properly finish the year with my current class. It’s a lot more responsibility, though. More meetings, more paperwork… but it's what I want. It sounds perfect for you. And it's a real achievement. We're all so proud. Speaking of big events… Have you and Ben finalised details for Amelia’s christening?

Honestly, this marking is never-ending. I feel like all I do is read essays about… well, usually just badly paraphrased Wikipedia articles. How are things with Year 11? Any closer to sanity? Don’t even  start  me. They're driving me round the bend. The drama, the entitlement, the sheer refusal to engage with anything that vaguely resembles effort. It’s exhausting. I had one girl actually  ask  me if she could have extra credit for having a bad day. You’re joking! I wish I was. Honestly. It’s like they think school is some sort of personal entertainment service. How’s Leo taking to Year 4? Settled now? He’s loving it, actually. He’s started doing this little science club after school, which is brilliant. He came home yesterday trying to explain the water cycle using just ping pong balls and a watering can. It was… chaotic, but adorable. Oh, that sounds like him! He's always been a little inventor. My niece, Chloe, is obsessed with animals at the moment. She wants to be a vet, a marine biologist  and  a dog groomer, all at the same time. It changes weekly! That’s lovely. It’s good they’ve got passions, isn’t it? Though slightly terrifying when they start talking about wanting to rescue every stray animal in the country. Tell me about it! Her mum's trying to gently steer her towards something more…realistic. Speaking of animals, how’s Winston? Still shedding like a snowstorm? Oh, Winston. Always shedding. I swear he multiplies fur overnight. I’ve invested in one of those robotic vacuum cleaners, and it’s constantly battling a losing war against the fluff. But he’s worth it. He's started stealing socks again though. Oh, Winston! He’s a menace. My sister had a Labrador who used to do the same thing. Found one in the washing machine once. Mid-cycle. Oh, the horror! I’d probably cry. Although, I did try this new face mask last night… it was a clay one, supposed to be detoxifying. It made me look like a Martian. Oh, I know the type! I’ve been trying to find a decent retinol serum; everything seems to either do nothing or completely strip my skin. It's a minefield out there. Have you seen anything good? Not recently, I'm afraid. I've been sticking to the basics lately.

Honestly, this charoset is incredible, Eliana. Seriously. What  is  your secret? It’s not too sweet, it's got a good bite… Oh, stop it! It's just my grandmother’s recipe. The key is really good quality dates, and a tiny bit of orange zest. Don't tell anyone, it’s a closely guarded family secret. It's delightful, dear. Far better than the one my mother used to make. Too much apple, not enough… well, everything else. Though she tried her best, bless her. She always felt slightly guilty she couldn't keep a properly kosher kitchen. It’s a nice break from all the matzah ball soup, though, isn’t it? No offence to anyone’s matzah ball soup, of course. Mum’s is legendary. Absolutely no offence. Matzah ball soup is foundational. But, yeah, a bit of textural variety is appreciated. So, anyone making any exciting plans for after Pesach? I’m thinking of finally taking that trip to Italy. Oh, Italy! That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go to Naples – proper pizza, you know? And all the pastries! Though truthfully, I’m happy just being here, perfecting my sourdough. Italy is lovely, darling. Florence is a must. But you  must  be careful with the restaurants. Some of them are… rather overhyped. And absolutely avoid anything that sounds remotely like ‘ortolan’. Utterly barbaric. Ortolan? What even is that? Sounds… medieval. Apparently, it’s a small bird, they fatten it up in the dark, then you eat it whole, head and all, with a napkin over your head to catch the bones and juices. Don’t ask. Saw it on a documentary. Truly horrifying. Oh my god! No thank you. I'll stick to biscotti. Speaking of which, has anyone seen my recipe for the almond biscotti? I was hoping to try it out this week. I think I might have it, darling. It's somewhere amongst my chaotic collection of recipes. Your Great Aunt Ruth sent it over, didn’t she? She always had the best ones. Reminds me, she insisted on calling you “Leah” for years, even after you corrected her! Oh, Aunt Ruth. She was convinced I was supposed to be named Leah. She had a whole elaborate story about Hebrew names and destiny. My mum is always trying to get me to learn more Hebrew. She keeps saying it'll ‘connect me to my roots’.

Right, so, who actually finished “The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo”? Because honestly, I started it and just… couldn’t get into it. It felt a bit… much. Oh, I adored it! Absolutely adored it. Cried buckets, naturally. Though, I do think it’s massively overrated, if I’m being honest. Everyone was raving about it, and it was good, but not  that  good. I’m with Sarah, actually. I sped through it. Had to know what happened. I did the audiobook though, which might have helped. The narrator really brought Evelyn to life. Though, I’m slightly side-tracked. Has anyone been watching “The Diplomat” on Netflix? Oh! Yes! I binged that in two days. Brilliant, wasn’t it? The twists and turns… and Rufus Sewell is just…  chef’s kiss . Rufus Sewell does have a certain… something. But I found it a bit implausible, didn’t you? All that international intrigue happening so quickly. Felt a bit like a James Bond film dressed up as a political drama. I thought it worked  because  it was a bit heightened. It’s entertainment, after all. You’re not expecting realism. Speaking of entertainment, I’ve been trying to get back into knitting. Remember when we all tried that during lockdown? Oh god, yes. My attempt at a scarf looked like something a cat dragged in. I stuck to eBooks, far less stressful. Honestly, I’ll never understand the appeal of physically making things. I like instant gratification. I rather enjoy it! It’s meditative. I’m crocheting a blanket for my nephew’s new baby. It’s going to be… a process. And I’m definitely more of a physical book person. I love the smell, the feel of the paper... you just don't get that with a Kindle. I'm on team both, really. eBooks for when I’m travelling or need something light, and physical books for when I want to really  savour  a story. Though I did get my mum a Kindle for her birthday. She’s a committed physical book fan, but her eyesight is getting worse. Good thinking. My dad is refusing to get a Kindle, says it ruins the experience. He's still ploughing through Tolstoy, bless him. Speaking of family, did anyone manage to get through to Auntie Mavis to wish her happy birthday? She's been a bit off the radar lately.

Right, so this… this is the bit I’m most worried about, innit? Transferring everything over. You’d think, wouldn’t ya, after all these years, it’d be seamless. But it never is. Seamless is a strong word for technology, especially when we’re dealing with Android to Android. It  should  be relatively straightforward though, yeah? I mean, Google’s supposedly got everything backed up in the cloud. Supposedly. That's the key word, isn’t it? “Supposedly.” Remember last time? With the Samsung? It was a nightmare. Lost half me photos, contacts were a mess. Took weeks to sort it out. Oh god, don’t remind me. You were apoplectic. This is a Pixel though, supposedly Google's own hardware. It  should  play nicer. Have you got the cable? I can try and plug mine in and show you how the quick transfer thing works? Aye, here. USB-C to USB-C. Brand new, still in the bag. Go on then, you’re the tech wizard. I still think it’s a conspiracy, you know? They  want  you to struggle. Keeps people buying new ones. Like Nokia back in the day. Solid as a rock, nearly indestructible. They just… vanished. Vanished is a bit harsh. Apple happened. And Android. Nokia were slow to adapt. Remember everyone had a 3310? You could literally throw that thing down the stairs and it wouldn’t break. You could. And they still worked! My first proper mobile phone. Texting was a revelation. Now look at ‘em, all glass and fragile. Honestly, I’m scared to even  hold  this thing properly. Right, okay. So, let’s power yours on. Okay, it’s asking if you want to copy data from your old phone. Yes, obviously. Now, it should detect mine. It says… “Nearby Devices.” Give it a sec… What about the SIM card? That's a faff, isn’t it? They never made those a standard size. Always a different one. It’s nano-SIM, thankfully. I’ve got that little tool thingy with my phone. One sec… okay, got it. Just need to pop that in. So, it’s connecting now. It’s saying it’ll copy apps, data, photos… it looks like it’s actually recognising everything. This is good. Fingers crossed. How long does it reckon it’ll take? I don't wanna be sat here all night. We've got a sauna booking, remember?

Right, so Leo’s party. Are you still set on having it at the soft play centre? Yeah, definitely! All my mates said it’s the best one. They’ve got like, a massive slide and everything. Doggy! Doggy! Yes, darling, that’s a doggy. A very fluffy doggy. Now, Leo, we need to finish talking about your party. Have you made a list of who you want to invite yet? Almost. I’ve got most of them, but I need to check with Mum about Ben. She said something about his mum being a bit… difficult? She’s just a bit overprotective, love. It’s fine. Just make sure you say everyone's invited. We don’t want anyone feeling left out. Oh, and did you decide on the theme? You were talking about Red Pandas yesterday? Yeah! Red Pandas! They’re awesome. They’re like, tiny bears but super fluffy and they eat bamboo. I saw a documentary about them. Panda! Panda! He loves pandas too. They’re very cute. Now, we need to think about the cake. Do you want a Red Panda cake? We could get one with little bamboo shoots on it. Ooh, yeah! That’d be amazing! Can it be chocolate? Of course. Chocolate Red Panda cake it is. Right, let’s see... soft play centre booked, theme decided, cake sorted… what about presents? You’re getting something for Finn, aren’t you? His birthday’s next week. Yeah, I was thinking a new Malamute puppy toy. He loves dogs, but he's always wanted a Malamute. He saw one at the park last week and wouldn’t stop talking about it. That’s a good idea. He'll love that. Do you want me to take you shopping for it this weekend? We can also get a card. Yeah, that’d be good. Oh, and can we watch that Japanese film you downloaded? The one about the girl and the cat?  Whispering to herself  …Studio Ghibli one? Yes, of course. We can watch it on Saturday. After we go to gymnastics with Rory. ‘Pad! ‘Pad! Can I use the iPad after? I need to finish my research for school. We’re learning about different ecosystems, and I want to find out more about Red Panda habitats. It’s much easier to type on a laptop though, isn’t it? It is, but the iPad’s portable.

Honestly though, Christmas at Nana’s was  always  mental. Not in a bad way, just… chaotic. Chaotic is a polite word for it. It was a full-on assault on the senses. All the aunties crammed into that tiny kitchen, smelling of sherry and burnt Brussels sprouts. Oh, don't I know it. I’ve lost count of the Christmases where someone inevitably ended up arguing over the last Quality Street. It was a tradition in itself, really. You lot had Quality Streets? We never had those. It was always Roses down in Bognor. Though, the arguments were exactly the same. The coffee creams were the most fought over, naturally. Roses are worse! They’ve got those weird coconut ones that nobody likes, but someone  always  gets stuck with three. It’s funny, isn’t it? How deeply ingrained these little traditions are. I remember my Lola – my grandmother from the Philippines – would always make this dish called  lechon . Roast pig, whole, on a spit. It was incredible, but… incredibly messy. Oh, that sounds lovely! Bit different from our turkey and stuffing. We always had a proper British Christmas dinner. Though, I did once try to introduce a mango chutney. Didn’t go down well. “Too exotic,” they said. Exotic? Honestly. People are so stuck in their ways. I remember when we first went to Italy, decades ago, and tried to order a proper English breakfast. The look on the waiter’s face! He thought we were mad. Speaking of different cultures, I was reading an article about how Christmas is celebrated in Japan. They eat KFC! Apparently, it’s a huge marketing success story from years ago, and now it’s just…normal. KFC? Seriously? That’s bizarre. Though, I suppose it's no weirder than stuffing a whole pig with spices and roasting it. It just…doesn’t scream ‘Christmas’ to me. It's the thought that counts, dear. Though, I must say, I’ve noticed things have changed a lot over the years. It feels…more commercial now. Less about family and faith, and more about getting the perfect present. Absolutely. When I was a boy, Christmas felt… simpler. We didn't have all this fuss. And people weren’t so quick to judge, either. I remember a chap moved to Bognor, an Indian fella. Got some terrible stick for it, initially. Made me so angry. It’s awful, isn’t it?

Honestly, I’m absolutely shattered. This transcription job is… relentless. Four hours of someone talking about plumbing fittings. Plumbing! Oof, sounds thrilling. Is it at least paying well? You deserve a break. I’m just wading through spreadsheets all day, it’s soul-destroying. Oh don’t even start, spreadsheets are the bane of my existence. I’m trying to wrestle this new chapter into shape, and it’s fighting me every step of the way. Honestly, sometimes I think the characters have a mind of their own. Sounds more interesting than pipe joints, anyway. What’s it about this time? More village intrigue? A bit. But with a definite… shadowy figure. I’m trying to channel a bit of Ruth Rendell, you know? That unsettling feeling that something is terribly wrong just beneath the surface. Have you been watching any good detective shows? We started that  Shetland  one. Quite good, isn’t it? Very atmospheric. Although, honestly, after a day staring at numbers, I sometimes struggle to follow the plot. Oh,  Shetland  is fantastic. The landscapes are just stunning. I'm rewatching  Vera  at the moment. Brenda Blethyn is brilliant. And she's always eating biscuits, which is a bonus. Biscuits are essential viewing companions. Speaking of food, are we still on for that Thai on Friday? I need a proper meal that isn’t microwaved leftovers. Definitely! I’ve already booked a table. It’s been ages since we’ve all managed to get together. Perfect. It’ll be good to just… switch off. I’ve been meaning to ask, Sarah, how’s Maggie doing? I haven’t spoken to her in ages. She’s good! She finally finished her pottery course. She’s utterly obsessed now. Her flat is filling up with wonky vases. She's started selling some at a little craft fair and actually made a profit. That’s brilliant! She’s always been so creative. I remember when she… oh, never mind. A story for another time. Go on, spill! It involved a questionable shade of purple hair dye and a very angry headmistress. We were teenagers, it was a disaster. Oh,  that ! I’d almost forgotten. That was epic. She truly thought she could pull off lavender. Oh, brilliant. I need some gossip. This transcription work is turning my brain to mush. Have either of you read anything good lately? I’m thinking of getting a Kindle, but I’m a bit of a book purist.

Now, you’re sure you’ve got everything for that trip to see young Thomas, eh? Passport, tickets…the lot? Oh, honestly, Arthur, you fuss more than my own mother ever did. Yes, I’ve got it all. Checked it three times. Passport’s in the little blue wallet, tickets are with the booking confirmation. Honestly, I’m not a complete scatterbrain, you know. Your mother was a worrier, Margaret. No offence meant, of course. Arthur just has a good head for details. Comes from years of… well, observing things, really. Observing things? That’s a polite way of saying ‘doing nothing much all day’! No, he observes the dust motes dancing in the sunlight and critiques the neighbour’s petunias. Now, now. There’s a lot to be said for a peaceful life. And I  do  keep an eye on things. Saw young Pidgeon’s cat trying to get into Mrs. Higgins’ bird feeder this morning. Absolute menace, that cat. Right. Well, I’m just saying, it’s good you’ve got a sense of what's going on. Margaret, seriously though, did you remember the adaptor for the phone? Thomas said their sockets are different. Oh, good point, David! Nearly forgot that. It’s in the little bag with the travel toothbrush. Always the little things… Thank you, darling. You're a lifesaver, you are. Travel toothbrush? Fancy that! In my day, we just rinsed our mouths out with water on long journeys. Didn't do us any harm. Though I suppose things are rather different now. They are, Arthur. They are. Listen, Margaret, about the money… are you sure you’ve got enough for a taxi from the airport? Thomas is working, isn’t he? And it’s a fair distance into town. Yes, yes, I’ve got it sorted. I withdrew some extra, just in case. I’m not reliant on Thomas providing everything. I’m perfectly capable of managing. Honestly, you two treat me like I'm helpless! No, no, dear, not at all. Just…wanting you to be comfortable. It's a long trek from that airport, and you don’t want to be stranded. Exactly. Just a little pre-planning. And, Margaret, is the insurance up to date? Just in case of… well, you know. Lost luggage or… worse. David! You’re starting to sound like Arthur now. Yes, the insurance is fine. I renewed it just last month.

Right, so, Friday. Is everyone still good for Friday? Seven-thirty at The Eagle? It's the easiest place for everyone to get to, yeah? Yeah, sounds perfect, love The Eagle. Their chips are unreal. Honestly, they’re worth the trip alone. Seven-thirty’s good for me. Just need to, uh, mentally prepare myself for a proper Cambridge pub on a Friday night. It’ll be  busy . Aye, busy is an understatement. But it’s tradition, innit? We  have  to kick off the new project somewhere iconic. I'm in. Sounds good to me! I’m looking forward to celebrating wrapping up the Horace phase, honestly. It’s been… a journey. A journey is putting it mildly. Honestly, I think I dreamt in phonetic transcription for a solid month there. And the metadata… don’t even get me started. Tell me about it! I’m still finding rogue tags in my dreams. Speaking of rogue, did anyone else see that massive moth flapping around the window in the server room this afternoon? Oh, aye! The one that looked like it was wearing a tiny velvet waistcoat? I swear it sized me up. Proper intimidating. I tried to shoo it out, but it just kept flying into the glass. Poor thing. I felt awful. Oh no! Did you manage to help it? Eventually, yeah. I grabbed a cardboard box and gently… guided it in. Then released it outside. Felt like a proper wildlife rescue operation. That’s lovely of you! You’re a softie, aren't you? I once spent twenty minutes rescuing a ladybug from a potted plant in my office. My team thought I’d lost it. You’re both saints! I’d probably just panic and run. I’m a bit rubbish with insects. Especially the big, fluffy ones. Aye, big moths and wasps… nah. Give me a tiny spider any day. They’re just wee things. Okay, bringing us back to Friday… should we think about booking a table? Even if it’s just for a heads-up, might save us battling for a spot. Good shout. I can give them a ring now, actually. How many should I say? We're five, right? Five is perfect. Actually, would it be alright if I brought Ben along? He's my flatmate and he's been saying how much he wants to meet you all. He's a linguist too, actually.

Ugh, history was  brutal  today. Mr. Davies decided to spring a quiz on us. A quiz! On the Tudors! No way! Seriously? He said we weren’t having a quiz until next week. I actually revised a little bit. A  little . Liar. You hate the Tudors. You said Henry VIII was a “massive drama queen.” Okay, fine, I said it. But still! He’s so unfair. What was on it? EVERYTHING. Dates, wives, battles, the Pilgrimage of Grace… it was endless. I think I answered, like, three questions correctly. Ouch. I'm pretty sure I'd fail. Did anyone do well? Chloe did, obviously. She's practically a walking encyclopedia. She was smugly writing away for the whole lesson. And Ben, surprisingly. He usually doodles robots. Ben? Really? Maybe he secretly loves history. Speaking of disasters, English was… interesting. Interesting how? Did Ms. Peterson make someone read their story out loud and then dissect it for an hour again? Worse. Liam brought in a pet rat. NO. WAY. A  rat ? A tiny, fluffy one, apparently. He said it was called Winston. Ms. Peterson nearly had a heart attack. She had to send him and Winston to the head’s office. That’s…amazing. I wish I’d seen that. Was Winston in a cage? Apparently, Liam had him in his jacket pocket. Like, just…hanging out. It ran across the desk at one point. Sarah screamed. Oh my god. That’s seriously the most Liam thing ever. He’s always trying to push boundaries. What about Maths? Please tell me Maths was normal for once. Nope. Mr. Harris decided we needed to practice simultaneous equations by pretending we were ordering pizzas. …What? Yeah, like, ‘If one pizza costs £12 and two garlic breads cost £6, how much is the total bill?’ It was so bizarre. And he kept calling us “mathletes”. This school is a constant source of chaos. I need a holiday. Seriously. Maybe we can sneak out and get ice cream later? To, like, recover from the trauma of today. Definitely. Ice cream is the only logical response. And maybe we can plan our revenge on Mr. Davies for the quiz. I’m in. He deserves a glitter bomb, honestly. Although, probably not. We’d get in so much trouble. True. But the thought is satisfying. Very satisfying. Let’s just stick to ice cream. Deal. Right. Back to the academic hellscape, then.

Honestly, this lasagne is… okay. It’s just a bit bland, isn’t it? I was hoping for a bit more…oomph. It’s alright. I’m starving so anything goes down a treat, really. Long day at work, you know? Spent the whole afternoon dealing with that Henderson account. He keeps changing his mind about everything. Aye, you get all sorts, don’t you? Sales is the same. One minute they’re all keen as mustard, next they’re saying they’ve found something cheaper down the road. It’s exhausting really. Did you manage to get that report finished, love? The one for your boss? Nearly. Just the conclusions section left, then I need to run all the figures through again. It’s just… draining. Data analysis isn’t exactly glamorous, is it? I swear, sometimes I dream in spreadsheets. Tell me about it. I’ve been looking at project timelines all day. Excel is my nemesis. Speaking of draining, how was your day, Mum? Still battling the customers at the garden centre? Oh, you wouldn’t believe. Old Mrs. Higgins was convinced we’d sold her the wrong compost. Apparently, her petunias weren’t thriving. Honestly, it was a twenty-minute debate about the nitrogen content. I ended up just giving her a tenner off a bag of fertiliser to get rid of her! Oh, Mum! You're too kind. Tenner? That's a bit much, isn’t it? She probably just wanted attention. Well, it was either that or listen to her complaining for another half an hour. My feet were killing me. And then young Kevin, bless him, flooded the entire patio section trying to water the plants. Oh dear! Was everything okay? Aye, just a bit of a panic. He got right flustered, poor lad. Manager had to send for maintenance. Honestly, it was chaos. But the chrysanthemums are lovely this year, they're really selling well. Good to hear something’s going right. So, any plans for the weekend? Are you still going to Auntie Brenda's on Sunday? I am. She's been on at me for weeks about needing help with her tablet. Says she can't work the email and is worried about scammers. Honestly, she’d believe anything. Poor Auntie Brenda. Maybe I could come with you? I’m quite good with tech. Oh, that would be lovely, actually. You’re a whiz with those things.

Honestly, the week’s been a blur. Mum’s operation went okay, thankfully. They said it was more complicated than they initially thought, but they got everything they needed to get out. Oh, bless her. That's good to hear, even if it was a bit tricky. How is she feeling now? Still in hospital? She’s home, but massively tired. And sore, obviously. She’s having to sleep downstairs, which she hates. It’s just… a lot. And then, on top of that, Leo’s been a nightmare at school. Oh, that boy. What’s he been up to now? Detention. Again. Apparently, he was disrupting the class, arguing with the teacher… the usual. Honestly, I’m at my wit’s end. He says the teacher is picking on him, but… They always say that, don't they? Though, teachers can be a bit… heavy-handed sometimes. Is it just one teacher, or is it happening in all his classes? It seems to be mainly Mr. Henderson, the history teacher. He’s a bit old school, very strict. Leo just… winds him up. I had a meeting with the school this morning, and they suggested we might need to look into some counselling. Counselling might be a good idea. It’s worth exploring, isn't it? At least to find out what’s going on. Is Lily okay? Is she getting caught in the crossfire? She's trying to stay out of it, bless her, but it’s hard. She’s worried about Leo, and she’s got her own stuff to deal with, you know? Preparing for her GCSEs. It's just a constant juggling act. It is, isn't it? Being a mum is never ending. Anyway, enough about my chaotic family! How are things with you? You mentioned you were going to visit Sarah last weekend? Oh, it was lovely. Sarah and the kids are doing really well. Little Ethan's growing like a weed. She's thinking of moving though. Moving? Where to? Over towards Stamford. She says it’s a bit quieter, better schools. It's a shame, I'll miss her being so close. We always used to meet up for coffee. Oh, I need to pop to the bank tomorrow. I completely forgot to sort out a direct debit for Mum's care. Oh dear. Don't forget, they're always quick to charge you penalties!

Right, honestly, last night was  mental . Proper slammed. Oh no, really? What happened? Usually Tuesdays are a bit quieter, aren't they? Usually, aye. But there was some sort of student event on, I think. Like, a society social or something. Suddenly, everyone descended on the pub at once. I was just running around like a headless chicken all night. Ugh, the worst. I can imagine. I’m so glad I just have lectures today. Relatively chill. Although Dr. Lewis threatened a pop quiz in History, so… never mind. Oh, brilliant. Sounds fun. I swear, if I have to pour another pint of Carling I’m gonna scream. It’s all anyone ever orders. Like, expand your horizons, people! Have a craft ale! Ha! You sound exactly like old man Hemmings down at the Black Horse. He’s always going on about proper real ale. Well, he’s not wrong, is he? Anyway, I’m saving up for that trip to Amsterdam, so I can’t exactly be picky. Every Carling poured is a step closer to stroopwafels and museums. Oh yeah! How’s the saving going? It’s not easy, is it, when you’re working part-time and trying to, you know,  live . It’s slow. Really slow. Landlord just gave me another shift, thankfully, a Saturday lunchtime. That should help a bit. Although Saturdays are always full of stag-dos and Hen parties, so… potentially equally chaotic. Ugh. Sounds… festive. I’ve been thinking about getting a job, actually. I’m a bit worried about balancing it with my degree, though. It’s a juggling act, definitely. But it’s good to have some money coming in, isn't it? I’ve been doing the pub for nearly four years now. It’s… a skill, I suppose. Dodging flying glasses, remembering complicated orders, pretending to be cheerful at 11pm on a Sunday… Definitely a skillset. I was thinking maybe something in a shop, or even tutoring. Less… physically demanding than pulling pints, I guess. Tutoring could be good. You’re brilliant at English Lit. You could make a fortune helping people with their essays. Ha! Maybe. I just don’t want to get completely overwhelmed. This degree is already stressful enough. And I need to actually  enjoy  some of my uni life, you know? Totally. Work-life balance is a myth, though, isn’t it? Especially when "life" includes trying to afford a holiday to Amsterdam.

Right, so I was thinking, actually getting away from it all this year. Proper getaway. Not just a day trip to Blackpool. Blackpool? Oh, don't even start. Remember last time we tried that team-building exercise there? Nearly lost poor old Mr. Henderson on the Pleasure Beach. Thought he’d gone for a final ride on the Big One, turned out he was just queuing for a stick of rock. Oh, that man. Always a bit of a wanderer, wasn't he? No, a proper holiday is what’s needed. I’m dreaming of Galway again. Just sitting in a pub, listening to the music. Bliss. Galway’s lovely. A bit… wet, though, isn’t it? I’m leaning towards somewhere hotter. Maybe the Greek Islands? Santorini, perhaps. All those whitewashed buildings… Instagram gold. Santorini sounds nice, but expensive. I was looking at Croatia. Split, specifically. Apparently, it’s got Diocletian’s Palace. That’s a bit of history for you, eh? Always good for justifying the cost. "Educational holiday," I'll tell the wife. Educational? You’ll be spending most of your time trying to find the best gelato place, Mark. Be honest. A man needs his priorities. Though, the Palace  is  fascinating. Apparently, people still live within the walls. Can you imagine? “Excuse me, sir, could you move your laundry? I’m trying to admire a Roman ruin.” Oh, the cheek! That's brilliant. I was thinking of taking a bus tour around Connemara. Saw a lovely picture of Kylemore Abbey. It looks just like a castle out of a fairy tale. You'll need wellies, Nora. Connemara is proper bogland. More sheep than people, I’d wager. Speaking of sheep, my sister went to New Zealand last year. Said it was overrun with the things. Apparently, they block the roads. She had to wait twenty minutes while a farmer herded them across! Twenty minutes? That’s outrageous! You’d never get away with that in Manchester. People would be honking their horns and getting terribly agitated. Ah, New Zealand... Now that’s a place I'd like to see. Though, I'm not sure my knees would hold up to all that hiking. I'd be needing a mobility scooter. Don’t knock the mobility scooter, Nora! They're making them look rather chic these days. Some come with cup holders. And Bluetooth speakers. You could have a party on one.

Honestly, that was a terrible challenge. Absolutely shocking. You’d think a professional footballer could actually  jump . Harsh. He went up for it. Just… misjudged it slightly. Probably thinking about his lunch. His lunch? What’s that got to do with anything? You don't need to be thinking about your lunch when you’re trying to win a header! Well, you know. Fuel. Performance. Maybe he had a particularly heavy burger before the game. It’d weigh you down, wouldn’t it? A heavy burger?! You think Premier League footballers are fueled by burgers? They’ve got nutritionists, diet plans… I’m just saying, a cheeky Nando’s doesn’t hurt anyone. Remember that time we tried to recreate the peri-peri sauce? Disaster. Don’t remind me. The kitchen smelled of chili for a week. And it tasted nothing like the real thing. Still, better than that greasy takeaway we had last Tuesday. What  was  that place anyway? "Burger Bliss"? Don't ask. It was a moment of weakness. I was stressed about the coding not working and needed…comfort. Comfort food gone wrong. That's a dangerous combination. They should have a warning label on those places. "May induce regret and heartburn." Ooh, good pass! See, that’s what happens when you don't weigh yourself down with excessive processed food. Agile, quick thinking... You're attributing footballing prowess to diet now? That's a stretch, even for you. No, but I’m saying there’s a correlation! It’s science. You need energy, you need to be light on your feet… proper fuel. Not a double cheeseburger with extra bacon. Right, well, I’m just saying, sometimes a double cheeseburger with extra bacon is exactly what the doctor ordered. Especially after a long day of…research managing. Fair enough. But don't come crying to me when you can't outrun a slightly determined pensioner. I can definitely outrun a determined pensioner. Now, focus! This game is getting interesting... Does this fit the context and relationship you were hoping for? I can continue the conversation or adjust it if needed. Certainly, here is my answer: They're just passing it back and forth. It's so frustrating to watch! Honestly, you'd think they'd try and actually  do  something with the ball. They're working the space, building the play. It's tactical. You've got to appreciate the strategy.

Honestly, Mum, the traffic getting over here was a nightmare. Roadworks on the M56 again. You’d think they’d finish it by now, wouldn’t you? M56… always trouble on that road. Used to be fields, you know. Just fields between here and Manchester. Could cycle anywhere. Oh, you and your cycling, Mum. You were fearless. Remember that time you cycled all the way to Blackpool with your friend Elsie? Blackpool! Oh, aye. Elsie and I. Thought we were the bee’s knees. Packed a picnic, little flask of tea. Didn’t tell anyone where we were going, mind. Your Grandad nearly had a fit when we got back. Said we were lucky we hadn’t been kidnapped! Sounds… adventurous. You weren’t allowed much freedom, were you? Freedom? In my day, freedom was a cup of tea and a good book. We didn’t  need  all this… fuss. Still, it sounds nice. We're always rushing around. I saw that new Bond film last night, though. Brilliant. Bit long, but brilliant. Oh yeah? I’ve been meaning to go. Is it as good as everyone says? Definitely. Proper action, good story. Though, honestly, Daniel Craig’s getting a bit old for all the running and jumping. Bond… They keep changing him, don’t they? Never as good as Sean Connery. Now  he  was a Bond. You always say that, Grandma. It’s true! And he had manners. These new ones just swagger about. No respect. Speaking of respect, has your cousin David fixed that car of his yet? The red one? Oh, that’s a disaster. Apparently, it was a faulty sensor. Cost him a fortune. Said he’s thinking of getting a bike. A bike? David? He wouldn’t last five minutes. He’s about as coordinated as a newborn giraffe. I know! But he’s saying it’s better for the environment. And cheaper. More likely he’s skint. Work’s been slow lately. I’ve been putting in ridiculous hours on this project. Trying to get this new software implemented. Total chaos. Software? What's all that about? Give me a good cookbook any day. I made a lovely Victoria sponge yesterday. Would you like a piece? Oh, yes please! Your Victoria sponge is the best, Mum. I’d love some, actually. Stress baking is a life skill, you know. Honestly, the things I deal with at work... it's like herding cats.

Honestly, Leo, you've barely touched your pancake! It’s Pancake Day! You made a wish  with  it – that’s the rule! It's yummy, Mummy, but I'm full now. Mine’s gone! Can I have some sprinkles now? Please? Yes, you can have sprinkles, darling. A little bit. And Leo, just  one  more bite. It’s a waste if you don’t finish it. Honestly, sometimes I think children in my class eat more than you do! And they don’t even  have  pancake on Pancake Day. Why not? Well, some families don’t have much money, sweetheart, and they can’t always afford special treats. It's just...sad. Makes you appreciate what we have, doesn’t it? Sad. It is. Right, sprinkles are happening. Anyway, how was school today? Did you both have a good day? I did a really good painting of a dinosaur! Miss Jones said it was the best one. Oh, fantastic! I bet it was! And you, Elsie? Anything exciting? We had assembly. And Mrs. Peterson told us a story about Green Knowe. It was spooky. Oh, Green Knowe! That's a lovely story, isn't it? All those children visiting the past… it makes you think about how much things change, and how quickly everything goes by. Makes  me  feel old! Mummy, when we grow up, will we be old? Eventually, yes, you will. But not for a very long time! You’ll have lots of adventures first. We're thinking of going to the Science Museum this weekend, aren't we? Yay! Can we see the dinosaurs? Absolutely. And maybe we can go to that festival at the Festival Hall next week. They’re doing something with puppets. Puppets! Yes! Now, before we get too carried away planning fun things, have you both brushed your teeth properly? And washed your hands? I saw chocolate on your face, Leo! I washed my hands! I brushed mine. Good. Because we are going to Paris soon, remember? And we don’t want any germs ruining our trip. I’m thinking next half term. Paris! Will we see the Eiffel Tower? Of course! And we can eat croissants and go on a boat on the river. It will be lovely. Although, knowing you two, you’ll probably just want to go to the beach, won’t you? The beach is best! We can build sandcastles!

This is actually really good. I was worried ordering from here, their online reviews are…mixed. Mixed is putting it mildly. I saw someone claim their chow mein tasted exclusively of despair. Despair? That’s… a strong culinary critique. Honestly, I’m just glad it arrived in under an hour. Remember that time we ordered Indian and it took two and a half? Oh god, the Great Curry Wait of ‘21. I was starting to suspect the delivery driver had decided to  become  a curry chef. Seriously! I was pacing. Anyway, this egg fried rice is surprisingly decent. Yeah, I’ll give them that. Although, it does taste a bit… suspiciously yellow. Don't look a gift horse, or suspiciously yellow rice, in the mouth. So, anyone catch the news today? More depressing stuff as usual. Briefly. Something about another politician being investigated. Honestly, it's just a relentless cycle at this point. It feels like you can’t trust anyone. Exactly. Remember old Mr. Henderson? He used to say politicians were all the same, just different shades of grey. He was a character, old Mr. Henderson. Always muttering about Bob the Builder and claiming he knew the secret to a perfect lawn. And perpetually offering everyone digestive biscuits. I miss his biscuits. Speaking of missing people, have you heard anything from Liam? I haven’t seen him post on social media in ages. No, not since he went to that cricket match last weekend. I messaged him, no reply. Hopefully, he’s just enjoying a digital detox. A digital detox? Liam? The guy who live-streamed himself making toast? I find that hard to believe. Maybe he finally realised he needed a break. Or maybe he’s gone off-grid to become a professional lawn enthusiast, inspired by Mr. Henderson. Now  that  would be a twist. We should probably check in with him properly though. It's just, he’s been a bit down lately, about… you know. Right. About Sarah. It’s awful what happened. That funeral was… something. Just so many people. It was. And so sad. She was way too young. I keep thinking about how much she loved terrible rom-coms. She truly did. We had a marathon the week before… watched five in a row. Pure cinematic trash. She had such a good spirit. Do you guys fancy going to the cinema next week? There’s that new sci-fi film everyone’s talking about.

Honestly, Old Man Hemmings next door… you wouldn’t believe what he tried to tell me this morning. He’s convinced Mrs. Peterson is secretly a spy. A spy? That woman? Goodness me. She can barely remember where she put her spectacles, let alone orchestrate international intrigue. It's probably just loneliness getting to him. He did lose his wife last year, didn’t he? Though, to be fair, she  was  rather secretive about her garden club meetings. That’s what I said! But no, apparently, she’s using the prize-winning marrows as a cover. A cover, I ask you! He was utterly serious. He said he’s been watching her… “for weeks,” he said. Reminds me of your Uncle Arthur. Used to be convinced the milkman was reporting back to the Soviets. Claimed the bottles were coded messages. Always drank his milk straight from the bottle, wouldn’t trust a glass. Oh, Arthur! We all used to tiptoe around him, afraid to say the wrong thing. So, what did you say to Mr. Hemmings? I just gently suggested he might be letting his imagination run away with him. He grumbled something about “young people these days” and went back inside. Honestly, he’s a sweet man, but… a bit. They’re all a bit, at that age. Memory starts to play tricks, and a bit of drama fills the void. It’s sad, really. Although, thinking about it, I rather liked Arthur's milk-from-the-bottle habit. Seemed rather… efficient. Efficient and slightly alarming. Speaking of efficiency, did you see that article about driverless cars? Apparently, they’re doing trials on the A38 now. I did! Terrifying, isn’t it? I can barely trust  people  to drive properly, let alone a computer. What if it malfunctions and just… goes rogue? Progress, my dear. Progress. They said the same about aeroplanes, you know. Remember when people thought flying was the height of recklessness? Now look at us, jetting off to Spain for a week with barely a thought. Though I must say, the queues at security are getting worse every year. That’s an understatement. Honestly, it's a nightmare. I was thinking about those scan-as-you-go things in supermarkets. Do you use those? I'm always too worried I'll accidentally scan something twice. I do! It makes such a difference, especially when you’ve got a full trolley.

Right, so, Chinese New Year! Did you two have fun at school making lanterns? Yeah! Mine was red and sparkly! And I drew a dragon on it! Mine was… blue. And my dragon had, like,  lots  of teeth. Scary teeth. Ooh, scary! Dragons are very important in Chinese New Year, aren’t they? They bring good luck. Did you learn about that? Miss Davies told us! Dragons fly in the sky and… and breathe fire! And they're really long! Longer than our garden! That’s right! They are very long. Speaking of the sky… what did you learn about in science today? Was it planets again? Yeah! Saturn has rings! And Jupiter has a big red spot! Miss Thompson said the red spot is a storm! A  really  big storm! It’s been happening for ages. Wow, that’s incredible.
