It’s amazing how long those storms can last. Right, I think I smell something burning… oh dear. The spring rolls! Spring rolls! Are we having Chinese food for Chinese New Year? I love spring rolls! Especially with the sweet chilli sauce! You are both obsessed with that sauce! Yes, we're having spring rolls, noodles, and a little bit of everything. It's not  proper  Chinese food, I know, but it's a start! Can I help set the table? I can put the chopsticks out! I wanna get the plates! The red ones! Because red is a lucky colour! Excellent! Teamwork makes the dream work. Now, after dinner, how’s the practicing going? Are you still enjoying piano, Leo? It’s okay. Mr. Peterson makes me do scales. Scales are boring. I know they can be, but they're important! It's like learning your ABCs before you can write a story. And Maya, are you excited for your drum lesson tomorrow? Yes! I'm learning a new beat! It’s really loud! Oh, wonderful. I’m sure the neighbours will love that! And what about aerial hoop on Saturday? Are you still brave enough? It’s scary, but fun. I can almost do a roll now! That’s amazing! You're getting so strong. Oh, and I nearly forgot! You two were telling me about a film you want to watch, wasn’t it? Something with Barbie?  Barbie and the Great Adventure ! It’s got horses and a secret kingdom! And Barbie has to save everyone! It's so good!

Honestly, this is… bliss. Proper bliss. Needed this. Rome is doing bits, innit? It really is. Sun’s actually out, which is a miracle considering the forecast. And this little bar is perfect – not rammed, good vibes… and the Aperol Spritz is  chefs kiss . It's lovely, yeah. Way better than that AirBnB though. Seriously, the photos were…optimistic. I thought we were getting a balcony overlooking the Colosseum, and it was overlooking a bin alley. Fair dinkum? A bin alley? That’s rough, Rach. I thought you were the AirBnB queen. You always find the hidden gems. I  usually  do! I think I got caught out by the hype. Everyone raves about Rome AirBnBs, I just… trusted too much. Lesson learned. Right, so, dinner. We sticking with the plan to wander around Trastevere? I heard there's some proper authentic stuff over there. Yeah, I'm up for that. I did a little research – there’s a place called Roma Sparita, apparently their Cacio e Pepe is legendary. We  have  to try it. Oh, I've heard of that place! It’s supposed to be tiny and booked solid, but we can give it a shot, right? Maybe if we go early? Early’s good. I’m still adjusting to the Italian timeframe, everything happens… later. Like everything. It’s a vibe, but my internal clock is confused. Tell me about it. I tried to order a coffee at like, ten past seven this morning, and the barista looked at me like I’d asked him to solve world peace. Oh, bless him. They take their coffee seriously here. You’ve gotta commit to the whole ritual. No grabbing a takeaway latte on the go. Speaking of serious… my mum keeps texting me asking if I'm speaking Italian yet. She's convinced I should be fluent after two days. Oh, mums. Ours is the same. She called yesterday to ask if I'd learned to haggle in Italian. Apparently, that's the key to a successful holiday. Haggle? I tried to buy a postcard this morning and completely butchered the pronunciation of ‘prego’. The shopkeeper just looked… amused. They probably charged me extra. You'll get there. It's a tricky language. I did a bit at uni, but mostly I just remember how to order wine. Which, let's be honest, is the most important skill. Exactly!

Honestly, the planning for Chloe’s hen do is  stressful . I feel like I'm her mum, not a friend! Oh, tell me about it! Whose bright idea was it to make personalised bunting? It's going to take forever. It's Sarah, isn't it? She always goes overboard. Remember her 30th? The glitter…  everywhere . Oh god, the glitter. We were finding it for weeks! But Chloe will love the bunting, she’s really into that crafty stuff. I’m more worried about the escape room. Apparently, it's really hard. Hard is good! We need something challenging. Although, knowing the group, someone will probably start panicking and yelling within five minutes. Probably Jess. She gets super competitive. Remember that game of charades at New Year’s? She nearly threw the TV remote. Classic Jess. I volunteered to do the cake, by the way. I’m thinking maybe a lemon drizzle? Or something with raspberries? Lemon drizzle is always a winner! Oh, and you  have  to make those little sugar flowers you did for my birthday. They were gorgeous. Ooh, yes! Those were amazing. I'm rubbish at baking, so I’m happy to leave the cake to you. I've been put on decorations duty. Which, as we established, involves a lot of bunting. I’m handling the playlist. I'm trying to get a good mix of cheesy pop and stuff everyone knows. Any requests? 90s classics are essential! And definitely some Spice Girls. Oh, and anything by Destiny’s Child! Perfect for belting out on the dance floor. Right, noted. Okay, so we've got bunting, cake, playlist, escape room... have we sorted out a photographer? I asked Liam's cousin, he does wedding photography, and he said he'd do a few hours for a good price. He’s coming. Perfect! That's one less thing to worry about. I'm a bit worried about Auntie Maureen though. She promised to come but she's always a bit...much. Oh dear. True. We might need to strategically position ourselves away from her. We could distract her with the cake? She loves a good slice of lemon drizzle. Good thinking! Right, I'm going to quickly check on the venue. I need to confirm the booking and make sure they've got enough space for our chaos. I’m off to the supermarket to gather supplies for the cake.

Right, so you reckon this much chilli is good for a curry for four? Seems… ambitious. Trust me. It's not that bad. Unless you're, like,  really  sensitive. Remember that time you had that vindaloo in uni and spent the next hour regretting every life choice? Don't remind me. That wasn’t a vindaloo, it was a weapon. I swear the chef was actively trying to harm me. Honestly, I felt sick for a full day. This feels different though, you’re actually, you know, cooking properly. Not just throwing a load of things in and hoping for the best. Hey! My student cooking was perfectly adequate. Relatively speaking. Anyway, this chilli is mild in comparison. Speaking of sick, how are you feeling? You sounded a bit rough on the phone yesterday. Just a bit of a bug, I think. Woke up feeling dreadful, achy and all that. Definitely couldn’t face work. Slept most of the day. Still a bit knackered, to be honest. Probably needed the sleep anyway. Been running myself ragged with that commission. Yeah, you were complaining about the deadlines. Seriously though, look after yourself. Don’t push it. Remember what happened last time you tried to work through a cold? Ended up in bed for a week. Point taken. This is why I have a brother who's a sensible English teacher. You'd be terrible at art though. Too…precise. And you’d be terrible at explaining grammar to a class of teenagers. Trust me, it's a skillset. Anyway, hotel situation sorted for Barcelona? You said you were looking at places. Yeah, booked it actually. Found a little place near the Gothic Quarter. Looks alright, bit basic, but it’s close to everything. And surprisingly cheap. Always worry though, you know? Hotels. Bed bugs, dodgy plumbing, weird smells… You’re such a worrier. It’ll be fine. Barcelona’s amazing. You'll have a blast. Just… maybe pack some disinfectant wipes. For your peace of mind. Good shout. Right, shall we get this onion diced? I’m suddenly feeling a bit peckish, despite feeling awful yesterday. This curry better be worth it. It will be. And before you ask, yes, I’ve already chopped the garlic. I’m not a complete monster. Though, I am considering adding a  tiny  bit more chilli… Don’t you dare. I’m already bracing myself for a mild burn.

Right, shopping list. We need milk, definitely. And…oh, biscuits. Chocolate digestives, your favourite. And bread – a proper loaf, not that sliced stuff. Ooh, lovely. And some apples, I fancy a baked apple later. Do you remember Mrs. Higgins from primary school? She used to make the most amazing apple crumble. Mrs. Higgins… vaguely. She was the art teacher, wasn’t she? Always covered in paint. She made us do the most awful papier-mâché. I remember being utterly disgusted with the mess. Oh, she loved her papier-mâché! And the glitter. Everywhere, glitter. Honestly, it took weeks to get it out of the classroom. Speaking of the classroom, do you remember those calendars they used to sell, with little fob bits on? Each month had a different one. I always collected them. Oh, the plastic fobs! Yes! I had a whole string of them. Usually animals, weren’t they? Or little cartoon characters. I wonder what happened to those. Probably thrown away. Me too. It's funny the things you remember, isn’t it? Remember young Timmy Bates playing hockey? He was dreadful! All legs and no coordination. He always needed help with his boots. Oh, dreadful! He'd fall over his own feet. And that new ‘sports day’ initiative wasn't very effective. I remember Miss Davies trying to explain the importance of teamwork. It all fell apart when little Jenny Smith started crying because she didn’t win the egg and spoon race. Oh, she was a drama queen, that one! It's amazing how much primary school stays with you. It forms you, doesn’t it? I sometimes wonder what direction my students went in. Did they fulfill their potential? It’s interesting thinking about what I’d study now, if I was going to University. I think I’d love to do something with sound recording. All those old radio programs… capturing and preserving that. That's fascinating. Though you always had a knack for history. Social history, specifically. Really digging into how people  lived . That’s true. But I find the technology side appealing too. Imagine, going back and restoring recordings from the 1920s... It's practically archaeology, isn't it? It is. Speaking of technology, you’re getting rid of that old computer, aren't you? The one you bought back in… what was it, ‘98? Yes! It’s ancient. It barely runs anymore.

So, Old Man Hemmings next door, apparently he’s been complaining about the lights on the barn. Says they’re too bright. Oh, really? He’s always moaning, isn’t he? Mum said he complained about her hanging washing out on a Sunday! Honestly, some people. It’s a barn, for goodness sake! What’s he expect, darkness? Though, I suppose it  is  quite a bright light. Did you get a chance to talk to him, David? I did. Popped over with a mince pie, tried to be neighbourly. He grumbled on for about ten minutes about light pollution and the disruption to the badgers. Badgers! As if a barn light is going to bother a badger. Oh, Hemmings. He sounds… delightful. It's good you took a mince pie, though. Defuses things, usually. Absolutely. Works wonders. Although, knowing him, he probably checked for walnuts before accepting it. He’s allergic, you know. I did! Made sure they were walnut-free. Learned that lesson last Christmas. He practically had an anaphylactic shock over a trifle. Oh dear! That sounds dramatic. How’s the decorating going, by the way? Have you managed to tackle the living room yet? Slowly. Very slowly. I tried to put up that shelf yesterday, you know, the big one for all my books? And it kept falling down. Nearly took out the cat. Oh, David! You and DIY are not a good combination. Remember the time you tried to fix the garden gate, and it ended up hanging sideways? Don’t remind me. That was a disaster. Ended up calling Phil in the end. He’s the only one who can actually wield a screwdriver properly around here. Phil’s a lifesaver, isn’t he? Speaking of which, did you manage to find that local walking group I told you about? The one that does the coastal path? I did! I emailed them. Apparently they meet every Saturday morning. Thinking of joining next week, try and get some fresh air. And get away from that blasted shelf. That sounds lovely. It’s such a beautiful coastline round here, you'll love it. Though, wrap up warm, it can get quite blustery. And don’t forget your walking boots! It can get muddy. I've been meaning to ask – have you tried the pub yet? The Badger’s Holt? Not yet, no. Been a bit busy unpacking and fighting with furniture.

Right, so I was scrolling through TikTok, yeah? And this advert pops up for these trainers, right? Absolutely mint. Like, proper retro Adidas. Oh yeah? What were they like? White with the blue stripes, classic. But get this, they were like, a hundred and fifty quid. A hundred and fifty! For trainers. Blimey. That  is  a bit steep, isn’t it? Especially when you can get decent ones in Sports Direct for half that. Exactly! I clicked on it, thinking maybe there's a sale or something, but nope. Full price. It's all these influencers, though, isn’t it? Wearing expensive stuff, making everyone want it. Definitely. It's the same with clothes. I saw someone on Instagram with this designer jacket… ridiculous price. I just showed Mam and she nearly choked. Haha! Mam would. She’s brilliant. Speaking of online stuff, I tried to apply for that job at Amazon again. Still? Did you hear anything back? Nah. Automated rejection email, like always. Says they've had loads of applicants. What's the point, honestly? It's all just robots reading CVs now. No one even looks at them properly. It’s awful, isn’t it? I was looking at internships for uni, and they all want like, five years’ experience. How can you get experience  without  an internship? It’s a catch-22. Seriously. They want you to be a fully qualified professional before you've even finished your A-Levels. I’m starting to think I should’ve just stuck to Playstation. At least I’m good at that. Don't say that! You’re way too clever to just… play games all day. Though, I wouldn't mind a gaming session later, to be fair. I'm knackered after revision. Yeah, I’m up for that. What are you watching on telly these days? Anything good? I've been hooked on that new true crime documentary on Netflix. It’s about this guy who… oh, I won’t spoil it. It’s proper gripping. Ooh, I love a good true crime doc. Send me the link. I need something to binge when I’m inevitably rejected from another ten jobs. Will do. Actually, talking of Netflix, have you seen what they’re doing with the password sharing? Oh aye, I read about that. Charging extra? Mental. As if they don’t make enough money already. I know, right?

Right, well, the central heating’s still playing up. I’ve had a fiddle, but it’s one of those things, isn’t it? You touch one wire and three others go wrong. Honestly. Could spend a fortune calling someone out, though. Sounds about right. You’d think with a new-build it wouldn't be so temperamental already. What did they say when you first moved in about the warranty? Warranty ran out last month. Typical. And of course, it started acting up  the  week after. Anyway, lunchtime. What’s everyone fancy? I was thinking soup… bit of bread? Soup sounds lovely, actually. A bit of crusty bread would be perfect. Though, don't go making a huge pot, alright? I’m trying to be good. Good? What, a sudden attack of healthy eating? Well, relatively! I’m walking that bit of the coastal path on Saturday, remember? Need the energy, but not… too  much energy. Oh, that sounds brilliant! How far are you planning on going? Just Hartland Quay to Welcombe Mouth. Roughly six miles, I think. Should be manageable, and the views are spectacular. Six miles, eh? You’re a braver woman than me. I’d be needing a lie-down after two. Remember your Uncle George trying to do those walks? Ended up needing an ambulance that time. Oh, God, yes! The one where he insisted he was ‘perfectly fine’ and then collapsed halfway up a hill? That’s the one! Stubborn as a mule, that man. Still, he lived to a good age, didn’t he? Ninety-two. Though, if he'd listened to his body… It's funny, isn't it? How long things last. My mum’s washing machine is older than I am, and still going strong. Whereas, Dad’s Volvo packed it in at twelve years. Twelve years! Said it was ‘built to last,’ he did. I know! Ours is a Ford, and I’m already bracing myself for it to give up the ghost any minute. It’s seven now. Speaking of things giving up the ghost, we need a new sofa. This armchair’s alright for me, but you two need something comfortable. We could have a look at that furniture shop in Holsworthy on Monday? Oh, that’s a good idea! They had some nice-looking things when I popped in last week. Though, the prices… a bit steep, weren’t they?

Right, that was a good lasagne. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, thanks. It was mostly the passata, I think. Found a new brand, proper Italian stuff. Makes all the difference. You seemed to enjoy it, you barely spoke a word while you were eating. That’s high praise, coming from you. It just… hit the spot. Long day. Honestly, this research is slowly killing me. Oh, still battling the data demons? What’s the issue this time? It's just… nothing is  significant . Everything is hovering around the .06 mark. It’s infuriating. All these hours, all this effort, and I’m getting… suggestive trends. Not proper results. Ugh, that’s the worst. The grey area. You’re definitely not the first person to fall into that pit. Have you spoken to Professor Davies? Yeah. He just said, “Robustness checks, more participants, consider alternative analytical approaches.” Groundbreaking advice, really. I already  am  doing all of those things! He's good at the vague encouragement, isn't he? Classic academic. Look, it’s probably just a blip. Sometimes it takes a bit of tinkering. You’ll get there. You always do. Easy for you to say, Assessment Manager extraordinaire. Your data probably jumps out and screams its conclusions at you. Don’t be ridiculous! Try wading through thousands of anonymised student assessments, looking for patterns in behaviour. It's less screaming, more… a very faint whimper that requires a lot of statistical coaxing. Still sounds marginally less soul-crushing than what I’m doing. How’s work, anyway? Any dramas in the education world? Oh, you know. The usual. Pressure to raise attainment, funding cuts, stressed-out teachers. We're rolling out a new intervention program for Year 7s who are falling behind in reading. It's… ambitious. Sounds it. Is it actually going to make a difference, or just tick boxes? Honestly? Probably a bit of both. But you have to start somewhere, right? And I genuinely think some of the one-to-one support will help. Though I did have a headteacher question whether we could measure the “soft skills” gained through it. Oh dear. Not that again. The obsession with quantifiable results. Exactly! It's like they think you can put joy or resilience into a spreadsheet. Anyway, enough work talk. We  are  supposed to be enjoying a relaxing evening. Have you thought about what we’re doing this weekend?

Honestly, the price of everything is just… ridiculous now, isn’t it? Even cat food. Jasper’s demanding the salmon pate, the little monster. He knows a good life, that cat. Still, you’ve got to remember what things were like when we were kids, though. My mum used to tell stories about rationing. Proper hardship. Gran always says the same thing, about making do and mending. It makes you feel a bit guilty complaining about petrol prices, doesn't it? Guilty? Nah. Times change. I remember petrol being, what, 30p a gallon? Now it's nearly two quid a litre! You gotta acknowledge the difference. And Jasper deserves his salmon pate. He’s a handsome feline. He  is  rather magnificent. Though, he does look at you with a very judgemental expression if you offer him the cheaper stuff. Reminds me of my Uncle Barry, actually. Always knew exactly what he wanted. Speaking of judgemental, did anyone else notice how meticulously David arranged his peas on his plate earlier? Like he was building a tiny fortress. Oh my god, yes! It was a work of art. I was trying not to stare. Is he always like that? Always. He’s a stickler for order. Says it calms him. Funny, considering his job, isn't it? Dealing with… chaos, basically. He gets it from his mother. She wouldn’t let a wonky picture frame survive for five minutes. Everything had to be  just so . It’s fascinating, isn’t it, how things get passed down through families? Like, I’m left-handed, and apparently, my great-grandmother was too. They used to think it was a sign of… well, something bad. Oh, I remember that! They used to make children write with their right hand. It’s barbaric. Poor things. Apparently, there's a genetic component. Though, you get all sorts of theories. I read something about it being linked to language skills… That’s interesting! I'm right-handed, but I’ve always been quite good with words. Maybe there's something to it. Though, maybe I'm just good at making things up for a living. You’re a copywriter, love. Making things up  is  your job. Remember young Timmy Williams at school? Absolute terror, couldn’t sit still for a minute. His mum swore he’d grow up to be a criminal. Became a brilliant architect. Go figure.

Honestly, this cake is amazing, ANON. You’ve really outdone yourself. What did you put in it? It’s…so moist. Oh, it’s just a Victoria sponge, lass. Nothing fancy. A good dollop of jam, though. Can’t skimp on the jam. Reminds me of my mother’s. She used to make a cracking Victoria sponge. Though hers always had a bit too much sherry in the filling, if you ask me. Nearly knocked you sideways. Sherry in a Victoria sponge? That’s…unexpected. Well, it was the 50s, lad. Everything had sherry in it! Or gin. They thought it improved things. Not always, mind. Though a gin and it in a hot summer’s day…that’s not bad. It sounds like you’ve done a bit of travelling in your time, ANON. You always have the best stories. Where was your favourite place you’ve ever been? Oh, travelling. Aye, I did a bit with BT. Used to send me all over the place fixing cables. Didn’t feel like travelling back then, more like work. But I suppose I saw a fair bit. Italy was lovely. Rome. Florence. The food, of course. Couldn’t get enough of the pasta. Real pasta, mind, not that dried stuff. I was in Italy last year, near Cinque Terre. The food  was  incredible. I tried to replicate a pesto I had there when I got back but it just wasn’t the same. Something about the basil, I think. Ooh, Cinque Terre! I’ve seen pictures. It looks stunning. It’s on my list. That’s a bonny spot, that is. Though a bit crowded for my liking these days. I went to Naples once. Now  that  was an experience. A bit chaotic, but full of life. And the pizza! Honestly, a proper Neapolitan pizza is something else. None of that thin crust nonsense. I’ve heard Naples is…intense. I’m not sure I’d be brave enough. I tend to prefer somewhere a bit more…organized. I get that. I’m a bit of a planner myself. Though I do like the idea of just wandering around and getting lost. That's what I'd like to do in Japan. Japan, eh? Now that's a long way to go to get lost. I always wanted to see Japan. Never quite made it. Too expensive back then, I think. And the flights were a right palaver.

Right, so I was thinking about the Baudrillard lecture for Tuesday. I’m still not entirely convinced the students are grasping the concept of simulacra and simulation. They keep getting it confused with just…representation. Yeah, it's a tough one. It’s abstract. Maybe we need to bring in more contemporary examples? They all seem to be obsessed with TikTok, could we deconstruct a few popular trends through that lens? Ooh, that’s a good shout. Actually, really good. That might click. I was trying to use Disneyland as an example, but I think it just sounded like I was bashing Disney to a generation who grew up with it. Probably not the best approach. TikTok’s a safer bet. Speaking of things people are obsessed with, have you seen that new cooking show, ‘Flavour Frontier’? No! Is it any good? I haven't had much time for TV lately, marking's been relentless. It’s fantastic. It’s this chef travelling around rural China, learning traditional recipes from village cooks. The food looks incredible. And the presenter is genuinely enthusiastic, not one of these overly dramatic ones. Sounds perfect. We need something relaxing to watch. I’ve been dreaming about proper dumplings all week. This canteen food is…functional. Functional is being generous. Honestly, I’m starting to miss a good Sunday roast. Remember Mum’s Yorkshire puddings? Don't even. I can practically smell them. Anyway, back to Baudrillard. I was also thinking of showing a short clip from ‘The Matrix’. That visual demonstration of reality being a construct might help. That’s clever! That could really solidify it for them. We could then spend ten minutes debriefing - what are the ‘real’ things in their lives? What’s manufactured? Exactly. And then for Thursday’s seminar on Poststructuralism, I’m trying to work out how to make Derrida less…intimidating. The students look utterly terrified when I mention ‘deconstruction’. Right, because it sounds like you're just dismantling everything! Perhaps focus on the idea of challenging assumptions rather than ‘destroying’ meaning? Frame it as a freeing process? That's a good way of putting it. ‘Freeing’. I like that. We’re basically teaching them to be critical thinkers, aren't we? It feels like an uphill battle some days. It is. But they're bright students. They’ll get there. Oh, and I managed to find a decent source for Sichuan peppercorns.

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me round the bend. It makes a lovely cup, when it  works , but half the time it just splutters and complains. Feels like a right faff just to get a decent brew. Is it the descaling again? You were saying last week it needed doing. Descaling, cleaning, praying to the coffee gods. It’s all been tried, dear. I think it’s just… temperamental. Like someone we know.  looks pointedly at Speaker_3   chuckles  Now, now, Mary. Temperamental? I’m simply… discerning. And I’ve offered to have a look at it, haven’t I? I used to be quite good with mechanical things, you know. Before they all became digital monstrosities. That's kind of you, David. Though, honestly, sometimes I think it’s just cheaper to buy a new one. Speaking of costs…have you two got any further on sorting out quotes for the storage unit? We need to get a move on with clearing out the spare room before the builders arrive. Oh, don’t even mention it. The prices are outrageous! They’re charging a fortune just to store a few boxes. It’s daylight robbery. I mean, what are they going to do with it all, store it in Fort Knox? It’s supply and demand, Mary. There's a lot of people downsizing these days. And storage is convenient. Though, I agree, it's expensive. I got a quote from that place near Penrith - it was slightly less, but then you have to factor in the travel time if we need anything. I had a look online as well. There’s one in Carlisle, but the reviews aren’t great. Apparently, they’ve had a few break-ins. Break-ins?! Absolutely not. I’m not risking my grandmother’s china being stolen. That’s going to stay with us, even if we have to stack boxes around it. Sensible. Though, you know, it's all a bit depressing, isn’t it? Having to get rid of things. It feels like a… a letting go of a whole life. It’s just stuff, David. And we’re not getting rid of  everything , just things we don’t use anymore. That’s what I keep telling myself, dear. Easier said than done though, isn't it? It’s funny, you spend years accumulating things, and then suddenly you’re trying to figure out how to minimize your existence.

Right, so, like, seriously, you’ve been calling me ‘Barnaby’ all week? Barnaby?! It just… slipped out! You said your middle name was Bernard didn’t you? And Barnaby felt… right. It suits you. It’s a bit posh, innit? Barnaby. He’s more of a ‘Dave’ if you ask me. Mate, both pretty average names. Honestly, I reckon you could pull off Reginald. Reginalddd? Stop. You're winding me up. Anyway, enough about my alleged pseudonym. What river even  is  the Lea? It sounds… sad. Sad? The Lea? It's historically important! Loads of Roman stuff, mills, industry… It's mostly just canal boats now, isn't it? All those colourful narrowboats chugging along. Saw one the other day, looked like someone's living room on water. Yeah, proper bohemian. Reminds me of the Hawkesbury River back home, but, like, ten times more polluted. Oh god, polluted. Speaking of questionable things, anyone know anything about kosher law? Old Man Hemmings at the market was going on about it this morning. Something about not mixing meat and dairy. Oh, yeah. It’s a set of dietary laws in Judaism. Like, no pork, shellfish… and definitely no mixing milk and meat in the same meal. It’s pretty strict. Sounds intense. Can’t even have a cheeseburger? Seriously? That’s… restrictive. Though I’ve never understood the fascination with cheeseburgers anyway. Give me a decent lamb souvlaki any day. Okay, we're getting sidetracked. Cheeseburgers are a sacred cow, mate. But back to Hemmings… he was convinced his pickled onions weren't kosher. Which, honestly, seemed a bit dramatic. Probably just an excuse to charge extra. He's a shrewd one, Hemmings. Has anyone been to that new club, ‘The Void’? Supposedly the sound system is mental. Heard about it. Bit too much techno for me, I reckon. I'm more of a reggae kinda guy. The Void… sounds like a microwave. Which, speaking of, is anyone else deeply suspicious of microwaves? Like, what  happens  inside those things? It heats food, Dave. That’s what happens. Through radiation, but it's not  dangerous  radiation. They ruin everything. Pizza tastes like rubber after a microwave. True. Though they’re pretty handy for reheating a leftover kebab. And honestly, after a night at ‘The Void’, a kebab is essential. Okay, okay, point taken. Speaking of leftovers… anyone fancy an Italian tonight? There's that place on Brick Lane, Lorenzo’s, does a pretty good carbonara.

Honestly, Tinder’s been a right disaster zone lately. Just endless photos of lads holding fish. What is  with  the fish? Oh, don’t even get me started. It’s the new peacocking, apparently. Showing off their… fishing skills. As if. I swiped left on three in a row yesterday. Three? I swiped left on, like, seven. One was wearing a full suit of armour. A  full  suit. Said it was for LARPing. No way! That’s… dedicated. Though, slightly terrifying. Did you match with anyone decent, Liv? Decent is a strong word. I matched with a guy who, in his bio, literally just wrote “I like breathing.” Groundbreaking stuff. Breathing! Seriously? Are people just giving up trying? I’m starting to think I should just delete it. It’s more depressing than useful. Don’t delete it! Think of the entertainment value, if nothing else. Remember Mark from last month? The one who said his spirit animal was a garden gnome? Oh god,  Mark . He messaged me too. Kept asking if I wanted to build a miniature village with him. Speaking of… have you guys heard back about housemates for next year yet? I’m starting to panic. Honestly, living with Sarah last year was… an experience. No news here. My mum’s already started sending me links to flat viewings in Wakefield. Like I’m going to move back home after the first term! My flat last year was a disaster. It smelled permanently of pot noodles. And Liam wouldn’t flush the toilet.  Wouldn’t . Ugh, sounds awful. I’m hoping to find a house with people who actually clean. Is that too much to ask? Seriously, I need less chaos in my life. Uni's stressful enough already. Totally. I just want a functioning kitchen and someone who won’t leave dirty socks everywhere. Is that a dream? It shouldn’t be! Honestly, I’m thinking of just going for a studio. Expensive, but at least no housemate dramas. Plus, full control of the thermostat. A studio? You'd go mental on your own! You need people around, even if they’re slightly weird. Remember when we all tried to learn to knit and failed spectacularly? Oh god, the yarn explosion. I'm still finding bits of wool in my bag. That was a good night, though. Even if none of us could make a scarf to save our lives.

Honestly, the state of it. Did you see Question Time last night? Utter shambles. Shambles is a polite word for it, Arthur. A right carry-on, that’s what it was. All shouting over each other, no one listening. And that woman from the Lib Dems… hopeless. Oh, don't even start me on the Lib Dems. They say one thing to get your vote, then do exactly the opposite once they’re in power. Remember all that talk about tuition fees? Don’t I just. Promises, promises. And then they jacked them right up. It’s all smoke and mirrors, isn’t it? Just trying to keep us distracted while they line their own pockets. The benefits system's a mess too, you know. Old Mrs. Higgins down the road was telling me they’ve cut her housing benefit again. Says she doesn't know how she's going to manage. It’s scandalous. They expect people to live on air. And then they wonder why there’s so much hardship and… well, you read about it in the papers, don’t you? People turning to desperate measures. It’s this obsession with austerity. They keep saying the economy’s improving, but I’m not seeing it. Prices are going up, and wages are staying the same. It’s a squeeze for everyone. They said they’d get inflation down, didn’t they? Still seems pretty high to me. Everything’s more expensive. Even a loaf of bread. Don't remind me. I was at the supermarket yesterday, and I nearly had a heart attack at the price of butter! It’s ridiculous. Speaking of ridiculous, have you been watching that new detective show on ITV? “Crimson Coast”? Oh, aye. It's alright. A bit predictable, though, isn’t it? You can always guess who the killer is after the first ten minutes. I quite like it. The scenery's lovely. They film it somewhere down in Cornwall, I think. All those cliffs and beaches. It’s a bit slow-paced for my liking. I prefer something with a bit more action. Have you seen that American show, “Bosch”? Now  that’s  a good detective. Too much shooting for me, Arthur. I prefer a cozy mystery. Something like “Midsomer Murders” maybe. Though even that gets a bit gruesome sometimes. I watched a documentary about the Royal Family last night. So much pomp and ceremony for… well, for what exactly?

Right, so how was your day then? Anything exciting happen in the world of fundraising? Oh, you know. Same old, same old. Endless phone calls to people who don’t want to be bothered. Managed to get a couple of decent pledges though, for the new hospice wing. Lady down the road, lost her husband there last year, very generous. That’s nice. It’s good when you feel like you’re actually making a difference, isn’t it? Even if it’s just a small one. This stew’s alright, isn’t it? I tried a new recipe. It’s lovely, actually. A bit more…herby than usual? Yeah, I threw in a load of thyme. Thought it needed something. How was your Mum? Did you manage to speak to her today? Briefly. She was at bingo. Said she won a tenner. Typical. She’s convinced she’s going to win the big prize one day. She’ll be waiting a while. Still, it keeps her entertained. Did she mention anything about Dad? He hasn’t been sounding too cheerful lately, has he? He didn’t really come up. Just complained about the garden. Said the roses are getting eaten by greenfly again. I told him to ask Mrs. Higgins next door, she’s a bit of a gardening guru. Good idea. He’s hopeless in the garden, bless him. Always has been. Remember when he tried to build that pond? It looked like a swamp for months. Oh, don’t remind me. The state of the lawn afterwards. And all those frogs. Sarah was terrified of them. She was, wasn’t she? Speaking of Sarah, any news from her? Did she say anything about the interview? She texted earlier. She’s still waiting to hear back. She’s trying not to get her hopes up, but you know how it is. She really wants this job. She deserves it. She’s worked so hard. It’s just…such a competitive market at the moment. What were you watching on telly last night? I was flicking through, couldn’t find anything decent. I was watching that new detective drama, ‘Silent Witness’. It was actually quite good. A bit gruesome in places, but gripping. Oh, I’ve heard about that. Is it worth a watch? I might record it. I'm in the mood for something a bit…murderous. Definitely. Although, be warned, it's a bit of a slow burn.

Honestly, this weather is just… relentless. Grey, grey, grey. I feel like I haven’t seen the sun in weeks. It's a bit depressing, isn’t it? Even for Poland in November. Tell me about it. Manchester was exactly the same when I left. Just constant drizzle. I’m almost glad I escaped it, even if it’s for slightly different grey here. Though, I did see on Facebook, Auntie Brenda’s garden is completely flooded. Oh dear. Brenda and her roses. She’ll be beside herself. You know, it’s really hit me, seeing all the photos from… well, from Uncle George’s funeral. It feels so strange being here, so far away when everyone else is there. It must. Was it a good turnout? I saw a few photos, looked really packed. Huge. Apparently, the church was overflowing. Mum sent me loads of pictures. Everyone said it was a lovely service, very much  him . I just feel so guilty not being there. Don’t beat yourself up about it. You explained why you couldn’t manage it, and it’s a long way to come for a few days. Plus, you didn’t want to risk bringing anything back with you, considering how you were feeling. You’re right, of course. I was feeling dreadful last week. Still a bit shaky, to be honest. I think it was just a really nasty bug. It knocked me for six. It sounded awful. You were practically living on lemon and ginger tea. I think I preferred teaching online sick than facing a classroom full of teenagers when I last felt like that. Oh god. What  is  it with teenagers? I remember trying to teach a group of them when I did that short contract at the language school back in Cambridge. It was…challenging. Always questioning everything, needing constant entertainment. They can be. But honestly, I’ve found teaching abroad is generally much more rewarding. More appreciative students, a different kind of energy. It’s just… different. What did you enjoy most about your teaching experience back then? Hmm. I liked the one-to-one tuition actually. Building a rapport with someone and watching them genuinely progress. That was really satisfying. Though, the admin was a nightmare. I’m definitely not cut out for bureaucracy. That's why I ended up drifting away from it, really. I never really felt like I  belonged  anywhere in that world.

Honestly, this tea is a lifesaver. I swear, copywriting is draining all my… creative fluids. It’s just churn, churn, churn sometimes. Tell me about it. I thought postgraduate research would be solely about the intellectual thrill, but data cleaning is a special kind of purgatory. Honestly, hours spent staring at spreadsheets, questioning my life choices. Purgatory is a good word for it. It’s not  bad , exactly. It’s just… a lot of writing things like “fluffy kittens enhance your life” for cat food brands. You know? I’m really hoping to get onto some more substantial campaigns soon. Oh god, “fluffy kittens.” That’s… intense. Is Mark still loving his new job? Last I heard he was utterly obsessed with artisanal cheese. Utterly. He’s a man possessed. He’s started talking about opening his own cheese shop. A tiny, bespoke, entirely impractical cheese shop. He keeps sending me links to properties in Tooting. Tooting, really? Is that where he wants to be? I always thought he’d aim for somewhere a bit…shoreditch-ier. Apparently, Tooting has ‘good vibes’ and ‘rising property potential’ according to his research. It’s all very serious. I'm worried he'll end up mortgaged up to his eyeballs selling Brie. Fair enough. Speaking of mortgages… I went food shopping yesterday and I’m genuinely horrified by the price of everything. A single avocado cost me two pounds fifty. Two pounds fifty! Seriously?! That  is  criminal. I’ve started exclusively eating baked beans on toast. It's cheaper than therapy at this point. And honestly, just as fulfilling. You're a woman after my own heart. I’ve been trying to make a weekly meal plan, mainly to prevent panic buying, but it’s a disaster. I end up just buying random ingredients and hoping for the best. That’s my entire cooking style. Optimistic chaos. Last week I tried to make a pasta bake with courgettes, sun-dried tomatoes, and… surprisingly, pickled onions. It did  not  work. Oh dear. Pickled onions in a pasta bake? That sounds... adventurous. Adventurous and profoundly wrong. Lesson learned. Maybe I should just stick to writing about fluffy kittens. At least they don't judge my cooking. Maybe. Or just order a takeaway. We both deserve it after a week of spreadsheets and cat food slogans. Now  that’s  a plan. Indian? Indian sounds very, very good.

Right, who woke me up at six this morning? Honestly. Was that me? It absolutely was you. What were you doing? I wanted breakfast. At six o'clock? It's a school holiday! You're allowed to lie in. I slept really well. That’s lovely, darling. You always do. Right, what are we doing today then? Any brilliant plans? Circus skills! Can we do circus skills? Oh, circus skills. Mmm, that’s a good idea. We could. The weather looks alright, doesn't it? Maybe in the garden. And after that can we go to the park? Possibly. Depends how exhausting the circus skills are. We need to actually  eat  at some point too. Have you thought about breakfast yet, apart from wanting it at half six? Toast! With jam. Strawberry jam. Okay, toast with strawberry jam. And you, sweetheart? What will you have? Cereal. Chocolate cereal! We'll see about the chocolate cereal. Perhaps something a little more sensible. We don’t want a sugar rush before circus skills, do we? What does ‘sensible’ mean? It means… a better choice for your tummy. Like Cheerios. Cheerios are boring. They’re not boring! They’re…round! Right, I need coffee. I heard my mum talking about this ‘Neon Moon’ event thing, apparently it's like a night market. What's a market? It’s a place where people sell things. Food, clothes, toys… all sorts of stuff. Like a shop but outside? Exactly! Apparently, it’s on this weekend. Mum was saying it’s got a really nice atmosphere. Can we go? We’ll have to see. It might be a bit late for you two. It's a grown-up sort of thing. Grown-ups are silly. Sometimes we are. Right. I was talking to Auntie Sharni on the phone yesterday and she’s started saying everything in Australian. Australian? What's that? It’s how people talk in Australia! Apparently, they say “G'day” instead of hello. And they call breakfast "brekkie." Brekkie? That  is  silly! It is a bit. She was trying to tell me to "chuck a U-ey" when I missed the turning on the way to the shops. What does that mean? It means to turn around! It’s all very confusing. Okay, toast and cereal it is. Let's get this show on the road. Or…circus skills on the grass, perhaps. Hopefully, this conversation fits your criteria!

Honestly, the state of things… you’d think after all this time, they’d have figured out a coherent strategy. It’s all just… reactive. Reactive is a polite word for it, isn’t it? More like flailing, I’d say. And the constant U-turns! It’s exhausting just  watching  it, let alone trying to follow any kind of logic. It’s mostly performative, I think. Get the headlines, worry about the consequences later. Social media’s driven everything completely mad, hasn't it? Everything's about the instant reaction, the outrage cycle. Absolutely. My brother was trying to explain the latest policy to his very sensible, very apolitical neighbour and she just threw her hands up and said, "Honestly, it's just noise now. All noise." Perfectly put. Reminds me of Old Man Davies down the valley. He used to say the same about the miners’ strikes, back in the eighties. Said the politicians weren't listening to what people actually  needed , just shouting slogans at each other. Different context, same problem. That’s depressingly true. It feels… cyclical, doesn’t it? We go through these periods of upheaval and then things settle, but the underlying issues never really get addressed. True, and then different demographics get angry. It’s like the pendulum swings, but never finds a stable centre. I was reading a paper on voter realignment… Oh, spare me the academic analysis, boy! Sometimes you just need to look at people’s lives, see what's actually bothering them. My grandmother, for example. She never talked about politics directly. But she remembered the interwar years, the hardship. That shaped her entire worldview. That’s a good point. Family history  does  colour things, doesn’t it? My grandfather fought in the war, came back and built a life from nothing. He was a staunch Labour man, but it wasn't about ideology, it was about fairness and opportunity. He just wanted a better future for his children. My great-grandfather was a bit of a firebrand, apparently. A bit of a socialist, very involved in local politics. He was a teacher, actually, in Aberystwyth. Taught history, ironically. A teacher? That’s interesting. It explains a lot, perhaps. That passion for social justice, that desire to make a difference… it runs in families, that sort of thing. Though, goodness knows, some of the things  they  teach these days! Don’t get me started on education policies!

Right, so the brave knight, Sir Reginald… he didn’t have a shiny helmet, did he? He had a… a colander on his head! A colander? Why? Because all the proper helmets were being used by the chefs! They were having a massive cooking competition, and Sir Reginald needed to protect his head, and a colander was the only thing available. Chefs need helmets? Well, sometimes! If things get  really  chaotic in the kitchen, you need to protect your head from flying… carrots! And peas! Flying carrots! Exactly! And then he had to rescue the Princess Penelope, but the Princess Penelope wasn’t in a tower, she was… stuck in a giant bouncy castle! A bouncy castle? That’s a silly tower! It is a silly tower! A very,  very  bouncy tower. And she couldn’t get out because the king had hidden the pump! Oh no! Why did he hide the pump? Because he thought she was bouncing  too  much! He said, “Penelope, you’re giving me a headache! Stop bouncing!” But she couldn’t stop! It’s a very bouncy bouncy castle. Did Sir Reginald bring a pump? No, he didn’t. He had to find a… a giant straw! And he blew and blew and blew until the bouncy castle deflated a little, and Princess Penelope could climb out. That's a good story! Better than the Helen Moss one. Oh really? What didn’t you like about the Helen Moss one? The one about the explorers? It was too… slow. And there weren't any flying carrots. Or bouncy castles! No, there weren’t any flying carrots or bouncy castles. It was a bit more… sensible. Maybe we should write a letter to Helen Moss and tell her she needs more bouncy castles in her stories. Yes! And flying carrots! Okay, okay. We can do that. Though first, we need to finish Sir Reginald’s story! What happened after Princess Penelope climbed out of the bouncy castle? They had to fight a dragon! Ooh, good one! But this wasn't just  any  dragon… it was a dragon who was really,  really  good at knitting. A knitting dragon? Yes! And it was attacking the kingdom with… knitted scarves! Very itchy knitted scarves! That  is  silly! It is, isn’t it? And this weekend, remember, we're going to the Linton Book Festival. Maybe we’ll meet another author who likes bouncy castles  and  flying carrots.

Right, so I was reading this article, and they’re saying lab-grown meat, like, proper ‘shmeat’ as they call it, is gonna be way more environmentally friendly than even vegetarianism. Apparently, the land use for soy production is… insane. Oh, really? I thought soy was the ethical option. I mean, less harm to animals, right? Although, I’ve read about the monoculture issues with soy, it’s pretty damaging to ecosystems. It's a whole thing, isn’t it? Like, you try to do the right thing, but everything's got a downside. I've been trying to cut down on dairy, but the alternatives are… questionable. And expensive. Exactly! And this lab-grown stuff, they reckon it’ll massively reduce greenhouse gas emissions. No methane from cows, no deforestation for grazing… it sounds almost too good to be true. I’m still a bit squeamish about it. It just feels… unnatural. Like, meat grown in a petri dish. It’s creepy. I’d rather have lentils, thanks. Though I do often wonder, is a factory farm  more  natural than a lab? Because that feels actively horrific. It’s a fair point. Thinking about where actual meat comes from… it’s not exactly a natural process either, is it? More like industrialised oppression. I was watching a documentary about hunting, and even that felt less… disturbing… than the idea of an abattoir. See, that’s where I get confused! Because hunting is still taking a life, isn’t it? It feels actively cruel. At least with an abattoir, it’s, like, efficient cruelty. Is that awful to say? No, it’s honest! It’s brutally honest. Though, thinking about efficiency, that's the whole thing with abattoirs  isn't  it? The sheer scale of it. It feels… detached. Like, no respect for the animal. Whereas a hunter… theoretically… needs to have some sort of connection to what they’re doing. Mmm, maybe. My Grandad used to hunt, and he always said it was about respecting the animal, using all of it. But I also know he just enjoyed shooting things. It's complicated. You know what I respect? People who have the discipline to take all their vitamin tablets. Oh, god, don't even. I’ve got a whole container full, and I've taken maybe three this month. I keep forgetting. And they're expensive! I’m the same.

Right, who wants a gin and tonic before dinner? I’ve got the prosecco chilling too, if anyone’s feeling festive. Gin and tonic for me, please, darling. Long day. Though festive feels a bit… premature, doesn't it? It’s barely December. Prosecco, please! I've been craving bubbles all week. I’m already thinking about New Year’s Eve, though. Any ideas? Oh, don't even  mention  New Year’s. Your Aunt Carol’s already started on about wanting us all at her place again. Last year was… an experience. An experience is putting it mildly. She insisted on playing ABBA non-stop until 3am. And the karaoke. Oh, the karaoke. Seriously? ABBA  and  karaoke? That sounds… intense. I was thinking maybe a slightly quieter affair this year. A pub maybe? A pub sounds lovely. Though knowing Carol, she’ll find a way to infiltrate our plans. She’s like a heat-seeking missile for social gatherings. Did you hear from Uncle Barry about his trip to Scotland? Briefly. Apparently, he tried ordering a pint of bitter and the barman looked at him like he’d asked for the moon. Said it's all lager and ale up there. Oh, really? That's so funny. Language differences are weird, aren't they? I was talking to a friend from America the other day and realized half the words we use mean completely different things. Oh, absolutely. I remember when my cousin moved to Australia and kept asking for “chips.” Nearly caused a riot when they brought him French fries. Speaking of causing a riot, has anyone figured out what’s wrong with the washing machine? It’s making a noise like a strangled walrus. I haven’t looked at it yet. I’m hoping it’ll just… fix itself. Like magic. Though honestly, considering its age, I think we’re looking at a replacement. A replacement. Wonderful. Another expense. I swear, things just break down the moment you turn your back. Remember when your mum's dishwasher flooded the kitchen? Don't remind me. That was chaos. She was convinced the cat had somehow turned on the tap. The cat? Really? Yes! She’s absolutely convinced Jasper is a secret agent of destruction. He  does  have a mischievous glint in his eye, though. He’s a cat. They all have a mischievous glint. Right, drinks are served. Let’s enjoy these before I start worrying about dinner and potential washing machine disasters.

Honestly, the most ridiculous thing happened at a work lunch today. What? Did someone spill soup on their boss? Worse. Someone  asked  for a butterfly fork. A butterfly fork! Apparently, it's the only one that allows for proper asparagus consumption. A butterfly fork? Is that even a real thing? Apparently! It's tiny, ornate… utterly pretentious. I just stared at him. He was completely serious. You’re making that up. I wish I was. It was… a moment. Anyway, how was school? Anything interesting happen? We had two minutes silence for Ukraine. It was… heavy. Yeah, it was pretty quiet. Miss said it’s important to remember what’s happening. It absolutely is. It’s awful. Do you two understand much about what's going on with Russia? Sort of. It's like, Putin’s being a bit of a bully and wants to take over Ukraine? That's what I think anyway. That's a good basic understanding. It’s… complicated, obviously. Lots of history involved. It’s just heartbreaking to see the people suffering. Is it going to be a war? A big war? That's what everyone's worried about. Hopefully, it won't come to that. Lots of countries are trying to stop it. My dad was talking about sanctions. What are those? Sanctions are basically punishments for countries when they do something wrong. Like stopping trade with them, to try and make them change their behaviour. Oh. Like taking away their toys? A bit like that, yes. A very grown-up version of taking away toys. Right, who wants more peas? Speaking of grown-up things, are you two excited about birthdays coming up? I’m hoping for the new Lego Star Wars set. The Millennium Falcon one. It’s massive. I want a new skateboard. Mine’s completely wrecked. We'll see what we can do. We need to start thinking about what you both want to  do  for your birthdays as well. Party? Quiet meal? Definitely a party. With friends. And cake. Yeah, a party! And pizza. Maybe laser quest? Laser quest sounds… energetic. We'll see. We’ll look at dates and stuff. Just finish your supper first, alright? And no requesting butterfly forks, please. No promises. I don’t even  like  asparagus. That’s probably a good thing. Honestly, a butterfly fork. What  is  the world coming to? Don’t even ask.

Right, so Adventure Island is officially booked for the last week in July. Four days, Monday to Thursday. Think that’s manageable, yeah? Adventure Island! Are we going on the Scorpion Express first? It's  so  fast! Can I go on it, too? Even though I'm a bit scared? You absolutely can, darling. We’ll all go on it together. Maybe we’ll start with something a bit gentler first, eh? There’s that lovely little train ride. Remember that one? But the Scorpion Express has loops! And drops! Yes, it does. And we’ll get to it, promise. So, Adventure Island sorted. Now, Cornwall… I was looking at cottages yesterday. There's one near Padstow, looks really nice, sea views… but it’s pricey. Cornwall again? We  always  go to Cornwall. Can’t we go somewhere different? Like… Scotland? Scotland is lovely, but it's a very long drive. And with marking exams looming, I don’t think I can manage a massive road trip. Cornwall is… reliable. We know what to expect. Plus, you both love building sandcastles on the beach. And getting ice cream! And getting ice cream. Exactly. Though, speaking of things we know, I’m still trying to work out what’s triggering my tummy issues. I swear it was that sourdough bread last night. I feel dreadful. Mummy, are you sick? No, sweetie, just a bit… uncomfortable. It’s probably just a food intolerance. I’m going to cut out gluten again and see if that helps. It’s just annoying, I really like sourdough. Maybe it was the chocolate cake at Nana’s house? You had loads! You are not wrong. Possibly. Right, back to Cornwall. This cottage has a games room, which is promising. And it’s close to the Eden Project. Have you two been before? I liked the big bubbles! And the rainforest bit! It was all hot and steamy! Exactly! Okay, I think we’re leaning towards Cornwall. It’s just… I saw this amazing exhibition at the V&A in London – “Alice: Curiouser and Curiouser”. It looked incredible. But again, London feels like too much effort right now. Alice in Wonderland! I like the Cheshire Cat! Me too! Maybe another time. Right, Cornwall it is. I’ll book it this weekend. In the meantime, has anyone started thinking about what they want to pack for Adventure Island? Suncream is essential, obviously.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is  obsessed  with the semicolon. Like, every feedback point is just “Semicolon usage needs improvement.” It’s a coursework essay, not a grammar test! Tell me about it. He marked down Liam for using “like” in a sentence. “Like,” as a filler word. It’s a natural thing to say, innit? He’s such a stickler. It's worse than Mrs. Patel. She actually smiled when she told me my analysis was "adequate." Adequate! That’s basically a polite way of saying it’s rubbish. Haha, brutal. Did you finish the physics practical report though? I’m still stuck on calculating the uncertainty. Nearly. Just gotta tidy up the conclusions. It’s boring as heck, though. Speaking of boring, did you see Sarah in art today? She was attempting pottery and it looked… disastrous. No way! Really? She’s usually so good at everything. Yeah, she just kept collapsing the clay. Mr. Henderson was trying not to laugh. It was pretty funny, actually. Right, speaking of funny, did you hear about what happened with Ben and the prefects? No! Spill the tea. Apparently, he was trying to film a TikTok in the library. Like, full-on dance routine. The head prefect, Emily, went ballistic. No! Ben? Seriously? That’s so… Ben. Did he get in trouble? Got a detention, obviously. Plus, he’s banned from using his phone on school grounds for a week. Which, let’s be real, is like torture for him. He’ll survive. Anyway, are you still going to Jamie’s party on Saturday? Yeah! Should be good. Apparently, he’s hired a DJ. Just gotta convince my mum I’m not going to cause any trouble. Good luck with that. My parents are cool as long as I'm back by midnight. Oh, and they made me promise not to cycle home after. Said it’s too dangerous. Annoying, right? It’s only a ten-minute bike ride. Saves loads of time. I hate waiting for the bus. Tell me about it. Hey, have you seen the new Marvel movie? I was thinking of going next week. Ooh, yeah! I’ve heard it’s really good. But… I’m allergic to something in the cinema popcorn. Makes my face swell up. It's a nightmare. Oh, blimey. That’s… not ideal. Maybe we could just grab something afterwards then? Yeah, that’d be good.

This road is absolutely mental, isn’t it? Honestly, the traffic is building up for no reason. It always does at this time, doesn’t it? People just seem to decide to merge into one lane for fun. It's baffling. Aye, it’s daft. Remember when we were trying to get to Durham last summer? Took us ages just to get past Washington. Oh god, don’t remind me. That was a nightmare. At least we had a good view of the cricket ground, though. Did you see England were playing India last week? I caught a bit of it on the radio. Sounds like they did alright? I’m not the biggest cricket fan, mind. They won! Ben Stokes was on fire, apparently. It was a really good match. You should come with me next time, it’s a good atmosphere. Maybe. I’m more of a football person, you know? Though I appreciate a nice sunny day for watching  something  sporty. Speaking of sunny days… are you still planning on cycling to Brighton next month? Yeah, definitely. I’ve booked the route and everything. Hoping the weather holds up. It's a fair distance, but it’ll be worth it. Have you ever done a long distance cycle ride before? No, never. I can barely manage a trip to the shops and back on my bike without getting completely out of breath! You’re proper keen, you are. Well, I've been training a bit. Trying to build up my stamina, mostly. It's less about speed and more about endurance, you know? It's all about pacing. That sounds… sensible. I’d probably just sprint for the first five miles and then collapse in a heap. Don’t do that! Seriously, you'll ruin your entire trip. You need to start slow and steady. Plenty of water, lots of snacks… and a comfortable saddle. That's crucial. A comfortable saddle? That sounds like a very important piece of cycling advice. I’ll remember that if I ever decide to take it up. It is! Trust me. I learned that the hard way. You wouldn't believe the state of my… well, never mind. Oh, I can imagine! You and your fancy bikes. Honestly, you're a machine. Just trying to stay active. It beats sitting in front of a computer all day, anyway. This traffic isn't helping my stress levels though...think we're going to be here a while.

Right, okay, so Golden Dragon or Lucky House? Honestly, I’m struggling. Last time from Golden Dragon the sweet and sour sauce was… questionable. Questionable? It tasted like straight vinegar. I swear they just emptied a bottle in. Lucky House is usually a safer bet, though their portions are a bit smaller, aren't they? Definitely smaller. I remember ordering a portion of chicken chow mein from there once and I genuinely thought they’d forgotten the chicken. It was like, 90% noodles. See, that’s my fear! I want  food , not a noodle mountain. But the vinegar… oh, the vinegar. Did you see my face when I tried it? It was a picture! You genuinely recoiled. Honestly, I think you made a noise usually reserved for accidentally touching something really hot. It was a reflex! It was  that  bad. Right, okay, new plan. What about New City? They’re a bit further, but apparently their sesame prawns are amazing. Ooh, I’ve heard good things about New City. Apparently, they actually use sesame seeds, which is a revolutionary concept for some of these places. I’ve had prawns that tasted suspiciously of… nothing. Sesame seeds  and  prawns? Bold. I'm worried about the delivery charge being astronomical though, especially if it’s coming from further out. Remember the last time we ordered from that Thai place? It was nearly ten quid just for delivery! Okay, valid point. Let’s quickly check their delivery charges. One sec… Oh, it’s… six fifty. Not terrible. But still. Six fifty. Hmm. Maybe Lucky House is the least offensive option. We could order extra portions to compensate for the noodle deficiency. That’s…actually a sound strategy. We could get two portions of chow mein, just in case. And maybe some spring rolls. Always a safe bet, spring rolls. Okay, okay. Lucky House it is. But if I get another vinegar-based sauce, I’m writing a strongly worded letter. And possibly leaving a scathing online review. You do you. I'm happy with spring rolls. And maybe some dumplings? Do they do good dumplings? I think so. They had a picture of them on their online menu, and they looked…promising. Right, shall I order? I’m feeling proactive. Yes, please! You’re a lifesaver. And maybe, just  maybe , order a small portion of sweet and sour chicken. But if it's vinegary, you have my permission to throw it at the wall.

Honestly, the state of it, eh? Been trying to get me mum an appointment with the GP for weeks now. You’d think being retired she’d get priority, wouldn't ya? Tell me about it. It's a nightmare. I'm a nurse practitioner, I  work  in the system, and even  I  struggle to navigate it sometimes. It’s just… constantly fire-fighting. Never enough resources, never enough time. Aye, well you’re on the front line, love. I can only imagine. It’s a miracle any of it still functions, really. I was reading an article the other day about the Finnish healthcare system… apparently it's completely different. Preventative, properly funded, the whole shebang. Oh, I’ve heard good things. Everything's centralised isn't it? No postcode lottery like we have here. They invest properly in primary care. It's a totally different philosophy. But, you know, good luck trying to implement that here. Too many layers of bureaucracy, too many vested interests. Exactly. It's always the same story, innit? Anyway, speaking of frustrating situations… have you heard anything more about old Mrs. Delaney next door? Oh, her? Not really. Just seen her pottering about in the garden, same as always. Why? Well, I saw her son, Kevin, the other day, loading a van full of her stuff. Said she was "downsizing." Downsizing at eighty-five? Seems a bit dodgy, if you ask me. Oh, that doesn't sound right. She always seemed alright to me. Little bit of a gossip, maybe, but harmless enough. Is he taking her with him? That's what I'm worried about. He’s never been one for looking after anyone but himself, that Kevin. Always asking her for money, always "borrowing" things. I’ve seen him, sneakily, taking her post. Oh, that’s awful! He’s always struck me as a bit of a scoundrel. Has anyone else noticed anything? Old Mr. Henderson across the road said he saw a removal firm he didn't recognise. Apparently, they weren’t local. He said they looked a bit shifty. Henderson’s nosey, but he’s usually spot on. That  is  concerning. Maybe someone should just pop round and have a chat with her, see if everything's alright? I can slip round after work if you like. That would be brilliant, honestly. Just a friendly face, ask her if she's happy.

…and then young Kevin, bless ‘im, he’s arguing with the postman about a parcel. Said it weren’t his, despite bein’ addressed to ‘K. O’Connell, Number 7’. Said the postman was tryin’ to scam ‘im! Kevin, eh? Always a drama with that lad. Reminds me o’ me brother, Billy. Now  he  could argue the hind legs off a donkey. Once argued with a copper over a parking ticket, said the lines weren’t clear enough. Ended up gettin’ a bigger fine for bein’ obstructive. Ah, the police. There’s been a lot of ‘em around lately, hasn’t there? Seems a bit heavier handed than usual. Heard they raided that flat on Upper Stanhope Street again. Aye, heard that. Drugs, they say. Though I reckon half the trouble is caused by these…these newcomers, comin’ over here takin’ our jobs. Not all o’ them, mind, but there’s a good few. That's…a complicated issue, isn’t it? A lot of these jobs aren’t ones people  want  to do, to be honest. And a lot of them work incredibly hard. I teach a few students who came over with their families. Bright kids, desperate to learn. Hard work don't fill an empty belly, lad. And desperate… desperate people do desperate things. Back in my day, you knew everyone on the street. Now? Faces you've never seen before. It’s not the same, not the same at all. Used to be able to leave your door unlocked. Not anymore, not anymore. Things certainly change. Though I remember me Nan always sayin’ you could never truly trust anyone, even your own neighbours. She'd seen a bit in her time, lost her husband in the war. She was right, y’know. She was a smart woman, your Nan. Mine… well, she worried about everything. Especially me. Said I was too soft. Used to say, “Arthur, you’d let a burglar help himself to the silver and then offer him a cup of tea!” Sounds like her. My Dad was the worrier. Constantly fretting about the welfare state, said it was breeding dependency. He used to say if everyone had to work for a livin’, there’d be less trouble. He weren’t wrong, y'know. Though it’s alright sayin' that when you  have  a livin’. What about the ones who can't work? The sick, the disabled… the old like me?

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think I’ve identified at least four different shades of beige on my plate. It’s Cambridge University Press, not a Michelin-starred restaurant, Liv. You get what you get. Though, I’ll admit, the ‘mystery meat’ is always a gamble. It’s functional. Fuel. That's all it needs to be. I’ve got a stack of transcripts to annotate this afternoon, I need the energy. You guys are too polite. It’s… institutionally bland. Though, I’m used to American university dining halls. They often operate on a similar principle of mass-produced lukewarmness. I’m just grateful I managed to snag a seat. It was like the Hunger Games in here. Did anyone see old Mr. Henderson elbowing that poor PhD student out of the way for a Yorkshire pudding? No way! Henderson? He’s usually such a gentle soul. Though, he  does  have a legendary appetite. I heard he single-handedly cleared out the biscuit tin at the last departmental meeting. Apparently, he said they were “a vital component of cognitive function.” That’s amazing. He’s a character, isn't he? Reminds me of my grandad, always sneaking extra portions. It’s funny how consistent those little personality quirks are across generations. My grandfather was the same way with pudding. Couldn’t resist a good custard. Speaking of which, is anyone braving the dessert selection? I might. I’ve heard whispers of a chocolate brownie. Though, it’s probably 90% icing and 10% actual brownie. You’re brave, Ella. I’m sticking with the vaguely fruit-like substance they’re calling ‘compote’. It’s…texturally interesting. So, anyone actually made any progress on the phonological analysis today? I’m hitting a wall with the Northern English vowel shifts. It’s… complex. I’m slowly getting there. It’s the subtle variations that are killing me. You think you've got it pinned down, then you find a recording with a completely different pronunciation. It's fascinating though, isn’t it? The way language evolves and changes with geography. Keeps things interesting. That’s why I love working on these dialect projects. It’s mad how different things are even just between Leeds and Sunderland, Liv. You’d think being relatively close, it'd be more similar. Tell me about it! I was trying to explain to my aunt what you meant by ‘quid’ last week and she just looked at me like I’d grown a second head.

…and honestly, the buffering was atrocious. I mean, I’m paying for fibre, supposedly ‘superfast’ fibre, and I was watching a nature documentary, right? David Attenborough, majestic stuff. But every time a particularly stunning shot of a snow leopard emerged, it would freeze. Freeze! Ruined the whole dramatic effect. Oh, the indignity! You’re missing the apex predator in its natural habitat because of… BT? Is that who you’re with? Yeah, BT. They claim it’s the line, the ancient wiring in this Victorian house. I’m starting to suspect it’s just a conspiracy to keep me from discovering the secrets of the snow leopard. A snow leopard conspiracy. I like it. Makes more sense than their customer service, anyway. I’ve been thinking about trying to pick up some Mandarin. Mandarin? Seriously? That’s a bold move. Well, I’ve been working with a couple of Chinese colleagues on this latest project, and it’s become acutely apparent how hopeless I am. I mean, I can manage ‘Ni hao’ and ‘Xie xie’, but beyond that… nothing. It’s frustrating. You feel like you're constantly relying on translation, missing nuanced understanding. I can imagine. I attempted Spanish once. Got as far as ordering beer and asking where the toilet was. Highly practical, admittedly, but not exactly fluent conversation. What are you thinking of doing? Online course? Probably. Duolingo’s tempting, but I worry it’s a bit… superficial. I was looking at some evening classes at the local college. It’s just fitting it into the schedule is the killer. You’re still teaching that adult education class, aren’t you? Sadly, yes. Though ‘teaching’ might be a generous term. It's mostly trying to coax reluctant learners through basic essay structure. It’s surprisingly draining. You get one or two who are genuinely enthusiastic, then a sea of blank stares and sighs. Sounds familiar. The joy of public service, eh? I’ve always admired people who are good at teaching. It requires a patience I definitely don’t possess. It’s more about lowering your expectations, honestly. And having a good sense of humour. One lady last week honestly thought footnotes were some sort of secret code. Oh, bless her. That's brilliant. You'd think in this age of instant information, footnotes wouldn't be so mysterious. It’s funny, isn’t it? How differently people approach things depending on their cultural background, their education… Absolutely.

Right, now then, love, you’ve made a proper mess of this cushion arrangement, haven’t you? Looks like a flock of pigeons landed on it. Grandma! I didn’t  make  a mess. I was just…rearranging. It needed a bit of life. Life? It needed a good plumpin’ and settlin’, not scatterin’ about like confetti. Your grandad always said a tidy room is a tidy mind. Though, mind you, his mind was often a bit of a muddle anyway. Aye, that’s true. Used to look for his glasses when they were on his head. Happened more times than I care to remember. Don’t encourage him, Arthur! Now, are you two hungry? I’ve made a victoria sponge. Proper one, with raspberry jam and a dusting of icing sugar. Ooh, yes please! That sounds amazing. Lovely. Though, I’m not sure I should. Doctor said I need to watch my sugar. Oh, don’t be daft, Margaret. One slice won't hurt. Besides, a little bit of what you fancy does you good. I’ll cut you a small one. I'll have a slice then, whilst you're at it. Can’t let all that good cake go to waste. That’s what I thought. Now, that dripping from the guttering… I really need to get someone to look at that. It's been like that for weeks. I told you, Gran, I could have a look. I’m pretty good with DIY stuff. I fixed Mr Henderson’s shed last summer, remember? You  helped  Mr Henderson. His son did most of the work. And you nearly took your finger off with the hammer. It was a slight mishap. Always best to get a professional in for something like that. Don't want you falling off a ladder, lad. We'd have another one to worry about then. Speaking of worrying, have you seen that new program on the telly? About the escaped emu? Oh, Arthur, honestly! Emus! It's ridiculous. It’s hilarious! Apparently it ran through a primary school playground. Well, I never. Imagine the chaos. I'm more concerned about the heating. It’s been acting up again. Keeps going on and off. I've tried everything. Do you think I should call Billy next door? He's quite handy. Billy? He charged Mrs. Patterson a fortune for changing a light bulb. Oh, don't remind me.

Oh, look at that little courtyard. Isn’t it lovely? All those potted plants… makes such a difference, doesn’t it? It does. It's amazing what a bit of green can do. I was thinking about old Mrs. Higgins’ garden back in Norwich, remember? She had prize-winning roses. Oh,  Mrs. Higgins ! Yes! She was utterly terrifying if you dared to step on her lawn. She’d be out there with her watering can like a weapon. Exactly! But the roses were spectacular. Do you think we’ll ever… I don’t know… have a proper garden again? Just space to potter about? Eventually, I hope so. It feels a bit… surreal, doesn’t it? Being here, so far from everything that feels normal. Though, increasingly, ‘normal’ feels a long way away. Tell me about it. I was scrolling through photos on my phone earlier. Liam and Chloe’s wedding… feels like a lifetime ago. Everyone looking so happy and…  there . Oh, God, that was a good wedding. So much gin. Did you see Sarah’s photos too? She posted loads of them from her trekking trip in Nepal. Incredible. Makes you want to just… go. Completely. Though Nepal feels a little ambitious at the moment. Maybe something closer to home, when we get back. A week in the Lake District? Ooh, yes! That sounds perfect. We should start planning something. A proper break. I keep meaning to look at the flight prices, but I always get distracted with marking. It's the same story. Honestly, marking essays about the symbolism of rain in Victorian poetry is not nearly as appealing as a walk in the fells. You’re telling me. I had one student write an entire essay arguing that rain represents the repressed desires of the upper class. Oh,  seriously ? That’s… dedicated. Or completely bonkers. A little of both, I think. Speaking of slightly bonkers…did you hear back from Mark about his trip out here? He was talking about trying to visit over the summer. He emailed! He’s decided to postpone. Something about work commitments. He said he’s gutted, though, and promised to try next year. Ah, that’s a shame. It would've been lovely to show him around. He’d love the food, I think. Or, at least, complain about it in a very amusing way. Absolutely. He's the master of polite complaints.

Honestly, my feet are  killing  me. I swear those shoes were designed by someone who's never actually walked anywhere. Tell me about it! I think I’ve permanently ruined my blisters. Did you see Liam trying to dance? Honestly, it was… a choice. Oh, God, Liam. He thinks he’s John Travolta, doesn’t he? It’s tragic. He was practically knocking people over. He was! And then he kept trying to offer everyone shots. Shots of what, I don’t even want to know. He was a menace. At least it was a good laugh though, right? I haven’t laughed that much in ages. Even Chloe managed a smile, and you  know  how grumpy she gets when she’s not getting enough attention. True. She was glued to Ben all night. Honestly, I don't get it. He's nice, yeah, but he talks about football  constantly . It’s exhausting. I know! My dad talks about football less, and he literally watches it every single day. Speaking of dads, mine’s been going on about getting a dog again. Oh no, not again! He was obsessed last time. Remember when he was researching Great Danes? In our tiny flat! Don't remind me. He forgot we live in a shoebox. He’s now talking about a Labrador puppy. Says it’ll “get us all out more.” Right, because hours of puppy training and cleaning up accidents is exactly what we need to make our lives more exciting. Tell him to get a goldfish. Honestly, I will. He’s already sent me links to breeders. It’s terrifying. Did you manage to eat anything last night, by the way? I was too busy dodging Liam's shots to even look at the food. I had a chip. One. It was swimming in grease, but it was a chip and I was starving. I spent all day at placement, honestly I’m wrecked. Placement sounds brutal. I'm just doing essays, which is… another kind of brutal. I'm trying to get motivated to start mine on Victorian literature. It's so dull. Oh god, Victorian lit. That sounds awful. I’d rather have Liam offering me dodgy shots. What’s the essay on? Dickens. Specifically, the portrayal of poverty. Riveting stuff. I think I’m going to need a lot of coffee. You and me both. I saw Jess posting photos on Insta this morning, looking  amazing .

Right, so have we actually finalised when your mum’s coming? I keep forgetting to ask. It feels like it’s been 'next week' for a month now. It has, hasn’t it? She’s confirmed for the 18th. She’s booked the train, everything. Luckily she managed to get a reasonably priced ticket, though she was grumbling about the cost. She's aiming to arrive around lunchtime. The 18th… that’s good. Gives us time to… well, to generally tidy up. This place isn't exactly presentation-ready, is it? Oh, don't be daft, John. It's perfectly homely. She’s not expecting the Ritz. Though, maybe a quick once-over with the hoover wouldn't go amiss. And I’ll get the guest room aired. I can help with that. I’ve finished most of the transcription work for today, so I have a bit of free time. Speaking of which, did you see the latest FIFA update? They’ve completely reworked the player movements.
