Oh, no, I haven’t touched it since… well, since last month, probably. I’m getting too old for these things. My reflexes aren’t what they used to be. I was getting utterly thrashed by that young lad, Ben, online. You’re just being modest, John. You’re still very competitive. Remember that time you beat your brother at tennis when you were… oh goodness, must have been forty years ago? He never let you forget it. That was a different time. And it was partially due to him having a dodgy knee. He’d just come back from a football injury. Though, he’d never admit that. Stubborn man, your father. Speaking of stubborn, I was reading an article about the situation with that football manager, Gareth Southgate. Everyone’s blaming him for the team’s performance, but I think the board are just as culpable. They haven't invested properly in youth development. It's always easier to blame the visible figure, isn't it? No one wants to admit their own part in a failure. It reminds me of school – a student failing a maths test and instantly blaming the teacher, rather than acknowledging their own lack of preparation. Exactly. No accountability. It’s a modern malaise. It's all about passing the buck. Honestly, you see it in politics, you see it in business… It’s frustrating. It's like, where does the responsibility  actually  lie?

Right, well, that was lovely wasn’t it? Biscuits were a bit stale, but…you can’t win ‘em all. They weren't  that  stale, honestly. It’s just you're a biscuit snob, Liam. And honestly, Dad, complaining about free biscuits is a bit much. No, no, she’s right. A bit crumbly, maybe. Still good with the tea though. Lovely tea, actually. Better than what I make, I’ll admit. You always say that, Reg. You make a perfectly good cup of tea. It’s just…we use posh tea here, isn’t that right? It’s just a slightly fancier blend, yeah. Worth the extra quid, I reckon. Anyway, are you sure you’ve got everything? Bags packed? Yep. Phone charger, toiletries, emergency chocolate...the essentials. I’ve got my glasses. Found them under the cushion, of all places. Honestly, I swear they have a life of their own. Tell me about it. I’m  always  losing mine. It’s the age, I think. Everything starts to go. It’s not age, it’s just being…distracted. Like when I tried to fix that wonky shelf last week and ended up nearly taking the whole wall down. DIY is officially beyond me. You and DIY are a tragic combination. Remember the time you tried to assemble that flat-pack bookcase? Don't remind me. It took three of us and a lot of colourful language. Anyway, did you two manage to figure out that phone, Dad? The Blackberry? Ah, that thing. Still a mystery. It’s…complicated. Young Liam here was trying to show me, but it’s all touchscreens and swipes. I miss a good button. Solid, you know? It’s different, definitely. I’m pretty good with technology, but even I find some of it a bit baffling. Speaking of baffling, did you hear about the bin strikes? Absolute chaos. Oh god, no. Still going on? That’s disgusting. Brighton will be a tip in a week. Apparently the water company’s involved somehow. Something about…waste processing and needing more water? Typical. They’re always finding a reason to increase the bills. It’s mad isn’t it? You can’t even trust them to just take your rubbish away. And the water, honestly, I’ve been reading about different filters you can get, to improve the taste. Apparently, tap water isn’t as clean as they say.

Right, have you checked the football? Any sign of a miraculous recovery from United? You know it's pointless even looking, honestly. It was another…well, let’s just say it wasn’t a good weekend for them. I saw a few headlines. Didn’t bother digging deeper, saved myself the pain. Sensible. It’s just…it's getting to the point where I dread even glancing at the scores. It’s affecting my mood, which, given the general grey-ness of everything, is not ideal. This gloom is really getting to me, actually. Proper SAD vibes going on. I can imagine. Poland in November isn’t exactly known for its sunshine, is it? Is it worse than Cambridge this time of year, do you think? Oh, massively. Cambridge gets damp, but it doesn’t have  this …oppressive feeling. Everything feels heavy. Though, this coffee is good. Really good. This place is a find. Have you tried the latte macchiato? Not yet, but I will. I'm on my second flat white, and it’s perfect. Bit stronger than what I’m used to back home. Speaking of home… I had a message from Sarah this morning. She’s booked a weekend away, hiking in the Lake District. Oh, lovely! Good for her. Are you feeling…homesick? A little, if I’m honest. It's not so much missing  things , it's missing having everything familiar. You know? Like knowing where to get your favourite biscuits, or just being able to pop to the pub without needing to translate the beer menu. And my students… I’m starting to feel so responsible for them all. Their exams are looming, and I’m terrified I haven’t prepared them well enough. Ah, that's awful. The weight of expectation, right? You’re a good teacher, though, you’ll have done your best. It's easy to get caught up in worrying. I know, I know. It’s just…Agnes, one of my students… she’s so bright, but she struggles with speaking. I've been trying to build her confidence, but I feel like I'm failing. I spend hours thinking about different approaches. That sounds exhausting. You’re such a conscientious person. Remember that time you volunteered on the organic farm in France for a summer? You threw yourself into everything. Absolutely covered in mud, but happy as could be. Oh god, don't remind me!

Right, this sauce needs a proper good stir, doesn’t it? I swear, pasta sauce always separates when you’re not looking. It does, it's the law. Honestly, you'd think it  wants  to look sad and watery. So, how was work today, Liam? More heavy lifting? You know it. Pallets of… something. Honestly, I rarely look. It’s just shift it from A to B. The lads are alright though, keeps you sane. You? Still wrangling conference centres? Still wrangling. Honestly, it was a nightmare. Apparently, someone booked the main hall for a poodle grooming competition  and  a taxidermy convention on the same day. No way! Seriously? That's…quite a clash of interests. Tell me about it. I had to explain to Mrs. Higgins – the poodle lady – why she couldn’t have glitter cannons during the taxidermy demonstration. Apparently, the stuffing is flammable. Woah. Okay,  that's  a story. See, my day lacked any kind of drama like that. Just sweat and splinters. Sounds… fulfilling. I swear, corporate life is just a constant fire drill these days. Had a full meltdown from Brenda in marketing because the font on the new brochure was “too assertive.” Oh, Brenda. She's a special breed, isn't she? Still, at least you get paid a decent wage for handling assertive fonts. Speaking of which, have you guys seen that new shop that opened on Mill Road? The vintage one? Nah, not yet. Is it any good? I’m always needing new work clothes, something that doesn’t look like I’ve been wrestling with timber all day. It’s brilliant! I found this amazing leather jacket, secondhand of course, for like thirty quid. It's proper 80s, all oversized and a bit rebellious. Ooh, send me a pic! I’m always on the hunt for a statement piece. I’ve been trying to avoid fast fashion lately, it feels…wrong. Will do! It's definitely a good find. It’s a shame you're always working, Liam, we could have gone browsing this afternoon. Tell me about it. Shifts are crazy at the moment with Christmas coming up. Everyone’s panicking about deliveries. Speaking of Christmas, are we still doing Secret Santa this year? I think so. I was thinking we could set a limit of twenty quid. Keeps it reasonable. Sounds good to me. Have either of you had any luck on the dating front?

Honestly, this square is…odd. It’s all these straight lines, isn’t it? Very formal. Reminds me of a chessboard. Not a patch on a proper park with meandering paths and… well, character. Yeah, it’s a bit stark. Though I suppose it’s useful for, you know, meeting people. Look at that kid though, actually caught a pigeon! Bit rough, isn’t it? The poor thing. Kids will be kids. Makes you wonder what they’re teaching them these days. Speaking of which, I’m still reeling from Mrs. Chen’s stories about teaching English in China. The sheer scale of it… thirty students in a class? And the emphasis on rote learning. It’s a world away from our TEFL courses, eh? I remember old Professor Davies banging on about communicative methodology. She said the Chinese system is changing, slowly. More demand for conversational English, especially with the rise in tourism. Tourism… that’s an interesting one. Apparently, Paris is completely overrun. Chinese tourists, specifically. All wanting the Eiffel Tower selfies. I read something about it – queues stretching for miles. Yeah, it's a bit mad. I was talking to Li Wei last week and he was saying the Chinese middle class are desperate to travel, see the world. They’ve been cooped up for so long. He was telling me about his family’s trip to Tibet. Said it was… transformative. Tibet… wow. Must be incredible. Completely different landscape, isn't it? He also mentioned seeing pandas, of course. Apparently, they're obsessed with pandas. They used to keep bears as pets, apparently. Real, proper bears. Really? That sounds… perilous. Bit different from a golden retriever. You realize how much about China I’m learning through anecdote, don’t you? It's all second hand from students and Li Wei. It’s the best way, sometimes. Textbooks can only tell you so much. Speaking of textbooks… how’s the PhD going? Still battling with Professor Albright? She's notoriously… demanding. Oh, Albright. Don’t even get me started. She wants me to completely re-frame my argument. Says I’m being too… optimistic about the role of social media. She's practically breathing down my neck. It’s exhausting. Fancy another coffee? There's that place on Tottenham Court Road. Absolutely. I need the caffeine. Plus, I saw they do that coconut cake… the one you like.

Right, so are we still on for Friday then? Yeah, Friday's good. Unless… oh wait, actually, Sarah’s mum is coming to stay. Friday night. Blast. Oh no, really? Thought she was away on that cruise? She was, but it got cancelled. Bad weather, apparently, in the Mediterranean. So, she’s descended on us. Friday’s a non-starter, then. Sorry. No worries, happens. What about Saturday? Are you free Saturday afternoon? We could finally hit that new climbing place. Saturday… hmm. Let me just check.  taps on phone  Okay, yeah, Saturday's looking clear. No pre-booked doom and gloom. Climbing sounds brilliant, actually. Been needing to get back into it. Wicked! It's supposed to be really good there. Proper high walls and everything. I've been watching videos online, looks intense. Excellent. Should be a good workout. What time were you thinking? How about… 2pm? Gives us time to grab a coffee beforehand, maybe a quick bite to eat? 2pm sounds perfect. There’s a little café just round the corner from the climbing centre, does cracking sandwiches. Proper sandwiches, or the sad, pre-made kind? Proper, I promise. Fresh bread, actual fillings…the works. They even do a decent veggie option, which I know you'll appreciate. You know me too well. Okay, brilliant. Let's do 2pm Saturday then. Sorted. And have you managed to get hold of Liam about that gig next week? Aye, yeah, I spoke to him yesterday. He’s in, definitely. Says he’s already started thinking about the setlist. Apparently, he's unearthed some old gems from university. Oh lord. That sounds… potentially concerning. Liam's university tunes are a bit… experimental. That's what I said! I told him we're aiming for "fun" not "avant-garde jazz fusion". He assured me he's toning it down. We'll see. Right. Well, as long as there's something vaguely recognisable. I'm bringing my sister, and she has zero tolerance for anything that sounds like a dying cat. Noted. I'll subtly steer him towards the more mainstream choices. Maybe slip a bit of The Killers into the mix. Excellent plan. Operation: Keep Sister Happy is a go. Aye. Operation: Keep Sister Happy. It’s a crucial mission. Absolutely. So, Saturday, climbing, and a delicate negotiation with Liam. Sounds like a plan. Sounds perfect. Now, if you don't mind, could you turn the music down a  little ?

Honestly, I feel like I’ve been run over by a bus. This cold is absolutely brutal. You look it, lass. Proper peaky. You shoulda stayed in bed, should’ve you? I  tried  to, but I had that conference call first thing. Absolutely essential, apparently. Felt like my head was going to explode during it. I kept having to mute myself to cough. So professional, right? Oh, the joys of working from home when you’re ill. At least you weren’t spreading germs around the office. Still, sounds awful. Are you taking anything? Just paracetamol, loads of hot lemon and ginger, and trying to sleep. Feel like a zombie, though. Everything smells weird. Lemon and ginger’s good stuff. Me nan swore by that. Though she always added a good slug of brandy, said it ‘opened up the airways’. Your nan sounds…sensible. She was! Right, practical woman. Speaking of practical, I need to sort out my dating life, or lack thereof. It's a disaster. Oh, go on then. Spill the beans. What’s happened now? Well, remember Mark? The vegan architect? Vaguely. Wasn’t he a bit… intense? Intense is an understatement. He messaged me yesterday, after barely speaking for a week, to tell me I wasn’t “aligned with his energy” and therefore we shouldn’t see each other anymore.  Aligned with his energy ? What in the world does that even mean? Sounds like something off a mindfulness retreat brochure. Exactly! I said as much, actually, but he just sent back a load of emojis - a sprout, a crystal, and a little meditating person. I blocked him. Good. You did the right thing. That’s just… weird. Honestly, dating apps are a minefield. Tell me about it. I'm considering deleting them all and taking up knitting. Least then my biggest problem will be tangled yarn, not questionable life choices. Knitting's alright. Me mum makes amazing jumpers. You could learn, might meet someone at a knitting circle! You never know! Although, maybe stick to recovering from this cold first. We’re going out on Saturday, remember? You need to be semi-functional for that. Oh god, Saturday. I'd forgotten. Right, operation ‘get better’ is now in full swing. I'm accepting all medicinal offers – chicken soup, a hot water bottle, terrible reality TV… It’s all on the table. I can certainly offer terrible reality TV.

Honestly, the day just… wouldn’t  end . Mr. Henderson kept asking me to re-format the same spreadsheet, like, five times. Five! And each time he’d just squint at it and say “Hmm, doesn’t quite  pop .” Pop?! It's a budget spreadsheet, not a fireworks display. Oh my god, Henderson. He sounds… intense. You’d think after all this time he’d have learned to specify what ‘pop’ means. Exactly! I tried to ask, but he just waved his hand dismissively and said “You know,  pop .” It felt like being back in art class with a painfully vague brief. Ugh. Well, at least you're home now. Wine time? I need to decompress after a twelve-hour shift dealing with… well, everything. Definitely wine time. Though, you won’t believe who I saw today at lunch. Oh? Spill. Liam. From university. Remember him? The one who was obsessed with interpretive dance? Liam! Oh god, yes. The tights. I’ve blocked a lot of that out. What was he doing there? Apparently, he’s working for that marketing firm near the office now. He looked… good. Scarily good. Like, actual adult human being good, not ‘needs-to-be-chaperoned-through-Freshers’ good. No way! Good for him, I guess. Still doing the dance thing on the side? I didn’t ask! He saw me and just sort of… froze. Then mumbled something about “catching up sometime” and practically sprinted back to his office. It was awkward. That’s hilarious. Okay, that's a good story. Mine's less funny, more… sad. Chloe from work just told me she's splitting up with Ben. Oh no! Seriously? I didn't even know they were having problems. They always seemed so solid. Apparently, it’s been brewing for a while. Something about him wanting kids now and her… definitely not. It’s a big thing. She was absolutely gutted. She was crying in the stationary cupboard. Oh, the stationary cupboard. The professional weeping place. That’s awful. Poor Chloe. It’s just… everyone’s going through something, isn’t it? It really is. It's exhausting. Makes you appreciate the small things, like not having to explain to a man what ‘pop’ means in a spreadsheet. Absolutely. And a good glass of wine. Pouring now! So, interpretive dance Liam, crying Chloe… anything else exciting happen in your day? Just the usual. A patient trying to convince me they could fly, a locked medication cabinet, and a near-miss with a rogue sandwich.

Right, so the thing about Baba Yaga is, she’s not  always  evil. It depends how you treat her, doesn’t it? It’s a bit like… well, like Mrs. Higgins next door. She seems grumpy, but she always brings us apples from her tree. Is Baba Yaga grumpy? Sometimes. She’s… complicated. She lives in a house that walks on chicken legs! Can you imagine? Woah! Does it  really  have chicken legs? Big ones? Huge ones! And it spins around, so you have to shout the right words to make it stop and let you in. It’s a very old story, a Russian folk tale. They used to tell these stories to teach children lessons, you see. About being polite, and not being greedy. So, if you’re nice to Baba Yaga, she helps you? Sometimes. Or she tests you. Like, she might ask you to do a really difficult job, just to see if you’re kind and brave. And if you are, she’ll reward you. What kind of jobs? Like tidying her house? Maybe! Or sorting seeds, or helping her clean the oven. She has a very big oven, you know. And some stories say she eats people! Eeeeew! But those are usually the stories told to naughty children! She’s much more likely to give you advice, or a magic object. It’s all about respect, really. Respecting your elders and respecting the forest. So, she’s like a… a witch? Well, she  is  a witch, but not like the witches in fairy tales who just want to turn everyone into frogs. She’s powerful, and she represents the wild, untamed parts of nature. And sometimes, that can be scary. What about dragons? Are dragons always evil? That’s a good question! Dragons are… tricky. In some stories, they’re horrible monsters who hoard gold and breathe fire. But in others, they’re wise and noble creatures who help heroes. It really depends on the story. Remember St George and the Dragon? Yeah! He killed the dragon! He did, but that dragon was terrorizing a village. Sometimes, you  have  to fight evil, even if it's scary. But it's also important to remember not all scary things  are  evil. So, Baba Yaga might not be evil? Exactly. And that’s what makes these stories so interesting, isn’t it? Nothing is ever quite as simple as it seems.

So, how was the filming trip today, Lily? Did you enjoy it? It was really good! We filmed at the castle! It was HUGE! And there were knights! Knights? Proper knights in armour? No, silly! People  dressed  as knights. But they had swords and everything! And I got to be an extra! I had to pretend to be a village girl bringing bread. Did you drop the bread? No! I held it  really  tight. It was pretend bread anyway. It was plastic! Sounds brilliant. Was it cold though? I was worried about you all being out in that wind all day. They said it was quite bracing. Honestly, I’m still trying to convince myself it’s properly warming up at night. I had the heating on a little bit last night. Me too. Just a little bit. I’m a wimp, I know. My legs hurt. Oh, darling. Still hurting from yesterday? From falling off your scooter? Yeah. It feels… stingy. Let me have a look. Oh, it’s already looking much better. Just a bit of a scrape. We put the cream on, didn’t we? We did. She was very brave. Right, I’m thinking I need to get myself to the gym tonight. I feel like I haven't done anything proper all week. Good idea. I might join you. I'm feeling restless. Are you going to run on the… the thing? The treadmill? Maybe. I usually walk. It feels less… punishing. You know, less like I'm actively trying to hurt myself. I just switch it to ‘hills’ and pretend I’m climbing a mountain. It distracts me from the pain. That’s… dedication. I usually just people-watch. See who's struggling the most and feel slightly better about my own suffering. Can we get doughnuts after? Yeah! With sprinkles! We’ll see. Maybe if you both behave yourselves. And maybe if  I  manage to run up a virtual mountain without collapsing. Fair enough. Although, if you do collapse, I’m definitely getting a doughnut. For medicinal purposes, of course. I want a pink one! Mine needs chocolate! And sprinkles! Lots of sprinkles! Alright, alright! We’ll discuss the sprinkles later. Now, who wants a snack  before  dinner? Don't tell your father. Our lips are sealed. Although, he always finds out, doesn’t he? He has magic ears! Yeah! Magic ears! Something like that.

Honestly, this paella is… perfectly adequate. Not exactly transporting me back to Spain, is it? Adequate sums it up, Arthur. It's fuel, isn't it? Fuel for moaning about the state of the world. Speaking of which, saw old Maggie down at the boot sale on Sunday. Maggie? Still at it, is she? Always had an eye for a bargain, that woman. Find anything good? She snagged a rather alarming ceramic gnome for a quid. Said it reminded her of Brenda’s garden. Brenda being her sister, who’s got… well, let’s just say a  robust  garden aesthetic. Oh, lovely. Sounds about right. She’s a character, Maggie. How’s business, by the way? Still keeping busy with the shop? Keeping afloat. Just. It's tougher now, isn't it? Everyone's online. Trying to compete with Amazon is like bringing a water pistol to a tank battle. Thinking about maybe… scaling back a bit. More time for myself, perhaps. You deserve it, Geoff. Run that place for years. Though what you’d  do  with yourself is another matter. You’d be under my feet at school within a week, volunteering to tell stories. Don't you start! I can already picture it. “Mr. Thompson, the shop’s quiet, I thought I'd regale Year 7 with tales of retail life…” Exactly! Seriously though, you need to look after yourself. I had old Mrs. Higgins in last week, practically collapsed in my office. Blood pressure through the roof. Stress, she said. The modern world is exhausting. That’s what I’m saying. You know, I’ve been thinking about this Green Party stuff. They’re gaining traction, aren't they? They are. Getting a lot of support locally, surprisingly. Though some of their proposals… a bit radical for my taste. Still, anything to get people talking about the environment. I’m tempted to give them a vote. Though I worry it’s all a bit idealistic. My son, Ben, he's fully on board. He’s lecturing me about carbon footprints now. The irony! He spends his life flying around the world as a photographer. Ah, the contradictions of youth. It’s all part of the learning process. Speaking of families, how’s Sarah? Still happily married to the barrister? Oh, they’re fine. No dramatic news there, thankfully. She sends her love, by the way. Says she saw you at the theatre last month.

Honestly, I’m convinced my fiddle leaf fig is actively plotting my demise. It’s just  judging  me with its leaves. Oh, they’re dramatic, aren't they? Mine just drops leaves whenever I look at it wrong. It’s passive aggressive horticulture. Exactly! Like, I water you, I mist you, I even talk to you… what more do you want? It's worse than trying to explain Brexit to my grandad. Speaking of which, did you see Trump’s latest… pronouncements? Honestly, the man is a walking, talking headline generator. It’s exhausting. Don't even get me started. It's just…constant. And people actually  believe  it. It’s terrifying. I had a whole debate with someone on Twitter last night – needless to say, it ended with me muting them. Sensible. Twitter is a wasteland. I try to avoid it after 6pm. Too much… energy. How’s the research going, by the way? Still battling the data demons? Oh, always. I’ve hit a bit of a snag with the qualitative analysis. It’s all just… opinions. So many opinions. And trying to find themes is like finding a needle in a haystack made of other needles. Sounds delightful. My PhD is feeling increasingly like a very expensive exercise in self-doubt. I’m starting to question if anyone will  actually  care about the migratory patterns of garden snails. Oh, come on! Garden snails are fascinating! Think of the tiny adventures! Seriously though, it  will  be valuable. You’re doing important work. And at least you're not dealing with… people’s opinions on everything. True. Though sometimes I think snails are more opinionated than people. Have you seen what they do to your hostas? Don’t remind me. My mum’s garden is a battlefield. Oh! And my new blazer arrived. I got the one we were looking at online - the teal corduroy. Ooh, nice! Teal suits you. It’ll look great with that patterned shirt you have. You always have excellent style. I’m still stuck in a rut of jeans and vaguely academic-looking jumpers. You pull off the academic look! It’s very… distinguished. Although, we should probably both be thinking about saving a bit more money, to be honest. These Cambridge pubs are draining my account. Tell me about it. I swear, a pint costs more here than a pasty back home in Brum.

Honestly, the student feedback this year was… bracing. Apparently, I “lack energy.” Can you  believe  it? Lack energy? You’re practically a dynamo in seminars! They just want someone to spoon-feed them everything, don’t they? It's more than that. One said my lectures were “visually dull.” Visually dull! I showed them Rothko! Rothko! Oh, that’s brilliant. What did they want, flashing lights and interpretive dance? Honestly, I wouldn’t be surprised. I was trying to explain post-structuralism and I swear one of them was scrolling TikTok. The eternal struggle. Mine were complaining about workload. Apparently, reading a 20-page article is “too much.” Ugh, the entitlement. Speaking of which, have you seen that documentary about killer whales in captivity? It’s absolutely harrowing. No, not yet. Is it the Blackfish one? I heard it was pretty bleak. It is. It completely changed my perspective. I mean, these incredibly intelligent, social creatures, stuck in tiny tanks... it's awful. Makes you think about everything, really. All sorts of captivity. It does. It’s like that debate about TV violence. Everyone worries about kids being desensitized, but then you see something like that and you think maybe it's not the  violence  that's the problem, it's the lack of empathy it fosters. Precisely! Although, I did see a rather alarming thing on the news today about a rise in squatting in abandoned properties. Apparently, they're getting quite organised. Really? That's a bit unsettling. Though, I suppose it’s a symptom of the housing crisis, isn’t it? No easy answers. None at all. It just reminds me of being a kid, and all those stories about squatters in London. Mum was terrified we’d end up living in one. She worried about everything. Remember when you were obsessed with getting a Blue Peter badge? Oh God,  obsessed . I sent in, I swear, at least fifty letters. Designs for puppets, poems... everything. All for that orange badge. And you never got one. The injustice! Never! I was heartbroken. Actually, I think it fuelled my academic ambition. Proof I needed external validation from a young age. Well, you've got a doctorate  now , darling. I think you've done alright for yourself. And you don’t need a Blue Peter badge to prove it. Cheers to that. Though, secretly, I still want one. Just for the nostalgia.

…and then young Timothy, bless him, decided to paint the dog. With glitter glue. Honestly, the state of poor Winston! Took me an hour to get it all out of his fur. Glitter glue, eh? They'll think of anything, these youngsters. Reminds me of when my sister, Mabel, tried to give our old terrier, Buster, a haircut. Ended up looking like he'd been attacked by a particularly vicious sheep. Sounds chaotic. It’s amazing how much energy small children have. Though I’m starting to think my Year 9s have a similar level, just…directed differently. More towards eye-rolling and passive aggression. Oh, teenagers. Don't get me started. At least the little ones are honest about wanting to make a mess. Speaking of messes…did your cousin Arthur ever manage to sort out that hostel he was running? I heard it was a bit of a…situation. Arthur? Bless his heart, he tried. He always had big ideas, that one. But managing a hostel full of…well,  people … wasn’t quite the same as tinkering with engines in his shed. Said he found it all a bit overwhelming. Too much paperwork, too many complaints. Said one chap tried to pay his rent with a jar of pickled onions. Pickled onions? Seriously? Swears on it. Honestly, the stories he used to tell. Remember old Mrs. Higgins? She kept insisting the hostel was haunted by the ghost of a former cook. Oh yes! She was convinced. Always talking about cold spots and the smell of roasting beef. Though, knowing Arthur, the ‘smell of roasting beef’ was probably just his questionable cooking. Speaking of smells…my grandfather used to work in an abattoir. He always said he lost his sense of smell years before he retired. I used to go with him occasionally, as a kid. It was…an experience. Certainly put me off sausages for a while. Abattoirs. My mother’s father had a butcher's shop, you know. A proper family business. They worked so hard, my grandparents. Up at dawn every day, sorting through the meat, serving customers. No fancy refrigeration back then, just ice and a lot of elbow grease. And they ran it alongside a little greengrocery too. Hardworking folk. It’s true, isn’t it? That generation really knew the value of hard work. My parents had a little sweet shop. Always bustling, always full of sweets.

So, recruitment, huh? That’s… quite a leap to lecturing, isn’t it? I mean, no disrespect intended, it's just a very different world. Yeah, tell me about it. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m speaking a different language. Not just academically, though that’s a big part of it, but… the motivations, the timescales. Everything is so much slower paced here. Slower paced is good, isn't it? After the fire drills of teaching teenagers, a bit of contemplative academic work feels rather lovely. But really, recruitment? What drew you to that in the first place? Money, to be honest. Straight out of undergrad, needed to pay off a student loan the size of a small house. It was… easy enough to get into. A lot of phone calls, a lot of rejection handling, a lot of pretending to care about people’s career aspirations when really you just wanted to hit your targets. Sounds… draining. It was. It really was. You become very good at reading people, though. Spotting the BS a mile off. Which, oddly, is a skill that’s surprisingly useful in academia. Students can be very skilled at… let’s say  optimising  their work. Optimising. That’s a polite way of putting it. Speaking of students, how are you finding the academic literacy levels on your course? It’s something we’ve been discussing in the department. I’m worried they’re just not prepared for the demands of university-level writing. Honestly? It's… patchy. I’ve got a handful who are genuinely brilliant, can construct a coherent argument with sources, the whole shebang. But then you get others who struggle to even form a proper paragraph. It’s less about the actual content and more about the structure, the referencing, the ability to synthesize information. Exactly! It feels like they’ve been taught  what  to think, but not  how  to think. And the referencing! It’s a disaster. I had one essay last week with a bibliography that included… a meme. No way! Seriously? I wish I was joking. It was a picture of a slightly disgruntled cat with the caption “Academic Integrity.” Oh, that’s incredible. You have to show that to the department. That’s… peak student. Maybe it’s a commentary on the futility of academic pursuit? Maybe. Or maybe they just don’t understand what a source is.

Right, so you’re saying you’ve never actually  been  to Blackpool? Seriously? Never. It just… never happened. Family holidays were always the Lake District. Nice enough, but no donkeys and sticks of rock, you know? Oh, the Lake District is lovely. Bit… subdued, though. Blackpool's a full-on assault on the senses. That’s the whole point! Hi. Sorry to eavesdrop, but… Blackpool sounds… chaotic. I’ve only been in the UK a few years. I’m Priya, by the way. Oh, hello! No worries at all, we’re just being ridiculously northern. I’m Chloe. This is Liam, and that’s Sarah. Nice to meet you, Priya. Yeah, Blackpool  is  chaotic. Gloriously so. I’m Sarah. Where are you from originally, Priya? India. Mumbai. It’s… a bit different to Salford, to say the least. Though, Salford’s growing on me. The people are very friendly. Aw, that's good to hear! Mumbai must be amazing. Do you miss the food the most? Because I’d be gutted if I couldn’t get a good curry anymore. The street food, definitely. And my grandmother's cooking. Nothing compares. Although, I did discover a fantastic Indian restaurant just around the corner from campus… Oh, which one? I’m always on the lookout for somewhere decent. It’s called ‘Spice Haven’. It’s small but the food is authentic. Ooh, noted! I’m a fiend for a vindaloo. Liam, you’re not brave enough for a vindaloo, are you? I am so brave! I once had a… a medium strength korma. It was fiery. A medium strength korma? That barely registers on the Scoville scale! You’re such a softie. So, Priya, what are you studying here at Salford? I’m doing a Masters in Environmental Science. It’s a big change from what I did for my undergrad - film studies. Wow, that’s a leap! What made you switch? I loved film, but I realized I wanted to do something more… practical. Something that could actually make a difference. Good for you. It's good to know what you want to do, isn’t it? I’m still working that out. I’m just plugging away at a retail job while I figure things out. Don’t beat yourself up about it, Liam. It takes time. I’m doing a PhD, and honestly, some days I wonder if I made the right choice.

Right, so then Uncle Barry starts going on about his time in the Falklands, again. Honestly, you’d think he single-handedly won the war, the way he carries on. Oh god, not Barry with the war stories. Does he still claim he was a sniper? Claims he  trained  as a sniper. Which is, like, drastically different. And then started questioning why everyone's so obsessed with, like, Marvel films instead of documentaries about actual bravery. Ugh. Family dinners, eh? It’s always something. I had to actively disengage to avoid getting drawn into a debate about Brexit with my dad. He’s convinced everything is going to fall apart. Sounds delightful. At least yours doesn’t dredge up the Falklands every five minutes. Though, speaking of things falling apart, have you seen the new issue of ‘Wired’? They’ve got this long piece about the potential for cyber warfare. Proper scary stuff. Oh, I skimmed that online! It’s a bit… intense. My brother's really into all that, building his own computers and stuff. He's convinced we’re all heading towards a digital apocalypse. He keeps trying to get me to learn coding. Oh, bless him. Coding sounds like my personal hell. I can barely work the office printer, let alone write algorithms. Though, I did try that online course on graphic design, remember? Lasted about a week. Oh yeah! And then you realised Photoshop was way more complicated than Instagram filters? Exactly! It’s just… too many options. I like things simple. Speaking of simple, I’ve been rewatching ‘Paddington 2’. Honestly, such a feel-good film. It genuinely makes me happy. You and ‘Paddington’. You’re a softie at heart, you are. I've been on a bit of a 80s kick actually. Watched 'The Breakfast Club' again last night. Still holds up. Oh, classic! Though, I always felt bad for Bender. He’s just a product of his environment, isn’t he? I liked the brain. Yeah, he was a bit of a rebel. Makes you wonder what happened to them all afterwards. I saw an article online claiming Ally Sheedy is now a poet. Really? That’s nice! It’s good when people don’t just… disappear after being in a big film. Though, honestly, I’m more interested in what they're  doing  rather than what they were  in . I'm thinking of trying to get into magazine layout, maybe doing something a bit more creative alongside the events stuff.

Honestly, the state of dating apps right now is… a disaster. It’s just endless photos of guys holding fish. Or posing with tigers. Like, what is  that  about? Tigers are a red flag, absolutely. Signals either you're funding illegal wildlife trade, or you think it’s cool to exploit animals for Instagram likes. Both bad. The fish thing, though… I almost get that. It's a talking point, right? Something to break the ice. It’s just… boring. And feels like they’re trying too hard. Like, “Look at me, I’m adventurous!” No, you just went to a tourist trap. I swiped left on a guy whose entire profile was photos from a stag do in Magaluf. Oh,  god . That’s… dedicated commitment to being awful. Did anyone actually enjoy the basketball, by the way? I was mostly people-watching. It was alright. Felt a bit… aggressive, honestly. Lot of elbows flying. I was worried someone was going to take an eye out. Yeah, I got accidentally clocked in the arm a couple of times. Not exactly graceful. Speaking of aggressive, did you see that article about the new planning regulations? Absolute shambles. Oh, don’t even get me started. They’re trying to push through that ridiculous housing development on the green belt, aren't they? It's horrifying. It’s completely ignoring local objections. It’s the same everywhere. Politicians making decisions that benefit developers and completely screw over communities. It's infuriating. Reminds me of that documentary I was filming last month… the guy was fighting a similar battle in his village. Honestly, politics just feels… hopeless sometimes. Especially with everyone down south getting all the investment. It’s always ‘London, London, London’. My cousin's coming up from London next weekend, actually. She’s visiting. Prepare for a full report on how much better everything is ‘down south’. Oh, lovely. Can't wait for her to tell us how ‘vibrant’ and ‘cultural’ it is while simultaneously complaining about the tube being delayed. She always does that. It's predictable. Although, she did bring me back some amazing pastries once... Right, bribery. It's her tactic. Hey, anyone fancy thinking about, like, actual future plans? Apart from dodging rogue elbows and avoiding Londoners? I’m starting to think about applying for that job in Bristol. Bristol’s cool! Good music scene, decent film festivals… how competitive is it?

So, yeah, the bike’s getting a full service next week. Bit pricey, honestly, but worth it. Don’t want anything going wrong on a long ride. Ooh, good plan. You doing that coastal route again, the one down to Rye? It looks beautiful on Instagram, though I imagine it’s absolutely brutal going uphill. Rye? Lovely little place, Rye. Used to go down there with your mother, years ago. Before all this… modern nonsense. Just a good old-fashioned seaside town then. Not all fancy shops and…what do you call ‘em…artisanal bakeries. Oh, Reginald. You and your ‘modern nonsense’! They’re nice bakeries, though. And a good scone makes all the difference. Speaking of scones… cream tea is definitely on the cards while you’re here. Though, the debate rages on – jam first or cream first? Cream first, always. Absolutely always. It’s the Cornish way! Though, I’ll admit, I’ve heard arguments. Silly arguments, mind you. I’m with Reginald, cream first. It creates a nice little…barrier, doesn't it? Stops the jam soaking right in. Hmm. I’m a bit of a jam-first girl myself. But I won’t start a fight. Honestly, I’m just happy to have a proper cream tea. It’s been ages. Right, operation cream tea is a go. We’ll get everything sorted. I even think I found a decent clotted cream supplier online. Though, I'm feeling a bit guilty about the cost of everything lately. The utility bills are… astronomical. Oh, tell me about it. Rent’s ridiculous everywhere now, isn’t it? Even up in Brighton. Brighton! Full of students and…well, people behaving badly. Not like it used to be. Used to be a lovely place for a day trip. Now it’s just…loud. And expensive. Brighton’s alright. A bit hectic, maybe, but there's always something going on. It’s good for a change of scene. You should come down with us, Reginald. We can take the train. Me? On a train? With all those…youngsters? No, thank you very much. I’m quite happy here, thank you. Though, is that…paprika? What are you doing with paprika in the kitchen? Just experimenting with a new spice blend. Trying to make a really good rub for chicken. Had a friend who went travelling in India, brought a whole suitcase full of spices back.

Honestly, the internet was  down  all morning. Proper down. Not just slow, like, completely non-existent. How am I supposed to doomscroll before work, honestly? It's a fundamental human right at this point. No way! Seriously? That's awful. I rely on it for, well, everything, really. Work mostly. I was preemptively stressed about a Teams meeting this afternoon, picturing myself just… staring blankly into the void while everyone else carries on. Thankfully, it seems to be behaving now. It came back on around ten, thankfully. I’d already had three coffees trying to distract myself. And checked the router about fifty times. It's always the router, isn't it? Even when it's definitely  not  the router. Always. It’s like blaming the kettle when you’ve just run out of water. Speaking of work, it's… a lot. They’ve thrown another project at me. Something about flood risk modelling for a new development just outside of town. It’s fascinating, genuinely, but the deadlines are  insane . Oh, that sounds stressful. Corpus is… Corpus. It's usually pretty calm, but even  we’ve  been busy. Freshers’ Week fallout, you know? Endless forms, lost students, parents emailing asking why their child hasn’t received their welcome pack. The usual chaos. Sounds…exhausting. Still better than being on a building site in November though, I reckon. It's already freezing. Did you see the forecast? They're predicting snow next week. Oh, brilliant. Just what we need. And speaking of freezing, I tried to make that butternut squash soup you told me about last week. It was... an experience. Oh no! What happened? Was it the spices? I remember mentioning a pinch of nutmeg... No, it wasn’t the spices. I think I just… overestimated my blending skills. It was like butternut squash baby food. Smooth as silk, but tasted solely of regret and slightly burnt onions. Oh dear. Well, Rome wasn’t built in a day, and neither is a perfect butternut squash soup. It takes practice! True. I might just stick to toasties. It's safer. Anyway, have you been following this whole… political mess? It's just endlessly depressing. Honestly, I try to avoid it as much as possible. It's just a constant stream of negativity. Plus, it makes my head hurt. I did see something about house prices going up again though. Absolutely mental.

Honestly, the shift was  mental  yesterday. Old Mr. Henderson decided he was a concert pianist and kept demanding I fetch his “audience.” No way! Seriously? Oh, bless him. He's always been a bit…eccentric, hasn’t he? Is he new to the home or has he always been like that? Always. But it's usually just humming. Yesterday was full-blown requests for applause and a spotlight. I had to gently remind him he wasn't at the Royal Albert Hall. That's rough. I had Mrs. Davies convinced her cat had followed her into the care home. Spent half an hour searching under beds for a phantom feline. Oh my god, you're kidding! People are wild. Speaking of wild, did you hear about Chloe’s party last night? Apparently, Ben showed up wearing a full dinosaur costume. Ben?  Ben ? He’s usually the sensible one. I know, right? Apparently, it was a dare. Lots of tequila involved, naturally. I didn’t go, felt a bit wiped after working all weekend. Speaking of work, I’m so exhausted. My feet are killing me. Old Mrs. Peterson keeps trying to “walk” and I have to practically hoist her up every five minutes. Honestly, I need a holiday. Tell me about it. It’s relentless. At least with animals, they mostly just sleep and eat. My neighbour's dog is driving me mad though, barking all the time. Oh, that’s awful. We’re lucky, Buster’s pretty chilled. He mostly just snores on the sofa and judges everyone. He's adorable though! How’s your mum, by the way? You said she had a doctor's appointment? She went. It’s just her back playing up again. Apparently, it's arthritis. She’s being stubborn about taking the painkillers. Says she doesn't want to feel “doped up.” Oh, mums. They're all the same. Mine refuses to wear sensible shoes, swears her bunions are “just a bit of a twinge.” My nan is the same. Completely ignores all medical advice. Gets everything from Facebook, honestly. That’s terrifying! I’m trying to convince my dad to get a smart watch, just so I can track his steps and make sure he's not collapsing in the garden. Good idea. Mine's hopeless with technology. She thinks Facebook is just for looking at pictures of cats. My sister’s thinking of moving to Australia.
